name: Pan-browned braised rice
summary: Dry long-grain rice toasted in an oiled pan until golden, then simmered in hot broth until tender.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: to coat the bottom of the pan

steps: Pour enough oil into a cold skillet to coat the bottom, add the dry long-grain rice, and spread it in an even layer.
Fry the rice, stirring occasionally and re-spreading into an even layer until most grains are golden, while heating the broth in a separate pot.
Gradually pour the hot broth in small splashes through a gap under a slightly tilted lid, waiting each time until the liquid stops violently steaming and splattering.
Once all the broth is added, cook the rice covered over higher heat until the grains swell and absorb all the liquid.

name: Sałatka winogronowo-porzeczkowa (grape and currant salad)
summary: A light salad of green lettuce, salty feta-style cheese, grapes and currants, drizzled with vinaigrette.
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, then cut them into narrow strips.
Cut the cheese into batons.
Halve the grapes and remove the seeds, then rinse and dry the currants.
Combine all the prepared ingredients in a bowl, season lightly with salt, sprinkle with parsley, and drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Toss the salad gently and serve immediately.

name: Raffaello (no-bake coconut slice)
summary: No-bake coconut dessert layered with salted crackers and coconut-custard buttercream.

ingredients.name: shredded coconut
ingredients.note: 100 g for the cream, 100 g for sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: 250 ml to bring to a boil, 750 ml to mix with flour and yolks

steps: In a heavy-bottomed pot, bring 250 ml of milk to a boil with 100 g of shredded coconut and the vanilla sugar.
In a separate bowl, thoroughly mix the remaining 750 ml of milk with the plain flour, potato starch, and egg yolks.
Slowly pour the mixture into the boiling milk while stirring constantly until a thick custard forms, then set aside to cool completely.
Beat the softened butter or margarine with a mixer, gradually adding the cooled coconut custard one spoonful at a time.
Line the bottom of a square baking pan with a layer of crackers and spread half of the cream over them.
Arrange a second layer of crackers, spread the remaining cream, sprinkle the top with the rest of the shredded coconut, and chill in the refrigerator.

name: Sweet and spicy skewers (Szaszłyki słodko-pikantne)
summary: Grilled skewers of cooked ham, ripe peaches, orange segments, and fresh lemon balm leaves.
steps: Wash the peaches, cut into quarters, and remove the pits.
Scrub the orange, grate a little zest, peel the fruit, divide into segments, and slice each crosswise into three pieces.
Cut the cooked ham into thick slices, then cut into quarters.
Thread onto skewers alternately pieces of ham, peach, a lemon balm leaf, and a piece of orange.
Brush the skewers with oil, sprinkle with grated orange zest and pepper, and grill away from direct flame until lightly browned.

name: Kaczka z winogronami (duck braised with red wine and dark grapes)
summary: Duck braised in red wine with dark grapes and a hint of nutmeg.
steps: Wash and pat dry the whole duck, cut into 8–10 pieces, sprinkle with half of the red wine, and place in the refrigerator.
Pluck the grapes from their stems, rinse, and dry them.
Sear the duck pieces on all sides in heated oil and transfer to a saucepan.
Season the meat with salt and pepper, cover, and braise, basting with the remaining wine and water with the dissolved bouillon cube.
Towards the end of braising, add the grapes and heat briefly so they release juice without bursting apart.
Season the dish with ground nutmeg, salt, and a pinch of sugar.

name: Barszcz czerwony (Clear Polish beetroot borscht)
summary: A clear, full-flavoured beetroot borscht made with homemade beet sour and dried mushroom broth.
steps: 5 days before cooking the borscht, prepare the beet sour: place half-slices of 3 beetroots, crumbled wholemeal bread, and halved garlic heads into a jar, cover with lukewarm water, seal, and keep in a dark place at room temperature, then strain once fermented.
Rinse the dried mushrooms thoroughly, soak them in water, and simmer separately in the same liquid, then carefully pour off the clear mushroom broth from the sediment.
Slice the beetroots and onion, cut the unpeeled apple into wedges, and cut the peeled garlic cloves in half.

Cover the prepared vegetables with cold water or clear beef broth, add the cooked mushrooms along with their broth, leek leaves, thyme, bay leaf, parsley leaves, celery rib, marjoram, and whole peppercorns.
Pour in the beet sour starter, bring to a boil, and simmer gently for at most 10 minutes.
Toward the end of cooking, stir in the lemon juice and a splash of red wine vinegar, then leave the unstrained borscht in a cool place until the next day.
The next day, strain the borscht, heat thoroughly without letting it boil, and season to taste with salt, sugar, and pepper.

name: Stuffed melon with berries and orange liqueur
summary: Ripe melon halves filled with a chilled fruit salad of melon balls, raspberries, orange liqueur, and almonds.
steps: Wash the melons thoroughly, cut in half, scoop out the seeds, and scoop the flesh into small balls, leaving a layer of about 5 mm next to the rind.
Hull the raspberries, rinse, and leave in a sieve to drain.

Combine the raspberries with the melon balls, drizzle with the orange liqueur, dust with powdered sugar, season with lemon juice, and chill in the refrigerator together with the hollowed-out melon halves.
Scald the almonds, peel off the skins, chop, and mix with the chilled fruits, then spoon the salad into the melon halves.

name: Sałatka pikantna (spiced fruit salad)
summary: A spiced fruit salad of peaches, pears, apple, and red gooseberries marinated in white wine with ginger and nutmeg, served as an accompaniment to roast meats.
steps: Peel the peaches, pears, and apple, remove the pits and cores, cut the fruit into large dice, and sprinkle with freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Wash the red gooseberries and slice them in half lengthwise.
Mix all the fruit in a bowl, add a pinch each of ground ginger, nutmeg, and icing sugar, and pour in the white wine.
Set the salad aside for 60 minutes for the flavours to meld, then serve as an accompaniment to roast meat.

name: Chir (Middle Eastern milk and rice dessert)
summary: A traditional milk and rice dessert with cardamom, raisins, rose syrup, and nuts, served at the end of Ramadan.
steps: Bring the milk to a boil in a wide pot, stir in the rice, and simmer over medium heat for about 5 minutes until the mixture begins to thicken.
Stirring continuously, add the sugar, raisins, seeds from the cardamom pods, and butter.
Cook for another 10–15 minutes until thick, stirring in the rose syrup along the way.
Pour the pudding into a serving dish or mould, scatter chopped pistachios over the top, cover, and chill before serving.

name: Krówki (Polish milk fudge)
summary: Homemade Polish dairy caramels cooked from milk and sugar enriched with butter.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the dish

steps: Combine the milk and sugar in a heavy-bottomed pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer slowly, stirring regularly and scraping down the sides of the pot, until the mixture turns golden and a drop placed on a plate sets quickly.
Remove the pot from the heat, add the butter, and beat the mixture vigorously with a wooden spoon.
Pour the mixture into a shallow greased dish, wait a few minutes, and slice into bars using a knife dipped in cold water.

name: Puffed rice caramel cones (Szyszki)
summary: A traditional homemade Polish sweet made from puffed rice bound with melted krówki cream fudge and butter.
steps: Unwrap the cream candies and transfer them to a pot together with the butter.
Heat the ingredients over low heat, stirring, until the fudge candies and butter have completely melted.
Gradually pour in the puffed rice and mix thoroughly so the grains are evenly coated in the caramel mixture.
Put on plastic gloves and shape the warm mixture into oblong cones, then set aside to firm up (if the mixture cools and hardens too much during shaping, warm it slightly).

name: Burritos (chicken and red bean burritos)
summary: Mexican wheat tortillas filled with a spicy mixture of chicken, red beans, tomatoes, and grated yellow cheese.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: about 300 g for making dough for 6 flatbreads

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: about 180 ml of warm water for making the dough

steps: Dice the chicken breast, season with salt, black pepper, oregano, cinnamon, and hot paprika, then fry in hot olive oil and transfer to a pot.
In the same pan, fry the minced garlic and sliced onion rings, add the drained canned red kidney beans and canned tomatoes, and cook together briefly.
Transfer the pan contents to the pot with the chicken, add the chopped chili pepper, and braise for about 10 minutes, finishing with the basil and chopped chives.
Knead a pliable, soft dough from wheat flour, water, and a splash of olive oil, then rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into portions, roll each into a thin round flatbread, and cook on both sides in a hot dry skillet.
Place the grated yellow cheese and hot filling on the cooked flatbreads, then fold them in half or roll them up.

name: Red soup with rice and minced beef
summary: A hearty tomato soup with ground beef, white rice, onion, and ground caraway, finished with sour cream.

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: from fresh vegetables or a bouillon cube

steps: Peel the onions, dice them finely, and cook in a pot with heated olive oil until translucent.
Add the minced garlic, ground beef, and white rice, and fry for a few minutes while stirring constantly.
Pour in the tomato juice and vegetable broth, add the bay leaf and ground caraway, then simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes.
Season the soup to taste with salt, pepper, and sugar.
Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the sour cream, and serve.

name: Spaghetti con sugo alla diavola
summary: Italian spaghetti in a spicy vegetable and tomato sauce cooked with rosemary, dried and fresh chili, and grated cheese.
steps: Blend the celery, carrots, onion, garlic, and fresh rosemary leaves, then sauté well in heated olive oil.
Add the finely diced peeled tomatoes, salt, coarsely ground black pepper, and dried chili, pour in 250 ml of water, and simmer over low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
A few minutes before finishing the sauce, stir in the fresh chili sliced into rings.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water, drain, toss with the hot sauce and grated cheese, and arrange on plates.

name: Garlic mayonnaise
summary: Creamy garlic mayonnaise in the style of aioli made with sunflower oil, olive oil, and egg yolks.
steps: Leave all ingredients at room temperature for 30 minutes so they reach an even temperature of about 20–25 °C.
Mash the garlic with salt into a smooth paste, then add the egg yolks, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice.
Whisking constantly, pour in the mixture of 250 ml of sunflower oil and 250 ml of olive oil in small portions until the mayonnaise becomes creamy and fluffy.
Season to taste with black pepper, sugar, and salt, stir, and transfer into sterilized jars.

name: Kung Pao chicken
summary: Classic Chinese stir-fry of chicken pieces marinated in egg white and cornflour (cornstarch), cooked in a wok with garlic, soy sauce, rice wine, and sesame oil.
steps: Place the diced chicken into a bowl, add the egg white, salt, and 1 tablespoon of cornstarch, mix thoroughly, and set aside for 30 minutes.
Cook the rice according to the package instructions.
Heat 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a wok, stir-fry the chicken until lightly browned, and transfer to a plate.
Pour the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil into the wok, add the crushed garlic, and fry for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir in the soy sauce, rice wine or sherry, sugar, vinegar, and sesame oil.
Mix the remaining 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of water, pour into the wok, and simmer gently until the sauce thickens and becomes clear. Serve with rice.

name: Chiński bulion (Chinese chicken and pork broth)
summary: An aromatic broth made from chicken backs and pork bones with fresh ginger, spring onions, and garlic, used as a base for Chinese dishes.
steps: Place the chicken backs, pork bones, sliced spring onions, minced fresh ginger, garlic, and salt in a large pot and add the water.
Stir the ingredients, bring the broth to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 15 minutes.
Skim off excess fat from the surface, strain the broth through a sieve, and let cool.

name: Kakao korzenne (spiced hot cocoa)
summary: Warming hot cocoa made with milk, cinnamon, ginger, vanilla, and a pinch of chili.
steps: Bring the milk and brown sugar to a boil in a saucepan.
Slit the vanilla bean lengthwise in half and scrape out the seeds.
Dissolve the unsweetened cocoa powder in cold water, then add the cinnamon, ginger, ground chili, and vanilla.
Pour the cocoa mixture into the boiling milk, stir thoroughly, remove from the heat, and serve hot.

name: Pizza dough (Pizza - ciasto)
summary: Homemade yeast pizza dough for two thick, fluffy crust pizzas made with plain wheat flour.
steps: Place the yeast in a bowl, sprinkle with sugar, add a pinch of salt and warm water, and stir until the yeast dissolves.
Add the wheat flour and knead the dough by hand until smooth and coming away cleanly from the sides of the bowl.
Divide the dough into 2 equal parts, shape into balls, cover with a kitchen cloth, and let rise in a warm place for 10–15 minutes.
Knead the risen dough briefly on a work surface and stretch by hand into 2 round pizza bases.
Place the bases on baking sheets and bake with your choice of toppings in an oven preheated to 220–250 °C for about 15–20 minutes.

name: Ciapkapusta (Silesian mashed potatoes with sauerkraut)
summary: A traditional Silesian dish of mashed potatoes combined with cooked sauerkraut and dressed with smoked bacon, fatback, and golden fried onions.
steps: Rinse the sauerkraut and boil until tender in a separate pot, while boiling the peeled potatoes in another pot.
Peel and finely dice the onion, and cut the smoked bacon and pork fatback into small cubes.
Render the pork fatback in a skillet, add the smoked bacon and diced onion, and fry until golden.
Drain and finely chop the cooked sauerkraut, combine with the mashed potatoes and the fried bacon and onion, mix well, and season to taste with salt and black pepper.

name: Pork tenderloin in mustard and cheese sauce (Polędwica z sosem musztardowo-serowym)
summary: Slices of pork tenderloin pan-fried in butter, served in a rich creamy white wine sauce with Camembert cheese, Dijon mustard, and fresh herbs.
steps: Cut the pork tenderloin into slices and gently pound them.
Melt the butter in a skillet, fry the pork slices for about 6–7 minutes on both sides, then transfer to a warm place.
Pour the white wine into the pan drippings and bring to a boil.
Add the heavy cream, chopped herbs, skinned Camembert, and Dijon mustard.
Simmer the sauce over low heat, stirring until the cheese has melted, and season with freshly ground pepper.
Arrange the pork slices on plates and spoon the hot sauce over them.

name: Roast pork loin with almonds (Schab w migdałach)
summary: Roast pork loin marinated in white wine and lemon juice, finished with a sweet crust of honey and flaked almonds.

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp reserved for the almond paste, the rest for the marinade

steps: Rub the pork loin with salt, pepper, and traditional Polish seasoning, then prick the meat deeply all over.
Drizzle the pork with the lemon juice and wine (reserving 1 tbsp of wine for later), then refrigerate for 3 hours.
Tie the marinated roast with kitchen twine and brown on all sides in hot melted margarine.
Transfer the pork loin to a baking dish and roast for about 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C, basting regularly with the pan juices.
Place the flaked almonds in a plastic bag, crush them into smaller pieces, and mix with the honey and reserved tablespoon of wine.
Remove the roast from the oven, cut away the twine, spread the almond paste evenly over the top, and bake for another 10–15 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Shrimp skewers (Szaszłyki z krewetek)
summary: Grilled shrimp skewers marinated in garlic olive oil with pickled shallots and bell peppers, served with a white wine pan sauce.
steps: Mix 100 ml of olive oil with 8 blended garlic cloves, immerse the shrimp in the marinade, and chill in the refrigerator for about 120 minutes.
Cut the red bell peppers into pieces, then thread the shrimp onto skewers in a horseshoe shape wrapping around a pickled shallot, alternating with pieces of bell pepper.
Dust the skewers with fish seasoning and cook on a hot grill.
Chop the onion and 4 cloves of garlic, sauté in olive oil, add the white wine and a few drops of Tabasco sauce, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Brush the grilled skewers with the prepared sauce and serve hot.

name: Eggplant moussaka
summary: Greek casserole of fried eggplant slices and minced beef simmered with tomatoes and white wine, baked under cheesy béchamel sauce.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: plus extra for dusting the dish

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the dish

steps: Char the eggplants over an open flame, rub off the charred skin, slice, sprinkle with salt, and let stand in a cool place for 60 minutes.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the finely chopped onion until translucent without browning.
Pour in the hot water, add the minced beef, and fry while breaking it up with a fork to prevent lumps.
Add the peeled, seeded tomatoes, chopped parsley leaves, and white wine, season with salt and pepper, and braise covered over very low heat for about 45 minutes.
Remove the meat from the heat, stir in the breadcrumbs, then fold in the lightly beaten egg whites.
Rinse the eggplant slices, dry thoroughly on a kitchen cloth, and fry in heated olive oil on both sides until golden.

Butter and coat with breadcrumbs a shallow baking dish measuring about 30 × 20 cm, arrange a layer of eggplants on the bottom, spread the meat and tomato mixture on top, and cover with the remaining eggplants.

Mix the béchamel sauce with the egg yolks and 60 g of grated cheese, pour over the casserole, scatter with the remaining cheese, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 45 minutes until golden.

name: Knedle z wiśniami (cherry potato dumplings)
summary: Potato dough dumplings filled with sweetened sour cherries, served with melted butter and breadcrumbs.
steps: Wash the potatoes, boil until tender, peel, and pass through a grinder.
Add the plain flour, egg, and salt to the potatoes and briefly knead into a uniform dough.
Roll the dough into logs 2.5 cm in diameter and cut them into equal rounds.
Place the pitted sour cherries sprinkled with sugar and vanilla sugar onto each dough disc, then pinch the edges together and roll into a ball.
Drop the knedle in batches into salted boiling water, bring back to a boil, and cook until they float.
Serve the knedle drizzled with melted butter, dusted with breadcrumbs, and sprinkled with sugar.

name: Modro kapusta (Silesian braised red cabbage with bacon)
summary: Silesian braised red cabbage cooked and seasoned with smoked bacon, onion, vinegar, and sugar.
steps: Shred the red cabbage, boil until tender, and drain off any excess liquid.
Season the cooked cabbage with vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Finely dice the onion and smoked bacon, fry the bacon with the onion, and add to the cabbage.
Toss all ingredients together thoroughly before serving.

name: Makówki (Silesian poppy seed bread pudding)
summary: Traditional Silesian Christmas Eve dessert made of layered challah bread and sweet poppy seed mixture simmered in milk with dried fruits and nuts.
steps: Cut the challah bread into slices.
Bring the milk, sugar, vanilla sugar, and butter to a boil in a pot, add the ground poppy seeds, and simmer over low heat for 10–15 minutes until thick, stirring constantly.
Cut the dried figs into thin slices, and scald and drain the walnuts, almonds, and raisins; stir most of the dried fruits and nuts into the simmering poppy seed mixture, then remove from the heat.
Arrange alternating layers of challah slices and poppy seed mixture in a bowl, finishing with the poppy seed mixture.
Garnish the top with the remaining almonds, walnuts, and raisins, and sprinkle with desiccated coconut.

name: Ajnlauf (Silesian drop noodle chicken soup)
summary: A traditional Silesian chicken broth served with delicate drop batter noodles and fresh parsley leaves.
steps: Whisk the eggs with a fork, gradually adding the wheat flour and one tablespoon of water or milk, and beat for about 4 minutes until a smooth batter with the consistency of thick sour cream forms.
Pour the batter in a thin stream into the boiling chicken broth while gently stirring the soup.
Cook briefly until the drop noodles float to the surface, then serve the soup sprinkled with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Wodzionka (Silesian bread and garlic soup)
summary: A traditional Silesian soup of stale bread, mashed garlic, and homemade lard with boiling water poured over them, also made with mashed potatoes and cracklings or as germuszka, in which the bread is cooked until it breaks down, with caraway and egg.
steps: Peel the garlic and mash it with salt.
Add the mashed garlic to boiling water with lard, remove the pot from the heat, and season with salt to taste.
Dice the stale bread and add it to the soup immediately before serving.

In variant II (with potatoes), boil 1 kg of potatoes separately, mash them with cracklings made from 50 g of fatback and 1 small onion, arrange on plates in a cone shape, and pour hot wodzianka over them; in a related variant (germuszka), cook down 6 slices of bread in 2 l of water with a teaspoon of caraway and salt, pour in 2 beaten eggs, bring to a boil, and finish with 2 tablespoons of butter.

name: Hekele (Silesian herring and egg spread)
summary: Traditional Silesian sandwich spread made from salted herring, hard-boiled eggs, fermented brine pickles, and onion.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs, let them cool, and peel them.
Soak the salted herring in cold water and remove any bones.
Grind the herring fillets in a meat grinder together with the eggs, peeled onion, and fermented pickle.
Season the mixture with black pepper to taste and mix thoroughly.

name: Kartoffelsalat (German potato salad)
summary: German potato salad with fermented pickles, onions, smoked meat, and mayonnaise.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins, allow them to cool, peel, and cut into cubes.
Finely chop the fermented pickles and onions, then combine them with the potatoes.
Dice the smoked meat, render in a skillet until crisp, and add to the salad.
Season the salad with salt and pepper, mix with mayonnaise, and garnish with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Karminadle (Silesian broth meat patties)
summary: Silesian minced meat patties made from cooked soup meat and Polish soup vegetables.

ingredients.name: soup greens (włoszczyzna)
ingredients.note: carrot, parsley root, celeriac, white cabbage

steps: Rinse the meat and simmer in water until tender (for 45–60 minutes) with the peeled soup greens, allspice berries, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Remove the cooked meat and vegetables from the broth, debone the meat, and grind both in a meat grinder.
Peel the onion, finely dice it, and add to the minced meat and vegetable mixture.
Crack in the egg, add breadcrumbs, season with salt and pepper, and knead the mixture thoroughly.
Shape into round patties about 1.5 cm thick and 5 cm in diameter.
Fry the patties in hot oil for 2 minutes on each side.

name: Rolada śląska (Silesian beef roulade)
summary: Traditional Silesian beef roulades stuffed with smoked bacon, brine pickles, onion, and mustard, braised in a rich gravy.
steps: Rinse the beef, slice it into cutlets, and pound gently with a water-moistened meat mallet.
Rub the meat slices with salt and pepper, then spread each with mustard and tomato paste.
Cut the onion, brine pickles, and smoked bacon into thin strips and place them onto the beef slices.
Roll the meat tightly into roulades and secure with toothpicks or tie with white kitchen twine.
Melt the lard in a saucepan, add the roulades, and brown thoroughly on all sides.
Add water or broth to the pan, cover, and braise for about 60 minutes until the roulades are tender.
Remove the toothpicks or twine from the finished roulades, thicken the sauce with sour cream stirred with plain flour, and bring briefly to a boil.

name: Tomato and mushroom tart (Tarta z pomidorami)
summary: A covered shortcrust tart layered with tomatoes, button mushrooms, sweetcorn, firm cheese, and fresh basil.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the tin

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.note: added tablespoon by tablespoon to bind the dough

steps: Sift the flour with the sugar and salt, add the diced butter, chop with a knife into fine crumbs, and rub together with your fingertips.
Add the cold water tablespoon by tablespoon and knead into a springy, uniform dough, then wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C, wash and slice the tomatoes into rounds, slice the button mushrooms and firm cheese, drain the sweetcorn, and prepare the basil leaves.
Divide the chilled dough into two portions in a 2/3 and 1/3 ratio, roll out the larger portion, and press it into the bottom and sides of a buttered 28 cm tart tin.

Arrange a layer of firm cheese, button mushrooms, tomatoes, and basil leaves over the base, sprinkle with sweetcorn, oregano, and thyme, and top with another layer of cheese, tomatoes, and mushrooms, pressing the filling down gently.
Roll out the remaining portion of dough, cover the filling, and bake for 50 minutes, making sure the edges do not burn.

name: Kluski na parze (steamed yeast dumplings)
summary: Fluffy steamed yeast dumplings, served sweet with melted butter and sugar.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 60–70 g, very soft, plus extra for drizzling

steps: Mash the yeast with 1 tsp of sugar, 1 tsp of plain flour, and 75 ml of warm milk to make a starter.
Pour the remaining plain flour into a bowl, make a well, pour in the starter, cover with a cloth, and set aside for about 30 minutes until active.
Add the egg, remaining milk, very soft butter, remaining sugar, and a pinch of salt to the bowl, and knead the dough by hand or with a mixer until smooth.
Dust the dough with plain flour, roll out to a thickness of 1.5 cm, and cut out rounds with a round cutter.
Cover the shaped dumplings with a cloth and leave for about 30 minutes to double in volume.
Arrange the risen dumplings in batches on a steamer insert and steam, covered, for 5–10 minutes.
Serve the ready dumplings drizzled with butter and sprinkled with sugar.

name: Omlet (classic French omelette)
summary: A classic fluffy egg omelette made with milk and flour, served either sweet or savoury.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the milk, flour, and optional sugar, and whisk thoroughly.
Heat the butter or oil in a frying pan and pour in the prepared egg mixture.
Fry over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until the bottom is lightly browned and the top is softly set.
Slide the finished omelette onto a plate and serve immediately after frying.

name: Silesian miner-style stuffed pork loin (Schab po sztygarsku)
summary: Silesian pork loin stuffed with Silesian kiełbasa, braised with onions, garlic, and caraway, served with a rich sour cream gravy.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or broth, for basting and 150–200 ml for the sauce

ingredients.name: liquid seasoning (such as Maggi)
ingredients.note: a few drops for the gravy

steps: Cut a deep pocket lengthwise through the center of the pork loin and insert the skinned Silesian kiełbasa inside.
Rub the pork with salt and pepper, then sear it on all sides in hot lard until browned.
Transfer the meat to a roasting pan, pour in water or broth, cover, and braise in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes.
Remove the lid, sprinkle the pork with caraway and sweet paprika, scatter the sliced onions and garlic cloves around it, and roast uncovered for another 20 minutes, adding more water if needed.
Remove the roasted meat, stir the flour into 150–200 ml of cold water until smooth, pour into the roasting pan juices, and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Season the thickened gravy with sour cream and a few drops of liquid seasoning, and serve with the sliced pork loin.

name: Hollandaise sauce
summary: A classic French emulsified sauce made with egg yolks whisked with lemon juice and melted butter, seasoned with white pepper and nutmeg.
steps: Melt the butter in a small saucepan.
Whisk the egg yolks with part of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and white pepper.
Without stopping whisking, slowly pour in the melted butter until the sauce becomes smooth and creamy.
Season the finished sauce to taste with salt, white pepper, nutmeg, and a few drops of lemon juice.

name: Placki ziemniaczane (potato pancakes)
summary: Crispy traditional Polish pancakes made from freshly grated potatoes and onion bound with egg and flour, pan-fried to a golden brown.
steps: Wash and thinly peel the potatoes, rinse them again, and grate on a box grater into a bowl.
Peel the onion, finely dice it, and add to the grated potatoes along with the egg, wheat flour, and salt.
Mix the batter thoroughly with a spoon until the potatoes and onion release their juices and the mixture becomes cohesive.
Heat the fat well in a skillet and drop spoonfuls of the potato batter into the hot pan, stirring the mixture in the bowl before each batch.
Fry the pancakes on both sides until golden brown, flipping them with a spatula.

name: Panna cotta (caramel cream with red wine reduction)
summary: An Italian cream dessert with a hint of caramel, set with gelatine and served with a reduced red wine sauce.
steps: Bring the cream to a boil in a saucepan and remove it from the heat.
In a separate saucepan, melt 150 g of sugar, heating and stirring until a golden caramel forms.
Remove the caramel from the heat, slowly pour in the hot cream while stirring continuously, then bring the mixture back to a boil.
Take the saucepan off the heat, stir in the dissolved gelatine, and mix until completely incorporated.
Pour the cream into ramekins and refrigerate until fully set.
Combine the wine, remaining sugar, and raspberry vinegar in a saucepan and simmer until the liquid reduces to about 190 ml.
Let the reduced sauce cool, stir in the citrus zest, and drizzle over the chilled dessert before serving.

name: Kerststol (Dutch Christmas fruit bread)
summary: Dutch Christmas yeast bread studded with rum-soaked dried fruits and filled with homemade almond marzipan paste.
steps: Grind the blanched almonds in a food processor or grinder, add the beaten egg and granulated sugar, and mix into a uniform, compact almond paste, then wrap in cling film and chill in the refrigerator.
In a bowl, combine the raisins, candied lemon peel, candied orange peel, and candied cherries, pour over the rum, cover, and set aside for at least 2 hours.
Dissolve the dried yeast in 80 ml of warm water, and in a separate pot heat 120 ml of milk with 60 g of butter and brown sugar until the fat melts.
Sift the plain flour with the salt into a bowl, make a well, and pour in the dissolved yeast, cooled milk with butter and sugar, and beaten egg.
Mix the ingredients and knead the dough on a floured board for at least 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Brush the dough with a little butter, place into a bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and set aside in a warm place for 60 minutes to rise.
Turn out the dough, knead for 1 minute, flatten into a disc, scatter the drained soaked dried fruits on top, and gently knead them into the dough.
Roll out the dough into an oval measuring 20 by 30 cm, transfer to a greased baking tin, and brush the top with the extra 20 g of butter.
Press a lengthwise indent along the centre with a rolling pin, shape 100 g of the prepared almond filling into a log, place it into the groove, and fold the dough over the filling.
Cover the shaped bread with a cloth and set aside in a warm place for another 60 minutes to rise.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 30–35 minutes until golden brown, and once cool, dust generously with icing sugar.

name: Zupa marchwiowa z curry (Carrot curry soup)
summary: A warming soup made with grated carrots and apple flavoured with ginger and curry powder, enriched with sour cream and egg yolk.
steps: Peel and chop the onions and garlic, and peel and grate the carrots and apple.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the onions, garlic, apple, carrots, and ginger, and fry everything together.
Dust the vegetables with the flour and curry powder, stir, and pour in the broth.
Cook the soup covered for about 10 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the egg yolk, pour into the soup, mix thoroughly, and bring briefly to a boil.
Season to taste with salt, and just before serving sprinkle with the chopped chives.

name: Snails with rosemary and potatoes
summary: In-shell snails blanched and braised in olive oil and white wine with potatoes, garlic, shallot, rosemary, and green peppercorns.
steps: Wash the snails in shells several times, and cut the peeled potatoes into thick chunks.
Drop the snails into salted boiling water for 1 minute, drain, and then fry briefly in heated olive oil over moderate heat.
Add the cut rosemary sprigs, garlic, green peppercorns, and salt, and gently sauté for 12 minutes.
Add the cut potatoes and chopped shallot, and pour in the white wine.
Simmer covered over low heat for about 20 minutes, adding a little water if needed so the snails remain in liquid.

name: Escargots de Bourgogne (Burgundy snails)
summary: A classic French appetizer of Burgundy snails baked in shells with garlic-herb butter, shallots, and parsley.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160 °C, remove the cooked snails from their shells, and drain thoroughly.
Finely chop the parsley, garlic, and shallots, then cream together with the softened butter, salt, and pepper into a smooth paste.
Place a small dab of herb butter into each shell, insert a snail inside, and fill the shell with butter, pressing lightly.
Arrange the stuffed shells on a flat baking dish and bake for 10–15 minutes at 160 °C.

name: Zupa zielona (Polish green herb and potato soup)
summary: Potato soup in vegetable broth with plenty of fresh greens (spring onions, parsley, chives, and dill), garnished with smoked bacon cracklings and finished with sour cream and lemon juice.
steps: Peel the potatoes, dice them, rinse, cover with hot vegetable broth, and cook for about 15 minutes.
Finely chop the spring onions, chives, and parsley, and cook gently covered in the plant-based butter.
Add the cooked greens to the simmering potatoes and cook everything together for about 10 minutes.
Dice the smoked bacon, render the fat in a frying pan, and add the bacon cracklings to the soup.
Thicken the soup with the flour whisked into the sour cream and the freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper, and sprinkle with fresh dill before serving.

name: Piernik (traditional Polish spiced gingerbread)
summary: A traditional old-Polish long-matured gingerbread made with buckwheat honey, wheat and rye flour, an aromatic spice blend, dried fruit and nuts, and spirit.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the batter and for caramel

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: or lard, or a half-and-half mixture

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 yolk reserved for brushing the top

steps: Dissolve the baking soda in the milk.
Add 4 tablespoons of sugar to a pan, caramelise, and dissolve with the brewed grain coffee.
In a wide saucepan, combine the remaining sugar with the caramel, add the butter and buckwheat honey, and heat gently over low heat, stirring and skimming any foam, without letting it boil.

Sift the wheat and rye flour into a large pot, add the mortar-crushed cloves, ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg, anise, lavender, pepper, coriander, allspice, and bay leaf (2–4 tablespoons of spices in total), along with the salt and cocoa powder, then mix thoroughly.
Remove the hot honey mixture from the heat, slowly pour in the spirit, add everything to the spiced flour, and stir thoroughly from the bottom.
Add the baking soda dissolved in milk, chopped walnuts, orange peel, and eggs (reserving one yolk for brushing), and knead the dough by hand on a pastry board.
Dust the kneaded dough with flour, cover with cloths, and set aside in a cool place for 3–4 weeks to mature.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C, roll out the matured dough thickly onto a rectangular baking sheet, brush the top with the reserved egg yolk, and bake for 25–35 minutes.

name: Cod in hazelnut sauce
summary: Baked cod fillets covered in a rich sauce of hazelnuts, grated semi-hard cheese, milk, and cherry liqueur.
steps: Finely chop the hazelnuts, combine them with the grated cheese, milk, and cherry liqueur, and season the sauce with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle the cod fillets with lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and set aside for a few minutes.
Arrange the fish in a baking dish, pour over the hazelnut sauce, sprinkle with breadcrumbs, and top with shavings of butter.
Place the dish into the preheated oven and bake for about 30 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Stuffed baked potatoes (Ziemniaki faszerowane)
summary: Vegetarian hollowed-out potatoes stuffed with braised grated root vegetables and onion, baked under a topping of kefir and firm cheese.
steps: Peel the potatoes and hollow out their centers.
Peel the carrots, parsley root, and celeriac and grate them on a coarse grater, then peel and finely chop the onion.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the prepared vegetables, season with salt and pepper, and cook gently covered until tender.
Fill the potatoes with the prepared stuffing and arrange them in a baking dish.
Mix the kefir with the grated firm cheese, pour over the potatoes, and bake in the oven.
Before serving hot, sprinkle the dish with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Saffron sauce (Sos szafranowy)
summary: A quick sauce for fish and puff pastry made with dry white wine, saffron, garlic and thick mayonnaise.
steps: Pour the white wine into a pot, bring to a boil, and add the saffron threads.
Stir the infusion, remove from the heat, and let stand for 3 minutes.
Add the ground black pepper and finely minced garlic.
Gradually add the mayonnaise, stirring continuously until a smooth sauce forms.

name: Spaghetti alla carbonara
summary: Spaghetti with fried smoked bacon in a sauce of sour cream, egg yolks, Parmesan and parsley.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water and drain, keeping it warm.
Dice the smoked bacon and fry it in a pan.
Warm the sour cream, combine it with the grated Parmesan, egg yolks and chopped parsley, and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Toss the warm pasta with the fried bacon and pour over the prepared sauce.

name: Cannelloni po florencku (Florentine cannelloni)
summary: Baked Italian cannelloni pasta tubes stuffed with minced poultry and garlic, served over a layer of braised tomatoes and celery stalks under béchamel sauce.
steps: Blanch the tomatoes, peel and chop them, then cut the celery stalks into strips.
Stew the tomatoes and celery in half the heated oil, seasoning with salt and dried oregano.
Fry the minced poultry in the remaining oil together with the crushed garlic paste.
Crack the egg into the slightly cooled meat, mix well, and season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Using a piping bag or cone, stuff the cannelloni pasta tubes with the prepared meat filling.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Spread a layer of braised vegetables over the bottom of a baking dish, arrange the stuffed cannelloni on top, and pour over the béchamel sauce.
Bake for 30 minutes at 200 °C, sprinkling the grated firm cheese over the top 10 minutes before the end.

name: Zupa z sera żółtego (Polish firm cheese soup)
summary: Creamy potato and firm cheese soup with leek in meat broth, seasoned with curry and nutmeg, served with fresh chives.
steps: Peel, wash, and dice the potatoes.
Pour 1 litre (4 glasses) of broth into a pot, add the potatoes, and cook for about 15 minutes.
Blend the cooked potatoes together with the broth, place the pot over low heat, and stir the sour cream into the soup.
Trim, rinse, and slice the leek, add it to the soup, and cook for 5 minutes.
Grate the firm cheese on a fine grater, add it to the pot, and heat until the cheese has melted completely.
Season the soup with salt, white pepper, curry powder, and nutmeg, and sprinkle with chopped chives just before serving.

name: Żur postny (Lenten sour rye soup)
summary: A meatless Lenten sour rye soup prepared with soup vegetables and dried mushrooms, flavoured with rye sour, potatoes, and garlic.

ingredients.name: celeriac
ingredients.note: small or a piece of root

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the vegetable and mushroom broth

steps: Trim, peel, and cut the carrots, parsley root, celeriac, and leek into pieces.
Pour one litre of water into a pot, add the prepared vegetables and dried mushrooms, and cook a broth.
Strain the broth, pour in the rye sour, and bring the soup to a boil.
Crush the garlic cloves and add them to the simmering soup.
Peel the potatoes, rinse, dice them, and add to the soup; cook until the potatoes are tender, then season with salt to taste.

name: Zupa piwna po staropolsku (Traditional Old Polish beer soup)
summary: Traditional Old Polish beer soup thickened with egg yolks whisked with sugar and sour cream, spiced with cloves and cinnamon, and served over diced farmer's cheese.
steps: Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy, then slowly pour in the sour cream, whisking continuously.
Place the pot with the egg and sour cream mixture over low heat and pour in the beer in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Season the soup with the cloves and a pinch of cinnamon, and heat over low heat until it begins to thicken.
Cut the farmer's cheese into small cubes, arrange several pieces in bowls, and ladle the warm beer soup over them.

name: Exquisite button mushroom soup (Wykwintna zupa pieczarkowa)
summary: Button mushroom soup in vegetable broth with broccoli florets, carrots, and noodles, finished with sour cream, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
steps: Rinse the mushrooms, cut them into thin slices, and fry in butter until golden.
Peel the carrot and onion, dice them, add to the mushrooms, and fry for a moment longer.
Cover the vegetables with vegetable broth, add the broccoli florets and a pinch of thyme, and simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately according to the package instructions and drain.
Stir the sour cream, nutmeg, lemon juice, salt, and pepper into the soup, add the cooked noodles, and heat through.

name: Fasolowa na ostro (spicy Polish beef and bean soup)
summary: A hearty and spicy beef and runner bean soup with tomatoes, seasoned with garlic, ginger, vinegar, and chili.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the beans and cooking the soup

steps: Cover the beans with part of the water and leave to soak overnight, then drain.
Cut the beef into cubes, sear in the heated olive oil, and remove from the pot.
In the remaining fat, cook the chopped onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the crushed canned tomatoes with their juices, season with chili, ginger, and wine vinegar, stir thoroughly, and bring to a boil.
Return the browned beef to the pot, add the water, cover, and simmer for about 30 minutes.
Add the drained beans and simmer the soup for another hour, until the beans and meat are tender.
Season the soup to taste with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with herbs before serving.

name: Zupa z kapusty pekińskiej (Napa cabbage soup)
summary: A light vegetable soup with shredded Napa cabbage, button mushrooms, and potatoes, finished with thick sour cream and marjoram.
steps: Peel and chop the onion, cook until translucent in heated oil in a pot, then pour in the broth.
Clean, wash, and shred the Napa cabbage, then add it to the pot.
Peel the potatoes and cut into cubes, and slice the cleaned button mushrooms thinly.
Add the potatoes and mushrooms to the soup, season with salt, pepper, and marjoram, and cook over low heat, taking care that the vegetables do not become overcooked.
Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the thick sour cream, and garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Pstrąg z boczkiem i migdałami (trout with pork belly and almonds)
summary: Foil-baked trout stuffed with garlic-almond butter and wrapped in slices of pork belly.

ingredients.name: flaked almonds
ingredients.note: 2/3 for the garlic butter, 1/3 for browning

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 100 g to beat with the almonds, 20 g to brown the flakes

steps: Peel and finely mince the garlic, then beat it with 100 g of butter and two-thirds of the flaked almonds, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Brown the remaining flaked almonds in a skillet with the remaining 20 g of butter.
Clean and wash the trout, pat dry, and spread the inside of each fish with the almond-garlic butter.
Wrap each fish in three slices of pork belly, wrap tightly in aluminium foil, and bake for about 8 minutes on each side.
Before serving, drizzle the trout with the butter and browned almonds and with lemon juice.

name: Ryba w sosie koperkowym (fish in dill sauce)
summary: Fish fillets braised in dry white wine with mushrooms and onion, served in a velvety sour cream and dill sauce.

ingredients.name: fish fillets
ingredients.note: any kind of fish, fresh or frozen

steps: Rinse and pat dry the fish fillets, drizzle with lemon juice, set aside for about 15 minutes to dry, and then sprinkle with salt.
Peel the onions and finely chop them; peel the mushrooms and slice them thinly.
Cook the onion and mushrooms gently, covered, in the melted butter, arrange the fish on top, and pour in the white wine.
Braise the fish until tender, then remove the fillets and keep them in a warm place.
Stir the sour cream into the braising liquid, bring the sauce to a boil, stir in the chopped dill, season with salt to taste, and pour over the fish.

name: Sole in sour cream and dill sauce
summary: Sole fillets drizzled with lemon juice, pan-seared, and simmered in a fresh dill sour cream sauce.
steps: Drizzle the sole fillets with lemon juice and set aside in a cool place for 10 minutes.
Heat a dry skillet without fat, place the fillets in it, and fry for about 4 minutes on each side.
Meanwhile, mix the sour cream with finely chopped dill and season generously with salt.
Pour the prepared sour cream and dill sauce over the fish and simmer gently for about 5 minutes more.

name: Łosoś w śmietanie (salmon baked in cream)
summary: Salmon fillets baked in cream with lemon juice and parsley leaves.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease an ovenproof dish with butter.
Place the salmon fillets in the dish, season them with salt and black pepper, and drizzle with lemon juice.
Pour 200 ml of cream over the fish and sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes at 180 °C and serve hot.

name: Ryba w sosie pieczarkowym (fish in mushroom sauce)
summary: Foil-baked fish fillets served hot with a delicate sour cream and mushroom sauce seasoned with sweet paprika.
steps: Arrange the fish fillets in an ovenproof baking dish, add a splash of water, season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with lemon juice.
Cover the dish with aluminum foil, place in an oven preheated to 200 °C, and bake for about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the thinly sliced mushrooms, pour in the sour cream, and season with sweet paprika, salt, and pepper.
Heat the sauce gently over low heat, taking care not to let it boil.
Transfer the hot fish to plates, spoon the mushroom sauce over the top, and sprinkle with parsley.

name: Karmazyn pieczony (baked redfish with leeks and tomatoes in beer sauce)
summary: Redfish fillets baked with leeks, shallots, and tomatoes in a beer and fish stock sauce.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Melt part of the butter in a saucepan, add the thinly sliced white parts of the leeks, cover, and cook gently for 2–3 minutes.
Add the chopped shallots, cover, and cook gently for another 3–4 minutes.
Pour in the lager beer and fish stock, season with salt and pepper, and simmer uncovered until reduced by about 1/3.
Arrange the redfish fillets in the saucepan, cover with sliced tomatoes, season, and bake in the oven for about 10 minutes.
Transfer the fish to plates, stir the remaining butter into the sauce, adjust seasoning to taste, and pour over the fillets.

name: Ryba z czosnkiem (baked fish with garlic)
summary: Fish fillets baked in a casserole dish with garlic, onions, tomatoes, white wine, and a golden breadcrumb topping.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and place a lightly oiled baking dish inside.
Sprinkle the bottom of the hot dish with parsley and 1 teaspoon of finely chopped onion, then heat for a few minutes.
Place the fish fillets in the dish, season with salt and pepper, and top with the pressed garlic and remaining chopped onion.
Arrange tomato slices over the fillets, drizzle with the white wine and remaining oil, and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake the fish in the oven at 180 °C for 20 minutes.

name: Ryba duszona z bakaliami (fish braised with dried fruit and nuts)
summary: Pan-fried sea fish fillets braised with tart apples, prunes, raisins, walnuts, and cloves.
steps: Cut the fish fillets into smaller portions, drizzle with lemon juice, and set aside for 30 minutes.
Drain the fish, season with salt and pepper, dredge in flour, fry in hot oil until golden, and transfer to a pot.
Add the scalded raisins, finely chopped apples and prunes, chopped onion, butter, and cloves to the fish.
Pour in a small amount of hot water and braise covered for about 15 minutes.
Towards the end of braising, stir in the chopped walnuts and mix gently.

name: Baked salmon on zucchini with mint salsa
summary: Salmon steaks baked in foil on zucchini rounds, served with fresh tomato-mint salsa.
steps: Mix the extra virgin olive oil with the wine vinegar and juice from half a lemon.
Peel the skin off the tomatoes, remove the seeds, dice the flesh finely, and combine with the dressing and finely chopped mint; season the salsa with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Slice the zucchini into rounds 0.5 cm thick, arrange 4 rounds on each of four sheets of aluminium foil, and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Salt the salmon steaks, sprinkle generously with coarsely ground black pepper, and arrange on the zucchini.
Place a portion of butter on each piece of fish, wrap the foil tightly, and bake for about 30 minutes at 180 °C. Serve with the salsa in separate small bowls.

name: Eggnog
summary: A traditional festive milk-and-egg cocktail with rum, cognac, whipped cream, and nutmeg.
steps: Separate the egg yolks from the whites.
Beat the egg yolks while slowly adding the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Stirring continuously, pour the rum and cognac into the yolks, then chill in a cool place for at least 3 hours.
Whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, and whip the 30% whipping cream in a separate bowl.
Pour the milk into a glass bowl and gently fold in the alcoholic egg mixture, whipped cream, and beaten egg whites.
Pour the drink into glasses, dust with grated nutmeg, and serve.

name: Staropolska zupa cebulowa (Old Polish onion soup)
summary: A traditional Polish soup of gently cooked onions and browned wholemeal bread, passed through a sieve and enriched with egg yolks and sour cream.
steps: Dice the crustless wholemeal bread, arrange it in an ovenproof dish with half the butter, and bake until browned and dried.
Peel and chop the onions, then cook them gently, covered, in the remaining butter.
Add the browned wholemeal bread to the onions, pour in 1.5 litres of boiled water, and simmer gently for about 30 minutes.
Pass the soup through a sieve, bring it back to a boil, stir in the egg yolks mixed with sour cream, and season to taste with salt.

name: Kotlety schabowe z ananasem (pork cutlets with pineapple and cheese)
summary: Breaded pork loin cutlets topped with honey-braised pineapple, red bell pepper, onion, and melted firm cheese.
steps: Wash and dry the pork loin, cut into slices, and pound lightly with a meat mallet.
Season the meat with salt, pepper, and meat seasoning, coat in the beaten egg and breadcrumbs, and fry in heated olive oil until golden.
In a second frying pan, heat olive oil and sauté the diced pineapple, chopped red bell pepper, and chopped onion until softened.
Pour a splash of the pineapple syrup from the can into the pan, add the honey, and braise everything for 5 minutes.
Top the fried pork cutlets with the braised pineapple, bell pepper, and onion mixture and the sliced firm cheese, then warm covered for a moment until the cheese melts.

name: Cannelloni ze szpinakiem (spinach cannelloni)
summary: Italian cannelloni pasta stuffed with spinach, feta cheese, and parmesan, baked under a creamy layer of béchamel sauce.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic, then sauté in butter together with the thawed spinach until the water evaporates, and let cool.
Mix the spinach with the egg yolk, crumbled feta cheese, and half of the parmesan, then season to taste with salt, black pepper, and nutmeg.
Stuff the cannelloni tubes with the prepared filling, pour half the béchamel sauce into a baking dish, and arrange the tubes on top.
Sprinkle the pasta with the remaining parmesan and pour over the rest of the béchamel sauce.
Bake for 30 minutes in an oven preheated to 210 °C, and sprinkle with basil leaves before serving.

name: Jajka w mięsie (Scotch eggs with sweetcorn and parmesan)
summary: Hard-boiled eggs baked in a mixture of minced meat, sweetcorn, and parmesan, and deep-fried.
steps: Hard-boil 4 eggs, let them cool, and peel them.
Combine the minced meat with the remaining raw egg, canned sweetcorn, grated onion, grated parmesan, and the stale roll soaked and squeezed dry.
Season the meat mixture with herbs, salt, pepper, and minced garlic, knead until smooth, divide into 4 portions, and flatten into thin patties.
Place a peeled hard-boiled egg in the center of each patty and wrap the meat around the egg to form smooth balls.
Fry the meat-wrapped eggs in deep hot oil for about 15 minutes.
Remove the fried meat eggs, drain on paper towels, and cut into portions.

name: Sweet roasted pork loin (Schab na słodko)
summary: Roast pork loin marinated in honey, garlic, and rosemary, then braised in apple juice with raisins.
steps: Peel and crush the garlic through a press, then mix with the rosemary, honey, oil, salt, and pepper.
Coat the pork loin thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C, transfer the meat to a heatproof roasting dish, and bake for about 15 minutes until it begins to brown.
Pour the apple juice into the dish, cover with a lid, reduce the oven temperature to 160 °C, and roast for about 60 minutes.
Stir the raisins into the pan sauce a few minutes before the end of roasting.

name: Czulent (traditional Jewish Sabbath stew)
summary: A traditional Ashkenazi Jewish Sabbath stew made with goose legs, large white beans, pearl barley, and root vegetables, slow-baked for a full 24 hours.

ingredients.name: goose legs with fat
ingredients.note: or half a goose with fat

steps: Soak the large white beans in cold water the day before preparing the stew.
Peel the onions, potatoes, carrots, and garlic and cut into large chunks, and divide the goose legs with fat into portions.
Place the meat, drained beans, pearl barley, vegetables, bay leaves, and allspice berries into a roasting pan, and season with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Pour in water to about 2 cm above the ingredients and cover the pan tightly.
Place the roasting pan in an oven preheated to 100 °C (reduce temperature to 80 °C if needed) and bake for 1440 minutes.

name: Bacon-stuffed pasta nests
summary: Baked thin vermicelli noodle nests filled with sautéed bacon and onion, topped with tomato slices and chives.
steps: Cook the vermicelli noodles until tender and drain.
Finely dice the bacon and onion, fry in 1 tablespoon of oil, and season with salt and thyme.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a baking tray with 1 tablespoon of oil.
Shape the cooked noodles into nests, arrange them on the baking sheet, and fill the center of each nest with the bacon and onion mixture.
Drizzle the nests with the remaining oil, place a tomato slice on each, and sprinkle lightly with salt.
Bake in the oven for 10 minutes, and sprinkle with chopped chives before serving.

name: Lasagne bolognese
summary: Italian pasta bake with meat sauce, button mushrooms, béchamel, and firm cheese.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Peel the garlic, mince it finely or press it through a garlic press, and fry in 2 tablespoons of oil or olive oil.
Add the minced meat and fry for 10–15 minutes until the fat renders, breaking up any lumps.
Add the tomato paste or canned tomatoes and simmer for about 5 minutes, then season with salt, oregano, thyme, and basil.
Clean the button mushrooms, slice them, and leave them raw or fry them in the remaining fat.
Layer the meat sauce, mushrooms, lasagne pasta sheets, 500 ml of béchamel sauce, and part of the grated firm cheese in an ovenproof dish.
Sprinkle the top with the remaining firm cheese and herbs, arrange the tomato halves, and bake for 30 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Snikers (Polish honey walnut and caramel layer cake)
summary: A three-layer honey cake filled with coffee custard cream and dulce de leche, topped with a baked honey-walnut glaze.

ingredients.name: baking margarine
ingredients.note: plus a little for greasing the pans

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: reduced by one third compared to the package instructions

steps: Sift the flour with the baking soda onto a pastry board, chop in 200 g of margarine, then add 150 g of sugar, eggs, egg yolks, 3 tablespoons of milk, 3 tablespoons of honey, and vanilla sugar, knead into a smooth dough, and divide into three equal parts.
Line three greased and parchment-lined 20 × 30 cm rectangular baking pans with the rolled-out dough.

Heat 125 g of margarine in a saucepan with 4 tablespoons of sugar, 2 tablespoons of honey, and chopped walnuts, pour the hot topping over one of the dough layers, and bake all three layers in the oven (about 15–20 minutes at 180 °C), then cool.
Cook the custard in one-third less milk than directed on the packet, let cool, and then beat with the margarine and 2 teaspoons of dissolved coffee.
Place the unopened can of condensed milk in a pot of water, boil for 180 minutes to make thick dulce de leche, and cool.
Spread the custard cream over the first baked cake layer, cover with the second layer spread with caramel, and top with the third layer finished with the walnut topping.

name: Chili con carne (Mexican beef and bean chili)
summary: A hearty Mexican spiced stew of minced beef, red kidney beans, tomatoes, bell peppers, and sweetcorn simmered with chili peppers and cayenne.
steps: Dice the red bell pepper and onion, and finely chop the red chili peppers and garlic.
Brown the minced beef in heated olive oil together with the onion and garlic.
Add the chili peppers, red bell pepper, tomato purée, and cayenne pepper, and braise briefly.
Pour in the broth, add the bay leaves and canned tomatoes with their juice, and simmer covered for 15–20 minutes.
Stir in the canned red kidney beans and canned sweetcorn, and cook for another 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season to taste with salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper, then garnish with fresh basil before serving.

name: Zupa kremowa z kukurydzy (Cream of corn soup)
summary: A thick puréed soup made with canned corn, potatoes, and sour cream, served with whole corn kernels, spring onion, and paprika olive oil.
steps: Mix the ground sweet paprika with the olive oil and set aside.
Peel, rinse, and finely dice the potatoes, place in a pot, add half of the sweetcorn, vegetable broth, and sour cream, season with salt and pepper, and cook covered for 15 minutes.
Peel the spring onions and slice into thin rings.
Let the soup cool slightly and blend until smooth, then add the sliced spring onion bulbs and the remaining sweetcorn.
Stir everything together and cook for about 3 minutes more.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, and drizzle with the paprika oil before serving.

name: Benedictine soup (Zupa benedyktyńska)
summary: A vegetarian soup made with porcini mushrooms, sautéed onions, and potatoes in vegetable broth, served with a poached egg.
steps: Thaw the porcini mushrooms, rinse them, and dice them.
Peel the onions, slice into feathers, and fry in butter until golden, then add the mushrooms and continue frying.
Transfer the mushrooms and onions to the broth, add the peeled and finely diced potatoes, season with soup seasoning, and cook until the potatoes are tender.
Crack the eggs into boiling water with vinegar in a separate pot so that they gently set.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve each portion with a poached egg.

name: Ryba w sosie wiosennym (fish in spring yogurt sauce)
summary: Quick cod fillets cooked in the microwave and served in a refreshing plain yogurt sauce with cucumber, green grapes, and a hint of mint.
steps: Arrange the cod fillets in a shallow microwave-safe dish, sprinkle with lemon juice, and cook in the microwave for about 5 minutes.
Peel the small cucumber, scoop out the seeds, and finely dice the flesh.
Cut the grapes in half, remove the seeds, and set aside a few halves for garnish.
Stir the thick plain yogurt with the mint syrup, diced cucumber, and remaining grapes, then season the sauce with salt and pepper.
Spoon the sauce over the fish and heat in the microwave for another 3 minutes.
Garnish the dish with cucumber slices and the reserved grape halves, then serve.

name: Herb-marinated herring
summary: Herring fillet pieces marinated in oil with onions, marjoram, oregano, allspice, and a touch of sugar.
steps: Mix the sugar, marjoram, oregano, and ground allspice with the vegetable oil to create a herb marinade.
Cut the onions into quarters, slice into thin strips, combine with the marinade, and set aside for about 15 minutes for the flavours to meld.
Cut the herring fillets into bite-sized pieces, add to the onion in marinade, mix well, and chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes before serving.

name: Pork loin stuffed with dried fruit (Schab nadziewany suszonymi owocami)
summary: Roast pork loin stuffed with dried apricots and prunes soaked in dry red wine.
steps: Wash and pat the pork loin dry, rub it with salt, pepper, marjoram, and crushed garlic, then cover and refrigerate for about 60 minutes.
Pour the red wine over the dried apricots and prunes and set aside to soak.
Cut a deep pocket lengthwise along the grain of the meat and stuff it with the soaked fruit.
Sear the pork loin in hot melted butter on all sides until golden brown.
Transfer the meat to a roasting pan, pour over the pan fat, remaining wine, and a few tablespoons of water, and cover with a lid.
Roast for 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C, basting the meat frequently with the pan juices.

name: Herb-roasted pork loin (Schab pieczony w ziołach)
summary: Juicy pork loin roasted in an aromatic crust of chopped shallots, celery, parsley, oregano, and thyme.
steps: Rinse and pat the pork loin dry, trimming away any silver skin.
Peel the shallots, wash and pat dry the parsley leaves and celery stalks, then finely chop everything.
Mix the chopped vegetables with the oregano, thyme, and coarsely ground black pepper.
Rub the pork with olive oil, coat it evenly on all sides in the herb-vegetable mixture, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Place the roast in a heatproof dish, put it in an oven preheated to 240 °C, and bake for 15 minutes.
Reduce the oven temperature to 180 °C and bake for another 30 minutes.
Remove the roasted pork loin from the oven, season with salt, cover with a cloth for 10 minutes, and carve into thick slices.

name: Cornflake-crusted chicken cutlets (Pierś z kurczaka inaczej)
summary: Tender chicken breast cutlets coated in egg white and crunchy crushed cornflakes, pan-fried until crisp and golden.
steps: Slice each chicken breast fillet lengthwise into 2 thinner cutlets and season with salt, pepper, poultry seasoning, and sweet paprika.
Finely crush the cornflakes, and lightly beat the egg whites in a shallow bowl.
Dredge the chicken pieces sequentially in wheat flour, beaten egg white, and crushed cornflakes.
Fry the cutlets in hot vegetable oil on both sides until golden, and garnish with sprigs of parsley leaves and dill before serving.

name: Roast chicken legs with potatoes and garlic (Udka z kurczaka z ziemniakami)
summary: Sheet-pan roasted chicken legs brushed with mayonnaise, served with potato wedges and garlic roasted in its skins.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease a baking sheet with oil.
Sprinkle the chicken legs with poultry seasoning and all-purpose seasoning, then arrange them on the baking sheet.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into quarters, and arrange them around the chicken legs along with the unpeeled cloves from the two heads of garlic.
Brush the chicken legs with mayonnaise, sprinkle everything again with seasonings and herbs, and roast for about 50 minutes until the meat is browned and the potatoes are tender and golden.

name: Chinese-style chicken fillets with mushrooms and walnuts
summary: Chicken breast strips marinated in soy sauce and braised with button mushrooms, celery, walnuts, and sesame seeds.
steps: Slice the chicken fillets crosswise into thin strips and marinate in the soy sauce.
Thinly slice the mushrooms and celery stalks, and finely chop the onion and garlic.
Cook the onion and garlic in part of the heated oil until translucent.
Add the chicken strips drained from the marinade, fry for 2 minutes, and transfer the meat to a plate.
In the remaining oil, sauté the mushrooms and celery, pour in the leftover soy sauce marinade, and simmer for a few minutes.
Return the meat to the pan, add the dried basil and chopped walnuts, stir well, and garnish with sesame seeds before serving.

name: Kotlety mielone z farszem z ziół (herb-butter stuffed beef patties)
summary: Juicy minced beef patties stuffed with frozen herb butter made of parsley, chives, and thyme.
steps: Cream the butter with finely chopped parsley, chives, thyme, and minced garlic.
Transfer the herb butter to a piping bag, pipe out 6 equal portions, and place them in the freezer to set.
Soak the stale roll, squeeze dry, and combine with the minced beef, chopped onion, plain yogurt, mustard, and eggs.
Season the meat mixture with salt and pepper, knead thoroughly, and divide into 6 portions.
Place a frozen herb butter portion into the centre of each meat portion, shape into tightly sealed patties, and fry in hot oil on both sides.

name: Braised veal with prunes
summary: Veal leg barded with fatback strips and braised in dry white wine and broth with onion and dried prunes.
steps: Cut the fatback into strips, bard the veal leg with them, and tie the meat securely with kitchen twine.
Brown the meat on all sides in heated butter, then transfer it to a roasting pan.
Peel and slice the onion, arrange it around the meat, then pour in the broth and dry white wine, and season with salt and pepper.
Braise covered over low heat for about 120 minutes, adding the prunes to the pan halfway through the cooking time.
Let the meat cool slightly, cut into slices, surround with the braised onion and prunes, and spoon over the pan juices.

name: Lemon rice soup (Zupa cytrynowa z ryżem)
summary: A light and quick poultry broth soup with rice, finished with lemon juice blended with yogurt, and sprinkled with fresh dill.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and drain.
Cut the lemon in half and squeeze out the juice.
Bring the water to a boil, stir in the broth powder, and cook for several minutes, then add the drained rice.
Mix the yogurt (or sour cream) with lemon juice, pour into the soup, and season with salt if needed.
Sprinkle the soup with chopped dill before serving.

name: Ryba duszona z warzywami (fish braised with vegetables)
summary: Pan-fried fish warmed in grated root vegetables braised in butter and oil with onion and tomato paste.
steps: Clean and peel the carrots and parsley root, then grate them on a coarse grater.
Melt the butter in a skillet and lightly sauté the grated root vegetables.
Peel the onions, chop them finely, and cook in hot oil until translucent.
Combine the onion with the sautéed carrot and parsley root, add a little boiling water, cover, and braise until tender.
Stir in the tomato paste, season the sauce with salt and pepper, add the fried fish pieces, and heat through.
Divide the dish among plates and garnish with lemon slices.

name: Napa cabbage salad with firm cheese (Sałatka z kapusty pekińskiej)
summary: A crisp salad of napa cabbage, chicory, leek, bell pepper, cucumber, and firm cheese with a garlic and basil vinaigrette.
steps: Press the garlic through a garlic press and whisk together with the oil, wine vinegar, basil, a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper.
Wash the vegetables, remove the core from the chicory, then finely shred the napa cabbage, chicory, and leek, and sprinkle with lemon juice.
Slice the cucumber into rounds, and cut the red bell pepper and firm cheese into dice.
Combine all the ingredients in a salad bowl, pour over the dressing, and scatter the chopped parsley leaves over the top.

name: Kalmary w winie (calamari braised in red wine and cognac)
summary: Squid braised in red wine with onions, tomato purée, yogurt, cinnamon, and cognac.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: approx. 0.5 tbsp for boiling and to taste

steps: Thoroughly remove the membranes from the squid, wash the squid, cover with one litre of cold salted water in a saucepan, and cook covered for 4–5 minutes from the time it comes to a boil.
Drain the squid, slice into rings, and sauté in a skillet with melted butter.
Add the finely diced, briefly parboiled onions, tomato purée, bay leaves, salt, and pepper, and stir thoroughly.
Pour in the red wine and cook over low heat for 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the plain yogurt, sprinkle with ground cinnamon, bring to a boil, cover, and braise for 5–7 minutes.
Before serving, stir in the cognac, mix well, and transfer the dish to a platter.

name: Shrimp omelette
summary: Egg omelette filled with prawns, mushrooms, onion, bean sprouts, and soy sauce, pan-fried on both sides.
steps: Drain the prawns. Whisk the eggs with 2 tablespoons of cold water and a pinch of salt, then stir in the prawns.
Wash, peel, and finely chop the mushrooms and onion, then sauté them in a frying pan in heated oil and reduce the heat.
Combine the egg and prawn mixture with the bean sprouts and soy sauce, season with salt and hot paprika, and mix vigorously.
Pour the mixture into the pan over the mushrooms and onion. Once the underside is golden brown, carefully flip the omelette over and fry for a few minutes more.

name: Pstrąg w folii (foil-baked trout)
summary: Trout marinated in melted butter with lemon juice, garlic, and parsley leaves, baked in foil packets.
steps: Mix the melted butter with the freshly squeezed lemon juice, pressed garlic, chopped parsley leaves, salt, and pepper.
Immerse the cleaned trout in the prepared butter mixture and let marinate for about 60 minutes, turning them several times.
Wrap each fish tightly along with its marinade in aluminium foil.
Bake the trout in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 20 minutes.

name: Sole with spinach and béchamel
summary: Sole fillet baked under a layer of gently cooked spinach mixed with garlic, béchamel sauce, and grated firm cheese.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.note: alternatively use half this weight of frozen spinach

steps: Make a white roux with butter and flour and set a small portion aside. Whisk the milk into the remaining roux, bring to a boil, and season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg to make a béchamel sauce.
Cook the spinach gently, covered, then mix it with the finely chopped garlic and the reserved roux.
Place the sole fillet drizzled with lemon juice and sprinkled with salt in a baking dish, spread the spinach over it, pour on the béchamel sauce, and sprinkle with grated firm cheese.
Bake in a preheated oven (about 180 °C) for 20–30 minutes.

name: Avgolemono (Greek lemon chicken soup with rice)
summary: A Greek chicken or turkey broth with rice, thickened with egg yolks beaten with fresh lemon juice.
steps: Skim the fat from the cold broth, strain it, bring to a boil in a pot, and season with salt.
Add the uncooked rice to the boiling broth and cook for 20 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with the freshly squeezed lemon juice, then gradually whisk in a little hot broth to temper the mixture.
Pour the tempered egg-lemon mixture into the soup pot and heat thoroughly over low heat while stirring constantly, without letting it boil.

name: Easter walnut and chocolate bundt cake (Wielkanocna babka z orzechami i czekoladą)
summary: A fluffy, tender bundt cake folded with chopped walnuts and dark chocolate pieces, dusted with icing sugar.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the tin

steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C, and grease a bundt cake tin with butter and dust it with breadcrumbs.
Beat the eggs with the butter, sugar, and a pinch of salt, then add the plain flour, baking powder, and milk, mixing until smooth and combined.
Add the chopped walnuts and finely chopped chocolate, then gently fold into the batter with a spoon.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake for about 60 minutes.
Remove the baked bundt cake from the tin, let cool, and dust with icing sugar before serving.

name: Pork loin roasted in fresh herbs and pork belly (Schab pieczony w świeżych ziołach)
summary: Tender pork loin seasoned with fresh thyme, mint, and rosemary, wrapped in pork belly, and roasted with butter and white wine.

ingredients.name: fresh pork belly strips
ingredients.note: wide, for wrapping around the roast

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: half at the start, half after 30 minutes of roasting

steps: Rub the pork loin with sea salt, coarsely ground pepper, and part of the torn fresh herbs, then press the remaining herbs all over the outside of the meat.
Wrap the pork loin in strips of fresh pork belly, tie securely with kitchen twine, and place in a roasting pan.
Cut the butter into strips and arrange on top of the meat, drizzle everything with olive oil, and pour half of the white wine into the bottom of the roasting pan.
Place the roasting pan in an oven preheated to 200 °C, baste the meat with the remaining wine after 30 minutes, and continue roasting for another 60–90 minutes.
Remove the roasted pork loin from the oven, cover loosely with aluminium foil, and let rest for 30 minutes before carving.

name: Ryba z ryżem i warzywami (fish patties with rice and vegetables)
summary: Golden pan-fried minced fish patties with broccoli and carrots, breaded and served with fluffy boiled rice.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: half for the mixture, half for breading

steps: Boil the carrot and broccoli florets until tender-crisp, let them cool, and chop very finely.
Peel the onion, chop finely, and sauté in a little heated oil until translucent.
Rinse and pat dry the fish fillets, then finely mince them.
Combine the minced fish with the vegetables, onion, half of the breadcrumbs, and one egg, season with salt and pepper, and mix thoroughly.
Shape the mixture into small, flat patties, dredge in flour, dip into the second beaten egg, coat in the remaining breadcrumbs, and fry in oil until golden brown.
Cook the rice until fluffy and serve with the hot fish patties.

name: Pejzanka (Polish rustic cabbage, bean, and sausage soup)
summary: Hearty Polish rustic soup made with pork rib broth, Polish sausage, cabbage, white beans, potatoes and soup vegetables, enriched with tomato purée.
steps: Soak the white beans in water, then cook until tender in a separate pot.
Cover the pork ribs with water, simmer to make a meat broth, and strain it.
Clean and chop the soup greens, shred the cabbage, and braise the vegetables together covered.
Peel the potatoes, dice them, and cook in the strained rib broth, then add the braised vegetables and cooked beans.
Slice the kiełbasa, dice the onion, sauté both in hot vegetable oil, and add to the soup pot.
Add the tomato purée, allspice berries, pressed garlic clove, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, and serve sprinkled with parsley leaves.

name: Beef Stroganoff
summary: A classic dish of tender beef tenderloin strips simmered with mushrooms, onion, and fermented pickles in a rich tomato and sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: 150 ml (adjusted from 1 tsp for 500 g beef)

steps: Rinse and pat dry the beef tenderloin, slice into long thin strips, fry until browned, then transfer to a saucepan and pour in the beef broth.
Peel the onion and mushrooms, slice them along with the fermented pickle, add to the meat, and braise covered over low heat for about 30 minutes.
Stir the wheat flour into a little water, pour into the saucepan with the tomato paste, and bring to a boil.
Stir in the sour cream and season the dish with salt, coarsely ground black pepper, and a pinch of hot paprika powder.

name: Kotlety de volaille (Chicken Kyiv)
summary: Breaded chicken breast cutlets rolled around chilled butter, fresh parsley, and lemon juice.
steps: Wash and dry the chicken fillets, butterfly each lengthwise, and pound gently with a mallet on a board.
Season the meat with salt, pepper, and poultry seasoning, drizzle with the juice squeezed from half a lemon, and scatter with the chopped parsley.
Cut the chilled butter into 4 batons, place one on each piece of meat, and roll up tightly.
Coat the rolled cutlets successively in plain flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Heat the fat and fry the cutlets over high heat for about 3 minutes per side until golden brown, then finish cooking over low heat.

name: Kluski biołe (kluski śląskie) (white Silesian dumplings)
summary: Classic white Silesian dumplings prepared by dividing boiled potatoes in a four-to-one proportion with potato starch.

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: in a volume equal to one-quarter of the mashed potatoes

steps: Pass the cooked potatoes through a ricer into a bowl and level their surface with your hand.
Remove one-quarter of the potato mixture from the bowl, and fill the resulting hollow with potato starch.
Return the removed potatoes to the bowl, crack in the egg, add a pinch of salt, and knead by hand into a smooth, uniform dough.
Shape the dough into small, slightly flattened balls.
Drop the dumplings into boiling water, and once they float to the surface, lower the heat and cook for another 5–10 minutes.

name: Pieczona biała kiełbasa (baked Polish white sausage with onions)
