Brush the bread slices with the remaining oil, toast in the oven until golden, and once cooled, spread with the salmon mixture and garnish with dill and lemon slices.

name: Mashed potato and vegetable bake (Zapiekanka z warzywami)
summary: A vegetarian casserole of creamy mashed potatoes with egg yolks and cream, layered with braised broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, celeriac, and olives.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon for mash, 1 tablespoon for greasing the dish

steps: Mash the boiled potatoes and beat into a smooth purée with half the butter, cream, egg yolks, salt, and nutmeg.
Divide the broccoli and cauliflower into florets, slice the carrots and celeriac, then cook gently covered in hot oil and season with salt.
Grease an ovenproof baking dish with the remaining butter, spread half of the mashed potatoes on the bottom, arrange the braised vegetables with olives over it, and cover with the remaining mash.
Bake for 30 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Almond-stuffed dried figs in citrus syrup
summary: Dried figs filled with milk-poached almonds and gently simmered in a fragrant orange and lemon syrup.
steps: Wash and dry the dried figs, then make a hollow pocket inside each fruit.
Chop the almonds, simmer them briefly in the milk, drain, and stuff them into the fig cavities.
Dissolve the sugar in the water, stir in the orange juice and lemon juice, and mix well.
Place the stuffed figs into the citrus syrup and simmer over gentle heat until tender.
Serve warm or thoroughly chilled.

name: Hungarian-style cucumber salad (mizeria po węgiersku)
summary: Light Hungarian cucumber and onion salad in a mild vinegar dressing, dusted with sweet paprika.
steps: Wash and dry the cucumbers, then slice them thinly.
Peel the onion, slice into rings, combine with the cucumbers, sprinkle lightly with salt, and let stand for 60 minutes.
Dilute the wine vinegar with a little water, stir into the accumulated cucumber juices, and season with salt and pepper.
Chill the salad in the refrigerator, and dust with sweet ground paprika before serving.

name: Pomegranate and orange salad (Sałatka z granatem)
summary: A refreshing salad of orange slices and ripe pomegranate seeds drizzled with olive oil and sprinkled with herbs and a pinch of salt.
steps: Cut the pomegranate in half, squeeze the juice into a bowl, and pick out all the seeds from inside.
Peel the oranges and slice the flesh into rounds.
Arrange the orange slices in a shallow salad dish, scatter the pomegranate seeds on top, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with salt and herbs.

name: Migdałowy pischinger (almond chocolate wafer cake)
summary: Layered wafer cake filled with chocolate custard buttercream and coated with crunchy almond brittle.
steps: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a saucepan, add 150 g of sugar, simmer for about 10 minutes while stirring, then add the chopped almonds.
Spread the hot almond mixture over aluminium foil greased with vegetable oil, let cool, place between two sheets of baking paper, and crush with a rolling pin.
Mix 2 tablespoons of milk with the vanilla pudding powder, pour into the remaining milk brought to a boil with 80 g of sugar, cook briefly until thickened, and let cool.
Melt the dark chocolate in a water bath and let it cool slightly.
Beat 200 g of butter with the powdered sugar, add a spoonful at a time to the cooled pudding, and finally stir in the melted chocolate.
Set aside one-third of the cream, and use the rest to sandwich the wafer sheets, stacking them on top of each other.

Spread half of the reserved cream over the top and sides of the torte, coat with the crushed almond brittle, and pipe rosettes along the border with the remaining cream, decorating with chocolate leaves.

name: Legumina czekoladowa (chilled chocolate pudding)
summary: Chilled chocolate and egg mousse dessert with hints of strong coffee, orange, and cognac.
steps: Grate 100 g of dark chocolate into curls and set aside. Break the remaining 150 g of chocolate into pieces, melt over a water bath, and combine with the strong coffee, orange juice, and finely grated orange zest.
Whisk the eggs with sugar over a water bath for about 10 minutes, then set aside to cool.
Soak the gelatin in a small amount of lukewarm water to bloom, then fold it together with 200 ml of whipped cream into the chocolate mixture.
Fold the chocolate mixture into the cooled egg mixture and season with 50 ml of cognac.
Collar a soufflé dish with a strip of baking parchment extending above the rim, pour in the mixture, and refrigerate for 3 hours.
Before serving, remove the parchment collar and dust the top with the reserved chocolate curls mixed with powdered sugar.

name: Parówki nadziewane serem (cheese-stuffed bacon-wrapped frankfurters)
summary: Baked frankfurters brushed with mustard, stuffed with semi-hard cheese, and wrapped in thin slices of smoked bacon.
steps: Warm the frankfurters slightly, slit each lengthwise down the centre, and spread with mustard.
Cut the cheese into strips, tuck them into the slits, wrap each frankfurter with a slice of bacon, and secure with a toothpick.
Arrange the frankfurters on a baking tray, drizzle with melted butter, and bake for 10 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C, until the cheese melts and the bacon browns.

name: Indian-style baked chicken and lamb with peppers
summary: Pieces of chicken and lamb marinated in spiced yogurt, baked and served with sautéed onions and bell peppers.
steps: Cut the chicken breast fillet and lamb into small pieces, season with salt, black pepper, cinnamon, caraway, coriander, cloves, and nutmeg, and immerse in the plain yogurt for 10 minutes.
Remove the meat from the marinade and bake for 45 minutes in an oven preheated to 190 °C.
Peel the onions, cut into quarters, fry in heated vegetable oil, and remove from the pan.
Seed the green, red, and yellow bell pepper halves, cut into smaller pieces, and fry in the same pan.
Remove the baked meat from the oven and arrange the sautéed onions and bell peppers around it.

name: Karp w pieczarkach (pan-fried carp baked with mushrooms and cream)
summary: Fried carp steaks baked with sautéed mushrooms and onions in rich sour cream.
steps: Cut the carp fillets into portions, rub with salt and pepper, and set aside briefly in a cool place.
Dredge the fish pieces in wheat flour, fry in hot oil, and transfer to a baking dish.
Peel and slice the mushrooms and onions, sauté in a pan, and spread over the fish.
Pour over the sour cream and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 10 minutes until the fish absorbs the cream.

name: Babka z rodzynkami (Polish yeast babka with raisins)
summary: A traditional Polish Easter yeast bundt cake enriched with ten egg yolks, two types of raisins, chopped almonds, and vanilla.

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: clarified, plus a little for the tin

steps: Mix the fresh yeast with warm milk, a little sugar, and flour, allow to froth, then combine with the remaining wheat flour, egg yolks beaten with sugar, salt, and seeds scraped from the vanilla bean half.
Pour in the clarified butter and knead the yeast dough until smooth and elastic.
Scald both types of raisins with boiling water, pat dry, add to the dough along with the chopped almonds, and knead for another 30 minutes, then cover with a towel and let rise.
Transfer the risen dough into a buttered babka tin and let rise in a warm spot until it fills the tin.
Bake the tin in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Makagigi (poppy seed and walnut brittle)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve treat made from poppy seeds, walnuts, honey, and sugar.
steps: Bring 250 ml of honey to a boil in a pot with 125 ml of sugar and 250 ml of dry poppy seeds.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until lightly browned.
Stir in 125 ml of chopped walnuts, add the almond extract, and mix thoroughly.
Turn the hot mixture onto an oiled baking sheet, allow to set, and then slice with a sharp knife into squares or diamonds.

name: Jajka w sosie szczypiorkowym (hard-boiled eggs in chive cream sauce)
summary: Hard-boiled eggs served with a chilled sauce of sour cream, egg yolk, mustard, and fresh chives.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs, let them cool, peel, slice lengthwise in half, and arrange on a platter.
Whisk the egg yolk with mustard and a pinch of sugar until smooth, gradually beating in the sour cream in small portions.
Fold in the chopped chives, season to taste with salt, sugar, and lemon juice, and pour over the eggs.

name: Rice and lentil veggie burger
summary: Hearty vegetarian burgers featuring crispy breaded patties of rice, lentils, bell pepper, and cheese in toasted sesame buns.
steps: Cook the rice and lentils in salted water until tender, then drain.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a pan and saute the finely chopped bell pepper for 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat, combine the pepper with the cooked rice, lentils, and grated cheese, and season with salt and black pepper.
Shape the mixture into a round disk about 20 cm in diameter on a moistened plate, chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours, then cut into 4 patties.
Dredge each patty in flour, dip in beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs, and fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes per side.
Halve and toast the sesame buns, spread with mayonnaise, assemble with the patties, onion slices, shredded lettuce, and cucumber, and cover with the top buns.

name: Zupa zbójecka (bandit's mushroom and sausage soup)
summary: A substantial mushroom and meat soup with porcini, smoked bacon, and Polish kiełbasa, seasoned with sweet paprika and thyme, and finished with sour cream.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: for dusting and thickening the soup

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the soup and blending the sour cream

steps: Dice the smoked bacon and fry in the fat.
Add the finely chopped onion and sliced porcini. Season with salt, black pepper, thyme, the bay leaf, and one tablespoon of sweet paprika, then cook gently, covered, for a dozen or so minutes.
Pour in the water, add about two tablespoons of vegetable seasoning, and bring to a boil. Dust the soup with one tablespoon of flour and mix thoroughly.
Slice the kiełbasa, add it to the pot, and cook for another few minutes.
Finish the soup with the sour cream whisked with the remaining flour and a little water, bring briefly to a boil, and garnish with chopped chives before serving.

name: Pickled Camembert cheese (nakládaný hermelín)
summary: Czech appetizer of Camembert or Hermelín cheese rounds marinated in oil with garlic, herbs, juniper berries, and hot peppers.
steps: Peel the garlic cloves and slice them thinly.
Cut the cheese rounds horizontally in half and coat the inside with the garlic slices, sweet ground paprika, thyme, and rosemary.
Place the filled cheese rounds into a jar, add the juniper berries, bay leaves, and halved hot chili peppers.
Pour vegetable oil into the jar until the cheese is completely submerged, seal, and let stand for several days.

name: Barszcz lwowski (Lviv-style borscht with beef and crab apples)
summary: An exquisite Lviv beetroot soup in rich beef broth, flavoured with roasted beets, lemon slices, crab apple preserves, and sour cream.
steps: Cover the beef and soup greens with water, add the onion studded with a clove, bay leaf, allspice, and peppercorns, simmer into a rich broth, and strain.
Scrub the beetroots, roast them in the oven until tender, peel, and either coarsely grate or slice into matchsticks.
Peel the lemons, slice them thinly, and discard any seeds.
Place the beetroots, lemon slices, and crab apple preserves into a saucepan, pour in the strained beef broth, and simmer for a few minutes.
Add the diced cooked beef and hand-crushed marjoram, then season to taste with salt and ground pepper.
Whisk the thick sour cream with the wheat flour, stir into the borscht, and heat gently while stirring constantly.

name: Lviv-style stuffed veal roulades (Zrazy cielęce zawijane po lwowsku)
summary: Traditional Lviv-style roulades of thinly pounded veal spread with mustard, stuffed with batons of fatback, fermented pickles, carrots, and parsley root, braised in sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: for dusting roulades and thickening sauce

steps: Cut the veal into wide slices, pound into thin cutlets, spread each thinly with mustard, and sprinkle with chopped onion.
Cut the fatback, carrots, parsley root, and fermented pickles into batons, season with pepper, place on the meat slices, and roll up tightly, securing with toothpicks.
Dust the roulades with salt and some flour, and brown well on all sides in heated fat.
Transfer the roulades to a shallow pot, pour in the pan drippings and 125 ml of water, and simmer covered slowly until tender.
When the roulades are tender, sprinkle the remaining flour over the sauce, season with pepper, bring to a boil, and stir in the sour cream.
Arrange the roulades on a platter, spoon over the sauce, and serve with buckwheat groats, barley groats, or potatoes, alongside a raw vegetable salad and cooked vegetables.

name: Sałatka owocowa na ostro (spiced wine fruit salad)
summary: A summery fruit salad of pears, apples, peaches, apricots, and sweet cherries dressed in dry white wine, olive oil, mustard, lemon zest, and nutmeg.
steps: Peel and core the pears and apples, cut the fruit into eighths, and drizzle with 4 tablespoons of dry white wine.
Pit the remaining fruit, quarter the peaches, halve the apricots, and pit the cherries.
Whisk the mustard with the olive oil and 200 ml of dry white wine, then stir in the grated lemon zest, ground nutmeg, and icing sugar.
Combine all the fruit in a large bowl, pour over the prepared dressing, and chill in the refrigerator for 60 minutes.

name: Two-bean casserole (Zapiekanka z fasoli)
summary: A quick skillet dish of minced meat, Romano green beans, white beans, bell pepper, and tomato, cooked with meat broth, white wine, and fresh marjoram.
steps: Trim the green beans, cut into pieces, boil for 6–8 minutes in salted water, and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet, add the minced meat, season with salt and pepper, and fry for about 5 minutes.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper cut into small pieces to the meat and fry, stirring, for another 5 minutes.
Drain the canned white beans, and cut the tomato into eighths; add them along with the cooked green beans one minute before the end of frying.
Pour the broth and white wine over everything, cook for 5 minutes, and sprinkle with fresh marjoram leaves before serving.

name: Malinowa pianka (raspberry yogurt mousse)
summary: Light chilled dessert made of fresh raspberries, plain yogurt, and whipped egg whites set with gelatin.
steps: Rub half of the raspberries through a sieve into a smooth puree, set aside 4 whole raspberries for garnish, and divide the remaining berries among four dessert cups.
Dissolve the gelatin in a small amount of water, and separate the egg white from the yolk.
Whisk the plain yogurt thoroughly with the egg yolk, raspberry puree, lemon juice, sugar, and vanilla sugar, then mix in the dissolved gelatin and place in the refrigerator.
Beat both egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold into the yogurt mixture as it begins to set.
Pour the prepared mousse over the raspberries in the cups, chill for 60 minutes in the refrigerator, and garnish with the reserved raspberries and lemon balm leaves before serving.

name: Rolada fantazyjna (pork and beef meatloaf roll with potatoes)
summary: Foil-baked seasoned pork and beef meatloaf roll with fresh herbs, baked in a single parcel with potatoes and sour cream.

ingredients.name: mixed fresh herbs (chives, basil, parsley leaves)

steps: Soak the kaiser rolls in water, squeeze out excess liquid, and grind in a meat grinder together with the pork and beef.
Add the egg, chopped onion, mustard, salt, and pepper to the meat and mix thoroughly.
Spread the meat into a layer 1.5 cm thick on an oiled sheet of baking foil, sprinkle with chopped fresh herbs, and roll into a roulade without rolling the foil inside.
Arrange peeled, salted potatoes around the roulade and drizzle them with sour cream.
Wrap the edges of the foil to seal the entire dish, prick the foil on top, transfer to a roasting pan, add a splash of water, and bake for 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Polish meatloaf with porcini mushrooms and bacon (Pieczeń z grzybami)
summary: A classic Polish minced beef and pork meatloaf studded with porcini mushrooms, wrapped in smoked bacon strips and served chilled with diced broth aspic.
steps: Soak the kaiser roll in water, squeeze out thoroughly, and combine with the minced meat.
Peel and finely chop the onions, add to the meat along with the eggs, season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg, and knead the mixture thoroughly.
Slice the porcini mushrooms and gently fold them into the meat mixture.
Line a loaf tin with slices of smoked bacon, fill with the meat mixture, press down lightly, and bake for 40–50 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.
Dissolve the gelatine in the hot broth, chill until set, cut the aspic into cubes, and arrange around the cooled meatloaf.

name: Owoce pod kruszonką (strawberry and mango oat crumble)
summary: Fresh mango chunks and strawberries baked under a crisp buttery oat crumble.
steps: Peel the mangoes, chop into pieces, toss in a bowl with the strawberries, 3 tablespoons of sugar, and potato starch, and transfer to a baking dish.
In a separate bowl, mix the rolled oats with the remaining sugar, add the grated frozen butter, and rub together with your hands until clumps form.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the fruit layer.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 45 minutes.

name: Warm pickle sauce
summary: A traditional hot Polish sauce of stewed brine pickles on a lard-and-flour roux with meat broth, finished with sour cream and egg yolk.
steps: Melt the lard in a saucepan, stir in the flour, make a roux, and whisk in the cold meat broth.
Dice the fermented pickles, simmer gently in the pickle brine, then combine with the whisked roux and bring to a boil.
Whisk the egg yolk with the sour cream, stir into the sauce, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Breaded chicken cutlets (Pierś z kurczaka panierowana)
summary: Tenderised chicken breast cutlets dredged in garlic-and-curry seasoned egg, coated in crisp breadcrumbs, and fried until golden.
steps: Wash and dry the chicken breast, divide into 4 portions, and gently pound with a meat mallet.
Beat the egg in a shallow dish with the granulated garlic, curry powder, chicken seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Dip the cutlets in the egg mixture, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing the crumb coating firmly with your hands.
Fry the cutlets in hot sunflower oil on both sides until golden brown.

name: Likier kresowy (Borderlands linden flower liqueur)
summary: Homemade linden blossom liqueur made with rectified spirit, sugar syrup, and lemon juice.
steps: Place the fresh linden blossoms into a large jar and pour in 1.5 l of 70% rectified spirit.
Seal the jar tightly and set aside in a dark, warm place for 14 days, shaking it from time to time.
Strain the infusion through fine cloth and pour it into 1 l of hot sugar syrup mixed with 100 ml of lemon juice.
Stir the liquid thoroughly, strain again through cloth, and bottle.

name: Red curry rice with vegetables
summary: Single-serving vegan rice dish braised with carrots, cauliflower, onion, and garlic, flavoured with red curry paste.
steps: Slice the carrot and divide the quarter head of cauliflower into small florets.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet, add the sliced onion and garlic, sauté until tender, and season with salt.
Add the carrot and cauliflower, pour in a splash of water, and simmer in the skillet for 15 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, pour in a little more water, lower the heat, and stir to combine.
Stir in a quarter teaspoon of red curry paste, cook together for another 5 minutes, and transfer to a bowl.

name: Likier z czarnego bzu (elderberry liqueur)
summary: Aromatic elderberry liqueur spiced with cloves, cinnamon, and lemon zest.
steps: Wash and dry the elderberries, then transfer them into a jar.
Mix 1 l of rectified spirit with 250 ml of water, pour over the fruit, seal the jar tightly, and set aside for 2 weeks, shaking it daily.
Bring 750 ml of water to a boil with the grated lemon zest, cloves, and cinnamon bark, cover, and simmer over low heat for about 10 minutes.
Add the sugar, cook to a thick syrup, skim off any foam, and remove the pot from the heat.
Decant the spirit infusion from the fruit and gradually pour it into the syrup, stirring constantly, then pour everything into a jar and seal tightly.
After 3 days, filter the liqueur thoroughly, pour into bottles, cork, and set aside for 3 months.

name: Ryba po podhalańsku (Podhale-style baked fish)
summary: Pan-fried pollock fillets baked over sliced potatoes, root vegetables, onion, and prunes with a creamy garlic tomato sauce.
steps: Soak the prunes in water, drain, and cut into thin strips.
Rinse and pat dry the pollock fillets, drizzle with the juice of half a lemon, season with salt and pepper, dredge in flour, and fry in part of the oil on both sides until golden.
Peel the vegetables, slice the potatoes and carrots, dice the celeriac, and slice the onion into half-moons.
Sauté the prepared vegetables in a roasting dish in the remaining oil, then stir in the butter and prune strips near the end of cooking.
Arrange the fried fish on top of the vegetables, pour over the thick tomato juice mixed with sour cream, minced garlic, salt, and pepper, and bake for 10–15 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.
Sprinkle the hot dish with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Naleśniki z kwiatem akacji (acacia blossom crepes)
summary: Delicate, fluffy crepes folded with whipped egg whites and fresh black locust (acacia) blossoms.
steps: Whisk the milk with 2 whole eggs, 2 egg yolks, plain flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter.
Rinse the acacia blossoms, drain them thoroughly, and fold into the batter.
Beat the remaining 2 egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Melt margarine in a skillet and fry thin crepes about 2 mm thick on both sides until golden.

name: Sos chlebowy po lwowsku (Lviv-style bread sauce)
summary: A thick hot sauce made from grated dried wheat bread and wholemeal bread toasted in butter, simmered in broth, and thickened with egg yolks.
steps: Grate the dried wheat bread and wholemeal bread on a fine grater.
Sauté the grated bread in melted butter until lightly browned, then pour in the broth and simmer over low heat for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat, whisk in the egg yolks vigorously, and finally season the sauce with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

name: Italian-style chicken
summary: Chicken breast pieces seasoned with garlic and tarragon, sautéed in olive oil with onions, green bell pepper, mushrooms, sweetcorn, and fresh tomatoes.
steps: Rinse and dry the chicken fillets, rub with salt, pepper, crushed garlic, and tarragon, then cut into bite-sized dice.
Peel the onions and slice into half-moons. Seed and slice the bell pepper into strips, chop the tomatoes, and quarter any larger mushrooms while leaving smaller ones whole.
Heat the olive oil in a pan, sear the chicken, then add the onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms, continuing to fry.
Towards the end of cooking, stir in the drained sweetcorn and diced tomatoes, cook for another 3 minutes, and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

name: Cielęcina litewska (Lithuanian-style roast veal)
summary: Boneless roast veal leg marinated for three days in grated root vegetables and spicy mustard, larded with fatback, and baked with sour cream.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: approximately 20 g for thickening the sauce (corrected from 1 tsp)

steps: Peel the carrot, parsley root, and celeriac and grate them, and peel and finely chop the onion.
Mix the prepared vegetables with the spicy mustard, rub all over the veal, place in an earthenware crock, press down with a plate, and chill for 3 days.
Season the marinated veal with salt, lard it with the fatback strips, and transfer to a roasting pan greased with butter.
Roast in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 10 minutes, then lower the temperature to 180 °C and roast for another 80 minutes, basting with melted butter and the juices from marinating.
Shortly before the end of roasting, pour over the sour cream mixed with the wheat flour and bake for a few minutes.

name: Chłodnik po polsku (traditional Polish cold beetroot soup)
summary: A refreshing Polish cold soup of soured milk whisked with cooked grated beetroots, diced chicken, hard-boiled eggs, fresh cucumber, radishes, dill, and parsley.
steps: Wash and boil the beetroots until tender, then cool, peel, and grate on a coarse box grater.
Cook the chicken meat and chop finely, and hard-boil the eggs, peel, and dice into chunks.
Peel the cucumber and cut it into thin strips, grate the radishes, and finely chop the dill and parsley leaves.
Whisk the soured milk, stir in all prepared ingredients with the herbs, season to taste with salt, and serve well chilled.

name: Mazurek makowy (poppy seed Polish Easter shortbread)
summary: Polish Easter shortbread cake made with whole poppy seeds and warming spices, topped with chopped walnuts and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for the baking sheet

steps: Scald the poppy seeds and drain them thoroughly.
Finely chop the butter with the wheat flour on a pastry board, add the drained poppy seeds, sugar, most of the beaten eggs, and a pinch each of nutmeg, cinnamon, and cloves.
Knead into a smooth dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll out the chilled dough, transfer onto a buttered baking sheet, brush the top with the remaining beaten egg, and sprinkle with powdered sugar mixed with chopped walnuts.
Bake in an oven preheated to 160 °C for about 30 minutes.

name: Sardine and egg salad (Sałatka z sardynek)
summary: Mashed canned sardines, hard-boiled eggs, and tangy capers tossed with fresh lettuce leaves in a simple oil and vinegar dressing.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs, let cool, peel, and finely chop.
Drain the canned sardines and mash them with a fork.
Wash and pat dry the lettuce, tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces, and combine with the sardines and chopped eggs.
Add the capers, drizzle the salad with oil and vinegar, season with salt, and serve chilled.

name: Oscypek smażony (pan-fried smoked highland sheep's cheese)
summary: Thick slices of smoked sheep's milk cheese fried in butter and served hot with cranberry or cowberry preserve.
steps: Cut the Oscypek cheese into slices about 0.5 cm thick.
Heat the butter in a frying pan and fry the cheese slices on both sides until golden brown.
Arrange the hot Oscypek slices on a warmed serving dish and serve with cowberries or cranberries.

name: Spiced braised root vegetables with corn (Warzywa na sposób orientalny)
summary: Grated root vegetables braised with sweetcorn, onion, and garlic, flavoured with curry, ginger, and nutmeg.
steps: Peel the carrots, parsley root, and celeriac, and grate them on the coarse side of a grater.
Peel and chop the onion, then sauté it in hot oil.
Add the grated root vegetables, drained sweetcorn, and crushed garlic clove, season with salt, pepper, ginger, nutmeg, and curry powder, then pour in a splash of water.
Braise the vegetables covered over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, adding a little water if needed.

name: Okonomiyaki (Hiroshima-style Japanese savoury pancake)
summary: A layered Hiroshima-style Japanese savoury pancake with a thin crepe, shredded cabbage, bacon, fried noodles, and a fried egg.
steps: Shred the white cabbage into thin strips about 3 mm wide, slice the pork belly into thin ribbons, and cut the chicken breast into strips.
Thinly slice the celery and leek, chop the parsley, and toss the greens together in a small bowl.
Cook and drain the noodles, and whisk the flour, cold water, and one egg into a smooth crepe batter.
Heat two frying pans lightly greased with oil; in the first pan fry a thin crepe, flip it over, and splash with soy sauce.
Layer the shredded cabbage, chicken pieces, and pork belly slices on top of the crepe.
Invert the second pan over the top, flip so that the crepe is on top, and cook over medium heat until the cabbage softens and the bacon browns.
In the smaller pan, lightly fry the cooked noodles, then flip the pancake using the pan, layer the noodles on top, and invert again so the crepe is facing up.
Fry two sunny-side-up eggs in the small pan, place them on top of the pancake, and flip the whole stack one last time for a moment.
Transfer the okonomiyaki to a large plate, cut into at least four wedges, drizzle generously with okonomiyaki sauce, and scatter the celery, leek, and parsley mixture over the top.

name: Zupa jarzynowa z rzodkwią (Vegetable soup with white radish and bacon)
summary: A warming vegetable soup with white daikon radish, carrots, leeks, and potatoes cooked gently in butter, garnished with crispy smoked bacon.
steps: Clean, wash, and cut the carrots, leeks, onions, and white radish into sizeable pieces, then cook them gently covered in the butter for 15 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the bay leaves, thyme, salt, and pepper, and cook for about 20 minutes until the vegetables soften.
10 minutes before the end of cooking, toss in the peeled and finely diced potatoes.
Cut the smoked bacon into strips, fry in a pan, and add to the cooked soup.
Garnish the soup with finely chopped parsley before serving.

name: Dorsz po lwowsku (Lviv-style cod meatballs)
summary: Poached minced cod meatballs simmered in vegetable broth, served warm or cold with a sauce of pureed prunes, dry white wine, and mayonnaise.
steps: Soak the prunes in water for 120 minutes, then add the dry white wine, bring to a boil, blend into a smooth puree, and once cooled, stir into the mayonnaise.
Fillet the cod, removing bones and skin, and soak the bread roll in milk, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Mince the cod fillets together with the squeezed bread, chopped onion, and egg, then season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Shape the fish mixture into small meatballs and poach gently in the vegetable broth over low heat for 30 minutes.
Remove the poached meatballs from the broth, spoon over the prune-mayonnaise sauce, and serve warm or chilled.

name: Ciastka serowe (savoury Emmental cheese biscuits)
summary: Crisp and savoury shortcrust biscuits made with finely grated Emmental cheese, flour, and egg yolks.
steps: Grate the Emmental cheese on a fine box grater.
Add the plain flour mixed with baking powder, the egg yolks, and a little salt, then work into a smooth dough.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 2 cm and cut out biscuits using a cookie cutter.
Arrange the biscuits on a floured baking sheet and bake for about 15 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.

name: Jagoda świętych (Pistachio-crusted grape and quark truffles)
summary: Grapes coated in lightly salted full-fat quark and crushed pistachios.
steps: Rinse and thoroughly dry the grapes, and blend the quark with a pinch of salt until smooth.
Take small portions of quark and coat each individual grape evenly.
Arrange the shaped balls on a tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Crush the pistachios in a mortar or chop finely, roll the chilled cheese balls in them to coat, and serve.

name: Kotlety w sosie musztardowym (pork cutlets in mustard cream sauce)
summary: Browned pork loin or tenderloin cutlets braised in a creamy sauce of sour cream, broth, and wholegrain mustard.
steps: Season the pork cutlets with salt and pepper, dredge in plain flour, and brown on both sides in well-heated oil, then pour off excess fat.
Pour 100 ml of broth over the meat and braise, covered, for about 10 minutes.
Add 200 ml of sour cream and braise everything for another 10 minutes.
Stir the wholegrain mustard into the sauce and cook briefly to combine the flavours.

name: Sałatka szegedyńska (Szeged-style potato and pickle salad)
summary: A Hungarian-style salad of jacket-boiled potatoes, half-sour pickles, red bell pepper, tomatoes, lettuce, and hard-boiled eggs in olive oil and vinegar.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, allow to cool, and peel them; hard-boil and peel the eggs.
Remove the core and seeds from the red bell pepper and cut the flesh into strips.
Slice the potatoes, half-sour pickles, hard-boiled eggs, and tomatoes, and tear the lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Combine all ingredients in a salad bowl, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, pepper, and vinegar, and gently toss.

name: Schnitzels stuffed with cress and farmer's cheese (Sznycle nadziewane kiełkami i twarogiem)
summary: Turkey schnitzel pockets fried in butter and stuffed with a creamy mixture of farmer's cheese, butter, parsley, and cress sprouts.
steps: Wash and chop the parsley, snip the cress sprouts with scissors, then mix with 50 g of butter and the farmer's cheese, and season with salt and pepper.
Wash and dry the turkey schnitzels, cut a pocket into the centre of each, fill with the cheese stuffing, and secure with a toothpick.
Fry the schnitzels for 10–15 minutes on both sides in the remaining butter, seasoning with salt and pepper during frying, and serve immediately from the pan.

name: Anyżki (Polish anise sponge cookies)
summary: Crisp, airy Polish sponge biscuits infused with the distinct fragrance of freshly ground aniseed.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: plus a little for dusting the baking sheet

steps: Grind the aniseeds in a spice grinder or crush them in a mortar.
Beat the eggs with sugar for 3–4 minutes until thick, pale, and ribbony.
Fold in the sifted wheat flour and ground aniseed gently with a spoon.
Drop small round portions of batter onto a flour-dusted baking sheet and bake in an oven preheated to 150–160 °C for about 15–20 minutes.

name: Smalec ziołowy (Polish herbal lard spread with apple and prune)
summary: Homemade pork lard spread with cracklings, tart apples, prunes, marjoram, and thyme.
steps: Soak the prunes in boiled water for about 15 minutes, then slice into thin strips.
Peel the tart apples and cut into thin slices.
Dice the fatback finely and render slowly in a pot, being careful not to over-brown the cracklings.
Remove the rendered lard from heat, add the apples and prunes, and season with salt, marjoram, and thyme.
Stir the mixture for about 15 minutes until the lard begins to set, then transfer to stoneware crocks or jars.

name: Spanish scrambled eggs with tomatoes
summary: Scrambled eggs cooked with stewed tomatoes, onion, garlic, and olive oil.
steps: Scald the tomatoes with boiling water, remove the skins, and dice the pulp.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and sauté the peeled, finely chopped onion and pressed garlic.
Add the diced tomatoes, simmer for about 15 minutes, and season with salt and black pepper.
Pour in the beaten eggs, mix thoroughly, fry until set, and sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Pączki (traditional Polish doughnuts)
summary: Traditional Polish yeast doughnuts filled with marmolada (firm fruit preserve), deep-fried, and dusted with icing sugar.
steps: Mash the fresh yeast with part of the warm milk, 200 g of flour, and a tablespoon of sugar, then set the starter in a warm place to rise.
Beat the egg yolks and whole egg with the remaining sugar, then add the rest of the flour, the risen starter, remaining milk, lemon juice and zest, vanilla, salt, and rectified spirit.
Knead the dough until smooth, glossy, and coming cleanly away from your hands, gradually pouring in the oil toward the end.
Cover the dough and leave in a warm place for 15 minutes to prove.

Shape the dough into rounds, place a portion of marmolada (firm fruit preserve) in the centre, pinch the edges firmly to seal into balls, and arrange on a floured pastry board covered with a cloth to rise.
Heat the lard until very hot in a deep pot and fry the doughnuts in batches on both sides until golden brown.
Drain the fried doughnuts on paper towels and dust with icing sugar.

name: Kompot jabłkowy (apple compote drink)
summary: A simple homemade fruit drink made from fresh boiled apples, sweetened to taste and served chilled.
steps: Wash the apples thoroughly, cut them into halves or smaller wedges, and core them.
Bring 500 ml of water to a boil in a pot, add the prepared apples, and cook for about 5 minutes.
Strain the decoction into a vessel, sweeten the warm kompot with sugar, stir thoroughly, and chill before serving.

name: Potato salad with pickled mushrooms (Sałatka ziemniaczana)
summary: A salad of potatoes boiled in their skins and pickled button mushrooms with chives in a sour cream and olive oil dressing.

ingredients.name: pickled button mushrooms
ingredients.note: and 2 tbsp brine for the dressing

steps: Boil the potatoes in their jackets until tender, let cool slightly, peel, and dice into cubes.
Drain the pickled button mushrooms (reserving 2 tbsp of the brine) and dice the mushrooms.
Whisk together the sour cream, olive oil, and 2 tbsp of the mushroom brine, then season the dressing with salt and pepper.
Combine the potatoes, pickled mushrooms, and chopped chives, pour over the dressing, toss well, and chill in a cool place for 30 minutes.

name: Cocoa jam cake
summary: A simple cocoa cake leavened with baking soda, flavoured with strawberry jam and orange flavouring.
steps: Melt the margarine in a small saucepan, allow to cool, and whisk together with the milk.
Beat the eggs with the sugar until light and fluffy, then pour in the margarine and milk mixture.
Sift the flour with the baking soda and cocoa powder into the egg mixture and stir to incorporate.
Add the strawberry jam and orange flavouring and mix slowly until combined.
Pour the batter into a baking pan and bake for about 45 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.

name: Sex on the Beach cocktail
summary: A classic fruity alcoholic cocktail made with vodka, peach liqueur, orange juice, and cranberry juice, served over ice.

ingredients.name: lemon slice
ingredients.note: or lime or orange, for garnish

steps: Pour the vodka, peach schnapps, orange juice, and cranberry juice into a cocktail shaker and shake vigorously.
Put a few ice cubes in a tall glass.
Pour the cocktail from the shaker into the glass and garnish with a slice of lemon, lime, or orange.

name: Maczki drożdżowe (yeast poppy seed pinwheels)
summary: Flaky yeast pastry pinwheels with poppy seed filling, baked until golden.
steps: Chop the margarine into the flour, add the whole eggs and the yeast mixed with 250 ml of sour cream and the sugar, then knead into a smooth dough.
Place the kneaded dough into the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Roll out the chilled dough into thin sheets and spread the poppy seed filling over them.
Roll the dough into logs, slice into pieces 3 cm long, and arrange loosely on a baking sheet.
Brush the pastries with beaten egg yolks and bake for about 30 minutes in an oven preheated to 170 °C.

name: Zupa ziołowa (potato and fresh herb soup)
summary: A light puréed potato and onion soup made with broth, olive oil, and fresh herbs: basil, rosemary, mint, and thyme.

ingredients.name: Polish herb and spice seasoning (pieprz ziołowy)

steps: Peel and dice the potatoes, and finely chop the onion.
Place the potatoes and onion in a pot, add the olive oil, pour over the prepared vegetable broth, and cook until the potatoes are tender.
Blend the soup into a smooth purée and season to taste with salt and Polish herb and spice seasoning (pieprz ziołowy).
Before serving, sprinkle the soup with finely chopped leaves of basil, rosemary, mint, and thyme.

name: Spanish-style tomato and garlic sauce
summary: A zesty sauce of simmered tomatoes, garlic, wine vinegar, and hot paprika, thickened with crumbled bread and emulsified with olive oil.
steps: Scald the tomatoes with boiling water, remove the skins, and dice the flesh.
Press the garlic through a crusher and cook in a saucepan with 1 tablespoon of heated olive oil until translucent.
Add the diced tomatoes, crumbled roll, wine vinegar, and hot paprika, and simmer over low heat until the sauce is moderately thick but still fairly fluid.
Pass the cooked sauce through a sieve.
Stirring constantly, slowly pour in the remaining 3 tablespoons of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and warm gently for a moment.

name: Jajka po żmudzku (Samogitian egg salad in shells)
summary: Traditional Lithuanian-Samogitian style eggs: hard-boiled eggs chopped with onion, parsley, and mayonnaise, served in their shells.
steps: Peel the large onion and chop it finely.
Hard-boil the eggs, let them cool, cut them in half lengthwise through the shell, scoop out the contents, and chop finely.
Mix the chopped eggs with the onion, mayonnaise, and parsley leaves, and season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the egg salad back into the shell halves and arrange on a plate.

name: Sudovian breaded pork roulades (Zawijasy z Sudowy)
summary: Lithuanian breaded pork roulades filled with sautéed ham, cooked carrot, and onion, served with a sauce of white wine, sour cream, and cold butter.

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: e.g. pork loin or leg cutlets

ingredients.name: bay leaf
ingredients.note: leaves, to fasten the sides of the rolls

steps: Slice the pork into cutlets, pound with a mallet, and season with salt and pepper.
Chop the cooked carrot, ham, and onions, and sauté together in 1 tablespoon of butter.
Spread the filling over the pork cutlets, roll them up, and secure with toothpicks, affixing bay leaves at each side where the toothpicks are inserted.
Dredge the roulades in beaten egg and breadcrumbs, and fry on all sides in clarified butter.

Pour the white wine and sour cream into the pan drippings, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Stir constantly while adding 3 tablespoons of cold butter a piece at a time, then pour the sauce over the roulades.

name: Brownies (double chocolate brownies)
summary: Rich American brownies packed with semi-sweet and white chocolate drops, fudgy inside with a crackly crust.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175 °C and line a rectangular baking pan with baking paper.
Melt the unsalted butter and semi-sweet chocolate in a saucepan over low heat and let cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with sugar and vanilla extract in a separate bowl.
Combine the cooled chocolate with the egg mixture and beat thoroughly, then fold in the plain flour, salt, white chocolate chips, and semi-sweet chocolate chips.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for about 25 minutes at 175 °C, until the top becomes lighter and the centre remains slightly moist.
Slice the warm cake into squares, arrange on a serving plate, and dust with sifted icing sugar.

name: Kapuśniak czeski (Czech sauerkraut soup with pork, bacon, and wild mushrooms)
summary: Hearty Czech sauerkraut soup with diced pork, smoked bacon, dried forest mushrooms, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1 l for soup and 300 ml for potatoes

ingredients.name: sweet paprika
ingredients.note: 1 tsp in ingredients, 1 tbsp in method

steps: Dice the smoked bacon and pork into small cubes, and peel and chop the onion and garlic.
Boil the peeled potatoes in 300 ml of water until tender and mash them with a potato masher.
Render the fat from the bacon in a pan, remove the cracklings, and in the rendered fat sauté the onion until translucent and dust with sweet paprika.
Transfer the skillet contents into a pot, pour in 1 liter of water, and add the sauerkraut, bacon cracklings, dried mushrooms, allspice, salt, pepper, sugar, garlic, and sour cream.
Simmer the soup over low heat for 30 minutes, then add the diced pork and cook for another 10 minutes.
Stir the mashed potatoes into the soup, combine well, and serve with thick buttered slices of bread.

name: Strawberry jam
summary: A classic homemade strawberry jam made from ripe summer berries simmered with sugar and pectin sugar.
steps: Hull and sort the ripe strawberries, rinse thoroughly under cold running water, and drain well.
Transfer the strawberries to a wide pot, cover with the sugar, and set aside for a few hours until the sugar begins to dissolve.
Simmer the strawberries over low heat for about 60 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the jam sugar and heat for another 10 minutes, stirring constantly, then transfer the hot jam to clean jars and seal tightly.

name: Chinese toffee apples (Basi pingguo)
summary: Crisp batter-fried apple chunks tossed in molten sugar caramel and chilled in cold water for a brittle crust.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for thin batter and for chilling caramel

steps: Peel and core the apples, then cut the fruit into large chunks.
Whisk the plain flour, potato starch, egg, a pinch of salt, and water into a smooth, thin batter.
Dip the apple chunks into the batter, deep-fry in hot oil until golden, and drain on paper towels.
Heat one tablespoon of oil in a separate pan, add the sugar, and cook until a light caramel forms.
Add the fried apples to the caramel, toss quickly to coat, transfer to a greased plate, and dip briefly into cold water before eating so that the caramel hardens.

name: Kiszone ogórki (brined sour pickles)
summary: Homemade naturally fermented cucumbers in a jar with garlic, horseradish, dill, and spices, briefly pasteurised in the oven.
steps: Wash the cucumbers very thoroughly and pack them tightly upright into a sterilised one-litre jar.
Add the halved garlic cloves, dill sprig, peeled piece of horseradish root, allspice berries, peppercorns, and optionally the sour cherry or vine leaves.
Dissolve half a teaspoon of rock salt in 500 ml of hot water and pour over the cucumbers in the jar.
Tightly screw on the jar lid, invert it, and then pasteurise for 15 minutes in an oven preheated to 90 °C.

name: Citrus marmalade
summary: Homemade citrus marmalade made with fruit pulp and shredded peel cooked with gelling sugar.
steps: Peel the citrus fruits, remove the white membrane from the pulp, and chop finely.
Wash two whole citrus fruits thoroughly, thickly pare the peel, and slice into thin strips.
Combine the citrus pulp, sliced peel, and gelling sugar, and let stand for about 12 hours.
Bring the mixture to a boil while stirring constantly, and cook for several minutes until the proper gelling point is reached.
Ladle the hot marmalade into sterilized jars, seal immediately and tightly, and invert the jars several times while cooling to distribute the peel evenly.

name: Chocolate soufflé (Suflet czekoladowy)
summary: A light baked soufflé made from dark chocolate and stiffly beaten egg whites with icing sugar.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: softened, or margarine, for greasing ramekins

steps: Preheat the oven to 200–220 °C, grease ceramic ramekins with softened butter, coat with granulated sugar, and tap out the excess.
Melt the dark chocolate in a small bowl placed over a pot of hot simmering water.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt, add the icing sugar towards the end of whipping, and continue beating until stiff.
Add the melted chocolate to the whipped egg whites and gently fold together.
Fill the ramekins level with the rim, smooth the surface with a knife, and bake for 10–12 minutes.

name: Morszczuk duszony (braised hake with apples, tomatoes and white wine)
summary: Pan-fried hake fillets braised in dry white wine with apple wedges and fresh tomatoes.
steps: Wash and gently dry the hake fillets, drizzle with the juice squeezed from the half lemon, season with salt and pepper, and set aside in a cool place for 2 hours.
Cut each apple into eight wedges and remove the cores, then scald, peel, and chop the tomatoes.
Dredge the marinated fillets in wheat flour and fry on both sides in heated vegetable oil until golden.
Arrange the apple wedges and tomatoes around the fish in the pan, pour in the dry white wine, and braise covered over low heat for 5–10 minutes.
Sprinkle the finished dish with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Sałatka nicejska (Niçoise salad)
summary: A classic French salad of crisp lettuce, flaked tuna, tomatoes, hard-boiled eggs, olives, and white onion tossed in a garlic vinaigrette.
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce, then tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Hard-boil the eggs, let cool, peel, and cut into quarters.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the white onion into rings, and cut the olives in half.
In a salad bowl, combine the lettuce, tomatoes, onion, egg quarters, drained tuna, and olives.
Finely mince the garlic, mash it with a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper, stir in the lemon juice or wine vinegar, and gradually whisk in the olive oil.
Drizzle the salad with the dressing and gently toss.

name: Walnut glaze (Polewa orzechowa)
summary: A sweet Polish cake topping made of chopped walnuts simmered in melted margarine with sugar and honey.
steps: Pour a tablespoon of water into a pot, add the sliced margarine, sprinkle in the sugar, and add the honey.
Heat the ingredients over low heat, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved.
Stir in the chopped walnuts towards the end of cooking, heat together briefly, and mix thoroughly.

name: Spanish-style sheep cheese turnovers (Pierożki po hiszpańsku)
summary: Baked Spanish pastry turnovers made with white wine and lemon zest dough, filled with grated sheep's milk cheese, garlic, and sautéed onions.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 for the filling, 1 yolk for brushing the tops

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: melted, for brushing pastry and baking sheet

steps: Combine the wheat flour with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, dry white wine, and grated lemon zest, knead into a smooth dough, wrap in clingfilm, and chill in the fridge for 2 hours.
Peel and chop the onion, then cook until translucent in a tablespoon of olive oil.
Grate the sheep's milk cheese, mix with one egg, chopped parsley leaves, minced garlic, and the translucent onion, and season with salt and pepper.
Roll out the chilled dough, cut out rounds, and brush them with melted butter.
Spoon the filling onto the rounds, fold in half, crimp the edges to seal, and brush the tops with the yolk of the second egg.
Place the pastries on a buttered baking sheet and bake for about 10 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Tumbet (Mallorcan baked vegetables)
summary: A traditional Mallorcan vegetable bake of layered pan-fried potatoes, aubergines, and red bell peppers topped with a tomato and garlic sauce.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: for frying the vegetables and making the sauce

steps: Heat olive oil in a pan, fry the potato slices until golden, and drain on paper towels.
Fry the aubergine slices in the same oil, set aside, then fry the red pepper strips.
Arrange the vegetables in layers in a baking dish: potatoes on the bottom, aubergines over them, and peppers on top.
Sauté the chopped garlic in a little olive oil, add the diced tomatoes, season with salt and oregano, and simmer covered for about 20 minutes.
Pour the tomato sauce over the vegetables, bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 15 minutes, and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Tortilla de patatas (Spanish potato omelette)
summary: A classic thick Spanish omelette made with potatoes and onions gently fried in olive oil.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: generous amount for frying the potatoes

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin slices, and finely chop the onion.
Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a deep skillet, cook the onion until translucent, add the potato slices, and fry over moderate heat, turning every few minutes until tender and lightly golden.
Season the potatoes with salt towards the end of frying, remove from heat, and drain thoroughly along with the onion of excess oil.
Beat the eggs lightly in a bowl with a pinch of salt, gently combine with the drained potatoes and onion, then set aside for 10–15 minutes.
Heat a little of the reserved oil in the skillet, pour in the egg and potato mixture, and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, gently shaking the pan.
Cover the skillet with a large flat plate, invert the tortilla onto the plate, slide it back into the hot skillet uncooked side down, and cook for a few more minutes until the eggs are set.

name: Romesco sauce
summary: Catalan spicy sauce of dried and fresh chilies, roasted tomatoes, garlic, toasted almonds, hazelnuts, and fried bread.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for sautéing and roasting, 2 tbsp for the sauce

steps: Soak the dried hot chilies in warm water for about 60 minutes, then finely chop them together with the fresh chili.
Lightly sauté the chopped chilies and bread slices in a little olive oil.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C, toast the peeled almonds and hazelnuts until lightly golden, and roast the tomatoes in an oiled baking dish for 10 minutes.
Let the roasted tomatoes cool, peel off their skins, and chop finely.
Blend or pound in a mortar the sautéed chilies, bread, crushed garlic, hazelnuts, almonds, and 1 tablespoon of chopped parsley leaves.
Add the chopped tomatoes, blend again, then stir in 2 tablespoons of olive oil and season with wine vinegar and salt.

name: Marmitako (Basque tuna and potato stew)
summary: Traditional Basque fish stew made with fresh tuna, potatoes, green bell pepper, and onion.
steps: Cut the fresh tuna into bite-sized pieces.
Peel the potatoes and onion, dice the potatoes, chop the onion, and slice the green bell pepper into strips.
Heat the olive oil in a pot, add the onion and cook until translucent, then add the green bell pepper and fry for 3–5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and sweet ground paprika, stir, pour in the water, bring to a boil, and simmer over low heat for 20–25 minutes.
Season the soup to taste with salt, add the tuna pieces, and cook for about 5 minutes longer.

name: Torrijas (Spanish Easter French toast)
summary: Traditional Spanish sweet Easter toast made from bread soaked in sweetened milk, dipped in egg, and fried in olive oil.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the milk and extra for sprinkling

steps: Mix the milk with two tablespoons of sugar.
Cut the bread slices into smaller pieces, soak them in the sweetened milk, and leave until thoroughly saturated.
Lift the soaked bread pieces from the milk and coat them in the lightly beaten eggs.
Fry the toasts in hot olive oil on both sides until golden, and serve sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon.

name: Zupa z pulpecikami (Korean-style meatball and tofu soup)
summary: Korean-style soup in beef broth with delicate meatballs made from minced beef, tofu, leek, garlic, and sesame.
steps: Finely chop the cleaned leek and peeled garlic.
Mix thoroughly in a bowl the minced beef, mashed tofu, chopped leek, garlic, eggs, flour, sesame seeds, and sesame oil.
Shape the prepared mixture into small balls about 2 cm in diameter.
Pour the beef broth into a pot, bring to a boil, and carefully drop in the shaped meatballs.
Cook over moderate heat until boiling again and the meatballs are cooked through, and finish by seasoning with salt and soy sauce; serve alone or with bread.

name: Koulourakia (Greek butter cookies)
summary: Crisp Greek butter cookies (koulourakia) shaped into small rings and baked until golden.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the baking sheet

steps: Beat the butter with the sugar until smooth, light, and creamy.
Add 1 whole egg and 2 egg yolks and beat until smooth.
Add the flour mixed with the baking powder and knead into a soft dough.
Place the dough in the refrigerator to chill for 60 minutes.
Roll the dough into thin ropes and shape them into small rings or crescents.
Arrange the cookies on a buttered baking sheet, brush the tops with the remaining beaten egg, and bake for 10–12 minutes in an oven preheated to 150 °C.

name: Morkovcha (Korean-style spiced carrot salad)
summary: Spicy salad of thinly shredded carrots dressed with hot onion-infused oil, vinegar, garlic, and hot ground paprika.
steps: Peel the carrots and cut into long, thin matchsticks or shred on a coarse grater.
Salt the carrots, toss, set aside for 30 minutes, then drain off the released juices.
Add salt, sugar, and hot ground paprika to the drained carrots.
Peel and chop the onion, fry in the vegetable oil until deep golden, then remove the onion from the pan and discard.
Let the infused oil cool slightly, carefully pour in the vinegar, stir, and pour the hot mixture over the carrots.
Add the pressed garlic, toss thoroughly, and chill in the refrigerator for 2–3 hours before serving.

name: Krupnik (barley soup)
summary: Traditional Polish barley soup cooked on beef bone broth with pearl barley, potatoes, root vegetables, and dried mushrooms.

ingredients.name: lovage, celery leaves, and leek
ingredients.note: several herb sprigs and a piece of leek

steps: Place the beef on the bone into a pot of about 3 l capacity, cover with water, add the bay leaf, peppercorns, and allspice berries, and simmer, skimming off any foam that rises.
Once the stock stops foaming, add the rinsed lovage sprigs, celery leaves, leek, peeled celeriac, parsley roots, diced carrots, and dried mushrooms, and cook together.
Add the scalded (rinsed with boiling water) pearl barley and simmer over very low heat for 30 minutes.
Add the peeled and diced potatoes and simmer until tender, then discard the spent herb sprigs.
Season the krupnik to taste with salt and pepper and stir in the chopped fresh parsley.

name: Zupa julienne (Potage julienne)
summary: A classic French soup made with root vegetables, kohlrabi, savoy cabbage, cauliflower, and green peas cut into fine matchsticks in clear broth.
steps: Peel the carrot, kohlrabi, celeriac, and parsley root, and cut them into matchstick-sized strips (julienne).
Cut the savoy cabbage into narrow strips of similar size, and divide the cauliflower into small florets.
Cook the savoy cabbage until tender in broth or separately in salted water, and roast the onion in the oven or char it directly over a flame for a dozen or so minutes.
Cook the remaining sliced vegetables and green peas gently covered for a few minutes in the butter, then transfer them along with the cabbage and charred onion into the broth.
Simmer the soup over low heat for 15–20 minutes, season to taste with salt, and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Bulion z kurczaka (classic chicken stock)
summary: A classic homemade chicken stock slowly simmered with soup vegetables and a bouquet garni.
steps: Place the bone-in chicken meat into a large stockpot, cover with water, and place over medium heat.
When the water boils, reduce the heat and skim any scum from the surface with a slotted spoon.
Tie the thyme, parsley, bay leaf, black peppercorns, garlic, chives, coriander, and dill seeds into a bundle with string, or place them in a muslin bag.
Add the onion, carrot, celeriac with leaves, parsley root, leek, salt, and the prepared bouquet garni to the pot, and simmer gently for 120 minutes.
Strain the finished stock and chill quickly by placing the pot into an ice bath.

name: Bulion wołowy (white beef and veal stock)
summary: A traditional white beef and veal stock slowly simmered with marrow bones, beef shank, vegetables, and herbs.

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.note: to cover ingredients by about 5 cm

steps: Arrange the beef shank, beef marrow bones, beef ribs, veal leg, and bone-in chicken meat in a large stockpot, covering with cold water about 5 cm above the ingredients.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, reduce the flame, and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, skimming scum regularly.
Skim the scum once more, then add the onion, leeks, carrots, salt, and string-tied bundle of parsley leaves, fresh thyme, bay leaf, and black peppercorns.
Stir, partially cover the pot, and simmer over very low heat for 360–480 minutes.
Remove the bones and vegetables, then strain the stock through a double layer of damp cheesecloth into a clean pot.
Cool the stock quickly in a cold-water bath, refrigerate, and remove the layer of fat from the surface once it has solidified.

name: Crêpes
summary: Delicate French pancakes prepared from wheat flour, milk, eggs, and melted butter, rested before cooking.
steps: Put the wheat flour and salt into a bowl, make a well in the centre, crack in the eggs, and mix.
Slowly pour in 500 ml of milk while whisking vigorously to obtain a smooth, lump-free batter.
Melt the butter, stir it into the batter, and let the mixture rest for 720 minutes.
Stir in the remaining 100 ml of milk and mix thoroughly.
Ladle portions of batter (about 150 ml) into a heated, lightly buttered crepe pan and cook each crepe for 2 minutes on the first side and 1 minute after flipping.

name: Zupa pomidorowa (Traditional Polish tomato soup)
summary: A traditional soup made from fresh tomatoes braised in butter and passed through a sieve, simmered with chicken broth and served with rice, pasta, or croutons.

ingredients.name: white bread roll
ingredients.note: crust removed or half a glass of breadcrumbs (optional, for thickening)

steps: Wash the tomatoes, peel off skins (if you will not be passing them through a sieve), cut into quarters, and remove the seeds.
Melt the butter or heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan (optionally fry finely chopped garlic or onion in it).
Add the tomatoes along with the cubed crustless bread roll and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, adding a little broth if necessary.
Purée the cooked tomatoes through a fine sieve or blend on low speed.
Combine the tomato purée with the remaining broth and bring to a boil (according to traditional recipes, you can add half a glass of white wine near the end of cooking to enhance flavour).
Serve the soup with separately cooked rice, pasta, or butter-fried croutons.

name: Fasolka po bretońsku (Breton-style beans with kiełbasa and bacon)
summary: A hearty, iconic Polish stew of large white runner beans simmered with kiełbasa, smoked bacon, rich tomato paste, and marjoram.
steps: Rinse the beans, cover with water, soak for 12 hours, and then drain.

In a pot, bring 1.5 liters of fresh water to a boil, add the drained beans, a chunk of bacon, the bay leaf, and allspice berries, season with salt, and simmer covered for 60–90 minutes until the beans are tender.
Dice the remaining smoked bacon and fry gently in a dry skillet until the fat renders out.
Slice the kiełbasa, add it to the skillet with the bacon, and sauté together.
Mash a few cooked beans and dilute the tomato paste with a little of the cooking broth.
Add the diluted tomato paste, mashed beans, and the browned bacon and kiełbasa with their rendered fat to the pot.
Season the stew with sweet and hot paprika, black pepper, and a generous amount of marjoram.
Whisk the flour with a small amount of broth from the pot, stir into the stew, and simmer for another 15 minutes.

name: Chrupiący kurczak (crispy cornflake chicken)
summary: Tender chicken pieces marinated in spiced yogurt with honey, mustard, ginger, and lemon, coated in crushed cornflakes and fried golden.
steps: Rinse the chicken, remove skin, debone, and cut the meat into 10–12 pieces.
Mix the plain yogurt with the lemon zest and juice, grated onion, honey, grated ginger, and mustard, then season with salt and cayenne pepper.
Place the meat pieces into the marinade and refrigerate for 180–240 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and crush the cornflakes in another dish.
Remove the chicken from the marinade, dip into the egg, dredge in the cornflakes, and fry in hot vegetable oil until golden brown.

name: Jajka w koszyczkach (egg in a basket)
summary: Fried eggs cooked inside butter-toasted bread slices with cut-out centers.
steps: Cut round holes out of the centers of toast bread slices using a glass or a cookie cutter.
Butter the bread slices and the cut-out bread rounds on both sides.
Place the bread in a heated skillet and fry one side until golden brown.
Flip the bread slices over and crack one egg into the hole of each slice.
Season the eggs with salt and pepper, and fry until the egg whites are set.

name: French toast (savory egg bread)
summary: Slices of baguette or bread roll soaked in egg and milk, then fried in butter until golden.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: for savory version, or sugar for sweet version

steps: Crack the egg into a deep dish, pour in the milk, season with salt and black pepper, and whisk with a fork.
Slice the baguette or bread roll into rounds.
Melt the butter in a hot skillet.
Dip each slice on both sides into the egg mixture and fry in the pan on both sides until golden brown.

name: Crispy Parmesan crouton toasts
summary: Crispy baguette slices dipped in melted butter and baked with grated Parmesan cheese until golden.
steps: Trim the crusts off the baguette or roll and cut into small slices.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan or skillet.
Dip each slice on both sides in the melted butter, place onto a baking sheet, and sprinkle with grated Parmesan.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes until golden.

name: Classic poached eggs
summary: Fresh eggs poached without shells in gently simmering salted water with a dash of vinegar.
steps: Pour water into a wide, shallow saucepan to a depth of about 3 cm, add salt and vinegar, and bring to a boil.
Crack each egg individually into a small bowl and gently slide into the softly simmering water.
Poach for about 3 minutes until the white is firm and the yolk remains runny.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon onto a plate and sprinkle with salt and black pepper.

name: Crema catalana
summary: A traditional Catalan custard infused with cinnamon and lemon peel, chilled and crowned with a crisp caramelised sugar crust.
steps: Pare 3 strips of zest from the lemon, place them into a saucepan with the cinnamon sticks, pour in the cream and milk, and heat gently almost to a boil.
Remove the pan from the heat, let infuse for 3–5 minutes to cool slightly, then strain through a fine sieve, discarding the cinnamon and lemon peel.
Separate the yolks from 5 eggs and whisk with 1 whole egg and 75 g of icing sugar until smooth, then whisk into the warm cream and divide among 6 ramekins.
Place the ramekins in a roasting tin filled halfway up their sides with boiling water and bake at about 150 °C for 30–40 minutes until just set.
Lift the ramekins from the water bath, let cool, and refrigerate for at least 240 minutes.
Mix the ground cinnamon, brown sugar, and remaining tablespoon of icing sugar, sift over the chilled custards, and caramelise with a kitchen blowtorch or in a very hot oven.

name: Spicy Greek tomato and cucumber salad (Pikantna sałatka pomidorowa)
summary: A refreshing Greek salad of finely chopped tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and garlic tossed with fresh mint, parsley, and a spicy pinch of cayenne pepper.
steps: Finely chop the cucumber, peeled and seeded tomatoes, onion, garlic, parsley leaves, and mint leaves, and transfer to a bowl.
Season the salad with black pepper, cayenne pepper, olive oil, and lemon juice, and toss well to combine.

name: Grilled salmon on asparagus with citrus salsa
summary: Grilled salmon fillets served over tender green and white asparagus with a zesty citrus-kiwi-ginger salsa.
steps: Clean the salmon fillet, divide into four equal portions, season with salt and pepper, drizzle with part of the lime juice and olive oil, and grill.
Trim and peel the asparagus, and cook green and white separately in boiling water with a pinch of salt and sugar until tender.
Cut away the peel and white pith from the orange and grapefruit, segment the citrus and chop finely, and finely dice the peeled kiwi.
Combine the chopped fruit with the minced pickled ginger, remaining olive oil, balsamic vinegar, chopped mint, and lime juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the cooked asparagus spears on plates, top with the grilled salmon, and spoon the fruit salsa over top.

name: Chocolate Lava Cakes (Babeczki czekoladowe)
summary: Individual molten chocolate lava cakes baked from frozen batter for a warm, liquid chocolate centre.
steps: Melt the butter and chopped chocolate together in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water and let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs with sugar, stir into the melted chocolate mixture, fold in the wheat flour, and mix until smooth.
Butter and flour individual ramekins, fill with the batter, and place in the freezer until completely frozen.
Preheat the oven to 245 °C, bake the cakes directly from the freezer without thawing for about 4 minutes.

name: Lin po góralsku (Highlander-style tench)
summary: Fried tench strips baked under a tomato sauce with spring onions and chives.
steps: Separate the chives from the spring onions and chop them finely. Soak the onions for 60 minutes in 1 l of milk, then drain, fry in butter for 2–3 minutes, and simmer in 500 ml of thick tomato sauce.
Clean and gut the tench, slice into thin strips, season with salt, and drizzle with lemon juice.
Coat the fish pieces in flour and fry until golden.
Transfer the fish to an ovenproof dish, pour over the tomato and onion sauce, and bake for about 15 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.
After removing from the oven, sprinkle the dish with the finely chopped chives.

name: Grilled sesame salmon with horseradish sauce
summary: Grilled salmon fillets sprinkled with sesame seeds, served with a sauce of mayonnaise, plain yogurt, and grated horseradish.
steps: Clean the salmon fillets, place skin-side down on a hot grill, season with salt, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Grill the fish for about 12 minutes.
Combine the mayonnaise with plain yogurt, and season with grated horseradish and salt.
Serve the grilled salmon with the prepared horseradish sauce.

name: Fava bean purée
summary: Simple vegetable dip made from blended peeled fava beans with fresh thyme and olive oil.
steps: Rinse the fava beans and peel the skins from the beans.
Blend the peeled fava beans with thyme leaves and olive oil into a smooth purée, seasoning to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Sałatka świąteczna (festive sausage and potato salad)
summary: A hearty potato salad with kiełbasa, hard-boiled eggs, vinegar pickles and tart apples in a yogurt and mayonnaise dressing.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins, let them cool completely, peel, and cut into slices.
Hard-boil the eggs, let them cool, peel, and finely chop.
Dice the peeled apples, vinegar pickles, small onion and kiełbasa.
Mix the plain yogurt with the mayonnaise and season the dressing with lemon juice, salt, pepper and hot paprika.
Pour the dressing over the prepared ingredients, toss gently, and chill in the refrigerator before serving.

name: Kotlety schabowe faszerowane serem i ziołami (pork cutlets stuffed with herb cheese)
summary: Pounded pork loin cutlets folded into pockets stuffed with grated firm cheese, butter, egg yolk, and fresh herbs.
steps: Cut the pork loin into slices and pound thoroughly with a meat mallet.
Mix the butter, thyme, and oregano with the grated firm cheese, then add the egg yolk, breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, dill, salt, and pepper to knead into a uniform filling.
Place a portion of filling in the centre of each cutlet, fold the meat in half, and fasten the edges with toothpicks.
Season the assembled cutlets with salt and pepper, dredge in plain flour, and fry in hot oil on both sides until golden brown.
Remove the toothpicks from the fried cutlets before serving.

name: Spaghetti alla puttanesca
summary: Italian spaghetti in a punchy tomato sauce with black olives, anchovy fillets, capers, garlic, and hot paprika.
steps: Cook the spaghetti al dente and drain.
Peel and crush the garlic, sauté in heated olive oil, then add the black olives, finely chopped anchovy fillets, and capers.
Fry the ingredients briefly, add the canned tomatoes, and season to taste with hot paprika and pepper.
Simmer the sauce until excess water evaporates, then toss with the cooked pasta.

name: Colourful mixed salad (Surówka kolorowa)
summary: A colourful salad of green lettuce, radicchio, tomatoes, radishes, cucumber, and onion with a farmer's cheese and yogurt dressing.
steps: Wash and dry the green lettuce and radicchio, then tear the leaves into small pieces.
Slice the cucumber, tomatoes, and radishes into rounds, and cut the peeled onions into rings.
Gently toss the sliced vegetables with the lettuces.
Blend the farmer's cheese with the plain yogurt and chopped parsley, season with vinegar, salt, and pepper, and drizzle the dressing over the salad.

name: Kawa mrożona z lodami (iced coffee dessert with ice cream)
summary: Chilled coffee dessert made with black coffee, coffee liqueur, coffee ice cream, and chocolate wafer rolls.

ingredients.name: black coffee
ingredients.note: half a glass of strong brew

steps: Sweeten the hot black coffee with sugar, allow to cool, and stir in the coffee liqueur.
Place the coffee in the freezer to chill thoroughly.
Pour the chilled coffee into chilled sundae dishes and top with scoops of coffee ice cream.
Garnish the dessert with grated chocolate, chocolate wafer rolls, and lemon balm leaves.

name: Herb-marinated breaded schnitzels (Sznycle z ziołami)
summary: Breaded turkey schnitzels marinated in vegetable oil, lemon juice, garlic, marjoram, and thyme, pan-fried until crisp and golden.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for the marinade, plus extra for frying

steps: Lightly pound the turkey schnitzels with a dampened meat mallet.
Mix 3 tablespoons of oil with the lemon juice, finely chopped garlic, marjoram, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Brush the schnitzels with the marinade and chill in the refrigerator for 60 minutes.
Dredge the marinated schnitzels in flour, dip in beaten eggs, coat with breadcrumbs, and fry in hot oil on both sides until golden brown.

name: Murzynek (Polish cocoa cake with coconut)
summary: Classic Polish cocoa cake filled with dried fruit and nuts, glazed with a reserved cooked cocoa glaze and sprinkled with desiccated coconut.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: plus extra for dusting dried fruits and nuts

steps: Place the margarine in a saucepan, add the sugar and cocoa powder, pour in the water, and bring to a boil while stirring until the ingredients dissolve.
Cool the cocoa mixture and set aside 125 ml of it for the glaze.
Add the eggs, wheat flour, baking powder, vanilla sugar, and flour-dusted dried fruit and nuts to the remaining mixture and stir thoroughly into a batter.
Grease a baking tin with margarine, dust with breadcrumbs, pour in the batter, and bake for about 40 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.
Cool the baked cake, drizzle with the reserved cocoa glaze, and sprinkle with desiccated coconut.

name: Likier jajeczny na mleku (milk egg liqueur)
summary: Homemade egg liqueur made with milk and rectified spirit, whipped from egg yolks and sugar.
steps: Boil 1 l of milk and set aside to cool until lukewarm.
Thoroughly whisk the egg yolks with sugar into a pale, fluffy cream.
Without stopping whisking, gradually pour in the lukewarm milk until the ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Slowly pour in 500 ml of rectified spirit while stirring vigorously for a while, then pour the liqueur into bottles and cork tightly.

name: Baked avocado with curd cheese and walnuts (Twaróg z awokado)
summary: Baked avocado halves filled with a seasoned mixture of quark cheese, sautéed mushrooms, onion, fresh parsley, and walnuts.
steps: Dice the mushrooms and finely chop the onion, then cook the onion until translucent in hot oil, add the mushrooms, and cook gently.
Mash the farmer's cheese until smooth and combine with the cooled mushrooms, chopped parsley, and walnuts.
Wash the avocados, halve them lengthwise, remove the stones, and scoop out the flesh, leaving a rim about 1 cm thick along the skin.
Mash the scooped-out avocado flesh with a fork, sprinkle with lemon juice, combine with the cheese mixture, and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Fill the avocado halves with the prepared filling and bake for 10 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Chokeberry bread pudding
summary: A simple baked bread pudding layered with tart-sweet fresh black chokeberries, lemon, and a custardy milk bath.
steps: Whisk the milk with the egg in a wide shallow bowl and soak the slices of wheat bread in this mixture.
Rinse the chokeberries, toss with the sugar, and combine with the peeled, pureed lemon.
Butter a baking dish generously and dust with breadcrumbs.
Layer the soaked bread and chokeberry mixture alternately in the dish, ending with a layer of bread, and pour any remaining egg-milk mixture over the top.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes.

name: Country-style bean and barley soup (Wiejska zupa z fasolą)
summary: A hearty soup of white beans and barley simmered in a bone-in pork broth with browned Polish sausage, garlic, and juniper berries.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking beans and making broth

steps: Cover the white beans with water, add the caraway seeds, and leave to soak overnight (about 12 hours), then bring to the boil and set aside.
Cover the bone-in pork with water, add salt, peppercorns, and allspice berries, and bring to the boil.
Add the trimmed soup vegetables, crushed juniper berries, and bay leaf to the broth, and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the barley groats and parboiled beans to the soup and continue cooking until the ingredients are tender.
Chop the onion and garlic, slice the kiełbasa, fry everything together in a skillet, transfer to the soup pot, season with a pinch of marjoram, and simmer briefly.

name: Patatas bravas (Spanish roasted potato wedges)
summary: Golden crispy Spanish unpeeled potato wedges roasted with olive oil and garlic.
steps: Thoroughly scrub the unpeeled potatoes, halve them, and cut each half lengthwise into 3 wedges.
Transfer the potatoes to a bowl, add the olive oil, crushed garlic clove, and salt, and toss thoroughly.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C, arrange the potato wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet, and roast for about 90 minutes until golden and crisp.

name: Aioli
summary: A Mediterranean cold emulsion sauce made with garlic, egg yolk, white wine vinegar, and olive oil.
steps: Chop the garlic cloves, combine with the egg yolk, white wine vinegar, salt, and pepper, and pound in a mortar or blend in a food processor into a smooth paste.
Whisking constantly and gently, slowly drizzle in the olive oil a few drops at a time until a thick, stable emulsion forms.

name: Traditional English tea
summary: Classic loose-leaf black tea brewed in a warmed teapot, served with milk or lemon and sugar.

ingredients.name: loose-leaf black tea
ingredients.note: 1 teaspoon per person plus 1 for the pot

steps: Boil the water and warm the teapot by rinsing it with boiling water.
Put the loose tea into the teapot, pour in boiling water, cover, and steep for 3–5 minutes.
Pour a little milk into the bottom of the teacups or add a slice of lemon to each.
Pour the hot tea through a strainer into the cups and serve with sugar to taste.

name: Bigos hultajski (Roguish Polish hunter's stew)
summary: Traditional Polish hunter's stew made with sauerkraut braised in lard and beef broth, roasted or boiled beef, and a roux.
