steps: Melt 2.5 tablespoons of lard or diced fatback in the bottom of a pot, add the sauerkraut, pour in the beef broth, and braise for about 30 minutes.
Dice the roasted or boiled beef finely and transfer to the pot with the sauerkraut.
Peel and chop the onion, fry in the remaining tablespoon of lard with the wheat flour into a golden roux, and stir into the bigos.
Simmer everything together over low heat, stirring occasionally until the bigos darkens, and stir in sliced fried kiełbasa before serving.

name: Kawa po turecku (Turkish coffee with spices)
summary: Strong, aromatic coffee brewed in a cezve with sugar and warming spices.
steps: Pour water into the cezve, heat without bringing to a boil, stir in sugar until dissolved.
Add the finely ground coffee and cinnamon or cardamom, and stir.
Heat the coffee over low heat without stirring until foam starts to rise, then remove from heat just before boiling.
Repeat heating and taking off heat twice more, then pour the coffee with its foam into small cups.

name: Zupa poziomkowa (Wild strawberry soup)
summary: A classic Polish fruit soup made from fresh wild strawberries pressed through a sieve, mixed with icing sugar, sour cream, and white wine.
steps: Gently wash the wild strawberries and press them through a fine sieve, gradually pouring in the water.
Add the icing sugar, thin sour cream, and white wine to the strained purée, and mix thoroughly.
Warm the soup over medium heat, taking care not to bring it to a boil.
Serve with rusks, choux pastry puffs, Polish obwarzanki, or croutons soaked in cream and fried in butter.

name: Zupa wiśniowa (Old Polish sour cherry soup)
summary: A traditional Old Polish fruit soup made from sour cherries crushed with their pits and passed through a sieve, simmered with red wine, sugar, and cinnamon.
steps: Wash the sour cherries, pluck off stems, and crush the fruit together with the pits in a mortar or stoneware dish.
Add the cinnamon and optionally cloves and lemon zest, mix, and set aside for 30 minutes.
Press the cherry mixture through a fine sieve, then add the sugar, red wine, and 1 litre of water.
Bring the soup to a boil and thicken if needed with a teaspoon of potato starch dissolved in a little cold water.
Serve with croutons or small sponge biscuits.

name: Zupa śliwkowa (Polish plum soup)
summary: A classic fruit soup made from puréed European prune plums with cloves, cinnamon, and white wine, served with croutons.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: to dilute the purée (plus water to cook the plums)

steps: Wash the plums, halve them, and remove the stones.
Place the fruit in a pot, pour in just enough water to barely cover it, and simmer, stirring frequently, until completely soft.
Rub the cooked plums through a sieve or fine colander.
Add the sugar, cloves, cinnamon, optional white wine, and 500 ml of water to the purée, and bring everything to a boil.
Serve with crispy croutons.

name: Zupa z jabłek lub gruszek (Apple or pear soup)
summary: A traditional fruit soup made from puréed apples or pears with cinnamon, raisins, and sour cream, served warm or chilled with croutons.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: approx. (a little more for apples, a little less for pears)

steps: Wash the apples or pears, cut into unpeeled quarters, and core them.
Transfer the fruit to a pot, cover with water, and simmer until completely tender.
Press the cooked fruit through a colander or sieve, discarding the skins.
Add the sugar, cinnamon, and optional raisins to the purée, stir in the sour cream, and bring to a boil.
Serve warm or chilled with croutons.

name: Zupa z głogu (Lithuanian-Polish hawthorn berry soup)
summary: A traditional Lithuanian-Polish fruit soup made from hawthorn berries stewed with white bread and sieved, finished with wine and cinnamon.

ingredients.name: kaiser rolls
ingredients.note: 2–3 rolls (or half a baguette), crusts removed

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the wine syrup (plus water to cook the hawthorn and rolls)

steps: Trim the crusts off the rolls, crumble the bread into a pot, add the hawthorn berries (fresh or dried), cover with water, and simmer until completely soft.
Mash the cooked hawthorn thoroughly with the bread and press the mixture through a fine sieve.
In a separate pot, boil 500 ml of water with the wine, sugar, and cinnamon.
Pour the hot wine syrup into the sieved hawthorn, stir thoroughly, and serve with croutons.

name: Roast bone-in pork loin stuffed with cabbage and apples (Schab nadziewany kapustą i jabłkami)
summary: Traditional roast pork loin with skin and bones, stuffed with scalded cabbage, tart apples, and sautéed onion.

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.note: part finely diced for stuffing, part sliced for topping

steps: Shred the cabbage, pour boiling water over it in a colander, and drain thoroughly.
Peel the tart apples and dice them finely or grate on a coarse box grater.
Finely chop one onion and sauté it in hot lard, then slice the other onion.
Toss the cabbage with the apples and sautéed onion, and season the stuffing with salt.
Make deep incisions in the pork loin, stuff the prepared filling beneath the skin and between the rib bones, and tie securely with kitchen string.
Transfer the meat to a roasting pan and roast for 120 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.
Baste the pork with the pan drippings 15 minutes before the end of roasting and arrange the remaining onion slices over the top.

name: Kiełbaski w piwie (sausages braised in beer)
summary: Small Polish sausages braised in pale beer with onion, butter, and capers, with breadcrumbs to thicken the sauce, following an old Polish recipe.
steps: Arrange the small Polish sausages in a saucepan and pour in 300 ml of pale beer.
Add the butter, crumbled bouillon cube, and sliced onion.
Heat everything over low heat, making sure the sausages do not burn.
Just before boiling, stir in the breadcrumbs and capers, mixing thoroughly until the sauce thickens slightly.

name: Puff pastry
summary: Classic multilayered puff pastry made with wheat flour, egg, water, and a generous amount of butter through repeated folding and rolling.
steps: Knead the wheat flour, egg, and water into a soft, moderately firm dough, shape into a ball, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Flatten the softened butter into a layer about 2 cm thick and chill it in the refrigerator.
Roll out the dough, place the butter block in the centre, fold the edges over envelope-style, and roll out to a thickness of 1 cm.
Rest the laminated dough in a cold place for 30–120 minutes.
Fold the dough into 3 layers, roll out again, and chill, repeating this folding process 4 to 6 times before baking at about 200 °C.

name: Kartofle zapiekane ze śledziem (Polish potato and herring bake)
summary: A casserole of potatoes boiled in their skins, herring, and sautéed onions, topped with breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: herring
ingredients.note: 2 whole salted herrings or 4 fillets in oil

steps: Boil the potatoes in their jackets with salt, let cool, peel, and cut into thin slices.
Soak the herrings if salted, debone, and finely chop the fillets.
Peel and chop the onions, and sauté in a tablespoon of butter.
Grease a baking dish with butter and layer the potatoes, herring, and sautéed onions.
Top with breadcrumbs and drizzle with remaining melted butter or sour cream.
Bake for 20–30 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Kartofle nadziewane grzybami (stuffed potatoes with wild mushrooms and leeks)
summary: Hollowed potatoes stuffed with forest mushrooms, leeks, and eggs, braised in butter and broth.
steps: Rinse the fresh or dried mushrooms, simmer until tender while reserving the cooking broth, and finely chop.
Chop the leeks and sauté them in a tablespoon of butter.
Combine the leeks with mushrooms, breadcrumbs, whole egg, and yolks, then season the stuffing with salt and pepper.
Wash and peel the potatoes, slice a thin flat piece off the bottom for stability, cut a larger lid off the top, and hollow out the center of each potato with a teaspoon.
Fill the hollowed potatoes with the mushroom stuffing, replace the potato lids, and arrange closely in a wide braising pot.
Pour over the remaining melted butter and broth combined with mushroom cooking liquid, cover, and braise until tender.

name: Kartofle zapiekane ze śmietaną (baked potatoes in sour cream and onions)
summary: Jacket-cooked potatoes sliced and baked with thick sour cream and sautéed onions.
steps: Boil potatoes in their jackets, let cool, peel, and cut into slices or cubes.
Chop the onion and sauté in butter.
Transfer potatoes and sautéed onion to a baking dish, season with salt, add sour cream, and toss gently.
Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C until the sour cream thickens and turns lightly golden.

name: Kaczka z jabłkami (Polish roast duck with apples and marjoram)
summary: Traditional Polish roast duck stuffed with tart apple quarters, seasoned with marjoram and caraway.
steps: Rinse and pat dry the duck, then rub inside and out with salt, caraway seeds, and marjoram.
Quarter the tart apples, stuff the duck cavity with them, and top with sliced onion.
Place the duck in a roasting pan and roast in the oven, basting initially with broth and later brushing with butter, turning frequently.
Mix the pan juices with the wheat flour and bring briefly to a boil.
Place the roasted duck on a platter, surround with apples, and drizzle with the thickened gravy.

name: Potrawka z kaczek z kapustą (duck fricassee with cabbage)
summary: Duck quarters simmered with root vegetables and spices, layered with white cabbage, and baked under a creamy dill sauce.
steps: Boil the heads of white cabbage in salted water, drain, and cut into quarters.
Quarter the ducks and cook until tender in water with the carrots, parsley root, leek, onion, allspice berries, and bay leaves.
Arrange the cooked duck portions in a baking dish alternating with the cabbage quarters, and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.

Sauté 1 tablespoon of plain flour with 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet, add the chopped dill, whisk in broth from cooking the ducks, stir in the sour cream, and cook for a few minutes, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens.
Pour the prepared sauce over the duck and cabbage and bake for about 15 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Gęś pieczona z jabłkami (roast goose with apples and caraway)
summary: Traditional roast goose rubbed with caraway and stuffed with tart apples and marjoram, served with baked apples and pan gravy.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: a dozen or so small apples for stuffing and a few larger apples to bake separately

steps: Wash and dry the goose, then rub it inside and out with salt and caraway seeds.
Stuff the goose cavity with the small tart apples and the sprig of marjoram, then sew the opening closed.
Peel and slice the onions, arranging them across the bottom of the roasting pan beneath the goose.
Roast the goose in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 2.5 hours, basting first with the broth and later with rendered pan juices; bake the larger apples separately toward the end of roasting.
Pour off the pan drippings, whisk with the flour, and simmer briefly until thickened into gravy.
Arrange the roast goose on a serving platter, surround with the large baked apples, and spoon some of the gravy over top.

name: Paszteciki z grzybami (baked mushroom pastries)
summary: Baked butter-pastry parcels filled with a thick filling of dried mushrooms, onion, and sour cream.
steps: Boil the dried mushrooms until tender, drain well, and finely chop.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the finely chopped onion and flour, and sauté lightly.
Add the chopped mushrooms and sour cream, season with salt and pepper, cook until the filling thickens, and let cool.
Roll out the butter pastry, cut out small rounds or squares, spoon a portion of filling onto each, fold in half, and crimp the edges.
Sprinkle the pastries with breadcrumbs and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 15–20 minutes.

name: Ciasto na pierogi (pierogi dough)
summary: Soft, elastic homemade pierogi dough made with flour, scalded with hot water, and finished with cold water and egg.
steps: Sift the wheat flour into a large mixing bowl and combine with the salt.
Gradually pour in the hot water while stirring with a wooden spoon, then leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Add the cold water and egg, mix with the spoon, and let rest again for 10 minutes.
Turn the dough onto a floured board and knead by hand for about 5 minutes until soft and supple.
Roll the dough out thinly, cut out circles with a glass, spoon filling into the centres, pinch the edges closed, and boil the pierogi in salted boiling water until they float.

name: Uszka dumplings for borscht (Uszka do barszczu)
summary: Small dumplings for borscht filled with cooked beef, dried mushrooms, and onion fried in butter.
steps: Pass the cooked beef through a meat grinder or chop it very finely.
Peel and chop the onion, then fry it in a tablespoon of butter.
Add the ground beef, finely chopped cooked mushrooms, and a few tablespoons of mushroom broth to the onion.
Add a handful of breadcrumbs, crack in two eggs, season with salt and pepper, and mix the filling thoroughly.
Cut the thinly rolled dough into small squares, place a teaspoon of filling on each, fold diagonally into a triangle, pinch the edges firmly, and join two opposite corners together.
Cook the uszka in salted boiling water until they float to the surface.

name: Paszteciki z rybą (puff pastry fish pasties)
summary: Flaky puff pastry pasties filled with fish sautéed with onion and chopped hard-boiled eggs.
steps: Finely chop the fish and season with salt and pepper.
Chop the onions and fry in melted butter, then add the fish and sauté together for about 5 minutes.
Let the cooked fish and onion cool, chop finely, and combine with the finely diced hard-boiled eggs.
Roll out the puff pastry and cut out an even number of rounds with a glass, cutting a smaller hole in the centre of half of them using a small shot glass.
Brush the solid rounds with beaten raw egg, top with portions of fish filling, cover with the rounds with holes in the centre, and seal the edges firmly.
Bake the pasties in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 10–15 minutes until golden brown.

name: Kapusta z grzybami (braised fresh cabbage and sauerkraut with forest mushrooms).
summary: Braised white cabbage and sauerkraut with dried forest mushrooms, butter roux, and caramelized sugar.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking mushrooms and cooking cabbage

steps: Soak the dried forest mushrooms in water for at least 60 minutes.
Shred the white cabbage, cook in salted water for 30 minutes, and drain.
Add the sauerkraut and soaked mushrooms, cover, and cook gently for another 30 minutes, adding the mushroom soaking liquid as needed.
Cook butter and wheat flour in a skillet to make a roux and caramelize the sugar.
Stir the roux and caramelized sugar into the cabbage and season with salt and pepper.

name: Pierogi z kapustą i grzybami (sauerkraut and mushroom pierogi)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve pierogi stuffed with braised sauerkraut, dried forest mushrooms, and a rich dark roux.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking mushrooms and boiling sauerkraut and pierogi

steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in water for at least 60 minutes.
Squeeze excess brine from the sauerkraut, place in a pot, cover with water, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Drain the sauerkraut, add the chopped mushrooms and a tablespoon of butter, and braise covered for another 30 minutes.
Make a dark roux with the remaining tablespoon of butter and flour, stir into the cabbage and mushrooms, and allow the filling to cool.
Roll out the pierogi dough thinly, cut out rounds with a glass, place a spoonful of filling on each, fold in half, and seal the edges firmly.
Boil the pierogi in batches in salted boiling water until they float to the surface.

name: Krokiety z kapustą i grzybami (Polish croquettes with sauerkraut and mushrooms)
summary: Traditional crêpe croquettes stuffed with sauerkraut and dried mushrooms and coated in egg and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking mushrooms and boiling sauerkraut

steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in water for at least 60 minutes.
Squeeze excess brine from the sauerkraut, place in a large pot, cover with water, and boil for 30 minutes.
Drain the cooking water from the sauerkraut, add the chopped soaked mushrooms and 1 tablespoon of butter, and braise for another 30 minutes.
Prepare a brown roux with the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and the flour, then stir it into the sauerkraut towards the end of braising.
Spoon 2–3 tablespoons of filling onto each crêpe, fold two opposing edges inward, and roll up tightly.
Dredge the croquettes in beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden brown.

name: Krokiety z mięsem (Polish meat-filled crêpe croquettes)
summary: Crêpe croquettes stuffed with minced cooked or roasted meat and sautéed onion, coated in egg and breadcrumbs.
steps: Pass the cooked or roasted meat through a meat grinder or mince it very finely.
Finely dice the onion, cook until translucent in the butter or oil, then add the ground meat and season the filling with salt and pepper.
Place 2–3 tablespoons of filling onto each crêpe, fold two sides inward, and roll into a cylinder.
Coat the croquettes in beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes on each side.

name: Pierogi ruskie (potato and cheese dumplings)
summary: Classic Polish pierogi filled with mashed potatoes, farmer's cheese (quark) and onions cooked in butter until translucent, seasoned with freshly ground black pepper.
steps: Peel the potatoes, boil until tender in salted water, drain, and mash into a smooth puree.
Peel and finely dice the onions, then cook until translucent in melted butter.
Combine the mashed potatoes with the cooked onions and crumbled quark, then season with salt, black pepper, and pressed garlic.
Roll out the pierogi dough thinly, cut out rounds with a drinking glass, place a tablespoon of filling on each, fold in half, and pinch the edges together.
Drop the pierogi into salted boiling water and cook until they float to the surface.

name: Paszteciki z mięsem (beef-filled sour cream pastries)
summary: Shortcrust pastries made with sour cream dough and filled with cooked beef, onion, and butter.
steps: Mince the cooked beef in a meat grinder or chop it very finely, and mix with the melted butter.
Grate the onion, blanch it with boiling water, drain well, and add to the beef along with the broth and optional breadcrumbs.
Let the meat mixture cool, beat in 2 eggs, season with salt and pepper, and mix thoroughly.
In a bowl, mix the sour cream with the sifted flour, knead into a smooth dough on a pastry board, and divide into walnut-sized balls.
Flatten each ball and roll gently into a small round or oval disc.
Place a portion of filling onto each disc, fold in the sides, and pinch the edges firmly closed at the top.
Arrange the pastries on a buttered baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 15–20 minutes.

name: Ciasto drożdżowe (Polish sweet yeast cake)
summary: A traditional sweet yeast dough made with milk, egg yolks, and butter, suitable for a cake, babka, or buns.
steps: Warm the milk slightly, sift the flour with salt into a bowl, and make a well in the centre.
Crumble the fresh yeast into the well, add a pinch of sugar, pour in some warm milk, stir with a little flour, and leave the starter for 15–20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and beat the egg yolks with the remaining sugar until pale.
Combine the flour and risen starter with the beaten egg yolks and remaining warm milk, kneading into a smooth dough.
Work in the melted butter and vegetable oil, knead until the dough comes away cleanly from your hands, shape into a ball, cover, and let rise for 30–120 minutes.
Punch down the dough, knead in the raisins, transfer to a baking tin, brush the top with egg white, and bake for 40 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.

name: Kulebiak z mięsem (Meat coulibiac)
summary: Hearty Polish meat pie enclosed in yeast or butter pastry, layered with minced meat, sautéed onions, broth, and chopped hard-boiled eggs.

ingredients.name: roasted or boiled meat (such as veal, pork, or beef)

steps: Chop the onion and cook until translucent in the butter.
Pass the meat through a meat grinder, add to the onion, pour in the broth, season with salt and pepper, and braise for several minutes.
Cool the meat filling and pass it through the grinder a second time or mince it very finely.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool, peel, and dice finely.
Roll out the pastry to a thickness of about 1 cm, spread a layer of meat over it, cover with a layer of chopped eggs, and finish with another layer of meat.
Fold the pastry over the filling, seal the edges securely, and bake in a well-heated oven for about 50 minutes.

name: Kulebiak z rybą (Fish coulibiac)
summary: Baked coulibiac made with yeast dough and filled with fried fish, onion, hard-boiled eggs, and rice.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: hard-boiled; listed in the preparation instructions

steps: Chop the onion and sauté in the butter. Fry the fish, let it cool, remove all bones, and finely chop together with the onion.
Hard-boil the eggs and dice finely, and cook the rice until fluffy.
Combine the chopped fish with the diced eggs and rice, and season the filling with salt and pepper.
Roll out the yeast dough to a thickness of about 1 cm, spread over the fish filling, and top with sprats or sardines if using.
Enclose the filling in the dough, seal the edges securely, and bake in a well-heated oven for about 50 minutes.

name: Kulebiak ze słodką kapustą (Cabbage and egg coulibiac)
summary: Coulibiac made with yeast dough or puff pastry, filled with cooked white cabbage, sautéed onion, and hard-boiled eggs.
steps: Cut the head of cabbage into quarters and boil in salted water until tender.
Drain and squeeze excess liquid from the cabbage, remove the core, and finely chop the leaves.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool, peel, and dice finely. Finely chop the onion and sauté in the butter.
Combine the chopped cabbage with the diced eggs and buttered onions, then season the filling with salt and pepper.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1 cm, spread the cabbage filling over, fold the dough over, and seal the edges securely.
Bake the coulibiac in a well-heated oven for about 50 minutes.

name: Kulebiak z kwaśną kapustą (Sauerkraut and fish coulibiac)
summary: Baked Polish yeast pastry loaf stuffed with braised sauerkraut, sautéed onions, and tender pan-fried fish.
steps: Rinse the sauerkraut, squeeze dry, and chop finely.
Finely chop the onion, sauté in the butter, add the sauerkraut, season with pepper, and braise together until the cabbage is tender.
Debone the fish, cut into small pieces, season with salt, pan-fry separately, and fold into the braised sauerkraut.
Roll out the yeast dough to a thickness of about 1 cm, spread over the sauerkraut and fish filling, fold the dough over, and seal the edges securely.
Bake the coulibiac in a well-heated oven for about 50 minutes.

name: Kasza gryczana z fetą (buckwheat groats with feta, sun-dried tomatoes, and olives)
summary: Fluffy buckwheat groats tossed with feta cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, black olives, and parsley leaves.
steps: Pour hot water over the buckwheat groats, add salt and butter, and cook with lid slightly ajar over very low heat for 15 minutes without stirring.
Remove the pot from the heat and leave covered for 10–30 minutes until the groats absorb all the liquid.
Dice the feta cheese, slice sun-dried tomatoes into thin strips, and cut black olives into rings.
Finely chop the parsley leaves and fold all ingredients into the warm buckwheat with olive oil.

name: Nigiri sushi (tuna nigiri sushi)
summary: Classic Japanese nigiri with seasoned sushi rice mounds topped with thin slices of raw tuna and a dab of wasabi.
steps: Shape the prepared sushi rice into small oblong mounds.
Lay a slice of tuna in the palm of your hand and swipe a touch of wasabi paste down its centre.
Place a rice mound onto the fish and press gently so that the fish and rice adhere closely.
Turn the sushi piece fish side up, neaten the edges, and press gently again to shape.
Repeat with the remaining rice and tuna, and serve the finished nigiri with soy sauce.

name: Buckwheat Blini (Russian bliny gryczane)
summary: Traditional Russian yeast pancakes made with buckwheat flour, scalded with hot milk and fried in melted butter.
steps: 5–6 hours before frying, mix the buckwheat flour, 750 ml of warm milk or water, dry yeast, 2 egg yolks, and 1 tablespoon of melted butter, beat with a whisk, and set in a warm place for 2–3 hours to rise.
Beat the risen batter again, stir in the salt and sugar, pour in the remaining 500 ml of hot milk or water, and beat thoroughly.
Gently fold in the egg whites whipped to stiff peaks and leave the batter to rise once more.
Without stirring the risen batter, ladle spoonfuls onto a heated small skillet.
When the blini begin to puff and brown on the bottom, drizzle with the remaining melted butter, flip over, and finish cooking.

name: Wheat Blini (Russian bliny pszenne)
summary: Fluffy Russian yeast pancakes made with coarse wheat flour, enriched with whipped egg whites and whipped cream.
steps: Dissolve the sugar, salt, and dry yeast in 375 ml of warm milk, add 560 ml of coarse wheat flour, mix thoroughly, and leave covered in a warm place to rise.
Once the sponge has risen, add 2 egg yolks and the remaining 190 ml of flour, adjusting the consistency with the rest of the milk.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, separately whip the heavy cream, fold both gently into the batter, and let rise again in a warm place.
Without stirring the risen batter, ladle portions onto a heated small skillet.
When the blini rise and brown on the bottom, drizzle with melted butter, flip, and fry until golden.

name: Red cabbage and apple salad (Surówka z czerwonej kapusty)
summary: A simple salad of shredded red cabbage, tart apples, and fermented pickles dressed with vegetable oil.
steps: Remove the outer leaves from the red cabbage, wash the head, and shred finely.
Peel the tart apples and dice them or grate on a coarse grater.
Dice the fermented pickles.
Mix all ingredients together, drizzle with oil, and season to taste with salt.

name: Oładki (oladyi / thick yeast pancakes)
summary: Thick, fluffy East Slavic yeast pancakes spooned into the pan and fried in butter or lard until golden.
steps: Add the flour to a bowl, pour in the warm milk, eggs, fresh yeast, and salt, and stir into a thick batter.
Cover the bowl and set the batter in a warm place to rise.
Melt a portion of butter or lard in a frying pan.
Scoop spoonfuls of risen batter from the edge of the bowl using a large spoon dipped in the melted fat, dropping oblong mounds into the pan.
Fry the oladyi on both sides until golden brown and cooked through.

name: Parówki w cieście (battered fried frankfurters)
summary: Frankfurters dipped in a thick egg-and-flour batter and fried in hot oil until golden and crisp.
steps: Whisk the eggs into the water, then gradually beat in the flour and salt until a smooth batter slightly thicker than crepe batter forms.
Heat the oil in a frying pan, dip each frankfurter into the batter, and lower into the hot fat.
Fry the frankfurters for 2 minutes, turning them over, until the batter is evenly golden brown.

name: Battered fried zucchini
summary: Tender zucchini rounds coated in a thick, simple batter of flour and eggs, fried until golden and crisp.
steps: Wash and slice the zucchini into rounds, season with salt, let stand for 30 minutes, and pat dry with paper towels.
Whisk the eggs into the water, then gradually beat in the flour and a pinch of salt to form a batter slightly thicker than pancake batter.
Heat the oil in a frying pan, dip the zucchini slices into the batter, and fry for 1.5–2 minutes on each side until crisp and golden.

name: Buckwheat and Wheat Blini (Bliny pszenno-gryczane)
summary: Russian yeast pancakes made with a blend of wheat and buckwheat flours, scalded with hot milk before frying.
steps: 5–6 hours before frying, mix the wheat flour, water, dry yeast, and 1 tablespoon of melted butter, beat the batter, and leave in a warm place for 2–3 hours to rise.
Beat the risen dough again, stir in the salt, sugar, and buckwheat flour, and let rise once more.
60 minutes before frying, pour in the hot milk, mix thoroughly, and allow the batter to rise.
Without stirring the batter, ladle onto a hot skillet, drizzle with the remaining melted butter as the blini brown, and flip to finish cooking.

name: Yeast-Free Blini (Quick buckwheat and wheat pancakes)
summary: Quick Russian blini made with buckwheat and wheat flour, leavened with baking soda instead of yeast.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 4.5–5 glasses warm water plus 0.5 glass cold

steps: In a bowl, mix together the wheat flour, buckwheat flour, salt, sugar, and 1.2 litres of warm water into a smooth batter.
Just before frying, dissolve the baking soda in the remaining 125 ml of cold water and stir briefly into the batter.
Ladle spoonfuls of batter onto a heated small skillet, and when the blini puff and brown on the bottom, drizzle with melted butter and flip over.

name: Viennese cheesecake in chocolate (Sernik wiedeński w czekoladzie)
summary: A crustless baked Viennese cheesecake with mixed dried fruit and nuts, coated in dark chocolate and served with sour cherry preserve.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: part for the batter, a little for greasing the tin

steps: Pass the farmer's cheese through a mincer three times, beat it with the egg yolks and softened butter, then mix in the vanilla pudding powder and mixed dried fruit and nuts.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt and the icing sugar until stiff, then gently fold into the cheese batter.
Grease a springform tin with butter and dust with breadcrumbs, pour in the batter, and bake in an oven preheated to 170 °C for 75 minutes.
Melt the broken dark chocolate in a water bath and pour it over the baked cheesecake.
Serve slices of the cheesecake with sour cherry preserve.

name: Pork loin skewers (Szaszłyki ze schabu)
summary: Baked skewers of pork loin chunks, new potatoes wrapped in pork belly, red bell pepper, and grapes.
steps: Peel the baby potatoes and parboil in salted water until half-tender, then drain.
Rinse the pork loin and cut into large cubes. Rub the potatoes and meat with a mixture of olive oil, ground paprika, salt, and pepper, then leave in a cool place for 30 minutes.
Wrap the parboiled potatoes in slices of pork belly, and cut the red bell pepper into chunks.
Thread the pork belly-wrapped potatoes, pork loin cubes, grapes, and bell pepper alternately onto skewers.
Cook the skewers on a preheated grill or in the oven for about 15 minutes, turning every few minutes to cook all sides.

name: Avocado Stuffed with Hard-Boiled Egg Salad
summary: Avocado halves stuffed with a fresh salad of hard-boiled eggs, ripe tomatoes, chives, and mayonnaise.
steps: Wash the avocado, cut in half lengthwise, remove the pit, and scoop out the flesh leaving a half-centimetre rim next to the skin.
Dice the avocado flesh and toss it, along with the hollowed shells, with lemon juice to prevent discoloration.
Dice the hard-boiled eggs and tomatoes, and finely snip the rinsed and dried chives.
Gently combine the avocado with the eggs, tomatoes, chives, and mayonnaise, season with salt and pepper, and spoon the salad into the fruit halves.

name: Naleśniki (basic Polish crepes)
summary: Basic thin Polish crepes made with plain flour, water, and eggs, fried in a hot oiled skillet.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, pour in the water, and whisk together.
Gradually add the flour and salt while whisking continuously, until a smooth, lump-free batter with the consistency of sour cream forms.
Stir a splash of oil into the batter and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat a thin film of oil in a frying pan and ladle in portions of batter, tilting the pan to coat the surface evenly.
Fry thin crepes on both sides until golden.

name: Karkówka pieczona (Polish roast pork neck with caraway and marjoram)
summary: Pork neck steaks seared and slow-roasted with onions, caraway, and marjoram in broth.
steps: Rinse and pat dry the pork neck steaks, then rub with salt, ground caraway, and marjoram.
Sear the meat in hot oil on both sides until golden brown.
Arrange the pork steaks in a roasting pan and scatter finely chopped onions over them.
Bake in an oven preheated to 150 °C for about 90 minutes, basting occasionally with broth.

name: Chicken with pineapple in soy sauce
summary: Chicken breast strips stir-fried with canned pineapple chunks, ginger, and soy sauce, bound with potato starch.

ingredients.name: canned pineapple with its packing liquid

steps: Rinse and trim the chicken fillets, slice into strips, and fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Add the chopped pineapple, reserving its packing liquid, along with the ginger and soy sauce, and fry, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Mix about 190 ml of the pineapple packing liquid with the potato starch, pour into the pan, and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens.

name: Naleśnikowy tort warzywny (savoury vegetable crepe cake)
summary: A savoury baked crepe cake layered with thick tomato sauce, spinach gently cooked with garlic, leek, and semi-hard cheese.
steps: Finely chop one onion and 3 cloves of garlic, and sauté in heated olive oil.
Add the canned tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, simmer over low heat until the sauce is very thick, and stir in the oregano at the end.
Finely slice the leek, blanch it in boiling water until slightly softened, and drain.
Chop the remaining onion and garlic, cook gently with the spinach in a covered pan, and season with salt and pepper.
Grate the cheese, then layer the crepes in a springform tin alternately with spinach, tomato sauce, grated cheese, and leek, finishing with a crepe topped with sauce and cheese.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 10 minutes, until the cheese on top is fully melted.

name: Roladki z warzywami (turkey roulades with vegetables)
summary: Braised turkey escalope rolls spread with mustard, stuffed with pork belly, zucchini and carrot strips, and parsley leaves.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the vegetables, 1 tbsp for searing the rolls

steps: Peel the zucchini and carrots, slice lengthwise into strips, sauté in 1 tablespoon of butter, add the broth, and braise for 5 minutes.
Pound the turkey cutlets lightly, season with salt and pepper, and spread with mustard.
Place two slices of pork belly, the braised vegetable strips, and chopped parsley leaves onto each meat slice.
Roll the meat tightly into roulades so the ends of the vegetables stick out slightly, and secure with toothpicks.
Sear the rolls on all sides in the remaining butter and oil, add a splash of water, and simmer covered for 20–30 minutes.

name: Ciasto ze śliwkami (Polish plum cake)
summary: A butter cake topped with halved węgierka plums (prune plums).
steps: Wash and dry the węgierka plums, halve each one, and remove the stones.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form, then gradually beat in the icing sugar followed by the egg yolks one by one.

Melt the butter in a saucepan, mix the wheat flour with the baking powder, and add alternating spoonfuls of butter and flour to the egg mixture along with the vanilla flavouring, stirring continuously.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin, arrange the plum halves on top skin-side down, and bake for 50 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.

name: Adjika (Caucasian spiced pepper and tomato relish)
summary: An aromatic Caucasian vegetable relish made from red bell peppers, ripe tomatoes, carrots, tart apples, and garlic.
steps: Rinse the tomatoes, carrots, apples, and red bell peppers thoroughly, peel the carrots, apples, and garlic, and remove the seeds from the peppers.
Pass the tomatoes, carrots, apples, bell peppers, and garlic through a meat grinder.
Transfer the minced vegetable mixture to a large pot and simmer over low heat for 120 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped hot chili peppers, oil, sugar, vinegar, and salt, stir well, and cook for about 30 minutes more.

name: Samfaina (Catalan braised vegetables)
summary: A Catalan vegetable dish of aubergine, courgette, red bell pepper, tomatoes, onion, and garlic gently cooked in olive oil.
steps: Dice the onion and crush the garlic, then cut the courgette and aubergine into cubes.
Score the skins of the tomatoes, scald in boiling water, plunge into cold water, peel, and dice the pulp.
Remove the seeds from the red bell peppers and slice into thin strips.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot, add the onion, garlic, aubergine, and courgette, stir well, and braise covered for about 10 minutes.
Uncover the pot, stir in the tomatoes and bell peppers, season with salt and pepper, and simmer gently uncovered until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens.

name: Potjiekos (South African layered stew)
summary: South African one-pot layered stew of mutton neck, bacon, onion, potatoes, and cabbage, slow-cooked without stirring.
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a cast-iron Dutch oven or potjie pot, add the diced onion, bacon, and mutton neck pieces, and fry for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Layer the cut potatoes over the meat, top with cabbage wedges, pour over the water mixed with lemon juice, and season with meat spices, salt, and pepper, without stirring the layers.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and simmer over very low heat for about 120 minutes, adding a little water if needed, until the meat is falling off the bone.
Just before serving, stir the contents of the pot thoroughly.

name: Chleb na pyrach (Greater Poland sourdough potato bread)
summary: A traditional sourdough rye bread from Greater Poland made with cooked mashed potatoes and yeast, yielding a dense, moist loaf.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1.5–2.5 l water, buttermilk, or soured milk

steps: Pour part of the water over the sourdough starter and leave in a warm spot for 1440 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, boil until tender, mash thoroughly, and pour in the remaining water.
Add some of the rye flour and the yeast to the potatoes, mix the resulting loose sponge with the prepared sourdough starter, and leave overnight.
Gradually add the remaining rye flour, knead the dough thoroughly, and leave in a warm spot to rise for about 180 minutes.
Shape into a loaf and bake for 120 minutes in a preheated oven.

name: Chleb na młodziach (Old Polish yeast bread)
summary: A rustic yeast bread prepared according to an Old Polish recipe using warmed flour and milk.
steps: Mix the warmed dry flour with the milk and yeast.
Add salt, knead the dough, and leave in a warm place to rise.
Shape loaves on a pastry board and set aside for a second rise.
Place the risen loaves into a hot oven and bake until the crust is crisp and golden brown, brushing the top with water during baking.

name: Chleb na ziemniakach (Polish potato bread with coriander)
summary: Homemade yeast bread made with wheat flour, mashed potatoes, milk, and ground coriander.
steps: Peel the potatoes, boil until tender, drain, steam off moisture, and mash thoroughly.
Combine the wheat flour with salt and ground coriander, pour in the yeast dissolved in 100 ml of lukewarm water, and set aside for the sponge to rise.
Warm the milk with the remaining 200 ml of water, add along with the potatoes to the flour, and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and leave to rise for 90 minutes, then knead it again and shape a loaf on a baking sheet or in a baking tin.
Rest for 10 minutes, then bake the bread in an oven preheated to 225 °C for 45 minutes.

name: Chleb wiejski (Greater Poland country whey rye bread)
summary: A large-batch traditional Polish country rye bread kneaded with whey and whole milk, baked into rustic hearth loaves.
steps: Knead a dough from 12 kg of rye flour, the whey, whole milk, and yeast, and leave in a warm spot to rise for 300 minutes.
Add the remaining 4 kg of rye flour and salt, knead the dough again, and rest for 30 minutes.
Shape the risen dough into 4 loaves, wait 15 minutes, and bake in a hot oven.

name: Chleb żytni (rye bread with whey)
summary: A traditional Polish rye loaf made on an overnight yeast and whey pre-ferment, creating a deep flavour and hearty crumb.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in whey with a portion of the rye flour, cover, and leave in a warm place overnight.
Add the remaining rye flour to the risen pre-ferment, knead into a thick dough, and set aside to rise.
Divide the risen dough into portions, shape loaves, arrange on a baking sheet, and rest briefly in a warm spot.
Bake the loaves for 120 minutes, then sprinkle the hot bread with cooled boiled water after removing it from the oven.

name: Chleb z dyni (Greater Poland sourdough pumpkin rye bread)
summary: A hearty Polish sourdough rye bread enriched with cooked pumpkin purée and buttermilk for moisture and golden colour.
steps: Boil the pumpkin until tender, then rub through a sieve or blend with buttermilk.
Add part of the rye flour, rye sourdough starter, and yeast to the pumpkin, stir, and leave overnight (720 minutes).
Add the remaining rye flour, knead the dough thoroughly, and set aside to rise for 120–180 minutes.
Shape into loaves and bake in a preheated oven for 90 minutes.

name: Chlebki twarożkowe (small farmer's cheese loaves)
summary: Quick little bread rolls made from a farmer's cheese dough with baking powder.
steps: Sift the plain flour with the baking powder, add the farmer's cheese, butter, and some of the egg (reserving a little yolk for brushing), and knead thoroughly.
Chill the kneaded dough in a cool place for about 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into a log, slice into equal portions, and shape each into a small loaf.
Arrange the rolls on a greased baking sheet, brush the tops with the reserved egg yolk, and bake in a preheated oven until golden brown.

name: Chleb w cieście (savory Polish bread in egg batter)
summary: Slices of stale bread dipped into a light pancake-style egg batter and pan-fried golden and crisp.
steps: Separate the egg yolks from the whites, then whisk the yolks with milk, salt, and plain flour into a thin pancake-style batter.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold into the prepared batter.
Dip the thin slices of stale bread into the batter and fry on both sides in hot cooking fat until golden brown.

name: Chleb turecki (sweet honey bread, also called żulik)
summary: A sweet Polish yeast bread enriched with honey, milk, raisins, and almonds, traditionally known in Łódź as żulik.
steps: Sift and gently warm the plain flour, then mix the yeast with natural honey, half of the milk, and a little flour, setting aside to rise.
Beat the eggs with sugar (reserving a little egg for brushing), pour in the remaining milk, combine with the risen sponge, and knead with the rest of the flour.
Gradually incorporate the melted butter while kneading thoroughly, finishing with the raisins and salt.
Shape the dough into logs, place them into greased loaf tins up to 3/4 of their height, cover, and rest in a warm place for 60 minutes to rise.
Brush the risen loaves with the reserved egg beaten with a little milk, sprinkle with ground almonds, and bake in a thoroughly preheated oven.

name: Chleb razowy z ziarnami (seeded wholemeal sourdough bread)
summary: A hearty Polish sourdough loaf made from spelt or wholegrain flour packed with sunflower, pumpkin, and sesame seeds, flaxseed, oats, walnuts, and prunes.

ingredients.name: spelt flour
ingredients.note: or 1.25 l wholewheat flour and 750 ml wholemeal rye flour

steps: Prepare the sourdough starter by mixing a portion of dough from the previous bake with water and resting for 1440 minutes.
Combine the water, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, rolled oats, flaxseed, wheat bran, buckwheat groats, walnuts, prunes, soaked raisins, salt, honey, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the spelt flour and sourdough starter and mix to form a thick dough.
Divide the dough between two loaf tins lined with baking paper and leave overnight to rise.
Bake the bread in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 90–105 minutes, and after unmoulding, brush the hot loaves with water.

name: Kotlety wieprzowe w śmietanie (pork cutlets braised with potatoes in sour cream)
summary: Pork cutlets braised and baked over sliced potatoes with onion, garlic, bell peppers, and sour cream.
steps: Rinse the pork cutlets, pound with a mallet, season with salt, and brown on both sides in hot fat, then remove from the pan.
In the same fat, sauté the finely chopped onion and crushed garlic, add a splash of water, stir in the ground sweet paprika and chopped green bell pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices, and transfer to the pan with the onion.
Arrange the browned cutlets over the potatoes and braise, covered, until tender.
Towards the end of braising, pour in 250 ml of sour cream, shake the pan gently, then transfer the dish to a preheated oven and bake briefly.

name: Bobotie (South African spiced minced beef bake)
summary: A traditional South African baked dish of spiced minced beef, dried fruit and nuts, topped with an egg and milk mixture.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C, and brown the chopped onion, garlic, green bell pepper, grated carrot, and apple in a pan with oil or butter.
Soak the slices of bread in the milk, then squeeze dry, saving the leftover milk for later.
Combine the minced beef with the fried vegetables, squeezed bread, 1 egg, curry, turmeric, cinnamon, coriander, sugar, 9 ml salt, pepper, vinegar or lemon juice, almonds, raisins, and chutney.
Transfer the meat mixture to a baking dish, tuck the rolled bay or lemon leaves upright into the surface, and bake for 40 minutes at 180 °C.
Beat the remaining egg with the reserved milk and the rest of the salt, pour over the casserole, and bake for another 20 minutes.

name: Jajecznica po bacowsku (Highlander scrambled eggs with oscypek and wholemeal croutons)
summary: Highlander scrambled eggs cooked in fatback with wholemeal bread croutons, grated oscypek cheese, and lovage.
steps: Cut the slices of wholemeal bread into small cubes.
Whisk the eggs thoroughly with the milk, ground lovage, and grated oscypek cheese.
Finely dice the fatback, render in a skillet, and lightly brown the bread cubes in the rendered fat.
Pour in the egg mixture, add salt, cook over low heat while stirring until softly set, and sprinkle with chopped lovage or parsley leaves.

name: Zorba's delight (pork and bean stew)
summary: Greek pork and white bean stew braised with onions in tomato juice and olive oil, garnished with fresh parsley leaves.
steps: Cut the pork into bite-sized pieces and finely chop the large onion.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, brown the meat with the onion until golden, then pour in the tomato juice and simmer covered for 40–50 minutes.
Boil the white beans separately for 5 minutes, drain, and add to the simmering meat.
Add 250 ml of water to the pot and simmer until the liquid reduces and the sauce thickens, then sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Ryż po myśliwsku (hunter's style baked rice with chicken and mushrooms)
summary: A casserole of broth-cooked rice, chicken browned in hunter's seasoning and gently stewed mushrooms, baked under a sour cream and firm cheese topping.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying, 2 tbsp for the rice, for greasing the dish, and shavings for topping

steps: Peel the large onion, finely chop it, and cook in heated butter until translucent without browning.
Clean the button mushrooms, slice them, add to the onion, and cook gently covered over low heat until tender.
Dice the chicken fillets, sprinkle with salt, coat in the hunter's seasoning blend, and brown in butter.
Cook the rice in broth prepared from the vegetable stock cube, drain well, and toss with 2 tablespoons of butter.
Combine the rice with the browned chicken and gently stewed mushrooms and onion, then transfer everything to a greased baking dish.
Mix the sour cream with the grated firm cheese and chopped parsley, pour over the casserole, and dot the top with cold butter shavings.
Bake in a well-preheated oven at 180 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Sałatka gyros (Polish layered chicken gyros salad)
summary: A popular Polish layered salad with pan-fried gyros-spiced chicken breast, cucumbers, sweetcorn, chickpeas, tomatoes, and crisp napa cabbage.

ingredients.name: vinegar pickles or fermented brine pickles

steps: Dice the chicken breast, coat in gyros seasoning blend, fry in a skillet for 10–15 minutes, and let cool.
Shred the napa cabbage, dice the cucumbers, and slice or dice the tomatoes.
Spread the cooled chicken pieces across the bottom of a salad bowl and spread over a few tablespoons of ketchup.
Arrange the next layers: diced cucumbers, drained sweetcorn, and optionally the drained chickpeas.
Spread a layer of mayonnaise over the top, arrange the tomatoes, and cover everything with the shredded napa cabbage.
Season the top with salt and pepper and optionally drizzle with olive oil.

name: Sernik z rosą (dewdrop cheesecake)
summary: A classic Polish cheesecake on shortcrust pastry, with a runny farmer's cheese and milk filling and an egg-white topping that develops dewdrops after baking.
steps: Knead the plain flour, baking powder, 2 egg yolks, 1 whole egg, and margarine into a smooth dough, then press it evenly into the base and sides of a baking tin.
Mince the farmer's cheese twice, then blend it with the oil, milk, sugar, pudding powder, 2 whole eggs, 4 egg yolks, and lemon flavouring.
Pour the liquid cheese mixture over the prepared crust and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 50 minutes.
Whip the 6 egg whites until stiff peaks form, gradually beating in the sugar.
Spread the egg-white topping over the partially baked cheesecake and bake for another 15 minutes at 180 °C, then leave to cool until dewdrops appear on the surface.

name: Bajaderka (Polish chocolate rum cake slice)
summary: A homemade layered cake with jam and a filling of crumbled shortcrust pastry, milk, cocoa, rum, dried fruit, and nuts.
steps: Knead a shortcrust pastry from the wheat flour, butter, powdered sugar, eggs, and baking powder, divide into two halves, and bake into two cake layers at 180 °C.
Finely crumble one of the baked layers while it is still hot, then mix with the milk, cocoa, rum, dried fruit, and nuts until evenly combined.
Spread jam over the second baked layer, then spread the prepared dried fruit and nut mixture evenly over the top.

name: Sałatka kebabowa (kebab-spiced meat salad with garlic sauce)
summary: A satisfying kebab-style salad with spiced pork or chicken strips, lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and a garlic-yogurt sauce.
steps: Mix together the sweet paprika, hot chilli powder, herbes de Provence, and 4 tablespoons of oil or olive oil.
Cut the meat into thin strips, coat thoroughly in the prepared marinade, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Fry the marinated meat over high heat in the hot oil until cooked through.
Tear the lettuce leaves into pieces, cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the cucumber and onions thinly, and combine the vegetables in a bowl.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the plain yogurt, stir in the pressed garlic, and season the sauce with salt and pepper.
Toss the chopped vegetables with the garlic sauce and three-quarters of the cooked meat, then scatter the remaining meat over the top.

name: Provençal almond and orange torte (Tort prowansalski)
summary: An almond and orange sponge cake layered with a rich almond butter cream flavoured with strong coffee and orange liqueur.
steps: Separate the yolks from the whites of six eggs, beat the yolks with 250 g of sugar and the juice of two oranges, then mix in 250 g of ground almonds.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, dust with the potato starch, and gently fold into the almond mixture.
Transfer the batter to a springform cake tin and bake for 30 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C, and once completely cooled, slice horizontally in half.

Beat the butter until fluffy, adding 150 g of ground almonds, the remaining sugar, and three egg yolks previously beaten with some sugar, then pour in the strong coffee and orange liqueur while continuing to beat.
Spread most of the cream between the sponge layers, coat the top with the rest, and decorate with mandarin segments.

name: Chłodnik litewski (Lithuanian cold beetroot soup)
summary: The classic summer cold soup of young beet greens, beetroots, cucumbers, radishes, and fresh dill blended with kefir and plain yogurt.

ingredients.name: young beet greens with baby beetroots

steps: Finely chop the young beet greens and baby beetroots, cut the peeled beetroot into thin strips, add a little water, boil for about 20 minutes, and leave to cool.
Peel and finely dice the cucumbers, slice the radishes, chop the dill, and press the garlic.
Combine the cooled broth, including the beetroot and beet greens, with the kefir and plain yogurt.
Add the cucumbers, radishes, dill, and garlic, season with salt and black pepper, stir well, and chill in the refrigerator before serving.

name: Couscous with eggplant and tomatoes
summary: Vegetarian couscous tossed with olive-oil-braised eggplant slices, onions, canned diced tomatoes, and fresh parsley.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 2–3 tbsp plus extra for drizzling over eggplant

ingredients.name: sweet ground paprika or poultry seasoning

steps: Slice the eggplant, sprinkle with salt, leave for fifteen to twenty minutes, then pat dry with paper towels.
Cut the onion in half and slice thinly. Heat 2–3 tablespoons of olive oil in a pan and sauté the onion.
Add the eggplant slices, drizzle generously with olive oil, dust with sweet paprika or seasoning, and fry for about 10 minutes.
Pour the canned chopped tomatoes into the pan and braise everything for another 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the couscous in a bowl, pour over boiling water, cover, and let stand for 5 minutes to swell.
Fluff the couscous, combine with the braised vegetables, and sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Tzatziki sauce (Sos tzatziki)
summary: A chilled Greek-style sauce made with fresh curd cheese, grated cucumber, and garlic, finished with olive oil, wine vinegar, and thyme.
steps: Peel the cucumber, grate it or dice finely, and squeeze out excess juice thoroughly.
Peel the garlic and press through a garlic press or mince very finely.
Mix the cucumber and garlic with the plain curd cheese, then stir in the olive oil and wine vinegar.
Season the sauce with a pinch of salt, thyme, and pepper.
Mix thoroughly and refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.

name: Kwaśnica Żywiecka (Żywiec-style sauerkraut soup)
summary: Traditional Highlander sauerkraut soup with dried mushrooms in bone-in pork loin broth.
steps: Simmer the bone-in pork loin and soup greens in 2 l of lightly salted water until the meat is tender, then remove the pork loin, debone, and divide into portions.
In a separate pot, cook the sauerkraut with the finely diced onion until tender.
Cook the dried mushrooms separately and slice them into strips.
Combine the meat-vegetable broth with the cooked sauerkraut, mushrooms, and pork loin portions.
Add the garlic crushed through a garlic press, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.

name: Ajntopf (vegetable one-pot soup)
summary: A thick vegetable soup with potatoes, kohlrabi, savoy cabbage, and mixed soup vegetables, thickened with roux and finished with sour cream.
steps: Wash and peel the potatoes, kohlrabi, carrot, celeriac, and parsley root, chop along with the leek and savoy cabbage, and cook in water or broth until tender.
Heat the margarine or butter in a small saucepan, sprinkle in the wheat flour, and cook to make a pale roux.
Stir the roux into the simmering soup, bring to a boil, and season with salt, Maggi seasoning, caraway, and basil.
Temper the sour cream with a few tablespoons of hot soup, pour into the pot, bring briefly to a boil, and serve sprinkled with chopped parsley leaves and dill.

name: Orgeat almond syrup drink (Syrop orszadowy)
summary: A sweet traditional almond drink (orgeat) made from scalded, peeled sweet almonds ground with sugar and infused in water or milk.
steps: Pour boiling water over the almonds, soak for 5 minutes, and peel off their skins.
Finely grind or pound the peeled almonds together with the sugar and a small amount of water or milk.
Pour the remaining water or milk over the ground mixture, stir, and let stand for about 30 minutes.
Strain the liquid through a fine sieve or cheesecloth, squeezing the almonds firmly, and chill the drink for about 30 minutes before serving.

name: Kompot z suszonych owoców (dried fruit compote drink)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve drink of dried apples, pears, apricots, and prunes, flavoured with citrus peel and lemon juice.
steps: Place the dried apples, pears, apricots, and prunes in a sieve and rinse them with hot water.
Pour 1.5 l of cold boiled water over the fruit and leave to soak overnight.
Transfer the water with the soaked fruit to a pot, add the sugar, freshly squeezed lemon juice, lemon zest, and orange zest.
Simmer the kompot over low heat until all the fruit is tender, and serve chilled.

name: Zupa jarzynowa (Traditional Polish vegetable soup)
summary: A classic homemade vegetable soup made with fresh vegetables, Polish soup vegetables, beans, Brussels sprouts, and potatoes in meat broth, finished with tomato paste and sour cream.
steps: Clean, wash, and chop the soup vegetables, additional carrots, beans, and Brussels sprouts.
Pour the meat broth over the vegetables, season with salt, and bring to a boil.
Peel the potatoes, cut into cubes, drop into the simmering soup, and cook until all vegetables are tender.
Mix the tomato paste with the sour cream and flour, pour into the soup, and boil briefly.

Stir in the fat at the end and season to taste with salt (in a second variation, the soup can be prepared from frozen vegetables with Brussels sprouts in chicken broth with meatballs made from 200 g raw white kiełbasa and chopped greens).

name: White sugar glaze
summary: Classic white icing whipped from egg whites, powdered sugar, and lemon juice.
steps: Crack the eggs and separate the whites from the yolks.
Lightly beat the egg whites with a fork, add 200 g of powdered sugar, and stir.
Add 1 tablespoon of boiled water and beat the mixture until smooth.
Pour in the juice from half a lemon and mix the icing thoroughly.

name: Sałatka rosyjska (Olivier salad)
summary: A traditional Russian Olivier salad of diced boiled potatoes, carrots, green peas, fermented pickles, and hard-boiled eggs in mayonnaise, garnished with sieved yolks.
steps: Peel the potatoes, boil them in lightly salted water until tender, then let cool and cut into dice.
Separate the hard-boiled egg whites from the yolks, then finely dice the egg whites, cooked carrots, and fermented brine pickles.
Transfer the diced vegetables and egg whites to a bowl, add the drained peas, mayonnaise, and vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and mix well.
Garnish the top of the salad with finely chopped parsley and the egg yolks pressed through a sieve.

name: Béchamel sauce (Sos beszamelowy)
summary: Classic French white sauce made with a butter and wheat flour roux whisked with warm milk and seasoned with nutmeg.
steps: Melt the butter over low heat in a heavy-bottomed pot, taking care not to let it brown.
Add the wheat flour and cook over low heat for 5–10 minutes, stirring constantly until smoothly combined with the butter.
Warm the milk in a separate pan, then pour in a thin stream into the roux, whisking vigorously until smooth and creamy.
Season to taste with salt, white pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg, passing through a fine sieve if necessary.

name: Scrambled eggs with cheese
summary: Quick scrambled eggs cooked in butter and topped with melted grated Gouda or mozzarella cheese and marjoram.
steps: Coarsely grate the cheese.
Melt the butter or lard in a skillet, crack in the eggs, season with salt, black pepper, and marjoram, and stir gently.
Sprinkle the grated cheese over the eggs and cook gently covered for a moment until the cheese melts and the eggs set.

name: Ciulim (Lelów potato and meat bake)
summary: A traditional regional Polish potato bake layered with pork ribs, poultry wings, and fried pork belly with onion.
steps: Cut the ribs into small pieces, prepare the poultry wings, rub the meat with salt, pepper, and ginger, and set aside for about 120 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and grate them.
Dice the raw pork belly and onion, then fry them together in some of the lard until the onion is golden.
Combine the grated potatoes with the fried pork belly and onion, and season the mixture with salt, pepper, paprika, and marjoram.
Grease a pot with the remaining lard and layer the potato mixture alternating with the ribs and poultry wings.
Bake slowly in an oven preheated to about 100 °C for 480 minutes (preferably overnight) and serve hot.

name: Hachee (Dutch beef and onion stew)
summary: Traditional Dutch beef stew (hachee) slowly braised with plenty of onion, dark beer, and cloves.

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: from 1 bouillon cube dissolved in 250 ml warm water

steps: Cut the beef into large cubes and dredge in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Peel the onions and slice into thick chunks or rings.
Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the meat on all sides.
Add the sliced onions, bay leaves, and cloves, and cook while stirring until the onion becomes translucent.
Pour in the warm beef broth, dark beer, and wine vinegar so the liquid covers the meat, and bring to a boil.

Reduce the heat to low and braise with the lid slightly ajar for 3 hours, stirring regularly until the meat is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick, then remove the bay leaves and cloves and season to taste.

name: Haupia (Hawaiian coconut pudding)
summary: Traditional Hawaiian coconut milk pudding thickened with cornstarch and served in chilled squares.
steps: Combine the coconut milk, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a pot and warm over medium heat.
Gradually stir in the cornstarch, whisking constantly, and cook until the pudding thickens.
Pour the hot coconut mixture into a square baking dish.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 60 minutes, then cut into neat squares and serve.

name: Borsos tokány (Hungarian peppered beef stew)
summary: A classic Hungarian beef stew cooked in lard with onions, garlic, fresh bell peppers, tomatoes, and a generous amount of black pepper.
steps: Cut the beef into strips about 3 cm long, and finely chop the onion and fry in the pot in the hot lard until golden.
Salt the meat, add to the pot with the onion, and cook stirring until it releases its juices.
Add a small clove of garlic and a splash of water, cover, and braise over low heat in minimal liquid, adding water as needed to prevent scorching.
When the meat is half-tender, reduce the liquid until only the fat remains, then add the tomato pulp and diced bell pepper.
Continue simmering uncovered over low heat until the beef is fully tender, and season generously with freshly cracked black pepper towards the end.

name: Cola chicken
summary: Chicken breast pieces braised with onion, garlic, and curry powder in a thick sauce made from ketchup, cola, and soy sauce.
steps: Chop the onion, crush the garlic, and cut the chicken breasts into small dice.
Heat a small amount of oil in a wok or deep frying pan.
Add the curry powder and garlic and fry for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped onion and fry for another 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the diced chicken and fry for 5–6 minutes, stirring regularly.
Pour in the ketchup, cola, and soy sauce, stir, and bring the sauce to a boil.
Reduce the heat and braise for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.

name: Pork steaks with apple and onion sauce (Steki wieprzowe)
summary: Pork neck steaks in a honey-mustard marinade, seared in lard, finished in the oven, and served with an onion and apple sauce.

ingredients.name: Polish herb and spice seasoning (pieprz ziołowy)

steps: Take the pork collar out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before preparation, slice into steaks, trim membranes, and pound the meat very lightly.

Mix the mustard, honey, lemon juice, a little olive oil, Polish herb and spice seasoning, salt, some of the herbes de Provence, ginger and crushed garlic. Brush the marinade over the steaks and leave for 10 minutes.
Finely chop the onions and fry in olive oil with herbes de Provence until tender, then add the finely chopped apples and remaining marinade and fry for a few minutes.
Get the lard very hot in a skillet, quickly sear the steaks on both sides and edges, transfer to a roasting tin, and pour the pan drippings into the onion-apple sauce.
Place the steaks in an oven preheated to 140 °C, raise the temperature to 180 °C, bake for 12 minutes, and serve with the onion-apple sauce.

name: Zasypywane (layered semolina and fruit cake)
summary: A simple cake made with alternating layers of a dry flour, semolina, and sugar mixture and fresh fruit, topped with grated chilled margarine and baked.

ingredients.name: margarine
ingredients.note: half a block, straight from the fridge

steps: Mix the all-purpose flour, sugar, semolina, and baking powder in a separate dish into a uniform dry mixture.
Wash and chop the fruit; if using apples or peaches, preferably coarsely grate them and mix with cinnamon to taste.
Grease a baking pan with fat and dust with breadcrumbs.
Alternate 3 layers of dry mixture with 2 layers of fruit in the pan, starting with a dry layer.
Grate the chilled margarine straight from the fridge and distribute it evenly over the top of the cake.
Bake for 60 minutes in an oven (or for 50 minutes in an electric tabletop oven).

name: Pierożki pieczone z borowikiem (baked porcini pastries)
summary: Baked shortcrust pastries made with butter and sour cream, filled with a Christmas Eve mixture of sauerkraut, dried porcini and onion.
steps: Soak the dried porcini in water for 2 hours, boil until tender, drain (reserving the broth), and chop finely.
Squeeze and rinse the sauerkraut, then braise it in the mushroom broth with 100 g of butter.
Dice the onion, sauté in hot vegetable oil, add along with the chopped porcini to the sauerkraut, and braise until liquid evaporates, then season with salt and pepper and let cool.
Cut 150 g of chilled butter into the sifted flour, add the egg yolks, sour cream and salt, knead into a dough, and refrigerate for several hours.
Roll out the chilled dough, cut out squares or rounds, spoon portions of filling onto them, and crimp the edges tightly.
Brush the tops of the pastries with beaten egg and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C until golden brown.

name: Banana milkshake
summary: A chilled milk beverage made with banana, a scoop of vanilla or cream ice cream, and a pinch of cinnamon.
steps: Peel the banana, place it in a blender or food processor, and drizzle with lemon juice so it does not brown.
Add a scoop of vanilla or cream ice cream, pour in the milk, and optionally add 1–2 ice cubes to create a light froth.
Blend everything for 1–3 minutes until the ingredients are well combined and the ice is crushed.
Pour the cold drink into glasses and lightly dust the top with ground cinnamon.

name: Żurek śląski (Silesian sour rye soup)
summary: A traditional Silesian sour rye soup made with smoked pork belly and kiełbasa, potatoes, garlic, and a generous amount of marjoram.

ingredients.name: white kiełbasa or other cured meat
sour rye soup concentrate (koncentrat żurku)
ingredients.note: 100–200 ml, depending on thickness and acidity

steps: Dice the pork belly or cut it into strips, place it in a pot with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Add the smoked kiełbasa cut into pieces (and optionally the white kiełbasa or other cured meat), the diced potatoes, and the crushed garlic cloves.
Season the soup with a generous amount of marjoram, and salt and black pepper to taste.
Cook for 8–12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Pour in 100–200 ml of sour rye soup concentrate (depending on its thickness, acidity, and personal preference).
Simmer over low heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring constantly.

name: Fasolka szparagowa w cieście naleśnikowym (batter-fried green beans)
summary: Tender green beans coated in a thick pancake batter and pan-fried until golden.
steps: Trim the green beans, boil them until tender in water with a teaspoon of salt, and drain.
Add the flour to a bowl, crack in the egg, pour in the milk and water, and blend into a batter with the consistency of thick cream.
Transfer the drained beans into the bowl with the batter and toss until the pods are evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a pan, add the battered bean pods, and fry on both sides until golden brown.

name: Napoletana sauce
summary: A classic Italian sauce made with fresh or canned tomatoes simmered with olive oil, garlic, basil, thyme, and oregano.

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: canned or very ripe fresh tomatoes

steps: Dice the tomatoes, place them in a bowl, and puree with a food processor or blender at very low speed so the juice does not foam or turn pale.
Pour the olive oil into a skillet, warm it gently, and add the pureed tomatoes.
Fry the sauce in the skillet until it turns a darker shade.
Add torn fresh basil leaves, 2 pinches of dried thyme, and 2–4 pinches of oregano, then simmer everything for 5–10 minutes.
Add the finely chopped garlic cloves and simmer, stirring, for another 2–3 minutes.

name: Dal (Dhal - Indian red lentil soup)
summary: An aromatic Indian red lentil cream soup with carrots, parsley root, and tomatoes, enriched with coconut milk and garam masala.
steps: Peel the carrots and parsley root, cover with water and the vegetable bouillon cube, and cook for about 20 minutes.
Blend the cooked vegetables together with the broth until smooth.
Add the diced tomatoes, rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, garam masala, and hot paprika.
Simmer the soup over low heat for another 15 minutes until the lentils are tender.

name: Kotlety z kaszy gryczanej i ziemniaków (buckwheat and potato patties)
summary: Vegetarian patties (hreczki) made from cooked buckwheat groats and potatoes with browned onions and dill, coated in breadcrumbs.
steps: Cook the buckwheat groats until fluffy in salted water with the butter for 15 minutes over low heat, then leave covered for 10–30 minutes to absorb the liquid, and measure out 6 tbsp.
Boil the potatoes until tender, mash them, and measure out 3 tbsp.
Peel the onion, chop finely, and cook until translucent in a frying pan.
Combine the cooked buckwheat groats, potatoes, and translucent onion with the egg, potato starch, plain flour, and chopped dill.
Season the mixture to taste with salt, pepper, and thyme, and mix thoroughly.
Shape into patties, coat in breadcrumbs, and fry in hot oil on both sides until golden brown.

name: Zupa kremowa z dyni (Cream of pumpkin soup)
summary: A warming cream of pumpkin soup braised with onion and fresh ginger, blended with orange juice and cinnamon, served with sour cream and croutons.

ingredients.name: croutons
ingredients.note: or choux pastry puffs, for serving

steps: Cut the pumpkin into quarters, scoop out seeds and fibrous pulp, slice the firm flesh, peel off skin, and grate on a coarse grater.
Grate the fresh ginger, and peel and dice the onion.
Place the grated pumpkin, ginger, and onion in a pot, add the butter and oil, and cook gently covered until completely tender and beginning to break down.
Pour in the vegetable broth and squeezed orange juice and simmer gently for a few minutes (you may substitute carrots for pumpkin, slightly increasing the amount of broth).
Add the cinnamon, salt, and pepper, and simmer over low heat for another 10–15 minutes.
Blend the soup into a smooth cream, stir in the sour cream, and serve with croutons or choux pastry puffs.

name: Kluski śląskie (Silesian potato dumplings)
summary: Traditional Silesian dumplings made from boiled potatoes and potato starch, featuring a characteristic hollow in the centre.
steps: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water until tender.
Pass the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly with a potato masher.
Add the potato starch, salt, and optionally the egg, then knead into a uniform dough.
Dust your hands with potato starch, shape the dough into small balls, flatten them slightly, and press a dimple into the centre of each dumpling with your finger.
Coat the shaped dumplings in potato starch and drop them in batches into salted boiling water.
Once the dumplings float to the surface, lower the heat and cook for about 5 minutes, then drain.

name: Siemieniotka (Silesian Christmas Eve hemp seed soup)
summary: A traditional Silesian Christmas Eve soup made from mashed hemp seeds simmered with onion and dark roux, served with croutons.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or half water and half milk

steps: Rinse the hemp seeds, pour part of the boiling water over them, and cook until the seeds start to burst, then drain through a sieve, reserving the cooking liquid.
Transfer the drained seeds to a pot, add a small splash of boiling water, and cook while mashing thoroughly until a white milk is released, adding more water little by little if necessary.
Pour the reserved liquid over the mashed hemp seeds, add the sliced onion, and simmer over low heat until gruel-like in consistency, then strain or leave the onion in.
Prepare a dark roux from the vegetable oil and flour, stir it into the soup, and season to taste with salt, pepper, and sugar.
Dice the rolls finely, toast until golden croutons form, arrange on plates, and ladle hot siemieniotka over them.

name: Kwaśnica (Polish highland sauerkraut soup)
summary: Traditional Polish highland soup made with rich meat broth, sauerkraut and its juice, and mushrooms, served with separately boiled potatoes.

ingredients.name: fatty meat (mutton or pork: jowl, collar, shoulder, or ribs)

steps: If using dried mushrooms, soak them beforehand in water until softened and reserve the soaking liquid.
Rinse the meat and place it in a pot together with the bay leaf, allspice berries, and mushrooms (along with their soaking liquid).
Pour in enough water to just cover the ingredients and simmer over medium heat until the meat is tender.
Add the sauerkraut without squeezing out its liquid, then add sauerkraut juice until the soup is distinctly sour.
Simmer the soup gently until the sauerkraut is tender, adding the garlic towards the end of cooking.
Boil the potatoes separately. Arrange a portion of the simmered meat and boiled potatoes in bowls and ladle over the hot kwaśnica.

name: Owsianka z musem jabłkowym (rolled oat porridge with apple puree)
summary: A simple rolled oat porridge cooked in milk and water, served warm topped with apple puree.
steps: Add the rolled oats to a saucepan, pour in the milk and water, and add a pinch of salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the oats soften and absorb the liquid.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with apple puree.

name: Carrot cake
summary: A moist carrot cake made with coarsely grated carrots, chopped nuts, oil, and eggs.
steps: Beat the eggs with the sugar until smooth and light.
Pour the oil into the egg mixture in a slow, steady stream while continuing to beat.
Sift the wheat flour, baking soda, and baking powder into a separate bowl, then mix thoroughly with the egg and oil mixture.
Fold the grated carrots and chopped nuts into the smooth batter until evenly distributed.
Transfer the batter into a baking tin and bake for 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.

name: Strawberry crumble traybake (Truskawkowe ciasto z kruszonką)
summary: A large shortcrust sheet cake topped with fresh strawberry halves and a buttery vanilla crumble, dusted with icing sugar.
steps: Rub the plain flour, sugar, vanilla sugar, and butter together into a crumble, then place it in the refrigerator.

Mix the flour for the dough with the baking powder, cut in the soft margarine, add the whole eggs, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla sugar, and sour cream, knead into a uniform dough, and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Roll out the chilled dough, line a large baking tray lined with baking paper, and blind-bake until lightly golden for about 30 minutes at 180 °C.
Remove the pre-baked base from the oven, let cool slightly, arrange the washed, hulled, and halved strawberries on top, and scatter with the chilled crumble.
Bake the cake for another 15 minutes at 180 °C until golden, and once cool, dust with icing sugar.

name: Kisiel malinowy (raspberry fruit kissel)
summary: A traditional Polish fruit dessert made from fresh crushed raspberries thickened with potato starch.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus a little cold water to dissolve the starch

steps: Bring 500 ml of water to a boil in a saucepan.
Dissolve the potato starch together with the sugar in a small amount of cold water.
Pour the slurry into the boiling water, stirring vigorously all the while, until the kissel thickens.
Finally, stir in the crushed raspberries and mix thoroughly.

name: Köttbullar (Swedish meatballs)
summary: Classic Swedish minced meat meatballs blended with red onion, cream-soaked breadcrumbs, and a hint of honey.
steps: Mix the breadcrumbs with the cream and let stand for several minutes to swell.
Finely chop the red onion and sauté in a pan in butter or olive oil until softened.
In a bowl, combine the minced meat with the egg, honey, salt, pepper, soaked breadcrumbs, and cooked onion, working into a smooth mixture.
Shape into small spherical meatballs and fry in a pan until golden brown.

name: Nalewka ajerkoniak (traditional Polish advocaat / egg liqueur)
summary: A homemade no-cook egg liqueur prepared from fresh egg yolks, icing sugar, boiled milk, vanilla, and rectified spirit.
steps: Beat or whisk the egg yolks with the icing sugar and vanilla until smooth and fluffy.
Gradually pour in the cold boiled milk while continuing to whisk.
Add the rectified spirit in a slow thin stream, whisk until fully emulsified, and bottle the advocaat.

name: Nalewka ajerkoniak na 1 litr (steamed advocaat with brandy, 1-litre batch)
summary: A traditional advocaat made from egg yolks whisked with sugar over steam, scalded with boiling milk, and blended with rectified spirit and brandy.
steps: Whisk the egg yolks with sugar over a double boiler until thick, pale, and ribbony.
Bring the milk and vanilla to a boil and slowly pour it into the whisked yolks, stirring constantly.
Cool the mixture, stir in the rectified spirit and brandy, mix thoroughly, and bottle the advocaat.

name: Nalewka ajerkoniak na gęsto (thick homemade advocaat with powdered milk)
summary: A thick homemade vodka-based advocaat thickened with milk powder and egg yolks whisked over steam with icing sugar.
steps: Whisk the egg yolks with icing sugar and vanilla sugar over a double boiler until pale and fluffy.
Whisk in the milk and milk powder until smooth, then let the mixture cool completely.
