Slowly stream in the vodka while stirring constantly until uniformly smooth, then pour the liqueur into bottles.

name: Nalewka ajerkoniak pyszny (butter-enriched advocaat liqueur)
summary: A velvety, rich egg liqueur made from egg yolks beaten with icing sugar, fresh creamed butter, and vodka.
steps: Beat the egg yolks with icing sugar and vanilla sugar until pale, fluffy, and voluminous.
Gradually beat in the softened butter one tablespoon at a time, continuing to whisk until completely smooth.
Slowly pour in the vodka, beating constantly until fully incorporated.

name: Nalewka Fałszywy koniak (mock cognac infused vodka with prunes and tea)
summary: A homemade infused vodka crafted with pure vodka, honey, loose black tea, and dried prunes.
steps: Pour the vodka into a bottle or jar, add the honey, loose black tea, and dried prunes, and stir.
Seal the container tightly and refrigerate for 14 days.
Filter the infusion through filter paper or a coffee filter and decant into a clean bottle.

name: Nalewka Glögg (Nordic spiced mulled wine)
summary: A warming Scandinavian festive punch of red wine, port, brandy, and vodka infused with cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.
steps: Place the cardamom seeds, cloves, and cinnamon pieces into a jar, pour over the vodka, and leave to infuse for 3 days.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil to make a simple syrup.
Strain the spiced vodka from the aromatics and combine in a large pot with the red wine, port, brandy, simple syrup, and lemon juice.
Heat the mixture gently without letting it boil.
Drop a few raisins and almonds into small glasses and ladle in the steaming glögg.

name: Nalewka Orszada (almond horchata / orgeat drink)
summary: A refreshing milky almond beverage with cinnamon and sugar, served well chilled or lightly frozen.
steps: Rinse the almonds several times and soak them in part of the water for 12 hours.
Drain the almonds, rinse again, pat dry, and pound in a mortar or grind finely into a smooth paste.
Mix the almond paste with the remaining water and cinnamon stick, and leave in a cool place for 2 hours.
Remove the cinnamon stick, add the sugar, and stir until completely dissolved.
Strain the beverage through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth to obtain a smooth, milky liquid, and chill thoroughly before serving.

name: Brain booster oat and fruit energy bars
summary: Nutritious baked oat flapjack bars loaded with walnuts, dried apricots, pumpkin seeds, dark chocolate, and honey.
steps: Combine the rolled oats, cane sugar, spelt flour, baking powder, cinnamon, coarsely grated dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds, and desiccated coconut in a bowl.
Finely dice the dried apricots, mash into a paste, and mix with the honey and softened butter.
Fold the apricot-butter paste thoroughly into the dry ingredients until evenly moistened.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper, spread the mixture evenly while pressing down firmly, and bake for about 45 minutes at 160 °C.
Top the baked slab with the chopped walnuts, let cool completely, and slice into 12 bars.

name: Kurki duszone w śmietanie (Chanterelles braised in sour cream)
summary: Traditional Polish dish of fresh chanterelle mushrooms braised in butter with onion, fresh dill, and sour cream.
steps: Slice the onion and cook until translucent in the melted butter.
Add the washed and cleaned chanterelles, stir in half of the finely chopped dill as they cook, and braise over medium heat for about 20 minutes until excess moisture has evaporated.
Remove the pan from the heat, season the chanterelles with salt and pepper, stir in the sour cream and remaining dill, and warm through briefly before serving.

name: Pańska skórka (Warsaw two-tone honey-raspberry nougat candy)
summary: A traditional Warsaw feast-day confection made in white and pink layers from whipped egg whites scalded with hot honey-sugar syrup.
steps: Combine the sugar, honey, and water in a saucepan and simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes, until the syrup reaches 160–170 °C.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream while whisking continuously, until the meringue is glossy and bright white.
Add the vanilla sugar and beat briefly to combine.
Spread half of the white nougat mixture into a tin lined with baking paper.
Stir the raspberry juice into the remaining mixture, spread the pink layer over the white, leave in a cool place until completely set, and cut into cubes.

name: Gołąbki zawijane w liście funkii (rice and mushroom rolls in hosta leaves)
summary: Vegetarian rolls made with young hosta leaves, stuffed with rice, button mushrooms, onion, and ginger, and baked with olive oil.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and drain.
Finely chop the onions, ginger, and button or oyster mushrooms, then fry in the butter or vegetable fat until the onions begin to brown.
Add the cooked rice, pour in the soy sauce, mix well, and season with salt if needed.
Blanch the young hosta leaves for a few minutes in boiling water until pliable, then drain.
Place about 1 tablespoon of filling on each hosta leaf and roll into small parcels.
Arrange the rolls in a baking dish, pour over the olive oil and water, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for at least 50 minutes.

name: Gołąbki z kaszą i mięsem (cabbage rolls with barley and pork in sour cream sauce)
summary: Cabbage rolls stuffed with barley groats or rice and ground pork neck, baked under a sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: barley groats or rice
ingredients.note: fine pearl barley groats, whole pearl barley, or rice

ingredients.name: cooking fat for frying and cooking the barley
water
ingredients.note: boiling, for pouring over cabbage rolls

steps: Rinse the head of cabbage, core it, separate the leaves, and blanch them in batches in boiling water; drain, cool, and lightly flatten the thick central ribs with a mallet.
Cook the barley or rice with some of the fat, and fry the chopped onion in the remaining fat until golden.
In a bowl, mix the cooked barley or rice with the browned onion and raw minced meat, and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon a portion of filling onto each cabbage leaf, fold the opposite sides inward, and roll tightly into a parcel.
Line the bottom of a roasting dish with a few cabbage leaves, pack the cabbage rolls tightly on top, and cover with another layer of leaves.
Pour 250 ml of boiling salted water over the rolls and place in an oven preheated to 180 °C; once the top leaves brown, cover the dish, lower the temperature to 160 °C, and braise until tender.
Remove the top leaves, pour over the sour cream whisked with the flour and crumbled bouillon cube, and bake for another 10 minutes.

name: Pralinki lipowe (linden truffles)
summary: Homemade truffles made from lightly toasted unripe linden fruit and dried linden flowers ground with powdered sugar or honey and oil.

ingredients.name: cocoa powder
ingredients.note: optional, or instant coffee or liqueur

steps: Remove stems from the green, unripe linden fruits, lightly toast them in a dry skillet, and crush in a mortar or blend in a food processor until smooth.
Add the crushed dried linden flowers, icing sugar or honey, and optionally cocoa powder, instant coffee, or liqueur, and mix thoroughly.
Slowly pour in the grapeseed oil or melted coconut oil, kneading until a sticky, malleable paste forms.
Shape into six truffles by hand or in small moulds and chill thoroughly in the refrigerator before serving.

name: Kopytka marchewkowe z sosem szczawiowym (potato and carrot dumplings with sorrel sauce)
summary: Potato and carrot dumplings served with a velvety sauce of fresh sorrel gently stewed in butter and finished with sour cream.
steps: Boil the carrots until tender in about 375 ml of water, reserving the resulting vegetable stock for the sauce, then peel the cooked carrots and pass through a ricer.
Wash the sorrel, trim the tough stems, and sauté the leaves in butter until softened and darkened, then pass them through a sieve or blend.
Pour 375 ml of hot vegetable stock and 125 ml of sour cream mixed with 2 tbsp of plain flour into the sorrel, bring to a boil, and season to taste with salt, pepper, and sugar.
Peel the potatoes, boil them in salted water, and pass them through a ricer while still warm.
Mix the riced potatoes and carrots with 500 ml of plain flour, the potato starch, and the eggs, add salt, and knead into a soft dough on a pastry board.
Divide the dough into portions, roll out into logs 1.5 cm thick on a floured pastry board, flatten slightly, and cut diagonally with a damp knife into pieces 3–4 cm long.
Drop the kopytka in batches into salted boiling water, stir gently, and cook for 1–2 minutes after they float to the surface, then remove with a slotted spoon and serve with the sorrel sauce.

name: Red pizza sauce
summary: A thick, slow-simmered tomato pizza sauce with onion, garlic, green bell pepper, herbs, and Worcestershire sauce.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the minced garlic, finely diced onion, and green bell pepper, and cook until softened.
Add the peeled, seeded, and chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, oregano, thyme, basil, salt, and coarsely ground pepper.
Lower the heat and simmer the sauce for 120 minutes, stirring occasionally, until significantly thickened.

name: Five-cheese lasagne
summary: Baked green-pasta lasagne layered with tomato sauce, béchamel sauce made with poultry broth, and a five-cheese blend.
steps: Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets and cut them into rectangular strips measuring about 11 × 27.5 cm.
Combine the beaten eggs with the farmer's cheese, cheddar, havarti, ricotta, and most of the parmesan, setting aside about 50 g of parmesan for the topping, then chill the cheese mixture.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the wheat flour and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in 250 ml of milk and 250 ml of poultry broth and simmer over low heat until the sauce thickens.

Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Spread a thin layer of the 750 ml of tomato sauce over the bottom of a large greased baking dish, arrange a layer of pasta, drizzle with white sauce and tomato sauce, and cover with the cheese layer.
Continue layering until all ingredients are used up, finishing with tomato sauce, and sprinkle the top with the reserved parmesan.
Cover the dish with aluminium foil and bake for 25 minutes at 200 °C, then remove the foil and bake for another 8 minutes.

name: Four-cheese pizza (Pizza quattro formaggi)
summary: Italian four-cheese pizza topped with tomato sauce and a melted blend of mozzarella, medium-sharp cheese, Parmesan, and provolone.
steps: Preheat the oven to 230 °C.
Line a pizza pan with the pizza dough and spread the tomato sauce over it, leaving a 1.5 cm crust border.
Scatter an even layer of grated mozzarella, medium-sharp cheese, Parmesan, and provolone over the pizza and bake for 15 minutes until golden brown.

name: Beef and prosciutto ravioli
summary: Italian pasta parcels made from tomato pasta dough filled with minced beef, prosciutto, and romano cheese, served in a creamy tomato sauce.
steps: Prepare the tomato pasta dough, roll it out into thin sheets, and cover with a damp cloth.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet, brown the minced beef, drain off excess fat, let the meat cool, and transfer to a bowl.
Combine the cooled beef with chopped prosciutto, egg, basil, oregano, and grated Romano cheese.

Place portions of filling at even intervals on one pasta sheet, moisten the pasta around the filling with water, cover with a second sheet, press the edges together, and cut out the ravioli with a pastry wheel.

Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the plain flour, and cook over low heat for 2 minutes. Pour in the sour cream, bring to a boil and cook until thickened, then stir in the tomato purée and simmer for 20 minutes.
Cook the ravioli in a large pot of boiling water for about 2 minutes until they float, drain, divide among plates, and spoon the hot tomato and sour cream sauce over them.

name: Spinach lasagne
summary: Vegetarian lasagne with fresh spinach, ricotta, green bell pepper, tomatoes, Grana Padano, and mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the finely chopped seeded green pepper and chopped onion, and fry until golden. Towards the end, add the thinly sliced garlic, fry briefly, and let cool.

Beat the eggs in a bowl, add the ricotta, finely chopped spinach, half of the grated Grana Padano, and half of the grated mozzarella, season with salt and pepper, then combine with the cooled vegetables.
Finely chop the canned tomatoes and mix with their juices, season with salt and pepper, then spread half of the sauce over the bottom of an ovenproof dish.
Drop the lasagne sheets 3 at a time into boiling salted water and parboil briefly until slightly softened.

Layer alternately in the dish with 3 pasta sheets and one-quarter of the spinach-cheese filling; pour the remaining tomato sauce over the final pasta layer and sprinkle with the remaining Grana Padano and mozzarella.
Cover the dish with aluminium foil and bake for 30 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C, then remove the foil and bake for another 15–20 minutes until the cheese is browned.

name: Polenta (Italian cornmeal porridge)
summary: Traditional Italian polenta made from yellow cornmeal simmered in salted water to a thick, creamy consistency.
steps: Bring a litre of salted water to a boil in a large pot, and bring the remaining litre of plain water to a boil in a second pot.
Slowly pour 600 g of cornmeal in a steady stream into the boiling salted water, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring regularly and adding boiling water from the second pot as needed.
Add the remaining 400 g of cornmeal and simmer for another 15–30 minutes, gradually pouring in the rest of the hot water and stirring until the polenta pulls away cleanly from the sides of the pot.
Pour the cooked polenta onto a moistened board or tray, smooth to the desired thickness, and leave to set.

name: Pizza carbonara
summary: Homemade thin-crust yeast pizza with ham, button mushrooms, onion and a creamy carbonara sauce made with smoked bacon, eggs, sour cream and Parmesan.
steps: Crumble the yeast into a small bowl, mix with sugar, pour in warm water, dust with a pinch of flour, cover, and let stand in a warm place for 20 minutes.
Mix the wheat flour with paprika, salt, and Italian herbs, pour in the risen starter and olive oil, knead into a smooth dough, and leave covered for 20–30 minutes to rise.
Finely dice the smoked bacon, fry until crisp in a tablespoon of olive oil, drain on kitchen paper, and sauté the minced garlic in the remaining fat.

Whisk the eggs with sour cream, salt, and pepper, stir in the grated Parmesan, bacon, and garlic, and heat briefly over very low heat (thickening with a little flour if needed), being careful not to scramble the eggs.
Divide the risen dough into 2 portions, stretch onto baking sheets into thin rounds, and fold the crust edges.
Top the dough with sliced mushrooms, onion, and ham, sprinkle with pizza seasoning, spoon over the carbonara sauce, and top with grated cheese.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180–200 °C for about 20–25 minutes.

name: Chleb kukurydziany Ciotki Karoliny (Aunt Caroline's cornbread)
summary: A quick American cornbread made with baking powder, egg, and milk.

ingredients.name: liquid fat
ingredients.note: such as melted butter or fat rendered from pork fatback

steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C and grease a shallow baking pan well.
Mix together the cornmeal, plain flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, beaten egg, milk, and liquid fat into a smooth batter.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for about 25 minutes at 190 °C.

name: Kawa luizjańska (Louisiana egg coffee)
summary: Traditional Southern US coffee brewed in a pot with egg white to clarify the brew.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: mostly boiling, with a splash of cold water

steps: Scald a coffee pot with boiling water, add ground coffee, egg white, and a splash of cold water, then stir thoroughly.
Pour the remaining boiling water over the mixture and simmer gently over low heat for 5 minutes.
Set the pot in a warm place for 15 minutes without boiling to allow the grounds to settle, then pour the clear coffee.

name: Kleik kukurydziany (cornmeal mush)
summary: American cornmeal mush steamed slowly over a water bath, served warm or cooled, sliced, and fried.
steps: Bring 875 ml of water to a boil and add the salt.
Gradually sift 250 ml of cornmeal into the boiling water, stirring vigorously with your other hand the whole time to prevent lumps.
Cook the mixture over direct heat for about 10 minutes.
Transfer the pot over a water bath and steam the mush for 2 hours, then serve warm (or let cool in smaller portions, slice, and fry).

name: Pork curry with bell pepper and cream (Wieprzowina curry)
summary: Pork loin strips braised with onions and bell peppers in an aromatic sauce of curry, ginger, vegetable broth, and cream or coconut milk.

ingredients.name: whipping cream (30% fat) or coconut milk

steps: Wash and pat dry the pork loin, cut into small strips or cubes, and season with salt and pepper.
Remove the seeds from the fresh bell pepper and cut into strips or dice, and finely chop the peeled onion.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan or casserole, add the pork, sprinkle with curry powder and ginger, and fry stirring until lightly browned.
Add the onion and cook until translucent, then add the diced bell pepper and cook over moderate heat for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the sweet and hot paprika, pour in the vegetable broth, and simmer covered for 30–45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the whipping cream or coconut milk, simmer for another 5 minutes, season to taste with salt and pepper, and garnish with basil leaves.

name: Mississippi biscuits
summary: Quick South American biscuits made with wheat flour, lard, and milk.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: amount needed to form a soft dough

steps: Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the lard, then gradually pour in the milk and knead lightly into a soft dough.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut into pieces, and bake for about 8 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Mother's potato pudding (maminy pudding z kartofli)
summary: A sweet baked pudding made with potatoes, eggs, milk, butter, and vanilla.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing and topping

steps: Grate the peeled potatoes or boil and mash them into a smooth puree, and preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Whisk the sugar with the eggs, tablespoon of butter, and milk, adding the vanilla sugar and vanilla flavouring.
Combine the egg-milk mixture with the mashed potatoes and mix thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture into a buttered baking dish, dot with butter pieces on top, and bake for 60 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Fluffy cotton blossom (popovers)
summary: Traditional Southern American fluffy popovers baked from a rich egg and milk batter in muffin tins.
steps: Beat the eggs in a bowl, pour in the milk, add the salt and plain flour, and whisk thoroughly into a smooth, thin batter.
Pour the batter into muffin cups or into a single baking dish.
Bake for about 40 minutes in an oven preheated to 160 °C, then finish baking for 5 minutes at 180 °C and serve immediately.

name: Chleb jajeczny z Baltimore (Baltimore egg bread)
summary: A delicate bread baked from a thin egg-and-milk batter, traditional in the southern United States.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Beat the eggs thoroughly, then add the milk, plain flour, salt, baking soda, and baking powder.
Pour in the melted fat last and stir into a batter.
Pour the mixture into the tin and bake at 180 °C for about 40 minutes in the tin and for 10 minutes after unmoulding.

name: Sałatka z kartofli (potato salad)
summary: A simple American-style potato salad with hard-boiled eggs, celery, and parsley, drizzled with olive oil.
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, let cool, and cut into cubes.
Hard-boil the eggs, let cool, peel, and chop finely along with the parsley leaves.
Dice the celery into pieces matching the size of the potato cubes.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl, season with salt and black and red pepper, drizzle with olive oil, and mix thoroughly.

name: Przekładaniec (chocolate chip muffins)
summary: Homemade muffins made from simple milk and vegetable oil batter with embedded chunks of milk chocolate.
steps: Combine the plain flour, baking powder, sugar, and vanilla sugar in a large bowl.
Add the eggs, vegetable oil, and milk, and stir until well combined into a uniform batter.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C, line a baking sheet with muffin cups, and fill them with batter to a depth of about 1 cm.
Break the milk chocolate into chunks and press them into the batter in the muffin cups so they do not protrude above the surface.
Place the muffin cups into the preheated oven and bake the muffins for about 25 minutes.

name: Chleb na soli (salt-rising bread)
summary: A traditional Appalachian bread naturally fermented with an overnight cornmeal and hot milk starter, yielding a dense, cheese-like flavoured loaf.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: 500 ml for the starter, with the remaining flour used to make the dough

steps: Mix the cornmeal thoroughly with 500 ml of boiling milk and leave in a warm place overnight.
In the morning, warm the remaining 500 ml of milk and add it to the starter while still warm, along with the sugar and 500 ml of wheat flour.
Stir the mixture and rest in a warm spot for about 120 minutes until sponge-like and bubbly.
Add the salt, fat, and remaining wheat flour, then knead a soft dough for 15 minutes.
Shape into a loaf, rest to rise for 60–120 minutes, and then bake for 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.

name: Cream of celery soup
summary: A creamy soup of finely chopped celery stalks and onion cooked in milk, thickened with butter, flour, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: plus a splash of cold milk to blend the flour

steps: Finely chop the celery stalks and onion, place in a pot with 750 ml of milk, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the pre-melted butter and the flour smoothly blended with a splash of cold milk, bringing to a boil until thickened.
Season the soup with salt and pepper, stir in 250 ml of sour cream, mix well, and serve warm.

name: Frykas z jabłek (spiced apple and raisin relish)
summary: A spiced preserve of apples, raisins, and oranges cooked in a sugar-and-vinegar syrup with cinnamon and cloves.
steps: Peel and core the apples, then chop the fruit into small pieces.
Squeeze the juice and scoop out the pulp from the oranges.
In a large pot, combine the chopped apples, raisins, orange juice and pulp, sugar, vinegar, ground cloves, and cinnamon.
Simmer over moderate heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fruit is tender and the syrup thickens.

name: Sałatka Waldorf (Waldorf salad)
summary: A simple crunchy salad of diced apples, celery and nuts, drizzled with olive oil.
steps: Peel and core the apples, then dice the flesh.
Wash the celery stalks and slice them finely.
Combine the diced apples, celery and nuts in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and mix thoroughly.

name: Ciastka plantatora (coconut and cereal-flake cookies)
summary: Crisp cereal-flake and coconut cookies flavoured with vanilla.

ingredients.name: cereal flakes
ingredients.note: oat, spelt, or other cereal flakes

steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease a baking sheet well.
Cream the sugar with the butter until smooth, then incorporate the well-beaten eggs.
Mix the batter with the cereal flakes, desiccated coconut, salt, and vanilla flavouring.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the prepared baking sheet and bake for 15–20 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Evening raisins (baked lemon-glazed raisins)
summary: Baked raisins in sweet lemon syrup with grated lemon zest, served warm with crêpes or as pastry filling.
steps: Grate the zest from the scalded lemon and squeeze out its juice.
Combine the chopped raisins with the lemon juice and zest, add the sugar, and pour in the water.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish or use as a pastry filling, and bake for about 50 minutes in an oven preheated to 160 °C.

name: Pasta with tuna and leek
summary: Pasta in a creamy sauce of canned tuna, braised leek, garlic, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: canned tuna in its own juices

steps: Cook the pasta al dente and drain.
Slice the leek into rounds and gently fry in heated olive oil until tender.
Add the drained canned tuna and black pepper, and warm together for a moment.
Add the crushed garlic, remove the pan from the heat, stir in the sour cream, and pour the sauce over the cooked pasta.

name: Ciasteczka maślane (Polish vanilla butter cookies)
summary: Classic crumbly Polish butter cookies scented with vanilla, quick to prepare and baked until delicately golden at the edges.
steps: Chop the butter into the plain flour, icing sugar, egg, vanilla sugar, baking powder, and salt with a knife, then quickly knead into a smooth dough.
Chill the dough in the refrigerator for 15–20 minutes to firm up slightly.
Shape the dough into small balls, arrange on a baking sheet lined with baking paper, and flatten with the bottom of a glass.
Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 8–9 minutes until the edges are lightly golden, then allow to firm up on the sheet before removing.

name: Gołąbki z kapustą i pomidorami (stuffed cabbage rolls in tomato sauce)
summary: Classic savoy cabbage rolls with a pork-and-rice filling, braised in broth and served with tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: cooking oil
ingredients.note: for cooking the onion until translucent and parboiling the cabbage

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for mixing with the flour and starch to make a slurry

steps: Core the cabbage, place it core-side down in boiling water with a little oil, and parboil for about 10 minutes.
Peel off the softened leaves with tongs, plunge into cold water to stop cooking, and gently shave down the thick central ribs.
Dice the onion, cook in the remaining oil until translucent, and mix with the minced pork and cooled rice.
Season the filling with salt and pepper, shape into oblong portions, and wrap tightly in the cabbage leaves, folding the sides inward.
Line the bottom of a pot with a few cabbage leaves, pack the rolls tightly together seam-side down, pour in the broth, cover, and simmer for 50–60 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Transfer the cooked cabbage rolls from the pot to a dish, and stir the tomato paste or passata into the remaining cooking liquid.
Whisk the plain flour and potato starch into the cold water, pour slowly into the simmering sauce, season with salt, pepper, basil, and oregano, and simmer for a few minutes more.

name: Potato kugel
summary: Traditional Jewish potato casserole made from finely grated potatoes, onion, matzo meal, and whipped eggs.
steps: Peel and rinse the potatoes and onion, grate them finely, and squeeze out the excess liquid in a colander.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks and beat the whites until stiff peaks form.
Add the egg yolks, whipped egg whites, matzo meal, margarine, salt, and pepper to the potato mixture, folding together thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish greased with sunflower oil and bake in the oven for about 60 minutes until crisp and golden on top.

name: Creamy broccoli sauce
summary: A creamy vegetable sauce made of blended broccoli, onion, carrot, and parsley root braised in butter and broth, finished with sour cream.
steps: Rinse the broccoli, parboil for a few minutes in water with salt and a pinch of sugar, drain, and divide into florets.
Dice the onion, salt it, and set aside for a few minutes to soften, and grate the carrot and parsley root.
Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a deep skillet or wok and cook the onion until tender.
Pour in the vegetable broth, add the grated carrot, parsley root, and broccoli florets, season with black pepper, and simmer for several minutes, stirring occasionally.
Puree the simmered vegetables into a smooth sauce (or leave some florets whole) and stir in the sour cream at the end.

name: Ryba po grecku (Polish Greek-style fish)
summary: Poached fish fillets served under a bed of braised root vegetables and onion in a sweet and sour tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: Polish soup vegetables (carrot, parsley root, celeriac and leek)

steps: Poach the fish fillets in broth made with part of the soup vegetables, the bay leaf, allspice berries, salt, and pepper, then remove the fish and reserve 250 ml of the poaching broth.
Clean the remaining vegetables and onion, then shred or finely dice them.
Heat the oil in a skillet, add the shredded vegetables, season with salt, and fry for about 5 minutes.
Pour in 250 ml of the fish broth and simmer the vegetables covered until tender.
Mix the flour with a small amount of water, ketchup, salt, sugar, and lemon juice, stir into the braised vegetables, and simmer together for about 3 minutes.
Arrange the poached fish in a serving dish, cover with the hot vegetables in sauce, and sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Barszcz biskupi (Lviv-style beetroot borscht with egg)
summary: Traditional Lviv-style borscht made on meat broth with roasted young beetroots and steamed beaten eggs.
steps: Clean and rinse the young beetroots, bake them until tender in the oven (about 45–50 minutes at 190 °C), then peel and grate on a coarse grater.
Wash the eggs and crack them into a bowl with cool or lukewarm broth.
Place the bowl over a water bath and whisk the broth with the eggs for about 10 minutes, until the mixture thickens and becomes frothy.
Combine the whisked broth with the grated beetroots and season to taste with salt, pepper, sugar, and lemon juice.

name: Barszcz dziedzica (Squire's Lviv-style beetroot borscht)
summary: A thick Lviv borscht made with minced young vegetables and beef, enriched with sour cream and flour.
steps: Wash, peel, and rinse the beetroots, carrots, parsley root, and celeriac, then grind them in a meat grinder together with the beef.
Melt the butter in a pot, add the minced vegetables with meat, and fry until lightly browned.
Pour in the water, add salt, and simmer over low heat until the ingredients are tender.
Mix the sour cream with the wheat flour and pour into the simmering borscht.
Season the soup with pepper, sugar, marjoram, pressed garlic, and lemon juice, then simmer for a few more minutes.

name: Pascha (traditional Polish Easter cooked quark dessert)
summary: A rich traditional Easter dessert made by gently heating farmer's cheese with eggs, butter, sour cream, vanilla, and mixed dried fruit and nuts, pressed under weight.
steps: Separate the egg yolks from the whites; beat the yolks with sugar until pale and fluffy, then mix in the sour cream.
Slowly stream in the cooled melted butter while whisking, then gradually beat in the sieved farmer's cheese.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and fold them gently into the cheese mixture along with the chopped almonds, candied peel, raisins, and vanilla pod pieces.
Transfer the mixture to a heavy-bottomed pot and heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the first bubbles appear without letting it boil.
Remove the pot from the heat, fish out the pieces of vanilla pod, and allow the custard to cool, stirring regularly.
Spoon the mixture into a mold lined with cheesecloth, press with a weight, and chill in the refrigerator to drain and firm up.

name: Kołocz śląski z posypką (Silesian streusel yeast cake)
summary: Traditional Silesian yeast cake topped with a generous buttery streusel flavoured with lemon zest and vanilla.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: approx., plus extra for brushing the dough

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: plus 1 tbsp for brushing the dough

steps: Prepare a starter from the yeast, some of the warm milk, and a little plain flour, then set aside to rise.
Beat the whole eggs and egg yolks with the sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the risen starter, beaten eggs and yolks, remaining milk, salt, grated lemon zest, vanilla sugar, and melted butter to the sifted plain flour.
Knead thoroughly into a smooth yeast dough, cover, and set aside in a warm place to rise.

Prepare the streusel: mix the plain flour with the caster sugar and packet of vanilla sugar, add the chilled butter cut into small pieces, chop and briefly work into crumbs, then chill in the refrigerator.
Grease the baking pans with fat, turn out the risen dough, and stretch it out with greased hands.
Set the dough aside in a warm place for a moment to rise again, then brush the top with the milk mixed with 1 tbsp of sugar and scatter the chilled streusel thickly over it.
Place the baking pan in the preheated oven and bake for 45–50 minutes.

name: Szałot (Silesian potato and herring salad)
summary: A traditional Silesian potato salad with salted herring, fermented brine pickles, onion, and rendered smoked bacon or fatback.
steps: Wash the potatoes and boil in their skins in water seasoned with caraway seeds, then cool, peel, and cut into large dice.
Soak the salted herrings in cold water for about 60 minutes, remove skin and bones, and slice into thin strips.
Peel the fermented pickles, onion, and optionally the apple, then dice everything finely.
Combine the potatoes, herrings, pickles, onion, and apple, seasoning with salt, pepper, and vinegar or pickle brine.
Finely dice the smoked fatback or bacon, render in a skillet, pour over the salad together with the rendered fat, and toss gently.

name: Placki z cukinii (Polish zucchini herb fritters)
summary: Golden Polish summer fritters made from shredded zucchini folded with fresh mint, dill, and parsley leaves.
steps: Wash and peel the zucchini, grate on a fine grater, and squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly.
Transfer the squeezed zucchini to a bowl, crack in the eggs, add sifted wheat flour, chopped parsley leaves, fresh mint, and dill.
Season the mixture with salt, black pepper, and hot paprika, and stir into a cohesive batter.
Heat oil in a skillet, drop spoonfuls of batter, fry the fritters on both sides until golden brown, and drain on kitchen paper.

name: Mayonnaise
summary: Homemade mustard mayonnaise whipped from raw egg yolks and vegetable oil.
steps: Place the raw egg yolks into a bowl, add the mustard, and whisk thoroughly with a kitchen whisk.
Slowly pour in 250 ml of vegetable oil in small portions while whisking constantly, taking care that the emulsion does not split.
Whisk until a uniform, stiff emulsion forms, and finally season to taste with salt and black pepper.

name: Piña colada
summary: A sweet Caribbean cocktail made with fresh pineapple, coconut milk, buttermilk, and rum.
steps: Peel the half pineapple, cut out the tough core, chop the flesh into chunks, and blend in a blender until smooth.
Pour in the chilled coconut milk, buttermilk, and rum, then blend again until well combined.
Season the cocktail to taste with lemon juice and pour into glasses.

name: Italian pizza dough
summary: Classic Italian yeast pizza dough made with wheat flour, water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar.
steps: Add the dried yeast, sugar, and salt to a large bowl, pour in the cold boiled water, and stir until the yeast is completely dissolved.
Add the wheat flour, stir, and knead by hand on a work surface for about 5–10 minutes until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Return the dough to the bowl, slash a cross on top, cover with a clean kitchen towel, and set aside in a warm place for about 30 minutes until doubled in volume.
Briefly punch down the risen dough, divide it into 2–4 portions, and stretch by hand or roll out thinly into rounds.
Place the shaped dough on a preheated baking sheet and bake in an oven heated to maximum temperature for 4–15 minutes (or at 180 °C for about 30 minutes).

name: Lasagne napoli
summary: Vegetarian lasagne layered with Neapolitan tomato sauce, béchamel, and firm cheese.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
In an ovenproof dish, alternately layer the lasagne sheets, 750 ml of Napoli sauce, 500 ml of béchamel sauce, and grated firm cheese.
Sprinkle the top generously with the remaining grated cheese and season with oregano, thyme, and basil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes at 180 °C.

name: Lasagne pasta sheets
summary: Homemade lasagne pasta sheets made from wheat flour and eggs.
steps: Pour the flour into a bowl, make a well in the center, and crack the eggs into it.
Knead the flour with the eggs, gradually adding lukewarm water until you obtain a smooth dough suitable for rolling out.
Divide the dough into portions, roll out into thin sheets 1–2 mm thick, and cut into rectangular strips about 10 cm wide and 20–30 cm long.
Drop the pasta sheets one by one into boiling water with 1 tablespoon of olive oil added and cook.

name: Bolognese sauce
summary: A classic Bolognese ragù made with ground beef, smoked bacon, and soup vegetables (włoszczyzna), slowly simmered with milk, red wine, and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: canned tomatoes
ingredients.note: cans, or 1 can of tomatoes and 1 small jar of tomato puree

steps: Peel the carrots and grate them coarsely, finely dice the celery and smoked bacon, chop the onion and garlic, and blend the canned tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a deep frying pan with a lid, fry the smoked bacon until golden, then add the onion and garlic and cook until translucent.
Add the grated carrots and celery, and saute for a few minutes, stirring, until the vegetables soften.
Add the ground beef and fry, stirring constantly and breaking up lumps, until it has changed colour throughout.
Pour in the milk, stir, and simmer until partly reduced, then pour in the red wine and reduce as well.
Add the pureed tomatoes, bay leaves, and several peppercorns, and mix thoroughly.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer the sauce for at least 120 minutes, stirring occasionally, and towards the end season to taste with a pinch of sugar and salt.

name: Pizza calzone (folded stuffed pizza)
summary: Italian folded turnover pizza stuffed with sautéed sliced mushrooms, tomatoes, mozzarella, and Parmesan.
steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C and lightly brush a large sheet of baking parchment with olive oil.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a deep skillet, add the sliced mushrooms and crushed garlic clove, and fry for 7–10 minutes until the mushrooms soften and most of the liquid evaporates.
Stir in the chopped parsley leaves, season with salt, mix well, remove the pan from the heat, and discard the garlic.
Divide the risen pizza dough into 2 equal portions, roll them out into rounds 3 mm thick, and transfer onto the baking paper.
Spread the chopped canned tomatoes over half of each round, leaving a 2 cm border around the edges, then top with mozzarella, sautéed mushrooms, and grated Parmesan.
Fold the dough rounds in half over the filling and crimp the edges firmly with your fingers.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 30 minutes until golden brown and serve hot.

name: Tartar sauce (Sos tatarski)
summary: A cold mayonnaise-based sauce with fermented and vinegar pickles, canned peas, leek, and a touch of horseradish.

ingredients.name: leek
ingredients.note: about 10 cm of the white part

steps: Finely dice the fermented pickles and vinegar pickles.
Mince the white part of the leek as finely as possible and sprinkle with salt.
Combine the diced pickles and leek with the drained peas and mayonnaise.
Season the sauce with pepper and optionally a touch of horseradish, then mix thoroughly.

name: Egg salad with herb dressing (Sałatka z jajek w sosie ziołowym)
summary: A light salad for two featuring hard-boiled eggs, avocado, fresh crisp vegetables, and a creamy herb yogurt dressing with balsamic vinegar.

ingredients.name: fresh herbs
ingredients.note: finely chopped (such as parsley, mint, chives)

steps: Cut the hard-boiled eggs in half lengthwise.
Gently toss together the lettuce leaves, sliced tomatoes, cucumber slices, grated carrot, and avocado quarters.
Divide the vegetable mixture between two plates and arrange the egg halves on top.
Combine the plain yogurt, chopped herbs, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper in a small jar or blender, then shake vigorously or blend until smooth.
Drizzle the salad with the yogurt-herb dressing and dust with a pinch of ground paprika.

name: Mazurek cytrynowy (lemon Polish Easter flat cake)
summary: Traditional Polish Easter mazurek on a shortcrust base made with cooked egg yolks, covered in thick lemon curd and candied lemon slices.
steps: Rub the hard-boiled egg yolks through a sieve, chop the butter with the wheat flour, combine with the yolks and powdered sugar, and quickly knead with fingertips into coarse crumbs.
Chill the dough in the freezer, press evenly and flat onto a square baking tin, and bake at 150 °C until the edges are lightly browned, then cool.
Mix the lemon juice, 300 ml of sugar, and the eggs, and whisk in a water bath for 6–8 minutes until thick.
Chill the lemon mixture until set and spread in an even layer over the baked crust.
Bring the water to a boil with the remaining 150 ml of sugar in a wide pot.
Scrub the lemon, cut into very thin slices, place in the boiling syrup, and cook over high heat, shaking the pot, until the white pith becomes translucent.
Cool the lemon slices slightly, arrange them on top of the lemon layer, decorate with almond flakes, and store the cake in a cool place.

name: Charleston (warm chocolate brownie cake)
summary: A rich American brownie-style chocolate cake covered with a dark chocolate and cream glaze, served warm with whipped cream.
steps: Melt 400 g of dark chocolate (4 bars) together with the butter in a water bath, then let cool slightly.
Beat the whole eggs, add the plain flour and sugar, and mix into the cooled chocolate mixture.
Pour the batter onto a large baking sheet or baking pan and bake for 12 to 20 minutes in an oven preheated to 200 °C.
While the cake bakes, bring the whipping cream to a boil and melt the remaining 100 g of dark chocolate in it.
Pour the prepared chocolate glaze over the baked cake and serve warm with whipped cream.

name: Tiramisu
summary: A classic Italian layered dessert of ladyfingers soaked in coffee and amaretto, layered with a cream of mascarpone, egg yolks, and Marsala wine.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: additional egg yolks can be added

steps: Brew 200 ml of strong coffee (preferably espresso), add 2 to 6 tablespoons of amaretto liqueur, and set aside to cool.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites, and beat the yolks with the icing sugar using a mixer until pale and fluffy.
Gradually add the mascarpone and a tablespoon of Marsala wine to the yolks, mixing until a smooth, lump-free cream forms.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then very gently fold them into the mascarpone and yolk mixture with a spatula.
Briefly dip each ladyfinger into the cooled coffee with amaretto and arrange an even layer across the bottom of the dish.
Spread half of the cream over the ladyfingers and dust the top with sifted cocoa powder, then arrange a second layer of soaked ladyfingers and the remaining cream.
Refrigerate the dessert for 24 hours, and just before serving, generously dust the top with unsweetened cocoa powder.

name: Lemonade with lemon, orange, and mint
summary: Refreshing lemonade with lemon and orange juice and slices, sweetened with brown sugar syrup.
steps: Boil 250 ml of water, dissolve 3 tablespoons of brown sugar in it, let cool, and pour the syrup into a pitcher.
Thoroughly wash the lemon and orange, cut the fruits in half, and squeeze out their juice.
Slice the remaining portions of the fruits into rounds, place them into the pitcher, and pour in the squeezed juice.
Top up the pitcher with still mineral water, stir thoroughly, add fresh mint leaves, and refrigerate to chill.

name: Blood orange sorbet
summary: A refreshing Italian sorbet made from freshly squeezed blood orange juice and sugar syrup, served with an orange slice and mint.
steps: Squeeze the juice from the 4 blood oranges.
Dissolve the sugar in 400 ml of water and simmer over low heat until a thick syrup forms.
Combine the syrup with the orange juice, cool completely (about 15 minutes), and freeze for at least 180 minutes, stirring occasionally with a spoon.
Remove the frozen sorbet from the freezer, let stand for 2–3 minutes, then chop with a knife and blend.
Spoon the sorbet into tall glasses and garnish with orange slices and mint leaves.

name: Strawberry lemonade
summary: A quick lemonade made from blended strawberries, lemon juice, powdered sugar, and fresh mint.
steps: Wash the strawberries under cold running water, hull them, and place into a tall container or blender jug.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the strawberries, add a few fresh mint leaves and 3 tablespoons of powdered sugar, and blend into a smooth puree.
Pour the strawberry puree into a pitcher, add 1 l of water, stir thoroughly, and serve with ice cubes and the remaining mint.

name: Raspberry lemonade
summary: Homemade lemonade with sieved raspberry puree, fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup, and mint.
steps: Rinse the raspberries in a sieve, set aside 40 g of whole berries for garnish, and blend the remaining 260 g with a blender into a puree and strain through a sieve.
Wash and dry the lemons; cut one into half-slices about 0.5 cm thick, place in the bottom of a pitcher, and pour in 750 ml of cold water.
Squeeze about 200 ml of juice from the remaining two lemons.
Heat the remaining 250 ml of water in a pot, add 150 g of sugar, stir until completely dissolved, and chill the resulting syrup.
Pour the lemon juice, raspberry puree, and cooled syrup into the pitcher, add a mint sprig rolled in your hands, stir, and refrigerate to chill.
Before serving, drop ice cubes and the reserved whole raspberries into the pitcher or tumblers.

name: Limeade
summary: Zesty citrus limeade with fresh mint, sugar, and ice.
steps: Pound the fresh mint leaves with 1 tablespoon of sugar.
Squeeze the juice from one lime, and slice the other into rounds.
Dissolve the remaining 3 tablespoons of sugar in 1.5 l of spring water, then add the muddled mint, juice, and lime slices.
Stir everything thoroughly, add ice, and serve.

name: Watermelon lemonade
summary: Chilled lemonade made from blended watermelon with plenty of juice and zest from lemons and limes.
steps: Grate 1 teaspoon each of lemon and lime zest, and squeeze the juice from the fruits.
Transfer the watermelon flesh into a blender, pour in the lemon and lime juice, add the grated citrus zest and 6 tablespoons of sugar.
Blend the ingredients until smooth and the sugar is completely dissolved.
Pour in 500 ml of water, stir again, transfer into a pitcher, and refrigerate to chill.

name: Blackberry lemonade
summary: Lemonade with strained fresh blackberry puree, mint, and ice.
steps: Prepare a syrup from 200 g of sugar and 250 ml of water, then pour in 250 ml of lemon juice and stir.
Blend 60 ml of blackberries, pass the puree through a sieve, and combine with the lemon syrup.
Top up the drink with 1 l of water and stir.
Add ice and mint leaves, and garnish with lemon slices.

name: Lemon, lime, and mint lemonade
summary: Homemade citrus lemonade sweetened with honey, featuring fresh mint and ice.
steps: Cut the lemons and limes in half.
Squeeze the juice from three lemon halves and three lime halves, and slice the remaining two halves into slices.
Place the sliced citrus into a pitcher, add honey, pour in the squeezed juice and 2 l of water, and stir until the honey dissolves.
Add the sprigs of fresh mint and ice cubes to the drink.

name: Lody śmietankowe (traditional cream ice cream)
summary: Three-ingredient homemade ice cream made from rich whipping cream (30–36%), milk, and sugar.
steps: Pour 200 ml of whipping cream into a pot, add 65 g of sugar, and heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar dissolves completely.
Remove the pot from the heat, pour into a container, add the remaining 200 ml of whipping cream and 200 ml of milk, and mix thoroughly with a whisk or hand mixer.
Place the container in the refrigerator and chill the mixture.

Freeze the chilled mixture in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's instructions, or place the container in the freezer for 3–4 hours, blending the contents every 30 minutes to break up ice crystals.

name: Vanilla ice cream
summary: Classic vanilla ice cream based on crème anglaise made from egg yolks, whole milk, a vanilla bean, and whipping cream.
steps: Pour 500 ml of milk into a small saucepan, add two-thirds of the 125 g of sugar along with the seeds scraped from the vanilla bean, stir, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg yolks with the remaining sugar into a pale, fluffy cream.
Pour the boiling milk into the whisked yolks while stirring constantly with a whisk, then pour everything back into the saucepan.
Heat the custard over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until it thickens and lightly coats the back of the spoon, without letting it boil.
Remove from the heat, pour into a bowl, allow to cool, cover with cling film, and chill in the refrigerator.
Mix the cold crème anglaise with 100 ml of chilled whipping cream, churn in an ice cream maker, then transfer to a container and freeze for several hours.

name: Lody owocowe (fruit and meringue ice cream)
summary: Homemade whipped cream ice cream with crushed meringues, peaches, and fruit simmered in syrup.
steps: Cut the grapes in half lengthwise, place in a pot together with the raspberries, add 4 tablespoons of sugar, and pour in 250 ml of water.
Simmer the fruit over low heat for 20–30 minutes until a syrup forms, then set aside to cool completely.
Whip 300 ml of 30% whipping cream until stiff, add 125 ml of crushed meringues, diced peaches, and 2–4 tablespoons of the cooled fruit in syrup.
Gently fold the mixture and place in the freezer until set.

name: Coconut water lemonade
summary: Tropical lemonade made from fresh coconut water, red grapefruits, limes, melon, and agave syrup.
steps: Crack the top of the coconut and pour out the coconut water. Peel half of the melon and dice into cubes.
Squeeze the juice from the limes and red grapefruits.
Place the ice cubes into a blender, pour in the coconut water, squeezed citrus juice, and agave syrup, add half of the diced melon, and blend.
Pour the lemonade into tumblers and garnish with the remaining melon pieces and fresh mint leaves.

name: Grapefruit lemonade
summary: Zesty lemonade made from pink grapefruits, limes, and cardamom with fresh lemongrass and basil.
steps: Crush the cardamom seeds in a mortar, bring to a boil with 200 g of sugar and 200 ml of water, simmer over low heat for 3 minutes, then cool and strain through a sieve.
Squeeze the juice from 3 grapefruits and 2 limes and combine with the cardamom syrup.
Trim the lemongrass, cut into large pieces, add to the citrus base, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Peel the remaining grapefruit, slice into thin rounds, and distribute into tumblers together with ice cubes and fresh basil leaves.
Remove the lemongrass, pour the lemonade base into tumblers, and top up with 600 ml of chilled sparkling water.

name: Herbal lemonade
summary: Lemonade made with a syrup infused with fresh mint, thyme, basil, lemon balm, rosemary, and sage.
steps: Scald 2 lemons with boiling water, wipe dry, and pare the zest very thinly. Squeeze the juice from all 5 lemons, measuring out 300 ml of juice.
Combine 300 ml of lemon juice with 300 g of sugar and 100 ml of water, bring to a boil, boil over high heat for 3 minutes, then let cool.
Wash and dry the mint, thyme, basil, lemon balm, rosemary, and sage, add together with the lemon zest to the lukewarm syrup, and set aside for 2–3 hours.
Strain the base through a sieve into a pitcher or bottles and top up with 1.5 l of chilled sparkling water.

name: Lemon-ginger lemonade
summary: A bold lemonade made with freshly extracted lemon and ginger juice, sweetened with maple syrup or honey.
steps: Peel the lemons, leaving a little zest on one fruit. Scrub the ginger and cut into smaller pieces.
Pass the lemons and ginger alternately through a juicer.
Combine the extracted lemon-ginger juice with 80 ml of maple syrup or honey, apple cider vinegar, and 1.5 l of cold water.
Place ice cubes and lemon slices into a pitcher, pour in the prepared lemonade, and stir.

name: Strawberry mint lemonade
summary: Summer lemonade made with pureed fresh strawberries, fresh mint, and mineral water.
steps: Wash the strawberries, remove the hulls, add the washed mint leaves, and blend with a blender into a smooth puree.
Add powdered sugar or honey, juice from half a lemon, and 1.5 l of chilled mineral water, stir thoroughly, and strain through a sieve if desired.
Place ice cubes and slices from the other half of the lemon into tumblers and pour in the strawberry lemonade.

name: Honey lemonade
summary: Sparkling lemonade sweetened with honey and served with fresh mint and ice.
steps: Squeeze the juice from one and a half lemons.
Sweeten 1.5 l of sparkling water with honey and stir until dissolved.
Pour in the squeezed lemon juice, add ice and fresh mint leaves, and stir.

name: Szarlotka (Polish apple pie)
summary: Classic Polish apple pie made with shortcrust pastry and apples, topped with a pastry lattice, icing sugar and cinnamon.
steps: Mix the flour with the baking powder, add the diced butter, and chop the ingredients together with a knife.
Add the salt, sugar, egg yolk, and sour cream, quickly knead into a dough, and chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Peel and core the apples, then cut them into small slices or grate them on a coarse grater.
Roll out half of the dough, line the bottom and high edges of a greased and floured springform tin, and prick the base with a fork.
Bake the base in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 10 minutes, then remove and cool in the tin.
Spread the prepared apples over the partially baked base, shape the remaining dough into rolls as thick as your little finger, and arrange them in a lattice on top.
Bake the apple pie at 200 °C for about 40 minutes until golden, then dust the hot pastry with icing sugar and cinnamon.

name: Greek salad (choriatiki)
summary: Classic Greek village salad with tomatoes, cucumber, sweet bell pepper, red onion, olives, and feta, dressed with olive oil and oregano.
steps: Cut the tomatoes and sweet pepper into bite-sized wedges, and slice the cucumber and red onion into thick rounds.
Place the vegetables into a salad bowl and toss gently with the olives and diced feta cheese.
Drizzle with the olive oil and wine vinegar, then season to taste with salt and oregano.

name: Imam (stuffed eggplant)
summary: Baked eggplants stuffed with an aromatic filling of gently cooked onions, garlic, tomatoes, and parsley, drizzled with olive oil.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 4 tbsp for drizzling and about 2 tbsp for frying

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for braising onions and diluting paste

steps: Trim the stalks from the eggplants, make 2–3 lengthwise slits in each, salt well, and set aside for about 60 minutes.
Rinse the eggplants, squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly, and sauté in heated olive oil on all sides until golden.
Slice the onions and simmer in a splash of lightly salted water until the liquid evaporates.
Mix the braised onions with sliced garlic, diced tomatoes, and the tomato paste diluted in 125 ml of warm water, then season with salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Arrange the eggplants on a baking tray and stuff the slits with the prepared thick filling.
Sprinkle with the chopped fresh parsley leaves, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Mutzerta (moutzendra / Cypriot lentils and rice with browned onions)
summary: A traditional Cypriot dish of lentils cooked with rice and served with onions browned in olive oil.
steps: Cover the lentils with plenty of water and cook for about 30 minutes, until they begin to soften.
Add the rice to the simmering lentils, season with salt and pepper, and cook over low heat for another 20–30 minutes, until the grains absorb the liquid.
Slice the onions and fry in heated olive oil until golden.
Stir the browned onions along with their oil into the cooked lentils and rice before serving.

name: Corfiot veal sofrito (Sofrito Kerkyraiko)
summary: A traditional Greek dish from Corfu of veal cutlets braised with plenty of garlic in olive oil, white wine, and fresh parsley sauce.
steps: Brown the veal chops with finely chopped garlic in heated olive oil in a deep skillet.
Once the meat is browned, pour in 125 ml of water, season with salt and pepper, and braise covered over low heat for about 50 minutes until tender, then transfer the veal to a platter.
Dust the remaining sauce in the pan with the flour and stir until lightly browned.
Pour in the dry white wine and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens.
Pour the hot sauce over the veal chops and sprinkle with finely chopped parsley.

name: Keftedes (Greek meatballs)
summary: Greek veal meatballs flavoured with fresh mint, parsley, sparkling water, and anise-flavoured ouzo.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: for the meat mixture, plus extra for frying

steps: Soak the bread slices in water and squeeze out thoroughly, grate the onion, and finely chop the parsley and mint.
Combine the minced veal with the squeezed bread, grated onion, egg, 125 ml of sparkling water, the ouzo, parsley, mint, and 2 tbsp of olive oil.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper, knead thoroughly, and refrigerate for about 60 minutes.
Shape the chilled mixture into small balls, dredge them in plain flour, and fry in hot olive oil in a deep skillet for 15 minutes.

name: Sałatka szopska (Shopska salad)
summary: A traditional Bulgarian salad of tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, and onion drizzled with oil and generously topped with grated sirene or feta cheese and olives.
steps: Wash the vegetables, deseed the peppers, then dice the tomatoes, cucumber, and bell peppers, and finely chop the peeled onion.
Transfer the vegetables to a salad bowl, drizzle with olive or sunflower oil, and toss gently.
Top the salad generously with coarsely grated sirene or feta cheese, chopped parsley, and olives, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Barcelona-style chicken salad (Sałatka z kurczaka po barcelońsku)
summary: Tender roasted chicken tossed with sweet green peas, marinated bell pepper, walnuts, and raisins in an orange-olive oil dressing.
steps: In a salad bowl, combine the diced roast chicken, cooked green peas, and finely chopped pickled bell pepper, then chill in the refrigerator.
In a small bowl, whisk together the orange juice, olive oil, finely chopped scallion, raisins, and chopped walnuts.
Pour the prepared dressing over the chilled ingredients, toss gently, and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Line a clean salad bowl with fresh lettuce leaves and spoon the prepared salad onto them.

name: Kawarma (Balkan meat and vegetable clay pot bake)
summary: Balkan casserole of meat, potatoes, peppers, onions, and leek baked in wine with savory and mint.
steps: Cut the pork, veal, or chicken into chunks and season lightly with salt, and dice the peeled potatoes.
Dilute the tomato paste in 125 ml of water.
Pour olive oil into the bottom of an earthenware or baking dish, then layer the meat, finely chopped onions, sliced leek, potatoes, and bell peppers.
Pour the diluted tomato paste and wine over the ingredients, and season the top with summer savory, mint, sweet paprika, salt, and pepper.
Bake covered in an oven preheated to 170–180 °C for 45–55 minutes until the meat and potatoes are tender.

name: Gyuvech (Bulgarian pork and vegetable bake)
summary: A Balkan one-pot casserole of pork, potatoes, bell peppers, tomatoes, and okra, baked in a clay dish.
steps: Pour the olive oil into a clay or ovenproof baking dish, add the cubed and salted pork, and roast for about 20 minutes in an oven preheated to 180 °C.
Chop the potatoes, fresh bell peppers, tomatoes, okra, and onion into bite-sized chunks.
Add the vegetables to the partially roasted meat, season with salt, dust with the sweet paprika, and continue baking for about 45 minutes until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Garnish with the chopped parsley leaves and sliced hot chili peppers before serving.

name: Fanouropita (Greek spiced orange and walnut cake)
summary: A traditional Greek Lenten spice cake with orange juice, olive oil, walnuts, and raisins.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: plus extra for dusting the pan

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: approx. 80 ml, plus extra for the pan

steps: Beat the olive oil with the sugar until pale, then pour in the orange juice and stir in the grated orange zest.
Mix the flour with the baking powder, cinnamon, and ground cloves.
Combine the dry ingredients with the water and the orange-oil mixture, beating until a smooth batter forms.
Fold in the raisins and roughly chopped walnuts using a wooden spoon.
Pour the batter into an oiled and floured 25–30 cm round baking tin, and bake for about 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 175 °C.

name: Papryka po florencku (Florentine stuffed green bell peppers)
summary: Baked green bell peppers stuffed with ground beef, spinach, rice, sweet raisins, and fragrant herbs.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C, grease a baking dish with olive oil, and squeeze all excess liquid from the thawed spinach.
Slice off the stem tops from the bell peppers and scoop out the seeds and membranes.
Heat a little olive oil in a skillet, brown the minced beef over medium heat, and drain off any rendered fat.
In a bowl, combine the drained spinach, browned beef, cooked rice, beaten egg white, tomato paste, chopped onion, garlic, raisins, basil, and oregano, and mix thoroughly.
Stuff the hollowed peppers with the prepared filling, scatter with chopped parsley and pickled pepper, and arrange upright in the baking dish.
Bake for about 30 minutes at 190 °C, until the tops are nicely browned.

name: Kruszonka (Streusel crumb topping)
summary: Classic Polish buttery streusel made from plain flour, sugar, and butter, for topping yeast cakes and fruit tarts.
steps: Place the plain flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt into a bowl, then add the butter.
Rub the ingredients together with your hands (or initially using the dough hook attachment of a mixer, then finishing by hand) until evenly combined into coarse crumbs.
Scatter the streusel over cake batter before baking, or spread onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake separately in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 20 minutes until golden brown.

name: Vegan wholemeal streusel
summary: Plant-based crumb topping made with wholemeal flour, cane sugar, and melted vegetable margarine for fruit cakes and cookies.
steps: Place the wholemeal flour and cane sugar into a bowl, then pour in the melted vegan margarine.
Work the ingredients together with your fingers (or first with a mixer dough hook, then finishing by hand) until they form cohesive crumbs ready to scatter over the cake.

name: Banitsa with Cheese (Banica z serem)
summary: A traditional Bulgarian pastry made of layered phyllo pastry sheets filled with crumbled feta cheese and baked in an egg and sparkling water custard.
steps: Grease a baking sheet with a little oil, lay down a layer of phyllo pastry, and scatter with crumbled feta cheese.
Repeat layering the phyllo pastry and feta cheese until all ingredients are used, finishing with pastry on top, then cut into squares or rectangles.
Heat the remaining oil well and pour it over the sliced pastry.
Whisk the eggs with the sparkling mineral water and pour the mixture evenly over the top of the pastry.
Bake the banitsa in an oven preheated to 180–190 °C for about 35 minutes, until the pastry turns golden brown.

name: Banitsa with Minced Meat (Banica z mięsem)
summary: A Bulgarian layered phyllo pie stuffed with savoury seasoned minced meat, roasted peppers, and sautéed onions, baked in a sparkling egg custard.
steps: Roast the bell peppers in the oven or on a grill, peel off the skins, and finely chop.
Peel and finely dice the onions, fry for 1–2 minutes in a portion of the olive oil, then add the minced meat, salt, pepper, and savory, frying and stirring for 3–4 minutes.
Stir the chopped peppers into the meat and divide the filling into 3 equal portions.

Grease a baking sheet with olive oil, place 2 flat sheets and 1 gently crumpled sheet of phyllo on the bottom, spread the first portion of filling, then repeat with more pastry and the remaining portions of filling, covering the top with the last sheets.
Cut the layered pastry into squares or rectangles with a sharp knife.
Whisk the eggs with the sparkling water and remaining olive oil, pour evenly over the top, and bake at 180–190 °C until golden brown.

name: Ryż z fasolą (Spanish brown rice with white kidney beans)
summary: A nourishing Spanish dish of brown rice braised with spring onions, celery, carrot, canned tomatoes, cannellini beans, and fresh herbs.
steps: Dice the spring onions, celery stalk, and peeled carrot, and finely mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil over moderate heat in a large heavy-bottomed pot, add the prepared vegetables, and sauté until tender.
Add the brown rice, pour in the water and tomatoes with their juice, stir thoroughly, reduce the heat, and simmer covered for 40–45 minutes.
Rinse and drain the canned beans, stir into the pot along with the chopped mint or basil, and simmer covered for about 5 minutes, until the rice is tender and the beans are hot.
Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Zupa soczewicowa (Bulgarian lentil soup / Leshta supa)
summary: A traditional Bulgarian lentil soup simmered with olive oil, bell pepper, tomatoes, carrot, and leek.
steps: Rinse the lentils, place in a pot, pour in 1.5–2 l of water and the olive oil.
Peel and finely chop the onion, carrot, leek, and fresh bell pepper, and add to the pot.
Stir in the ground sweet paprika and salt to taste (optionally add crushed garlic mixed with a splash of vinegar).
Simmer the soup over low heat until the lentils are completely tender.
Add the finely diced tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.

name: Turkish spiced minced lamb kebabs (Kofte)
summary: Turkish ground-lamb kebabs with spring onion, garlic, and spices, cooked under a grill or fried in a pan.
steps: Finely chop the spring onions and mix in a large bowl with the ground lamb, granulated garlic, parsley leaves, sweet paprika, allspice, cumin, oregano, egg white, salt, and black pepper.
Divide the meat mixture into 6 portions and shape into elongated kebabs on skewers or 6 oval patties.
Cook under a preheated oven grill or fry in a pan for 4–5 minutes on each side until nicely browned.

name: Spanish almond snowball cookies
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth Spanish almond biscuits rolled into small balls, made with butter, powdered sugar, ground almonds, flour, and vanilla.
steps: Preheat the oven to 165 °C and line a baking sheet (25 × 35 cm) with baking parchment.
Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar in a bowl until pale and fluffy, gradually incorporating the ground almonds, vanilla extract, and flour.
Dust your hands with flour, shape the dough into small balls up to 3 cm in diameter, and arrange them on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15–18 minutes until crisp yet still pale.

name: Greek lemon butter lamb with rice (Arni lemonato)
summary: Greek lamb braised in fresh lemon juice and rich butter, served with rice simmered in the cooking juices.
steps: Trim the lamb and cut into serving portions, chop the onion, and squeeze the juice from the lemons.
Place the meat and onion into a pot, pour in the lemon juice, and braise until the liquid is absorbed.
Add the butter and brown the meat, then season with salt and pepper, pour in the water, and braise covered until tender.
Remove the cooked meat from the pot, stir the rice into the remaining cooking juices, and cook until tender.
Return the lamb to the pot with the rice, warm through for a moment, and serve hot.

name: Valencian orange chicken
summary: Spanish dish of paprika-seasoned chicken pieces braised with spring onions, tomato, parsley, raisins, and orange juice.
steps: Cut the chicken meat into 4 portions and rub evenly with sweet paprika.
Heat the olive oil or rapeseed oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, add the chicken portions, and brown on all sides until golden.
Dice the spring onions and tomato, and add to the chicken along with the chopped parsley.
Pour in the orange juice, stir in the raisins, reduce the heat, and braise covered for 15–20 minutes until the meat is tender, turning the portions once or twice.

name: Paluszki dam (daktyla kyrion / Cypriot almond pastry fingers in syrup)
summary: Traditional Cypriot fried pastries filled with almonds, cinnamon, and rosewater, soaked in a spiced sugar syrup.
steps: Mix the flour with salt, rub in the margarine and 3 tablespoons of olive oil with your fingertips, add the cold water, knead into an elastic dough, and rest for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the chopped almonds with 2 tablespoons of sugar, ground cinnamon, and rosewater.
Bring the syrup ingredients (water, sugar, lemon juice, cloves, and cinnamon stick) to a boil in a saucepan, boil for 5 minutes, and leave to cool.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut into squares about 8 cm on each side, place a teaspoon of almond filling on each, moisten the edges with water, and crimp into finger shapes.
Fry the pastry fingers in very hot olive oil until golden.
Remove the hot pastries with a slotted spoon, dip them one by one in the cold syrup, and arrange on a platter.

name: Zupa kurban (Bulgarian lamb kurban chorba)
summary: A traditional Bulgarian soup slowly simmered with lamb or mutton, root vegetables, hot chili pepper, and mint.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: a little for lightly frying the pepper

steps: Wash the lamb or mutton, place in a pot, and cover with cold salted water.
Add the peeled halved onion, roughly chopped carrot and potatoes, bay leaves, allspice, pepper, and mint.
Simmer the soup over low heat for about 2 hours until the meat becomes completely tender (in the traditional ritual version, the meat is simmered only in salted water without vegetables).
Towards the end of cooking, add the lightly fried hot red chili pepper and season the soup to taste.

name: Herb risotto
summary: Fragrant Greek-style herb risotto with scallions, parsley leaves, dill, tarragon, basil, thyme, and white wine, finished with Parmesan.
steps: Finely chop the scallions, parsley leaves, dill, basil, and tarragon.
Heat the olive oil in a pot, sauté the scallions, then add the rice and fry together for a few minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in 1.25 l of warm water and the dry white wine, add the chopped herbs, part of the thyme, salt, and pepper, and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes until the rice absorbs the liquid.
Sprinkle the finished risotto with grated Parmesan and the rest of the thyme, and serve immediately.

name: Cypriot baked lamb with vegetables (Tavas)
summary: Cypriot casserole (tavas) of lamb leg, potatoes, zucchini, and tomatoes seasoned with cinnamon and caraway.
steps: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes.
Clean, wash, and chop the potatoes, zucchini, onions, and peeled tomatoes, and place in a large casserole dish along with the meat.
Dissolve the tomato paste in the warm water, mix with olive oil, cinnamon, caraway, salt, and black pepper, pour into the dish, and toss thoroughly.
Bake covered in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 90–120 minutes until the meat is fork-tender, adding splashes of water if needed.

name: Pasta z ikry - taramosalata (Greek salted fish roe dip)
summary: A classic Greek dip made from salted fish roe blended with soaked bread, olive oil, lemon juice, and finely chopped onion.
steps: Soak the bread slices in water, remove crusts once softened, squeeze out excess water thoroughly, and mash into a smooth paste.
Add the fish roe and lemon juice, then whisk or blend while pouring in the olive oil in a slow steady stream until a smooth, creamy emulsion forms.
Season with pepper, fold in the very finely chopped onion at the end, and spoon onto a serving plate.

name: Psarosoupa avgolemono (Greek fish soup)
summary: Greek fish soup with rice and puréed vegetables, thickened with an egg-lemon sauce (avgolemono).

ingredients.name: fish such as cod or carp

steps: Clean and rinse the fish, cut into steaks, and season with salt.
Chop the onions, slice the carrot and celeriac into rounds, and peel, seed, and quarter the tomatoes.
Bring 1.5 liters of water to a boil in a pot, add the chopped vegetables, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and olive oil, and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Add the fish pieces to the broth and cook for another 15 minutes, then lift them out onto a plate.
Scoop out the cooked vegetables, puree until smooth, and stir back into the broth.
Add the rice and simmer for about 20 minutes until tender, then remove the pot from the heat.
Beat the eggs with the lemon juice, then slowly pour the mixture into the hot soup while stirring vigorously throughout.
Serve the soup garnished with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Cypriot pumpkin pastries (Kolokotes / Placuszki z dynią)
summary: Traditional Cypriot baked turnovers made with an olive oil pastry, filled with grated pumpkin, bulgur wheat, dark raisins, and cinnamon.
steps: Combine the wheat flour with 125 ml of olive oil and salt, add water, knead into an elastic dough, and set aside for 30 minutes.
Place the grated pumpkin in a colander lined with cheesecloth, toss with a tablespoon of salt, leave to release juices, and squeeze out firmly.
Peel and finely chop the onions, sauté in 6 tablespoons of olive oil, add the drained pumpkin, bulgur, raisins, and cinnamon, and fry while stirring until excess moisture evaporates.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of up to 5 mm, cut rounds 10–15 cm in diameter, place 1–2 tablespoons of filling on each, and crimp the edges.
Bake the turnovers in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes until golden.

name: Sałatka tapuli (Tabbouleh salad)
summary: A Cypriot-style tabbouleh of soaked bulgur wheat, tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, and generous fresh mint and parsley, tossed with olive oil and lemon juice.
steps: Cover the bulgur wheat with water and let stand for 120 minutes to plump, then drain thoroughly.
Combine the drained bulgur with the diced tomatoes and cucumbers and the finely chopped onion.
Add the chopped fresh mint and parsley and toss the ingredients together.
Pour in the olive oil and freshly squeezed lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and mix thoroughly.

name: Koupes (Cypriot bulgur and meat croquettes)
summary: Traditional Cypriot torpedo croquettes with a crisp bulgur and flour shell filled with spiced minced meat, onions, garlic, parsley, and cinnamon.
steps: Mix the bulgur wheat with 110 g of olive oil, add salt and 1250 ml of warm water, and set aside for 2 hours to swell.
Finely chop the onions and garlic, sauté in 3 tablespoons of olive oil, add the minced meat, and cook while stirring constantly until browned.
Stir the chopped parsley, cinnamon, salt, and pepper into the meat, remove from heat, let cool, and mix thoroughly with the egg white.
Add the flour to the soaked bulgur and knead into a dough. Take 1 tablespoon of dough at a time, flatten into an oval, place 1 teaspoon of meat filling in the centre, and seal into oblong croquettes.
Fry the croquettes in very hot olive oil until golden and serve hot.

name: Zupa rybna z włoszczyzny (Polish freshwater fish and vegetable soup)
summary: A classic Polish fish soup made with a broth of bream or pike and Polish soup vegetables, finished with sour cream and flour, and garnished with fresh parsley.

ingredients.name: freshwater fish
ingredients.note: bream or pike (including heads and backbones)

steps: Clean and rinse the fish, separate fillets, and place the meat along with heads, backbones, and chopped soup vegetables into a pot and pour in 2.5 l of cold water.
Simmer the stock over low heat for about 45 minutes, then strain thoroughly.
Whisk the wheat flour into the sour cream, stir into the strained stock, season with pepper, allspice, and salt, and bring briefly to a boil.
Sprinkle the soup with chopped parsley before serving; serve with fish dumplings, noodles, square pasta (łazanki), or firm groat cubes.

name: Kräftströmming (Swedish baked herring)
summary: Swedish casserole of rolled fresh herring fillets topped with tomato slices, fresh dill, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Preheat the oven to 225 °C.
Season the herring fillets with salt on the flesh side, roll them up skin-side inwards, and arrange tightly in a baking dish.
Top the herring rolls with tomato slices, pour over the tomato purée mixed with water, and dot with butter or margarine.
Scatter the chopped dill and breadcrumbs over the top.
Place the dish in the oven and bake for 20–25 minutes.

name: Kebapczeta (Bulgarian grilled minced meat rolls)
summary: Bulgarian oblong grilled minced meat rolls seasoned with summer savory, ground caraway, and black pepper.
steps: Mix the minced meat thoroughly with the ground caraway, ground pepper, summer savory, and salt into a uniform mixture, and refrigerate for 60 minutes.
Shape the chilled mixture into oblong rolls shaped like small sausages.
Grill slowly on a hot barbecue grate, turning regularly so the patties brown evenly and stay juicy inside.

name: French onion soup
summary: Classic onion soup with onions cooked in butter, garlic, and white wine, baked with baguette toasts and yellow cheese.
steps: Peel and slice the onions, cook in a skillet with most of the butter until translucent, dust with the flour, and fry briefly with the chopped garlic.
In a pot, bring 1.5 liters of water to a boil, dissolve the stock cubes, add the sautéed onions, and pour in the white wine.
Season the broth with salt, pepper, and thyme, and simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, butter the baguette slices with the remaining butter and toast in the oven for about 5 minutes.
Ladle the hot soup into ovenproof bowls, top with the baguette toasts sprinkled with grated yellow cheese, and bake briefly in the oven until the cheese melts.

name: Papryka faszerowana serem (baked feta-stuffed sweet peppers / burek piperki)
summary: A Bulgarian snack of sweet bell pepper halves filled with a mixture of crumbled feta and eggs, baked with olive oil.
steps: Cut the peppers in half lengthwise and remove the seeds.
Crumble the feta cheese into a bowl and mix thoroughly with the beaten eggs.
Stuff the pepper halves with the filling, brush generously on the outside with olive oil, and cover with the other halves.
Bake in an oven preheated to 165 °C for about 30 minutes.

name: Saltimbocca alla romana (veal escalopes with prosciutto and sage)
summary: Classic Roman veal escalopes layered with dry-cured ham and fresh sage, pan-fried and braised in dry white wine and cream.
steps: Rinse and pat dry the veal, slice into 6 escalopes, and gently pound to a thickness of about 3 mm.
Top each cutlet with a slice of cured ham and a fresh sage leaf, press firmly, and secure with a toothpick.
Mix the flour with salt and pepper and dredge the escalopes lightly in the seasoned flour.
