Heat the olive oil and butter in a large skillet, add the minced garlic, and fry the escalopes over medium heat for 2–3 minutes on each side.
Transfer the escalopes to a pan, deglaze the skillet with half the white wine, and pour the juices over the meat.
Simmer covered for 5 minutes, then add the rest of the wine and the heavy cream, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for another 10–15 minutes until tender.

name: Caponetti (Italian spinach and breadcrumb dumplings)
summary: Elongated Italian spinach dumplings made with toasted breadcrumbs, eggs, and marjoram, served tossed with melted butter and fresh sage.
steps: Peel and finely chop the onion and stew it gently in olive oil; in a separate pan, fry the breadcrumbs in some of the butter.
Combine the plain flour with the toasted breadcrumbs and onion, then add the beaten eggs, chopped spinach, and dried marjoram.
Pour in the milk, season with salt, work into a smooth dough, and shape into elongated, finger-shaped dumplings.
Drop the dumplings into boiling water, cook until they float to the surface, drain, and serve with the remaining melted butter and finely chopped fresh sage.

name: Carpaccio (beef carpaccio)
summary: An Italian starter of thinly sliced raw beef tenderloin marinated in olive oil and served with Parmesan shavings, capers, and lemon.

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin
ingredients.note: corrected from 50 g — beef and Parmesan amounts were swapped in source

steps: Place the beef tenderloin into the freezer to firm up slightly, then slice with a sharp knife into paper-thin slices.
Cover the meat with olive oil and rest in a cool place for about 120 minutes.
Grate the parmesan on a coarse box grater or shave into thin ribbons.
Lift the beef slices out of the olive oil and arrange them on a plate, season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with Parmesan and brined capers, and drizzle with lemon juice.

name: Salmon scaloppine on spinach
summary: Slow-roasted salmon served on spinach gently stewed in butter with garlic and onion, drizzled with balsamic vinegar.
steps: Rinse and pat dry the salmon, season with part of the sea salt, place in a baking dish, drizzle generously with olive oil, and bake for about 60 minutes in an oven heated to 70 °C.
Season the spinach with pressed garlic, the remaining salt, and pepper, and sauté in the melted butter.
Add the peeled and finely chopped onion to the spinach, simmer briefly together, and stir well.
Divide the slow-roasted salmon into portions, arrange over the spinach, and drizzle with the remaining olive oil and balsamic vinegar before serving.

name: Ciasteczka sanvigilini (San Vigilini cookies)
summary: Traditional crisp Italian cookies from Trentino made with brandy-soaked raisins, lemon zest, and butter, dusted with icing sugar.
steps: Pour the brandy over the raisins and set aside for about 60 minutes.
Sift the plain flour onto a pastry board, add the chopped chilled butter, sugar, eggs, baking powder, lemon zest, and salt, and knead into a smooth dough.
Add the drained raisins, knead briefly to distribute, wrap in clingfilm, and chill for about 60 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, roll the dough into walnut-sized balls, place onto a baking sheet lined with baking paper, and bake on the middle rack for about 15 minutes.
Cool the baked cookies, transfer to a platter, and dust with icing sugar.

name: Chicken escalopes with eggplant
summary: Tender chicken breast escalopes pan-fried in butter and olive oil, served over braised eggplant and tomatoes seasoned with scallions, garlic, and curry.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a deep skillet, add the chopped scallions, quartered tomatoes, and chopped eggplants, and fry over high heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the crushed garlic, sliced lemon half, salt, pepper, and pinch of curry, fry for another 5 minutes, then cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.
Rinse and pat dry the chicken fillets, slice into cutlets, lightly pound to a thickness of about 1 cm, and dredge in flour.
In a separate pan, heat the remaining tablespoon of olive oil with the butter, season the meat with salt and pepper, and fry on both sides for 3–4 minutes.
Transfer the braised vegetables to a serving platter, arrange the fried chicken escalopes on top, and drizzle with the juice squeezed from the remaining lemon half.

name: Ciasteczka novaroni (Novaroni sponge fingers)
summary: Delicate Italian vanilla sponge finger biscuits piped onto a baking tray and finished with crunchy granulated sugar.
steps: Sift together the plain flour and potato starch with a pinch of salt.
Whisk the eggs over steam with the sugar and vanilla sugar until fluffy, then gradually add the sifted flour mixture while continuing to beat.
Using a piping bag, pipe fingers of batter about 10 cm long onto a baking sheet lined with baking paper, and sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Bake in an oven preheated to 160–180 °C until pale golden, let cool slightly, remove from the paper, and leave to cool completely on a plate.

name: Lisbon-style spinach and sardine bake (Zapiekanka lizbońska)
summary: A quick Portuguese casserole of spinach squeezed dry, canned sardines, grated onion, and chopped hard-boiled egg, baked with a breadcrumb and butter topping.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: part for the mixture, part for topping

ingredients.name: butter (or margarine)
ingredients.note: for greasing the dish and dotting on top

steps: Cook the spinach until tender in a small amount of salted water, then drain and squeeze out all excess moisture thoroughly.
Grate the onion, drain the sardines from the oil, remove the backbones, and flake with a fork.
Mix the spinach with the flaked sardines, grated onion, some of the breadcrumbs, lemon juice, and finely chopped hard-boiled egg, and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the mixture into a greased baking dish, sprinkle the top with the remaining breadcrumbs, and dot with cold butter shavings.
Bake in a preheated oven for 20–30 minutes until the top is lightly golden; serve alone or as a side to fish or poultry.

name: Spanakopita (Szpinak w cieście)
summary: Greek spinach pie made with layers of filo pastry stuffed with fresh spinach, sheep's cheese, onions, dill, eggs, and unsweetened evaporated milk.
steps: Rinse the spinach, remove tough stems, finely chop the leaves, sprinkle with salt, and let stand for 15 minutes; meanwhile, finely chop the onions and dill.
Prepare the filo sheets and cover with a cloth to prevent drying out.
Firmly squeeze excess liquid from the spinach, combine with the onion, dill, crumbled sheep's cheese, unsweetened evaporated milk, beaten eggs, and half the oil, and season with pepper and nutmeg.
Brush a baking dish with part of the remaining oil, line bottom and sides with half the filo pastry, spread the spinach filling, cover with the remaining pastry, and brush the top with oil.
Bake in a well-preheated oven at 180 °C for 60 minutes and serve piping hot.

name: Kapuśniak portugalski (Portuguese savoy cabbage soup).
summary: Thick Portuguese soup made with savoy cabbage and potatoes in broth with olive oil, garlic, and parmesan.
steps: Bring the broth to a boil, add the peeled, diced potatoes, and cook for 15 minutes.
Wash and finely shred the savoy cabbage, add to the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and cook for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the olive oil, add the pressed garlic and grated parmesan, stir, and heat over low heat until the soup is very thick.

name: Filo pastry
summary: Paper-thin Greek and Balkan pastry made from wheat flour, olive oil, eggs, and water, used for baklava and savoury pastries.
steps: Sift the wheat flour into a large mixing bowl and slowly drizzle in the olive oil while working the dough vigorously.
Pour in the lightly beaten eggs whisked with water and knead firmly until a smooth, pliable dough forms.
Roll the dough out slightly on a floured surface, cover with a damp kitchen cloth, and let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions, roll each out on a floured surface until paper-thin, dusting with flour as needed, then leave to air-dry slightly.

name: Farfel (Jewish egg noodle pellets)
summary: Traditional Jewish small egg noodles made from a stiff egg-and-flour dough, served with soups and fish dishes.
steps: Whisk the eggs with a fork, pour into the flour, and knead by hand for about 5 minutes into a very stiff, compact dough.
Divide the dough into smaller portions, roll into finger-thick ropes, and set aside to dry slightly.
Chop the dried dough ropes into tiny pellets the size of rice grains and leave to dry completely.
Before serving, drop the farfel into boiling salted water and cook for about 5 minutes, then drain.

name: Beef scaloppine alla napoletana with capers
summary: Thin beef escalopes browned in butter and olive oil, then braised until tender with capers and wine vinegar.
steps: Slice the beef into escalopes, gently pound to a thickness of about 5 mm, and dredge in plain flour.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a skillet, add the scaloppine, and fry for 2–3 minutes on each side until golden.
Add the capers, pour in a few tablespoons of water, season with salt and pepper, and simmer covered over low heat until the meat is tender.
Pour in the wine vinegar, uncover the skillet, and cook for another 2 minutes.
Garnish with the chopped parsley leaves and stir gently before serving.

name: Fondue savoyarde (cheese fondue)
summary: Classic Alpine cheese fondue made from three melting cheeses—Beaufort, Comté, and Emmental—melted in dry white wine with garlic and kirsch.
steps: Cut the stale bread into bite-sized cubes, and finely slice or grate the Beaufort, Comté, and Emmental cheeses.
Peel the garlic clove and rub the inside of the fondue pot or heavy-bottomed saucepan thoroughly with it.
Pour the dry white wine whisked with the potato starch into the pot and heat gently over low heat, stirring constantly.
Gradually add portions of the cheese, stirring until the mixture is uniform and smooth.
Stir in the kirsch, season with ground pepper, and mix well.
Place the fondue pot over a tabletop burner and serve with the bread cubes for dipping.

name: Giouvetsi (Greek baked lamb with orzo pasta)
summary: Greek casserole (giouvetsi) of lamb slices and orzo pasta in a tomato, garlic, and wine sauce.
steps: Slice the lamb, season with salt, herbes de Provence, and sweet paprika, and sear in one-third of the olive oil.
Transfer the meat to a baking dish, drizzle with another one-third of the olive oil, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C until tender, basting with wine and water.
Finely chop the garlic, crush the canned tomatoes with a fork, and simmer together in the remaining olive oil over low heat until slightly thickened.
Mix the hot tomato sauce with the dry orzo pasta, pour over the baked meat, add extra water if needed, and bake in the oven until the pasta is tender.

name: Karp po żydowsku (Jewish gefilte fish carp in sweet almond jelly)
summary: Stuffed carp in a sweetish aspic with almonds and raisins (traditional gefilte fish).
steps: Scale the carp, cut off head, fins, and tail, eviscerate without slitting the belly open, and carefully peel the skin off whole.
Debone the meat, place the fish heads without eyes and the backbones in a saucepan with water, simmer to make a fish stock, and strain.
Grind the fish meat in a meat grinder together with the soaked and squeezed matzo and 350 g of peeled onions.
Combine the fish mixture with egg yolks, beaten egg white foam, and 80 g of blanched, peeled, and chopped almonds, then season with salt, sugar, and pepper.
Stuff the carp skin with the filling, arrange in a wide pan, pour over warm fish stock, and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining 200 g of finely chopped onions, 50 g of chopped almonds, and the raisins to the broth, season with salt, pepper, and sugar, and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Towards the end of cooking, dissolve the pre-soaked gelatin in the hot broth.
Remove the cooked fish, slice into portions, arrange on a serving platter, pour over the broth, garnish with celery leaves and dill, and chill until set.

name: Pstrąg po galicyjsku (Galician-style trout with horseradish)
summary: Whole pan-fried trout rubbed with garlic, stuffed with parsley leaves, drizzled with lemon juice, and topped with freshly grated horseradish before serving.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: part for juice, part sliced for garnish

steps: Clean the trout, leaving the heads on after removing the eyes, rinse several times in cold water, and pat dry thoroughly.
Mince and crush the garlic cloves, and squeeze the juice from the lemons.
Rub the fish with crushed garlic and salt, season lightly with pepper, stuff the cavities with parsley leaves, and drizzle with lemon juice.
Place the trout into a skillet with well-heated oil and fry for 15 minutes on both sides.
Before serving, sprinkle the fried fish with freshly grated horseradish and garnish with halved lemon slices.

name: Bob chorba (Bulgarian bean soup / Bob czorba)
summary: A traditional Bulgarian soup of dry white beans simmered with onions, hot chili peppers, and fresh mint, seasoned with vinegar (richer version includes soup vegetables and paprika roux).

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking and fresh for cooking

steps: Sort and wash the dry beans, cover with cold water, and leave to soak overnight.
The next day, drain the soaking water (or bring to a boil and discard the first water), cover the beans with about 2 liters of fresh water, and simmer over low heat until tender.

Add the chopped onions, hot chili peppers, and ground paprika to the tender beans and simmer for about 30 minutes more (in variant II, also add finely chopped carrot, celery stalk, and parsley greens, and thicken the soup with a roux of oil, flour, and paprika).
Towards the end of cooking, season the soup with salt and vinegar to taste, and after removing from the heat, sprinkle generously with finely chopped fresh mint.

name: Spicy garlic prawns in white wine
summary: Large prawns braised with garlic, fiery chili pepper, rosemary, and semi-dry white wine, finished in the pan with mayonnaise.
steps: Finely chop the onion, slice the garlic thinly, and deseed the chili peppers and cut them into strips.
Heat the grapeseed oil in a frying pan, add the onion and garlic, and cook until translucent without browning.
Add the chili strips and fry briefly.
Pour in the white wine, strip the leaves from the rosemary sprig into the pan, and reduce the liquid over high heat.
Add the prawns and cook over high heat until any released liquid evaporates, the prawns curl, and their tails turn pink.
Stir in the mayonnaise right in the pan and serve immediately while hot.

name: Coconut ice cream
summary: Four-ingredient frozen dessert made from coconut milk, Greek yogurt, agave syrup, and cane sugar.
steps: Pour 400 ml of coconut milk and 400 ml of Greek yogurt into a bowl and mix.
Gradually add the agave syrup and cane sugar, mixing thoroughly.
Place the mixture in the freezer for 1–2 hours or until the desired consistency is reached, taking it out halfway through freezing to stir.

name: Janssons frestelse (Swedish potato and anchovy casserole)
summary: Swedish potato casserole with anchovies, onions, and sour cream.
steps: Preheat the oven to 225 °C.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into strips, slice or finely chop the onions, and cut the anchovies into smaller pieces.
Grease a baking dish with butter.
Layer the potatoes, onions, and anchovies in the dish, starting and finishing with a layer of potatoes.
Pour half of the sour cream (150 ml) over the casserole, sprinkle with a thin layer of breadcrumbs, and place in the oven.
After 30 minutes of baking, pour the remaining sour cream over the dish and bake for another 15 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the potatoes are tender.

name: Naleśniki ze szpinakiem i serem feta (spinach and feta stuffed crepes)
summary: Savoury crepes filled with sautéed spinach, onion, sun-dried tomatoes, and crumbled feta, rolled into wraps and pan-seared.
steps: Combine the eggs, sea salt, milk, and olive oil in a bowl, add the flour and whisk, gradually pouring in water until a uniform batter forms.
Heat part of the rapeseed oil in a skillet and fry thin crepes.
Dice the onion and sauté in the remaining rapeseed oil until golden brown.
Add the washed and blanched spinach, sliced sun-dried tomatoes, crumbled feta, granulated garlic, and seasoning blend, and mix the filling well.
Spread the spinach-feta filling over the fried crepes, roll into tight cylinders, and sear briefly on both sides in a hot skillet.

name: Babka herbaciana (Polish black tea bundt cake)
summary: A delicate creamed bundt cake flavoured with strong brewed black tea, raisins, and lemon zest.

ingredients.name: margarine
ingredients.note: plus a little for the tin

steps: Sort and rinse the raisins, place them in a pot with the strong tea, bring to a boil, then set aside to cool and drain.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C, grease a bundt cake tin with margarine, and dust with breadcrumbs.
Cream the margarine with the sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg yolks, lemon zest, and salt.
Whisk the wheat flour with the baking soda and baking powder, add to the batter, and gradually pour in the cooled tea while mixing continuously.
Finally, fold in the raisins gently.
Transfer the batter to the prepared tin, bake for 50–60 minutes at 170–180 °C, and optionally drizzle with icing once cooled.

name: Sabayon
summary: A classic light French-Italian dessert of fluffy egg yolk, sugar, and white wine or champagne mousse, whisked in a water bath with lemon peel.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a larger saucepan to prepare a water bath.
In a smaller saucepan, combine the egg yolks, sugar, and white wine or champagne, and add the piece of lemon peel.
Place the smaller saucepan in the vessel of boiling water and whisk vigorously for 2–3 minutes, until the mixture doubles in volume and becomes a thick mousse.
Continue whisking for another 30 seconds, then remove the lemon peel, spoon the sabayon into dessert coupes, and serve immediately.

name: Rémoulade
summary: Classic French cold mayonnaise-based sauce with finely chopped gherkins, capers, anchovy essence, and fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: fresh herbs (chervil, tarragon, chives, parsley leaves)

steps: Place the mayonnaise in a bowl and dice the gherkins very finely.
Finely chop the chervil, tarragon, chives, and parsley leaves to yield 2 tablespoons of herbs, then add to the mayonnaise along with the gherkins, drained capers, and a few drops of anchovy essence.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper and mix thoroughly.

name: Pljeskavica (Balkan grilled spiced meat patty)
summary: Balkan grilled patties made from finely ground pork and mutton with hot chili pepper and onion.
steps: Grind the pork and mutton twice through a fine mincer plate together with the hot chili pepper.
Peel the onion, grate one tablespoon and add to the meat, and finely chop the remaining onion and dust with salt for serving.
Season the meat mixture with salt and pepper, splash with cold water, knead thoroughly by hand, and refrigerate for 3 hours.
Shape the meat into flat oval patties, grill on both sides on a barbecue grate or electric grill, and serve on a bed of chopped raw onion.

name: Cepeliny (Lithuanian stuffed potato dumplings)
summary: Traditional Lithuanian and northeastern Polish zeppelin-shaped dumplings made from raw and cooked potatoes filled with seasoned minced beef tenderloin.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: melted, or sour cream for serving

steps: Finely mince the beef tenderloin and beef suet with a knife, add the garlic mashed with salt, black pepper, and marjoram, and knead into a smooth filling.
Wash and peel 5 large raw potatoes, grate them, and squeeze out the juice into a bowl. Once the starch settles at the bottom, pour off the liquid and return the starch to the grated potatoes.
Mash 15 cooked large potatoes thoroughly, combine with the raw potato mixture, season with salt, and knead into a cohesive dough.
Shape portions of dough into large apple-sized balls, flatten, fill with a portion of the meat filling, and seal into large oval dumplings.
Lower the cepeliny into boiling salted water, simmer for 30 minutes, remove with a slotted spoon, and serve drizzled with melted butter.

name: Zupa z dyni (Simple pumpkin purée soup)
summary: A simple puréed pumpkin soup made by gently cooking pumpkin in fat, then blending it with chicken broth and sour cream and seasoning with warming spices.

ingredients.name: pumpkin
ingredients.note: weight before removing seeds and skin

ingredients.name: spices
ingredients.note: nutmeg, curry powder, saffron, turmeric, chopped parsley, salt

steps: Halve the pumpkin, remove seeds and fibrous centre, cut into quarters, peel, and cut into smaller pieces.
Melt the chosen fat in a pot, add the pumpkin pieces, and cook gently covered over low heat, stirring and checking for doneness every 10 minutes or so, until the pumpkin breaks down into a purée.
Remove the pot from the heat, pour the broth over the pumpkin, and blend until smooth.
Set the soup aside to cool slightly, add a tablespoon of sour cream, and stir until smooth.
Season to taste with nutmeg, saffron, turmeric, chopped parsley, and curry powder (omit curry if you plan to freeze the soup).

name: Kotleciki z groszku (green pea patties)
summary: Quick vegan patties made from blended canned green peas and garlic, served with smoked paprika and sunflower seeds.
steps: Drain the canned green peas and blend them with the peeled garlic and enough potato starch so that the mixture is easy to shape.
Shape the thick mixture into small patties.
Fry the patties in hot vegetable oil for about 3 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate, dust with smoked paprika, and sprinkle with sunflower seeds.

name: Halászlé (Hungarian fisherman's soup)
summary: A traditional Hungarian spicy fish soup made from a rich broth of small freshwater fish, onions, peppers, and tomatoes, served with carp steaks.
steps: Gut and rinse the fish, cut the cleaned carp into steaks, and rub with salt.
Melt the lard in a cast-iron kettle or deep pot and sauté the chopped onions with the sliced hot peppers.
Add the whole small fish (tench, perch, and roach) with heads and bones to the pot, cover with water, add the sliced sweet peppers, and salt.
Simmer the broth over low heat for 90 minutes, gently swirling the pot occasionally, and add the peeled tomatoes towards the end of cooking.
Once the tomatoes have broken down, pass the broth through a sieve, return it to the pot, top up with water if needed, and bring to the boil.
Add the crushed garlic cloves, season with pepper, add the carp steaks, and cook for about 7 minutes longer.

name: Caldeirada de peixe (Portuguese fisherman's seafood stew)
summary: A Portuguese fish stew (caldeirada de peixe) with cod, shrimp, and mussels simmered with bell peppers, tomatoes, and wine.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for adding to the pot during cooking

steps: Pour the olive oil into a pot, add the chopped sweet peppers, onions, fresh coriander, and cut-up cod fillets, and fry for 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Add the thyme, chopped chili pepper, chopped tomatoes, and chopped garlic, then add some water.
Add the cleaned mussels and shrimp, season with salt, and simmer, covered, until the mussels open.
Pour in the red wine at the end, stir gently, and heat through for a moment.

name: Herb rémoulade
summary: Mild French herb sauce whipped from hard-boiled and raw egg yolks, mustard, oil, flavoured vinegars, and sour cream.
steps: Mash the hard-boiled yolks and beat thoroughly with the raw yolks, mustard, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Whisking constantly as when making mayonnaise, pour in the salad oil in a slow, steady stream, then finish with the white wine vinegar, tarragon vinegar, and dill vinegar.
Once the sauce is smooth and uniform, fold in the sour cream or plain yogurt and the finely chopped herbs.

name: Kleftiko (Greek slow-roasted lamb with vegetables)
summary: Cretan bone-in lamb marinated in red wine, garlic, and herbs, slow-roasted covered over a bed of vegetables.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 65 ml for the marinade, 125 ml for roasting

steps: Mix 125 ml of red wine with 65 ml of olive oil, the oregano, thyme, and crushed cloves from the whole head of garlic, immerse the lamb in the marinade, and set aside for 6 hours.
Peel the potatoes and onion and cut into quarters, slice the scraped carrot into thick rounds, and cut the tomatoes into smaller pieces.
Pour the remaining 125 ml of olive oil into the bottom of a roasting dish, arrange the chopped vegetables, and place the lamb on top along with the marinade and rosemary sprigs.
Season everything with salt and pepper, cover the dish tightly with a lid or transfer the ingredients to a roasting bag, and bake for 150 minutes.

name: Averna Blood Orange Cocktail
summary: A refreshing Italian digestif cocktail combining herbal Amaro Averna liqueur with chilled blood orange juice over ice.
steps: Fill a glass with ice cubes and pour in the measured portion of Averna liqueur.
Top up the glass with cold blood orange juice, stir gently, and serve.

name: Kotlety z piersi kurczaka z cebulą (Chopped chicken breast cutlets with onion)
summary: Pan-fried cutlets made from finely diced chicken breast and onion bound with egg and potato starch.
steps: Finely dice the onion and chicken breasts, and separate the egg whites from the yolks.
Add the vegetable seasoning, salt, pepper, and ground paprika to the onion, then mix in the egg yolks, oil, and potato starch until thoroughly combined.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the onion mixture along with the diced chicken.
Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Shape portions of the mixture into cutlets and fry them in a pan until golden brown.

name: Processed cheese pasta sauce (Sos z serkiem topionym do makaronu)
summary: A simple, creamy cheese sauce made from a butter and flour roux, milk, and melted processed cheese.
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the flour, and mix thoroughly.
Stirring continuously, pour in the milk gradually to dissolve lumps, and heat until the sauce thickens.
Add the processed cheese, stir over low heat until completely melted, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Zupa mleczna (Polish milk soup with drop noodles)
summary: A classic Polish breakfast milk soup with delicate drop egg noodles, prepared sweet or lightly salted.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: level (in gluten-free version: gluten-free oat flour)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: optional (in sweet version: 1 tsp vanilla sugar, honey, or syrup)

steps: Place 5 level tablespoons of wheat flour (or gluten-free oat flour) into a bowl, crack in the eggs, and whisk with a fork, whisk, or blender into a smooth batter.
Bring the milk to a boil in a saucepan; in the sweet version add a teaspoon of vanilla sugar, honey, or syrup, and in the savoury version a pinch of salt.
Pour the batter in a thin stream into the gently simmering milk, without stirring right away, so the drop noodles keep their shape and puff up.
When the noodles float to the surface and become fluffy, stir everything, cook for another 1–1.5 minutes, and serve immediately.

name: Garlic and potato cream soup (Zupa czosnkowa)
summary: A velvety cream soup of two heads of garlic, potatoes, and translucent onions in broth, finished with mascarpone, caraway, and thyme.

ingredients.name: mascarpone cheese
ingredients.note: 1 tub (alternatively grated firm cheese with cream, or processed cheese)

steps: Cook the sliced onion in a pot in clarified butter and olive oil until translucent, about 10 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the peeled and diced potatoes, and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the peeled cloves from both heads of garlic to the pot and simmer covered for another 10 minutes.
Add the mascarpone (or grated firm cheese with cream, or processed cheese), along with salt, pepper, caraway, and thyme.
Cook the soup uncovered for the final 5 minutes, then blend until smooth and serve with croutons or crispy fried onions.

name: Kulajda (Czech mushroom and potato soup)
summary: Traditional Czech wild mushroom and potato soup flavoured with dry white wine and caraway, enriched with sour cream and served with a poached egg.

ingredients.name: fresh wild mushrooms (such as porcini, birch boletes)
vinegar
ingredients.note: plus a splash for poaching eggs

steps: Clean the fresh mushrooms and dice them, leaving any smaller caps whole.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a pot, add the chopped onion and cook until translucent, then add the mushrooms and sauté briefly over high heat.
Pour in 250 ml of dry white wine, reduce until evaporated, and sprinkle in several pinches of ground caraway.
Add the diced potatoes and 1250–1500 ml of broth, season with salt, and simmer covered until the potatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, poach the eggs by slipping them individually into simmering water with a splash of vinegar for about 3 minutes.
Temper 125 ml of sour cream with a little hot broth, then stir it into the soup to thicken it.
Season the soup with 1 teaspoon of vinegar, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and chopped parsley, and serve topped with a poached egg.

name: Zupa rumfordzka (Rumford's soup)
summary: A historic, hearty soup made from puréed yellow split peas in vegetable broth with caraway, served with potatoes, rice or pearl barley, and pork cracklings.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the vegetable broth (plus water to soak the peas and cook the rice)

steps: Thoroughly rinse the peas that have been soaked in cold water for several hours or overnight.
Peel the potatoes, carrots, parsley root, and celeriac, and cook until tender in 1.5 l of lightly salted water with the bay leaves and allspice.
Drain the cooked vegetables, add the split peas and ground caraway to the strained broth, and cook for about 45 minutes until soft.
Blend the cooked peas together with the broth into a smooth purée and season with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Cook the rice or pearl barley separately until tender with the grains remaining separate, then dice the fatback and render it in a frying pan until the cracklings are crisp.

Add the diced cooked potatoes, cooked rice or groats, and fatback cracklings along with rendered fat to the pea soup, and simmer together for several more minutes; serve with croutons and chopped dill.

name: Zupa naleśnikowa (German pancake soup / Flädlesuppe)
summary: German pancake soup (Flädlesuppe) made with chicken broth and roasted root vegetables, served with thin pancakes cut into strips.
steps: Peel the onion, carrots, potatoes, parsley root, and celeriac, cut into pieces, drizzle with olive oil, and roast in the oven until tender.
Fry thin crepes, roll them up, and cut into narrow strips.
Cover the chicken breasts with 1.5 l (6 glasses) of cold water, simmer the poultry broth, then add the roasted vegetables and cook briefly together.
Distribute the crepe strips into bowls and ladle the hot soup over them.

name: Zupa gulaszowa (Hungarian goulash soup)
summary: A hearty, thick goulash soup with pork and beef, bell peppers, potatoes, carrots, and tomatoes, slow-cooked with herbs and paprika.

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: e.g. shoulder, ham, collar, or sirloin

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: e.g. shoulder, round, rump, or chuck

steps: Dice the pork and beef, sear in the hot oil or lard for about 5 minutes, and transfer to a bowl.
In the same fat, fry the chopped onion or leek, then add the garlic, chopped carrots, parsley root, and red bell pepper, and fry together for about 10 minutes.
Add the seared meat, pour in 1250 ml (5 glasses) of water or broth, and add the sweet and hot paprika, salt, thyme, oregano, and pepper.
Cook the soup covered over low heat for 90 minutes.
Add the tomato passata or canned tomatoes, tomato paste, and peeled diced potatoes.
Cook covered for another 30 minutes until the potatoes and meat are tender; serve with bread, optionally sprinkled with fresh herbs.

name: Green zucchini and pepper cream soup (Zielona zupa)
summary: A creamy green soup of zucchini, green bell pepper, onion, and garlic with broccoli soup seasoning, served with crumbled feta cheese.
steps: Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic, wash, seed, and slice the bell peppers, and dice the zucchini.
Heat the olive oil in a pot, cook the onion and garlic until translucent, then add the green bell pepper and sauté briefly.
Add the diced zucchini and broccoli soup seasoning, pour in about 1.2 liters of water, and simmer over low heat until the vegetables are tender.
Blend the cooked soup until smooth, season with salt and pepper, and serve with pieces of feta cheese.

name: Kiszczonka (Polish blood sausage soup)
summary: Traditional Polish potato soup cooked with blood sausage with its casing removed and Polish soup vegetables, seasoned with marjoram and finished with sour cream.
steps: Peel the potatoes and dice them, remove the casing from the blood sausage, and peel and halve the onion.
Place the potatoes, skinned blood sausage, bunch of soup vegetables, and onion in a pot, pour in 1.5 l of water, and cook for about 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the bunch of soup vegetables from the broth, separate the cooked carrot, slice it, and return it to the pot.
Season the soup with salt, pepper, and marjoram, stir in the 18% sour cream, and bring briefly to a boil before serving.

name: Pie floater pea soup
summary: Thick Australian green pea soup blended with sautéed onions and leeks, served with barbecue sauce.
steps: Peel and chop the onions and cleaned leek, then sauté the vegetables in a pot in hot oil and butter for 2–3 minutes.
Pour in 2 litres of water, add the vegetable seasoning, and simmer covered over low heat for about 20 minutes.
Add the frozen green peas to the broth and return the soup to a boil.
Blend the soup until smooth and creamy, season to taste with salt and freshly ground pepper, and serve with barbecue sauce.

name: Caldo verde (Portuguese potato and kale soup with chorizo)
summary: A comforting Portuguese potato soup with thinly shredded kale, aromatics, and crisped spicy chorizo sausage.
steps: Cook the diced onion in melted butter until translucent, add the minced garlic towards the end, then pour in olive oil, add sliced leek, and braise for about 3 minutes.
Add the peeled, diced potatoes, season with salt, and cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the hot vegetable broth, season with black pepper, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Toss in the washed and shredded kale leaves along with the tomato paste, and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Fry the diced or sliced chorizo sausage in a skillet for 2–3 minutes.
Transfer the sausage and rendered fat into the soup, heat for 1 minute, and stir in the fresh dill.

name: Charczo (Georgian beef and walnut soup)
summary: A rich and spicy Georgian beef soup made with beef cheeks, rice, walnuts, tomatoes, adjika, and abundant fresh herbs.
steps: Finely dice the beef cheeks, chop the garlic, parsley leaves, fresh coriander, and tarragon, dice the red onions and leek, and grate the carrot, parsley root, and celeriac.
Heat some of the rapeseed oil in a pot, cook the onion, leek, and garlic until translucent, stir in the plain flour, then add the grated soup vegetables and sweet paprika, cooking together briefly.
Stir in the tomato paste and canned tomatoes, pour in the water, and bring everything to a boil.
Meanwhile, brown the beef in the remaining oil in a separate skillet, transfer into the soup pot, deglaze the skillet with several spoonfuls of broth, and pour back into the soup.
Add the wine vinegar, adjika paste, allspice berries, bay leaves, ground coriander seeds, ground fennel seeds, and chopped walnuts, and simmer gently for about 40 minutes, skimming any foam.
Stir in the rice and cook for another 40 minutes, stirring so the soup does not stick, and finish with the chopped parsley leaves, fresh coriander, and tarragon before serving.

name: Czosnianka (Highlander garlic soup)
summary: A fragrant Polish mountain-style garlic soup with potatoes, smoked tofu, dried mint, and sour cream in rich vegetable broth.
steps: Peel and dice the potatoes and onions, cut the smoked tofu into small cubes, and slice the peeled garlic cloves.
In a soup pot, saute the garlic, onion, some of the smoked tofu, and the dried mint with a pinch of salt until the onion turns translucent.
Add the bay leaves, allspice berries, remaining smoked tofu, and diced potatoes, cover with vegetable broth, and cook until the potatoes are tender.
Take a ladleful of hot soup, mix it with the sour cream, pour it back into the pot, and season to taste with salt and freshly ground pepper.

name: Rasam (South Indian tomato soup)
summary: South Indian warming tomato soup spiced with fresh ginger, toasted mustard seeds, ground cumin, black peppercorns, chili, and cilantro.
steps: Scald the tomatoes, peel, seed, and dice the flesh finely, and chop the fresh coriander.
Heat the vegetable oil, sauté the grated ginger, add a splash of water, and simmer for a moment.
Transfer the ginger to a large pot, pour in the remaining water, add the chopped tomatoes, and cook until they break down completely.
Toast the mustard seeds in a separate pan until they begin to pop, then add them to the tomato soup.
Season the soup with ground cumin, black peppercorns, and a pinch of hot paprika, add the chopped coriander, and stir to let the flavours meld.

name: Herbstmilch (Bavarian sour milk soup)
summary: Bavarian sour milk soup made with buttermilk, sour cream, and whipping cream, thickened with flour.
steps: Whisk the buttermilk, sour cream, 30% whipping cream, plain flour, and salt together in a pot until completely smooth.
Cook over moderate heat at about 100 °C for 8 minutes, stirring constantly until the soup thickens slightly.

name: Harira (Moroccan spiced meat and lentil soup)
summary: Classic Moroccan soup made with beef on the bone, chickpeas, red lentils, tomatoes, saffron, and fine vermicelli.
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Place the diced beef and the bone into a large pot, pour in 1.5 l of water, bring to a boil, and skim the foam.

Add the drained chickpeas, red lentils, butter, chopped onion, and diced celery, season with saffron, ginger, ground coriander, salt, and black pepper, and simmer covered over low heat for 75 minutes.
Add the blended canned tomatoes and tomato paste, season to taste with salt and black pepper, and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Add the dry fine vermicelli noodles, cook for about 15 minutes until the pasta is tender, and finish by stirring in chopped parsley leaves and fresh coriander.

name: Cullen skink
summary: A traditional hearty Scottish smoked haddock or cod soup made with potatoes, onions, and whole milk.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: about 2, peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes

steps: Melt the unsalted butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat, add the finely chopped onion, and cook for 5–8 minutes until translucent.
Add the diced potatoes and 300 ml of water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes.
In a separate pan, submerge the smoked cod in whole milk and poach gently for about 5 minutes until tender.
Lift the fish out with a slotted spoon, reserving the milk, let cool slightly, flake into large pieces, and discard any pin bones.
Pour the reserved poaching milk into the potato pot, add the flaked fish, simmer for another 5 minutes, and garnish with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Rumpuć (Wielkopolska meat and vegetable soup)
summary: Hearty traditional Wielkopolska one-pot soup with beef, pork shoulder, smoked bacon, sauerkraut, savoy cabbage, potatoes, carrots, and tart apples.
steps: Place the diced beef into a large pot of water, add the bay leaves, allspice berries, and salt, and simmer gently.
Melt the butter in a skillet, brown the diced pork shoulder, smoked bacon, and onion, and transfer everything into the pot with the beef.
Add the shredded savoy cabbage, sauerkraut, cut carrots, and potatoes, and cook until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Toward the end of cooking, stir in the tomato paste, add the tart apples cut into pieces, and season the soup with salt, pepper, and ground caraway.

name: Vichyssoise
summary: A classic French velvety puréed soup made with white leek parts gently cooked in butter and potatoes simmered in broth, finished with cream.
steps: Clean the leeks, cut off the green parts, and slice the white stalks into rings. Peel and dice the potatoes.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the sliced leeks gently, covered, until soft.
Add the potatoes, sauté briefly, then pour in the hot chicken or vegetable broth.
Simmer the soup covered over low heat for 20–25 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Season the soup with salt and white pepper, blend until completely smooth, stir in the whipping cream, and chill in the refrigerator before serving.

name: Suaasat (Greenlandic game soup)
summary: A thick Greenlandic soup of game meat, wild mushrooms, dried sour cherries, vegetables and pearl barley with herbs and lemon zest.
steps: Put the diced game meat, chopped onions, sliced carrots, cleaned wild mushrooms and dried sour cherries in a large pot.
Cover the ingredients with water, add the chopped rosemary, thyme, sage, sea salt, and pepper, and cook over medium heat for about 60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the pearl barley and grated lemon zest, season to taste, and simmer for another 30 minutes until the soup thickens.

name: Rassolnik (Russian pickle and barley soup)
summary: Traditional Russian soup in beef broth with barley groats, potatoes, root vegetables, and sautéed pickles.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the pickles, 3 tbsp for the vegetables

steps: Pour 2.8 litres of water into a large pot, add the diced beef, rinsed barley groats, and half a tablespoon of salt, and cook partially covered for about 30 minutes, skimming off any foam regularly.
Sauté the cut-up pickles in 1 tablespoon of olive oil, transfer them to the pot along with the diced potatoes and sliced carrot, and cook for another 10 minutes.

Heat the remaining 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a separate skillet, fry the chopped onion for 2 minutes, add the grated carrot and thinly sliced celery, and cook gently, covered, for 5 minutes until tender.
Stir the tomato paste into the skillet and transfer everything into the soup pot.
Add 2 bay leaves, black pepper, chopped dill, and salt to taste, and simmer over low heat for about 2 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

name: Aigo boulido (Provençal garlic and herb soup)
summary: A Provençal creamy potato and roasted garlic soup cooked with a bouquet of fresh herbs and olive oil.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: approx. 1 l for cooking the soup

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 1.5 cm dice

ingredients.name: herb bouquet (rosemary, sage, thyme, parsley, bay leaves)

steps: Remove the papery outer skin from the garlic heads, brush with a little olive oil, wrap in foil, and roast in the oven at 180 °C for about 45 minutes until tender, then cool and squeeze the cloves through a garlic press.
In a large pot, combine 1 litre of water, diced potatoes, roasted garlic, the herb bouquet, remaining olive oil, sea salt, and black pepper.
Bring the soup to a boil and simmer covered over medium heat for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Discard the herb bouquet, blend the soup until silky smooth, adjust seasoning to taste, and ladle into bowls with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Nyponsoppa (Swedish rosehip soup)
summary: A sweet traditional Swedish soup made from fresh rosehips, lightly thickened with potato starch.
steps: Trim the green tips from the rosehips, slice them into halves or quarters, and optionally remove some of the seeds.
Cover the rosehips with water and boil for 15 minutes, skimming off the foam and floating seeds regularly.
Puree the soup with an immersion blender until smooth, simmer for another 2 minutes, then press through a fine sieve into a clean pot.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved, and if desired, thicken the soup with potato starch slurried in a little cold water, bringing it briefly to a boil.

name: Czernina (Polish duck blood soup)
summary: A historic Polish sweet-and-sour soup cooked from poultry giblet stock and vegetables, thickened with duck blood, flour, and wine vinegar.
steps: Cover the poultry giblets with water, add the trimmed celeriac, carrots, leek, parsley root, bay leaves, allspice berries, and black peppercorns, and simmer into a flavourful broth.
Strain the cooked broth through a sieve.
Whisk the duck blood thoroughly with the wine vinegar and flour, temper with a ladle of hot broth, and pour slowly into the simmering soup while stirring constantly.
Season the soup with salt, ground pepper, sugar, and dried marjoram to achieve a distinct sweet-sour balance, and bring to a brief boil.

name: Kluski śląskie z sosem grzybowym (Silesian potato dumplings with mushroom sauce)
summary: Potato dumplings served with a rich sauce made from dried mushrooms, onion, garlic, and sour cream, sprinkled with parsley.
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in water, and once softened, drain them, reserving the liquid, and slice into strips.
Pass the cooked potatoes through a ricer, add the egg, a pinch of salt, the plain flour, and the potato starch, and quickly knead into a uniform dough.
Roll the dough into logs, cut them into two-centimetre pieces, and shape into balls with a dimple in the centre.
Drop the dumplings into salted boiling water, cook until they float to the surface, then drain.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and sauté the sliced mushrooms along with the finely chopped onion and garlic.

Pour the mushroom soaking liquid and 250 ml of fresh water into the pan, add 125 ml of sour cream, and cook for several minutes until the sauce thickens, then spoon over the dumplings and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

name: Chicken in creamy mushroom sauce
summary: Diced chicken breast marinated with garlic and poultry seasonings, braised with button mushrooms in a velvety cream and broth sauce.
steps: Dice the chicken breast fillet, mix with the pressed garlic, salt, pepper, poultry seasoning, and olive oil, and set aside to marinate for at least 60 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and sear the marinated chicken for 2 minutes.
Add the sliced mushrooms and fry everything together for another 3 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable broth and the whipping cream whisked with the flour, and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and creamy.
Scatter over the chopped dill or parsley before serving.

name: Zarzuela de mariscos (Catalan seafood stew)
summary: A traditional Catalan seafood stew of white fish chunks, shrimp, mussels, and squid braised in a thick tomato-pepper sauce with white wine and saffron.

ingredients.name: white fish fillets (cod, hake, or perch)

steps: Cut the fish fillets into chunks and clean the seafood.
Heat olive oil in a pot, cook finely chopped onion and garlic until translucent, then add chopped tomatoes and red bell pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes until a thick sauce forms.
Pour in the white wine and reduce by half, then add fish stock, tomato paste, sweet paprika, bay leaf, and optionally saffron, and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes.
Add the fish chunks to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the seafood, cover, and cook for 5–7 minutes until the mussels open.
Before serving, remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Sałatka szparagowa z kurczakiem i ananasem (asparagus, chicken, and pineapple salad)
summary: A refreshing salad of roast chicken, blanched asparagus, fresh pineapple, grapes, and apple dressed with Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, and soy sauce.

ingredients.name: fresh pineapple
ingredients.note: small, ripe, juice reserved for dressing

steps: Peel the asparagus, cut into 2 cm pieces, cook in boiling salted water for 2–3 minutes, then drain and let cool.
Quarter the pineapple, core and peel it, and cut the flesh into 1 cm slices, reserving any released juice.
Peel the apple, dice it, and toss with a splash of lemon juice; halve the grapes and remove the seeds.
Remove the roast chicken meat from the bones, cut it into two-centimetre pieces, and combine in a bowl with the prepared fruit and asparagus.
Whisk the Greek yogurt with the mayonnaise, remaining lemon juice, reserved pineapple juice, and soy sauce, and season with sea salt and white pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and chill in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes before serving.

name: Farfalle salad with chanterelles and Parma ham (Sałatka z makaronem i kurkami)
summary: A farfalle salad with fried chanterelles, Parma ham, shallot, and scallions, dressed with crème fraîche, red wine, and fresh herbs.
steps: Rinse, pat dry, and finely chop the fresh tarragon and garden chervil.
Whisk the crème fraîche with the red wine, season with sea salt and black pepper, stir in the chopped fresh herbs, and chill in the refrigerator for about 60 minutes.
Cook the farfalle pasta in salted boiling water for about 9 minutes until al dente, then drain and let cool.
Clean, rinse, and dry the chanterelles, peel and finely chop the shallots, slice the scallions into thin rounds, and cut the Parma ham into narrow strips.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet, cook the shallots briefly until translucent, add the chanterelles, and fry until tender, then let cool.
In a salad bowl, combine the pasta, cooled mushrooms and shallots, ham, and scallions, pour over the chilled dressing, and let stand for 60 minutes before serving.

name: Sałatka szparagowa z pomidorami (asparagus and tomato salad with herb dressing)
summary: A spring salad of white and green asparagus, peeled tomatoes, and green lettuce with a lemon and herb dressing made with sorrel, chervil, chives, and parsley.
steps: Peel the white asparagus and only the lower part of the green asparagus, trim the tough ends, and cut all the stalks into three-centimetre pieces.
Bring water to a boil with salt, sugar, and butter, add the white asparagus, after 5 minutes add the green asparagus, cook everything for another 10 minutes, and drain.
Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water, slip off the skins, remove the seeds, and cut the flesh into eighths.
Wash, dry, and finely chop the chives, curly parsley, and chervil, and slice the sorrel leaves into thin strips.
Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, trim away any tough ribs, and arrange on plates along with the asparagus and tomato wedges.
Whisk the freshly squeezed lemon juice with sea salt and pepper, gradually whisk in the oil until emulsified, stir in the chopped herbs and sorrel, and spoon over the salad before serving.

name: Sałatka z brukselki z kiełkami (Brussels sprout, lentil sprout, and grape salad)
summary: A vibrant salad of blanched Brussels sprout petals, lentil sprouts, grapes, and grapefruit segments in a creamy citrus-yolk dressing, garnished with almonds.
steps: Whisk the orange juice, juice from half a lemon, and fresh egg yolks together, then gradually drizzle in the grapeseed oil while whisking continuously until thick and creamy.
Season the dressing with sea salt, a pinch of sugar, freshly ground white pepper, and a few drops of Tabasco sauce.
Trim the Brussels sprouts, separate the individual leaves from the cores, rinse, and blanch for 2 minutes in boiling salted water, then refresh in ice water and drain.
Rinse and dry the lentil sprouts, halve the grapes and remove any seeds, and segment the grapefruits, removing all white pith and membranes.
In a bowl, toss the Brussels sprout leaves, lentil sprouts, and halved grapes with the prepared dressing.
Arrange the salad on plates, garnish with the grapefruit segments, and sprinkle with chopped almonds.

name: Sałatka pomarańczowa z bananem i pistacjami (orange, banana, and pistachio salad)
summary: A dessert salad of sliced oranges and bananas in a spiced coffee-chocolate marinade with honey and liqueur, topped with glazed pistachios.
steps: Scrub the oranges in hot water, peel them, julienne the zest into thin strips, blanch in boiling water and drain, and slice the fruit thinly.
Bring the instant coffee and a pinch of cinnamon to a boil in 500 ml of water, strain through a filter, and stir with the honey, grated dark chocolate, and orange liqueur until fully dissolved.
Peel the bananas, slice them thinly, combine with the orange slices and blanched zest, and pour the coffee marinade over the fruit.
Heat the shelled pistachios with butter and icing sugar in a skillet, stirring until coated in a glossy glaze, and place them on the salad before serving.

name: Sałatka z kiwi i truskawkami (kiwi and strawberry salad)
summary: A fruit salad of kiwi, strawberries, and candied citrus peel in a honey and almond liqueur dressing, sprinkled with caramelised almonds.
steps: Peel the kiwis and slice into rounds about 3 mm thick, then halve the washed and dried strawberries.
Wash the oranges and lemon in hot water, pare the zest thinly, cut into fine julienne strips, and simmer in a syrup of water and cane sugar until tender, then drain.
Squeeze the juice from the peeled oranges and lemon, then mix with the honey and amaretto liqueur.
In a bowl, combine the kiwis, strawberries, and drained citrus zest, pour over the dressing, and set aside for about 10 minutes.
Toast the blanched almonds in a skillet with the butter and icing sugar until golden brown and caramelised.
Divide the marinated fruit among salad bowls and scatter the candied almonds over the top.

name: Sałatka z bakłażanów (fried aubergine salad with red pepper puree)
summary: Pan-fried golden aubergine slices served on lettuce leaves with a smooth red bell pepper purée, herb vinaigrette, and toasted pine nuts.

ingredients.name: pine nut or almond oil
ingredients.note: part for stewing and frying, remainder for the vinaigrette

steps: Wash the red bell peppers, deseed and dice the flesh, and cook gently covered in part of the heated oil with a splash of water for 10 minutes until soft.
Blend the stewed peppers into a smooth purée, pass through a fine sieve, and season with sea salt and pepper.
Slice the aubergines into 0.5 cm thick rounds, fry in heated oil until golden brown on both sides, and season with salt and pepper.
Peel and finely chop the shallots and garlic, wash and chop the parsley, then mix them with the white wine vinegar, mustard, remaining oil, salt and pepper.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden.
Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, tear out any tough central ribs, tear into bite-sized pieces, and arrange on plates.
Arrange the fried aubergine slices over the lettuce, drizzle with the vinaigrette, spoon dollops of the red pepper purée over top, and scatter with toasted pine nuts.

name: Celery and nectarine salad with smoked ham (Sałatka z selera naciowego z nektarynkami)
summary: A refreshing salad of celery, ripe nectarines, smoked ham, and wheat sprouts in a milk and apricot dressing.
steps: Trim and wash the celery stalks, then slice them thinly into crescents.
Wash the nectarines, cut them in half, discard the stones, and slice into eighths.
Rinse the wheat sprouts under cold water in a sieve, drain thoroughly, and combine in a bowl with the celery, nectarines, and diced smoked ham.
Combine the whole milk, apricot juice, and lemon juice, then season the dressing with sea salt and cayenne pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad, chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes, and garnish with fresh mint leaves before serving.

name: Radicchio and kumquat salad with gouda (Sałatka z kumkwatami)
summary: A colourful salad of radicchio, gouda, kiwi, and fresh kumquats in a sweet and sour lemon, honey, and mustard dressing.
steps: Trim the radicchio leaves, rinse them in lukewarm water, pat dry, and cut into ribbons.
Wash the kumquats in warm water, pat dry, slice thinly, and remove any seeds.
Slice the peeled kiwis into rounds 3 mm thick and combine in a bowl with the radicchio, kumquats, and diced gouda cheese.
Whisk together the lemon juice, liquid honey, and mild mustard, season with salt and freshly ground pepper, then slowly drizzle in the corn oil while whisking constantly.
Pour the prepared dressing over the salad and toss gently just before serving.

name: Fennel and Corinthian currant salad (Sałatka z kopru włoskiego z rodzynkami korynckimi)
summary: Crisp marinated fennel bulb tossed with Corinthian currants, tomatoes, fresh dill, and crème fraîche on radicchio leaves, topped with toasted almonds.
steps: Pour hot water over the Corinthian currants, let soak for 15 minutes, then drain.
Trim, wash, and dry the fennel bulbs, reserving the feathery fronds for garnish; slice the bulbs into thin strips and marinate for 15 minutes in white wine vinegar seasoned with salt and pepper.
Scald the tomatoes with boiling water, peel off the skins, discard the seeds, and cut the flesh into eighths.
Toast the almond halves for about 5 minutes in an oven preheated to 250 °C.
Wash, dry, and finely chop the dill (reserving a sprig for garnish), then mix with the crème fraîche, drained currants, marinated fennel, and 3/4 of the tomatoes.
Arrange the washed and dried radicchio leaves on serving plates, mound the fennel salad onto them, and garnish with the toasted almonds, remaining tomatoes, and fresh dill.

name: Halibut and roasted pepper salad with saffron dressing (Sałatka z pieczoną papryką i halibutem)
summary: A salad of halibut marinated in a hot marinade with colourful bell peppers, onion, and garlic, served on salad leaves with saffron dressing and pine nuts.
steps: Wash and dry the radicchio and oak leaf lettuce leaves, removing any tough ribs.
Wash the bell peppers, remove the seeds, and slice into strips, then slice the peeled onion and garlic thinly.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet until golden.
Rinse and pat dry the halibut fillets, slice them into 1.5 cm thick pieces, and arrange in an oiled baking dish.

Bring the white wine vinegar to a boil with a splash of water, remaining olive oil, sea salt, cayenne pepper, black pepper, sliced onion, garlic, and pepper strips, pour the hot marinade over the fish, and let stand for 60 minutes.
Dissolve the saffron in 1 tbsp of the marinade liquid, whisk into the crème fraîche, and season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the salad leaves on plates, place the marinated halibut and drained vegetables on top, drizzle with the saffron dressing, and scatter with pine nuts and fresh parsley leaves.

name: Artichoke bottom salad with vinaigrette (Sałatka z karczochami w sosie winegret)
summary: An elegant salad of lollo rosso leaves, artichoke bottoms, cherry tomatoes, and quail eggs with a broth and peanut oil vinaigrette.
steps: In a bowl, whisk the chicken broth with the Dijon mustard, sherry vinegar, and peanut oil, then season with sea salt, sugar, and white pepper.
Stir the finely chopped shallots and diced artichoke bottoms into the dressing.
Trim, wash in cold water, and thoroughly dry the lollo rosso lettuce leaves, and halve the washed cherry tomatoes.
Boil the quail eggs for 1.5 minutes from the moment the water boils, then cool in cold water, peel, and cut in half.
Arrange the lettuce leaves on plates, spoon over the artichoke bottoms with vinaigrette, garnish with halved quail eggs and cherry tomatoes, and scatter fresh chervil leaves on top.

name: Sałatka z cukinii i orzeszków ziemnych (courgette and roasted peanut salad)
summary: Pan-fried courgette slices served on radicchio with diced tomatoes, oven-roasted peanuts, and a fresh thyme vinaigrette made with peanut oil.

ingredients.name: peanut oil
ingredients.note: part for frying, remainder for vinaigrette

steps: Wash the courgettes, cut into 0.5 cm thick rounds, season with salt and pepper, and fry in part of the heated peanut oil on both sides until golden.
Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water, slip off the skins, remove the seeds, and finely dice the flesh.
Preheat the oven to 250 °C, spread the peanuts on a baking sheet, and roast for about 10 minutes until golden brown.
Peel and finely mince the shallots, and rinse, dry, and chop the bunch of thyme leaves.
Whisk together the shallots, chopped thyme, mustard, and white wine vinegar, gradually pour in the remaining peanut oil while whisking, and season the vinaigrette with sea salt and pepper.

Wash and dry the radicchio, cut out any tough core parts, arrange the leaves on plates, top with the courgette slices, drizzle with vinaigrette, and scatter with diced tomatoes, roasted peanuts, and thyme sprigs.

name: Shrimp risotto
summary: Northern Italian arborio rice risotto simmered in an onion-tomato sauce with sautéed shrimp, finished with butter and parsley leaves.
steps: Thaw and pat the shrimp dry with paper towels, dredge in plain flour, sear briefly in hot olive oil, transfer to a plate, and drizzle with the juice of half a lemon.

Add the chopped onion to the remaining oil in the pan, sauté for a few minutes, stir in the tomato purée, season with salt and pepper, and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, then return the shrimp to the pan and remove from the heat.
Bring the arborio rice to a boil in a small amount of salted water, adding a few tablespoons of boiling water as needed to replace evaporated liquid.
Halfway through cooking the rice, after about 7 minutes, stir in the prepared tomato sauce with shrimp and cook until the grains are tender.
Remove the cooked risotto from the heat, stir in the butter and finely chopped parsley leaves, and serve hot.

name: Syrian Pistachio Baklava (Baklawa syryjska)
summary: Syrian baklava of layered phyllo pastry filled with ground pistachios and butter, soaked in a lemon and orange syrup.
steps: Grease a baking sheet with a little butter, line with 4 sheets of phyllo pastry, and scatter with half of the chilled butter shaved into thin curls.
Evenly spread the coarsely ground pistachios, cover with the remaining 4 sheets of phyllo, and top with the rest of the butter shavings.
Place the pan in an oven preheated to 170 °C, bake for 35 minutes, then increase the temperature to 210 °C and bake for another 10 minutes.
Dissolve the sugar in water, bring to a boil, stir in the lemon juice, and simmer until syrupy, then add a few drops of orange flavouring, cook for 2 minutes more, and allow to cool.
Slice the baked pastry into diamonds and soak evenly with the prepared syrup.

name: Palce wezyra (vezir parmağı / Turkish choux pastry fingers in syrup)
summary: Traditional Ottoman Turkish choux pastry fingers fried in olive oil and soaked in a thick fragrant lemon syrup.
steps: Boil a thick syrup from the sugar, 440 ml of water, and lemon juice, and set aside to cool completely.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add 375 ml of water and salt, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, dump in all the flour at once, and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough pulls away from the sides, then remove from the heat and let cool.
Add the eggs and egg yolk to the cooled dough and beat with a wooden spoon for about 10 minutes.
Pinch off portions of dough and, with oiled hands, shape into small finger-sized cylinders.
Fry the fingers in hot olive oil until golden, lift out with a slotted spoon, and drain on baking paper.
Submerge the cooled pastries in the cold syrup for 15 minutes, then drain and arrange on a serving platter.

name: Ciasto kruche (shortcrust pastry with streusel)
summary: A classic Polish shortcrust pastry base enriched with potato starch and topped with a buttery vanilla streusel crumble.
steps: Sift 100 g of wheat flour with the potato starch and baking powder, add 80 g of sugar, 80 g of butter, the egg, and a packet of vanilla sugar, and knead quickly into a shortcrust base dough.
In a separate bowl, rub together the streusel crumble ingredients: 150 g of wheat flour, 100 g of sugar, 100 g of butter, and the second packet of vanilla sugar.
Place both prepared doughs in the refrigerator to chill for 30 minutes.
Line a baking tin with the chilled base dough, crumble the streusel evenly across the top, and bake for 60 minutes in an oven preheated to 175 °C.

name: Pichelsteiner (Bavarian three-meat stew)
summary: Bavarian one-pot stew (Eintopf) layered with three kinds of meat, root vegetables, potatoes, and savoy cabbage, gently braised in rich broth.
steps: Cut the meat into small cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the onions, slice them, and lightly brown in melted butter in a large saucepan, then add the meat and sauté over low heat for about 5 minutes.
Peel the carrots and potatoes and slice them, and dice the cleaned celeriac and savoy cabbage.
Layer the prepared vegetables over the browned meat without stirring, add the bay leaf, and pour over the meat broth.
Simmer covered over low heat for about 90 minutes, topping up with broth if needed.

name: Pasta serowo‑czosnkowa (Polish cheese and garlic spread)
summary: A pungent savoury sandwich spread made from finely grated hard cheese, mayonnaise, and plenty of fresh garlic.
steps: Grate the cheese on the fine holes of a box grater and transfer to a bowl.
Peel the garlic cloves, pass them through a garlic press, and add to the grated cheese.
Add the mayonnaise and stir thoroughly until a uniform paste forms.
If needed, stir in cold boiled water one tablespoon at a time until the mixture reaches the consistency of very thick sour cream.
Season the spread with salt and pepper, then refrigerate for at least 60 minutes before serving.

name: Chleb z czosnkiem (garlic bread)
summary: A crisp wheat baguette cut partway into slices, spread with garlic-and-herb butter, and baked in aluminium foil.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Peel the garlic, press through a garlic press, and blend in a bowl with the softened butter, salt, and chopped parsley leaves into a smooth paste.
Cut the baguette crosswise into slices, leaving them attached at the base.
Spread the prepared garlic butter into each slit and over the top of the baguette, then wrap tightly in aluminium foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 15 minutes at 190 °C until the butter is completely melted, and serve hot right away.

name: Poznań-style potato and dried mushroom soup (Zupa ziemniaczana z grzybami po poznańsku)
summary: A traditional Greater Poland potato soup based on a stock of Polish soup vegetables and dried mushrooms, thickened with a golden roux with onion and lightly soured with vinegar.
steps: Rinse and clean the soup vegetables and dried mushrooms, cover with water, and cook a stock with allspice and the bay leaf.
Peel the potatoes and dice them.
Once the vegetables in the stock are tender, strain the stock and cook the diced potatoes in it, then chop the cooked soup vegetables and mushrooms.
Chop the onion and cook gently covered in fat, then add the flour and brown the roux.
Thicken the soup with the roux and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped vegetables and mushrooms to the soup, and finally season with salt and vinegar to taste.

name: Tortelli della Vigilia (Italian Christmas Eve ricotta dumplings)
summary: Traditional Italian dumplings from Emilia-Romagna filled with ricotta, Parmesan, and fresh parsley, served with a simple tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 2 for the dough and 1 for the filling

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: 30 g for the filling and 50 g for serving

steps: Knead a smooth dough from the plain flour, two eggs, and a pinch of salt.
Fry the finely chopped half onion in hot olive oil until browned, add the passata with a pinch of salt and sugar, then cook gently for about 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Grate the Parmesan and finely chop the parsley, then mix the ricotta, 30 g of Parmesan, parsley, and one egg in a bowl, seasoning the filling with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut it into rectangles measuring 10 × 5 cm.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each rectangle and pinch the edges firmly together with your fingers to seal the dumplings.
Cook the dumplings in salted boiling water for 4–5 minutes, drain, spoon over the thick tomato sauce, and sprinkle with the remaining grated Parmesan.

name: Grochówka (Polish pea soup)
summary: Traditional Polish soup made with yellow peas, potatoes, and smoked bacon, seasoned with marjoram.
steps: Cover the peas with water, add two-thirds of the smoked bacon, and cook until the peas break down completely.
Peel and dice the potatoes, add them to the soup, and cook until tender.
Dice the remaining smoked bacon, render it in a frying pan into cracklings, add the chopped onion, and fry until golden.
Transfer the cracklings and onion into the soup pot and season to taste with salt, black pepper, and marjoram.

name: Zupa z cukinii (Polish zucchini soup)
summary: Delicate puréed soup made with tender zucchini, potatoes, and onion in vegetable broth, finished with sour cream and served with fresh dill and parsley.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling, small amount to cook the potatoes

steps: Wash, peel, and cut the potatoes, pour in a small amount of boiling water, salt, and cook.
Peel the onions, cut them into quarters, add to the potatoes, and cook together until tender.
Wash the zucchini, trim off the stem ends and blossom remnants, and cut the flesh into pieces.
Add the zucchini to the simmering vegetable broth, add the butter, and cook until tender for about 10 minutes.
Combine the tender zucchini with the cooked potatoes and onions, then purée everything through a sieve.
Add the sour cream, warm the soup through, ladle into a tureen, and garnish with chopped parsley and dill before serving.

name: Baked brie in puff pastry with baguette toasts (Ser brie z bułką paryską)
summary: A wheel of brie cheese coated in garlic and herb olive oil, wrapped in flaky puff pastry and baked until molten, served with crisp toasted baguette slices.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: half for the cheese, half for the baguette toasts

steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (top-and-bottom heat) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Unwrap the wheel of brie, pat dry with paper towels, and lightly score the top rind in a criss-cross pattern.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, pressed garlic, dried basil, oregano, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Unroll the puff pastry sheet on a work surface, place the wheel of brie in the centre, and brush the top with half of the herb oil.
Fold the edges of the pastry inward to wrap the cheese securely, trim any excess dough, and place the parcel seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Lightly score the top of the pastry in a diamond pattern and bake in the oven for 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Slice the baguette on an angle, brush the slices with the remaining herb oil, and add to the oven for the last 5–7 minutes of baking until crisp.
Remove the baked brie in pastry from the oven, let rest for 5 minutes, and serve hot with the toasted baguette slices for dipping into the molten centre.

name: Chopped liver (Wątróbka po żydowsku z drobiu)
summary: Traditional Jewish chopped poultry liver spread with slow-caramelised onions and hard-boiled eggs, chilled before serving.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 8–9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel, and cut into pieces.
Peel the onions, slice into fine dice or thin half-moons, fry in half of the fat over low heat until translucent and lightly caramelised, then transfer to a bowl.
Trim the liver of membranes and veins, rinse, pat dry with paper towels, and fry in the remaining fat over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, until no longer bloody but still tender.
Season the liver with salt and pepper towards the end of frying, transfer to the bowl with the onions, let cool slightly, and add the chopped eggs.

Chop the ingredients very finely with a large knife or pulse in a food processor to make a slightly grainy spread. Add the softened butter and some of the chopped parsley, and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Garnish with the remaining parsley, cover, and chill in the refrigerator for 1–2 hours before serving.

name: Minced beef skewers (Szaszłyki z mielonej wołowiny)
summary: Grilled herb-seasoned minced beef skewers alternating with small button mushrooms and cherry tomatoes.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: plus extra for brushing the grill

steps: In a large bowl, combine the minced beef, very finely chopped onion, pressed garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, 2 tablespoons of oil, thyme, rosemary, sweet and hot paprika, salt, and pepper.
Knead the mixture for several minutes until sticky and homogenous, then chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes (in the meantime, soak wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes).
Clean and dry the button mushrooms (halving any larger ones), and wash and dry the cherry tomatoes.
Shape the meat mixture into elongated rolls or balls and thread them onto skewers, alternating with the button mushrooms and cherry tomatoes.
Preheat the grill or grill pan, brush the surface with a little oil, and grill the skewers for 12–15 minutes, turning frequently, until the meat is cooked through and the vegetables are browned.
Rest the cooked skewers for 3 minutes, sprinkle with chopped sage or parsley leaves, and serve hot.

name: Marinated pork skewers (Wieprzowe szaszłyki)
summary: Grilled or pan-seared skewers of pork shoulder or collar marinated in soy sauce, lime juice, honey, sesame oil, ginger, and curry, coated in toasted sesame.

ingredients.name: cooking oil for grilling or frying

steps: Rinse the pork, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into long strips or large cubes.
Mix the soy sauce, lime or lemon juice, honey or brown sugar, sesame oil, crushed garlic, grated ginger, curry powder, chili flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl.
Add the pork to the marinade, coat each piece thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours (or overnight).
Soak wooden skewers in cold water for about 20 minutes, then thread the marinated pork tightly onto the skewers, reserving the leftover marinade.
Grill or pan-fry the skewers in hot oil over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning regularly and brushing with the reserved marinade until browned and juicy.
Sprinkle the skewers with the toasted sesame seeds towards the end of cooking, pressing them down lightly.

name: Warm garlic roux sauce
summary: A simple hot garlic sauce made with a light lard and flour roux, thinned with broth and seasoned with vinegar.
steps: Melt the lard in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and prepare a light roux.
Add the finely chopped garlic and fry briefly.
Pour in the broth, whisk the roux until smooth, season with salt, and simmer for several minutes until thickened.
Finally, season the sauce to taste with black pepper and a splash of vinegar.

name: Barszcz biały (Polish white borscht with wild mushrooms)
summary: Traditional Polish white borscht made on dried mushroom broth and fermented sour starter, finished with sour cream.
steps: Rinse the dried mushrooms, cover them with lukewarm water, and leave to soak overnight.
The next day, cook the mushrooms until tender in the same water, then strain the broth.
Peel and finely chop the onion, cook in butter until translucent, and add to the mushroom broth.
Pour the white borscht sour starter into the pot and bring to a boil.
Stir in the sour cream, season the soup to taste with salt and pepper, and heat briefly.

name: Garlic bread sauce
summary: A thick, hot garlic sauce made with soft white bread simmered in milk with parsley and nutmeg.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a small pot, drop in the peeled garlic cloves, parboil for 3 minutes, then drain and crush.
Remove the crusts and cut out the soft crumb from the bread slices.
Warm the milk, then add the crushed garlic, bread crumb, and parsley sprigs.
Simmer the sauce gently for about 15 minutes, seasoning along the way with nutmeg, salt, and pepper while mashing the ingredients with a wooden spoon until smooth.

name: Barszcz ukraiński (Ukrainian-style hearty borscht)
summary: A rich Ukrainian-style borscht with pork, beetroots, white beans, savoy cabbage, and potatoes in meat broth, finished with thick sour cream.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1 l for soaking beans and 2 l for broth

ingredients.name: soup greens with savoy cabbage
ingredients.note: carrot, celeriac, parsley root, leek, and savoy cabbage

steps: The day before, soak the beans in 1 litre of lukewarm boiled water, and the next day boil them until tender.
Cover the pork in a pot with cold water and simmer over low heat until tender, salting lightly towards the end, to yield 2 litres of broth.
Grate the carrots, celeriac, parsley root, and onion on a coarse grater, add the finely shredded leek from the soup greens, pour in the meat broth, and bring to a boil.
Shortly after, add the grated beetroots, and once the vegetables begin to soften, toss in the diced potatoes and shredded savoy cabbage.
When all the vegetables are tender, season the soup with the tomato purée, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and sugar.
Add the cooked beans along with their cooking liquid and simmer gently for a short while longer.
Finally, stir in the finely chopped dill and thick sour cream, and mix well.

name: Italian New Year's lentils (Lenticchie di Capodanno)
summary: A traditional Italian New Year's Eve dish of lentils cooked with soup vegetables, then simmered in tomato passata with fresh sage.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking and boiling the lentils

steps: Cover the lentils with water and soak overnight (about 12 hours).
The next day, chop one carrot, one onion, and one celery stalk into pieces, add to the lentils with a pinch of salt, and cook in water for 60 minutes until tender.
Chop the remaining carrot, onion, and celery stalk, add to a skillet with heated olive oil, stir in the chopped sage leaves and tomato puree, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Transfer the cooked lentils and boiled vegetables to the skillet, stir into the tomato sauce, and simmer everything for another 10 minutes.

name: Zupa kremowa z pieczarek (Cream of mushroom soup)
summary: A velvety cream of mushroom soup cooked gently in butter in a pressure cooker, thickened with flour, milk, and thick sour cream with a hint of citric acid.

ingredients.name: citric acid
ingredients.note: dissolved in a little water, for sprinkling over the mushrooms and seasoning

steps: Clean, wash, and thoroughly dry the button mushrooms in a cloth, then chop them very finely.
Transfer the chopped mushrooms to a bowl and sprinkle with dissolved citric acid so they do not darken.
Melt the butter in a pressure cooker, add the mushrooms, and cook gently covered for 4–5 minutes, taking care that they do not brown.
Sprinkle the mushrooms with the flour, stir, pour in the water, and season with salt and pepper.
Close the pressure cooker and cook for 5 minutes from the moment full pressure is reached.
Open the pressure cooker after the pressure drops and slowly pour in the milk until the desired consistency is reached.
Enrich the soup with the thick sour cream and season to taste with citric acid; blend into a smooth cream if needed.

name: Zupa pieczarkowa (Polish mushroom soup)
