summary: Classic Polish button mushroom soup in broth, thickened with sour cream and flour, garnished with fresh parsley leaves.
steps: Clean and rinse the button mushrooms, then slice them or cut into strips.
Sauté the mushrooms in melted butter, transfer to a pot, pour in the broth, and simmer over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Thoroughly mix the sour cream with the flour, temper with a little hot broth, and stir into the soup until it comes to a boil.
Season the soup with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley leaves.

name: Greek-style bake (Zapiekanka grecka)
summary: A layered casserole of fried potato slices, red bell pepper, minced meat with rosemary, and firm cheese.

ingredients.name: fat
ingredients.note: for frying and greasing the baking dish

steps: Slice the potatoes, fry them in a skillet in heated fat, and transfer to a plate.
In the same fat, fry the bell pepper cut into large dice.
Fry the minced meat in a dry skillet, pour in 300 ml of water, add the casserole seasoning mix, stir, and braise for about 5 minutes.
Grease an ovenproof dish with fat and layer the potatoes, bell pepper, grated cheese, and meat with rosemary alternately.
Sprinkle the top of the casserole with grated firm cheese and bake in the oven for about 30 minutes.

name: Pierogi z owocami (fruit pierogi)
summary: Summer Polish pierogi made from tender elastic dough, filled with fresh seasonal fruit tossed in breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the dough, plus 2 l for boiling

ingredients.name: seasonal fruit
ingredients.note: strawberries, blueberries, pitted cherries, or blackberries

steps: Knead a smooth dough from wheat flour, water, and egg, roll out into thin sheets, and cut out rounds with a wide glass.
Wash the fruit, drain thoroughly, and toss with breadcrumbs.
Place spoonfuls of fruit filling onto the dough rounds, dab the edges with a little cold water, fold in half, and pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Bring 2 litres of water with olive oil to a boil in a large pot and drop the pierogi in batches of 5–6 into the boiling water.
Stir gently with a wooden spoon, and once they float to the surface, boil for another 2–3 minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain.

name: Buritos (machaca beef burritos)
summary: Mexican tortillas filled with shredded machaca beef marinated in garlic, lemon juice, and oregano, then browned with onions.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for marinade and extra to taste

steps: Rinse the beef and rub it with a blended paste of garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and black pepper, then marinate for 240–360 minutes.
Fry the marinated meat, shred it into small pieces, and air-dry in a well-ventilated spot for about 360 minutes.
Peel the onion, rinse it, finely chop, and sauté in heated oil in a pot.
Add the prepared beef to the onion, fry until well browned, then season with salt and stir.
Warm the tortillas in the oven, place several spoonfuls of meat onto each, roll up, and serve hot.

name: Kapusta z fasolą i kaszą jaglaną (Subcarpathian Christmas sauerkraut with white beans and millet)
summary: Subcarpathian Christmas Eve dish of sauerkraut, large white runner beans, and millet, garnished with sautéed onions.
steps: Rinse the large white runner beans, cover with cold water, and leave to soak overnight.
Boil the beans until tender in their lightly salted soaking liquid, then drain.
Briefly parboil the sauerkraut, drain, cover with fresh cold water, and simmer gently over low heat until it starts to soften.
Rinse the millet, spread in an even layer on top of the simmering sauerkraut, and cook over very low heat without stirring until the millet absorbs the liquid and softens.
Finely chop the onion and cook until translucent in a skillet with butter or linseed oil.
Add the cooked beans and sautéed onion with fat into the pot with cabbage and millet, mix thoroughly, and chill for at least 12 hours before reheating.

name: Lotus Biscoff cheesecake
summary: No-bake cheesecake on a spiced caramel biscuit crust, filled with cheese-caramel cream and topped with cookie spread.

ingredients.name: spiced caramel biscuits
ingredients.note: 200 g for the crust, 100 g for decoration

ingredients.name: spiced cookie spread
ingredients.note: 200 g for the filling, 100 g for topping

steps: Line the bottom of a 20 cm springform tin with baking parchment.
Blend or crush 200 g of spiced biscuits into fine crumbs, pour in 65 g of melted butter, mix, and press firmly into the base of the springform tin.
Mix 200 g of cookie spread with 650 g of cream cheese by hand or on low mixer speed, add 50 g of powdered sugar, and mix until combined.
Transfer the cream cheese filling into the springform tin and smooth the top.
Melt the remaining 100 g of cookie spread, pour over the cheesecake, and scatter the remaining 100 g of crushed spiced biscuits on top.

name: Gęsie udka wolno pieczone w białym winie (slow-roasted goose legs in white wine)
summary: Slow-roasted goose legs marinated with garlic, rosemary, and paprika, served with a white-wine-based sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for mixing with the starch to make a slurry

steps: Clean and pat dry the goose legs, rub with the pressed garlic, sea salt, pepper, and sweet paprika, drape with the rosemary sprigs, cover, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 10 hours.
Take the meat out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before roasting, place in a baking dish over the rosemary sprigs, and pour in the white wine.
Cover the dish tightly and roast in an oven preheated to 120 °C for 3.5 hours.
Remove the lid, brush any seasonings from the skin into the sauce, raise the oven temperature to 180 °C, and roast uncovered for another 30 minutes, basting with the pan juices.
Remove the roasted legs, pour off the pan drippings, skim the rendered fat off the top, and transfer the remaining dark juices to a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Whisk the potato starch into cold water, pour into the simmering sauce, and stir vigorously until thickened.

name: Cinnamon candied almonds
summary: Whole roasted almonds enrobed in a crisp, crunchy shell of caramelised sugar, warm cinnamon, and vanilla.
steps: Pour the water into a wide skillet or heavy-bottomed pot, add 150 g of white sugar, vanillin sugar, and ground cinnamon, and stir over medium heat until dissolved and boiling rapidly.
Add the whole almonds to the boiling syrup and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the liquid thickens noticeably.
Reduce the heat and continue cooking for another 5–10 minutes until most of the water evaporates and a thick syrup coats the almonds.
Sprinkle in the remaining 50 g of white sugar and roast for an additional 4–5 minutes, stirring vigorously until a crunchy crystalline crust coats the nuts.
Spread the hot candied almonds onto a sheet of parchment paper, separating them so they do not stick, and allow to cool completely.

name: Mini yeast-free coconut doughnuts
summary: Bite-sized yeast-free doughnuts made with thick coconut milk and desiccated coconut, dipped in sugar glaze and coated with coconut after frying.
steps: Whisk together the cake flour, 50 g of desiccated coconut, vanilla-flavoured sugar, baking soda, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Add the eggs and thick coconut milk, and stir vigorously with a spoon or spatula into a very thick, uniform batter.
Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan to 165–170 °C.
Shape small walnut-sized balls with greased hands or drop portions of dough with two teaspoons directly into the hot oil.
Fry the doughnuts in batches for about 3–4 minutes until deep golden, then lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Mix the powdered sugar with the boiling water in a small bowl into a thin glaze, and place the remaining 100 g of desiccated coconut in a second bowl.
Dip the warm doughnuts one by one into the glaze and immediately coat in the desiccated coconut.

name: Fettuccine with chicken and curry
summary: Pasta in a velvety cream curry sauce with chicken breast, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, and fresh ginger.
steps: Toss the diced chicken in a bowl with the vegetable oil, curry powder, sweet paprika, and turmeric, then set aside for at least 15 minutes to marinate.
Cook the pasta al dente in salted water, reserving 200 ml of the cooking water before draining.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet, add the chicken, dust with 1 tablespoon of wheat flour, and fry over medium heat for 10–12 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Pour 200 ml of 30% whipping cream and 200 ml of the reserved pasta water into the skillet with the chicken, add the chopped sun-dried tomatoes, pressed garlic, grated ginger, and salt.
Simmer over low heat for 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly, then toss in the cooked pasta, mix thoroughly, and serve immediately.

name: Vinaigrette dressing (Sos winegret)
summary: Homemade vinaigrette dressing with garlic, olive oil, and wine vinegar or lemon juice, prepared in a jar.
steps: Peel the garlic cloves, chop them finely, and place in a jar.
Add the salt, wine vinegar or lemon juice, and olive oil or vegetable oil.
Tightly close the jar and shake vigorously until a uniform emulsion forms.

name: Kisiel mleczny piegowaty (spotted milk pudding)
summary: Chilled milk pudding enriched with butter and fresh wild blueberries, served with whipped cream.

ingredients.name: custard powder with sugar
ingredients.note: packet (cream, vanilla, banana, chocolate, or almond flavour)

steps: Sort through the bilberries, rinse them, and pat dry.
Cook the pudding in the milk with the butter according to the package instructions.
Set the prepared pudding aside to cool to room temperature.
Mix the cooled pudding with the bilberries, transfer into small bowls, and chill.
Before serving, decorate the dessert with dollops of whipped cream.

name: Wuzetka (Warsaw chocolate and cream cakes)
summary: Classic Warsaw cocoa-cream cakes made of soaked cocoa sponge cake layered with whipped cream, spread with blackcurrant jam, and topped with dark chocolate glaze.

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.note: a few tablespoons, for soaking the gelatin

ingredients.name: blackcurrant jam
ingredients.note: for spreading over the sponge layer

ingredients.name: chocolate glaze
ingredients.note: preferably dark (or melted dark chocolate with a tablespoon of oil)

ingredients.name: soaking syrup for the cake
ingredients.note: e.g. strong tea with sugar and vodka, or sugar syrup with rum essence

steps: Beat the egg yolks with sugar until pale and fluffy, and in a separate bowl beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form.
Sift the all-purpose flour and cocoa powder through a sieve and mix.
Gradually fold the beaten yolks into the whipped whites, stirring gently, then add the flour and cocoa in batches and carefully combine.

Transfer the batter to a baking pan (e.g. rectangular approx. 30 × 20 cm lined with parchment paper), place in an oven preheated to 180 °C, and bake for 30 minutes (in an alternative version at 160 °C for 30–40 minutes; it is best to bake the sponge cake one day ahead).
Cut the cooled sponge horizontally with a long knife into two equal layers.
Soak the gelatin in a few tablespoons of cold water, then dissolve it by heating over low heat.
Whip the well-chilled cream, adding the icing sugar and cooled liquid gelatin towards the end of whipping.
Soak the bottom layer with syrup, spread most of the whipped cream (reserving some for decoration), and cover with the second layer.
Soak the top layer, spread it with a thin layer of blackcurrant jam, and coat with dark chocolate glaze (or glaze made of melted dark chocolate with a little oil).
Chill the cake in the refrigerator until the glaze sets, cut into square portions, and decorate each cake with a rosette of the reserved whipped cream.

name: Kaczka po pekińsku (Peking duck)
summary: Roasted duck glazed with honey and soy sauce, served with thin pancakes, cucumber, and chives.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large pot, place the cleaned duck in the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes, then remove and dry thoroughly.
Brush the duck with honey mixed with sweet soy sauce and hang in a dry, cool place for 60 minutes.
Brush the duck with honey again and leave in a cool place for another 420 minutes to dry.
Place the duck in an ovenproof dish in an oven preheated to 200 °C and roast for 45 minutes on each side.
In a bowl, mix the wheat flour with 100 ml of water, knead into a smooth dough, and set aside for 10 minutes.
Roll out the dough into thin pancakes, brush them with sesame oil, and fry in a pan.
Remove the roasted duck from the oven, separate the crispy skin, and slice the meat.
Cut the cucumber and scallions into thin strips. Arrange pieces of duck on the pancakes, drizzle the duck with hoisin and plum sauces, add the vegetables, and roll up.

name: Botwinka z patelni (pan-fried young beet greens)
summary: A simple vegan Polish side dish of young beet greens braised in a skillet with onions and fresh lemon juice.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.note: from about half a lemon or apple cider vinegar

steps: Rinse the beet greens thoroughly, trim the leaves from the baby beetroots, scrub or peel the beetroots and slice them, then cut the stems into 3 cm pieces and chop the leaves into slightly longer ribbons.
Dice the onion and fry it in heated olive oil over fairly high heat.
Add the sliced beetroots and stems to the pan, and after a moment pour in the lemon juice.
Toss in the beet leaves, add a splash of water if needed, and braise covered for several minutes.
Sprinkle the dish with freshly ground black pepper before serving.

name: American Pancakes
summary: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes fried until golden and served drizzled with maple syrup.
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan and set aside to cool.
In one bowl, whisk together the wheat flour, salt, sugar, baking soda, and baking powder.
In a second bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, egg, and cooled melted butter.
Combine the dry ingredients with the wet ingredients, stir to combine, and refrigerate the batter for 60 minutes.
Heat butter or oil in a frying pan and fry small pancakes on both sides until golden.
Serve the warm pancakes drizzled with maple syrup.

name: Spring sauce (Sos wiosenny)
summary: A cold sauce made with mayonnaise, sour cream and yogurt, mixed with pickled mushrooms, grated radishes and fresh herbs.
steps: Combine the mayonnaise, thick sour cream, and plain yogurt in a bowl.
Add the chopped pickled mushrooms, grated radishes, and chopped fresh herbs.
Mix the sauce thoroughly, season to taste with salt and pepper, and serve immediately after preparing.

name: Grape sauce (Sos winogronowy)
summary: A delicate cold sauce made from whipped cream and mayonnaise blended with seeded white grapes and lemon juice.
steps: Whip the cream with a pinch of salt until light and fluffy.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the mayonnaise along with the seeded, chopped white grapes.
Season the sauce to taste with lemon juice, salt, pepper, and icing sugar.
Chill the prepared sauce in the refrigerator for 15 minutes and serve no later than 30 minutes after preparation.

name: Deluxe button mushroom sauce
summary: A velvety hot sauce made with small button mushrooms braised in butter, thickened with frothed sour cream, milk, and flour, and spiced with white pepper.
steps: Rinse and thoroughly dry the small button mushrooms, then fry them in a saucepan with melted butter for about 5 minutes, shaking the pan often so they brown evenly.
Cover the saucepan and cook the mushrooms gently over low heat for another 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the milk until free of lumps, combine with the thick sour cream, and lightly beat until frothy.
Pour the frothed sour cream over the mushrooms, season with salt and freshly ground white pepper, and heat for no more than 3 minutes until the sauce thickens, then serve immediately.

name: Tuna and rice salad (Sałatka z tuńczyka)
summary: Chilled tuna salad with cooked rice, red onion, and ripe tomatoes tossed in a zesty spiced ketchup and lemon dressing.
steps: Thoroughly mix together the ketchup, olive oil, lemon juice, and icing sugar, then set the dressing aside in a cool place for 30 minutes.
Drain the canned tuna in a sieve and flake it into bite-sized chunks.
Finely chop the red onions, and cut the peeled tomatoes into wedges.
Combine the cooked rice with the chilled dressing, add the tuna, onion, and tomatoes, and gently toss.
Cover the salad bowl with cling film or foil and chill in the refrigerator for several hours.
Serve the well-chilled salad on crisp lettuce leaves, garnished with chopped fresh greens.

name: Sos staropolski z suszonych grzybów (Old Polish dried mushroom sauce)
summary: A dark, aromatic sauce made with ground dried porcini, a light butter roux, and mushroom broth.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: bottled table water or water from an Oligocene aquifer

steps: Rinse the dried mushrooms, place them in a pot with 750 ml of water, add the onion cut into quarters, and simmer over low heat until the mushrooms are tender.
Strain the mushroom broth, discard the cooked onion, and finely grind the softened mushrooms in a meat grinder or mince them in a food processor.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the flour, and fry briefly without browning.
Whisk the strained mushroom broth into the roux, bring to a boil, add the ground mushrooms, and season to taste with salt and white pepper.

name: Genoese-style meat sauce
summary: An Italian meat and tomato sauce made with minced meat, onion, garlic, broth, tomato paste, and dry white wine.

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: may be from a bouillon cube

steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic, and cook in heated olive oil until translucent, taking care not to brown them.
Add the minced meat and fry for a moment, stirring frequently, then dust with the flour and cook briefly until the raw flour taste is gone.
Pour in the broth and mix thoroughly until smooth.
Add the tomato paste diluted in 2 tablespoons of water, ketchup, thyme rubbed between your palms, salt, and pepper.
Finally, pour in the dry white wine and bring the sauce back to a boil.

name: Exquisite tomato sauce
summary: An aromatic sauce made from fresh peeled tomatoes simmered with onion, garlic, bay leaf, and Mediterranean herbs.
steps: Scald the tomatoes with boiling water, peel off the skin, and cut into wedges, removing the seeds.
Finely chop the onion and garlic and fry in heated olive oil until light straw-yellow.
Add the tomato wedges, bay leaf, herb mix, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the sauce over moderate heat for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, and adjust seasoning to taste at the end if needed.

name: Fresh yellow knight mushroom sauce (Sos ze świeżych zielonek)
summary: A hot wild mushroom sauce made from finely chopped fresh yellow knight mushroom caps, onions, broth, heavy cream, and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: dill
ingredients.note: chopped, measured in a heaped spoonful

steps: Wash, drain, and very finely chop the mushroom caps, and peel and chop the onions.
Melt the butter in a pan, cook the chopped onion until translucent, then add the mushrooms and fry, stirring frequently, until most liquid evaporates.
Dust the mushrooms with flour, cook briefly while stirring continuously, then pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Remove the sauce from the heat, stir in the whipping cream and chopped dill, and serve hot without boiling again.

name: Sos staropolski ze świeżych grzybów (Old Polish fresh wild mushroom sauce)
summary: A classic Polish sauce of finely chopped wild mushroom caps braised with onion in butter, finished with broth, sour cream, and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: fresh wild mushroom caps
ingredients.note: porcini, scaber-stalk boletes, or bay boletes

steps: Clean and rinse the wild mushroom caps, chop them very finely, and finely dice the onion.
Cook the onion in melted butter until translucent, add the mushrooms, cover, and simmer gently over low heat, stirring occasionally, until most liquid evaporates.
Dust the mushrooms with the flour and cook for a moment, stirring, until the raw flour flavour is gone.
Pour in the broth, bring the sauce to a boil, and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Remove the pan from the heat. Just before serving, stir in the lightly whisked sour cream and chopped dill, and serve without reheating.

name: Italian spaghetti sauce (Sos włoski do spaghetti)
summary: An aromatic tomato pasta sauce with raw pork belly, onion, garlic, white wine and herbs.

ingredients.name: chives
ingredients.note: chopped, measured in a generous spoonful

steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan, add the peeled garlic cloves, brown them lightly, and remove.
Add the chopped onion and diced pork belly to the oil and fry, stirring, until the onion turns golden.
Pour in the white wine, bring to a boil, then add the peeled and seeded tomatoes, about 150 ml of hot water, basil, chives, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover the saucepan and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes; serve the finished sauce whole or passed through a sieve.

name: Cold horseradish cream sauce
summary: A cold sauce made from scalded grated horseradish, mashed hard-boiled egg yolks, lemon juice, and whipping cream, served with pâté and cold meats.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.note: squeezed from half a large lemon

steps: Grate the horseradish roots on a fine grater, transfer to a fine sieve, pour boiling water over them, and set aside to cool.
Remove the yolks from the hard-boiled eggs and mash them with the lemon juice into a smooth paste.
Add the whipping cream and cooled horseradish to the egg yolks, then season everything to taste with icing sugar and salt.
Wrap the bowl in aluminium foil and chill until the next day (for about 12 hours) so the flavours meld.

name: Scalded horseradish cream sauce
summary: An aromatic sauce of boiling-water scalded horseradish sautéed in butter, combined with whipping cream and lemon juice.
steps: Grate the horseradish roots on a fine grater, place on a sieve, pour boiling water over them, and leave to drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the drained horseradish, and fry for 1 minute while stirring constantly, then remove from heat.
Pour in the whipping cream, return the saucepan to low heat, and warm gently without bringing to a boil.
Remove the sauce from heat, season to taste with lemon juice, salt, and sugar, and set aside to cool.
Wrap the cooled sauce tightly in aluminium foil and chill in the refrigerator until the next day (about 12 hours) before serving.

name: Horseradish and apple cream sauce
summary: A cold sauce made from scalded horseradish and grated tart apples with whipping cream and lemon juice.
steps: Grate the horseradish roots on a fine grater, transfer to a sieve, pour boiling water over them, and leave to cool.
Peel the apples, grate them on the same grater, and immediately mix with the lemon juice and chilled horseradish.
Add the whipping cream, season with icing sugar, a pinch of salt, and extra lemon juice if needed, and serve within 2 hours of preparation.

name: Horseradish cream sauce with white wine
summary: A delicate cold sauce made from scalded horseradish, whipping cream, dry white wine, mustard, and fruit juices.
steps: Grate the horseradish on a fine grater, place on a sieve, scald with boiling water, and leave to drain and cool.
Combine the cooled horseradish with dry white wine, whipping cream, sour cherry juice, redcurrant juice, and mild Polish mustard.
Season the sauce carefully with icing sugar, lemon juice, and salt, stir thoroughly, and serve within 2 hours of preparation.

name: Sos chrzanowy wykwintny (gourmet horseradish sauce)
summary: A spicy, fruity cold sauce made with grated horseradish, hard-boiled egg yolks, peaches from Polish kompot, orange, mayonnaise, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: peaches from Polish kompot
ingredients.note: halves, plus optionally 1 tablespoon of liquid from the kompot

steps: Peel the orange and thoroughly remove the membranes from the segments, then roughly chop the peach halves from the kompot.
Remove the yolks from the hard-boiled eggs, place in a food processor with the freshly grated horseradish, peaches, and orange, and blend until smooth.
Add the sour cream and mayonnaise, mix, and season to taste with salt, white pepper, icing sugar, and lemon juice. If too thick, thin with a tablespoon of liquid from the peach kompot.

name: Mayonnaise and egg sauce
summary: A cold sauce made from mayonnaise, sour cream, mild Polish mustard, and hard-boiled eggs.
steps: Separate the yolks and whites of the hard-boiled eggs; mash the yolks with the mild Polish mustard and lemon juice until smooth, and finely chop the egg whites.
Add the mayonnaise and lightly whisked sour cream to the mashed yolks, stir, and season to taste with salt, pepper, and icing sugar.
Stir in the chopped egg whites, combine well, and pour into a sauce boat; serve within an hour of preparation.

name: Zesty almond and cucumber mayonnaise sauce
summary: A cold mayonnaise sauce made with finely chopped almonds, fresh cucumber, ketchup, tomato paste, and dill.
steps: Scald the almonds with boiling water, remove the skins, and chop very finely or grind in a grinder.
Peel the fresh cucumber, scoop out the seeds, finely dice the flesh, and place on a sieve to drain excess juice.
Combine the mayonnaise with the chopped almonds, ketchup, tomato paste, chopped dill, and drained cucumber.
Season the sauce to taste with lemon juice, salt, and icing sugar, and serve within 30 minutes of preparation.

name: Pineapple mayonnaise sauce
summary: A sweet and sour cold sauce whipped from olive oil, lemon juice, mayonnaise, mustard, and pineapple juice and pulp.
steps: Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, then add the mayonnaise and pineapple juice, whisking until a smooth, thick sauce forms.
Finely chop the pineapple slices or blend them into a puree.
Add the chopped pineapple, mild Polish mustard, icing sugar, salt, and pepper, mix well, and serve within 30 minutes of preparation.

name: Sos tatarski delikatny (mild tartar sauce)
summary: A cold mayonnaise and sour cream sauce with pickled mushrooms, vinegar pickles, blanched onion, and hot peppers.

ingredients.name: pickled mushrooms
ingredients.note: chopped, measured in a heaped spoonful

steps: Finely chop the onion, scald with boiling water in a sieve, refresh with cold water, and set aside to drain.
Finely chop the vinegar pickle and the hot pickled pepper.
Combine the mayonnaise with the sour cream and fold in the onion, pickle, pepper, and pickled mushrooms.
Season the sauce with mustard, salt, icing sugar, pepper, lemon juice, and mushroom marinade vinegar, and serve within an hour of preparation.

name: Spicy tartar sauce (Sos tatarski pikantny)
summary: A spicy mayonnaise and sour cream sauce with pickled peppers, tart apple, mixed fresh herbs, and cayenne pepper.

ingredients.name: fresh herbs
ingredients.note: measured in heaped spoonfuls, such as parsley, dill, chives and cress

steps: Very finely chop the pickled peppers, peeled apple, and fresh herbs.
Combine the mayonnaise with the sour cream, add the chopped ingredients, and mix.
Season the sauce with mild mustard, cayenne pepper, salt, white pepper, and icing sugar.
Cover the dish tightly with aluminium foil and chill in a cool place for 60 minutes before serving.

name: Delicate spring herb sauce (Sos wiosenny delikatny)
summary: A light sauce made from plain yogurt and whipped sour cream folded with spring onions, dill, chives, parsley, and cress.

ingredients.name: borage leaves
ingredients.note: measured in a heaped spoonful, or young sorrel shoots

steps: Finely chop the spring onions, dill, chives, parsley, cress, and young borage or sorrel leaves.
Pour the plain yogurt into a bowl, add the chopped herbs and onions, and fold in the lightly whipped sour cream.
Season the sauce to taste with salt and pepper and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

name: Old Polish spicy egg sauce
summary: A bold cold sauce made from hard-boiled egg yolks and whites, lemon juice, thick cream, onion, horseradish, and parsley.
steps: Slice the hard-boiled eggs in half lengthwise, remove the yolks, and finely chop the egg whites.
Squeeze the juice from the lemons, discarding the seeds, then mash the yolks with the lemon juice in a bowl until smooth.
Add the thick cream a spoonful at a time, then stir in the onion mashed with a pinch of salt, the grated horseradish, chopped parsley, and icing sugar.
Add the chopped whites, mix again, adjust seasoning to taste if necessary, then wrap the dish in aluminium foil and refrigerate for a few hours (about 3 hours).

name: Sałatka wielkanocna (Easter salad)
summary: A traditional Polish Easter salad of hard-boiled eggs, potatoes, and tart apples in a fresh horseradish and sour cream dressing, garnished with quail eggs and garden cress.
steps: Grate the horseradish on a fine grater, immediately pour over the freshly squeezed lemon juice, and mix thoroughly.
Peel the boiled eggs and potatoes; peel and core the apples.
Cut the eggs, potatoes, and apples into uniform dice, and finely chop the onion.
Combine the diced ingredients with the horseradish in lemon juice.
Season the sour cream with salt, sugar, and white pepper, pour over the salad, and toss together.
Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and chill in a cool place for 60 minutes.
Before serving, garnish the top with sprigs of garden cress and halved hard-boiled quail eggs.

name: Sałatka serowa (cheese salad)
summary: A layered cheese salad served on lettuce leaves with two varieties of firm cheese, hard-boiled eggs, vinegar pickles and red onion in a mayonnaise and sour cream dressing.

ingredients.name: firm cheese
ingredients.note: 2 thick slices, 150 g each, of different varieties, such as Emmental and Gouda

ingredients.name: lettuce leaves
ingredients.note: for lining the bowl and garnishing

steps: Cut both types of cheese into thin strips, dice the vinegar pickles, and cut the red onion into thin slivers.
Chop the hard-boiled eggs.
Mix the mayonnaise with the thick sour cream, combine with the chopped ingredients and fresh herbs, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently.
Line a shallow salad bowl with part of the lettuce leaves, spread the prepared mixture over them, and chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Before serving, sprinkle the top with thin strips shredded from the remaining lettuce leaves.

name: Faszerowane pomidory (stuffed tomatoes with cheese and peas)
summary: Hollowed-out tomatoes stuffed with a savory salad of sharp cheese, canned green peas, and mayonnaise.
steps: Slice off the tomato tops and scoop out the pulp and seeds with a teaspoon.
Lightly season the inside of the tomatoes with salt and pepper, then set aside in a cool place.
Cut the cheese into small cubes the size of green peas, and drain the peas from their brine.
Mix the cheese and peas with the mayonnaise, and season the filling to taste with salt and pepper.
Fill the hollowed tomatoes with the prepared filling, arrange on lettuce leaves, sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves, and serve immediately.

name: Kutia (Christmas wheat pudding)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve dessert of cooked wheat berries, ground poppy seeds, honey, whipping cream, and brandy-soaked dried fruit and nuts.
steps: Rinse the hulled wheat berries, cover with lukewarm water, and leave to soak overnight.
The next day, drain the wheat, cover with fresh water, and boil until tender, changing the cooking water three times, then drain thoroughly in a sieve.
Rinse the poppy seeds, pour over 500 ml of boiling water, simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, and leave to cool.
Pour the brandy over the raisins and leave them to soak.
Drain the cooled poppy seeds in a fine sieve and pass them twice through a mincer, alternating with the icing sugar during the second grind.
Combine the ground poppy seeds with honey, the drained raisins (reserving the soaking liquid), candied orange peel, cream, chopped nuts, and cooked wheat berries.
Shape the mixture into a mound on a serving dish and refrigerate until chilled.
Before serving, arrange the sliced dried fruit around the edges and drizzle with the reserved soaking alcohol.

name: Vegetable risotto
summary: Vegetarian risotto with carrots, bell pepper, green beans, and broccoli florets, sprinkled with grated cheese.
steps: Dice the carrots and bell pepper, and finely chop the scallions with their greens.
Heat the oil in a pot or deep skillet, add the carrots, bell pepper, and scallions, and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and fry together for another 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the hot vegetable broth and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes.
Add the chopped green beans and broccoli florets, and cook for another 15 minutes until the vegetables and rice are tender.
Season the dish with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with grated cheese before serving.

name: Nut and chocolate torte (Tort orzechowy z czekoladą)
summary: A baked flourless nut torte made with whipped egg whites, covered with a thick glaze of dark chocolate and cream.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: squeezed juice of the whole lemon

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: heaped, plus extra for dusting the tin

steps: Preheat the oven to 160 °C, grease a medium springform cake tin with fat, and dust it generously with breadcrumbs.
Mix the finely chopped nuts with two heaped tablespoons of breadcrumbs.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites, beat the yolks with the icing sugar until pale and fluffy, and stir in the lemon juice.
Add the prepared nuts to the yolk mixture, top with the stiffly beaten egg whites, and gently fold together.
Transfer the batter to the springform tin and bake for 50–55 minutes, until the top is golden and the sides slightly pull away from the tin.
Leave the baked cake in the tin for a few minutes, then turn it out onto a board to cool completely.
Place the cooled torte on aluminium foil, pour over a thick glaze of dark chocolate melted with cream, decorate with nut halves or candied fruit, and serve with whipped cream.

name: Poppy seed torte (Torcik makowy)
summary: A rich no-bake poppy seed torte with butter, honey, raisins, and mixed dried fruit and nuts, covered with a homemade cocoa glaze.

ingredients.name: chopped mixed dried fruit and nuts
ingredients.note: heaped: figs, dates, apricots, and nuts

steps: Pour boiling water over the dry poppy seeds, simmer over very low heat for 10 minutes, then drain thoroughly on a fine sieve and let cool.
Pass the cooled poppy seeds three times through a meat grinder, adding alternating tablespoons of poppy seeds and icing sugar during the third grinding.

Beat the butter with three tablespoons of sugar until pale and fluffy, add the egg yolks one by one, then, continuing to beat, add the honey, ground poppy seeds, raisins, candied orange peel, and chopped mixed dried fruit and nuts.
Transfer the poppy seed mixture to a medium springform cake tin lined with cling film, press down firmly, and refrigerate for about 12 hours.
Place the cocoa powder, water, four teaspoons of butter, sugar, and vanilla sugar in a saucepan, bring to the boil, and simmer over low heat for 7 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove the saucepan from the heat, place it in a bowl of cold water for one minute, and beat the glaze until it begins to thicken.
Turn the chilled torte out onto a serving platter, pour over the thickening cocoa glaze immediately, and chill again before slicing into portions.

name: Couscous with vegetables
summary: Simple vegetarian dish of braised root vegetables, leek, and onion tossed with couscous.
steps: Peel and rinse the vegetables: slice the carrots, parsley root, and leek into rounds or matchsticks, slice the onion into thin strips, and chop the parsley leaves.
Transfer the vegetables to a pot, pour in enough water to just barely cover them, season with salt and pepper, and simmer until tender, topping up with water if needed.
Towards the end of cooking, stir in the couscous and simmer over low heat for 3–6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cover the pot and set aside briefly until the couscous swells, then serve in bowls scattered with chopped parsley leaves.

name: Spaghetti alla bolognese
summary: Spaghetti served with a meat sauce of minced beef, tomatoes, aromatic vegetables, and sour cream, topped with Parmesan.
steps: Finely chop the onion, carrot, and celery, and fry in heated olive oil.
Add the minced beef and cook, stirring, until it loses its raw pink colour.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, stir, and simmer gently over low heat. Towards the end, stir in the sour cream and season with salt, pepper, oregano, and basil.
Cook the pasta in salted water, drain, spoon the hot sauce over, and sprinkle with grated Parmesan.

name: Zupa minestrone (Minestrone)
summary: Classic Italian vegetable soup with beans, smoked bacon, seasonal vegetables, pasta or rice, and grated Parmesan.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the soup (plus water to soak and boil the beans)

steps: Cover the dried beans with cold water and leave to soak overnight, then the next day boil and drain them.
Dice the bacon, zucchini, peeled potatoes, and onion, and cut the celery and carrots into strips.
Scald the tomatoes with boiling water, rinse with cold water, peel off the skins, and cut into pieces.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic, and shred the savoy cabbage and sage or basil leaves into thin strips.
Trim the ends of the green beans and cut the pods into two-centimetre pieces (if using fennel, cut it into batons).
Place the bacon, onion, garlic, parsley, and sage or basil into a large pot, add the olive oil, and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the remaining vegetables except the tomatoes, beans, green beans, and peas, and fry briefly.
Pour in 2.5 l of water, add the cooked beans, season with salt, and simmer covered for 90 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, green beans, and peas (if using young peas, add them later together with the pasta or rice) and cook for 30 minutes.
Add the pasta or rice and optionally the young peas, and cook for another 20 minutes.
Season the soup with salt to taste and serve sprinkled with grated Parmesan.

name: Avocado Stuffed with Seafood
summary: Avocado halves stuffed with canned shrimp or crab salad tossed in a creamy cocktail sauce with mayonnaise and tomato purée.
steps: Drain the shrimp or crab meat in a sieve.
Mix the mayonnaise with the tomato purée and one tablespoon of cognac, brandy, or orange juice.
Cut the unpeeled avocado in half lengthwise, remove the pit, and scoop out the flesh without damaging the skin.
Drizzle the insides of the hollowed avocado skins with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Finely dice the avocado flesh, combine with the prepared dressing and seafood, and spoon the filling into the shells.

name: Polish dried mushroom sauce with sour cream
summary: A traditional Polish sauce made with dried mushrooms, onion cooked in butter until translucent, mushroom broth, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking and boiling the mushrooms

steps: Thoroughly rinse the dried mushrooms in warm water, soak for about 2 hours, then cook in the soaking liquid until tender and drain, reserving the broth.
Dice the onion, brown it in part of the butter, stir in the flour, and mix well.
Blend the roux with about 125 ml of cold mushroom broth, bring to a boil, and dissolve the half bouillon cube into the sauce.
Add the sour cream and remaining butter, stir in the chopped mushrooms, and season the sauce to taste with salt and black pepper.

name: Bigos (Polish hunter's stew)
summary: Classic Old Polish hunter's stew made with fresh and fermented cabbage, slow-braised with meats, smoked bacon, Polish sausage, wild forest mushrooms, and prunes.
steps: Finely shred the fresh cabbage and sauerkraut, place in a large pot, add the wild mushrooms, bay leaves, whole black peppercorns, and salt, and braise until tender for 2–3 hours.
Dice the smoked bacon and render the fat in a frying pan.
In the rendered bacon fat, fry the chopped onion, sliced meat, and kiełbasa until browned.
Drain any excess liquid from the stewed cabbage if needed, then add the fried meat, kiełbasa, bacon, and onion to the pot along with the pan drippings.
Add the dried prunes and simmer over low heat for several hours (ideally in stages over 2–3 days), until the bigos turns thick and dark brown.

name: Hummus
summary: Middle Eastern dip made from cooked chickpeas, tahini sesame paste, garlic, and lemon juice.
steps: Soak the chickpeas in cold water for several hours or overnight.
Drain the chickpeas, cover with fresh water, and cook until tender.
Blend the cooked chickpeas until smooth with the crushed garlic, freshly squeezed lemon juice, tahini, and olive oil.
Season the hummus to taste with salt, black pepper, and herbs and spices, then garnish with chopped parsley leaves before serving.

name: Chleb żytni na kwasie (Polish sourdough rye bread)
summary: Traditional country sourdough rye bread made from dried rye starter refreshed overnight, kneaded with whey, water, or milk, proved by floating in warm water, and baked for an hour.

ingredients.name: raw bread dough
ingredients.note: orig. 1 glass of raw dough reserved from a previous baking to dry as starter

ingredients.name: rye flour
ingredients.note: orig. 3 garnce (12 l) for the main dough, plus about 1 kwarta (1 l) for drying the starter and making the evening sponge

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish kwarta of warm water for refreshing the starter overnight

ingredients.name: whey
ingredients.note: orig. 3 historical Polish kwarty of whey, water, or fresh milk

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: orig. 1 teaspoon per garniec of flour

steps: To prepare the dry sourdough starter (at least 3 days in advance), crumble a glass of raw bread dough and rub it thoroughly with enough rye flour to form a dry, flour-like powder; transfer to a linen bag and dry in an airy place.

In the evening, tip the dried starter into a bowl, pour in a kwarta (1 l) of warm water, and mix with enough rye flour to make a batter as thick as sour cream; cover and leave in a warm place overnight until doubled in volume.

In the morning, sift 3 garnce (12 l) of rye flour into a kneading trough, set half aside for adding later, and into the other half pour 3 kwarty (3 l) of whey, water, or milk, add all the risen overnight starter and 3 teaspoons of salt, and beat thoroughly.
Leave the sponge in a warm place for 3 hours to rise.
Gradually work in the reserved half of the rye flour, along with optional caraway or dill, kneading thoroughly and vigorously. Leave in a warm place to rise again.

Shape into medium loaves (traditionally the loaves were proved by floating them in a trough of warm water until they rose to the surface, then scalded with boiling water) or leave to rise on a floured board.
Place the loaves in a hot oven (about 210 °C) and bake for 1 hour. After 30 minutes, pour hot water over the tops so the baked crust will be glossy.

name: Scalded Sifted Rye Bread
summary: Traditional Polish bread made from boiling-water-scalded sifted rye flour, fermented for 24 hours and given a long proof before baking.

ingredients.name: sifted rye flour
ingredients.note: orig. 5 garnce (20 l): 2 garnce (approx. 4.8 kg) for scalding and 3 garnce (approx. 7.2 kg) for kneading the dough

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for scalding the flour, lukewarm water for kneading the dough, and water for brushing the loaves

steps: On the morning of the first day, place 2/5 of the sifted rye flour (approx. 4.8 kg) into a kneading trough or large bowl and scald with boiling water, stirring into a loose, fairly thin mash.
Set the scalded mash aside in a warm place for 24 hours until well fermented.
The next day, add the remaining 3/5 of the flour (approx. 7.2 kg), add the salt, and pour in enough lukewarm water to obtain a suitably thick dough, then knead vigorously for about 60 minutes.
Leave the kneaded dough in a warm place for 8–10 hours until visibly risen.
Shape round loaves, brush their tops with water, and bake in a very hot oven (230–240 °C) for about 60 minutes.
Immediately after removing from the oven, moisten the hot loaves with water again.

name: Country Yeast Bread with Whey
summary: Traditional Polish country bread made with sweet whey and fresh yeast using a two-stage sponge method, brushed with water or beer for a crisp crust.

ingredients.name: bread flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 garniec (4 l): half for the sponge and half for the dough, plus a little for dusting

ingredients.name: whey
ingredients.note: lukewarm, non-sour, originally 1 kwarta (historical Polish measure)

ingredients.name: water or beer
ingredients.note: for brushing the loaves before baking

steps: Dissolve the yeast in 250 ml of lukewarm, sweet whey, add another 250 ml of whey, and mix with half of the flour (approx. 1.2 kg) to form a loose sponge.
Set the sponge aside in a warm place for about 60 minutes until it is visibly bubbling and active.
Pour in the remaining 500 ml of whey, add the rest of the flour and a tablespoon of salt, knead the dough at length until it pulls away from your hands, and set aside again to rise.
Transfer the risen dough onto a floured board and shape three round, smooth loaves, tucking the edges of the dough underneath.
Set the loaves aside to proof, brushing their surface several times with a pastry brush dipped in water or beer.
Bake in a very hot oven (220–230 °C) for about 50–60 minutes.

name: Chleb pytlowy na drożdżach (Bolted rye bread made with hop yeast)
summary: Traditional bolted rye bread made with homemade yeast prepared from hop decoction, scalded flour, and sourdough starter, with several rising stages and added caraway.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta of water for the hop decoction (plus water for mixing the dough and pouring over the loaves)

ingredients.name: bolted rye flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta (1 l) for scalding with hops, 2 garnce (8 l) for the sponge, and 2 garnce (8 l) for kneading the dough

ingredients.name: sourdough starter
ingredients.note: orig. an egg-sized piece of dough reserved from a previous baking

steps: Boil a handful of dried hops in half a kwarta (500 ml) of water, then strain the boiling decoction through a sieve into a pot to scald 1 kwarta (1 l) of the rye flour, beating the mixture for 30 minutes.
Once cooled to lukewarm, add an egg-sized piece of raw bread dough from a previous baking, knead thoroughly until lump-free, and leave in a warm place overnight.
The next day, mix 2 garnce (8 l) of the rye flour with the prepared hop yeast and lukewarm water, stir well, and leave in a warm place to rise.

Once the sponge has risen and begins to drop slightly, add a półkwaterek (125 ml) of salt and a little caraway, work in the remaining 2 garnce (8 l) of rye flour, knead the dough very thoroughly, and leave in the trough for 3 hours to rise.
Shape into small loaves and set them to rise again on boards or in floured bowls, brushing the loaves with warm water.
Before sliding into a hot oven (about 210 °C), pour boiling water over the loaves, space them apart, and bake for 1–1.5 hours until the loaves feel light in the hand.
Immediately after removing from the oven, brush the crust with clean water using a pastry brush.

name: Jajeczniki (Polish Egg-Enriched Bread Rolls)
summary: Rich yeast-leavened bread rolls made with milk, thirty egg yolks, clarified butter, sugar and lemon zest.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 garniec (4 l): half a garniec for the sponge and half a garniec for kneading, plus a little for dusting

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: lukewarm, originally 3 kwaterki (750 ml) for the sponge and 1 kwaterka (250 ml) for dissolving the yeast

ingredients.name: egg yolks
ingredients.note: originally half a kopa of egg yolks (a historical Polish counting measure), or 10 whole eggs and 10 yolks

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: originally half a kwarta (historical Polish measure), plus butter for greasing the baking sheets

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: beaten with water for brushing the rolls

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for beating the egg and brushing after baking

steps: Mix half of the flour (approx. 1.2 kg) with 750 ml of lukewarm milk, pour in the yeast dissolved in the remaining 250 ml of milk, dust the top with flour, cover, and set aside in a warm place to rise.
When the sponge rises and cracks on the surface, pour in the beaten egg yolks, melted clarified butter, sugar, salt, and grated lemon zest, and mix thoroughly.
Gradually add the remaining flour (approx. 1.2 kg) and knead the dough by hand for about 30 minutes until it pulls away from your hands, then cover and set aside to rise.
Shape rolls from the risen dough on a floured board, arrange on greased baking sheets, and leave to rise again.
Brush the risen rolls several times with an egg beaten with water and bake in a hot oven (200 °C) for about 20–25 minutes, then brush immediately after baking with cold water or translucent glaze.

name: Strucle parzone (scalded sweet yeast loaves)
summary: Rich sweet yeast loaves made with dough scalded with hot milk, enriched with egg yolks, clarified butter, raisins and chopped almonds.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta for scalding, plus 3.5 kwarty to add

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 3 kwaterki for scalding and 1 kwaterka for the yeast

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 4 łuty blanched and cut into strips

ingredients.name: coarse sugar and almonds for sprinkling

steps: Scald half a litre of flour with three kwaterki of boiling milk, beat it smooth with no lumps, and cool it.
Dissolve the yeast in a kwaterka of warm milk, mix it into the scalded flour, and leave it in a warm place until the starter has risen.
Beat the yolks with the sugar and salt, pour them into the risen starter, add the clarified butter and the rest of the sifted flour, and knead hard until the dough comes cleanly away from your hands.
Mix in the raisins and slivered almonds, divide the dough into portions and shape into long loaves, pressing a groove lengthwise down the centre with a rolling pin.
Set them on a baking sheet to rise, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with coarse sugar and almonds, and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes. Slide them onto a wooden board as soon as they are done.

name: Ground Poppy Seed Filling for Cakes
summary: Traditional poppy seed filling made from twice-scalded poppy seeds ground with sweet and bitter almonds, fine sugar and arrack, for filled yeast rolls and cakes.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for scalding the poppy seeds twice

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: originally a quarter of a funt, peeled and ground

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: whole, ground together with the sweet almonds

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: originally half a funt of granulated sugar

ingredients.name: arrack or rum
ingredients.note: originally 1 półkwaterek (historical Polish measure; a small glass)

steps: Pour boiling water over the poppy seeds and let stand for 2 hours, then drain the water, pour fresh boiling water over the poppy seeds again, and leave for another 2 hours.
Drain the plumped poppy seeds thoroughly in a fine sieve.
Pound or finely grind the blanched sweet almonds together with three bitter almonds.

Combine the drained poppy seeds with the almonds and sugar and grind thoroughly for about an hour, or pass the mixture through a grinder three times and then beat until smooth, gradually adding the arrack a teaspoon at a time.
Use the finished poppy seed filling between cake layers or to make filled yeast rolls.

name: Baby zwyczajne (Everyday yeast babkas)
summary: Classic yeast babkas made on a milk-and-flour sponge enriched with egg yolks, stiffly beaten egg whites, clarified butter, bitter almonds, and raisins.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 garniec of sifted, warmed flour

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta (1 l) of lukewarm milk and 1 kwaterka (250 ml) for the yeast

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: orig. 8 egg whites beaten to stiff peaks (added when using 30 yolks)

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish funt (plus extra for greasing the tins)

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish funt of seedless raisins

steps: Sift the flour into a large bowl and warm it slightly, make a well in the centre, pour in a kwarta (1 l) of lukewarm milk and the yeast dissolved in a kwaterka (250 ml) of milk, mix with part of the flour into a thin sponge, and leave to rise.

Once the sponge is actively bubbling, pour in the beaten egg yolks (along with the stiffly beaten whites of 8 eggs if using the smaller number of yolks), and add the sugar, clarified butter, pounded bitter almonds, and raisins.
Knead the dough by hand for a full 1 hour, then transfer immediately to tins greased with butter and coated with breadcrumbs.
Set the tins in a warm place until the dough rises to 3/4 of their height.
Place in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 1 hour.

name: Baby parzone (Scalded-flour Easter yeast babkas)
summary: Traditional tall Easter yeast babkas made with wheat flour scalded with boiling milk, sixty egg yolks, sugar, clarified butter, and vanilla, kneaded for a full hour.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 garniec (1 kwarta = 1 l for scalding and 3 kwarty = 3 l for kneading)

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 5 kwaterki (1.25 l) of boiled milk for scalding the flour and 1 kwaterka (250 ml) for the yeast

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish funts of grated sugar or fine powdered sugar (plus extra for dusting)

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish kwarta of lukewarm clarified butter (plus extra for greasing the tins)

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.note: orig. 1 pod of pounded vanilla (or 2 łuts = 25 g of bitter almonds)

steps: From the measured garniec (4 l) of sifted, dry flour, take one kwarta (1 l) and scald it in a large bowl with the hot milk (1.25 l), pouring slowly and beating vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture cools to lukewarm.
Beat the egg yolks with the icing sugar in a bowl set over a warm water bath until pale, fluffy, and mousse-like.

Slowly pour the yeast dissolved in a kwaterka (250 ml) of milk and the yolks beaten with sugar into the lukewarm scalded flour, beat thoroughly into a smooth sponge, and leave in a warm place (about 30 °C) to rise.
Once the sponge has risen noticeably and cracked on top, pour in the lukewarm clarified butter, add a teaspoon of salt, and gradually work in the remaining 3 l of flour.
Knead the dough by hand for a full 1 hour, adding the pounded vanilla or bitter almonds toward the end, until the dough is smooth and pulls away from your hands.
Leave the dough in the bowl until doubled in bulk, then divide it among tall babka tins greased with clarified butter and coated with breadcrumbs (filling them to 1/3 of their height).
Leave in a warm, draught-free place until the dough fills the tins nearly to the rims, then place in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 45–60 minutes (test with a skewer).
Wait at most 5 minutes after removing from the oven, gently unmould the babkas, and brush thinly with fresh butter and dust with icing sugar to keep them fresh longer.

name: Baby polskie (Traditional Polish yeast babkas)
summary: Fluffy yeast babkas made with scalded flour, sixty egg yolks, clarified butter, sugar, and almonds, with stiffly beaten whites from ten eggs folded in before the dough is transferred to the tins.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta (1 l) for scalding and 3 kwarty (3 l) for kneading

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 3 kwaterki (750 ml) of boiled milk, half a kwarta (500 ml) of cold milk, and 1 kwaterka (250 ml) of lukewarm milk for the yeast

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 4 łuts of grated almonds, or vanilla

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: orig. whites of 10 eggs beaten to stiff peaks

steps: Scald one kwarta (1 l) of the flour with three kwaterki (750 ml) of boiling milk, beating vigorously, and immediately pour in half a kwarta (500 ml) of cold milk.

Once the mixture has cooled to lukewarm, pour in the yeast dissolved in a kwaterka (250 ml) of lukewarm milk along with the egg yolks beaten over a water bath, mix well, rub through a coarse sieve, and set in a warm place to rise.

Once the sponge is bubbling, add the remaining 3 l of flour, pour in half a kwarta (500 ml) of clarified butter, add the sugar and salt, and knead by hand for a full 1 hour until the dough pulls away from your hands.
Toward the end of kneading, work in the grated almonds or vanilla.
Beat the ten egg whites to stiff peaks, fold them gently into the kneaded dough with a spoon, and immediately transfer the batter to prepared babka tins (filling them less than halfway).
Once the dough has risen nearly to the top of the tins, place immediately in an oven preheated to 185 °C and bake for 1 hour.
Unmould the baked babkas very carefully (historically they were laid on their sides on a soft pillow), taking care that they do not collapse.

name: Babki bez ambarasu (Easy thirty-yolk yeast babkas)
summary: Traditional Easter yeast babkas made with thirty egg yolks, sifted wheat flour, whole milk, sugar, and clarified butter, kneaded without scalding the flour beforehand.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec of well-sifted, warmed flour

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta (500 ml) of unskimmed milk for the sponge, plus 1 kwaterka (250 ml) for the yeast

ingredients.name: egg yolks
ingredients.note: orig. half a kopa of well-beaten yolks

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half historical Polish kwaterki of lukewarm clarified butter (plus extra for greasing the tins)

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: or several pounded bitter almonds for aroma

steps: In a large bowl, combine half a kwarta (500 ml) of the milk with the yeast dissolved in a kwaterka (250 ml) of milk, gradually adding the sifted, warm flour.
Finally, pour in the egg yolks beaten until fluffy, mix very thoroughly with a spoon so no lumps of raw flour remain, dust the top with flour, and leave in a warm place (25–30 °C) to rise.
Once the dough has risen well, punch it down, pour in the lukewarm clarified butter, add the sugar and vanilla, and knead by hand for at least 1 hour until the dough pulls away from your hand.
Divide the dough among three buttered babka tins, filling them to 1/3 of their height, and set in a warm place until risen nearly to the rims.
Place the risen babkas in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 45–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

name: Babka z mąki kartoflanej (Potato starch sponge bundt cake)
summary: A light sponge bundt cake made with fifteen eggs, sugar, ground almonds, lemon juice, and potato starch.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a historical Polish funt

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter of a historical Polish funt of almonds, including 4 bitter almonds

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice squeezed from a whole lemon

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish funt of potato starch

steps: Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds in boiling water, slip off their skins, and pound finely in a mortar or grind.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until fluffy and almost white, then stir in the ground almonds and the juice of the whole lemon.
Beat the remaining egg whites to very stiff peaks.
Add the potato starch and stiff egg whites alternately by the spoonful to the yolk mixture, folding gently so that the final addition is potato starch.
Grease a babka tin with clarified butter, coat with breadcrumbs, quickly pour in the batter, and place immediately in an oven well heated to 180 °C.
Bake for about 40–45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

name: Raisin filling for sheet cakes and crepes
summary: A fragrant, sharp filling of chopped and pounded large raisins, sugar and lemon juice.
steps: Rinse the large raisins, pick out any seeds, and chop them finely with a knife.
Put the raisins in a bowl, add the sugar and the freshly squeezed juice of half a lemon.
Grind the mixture with a pestle, or blend it, into a thick, tangy paste and use it to fill baked sheet cakes or crepes.

name: Placek ze śliwkami (yeast sheet cake with plums)
summary: A traditional yeast sheet cake topped with fresh halves of ripe plums and sprinkled with sugar.
steps: Stir the yeast with warm milk and part of the flour in a bowl, and leave the starter in a warm place until it rises.
When the starter is moving, add a teaspoon of butter, the sugar, the yolks and the rest of the flour, knead to a smooth yeast dough, and leave it until doubled.
Stretch the risen dough lightly on a buttered baking sheet.
Lay the plum halves closely on top, skin side down, leave the cake to rise again, and sprinkle with part of the sugar.
Bake in an oven heated to 190 °C for about 30 minutes, and sprinkle with the rest of the sugar as soon as it comes out.

name: Sour Cherry Yeast Flatbread Cake (Placki z wiśniami)
summary: A thin yeast or puff-pastry sheet cake densely topped with pitted szklanki sour cherries, sugared an hour beforehand and drained of excess juice, briefly baked and generously dusted with sugar while hot.

ingredients.name: yeast dough
ingredients.note: or puff pastry, for a very thin base

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.note: part for macerating the cherries 1 hour before baking, part for generously dusting the hot cake

steps: Pit the sour cherries, toss them with fine sugar, and let stand for 60 minutes to release their juice.
Stretch a very thin layer of yeast dough (or puff pastry) onto a baking sheet and leave to rise.
Pour off the juice released by the cherries, arrange the fruit densely over the risen dough, and place immediately into a hot oven with stronger bottom heat (200 °C, about 20–25 minutes).
As soon as you remove the cake from the oven, dust the hot top generously with sugar.

name: Grated Orange Mazurek (Mazurek z tartemi pomarańczami)
summary: A Polish mazurek on a thin arrack-scented shortcrust base topped with a thick citrus paste of 4 whole grated large oranges, 2 whole grated lemons, and powdered sugar cooked down over the fire for half an hour and garnished with candied orange peel.

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.note: large, whole, grated along with their juice without seeds

ingredients.name: candied orange peel
ingredients.note: cut into oblong rectangles, for garnish

steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from 400 g of wheat flour, 200 g of butter, 2 eggs, 100 g of sugar, and a splash of arrack, roll out thinly on a baking sheet, and bake in a moderate oven (180 °C, about 15 minutes).
Grate 2 whole lemons and 4 large oranges along with their juice, carefully discarding all seeds.

Beat the grated citrus fruit with 800 g of fine sugar, transfer to a saucepan, and cook over the heat for about 30 minutes, stirring constantly, until the excess moisture evaporates and the mixture thickens considerably.
Spread the hot orange mixture in a thick layer over the freshly baked shortcrust base, leave to dry on the surface, and garnish with pieces of candied orange peel.

name: Crustless Raisin Mazurek (Mazurek rodzynkowy bez ciasta)
summary: A flourless mazurek on wafer sheets, made from pounded sultanas, currants, and blanched almonds ground with sugar, potato starch, 4 beaten eggs, and warm spices.

ingredients.name: sultanas
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt Turkish raisins

ingredients.name: Zante currants
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt small black Corinthian currants

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt blanched almonds

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt potato starch

ingredients.name: warm spices
ingredients.note: ground cinnamon, cloves, and mace or nutmeg

steps: Pound in a mortar (or grind) 200 g each of sultanas, currants, and blanched, peeled almonds, grinding them together with 400 g of sugar.
Stir in 100 g of potato starch, pour in 4 well-beaten eggs, add 1 teaspoon of ground warm spices (cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg or mace), and mix thoroughly.
Spread the mixture onto wafer sheets in a 2 cm layer and bake in a moderate oven (175 °C) for about 25 minutes.

name: Mazurek daktylowy (Date Mazurek, a Polish Easter Flat Cake)
summary: Flourless Polish Easter flat cake on wafer sheets made from a thick white icing beaten from six egg whites, icing sugar, and lemon juice, folded with thinly slivered almonds and vanilla.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt, finely and thinly sliced

steps: Beat six egg whites with the icing sugar until a completely white, thick icing forms.
Squeeze in the juice of one lemon, add the thinly slivered almonds and a pinch of vanilla, and mix thoroughly.
Spread the mixture over wafer sheets arranged on a baking sheet.
Place into a moderate oven (150–160 °C) for about 20 minutes until the cake dries thoroughly.

name: Mazurek Layered with Preserves (Mazurek przekładany konfiturami)
summary: A four-layer Polish mazurek made from thinly rolled spiced almond pastry scented with cloves and cassia buds, stacked while hot with hawthorn marmalade, raspberry preserve, or currant jelly.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt blanched and peeled almonds

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt fresh butter (plus a little for greasing the baking sheets)

ingredients.name: cassia buds
ingredients.note: 50 pounded cassia buds (or 1 tsp ground cinnamon)

ingredients.name: fruit marmalade
ingredients.note: hawthorn or raspberry marmalade, or currant jelly, for layering

steps: Pound the blanched almonds in a mortar and knead them at length in a cool place with 400 g of sugar, 400 g of unsalted butter, 600 g of wheat flour, 3 eggs, 50 pounded cloves, and 50 pounded cassia buds.
Divide the dough into 4 portions, roll each out as thinly as possible, and bake separately on baking sheets or sheets of paper thinly greased with butter (about 10–12 minutes at 180 °C).

Spread the hot pastry layers immediately after baking with hawthorn or raspberry marmalade or currant jelly, stack them one on top of another, and leave until the next day so they bond firmly together.
The next day, optionally ice the top and cut the mazurek into pieces.

name: Hard-Boiled Egg Mazurek (Mazurek z twardych jaj)
summary: A flourless Polish mazurek on wafer sheets made from mashed hard-boiled egg yolks, finely chopped sweet almonds, powdered sugar, vanilla, and the stiffly beaten whites of 6 eggs, dried in a slow oven.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt, finely chopped

ingredients.name: hard-boiled egg yolk
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt yolks from 10–12 hard-boiled eggs

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt fine sugar (plus optional sugar or icing for the top)

steps: Mash 200 g of yolks from 10–12 hard-boiled eggs thoroughly with a spoon in a bowl, then cream them with 200 g of fine sugar, the pounded half vanilla bean, and 200 g of finely chopped sweet almonds.
Beat 6 raw egg whites to stiff peaks and fold thoroughly into the egg-yolk and almond mixture.
Spread the mixture over 6 wafer sheets glued together (if you do not plan to ice the mazurek after baking, sprinkle the top with sugar before placing it in the oven).
Place in a low oven (140–150 °C) for about 25 minutes until the mazurek dries out well, and optionally glaze after removing from the oven.

name: Dry Walnut Mazurek (Mazurek orzechowy suchy)
summary: A crisp shortcrust mazurek made from equal parts wheat flour, butter, mortar-pounded walnuts or hazelnuts, and sugar, enriched with cinnamon, whole eggs, and egg whites, glazed with clear icing once completely cooled.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt fresh butter (plus a little for greasing the baking sheet)

ingredients.name: walnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt shelled walnuts or hazelnuts

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: orig. half a łut (6.25 g), pounded and sifted

steps: Knead 400 g of wheat flour with 400 g of fresh butter on a pastry board in a very cool place.
Pound 400 g of shelled walnuts or hazelnuts in a mortar, gradually adding 400 g of sugar.
Combine the flour-and-butter mixture on the board with the nuts pounded with sugar, 6 g of sifted cinnamon, 2 whole eggs, and 2 egg whites, and knead very thoroughly.
Press the shortcrust dough out by hand directly onto a buttered baking sheet (without paper) and bake in a moderate oven (175 °C) for 30 minutes.
Once completely cool, carefully lift the mazurek from the baking sheet and coat with clear icing.

name: Christmas Eve Makagigi-Style Honey Mazurek (Mazurek miodowy na podobieństwo makagigi)
summary: A no-bake Christmas Eve mazurek on thick wafer sheets, made with golden-caramelized honey briefly boiled with cooked, chopped orange peel, grated wholemeal bread, cloves, and mace.

ingredients.name: grated wholemeal bread
ingredients.note: orig. a generous half kwaterka grated wholemeal bread (approx. 80 g)

ingredients.name: mace
ingredients.note: a small piece, pounded and sifted

steps: Boil the peel from half an orange until tender, trim away the bitter white pith (albedo), and chop finely.
Caramelize 250 ml (1 kwaterka) of honey in a stoneware or heavy-bottomed saucepan until golden brown.
Stir the chopped orange peel, 150 ml of grated wholemeal bread, and the pounded, sifted cloves and mace into the hot honey, then bring briefly to a boil together.
Pour the hot mixture onto thick wafer sheets, leave until completely set and hardened, and then slice diagonally into diamonds.

name: Poppy-seed torte
summary: An old Polish torte of dry, ground poppy seed with almonds, a great many eggs and spices, filled with jam.

ingredients.name: dry poppy seed
ingredients.note: orig. 24 łuty dry grey poppy seed

steps: Grind the dry poppy seed three times to a fine dust, or pound it with the sugar in a bowl.
Add the ground almonds, cinnamon and cloves, then beat in the whole eggs and the extra yolks one at a time until the mixture has grown a great deal and turned pale.
Pour the batter into a buttered springform tin.
Bake in an oven heated to 175 °C for about 45 minutes.
Once cool, cut the torte into two layers, fill it with sharp jam, and pour punch icing over it.

name: Baumkuchen (Sękacz spit cake)
summary: Traditional pyramidal Polish spit cake made from forty eggs, butter, sugar, potato starch, and sweet cream, baked in successive layers on a wooden spit rotating over an open fire and glazed to resemble birch bark.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish funts of fresh butter (plus extra for greasing the paper)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish funts of sugar (plus extra for the icing)

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter of a łut (about 3.1 g)

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: orig. from 40 eggs, beaten to stiff peaks (plus extra whites for the icing)

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish funts of potato starch

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish kwarty of rich cream

steps: Mount a conical wooden sękacz roller on a spit, wrap it in buttered paper, and bind closely with thin twine.

Cream the butter in a large mixing bowl with a wooden pestle until it has the consistency of cream. Continue beating for an hour, adding the egg yolks one at a time alternately with spoonfuls of sugar until all 40 yolks are incorporated.
Stir in the cinnamon and grated lemon zest.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them into the batter alternately by the spoonful with the potato starch, then finally pour in the 2 l of sweet whipping cream.
Heat the wooden roller rotating on the spit over the fire (or in a sękacz oven) with a drip pan set underneath to catch the excess batter.
Ladle a thin coat of batter over the rotating roller and brown it, then apply successive coats (6–8 layers in total), letting the dripping batter form the characteristic gnarls and spikes.

Once baked and slightly cooled, trim the sides evenly with a knife, untie the string, and slide the cake off the roller. When completely cold, coat unevenly with an egg-white and sugar glaze to resemble birch bark.

name: Sponge torte with lemon and almond cream
summary: A classic sponge layered with a fragrant cream of boiled lemons, ground almonds and sugar, finished with punch icing.
steps: Boil the whole lemons in water until soft, chop them, remove every seed, and cook them for 15 minutes over low heat in a thick syrup made with part of the sugar.
Grind or pound the blanched, peeled almonds finely.
Mix the lemons with the almonds and the rest of the sugar, and beat the mixture in a bowl or mixer to a smooth paste.
While the lemon-almond cream is still warm, spread it between the baked, cooled sponge layers.
Cover the assembled torte with punch icing and decorate it with whatever jam you like.

name: Orange torte on shortcrust
summary: An old English torte of whole oranges boiled soft and rubbed smooth, on a shortcrust base, baked in a tin.

ingredients.name: beef suet or butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of kidney suet or butter

steps: Cut the flesh out of the oranges and remove the seeds. Boil the peels in water until soft, drain them, and grate them to a smooth pulp.
Mix the peel pulp with the rubbed flesh, 400 g of sugar and a spoonful of butter, pour it into a saucepan, and cook over low heat for 1 hour until thick.
Knead a shortcrust from the flour, 100 g of fat (suet or butter), 100 g of sugar and the egg, and line the base and sides of a springform tin with it.
Bake the base in an oven heated to 180 °C until it is half done.
Spread the orange mixture on the half-baked base and finish baking at 170 °C for about 45 minutes.

name: Chestnut torte
summary: A delicate torte of roasted sweet chestnuts and ground almonds, on a fluffy foam of whites, with butter beaten with yolks.

ingredients.name: roasted sweet chestnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 12 łutów after roasting and peeling

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Rub the roasted, peeled sweet chestnuts through a fine sieve.
Beat the soft butter until fluffy, and add the ground almonds, the rubbed chestnuts and the icing sugar.
Without changing the direction of beating, add the yolks one at a time and beat for 20 minutes in all.
Whip the whites to a stiff foam. Fold the chestnut mixture gently into the foam (add the mixture to the foam, not the other way round).
Turn the batter into a buttered, crumbed springform tin, bake at 175 °C for 30 minutes, and serve warm, dusted with icing sugar or finished with icing.

name: Provence torte
summary: Meringue-almond layers filled with a cream of beaten butter, toasted hazelnuts and cream, and covered with punch icing.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt for the layers and half a funt do kremu

ingredients.name: hazelnuts
ingredients.note: orig. a funt of Turkish hazelnuts in the shell (dried and ground once peeled)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt young butter

steps: Grind the blanched, peeled, dried almonds finely with 200 g of icing sugar and sift them.
Whip the whites to a stiff foam, quickly fold in the almonds and sugar, spread the mixture on two cake tins lined with baking paper, and bake at 150 °C for 30 minutes so they do not brown too much.

For the cream, toast the hazelnuts, rub off the skins, grind and sift them. Beat the butter until fluffy, add 200 g of icing sugar, the nuts and the cream, mix, and chill in the refrigerator for 1–2 hours.
When the cream has set, sandwich the cooled almond layers with it to make the torte.
Pour punch icing over the top and, once it has dried, cut with a knife dipped in hot water.

name: Chocolate torte on Karlsbad wafers
summary: A quick wafer torte layered with a thick homemade fondant of cooked chocolate, sugar, cream and butter.
steps: Mix broken or grated chocolate, sugar, sweet cream and a teaspoon of butter in a small saucepan.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring all the time, until it has reduced by half and starts to pull into a thick mass.
Take it off the heat and, while it is still hot, spread it with a knife over round wafer sheets, stacking them on a plate lined with paper.
Cover with the last wafer, pour the remaining chocolate over the top and sides of the little torte, and leave it to set.

name: No-bake chocolate torte
summary: A fine unbaked torte of chocolate, ground almonds, sugar and cooked yolks, layered with an almond and cream filling.

ingredients.name: chocolate
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt for the mixture, plus 4 łuty for the glaze

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt for the mixture, plus 4 łuty for the filling

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt for the mixture and 1 łyżka for the filling

ingredients.name: wafer sheet
ingredients.note: a round wafer for the base

ingredients.name: whipping cream (30%)
ingredients.note: 1 łyżka do nadzienia i 2 łyżki for the glaze

steps: Mix grated chocolate, blanched peeled ground almonds, sugar and hard-boiled yolks rubbed through a sieve. Knead it by hand into an even, pliable mass and divide it in two.
Lay a round wafer on a flat plate and spread and press half the chocolate mixture evenly over it with your hands.
For the filling, beat finely ground almonds with a spoonful of sugar, pounded vanilla and a spoonful of cream, and spread that layer on the chocolate base.
Cover with the second half of the chocolate mixture and smooth the top.
Melt the remaining chocolate in 2 spoonfuls of hot cream, pour it over the whole torte, and leave it in a cool place to set.

name: Buckwheat-flour torte
summary: A gluten-free torte of buckwheat flour beaten with butter, sugar, ground almonds and eggs, filled with sharp jam.

ingredients.name: butter and gluten-free breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Beat the soft butter until fluffy, adding the eggs one at a time, then the sugar, the ground almonds and the vanilla.
At the end, sprinkle in the buckwheat flour a spoonful at a time, folding the ingredients together gently.
Pour the batter into a springform tin buttered and sprinkled with gluten-free breadcrumbs.
Bake in an oven heated to 175 °C for about 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Once cool, cut the cake into two or three layers, fill them with sharp jam, reassemble, and pour clear icing over the top.

name: Classic Vanilla Meringues
