summary: Classic French meringues made from twelve stiffly whipped egg whites with gradually added sifted icing sugar and vanilla bean, dried in a low oven until the next day.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt of sugar sifted through a fine sieve

steps: Sift the icing sugar mixed with the pounded half vanilla pod through a fine sieve.
Whip twelve egg whites to very stiff peaks.
Without stopping whipping, slowly add the vanilla icing sugar a little at a time until all of it is incorporated and the meringue is thick and glossy.
Spoon portions of the meringue onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Place the baking sheet into a preheated low oven (110–120 °C), dry for about 60 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the meringues inside until the next day to dry completely.

name: Translucent White Fondant Glaze
summary: Classic confectioner's poured fondant made from sugar syrup boiled with a tablespoon of vinegar to the thread stage and beaten after cooling into a white paste, thinned with rosewater, arrack, or citrus juice.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: as much as the sugar absorbs

ingredients.name: rosewater, arrack, or lemon juice
ingredients.note: for thinning the fondant paste before glazing

steps: Pour as much water over the sugar in a saucepan as it will absorb, set over the heat, and add a tablespoon of vinegar while boiling.
Boil the syrup to the thread stage (approx. 106–110 °C), then pour it out onto a porcelain platter or marble slab to cool completely.
Transfer the cooled syrup to a bowl and beat with a wooden pestle or mixer until it turns completely white and transforms into a smooth, thick fondant paste.

Before use, thin the required portion of fondant with rosewater for yeast cakes, or with arrack and lemon juice for pączki (Polish doughnuts) and mazurki (Polish Easter flat cakes), then brush onto the slightly cooled baked goods.

name: Opaque White Royal Icing
summary: Thick, chalk-white royal icing beaten for half an hour from icing sugar, four egg whites, and lemon juice, with optional arrack.
steps: Place the sifted icing sugar and four egg whites in a bowl.
Beat the ingredients in one direction for at least 30 minutes (or whip with a mixer on low speed) until a snow-white, thick icing forms.
Add freshly squeezed lemon juice to taste (along with a little arrack if a punch flavor is desired) and mix thoroughly.

name: Orange Zest Sugar Paste and Glaze for Cakes
summary: Aromatic sugar paste made by rubbing sugar cubes against fresh orange rind, boiled into a thick orange glaze for pouring over hot sponge cakes and tortes.

ingredients.name: sugar cubes
ingredients.note: originally half a funt for one cake

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.note: thick-skinned, for rubbing the sugar and squeezing the juice

steps: Rub the sugar cubes against the scalded, thick rind of the oranges until they are completely saturated with essential oils and turn yellow.
Pound the rubbed sugar in a mortar into a moist paste (which can be stored in an airtight glass jar).
To prepare the glaze for one cake, pour three tablespoons of water over 200 g of the orange sugar paste and boil to the thread stage (approx. 106–110 °C).

Pour the boiled syrup into a porcelain bowl, let cool, and beat with a pestle or spoon into a smooth glaze, adding lemon or sour orange juice a little at a time, then pour immediately over a sponge cake just taken from the oven.

name: Classic Puff Pastry
summary: Classic laminated puff pastry made with equal parts wheat flour and chilled butter, folded and rolled four times in a cool room.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, enough to make the dough supple without sticking to the rolling pin

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt, chilled in cold water and squeezed dry

steps: Wash the butter in very cold water and leave it in the water for an hour, then squeeze firmly in a cloth to remove excess water and roll out through the cloth into a square about 2.5 cm thick.
Knead a smooth, elastic dough from the flour, egg, a tablespoon of vinegar or spirit, and cold water, and let rest on the board for about fifteen minutes.
Roll out the dough in a cool place to the thickness of a finger, place the square of butter in the center, and fold the edges of the dough over it like an envelope.
Roll out the dough carefully in one forward motion away from yourself to a thickness of about 1 cm, fold into three or four layers, and set aside in a cool place for 10 minutes.
Repeat the rolling, folding, and 10-minute chilling a total of four times.
Roll out the finished pastry, shape your pastries, and bake in a very hot oven (220 °C) for about 15–20 minutes.

name: Yeast-Laminated Danish Pastry
summary: Yeast-leavened laminated pastry enriched with egg yolks, milk, and lemon zest, folded three times with chilled unsalted butter for crescents, turnovers, or rings.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole (1 whole egg for the dough and 1 for brushing the top)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon for the dough plus coarse sugar for sprinkling

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: originally half a funt, squeezed dry and chilled

steps: Mix the flour with the yeast dissolved in cold milk, add three egg yolks and one whole egg beaten with a tablespoon of sugar along with the lemon zest, knead the dough until air bubbles appear, and set aside in a moderately warm place to rise.
Squeeze the unsalted butter in a cloth, flatten it on a plate, and chill in the refrigerator until firm.
Roll out the risen dough into a square in a cool place, set the slab of butter in the center, and fold the corners of the dough over the center like an envelope.
Roll out the dough carefully and fold it three times, letting it rest for a few minutes between each turn.
Cut out pastries, crescents, or rings from the dough, let rise on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with coarse sugar, and bake in a hot oven (200 °C) for about 15–20 minutes.

name: Poppy Seed Lattice Pastries
summary: Round yeast or puff pastry tartlets with a raised rim, filled with a thick layer of dry-ground poppy seeds, sugar, almonds, and eggs, topped with a pastry lattice and glaze.

ingredients.name: yeast dough, Danish pastry, or puff pastry
ingredients.note: for round bases with a rim and a lattice for the top

ingredients.name: poppy seeds
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt, ground dry without scalding

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 8 łut, peeled and finely ground

ingredients.name: ground cinnamon
ingredients.note: half a teaspoon together with the cloves

steps: Thoroughly grind the dry poppy seeds with the sugar and the blanched, finely ground almonds.
Beat the egg yolks and whole eggs into the poppy seed mixture one at a time, add the ground cinnamon and cloves, and mix thoroughly.
Shape round bases with a raised rim from the yeast or puff pastry so that the poppy seed filling does not run out.
Spread a layer of the poppy seed filling about 1.5–2 cm thick onto the pastry bases and arrange a thin lattice of pastry strips on top.
Place the pastries immediately into a hot oven (200 °C) and bake for 15–20 minutes.
As soon as you take them out of the oven, brush the hot pastries with translucent sugar glaze.

name: Rogale drożdżowe (yeast crescents)
summary: Soft butter yeast crescents rolled from a sheet of dough and baked until golden.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in part of the warm milk with a little flour, and leave the starter in a warm place until it begins to move.
Add the rest of the milk, the beaten eggs, the melted warm butter and the rest of the flour to the risen starter, and knead until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Leave the dough to rise in a warm place, and when it has doubled, roll it out and cut triangles or diamonds.
Roll each crescent from the wide edge toward the point, set them on a baking sheet, and leave them to rise again.
Brush the risen crescents with beaten egg and bake in an oven heated to 200 °C for about 20 minutes, until golden.

name: Briosze (Brioche buns)
summary: French-style yeast-and-butter brioche buns rich in unsalted butter and eggs, proved overnight in a cool room and shaped with a characteristic topknot.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt (400 g) for the dough and a quarter of a funt (100 g) for the sponge (plus extra for dusting)

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: orig. 6 whole eggs for the dough (plus 1 for brushing before baking)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish funt of unsalted butter (plus a little for the baking sheet)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: lukewarm, or milk, for mixing the yeast sponge

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 large tablespoon of fine sugar

steps: In a separate bowl, mix 100 g (a quarter of a funt) of the flour with the yeast and a little lukewarm water or milk into a sponge, and set aside to rise.
Mound the remaining 400 g (1 funt) of flour on a pastry board, break in the 6 eggs, and crumble the unsalted butter into the flour.
Once the yeast sponge is bubbling, pour it onto the board with the flour, butter, and eggs, add a large tablespoon of icing sugar, and work gently from underneath into a smooth dough.
Transfer the dough to a floured bowl and leave overnight in a room at moderate temperature.
The next day, turn the dough out onto the board, knead thoroughly, and return it to the floured bowl to rise a little more.
Divide the dough into small buns, top the centre of each with a separately shaped small ball of dough, and set on a buttered baking sheet to rise.
Brush the risen brioches with beaten egg and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 15–20 minutes until golden brown.

name: Lenten Boiled Obwarzanki Rings (Obarzaneczki postne)
summary: Traditional Lenten Polish obwarzanki made from a firm water-based yeast dough, proofed, poached for 2 minutes in boiling water, sprinkled with poppy seeds, coarse salt, or nigella seeds, and baked crisp in a hot oven.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec flour (approx. 1.3 kg, plus a little for dusting the baking sheets)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: lukewarm, for kneading the dough (plus boiling water for poaching the rings)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the dough and for sprinkling

ingredients.name: poppy seeds
ingredients.note: or nigella seeds or coarse salt, for sprinkling

steps: Knead a fairly firm dough (like noodle dough) from 2 liters of wheat flour, 50 g of fresh yeast dissolved in lukewarm water, and salt.
Shape the dough into round or double-twisted oblong obwarzanki rings and set aside in a warm place for 30 minutes to rise slightly.
Drop the risen rings in batches into rapidly boiling water in a wide pot and poach for no longer than 2 minutes.

Lift the obwarzanki out with a slotted spoon, sprinkle with poppy seeds, coarse salt, or nigella seeds, arrange on floured baking sheets, and bake in a hot oven (210 °C) for about 15–20 minutes until lightly browned.

name: Sucharki papieskie (papal rusks)
summary: Crisp anise-and-lemon sponge rusks, baked as a sheet, sliced thin and dried again in the oven.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: about 420 g, weighed in the shell

ingredients.name: olive oil for the baking sheet

steps: Beat the whole eggs with the sugar in a bowl until the mixture is pale and fluffy.
Fold the sifted flour and the grated lemon zest (or pounded anise) into the beaten mixture with a spoon.
Pour the batter onto a baking sheet greased with olive oil and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 25 minutes, until nicely browned.
Take the cake out and let it cool.
Slice the cooled cake thinly with a sharp knife, lay the slices on a sheet, and dry them in a very slow oven heated to 120 °C for about 20 minutes.

name: Traditional molded wafers
summary: Crisp golden wafers cooked in a cast-iron waffle iron or wafer mould and sprinkled with cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 łyżka and more for the iron

steps: Separate the yolks from the whites. Beat the yolks with the sugar, add the flour, a spoonful of clarified butter and the milk, and mix well.
Whip the whites to a stiff foam and fold them gently into the batter.
Heat a wafer iron or waffle iron until very hot, grease it with a brush of clarified butter, and pour in portions of batter.
Cook the wafers on both sides until golden, and sprinkle them with sugar mixed with cinnamon as soon as they come out.

name: Andruty (Rolled wafer cookies)
summary: Thin, crisp wafers made from a thin batter of eggs, flour, cream or milk, and fine sugar, baked in a flat cast-iron wafer iron and rolled while hot around a dowel into tubes.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish kwaterka of dry flour

ingredients.name: sweet cream
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half historical Polish kwaterki of good-quality milk, or preferably cream

steps: Beat the two whole eggs with the wheat flour, gradually adding the milk or sweet cream as for crêpe batter.
Add the fine sugar and whisk thoroughly into a smooth, thin batter.
Heat a flat chequered wafer iron (waffle iron for thin wafers) and brush it lightly with butter.
Pour a spoonful of batter onto the centre of the iron, close it, and bake for about 1–2 minutes until golden.
Lift the baked wafer from the iron and, while still hot, immediately roll it around a wooden dowel into a tube.
Set the finished wafers aside in an airy spot so they cool quickly and stay crisp.

name: Choux Pastry Almond Squares
summary: Sheet-baked choux pastry squares made with butter, water, flour, and seven to eight eggs, generously topped before baking with chopped almonds and sugar.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: originally half a funt of clarified or fresh butter, plus a little for greasing the baking sheet

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: originally half a kwarta (historical Polish measure)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: a scant tablespoon for the water, a tablespoon for the batter, and sugar for sprinkling with the almonds

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally half a kwarta (500 ml) of fine flour

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: orig. 1 whole egg for the hot paste and 6–7 eggs after cooling

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: finely chopped, for sprinkling on top

steps: Bring the water, butter, and a scant tablespoon of sugar to a boil in a saucepan.
Gradually add the wheat flour over low heat, stirring vigorously with a spoon for several minutes until the paste thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan.

Transfer the hot paste to a bowl, immediately beat in one egg, and once cooled, beat in the remaining 6–7 eggs one at a time, thoroughly beating the batter with a spoon each time along with an additional tablespoon of sugar.
Spread the dough in a thin layer on a greased baking sheet, cut into large squares with a knife and sprinkle generously with chopped almonds mixed with sugar.
Place the baking sheet into a hot oven (210 °C) and bake for about 20–25 minutes until the squares puff up high and turn golden brown.

name: Salted Caraway Breadsticks (Paluszki słone)
summary: Crisp salted caraway breadsticks made from a buttery yeast-shortcrust dough (or in the alternative version from a yeast-free shortcrust dough with egg), brushed with egg wash, sprinkled with salt, and baked briefly in a hot oven.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta flour (approx. 325 g)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt fresh butter (for the yeast-free shortcrust version, half a funt = 200 g butter and 1 egg)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: half a teaspoon for the dough and half a teaspoon for sprinkling

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: beaten with a splash of water, for brushing

steps: Knead together 500 ml of wheat flour, 100 g of fresh butter, 12.5 g of yeast dissolved in 2 tablespoons of milk, half a teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and half a teaspoon of caraway seeds.
Once the dough starts to rise, work it in the bowl until it pulls away from your hands, and let it rise slightly again.

Divide the dough on a pastry board into equal pieces and roll between your palms into thin breadsticks 10 cm long (in the second method, knead a yeast-free shortcrust dough from 500 ml of flour, 200 g of butter, 1 egg, half a teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and half a teaspoon of caraway seeds and roll into sticks right away).
Arrange the sticks on a baking sheet, brush with egg beaten with water, sprinkle with salt, and bake in a hot oven (200 °C) for at most 10 minutes until golden.

name: Aniseed Sponge Drops
summary: Traditional sponge cookies made by beating eight eggs with sugar for half an hour, then folding in wheat flour and aniseed.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally three-quarters of a funt of sifted flour, plus a little for dusting

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the molds or baking sheet

steps: Beat eight whole eggs with the fine sugar in a bowl for a full 30 minutes (or whip with a mixer into a thick, pale cream).
Add the sifted wheat flour and a teaspoon of aniseed and fold in gently but thoroughly.
Spoon the batter into small buttered molds, or spread it on a board and cut out rounds with a small floured glass, arranging them on a baking sheet.
Place immediately into a hot oven (190 °C) and bake for 20 minutes without brushing the tops of the cookies.

name: Puff Pastry Cream Horns with Italian Meringue
summary: Baked puff pastry horns dusted with icing sugar and filled after baking with hot Italian meringue made from six egg whites whipped with thick sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: puff pastry
ingredients.note: originally pastry made with half a funt (200 g) of flour

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: whole, beaten for brushing the horns

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: for dusting the horns before baking

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for boiling a thick syrup to the thread or pearl stage

steps: Roll stiff parchment paper into tubes the thickness of a candle (or use metal cream horn molds).
Roll out the puff pastry to the thickness of the back of a knife (approximately 2–3 mm), cut into strips and wrap around the prepared tubes.
Arrange the horns on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, dust with icing sugar, and bake until golden in a hot oven (210 °C, approx. 15–20 minutes), then slide out the paper forms.
Boil a very thick syrup from the sugar and water (to approx. 115–118 °C, the pearl stage), and whip six egg whites to stiff peaks.
Remove the saucepan with the hot syrup from the heat and pour the whipped egg whites into it while whisking constantly into a smooth, glossy meringue cream.
Immediately after whipping, pipe the cream into the baked pastry horns using a pastry bag.

name: Shortcrust Cream Tartlets
summary: Tender shortcrust tartlets baked in fluted molds and filled before baking with a thick cooked custard of whipping cream, egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: originally half a funt of fresh butter, plus a little for greasing the molds

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: originally a quarter of a funt of fine sugar

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: originally 1 półkwaterek (historical Polish measure) of rich cream

steps: Cream 200 g of butter until fluffy, add 100 g of fine sugar, 2 whole eggs, and 300 g of wheat flour, and quickly knead by hand into a uniform, very tender shortcrust dough.
Shape thin rounds on a board and line the bottoms and sides of greased fluted tartlet molds (reserving part of the dough for covering the tops).

In a small saucepan, whisk 2 egg yolks with a tablespoon of sugar, the whipping cream, and the vanilla, and heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard thickens, then set aside in a cool place to cool.
Place a spoonful of cooled custard into each mold, cover with a flat round of dough, and press the edges together, trimming off any excess dough.
Bake in a moderate oven (180 °C) for 20 minutes.

name: Rhubarb Pastry Slices
summary: Layered shortcrust or puff pastry slices filled with a thick preserve made from blanched rhubarb, sprinkled with rosewater and dusted with icing sugar.

ingredients.name: shortcrust or puff pastry
ingredients.note: for two thin layers on a baking sheet

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt, for the marmalade syrup

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for blanching the rhubarb and a little water for the syrup

ingredients.name: rosewater
ingredients.note: for brushing the top of the pastry

steps: Peel the outer strings from the rhubarb stalks, cut into smaller pieces, drop into boiling water, boil briefly, and drain in a sieve.
Boil a thick syrup from the sugar and a little water, add the blanched rhubarb, and cook until a thick marmalade forms, then let cool.
Roll out half of the shortcrust or puff pastry into a thin sheet on a baking tray and spread the layer of rhubarb marmalade over it.
Cover the filling with a second thin sheet of pastry and lightly score the top into portions with a knife to make slicing easier after baking.
Brush the top with rosewater, dust generously with icing sugar, and bake in a hot oven (200 °C) for about 25–30 minutes.

name: Shortcrust Fruit Tartlets
summary: Buttery shortcrust tartlets enriched with ground almonds and baked with a pastry rim, filled after baking with fruit preserves or fruit cooked down until thick.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally half a kwarta, or three-quarters of a funt (historical Polish measures)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: originally a quarter of a funt

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: whole (yolk for the dough, white for brushing the rims)

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 4 łut, peeled and finely ground

ingredients.name: fruit preserves or fruit cooked down until thick
ingredients.note: e.g. gooseberries, cherries, wild strawberries, currants, raspberries, or apples

steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from the wheat flour, cold butter, sugar, one egg yolk, and finely ground almonds.
Roll out the dough on a board and cut out round bases with a glass.
Brush the edges of each round with egg white and attach a narrow strip of the same dough all around to form a rim.
Arrange the tartlets on a baking sheet and bake in a moderate oven (180 °C) for about 15–20 minutes until golden.
After removing the tartlets from the oven, fill their centers with preserves or fruit cooked down with sugar until thick.

name: Almond Macaroons
summary: Classic almond macaroons made from ground sweet and bitter almonds dried with sugar over heat, then cooled, mixed with five whipped egg whites and baked on wafer sheets.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: originally a few sugar lumps for pounding the almonds, plus 1 funt (400 g) of fine sugar

steps: Pound in a mortar or finely grind the sweet and bitter almonds with a few lumps of sugar.
Transfer the ground almonds to a saucepan, add 400 g of fine sugar, and heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the paste dries slightly and no longer sticks to your fingers.
Remove the almond paste from the heat and let it cool completely.
Whip five egg whites to stiff peaks and fold thoroughly into the cold almond paste.
Spoon round portions of the batter onto wafer sheets or parchment paper and bake in a moderate oven (160 °C) for about 15–20 minutes until lightly golden.

name: Marzipan Sugar Leaves
summary: Thinly rolled and cut-out sugar and almond cookies bound with egg whites and gently dried in a low oven.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt of pounded sugar, half for working with the almonds and egg whites and half for kneading

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: for dusting the board when rolling

steps: Pound the blanched and peeled sweet almonds in a mortar into a smooth paste, gradually adding the icing sugar a spoonful at a time.
Beat in two egg whites and continue grinding while adding icing sugar until you have used half of its total amount (200 g).
Turn the beaten mixture out onto a board and knead with the remaining 200 g of icing sugar into a smooth dough.
Roll out the dough thinly on a board lightly dusted with flour and cut out leaf shapes with a cutter.
Arrange the leaves on a parchment-lined baking sheet and dry in a low oven (140–150 °C) for about 15 minutes until they take on a delicate color.

name: Traditional Glazed Marzipan Pastries
summary: Traditional Polish marzipan pastries made from finely grated sweet and bitter almonds ground with sugar and rosewater, aged for several days, broiled from the top, and decorated with lemon icing and candied fruit.

ingredients.name: rosewater
ingredients.note: for grinding the paste and attaching the rims

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: originally 1 funt of ground sugar for the icing

ingredients.name: candied fruit
ingredients.note: cut into strips or triangles, for garnishing

steps: Briefly scald the sweet and bitter almonds with hot water, slip off their skins, spread on a cloth to dry completely, and grate on the finest grater.

Combine the grated almonds with 400 g of finely ground sugar and work in a bowl with the rosewater and a few drops of orange blossom water into a very stiff paste, then set aside in a cool place for 3–4 days.

Roll out the aged marzipan paste on a board dusted with icing sugar to a thickness of about 1 cm, cut out hearts, stars, or other shapes with cutters, and attach a narrow marzipan rim moistened with rosewater around the edges.
Arrange the marzipan pastries on a parchment-lined baking sheet and broil briefly under the top oven element (approx. 4–5 minutes at 200 °C) until browned only on top while remaining pale underneath.
Beat 400 g of icing sugar with the lemon juice and a tablespoon of water into a thick, glossy icing (beating for about an hour or using a mixer).
Spread the icing over the cooled marzipan pastries, leave in a warm place until the glaze sets, and garnish with pieces of candied fruit.

name: Pączki (scalded Polish doughnuts)
summary: Excellent, fluffy yeast doughnuts from a milk-scalded dough rich in yolks and whipped whites, filled with jam and fried in lard.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta for scalding, plus 1 kwarta for the dough

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of boiling milk for scalding, and 1 kwaterka for the yeast

ingredients.name: melted butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt young butter

steps: Scald half a litre of flour with half a litre of boiling milk, rub it smooth, and cool it.
Beat the yolks with the sugar to a white mass, mix in the scalded flour, the yeast dissolved in a kwaterka of milk, and the stiffly whipped whites, and leave the starter in a warm place to rise.

Add a litre of flour, the salt, the grated lemon zest and the melted warm butter to the risen starter. Knead hard for about an hour, until the dough comes cleanly away from your hands, then leave it in the warm to rise further.
When the dough is moving, tear off even pieces, flatten them lightly, put a teaspoon of thick jam on each, pinch the edges shut, and shape round doughnuts.
Set the doughnuts seam side down on a floured board and leave them to rise under a cloth.
Heat the lard in a wide pan to 175 °C. Fry the risen doughnuts in batches, covered, until browned, turn them, and finish uncovered. Drain on paper and dust with icing sugar.

name: Toruński piernik niezawodny (reliable Toruń gingerbread)
summary: A traditional hard old Polish honey-and-rye gingerbread, scalded hot with honey, with anise, cloves, potash, almonds and orange peel.

ingredients.name: rye flour
ingredients.note: orig. 2 kwarty of warmed, sifted rye flour

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: some chopped, some left whole to decorate

steps: Boil the honey in a saucepan with the water, dried orange peel, cloves and anise until it darkens slightly.
Scald the sifted, warmed rye flour with the hot honey, beating hard with a wooden spoon to a smooth dough with no lumps.
Beat 4 eggs into the hot dough, mix well, and leave it in a cool place to cool.
Add the baking soda or potash dissolved in a small glass of food-grade rectified spirit, the yolk, chopped almonds and candied peel to the cooled dough. Knead into a very firm, elastic dough.
Roll the dough out about 2–3 cm thick on a baking sheet lined with baking paper or on a waxed baking sheet. Brush with beaten egg, decorate with whole almonds and bake at 180 °C for about 45 minutes.

name: Makagigi (Polish Poppy Seed and Honey Brittle)
summary: Traditional crisp Polish confection of toasted poppy seeds cooked in thick sugar syrup and honey with a touch of wheat flour, rolled out thin and cut into squares.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for a thick sugar syrup and for moistening the board

steps: Boil a thick syrup from the sugar and a little water, and in a second saucepan heat the dry poppy seeds until very hot.
Pour the finished sugar syrup into the hot poppy seeds, mix thoroughly, and add the honey.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until it releases a distinct aroma of toasted poppy seeds.
Add half a tablespoon of wheat flour and cook for about 10 minutes longer, stirring constantly.
Turn the hot mixture out onto a marble slab or wooden board generously moistened with cold water, roll out thinly with a wet rolling pin, and cut into squares; once cooled, store in an airtight tin.

name: Makagigi tłuczeńce (Spiced Honey, Nut and Rye Wafer Confection)
summary: Caramel-like spiced makagigi made with honey, chopped almonds or other nuts, orange peel and ground baked rye flatbread, layered between wafer sheets.

ingredients.name: rye flour
ingredients.note: for a flatbread to be ground into a kwaterka (approximately 150 g) of baked rye flatbread meal

ingredients.name: sweet almonds or other nuts
ingredients.note: originally half a funt, washed and chopped

ingredients.name: ground cinnamon
ingredients.note: 1 level teaspoon in total together with the ginger and cloves

ingredients.name: wafer sheets
ingredients.note: sheets, for lining and covering the mixture

steps: Knead a simple dough from the rye flour and water, bake it into a flatbread in the oven (190 °C, approx. 20 minutes) until well browned, and once cooled, pound in a mortar or grind into meal and sift through a sieve.
Pour the honey into a saucepan and add the chopped almonds (or other nuts), chopped orange peel and 150 g (1 kwaterka) of meal made from the baked rye flatbread.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens like caramel.
Add a level teaspoon of the sifted spices (cinnamon, ginger, and cloves) and mix well.
Spread the hot mixture over wafer sheets, cover the top with a second layer of wafer sheets, leave until the next day to firm up, and then cut into pieces.

name: Gum Arabic Cough Drops
summary: Traditional homemade cough pastilles made from gum arabic, sugar, twelve egg whites, and orange blossom water, evaporated into a thick paste and cut into cubes.

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: plus a little for dusting the table

ingredients.name: wheat flour or potato starch
ingredients.note: for dusting the table with icing sugar

steps: Quickly rinse the gum arabic with cold water, cover with 1 liter of water, and warm gently until completely dissolved, then strain the solution through a fine cloth.
Add the sugar to the strained solution and reduce over low heat until it has the consistency of a thick syrup.
Gradually add the orange blossom water (or rosewater) and egg whites, stirring constantly over very low heat until the mixture becomes very thick and pliable like dough.
Turn the thick mass out onto a table dusted with flour sifted with icing sugar, roll out, and cut into even cubes.

name: Clear beef broth (rosół wołowy czysty)
summary: A clear beef broth simmered gently for a long time with soup vegetables, an onion roasted in its skin, dried mushrooms, and mace.

ingredients.name: bone-in beef for broth
ingredients.note: orig. 5 Polish funty (1 funt per person for a rich broth or 1/2 funt for a lighter one)

steps: Rinse the beef thoroughly in cold water, place in a pot, cover with 3 l of fresh cold water, salt, and simmer very gently for about 60 minutes, regularly skimming the scum.

Once no more scum forms, remove the pot from the heat, add 1 tbsp of cold water, skim off excess fat, and strain the broth through a fine sieve. Rinse the meat and return it to a clean pot with the strained broth.
Bring the broth back to a boil and add the parsley roots, celeriac, leeks, carrots, the whole onion roasted in its skin, dried mushrooms, and mace.
Simmer the broth over very low heat for another 2.5–3 hours (150–180 minutes) until the meat and vegetables are thoroughly tender.
Before serving, take the pot off the heat briefly, skim off the remaining surface fat, and strain the clear broth into a tureen containing chopped parsley.

name: Zupa à la Julienne (Julienne vegetable beef consommé)
summary: A clear, rich beef consommé coloured with a dark essence from thrice-browned beef and a roasted onion, served with finely julienned vegetables and toasted roll croutons.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: orig. 6 historical Polish funts (5 funts = 2000 g for the broth and 1 funt = 400 g for the browned essence)

ingredients.name: beef suet
ingredients.note: a piece of fresh suet for browning the meat

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the broth and deglazing the meat essence

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: whole, deeply roasted in the oven

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: optional, for gently stewing the vegetables

steps: Simmer a clear, strong broth from 2 kg (5 funts) of the beef together with a whole onion deeply roasted in the oven and salt, then strain.
Place the remaining 400 g (1 funt) of beef in a small saucepan with a piece of fresh beef suet and brown it deeply without adding water, shaking the pan constantly so it does not burn.
Pour off the browned juices that form, moisten the meat with a splash of water, and braise and brown again; repeat this process three times to obtain a dark meat essence.

Cut the carrot, kohlrabi, celeriac, and parsley root into fine matchsticks (julienne), break the cauliflower into tiny florets, dice the asparagus, and cut the scalded savoy cabbage into small pieces.

Add the vegetables along with the green peas to the clear broth and simmer until tender for 1–1.5 hours (alternatively, stew them gently in butter for 30 minutes first, then simmer in the broth for 1 hour).
Before serving, pour the dark braised meat essence into the tureen, ladle the hot vegetable soup over it, and serve with dried wheat roll croutons.

name: Brown caper sauce (sos kaparowy rumiany)
summary: A sweet-and-sour dark sauce made with a browned roux and meat broth, capers, lemon juice, and a little caramel, served with cutlets, roast poultry, and boiled meat.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 2 cubes + a bit of caramel

steps: Melt and brown the butter in a saucepan, stir in plain wheat flour, and cook to a dark golden roux.
Whisk 250 ml of hot meat bouillon into the roux, stirring thoroughly until smooth.
Add the capers, lemon juice, and sugar, caramelising some of the sugar beforehand if desired for a darker colour. Bring everything to a boil and pour over the hot meat.

name: Brown gherkin sauce (sos korniszonowy rumiany)
summary: A robust brown sauce of browned roux and broth simmered with sliced gherkins, vinegar, and a hint of dark caramel.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for sauce and 1 tsp for caramel

steps: Simmer the sliced gherkins for a few minutes in a separate small pot in a few tablespoons of broth until tender.
Brown the butter with plain wheat flour in a saucepan and whisk in the remaining hot broth, stirring constantly.
Stir the gherkins along with their simmering liquid into the sauce, season with vinegar, sugar, and caramelised sugar, and bring to a boil.

name: Sos pieczarkowy biały (white mushroom sauce)
summary: A classic pale sauce of fresh button mushrooms parboiled with lemon juice, thickened with a white roux made with clarified butter and thinned with meat stock and white wine.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: a small amount for parboiling the mushrooms

steps: Clean and rinse the button mushrooms, slice them into strips, and boil until tender in a small amount of water with the juice squeezed from half a lemon so they keep their pale colour.
Heat 1 tablespoon of clarified butter in a separate small saucepan, add 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour, and cook briefly into a pale roux without browning.
Thin the pale roux with the mushroom cooking liquid along with the mushrooms themselves and the hot meat broth or soup-vegetable stock.
Pour in the white wine, stir thoroughly, and bring everything to the boil; serve with roast poultry or cutlets.

name: Sos ogórkowy (pickled cucumber sauce)
summary: A sweet-and-sour sauce based on a dark roux thinned with dried mushroom stock and fermented cucumber brine, finished with diced fermented pickles and caramel.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of pieces of sugar, browned into caramel

steps: Brown 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour with 1 tablespoon of butter in a frying pan or small saucepan.
Thin the roux with the hot dried mushroom stock and pour in the fermented cucumber brine (or boiled vinegar if the brine is too mild).
Add the finely diced fermented pickled cucumbers and the sugar previously browned into caramel.
Bring the sauce to the boil several times and pour it over boiled beef or meatless potato or herring cutlets on a serving platter.

name: Sos szary z rodzynkami (Polish grey sauce with raisins)
summary: A traditional Polish sweet-and-sour sauce based on a golden roux with meat stock, wine, caramel, large raisins, vinegar, and lemon slices, served with tongue, calf's feet, or carp.

ingredients.name: meat stock
ingredients.note: or fish stock (for carp or bream)

ingredients.name: white wine
ingredients.note: for thinning the sauce together with the stock

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of pieces, moistened with water and browned into caramel

steps: Cook 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour with 1 tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan into a roux, thin with the meat stock (or fish stock) and white wine, and bring to the boil.
Moisten the sugar with a little water and brown it in a small pan into a dark caramel, then pour it into the sauce.
Add the thoroughly rinsed large raisins and 1 tablespoon of boiled vinegar, and simmer together for a few minutes.
Just before serving, add the sliced lemon to the sauce; serve with boiled tongue, calf's feet, or fish (carp, bream).

name: Sos szczypiorkowy (chive sauce)
summary: A punchy sauce for boiled beef made from a butter and flour roux thinned with clear meat broth, sharpened with strong vinegar and generously mixed with chopped chives.
steps: Cook 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour with 1 tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan into a roux and thin with the hot meat broth.
Pour in 1 tablespoon of strong vinegar and stir in a handful of finely chopped fresh chives.
Boil the sauce vigorously for a moment and serve hot with boiled beef.

name: Broth or white wine Hollandaise sauce (sos holenderski)
summary: An airy egg-yolk and butter sauce with lemon juice, a little sugar and flour, thinned with broth or white wine and gently heated until thickened.

ingredients.name: meat broth or dry white wine

steps: Beat the fresh butter until light and fluffy, whisk in the egg yolks, plain wheat flour, lemon juice, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Pour in the meat broth or white wine and whisk until smooth.
Set the saucepan over very low heat and warm while whisking continuously without letting it boil until the sauce rises and thickens.

name: White lemon sauce for poultry and fish (sos cytrynowy biały)
summary: A delicate pale butter-flour sauce thinned with poultry broth, freshly squeezed whole lemon juice, a splash of white wine or mushroom stock, and sugar.

ingredients.name: dry white wine or dried mushroom broth

steps: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook the plain wheat flour to a pale roux without browning.
Whisk the hot poultry broth or fish stock into the roux, stirring until smooth.
Squeeze in the juice of a whole lemon, add white wine or mushroom broth, sugar, and a pinch of salt, bring briefly to a boil, and ladle over the dish.

name: Dill and sour cream white sauce (sos biały z koperkiem)
summary: A creamy white sauce made from a pale butter-flour roux thinned with broth or fish stock, finished with sour cream and fresh chopped dill.
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook the plain wheat flour into a pale white roux without browning.
Whisk the hot broth or fish stock vigorously into the roux until smooth.
Stir in the sour cream, chopped dill, a pinch of salt, and optional sugar, bring briefly to a boil, and ladle over fricassee or fish.

name: Sos pomidorowy (fresh tomato sauce)
summary: A thick sauce made from fresh, ripe tomatoes stewed in butter and pressed through a sieve, combined with a pale roux and rich meat stock.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon for stewing the tomatoes and 1 tablespoon for the roux

ingredients.name: meat stock
ingredients.note: rich, for moistening the tomatoes and thinning the sauce

steps: Wash and cut up the large, ripe tomatoes, then cook them gently in butter in a saucepan, moistening with a little meat stock, until they break down completely into a pulp.
Press the cooked tomatoes through a sieve so that only the seeds remain behind, and mix the purée with 2 teaspoons of sugar.
In a separate small saucepan, cook 1 tablespoon of butter with 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour into a pale roux.
Combine the roux with the tomato purée, season with salt to taste, and thin with the rich meat stock to a fairly thick consistency.
Bring the sauce to the boil and serve with boiled beef, mutton, duck, or goose.

name: Sos śmietankowy (vanilla cream sauce)
summary: A sweet vanilla cream sauce thickened over low heat with egg yolks, served with cold desserts and puddings.

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a Polish quart (500 ml) for boiling and 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of cold cream for beating the yolks

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.note: a piece of pod, crushed and tied in muslin or cheesecloth

steps: Bring 500 ml of whipping cream to the boil in a small saucepan with 2 tablespoons of sugar and the crushed piece of vanilla pod tied in cheesecloth, then set aside to cool.
Whisk 4 egg yolks with 2 tablespoons of cold whipping cream.
Remove the vanilla from the cooled cream and combine the cream with the whisked egg yolks.
Heat the sauce over very low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens (taking care not to let it boil); once cooled, serve with cold sweet puddings.

name: Béchamel sauce with egg yolks (biszamel)
summary: A thick sauce made with fresh butter, wheat flour and unsweetened cream, cooled and enriched with egg yolks, for spooning over and baking veal, turkey or boiled beef.
steps: Cream the cold fresh butter with a full tablespoon of wheat flour until completely smooth.
Set the saucepan over the heat, bring the butter and flour briefly to a bubble, and whisk in the sweet cream, stirring constantly.
Boil until thickened, rub through a sieve, and set aside until completely cool.
Whisk the egg yolks thoroughly into the cooled sauce; spoon over roast veal or turkey, or use to top sliced boiled beef before baking.

name: Sos z soków do budyniu (fruit juice sauce for puddings)
summary: A quick sweet fruit and red wine sauce thickened with potato starch, served warm with steamed puddings and choux, sponge, or bread desserts.

ingredients.name: fruit juice
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of any fruit juice

steps: Thoroughly mix 1 tablespoon of potato starch with 250 ml of cold water to make a smooth slurry.
Pour the mixture into a small saucepan, add the fruit juice, red wine, and sugar, and stir well.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce comes to the boil and thickens; serve with steamed pudding or other warm sweet dishes.

name: Mustard sauce for fish and kiełbasa (Polish sausage)
summary: A tangy sauce on a golden roux and fish stock or broth flavoured with English mustard powder, white wine, vinegar, sugar, and thin lemon slices.

ingredients.name: English mustard powder or hot mustard

steps: Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in plain wheat flour, and cook into a golden roux.
Whisk the hot bouillon or fish stock vigorously into the roux until smooth.

Add the English mustard, white wine, vinegar, sugar, and lemon slices, bring to a boil and cook for a few minutes, then pour over cooked fish (pike-perch, sturgeon, or eel) or kiełbasa (Polish sausage).

name: Warm creamed horseradish sauce with egg yolks
summary: A thick horseradish sauce made by bringing grated horseradish to a boil with sour cream, flour, sugar, and lemon juice, then thickening it with raw egg yolks.
steps: Peel the horseradish roots and grate them on a fine grater.
Transfer the grated horseradish to a small saucepan, add the sour cream, sugar, and wheat flour, beat vigorously, drizzle with lemon juice, and bring to a boil.
Take the saucepan off high heat, whisk in the egg yolks, and warm briefly while stirring constantly (without letting it boil), then season with salt to taste and serve.

name: English Mustard
summary: Homemade mustard made from English mustard powder, dressed with olive oil after 12 hours and scalded with hot tarragon vinegar, with sugar and burnt caramel added.

ingredients.name: tarragon vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwaterka of strong tarragon vinegar, boiling

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: or more to taste (in the second method, half a funt = 200 g of fine sugar)

steps: Pour 200 g of English mustard powder into an earthenware bowl, drizzle with 3 tbsp of olive oil, and leave to stand for 12 hours.

Bring 250 ml (1 Polish kwaterka) of strong tarragon vinegar to a boil and pour the boiling liquid into the mustard a little at a time, beating constantly with a wooden pestle or spoon until completely cool.

Add 2 tbsp of sugar (or more to taste) and 1 tsp of burnt caramel for colour, and mix thoroughly (in the second method, mix the mustard directly with boiling tarragon vinegar, 200 g of fine sugar, and 1 tbsp of caramel, bring briefly to a boil over the heat, and stir until cool).

name: Masło serdelowe (anchovy butter)
summary: Classic compound butter made from anchovies pounded in a mortar and rubbed through a sieve, blended with an equal weight of fresh butter, black pepper, and optional chives.

ingredients.name: anchovy fillets
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of anchovies

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of fresh butter

steps: Rinse the anchovy fillets in cold water, pat dry, and pound in a mortar into a smooth paste.
Cream the pounded anchovies with 200 g of fresh butter and a pinch of pepper, then rub the mixture through a fine sieve.
Mix the butter well (optionally adding finely chopped chives) and serve with roast beef tenderloin or capon.

name: Sos szodonowy (chaudeau wine sauce)
summary: A classic fluffy chaudeau sauce (sabayon) of egg yolks whisked over steam or very low heat with caster sugar and white wine.

ingredients.name: caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kubek of fine sugar (approx. 200 g)

ingredients.name: white wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka of French white or Rhine wine

steps: Beat the egg yolks with the caster sugar in a bowl until pale and fluffy.
Pour in the white wine, mix well, and transfer the mixture to a small saucepan.
Set the saucepan over very low heat (or over a water bath) and whisk constantly until the sauce thickens and foams.
Remove the pan from the heat just before it reaches the boil so the egg yolks do not curdle, and serve immediately as a warm dessert sauce or in cups as a drink.

name: Krupnik (Polish barley soup)
summary: Traditional Polish barley soup made with a light beef broth, separately cooked barley groats beaten with butter, and fresh parsley.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: about 1.5 l for the broth and 0.5 l for cooking the groats

ingredients.name: barley groats or pearl barley
ingredients.note: originally 1 Polish kwaterka (250 ml) of barley, spelt, or pearl barley groats

steps: Simmer a light, clear broth from the beef bones and trimmings in salted water, then strain.
In a separate pot, cook the barley groats or pearl barley until thick and well softened.
Add the butter to the hot groats and beat thoroughly with a spoon into a smooth, creamy mass.
Thin the buttered groats with the hot beef broth, add the finely chopped parsley leaves, bring to a boil together, and serve.

name: Lenten almond milk blancmange (Galareta migdałowa postna)
summary: A dairy-free white blancmange made from rich almond milk pressed from blanched almonds and boiling water, whisked with sugar and isinglass or gelatine.

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 12 pieces as in the base recipe

ingredients.name: isinglass or gelatine
ingredients.note: orig. 3 łuty boiled down to 250 ml

steps: Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds in boiling water, slip off the skins, and pound in a mortar or grind to a smooth paste.
Pour 1 l of boiling water over the pounded almonds, let steep covered for 60 minutes, then wring firmly through a dense cloth.
Pound the almond pressings a second time, pour in the remaining 250 ml of hot water, and wring through the cloth again to extract a rich almond milk.
Simmer the isinglass or gelatine in 250 ml of water until dissolved and strain.

Stir the sugar and cooled isinglass or gelatine solution into the almond milk, whisk briskly until slightly thickened, pour into a mould, and set in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until firm.

name: White onion sauce Soubise (sos cebulowy à la Soubise)
summary: A velvety, thick white sauce made from ten white onions, scalded and slowly cooked in butter, thickened with flour and fresh cream, and passed through a sieve.
steps: Immerse the peeled white onions in salted boiling water to steep for 10 minutes, then remove, drain, and slice thinly.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the sliced onions, cover, and sweat over very low heat for about 20–25 minutes until thoroughly tender without browning at all.
Stir in the plain wheat flour, heat briefly, and whisk in the sweet cream.
Simmer over low heat for a few minutes while stirring constantly, season with a pinch of sugar and salt, and rub the thick sauce through a sieve.

name: Krem poziomkowy lub malinowy (Wild strawberry or raspberry Bavarian cream)
summary: A delicate Bavarian cream of fresh raspberry or wild strawberry purée whisked with egg whites and sugar, folded with whipped cream and jelly.

ingredients.name: raspberries or wild strawberries
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec (2 l) of fresh berries for 2 szklanki (500 ml) of purée

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of fine sugar, plus a little for dusting the mould

ingredients.name: whipping cream 30%
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of thick sweet cream

ingredients.name: calf's-foot jelly stock or dissolved gelatine
ingredients.note: originally a scant Polish kwaterka of stock from 2–3 calf's feet (modern equivalent: about 15 g gelatine in 200 ml water)

steps: Press the fresh raspberries or wild strawberries through a fine sieve to obtain 2 szklanki (500 ml) of smooth purée.
Combine the fruit purée with the egg whites and fine sugar and whisk until the mixture thickens noticeably.
Separately whip the thick whipping cream until stiff.
Fold the whipped fruit mixture together with the whipped cream and lukewarm jelly stock (or dissolved gelatine) until gently combined.
Transfer the cream to a mould rinsed with cold water and dusted with sugar, then refrigerate for about 3 hours until set.

name: Sago dessert with whipped cream and preserves (sago z bitą śmietaną)
summary: A dessert of white sago cooked in milk and drained, gently combined with cream whipped with sugar and vanilla, and decorated with fruit preserves.

ingredients.name: white sago pearls
ingredients.note: orig. 1/2 łut (approx. 6 g; possibly a source misprint for 1/2 Polish funt = 200 g)

steps: Drop the white sago into plenty of boiling milk and simmer over low heat for about 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain excess milk through a sieve and let cool.
Whip the well-chilled double cream with sugar and vanilla into stiff, airy peaks.
Gradually fold the cooled sago spoonful by spoonful into the whipped cream until combined.
Transfer the mixture to a serving platter and garnish with fruit preserves.

name: Chilled moulded wine sago dessert (sago na winie z formy)
summary: A chilled moulded dessert of translucent sago cooked with white wine, sugar, lemon juice, and orange zest, unmoulded and garnished with fresh orange wedges.
steps: Cook the sago in plenty of hot water for about 15–20 minutes until translucent, then pour off excess water.
Add the wine to the cooked sago, squeeze in juice from half a lemon, add sugar and grated orange zest, and simmer over low heat for about 10 minutes until very thick.
Spoon the hot mixture into a lightly oiled mould and chill for about 3 hours (180 minutes) until firmly set.
Before serving, unmould onto a platter, arrange orange segments around, and drizzle with pineapple or punch syrup.

name: Zupa pomidorowa klarowna (Clear tomato soup with white wine)
summary: A clear tomato soup made from tomatoes stewed in butter with bread crumb, pressed through a fine sieve, and combined with rich meat broth and dry white wine, served with croutons.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for stewing the tomatoes and frying the croutons

ingredients.name: white wheat roll
ingredients.note: cubed crumb for the tomatoes plus croutons for serving

steps: Cut the tomatoes into several pieces, remove the seeds, and place in a saucepan with melted butter.
Add the cubed bread crumb and cook the tomatoes gently over low heat for 30 minutes.
Press and strain the cooked tomatoes through a very fine sieve.
Combine the tomato purée with the hot broth, pour in half a glass of white wine, heat briefly, and serve with butter-fried croutons.

name: Zupa cytrynowa (Polish lemon soup)
summary: A soup made with beef broth or vegetable-and-mushroom stock, enriched with sour cream, egg yolks, and fresh lemon juice, and thickened with mashed pearl barley or rice.

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: orig. a half-garniec pot of soup (for a meatless version, stock from soup vegetables and dried mushrooms)

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: large; juice extracted, with a few thin slices optionally reserved for the tureen

ingredients.name: pearl barley
ingredients.note: or rice, for thickening the soup

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for cooking the barley or rice

steps: In a separate pot, cook the pearl barley or rice with butter until soft, then mash thoroughly with a spoon to thicken the soup.
Whisk the sour cream thoroughly with the egg yolks and the juice squeezed from the large lemon.
Temper the sour-cream and egg-yolk liaison with the hot beef broth (or, for a meatless version, stock made from soup vegetables, dried mushrooms, onion, and spices).
Combine the soup with the mashed pearl barley or rice and briefly bring to a boil, taking care not to let the egg yolks curdle. Serve in a tureen with thin slices of lemon.

name: Sos tatarski zimny do święconego lub do śniadania zimnego (cold egg-yolk tartar sauce)
summary: A thick cold sauce of smoothly mashed hard-boiled egg yolks emulsified with olive oil, English mustard, sugar, and strong vinegar, finished with chopped chives or capers.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: hard-boiled (only the yolks are used in the sauce)

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: strong, enough to give a fairly thick consistency

steps: Hard-boil the 10 eggs, cool, peel, and remove the yolks.
Mash the yolks in a bowl into a completely smooth paste, add a generous tablespoon of caster sugar (optional), and gradually work in the 4 tablespoons of olive oil.
Stir in the 3 teaspoons of English mustard and gradually add the strong vinegar a little at a time until the sauce reaches a smooth, fairly thick consistency.
Add the finely chopped chives or capers, mix well, and serve cold with cured meats, cold roasts, or eggs.

name: Pianka z konfiturami (baked meringue with fruit preserves)
summary: Quick baked meringue dessert made from 10 egg whites beaten into stiff peaks with fine sugar and a spoonful of drained raspberry or cherry preserves, sprinkled with almonds and baked for 15 minutes in a warm oven.

ingredients.name: fruit preserves
ingredients.note: raspberry or cherry, drained of syrup

steps: Beat 10 egg whites into stiff peaks.
Gradually fold in 400 g of caster sugar and 1 tbsp of raspberry or cherry preserves drained of syrup, mixing gently.
Pile the meringue onto an ovenproof platter, sprinkle the top with almonds, and place for 15 minutes in a warm oven (150 °C).

name: Chilled Semolina Pudding with Nuts and Cream Skins (Kaszka z orzechami na zimno)
summary: An elegant 19th-century dessert of semolina or fine buckwheat groats cooked in whipping cream with pounded nuts, layered with baked cream skins and fruit preserves.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for blanching and sprinkling the nuts while grinding

ingredients.name: semolina
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka (approximately 180 g), or fine buckwheat groats

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1/4 funt (plus a little for sprinkling the cream skins)

steps: Blanch the nuts and bitter almonds in boiling water, peel off their skins, and pound them in a mortar or grind into a fine paste, sprinkling with a little water to keep them from releasing oil.
Heat the whipping cream over very low heat and carefully lift off the skins as they form into a separate dish.
Once you have collected enough cream skins, stir the semolina or fine buckwheat groats into the remaining cream and cook into a loose porridge.
Add the ground nuts and sugar to the cooked porridge and mix thoroughly.
Layer the porridge onto an ovenproof platter (optionally bordered with a pastry rim), alternating it with the reserved cream skins dusted with sugar.
Place the platter into a warm oven preheated to 140–150 °C for a dozen or so minutes, then let cool and garnish with whole-fruit preserves before serving.

name: Krem z brzoskwiń (Peach whip jelly mousse)
summary: A light mousse of fresh peach juice beaten with sugar, gelatine, and stiffly whipped egg whites, chilled in a mould until firm.

ingredients.name: red food colouring or raspberry juice
ingredients.note: a few drops for colour (orig. alkermes juice)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 small glass, for dissolving the gelatine

steps: Beat the squeezed peach juice with the sugar for about 30 minutes (or more briefly with an electric mixer at high speed) until thick and fluffy.
Tint the mixture with a few drops of red food colouring or fruit juice.
Dissolve the gelatine in the hot water, let it cool slightly, and pour it into the peach mixture.
Beat the egg whites to very stiff peaks and fold gently into the cream.
Transfer the mousse to a mould greased with olive oil and leave in a cool place or refrigerator for 6–8 hours until completely set.

name: Mleczko (steamed egg custard)
summary: Delicate egg-and-milk custard made from 10 eggs beaten with sugar and vanilla (or bitter almond milk), thinned with light cream or whole milk, and steamed in a water bath.

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: crushed (or 15 bitter almonds pounded with a little milk and squeezed through a cloth)

ingredients.name: single cream 12%
ingredients.note: orig. misprinted as 5 kwarta (an obvious typesetting error for 5 kwaterka = 1.25 l of light cream or whole milk)

steps: Beat 10 whole eggs thoroughly with 200 g of sugar and crushed vanilla (or almond milk squeezed through a cloth from 15 pounded bitter almonds).
Thin the egg mixture with light cream or whole milk and strain through a fine sieve into a pudding mould.
Set the covered mould in a pot of boiling water and steam (like a steamed pudding) for about 35 minutes, until a knife inserted into the centre comes out completely clean.

Remove the mould from the boiling water, place it in a vessel of cold water until completely chilled, and before serving unmould onto a platter and garnish with fruit preserves or serve with a cream sauce.

name: Krem owocowy (Fruit mousse)
summary: A light fruit mousse made from fresh wild strawberries, raspberries, or apricots beaten with sugar and stiff egg whites and set with a touch of gelatine.

ingredients.name: fresh wild strawberries, raspberries, or apricots
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of ripe fruit

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of fine sugar

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwaterka, for dissolving the gelatine

steps: Press the ripe wild strawberries, raspberries, or apricots through a fine sieve.
Combine the fruit purée with the fine sugar and beat vigorously until light and fluffy.
Dissolve the gelatine in the hot water and let it cool slightly, and beat the egg whites separately to stiff peaks.
Combine the fruit mixture with the dissolved gelatine and stiff egg whites, folding gently.
Spoon the mousse into a serving bowl greased with almond oil and refrigerate for at least 3 hours until set.

name: Liście szczawiowe na rosole (Sorrel leaf broth with poached eggs)
summary: A clear, rich meat broth simmered with whole fresh sorrel leaves and served over poached eggs.

ingredients.name: fresh sorrel leaves
ingredients.note: large handful of rinsed and dried leaves

steps: Rinse and dry the sorrel leaves, place them in a smaller pot, pour in part of the hot broth, salt lightly, and simmer over low heat for about 20–30 minutes.
Pour the remaining hot broth into a soup tureen and add enough of the cooked sorrel leaves and their cooking liquid to give the soup a pleasantly tangy flavour.
Separately poach the eggs in boiling water.
Place the poached eggs directly into deep soup plates and ladle the hot sorrel soup over them.

name: Almond cream blancmange (Blanc-manger)
summary: A refined moulded almond cream jelly made from sweet cream infused with pounded sweet and bitter almonds, whisked with sugar and clarified calf's-foot stock.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 3 kwarty, for simmering the stock

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of whites, for clarifying the stock

steps: Remove the large bones from the thoroughly washed calf's feet, cover with 3 l of water, and simmer over low heat for about 3–4 hours, skimming off foam and fat, until the meat falls apart.

Strain the stock through a sieve, leave overnight (about 8 hours) to set, scrape the fat and sediment off the bottom, then melt the jelly with beaten egg whites, clarify over low heat, strain through a cloth, and reduce to 250 ml; let cool.
Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds in boiling water, remove the skins, and pound in a mortar to a smooth paste, moistening with milk.
Bring 1 l of sweet cream to a boil, pour the boiling cream over the pounded almonds in a bowl, and let steep covered for 60 minutes.
Squeeze the almond mixture very firmly through a tightly woven cloth (you can pound the pulp again and rinse it with some of the same cream until the pulp is dry).
Stir 200 g of sugar and 250 ml of cold clarified calf's-foot stock into the strained almond cream and whisk briskly until the mixture begins to thicken.
Pour into a 1 l mould lightly brushed with olive oil and set in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until completely firm.

name: Shortcrust tartlets with whipped cream
summary: Crisp fluted shortcrust pastry shells filled just before serving with vanilla-scented sweetened whipped cream.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 tbsp (15 g) for the pastry and 1/4 funt (100 g) for the cream

steps: Knead a smooth pastry from the wheat flour, butter, 15 g of sugar, and the egg, then roll it out thinly.
Lightly grease fluted metal tartlet tins with lard and line them neatly with the pastry, pressing it into the ridges.
Bake in an oven preheated to 170–180 °C for about 20 minutes, unmould the tartlet shells immediately after baking, and let cool.
Whip the cream until stiff, fold in the remaining 100 g of sugar and the vanilla, and fill the cooled tartlet shells just before serving.

name: Choux pastry for doughnuts, rings, and cream puffs (Ciasto parzone)
summary: Classic choux paste made by scalding wheat flour in boiling water and melted butter, then beating in eight whole eggs one by one once cooled.
steps: In a saucepan, bring 500 ml of water to a boil with the butter and a pinch of salt.
Gradually pour the wheat flour into the boiling liquid, beating vigorously over the heat for several minutes until the paste pulls away from the sides of the pan into a smooth ball.
Remove the pan from the heat, let cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one at a time along with the sugar, mixing thoroughly after each egg until smooth and glossy.
Pipe rings or round puffs onto a greased baking sheet and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 20–25 minutes (or drop spoonfuls into hot fat and fry until golden).

name: Chestnut Purée with Whipped Cream (Kasztany z bitą śmietaną)
summary: Classic Mont Blanc-style dessert of sweet fresh chestnut purée pressed through a sieve around a mound of vanilla-scented whipped cream.

ingredients.name: 30% heavy cream
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta of thick sweet cream, for whipping

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of sifted sugar, for the cream

ingredients.name: fresh sweet chestnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 2 funty, for the chestnut mixture

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt, for the chestnut mixture

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. 1 teaspoon of potato starch, for the chestnut mixture

steps: In a cool place, whip the thick cream with the sifted icing sugar and vanilla, skimming off the whipped foam with a spoon and draining any liquid that collects at the bottom.
Cover the fresh chestnuts with water, boil until tender, drain, and carefully peel off the skins.
Mash the hot chestnuts and press them through a fine colander or sieve, just like potatoes.
Thoroughly mix the sieved chestnuts with the sugar, potato starch, and 1 tablespoon of cream.
Mound the whipped cream in the centre of a serving platter, then press the chestnut mixture through a wire sieve or potato ricer directly onto the platter in a ring around the whipped cream.

name: Zupa grochowa (Grochówka split pea soup)
summary: Classic thick Polish pea soup made from sieved peas simmered with marbled pork or smoked meat, seasoned with marjoram and served with butter-fried croutons.

ingredients.name: dried shelled peas
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish kwarta of peas

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 3 historical Polish kwarty of soft water

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: orig. 1.5–2 historical Polish funts of streaky pork (or a scalded pig's tail, or 1 funt = 400 g of smoked meat)

steps: Cover the peas with the water and bring to a boil, then add the streaky pork (or scalded pig's tail or smoked meat), season with salt, and simmer over low heat for about 1.5–2 hours until the peas are completely soft.
Remove the cooked meat and press the peas along with their cooking liquid through a fine sieve or colander.
Cut the meat into pieces, return it to the sieved soup, and bring back to a boil.
Cut the wheat roll into small cubes and fry in butter until golden croutons form.
Put the crushed marjoram in the tureen, pour in the hot pea soup, and serve with the croutons.

name: Zupa grzybowa (Polish dried mushroom soup)
summary: A meatless soup of dried mushrooms simmered with soup vegetables, onions, and allspice, thickened with a butter-and-flour roux and served either tangy with vinegar or mild with noodles.

ingredients.name: dried mushrooms
ingredients.note: orig. 10 large dried mushrooms for 4–5 people

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of whole onions (plus optionally 1 chopped onion for the roux)

ingredients.name: hand-cut noodles
ingredients.note: oblong noodles or fine groats rubbed with beaten egg

steps: Scald the dried mushrooms with boiling water, wash thoroughly, cover with cold water, and set over the heat.

Once the mushrooms have parboiled slightly, add the soup vegetables, peeled whole onions, allspice, and pepper, and simmer over low heat for about 45 minutes until the mushrooms are completely tender.
Strain the stock through a sieve, remove the cooked mushrooms, slice them into thin strips, and return them to the clear stock.
Season the soup with salt, add good vinegar to taste for the sour version, and thicken with a butter-and-flour roux, optionally including sautéed onion.
Bring the soup to a boil and cook the oblong hand-cut noodles in it (or, for the mild version, add fine groats rubbed with beaten egg). Season in the tureen with freshly ground pepper and serve.

name: Zupa biała z kaszą perłową na podrobach (White pearl barley giblet soup)
summary: A soup made with poultry giblet broth, thickened with pearl barley creamed with butter and generously enriched with sour cream.

ingredients.name: poultry giblets
ingredients.note: goose or chicken, for the broth

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the broth and the barley

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta

steps: Simmer a clear broth from the goose or chicken giblets and soup vegetables in salted water, then strain.
In a separate pot, cook the pearl barley until tender, add a generous tablespoon of butter, and beat with a spoon until the mixture turns white.
Stir the sour cream into the barley, thin with the hot broth, bring everything to a boil together, and serve.

name: Zupa biała karlsbadzka (Carlsbad white veal and barley soup)
summary: A nourishing, creamy spa-style soup of rich veal or chicken broth blended with a sieved purée of pearl barley, oat groats, or rice.

ingredients.name: veal
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of historical Polish funts of veal (or 1 hen and poultry giblets)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the broth and the groats

ingredients.name: pearl barley
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta of spelt groats, pearl barley, oat groats, or rice

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a little for cooking the groats and for frying the croutons

ingredients.name: wheat roll croutons
ingredients.note: cubed and fried in butter, optional

steps: Cover the veal (or hen with poultry giblets) with water, bring to a boil, skim thoroughly, add the soup vegetables and salt, and simmer over low heat for about 2–2.5 hours until a rich broth forms.
In a separate pot, cook the pearl barley, oat groats, or rice in unsalted water with a bit of fresh butter, taking care that it does not scorch and cooks down completely into a thick mass.
Transfer the soft-cooked groats to a sieve and rub them through, moistening with the strained broth until the soup reaches the thickness of split pea soup.
Beat the soup thoroughly with a spoon, bring to a brisk boil, and serve (for healthy diners, garnished with chopped parsley leaves and butter-fried croutons).

name: Zupa migdałowa (Polish Christmas Eve almond soup)
summary: A traditional meatless Christmas Eve soup made from sweet and bitter almonds pounded into almond milk, sweetened with sugar, and served over rice cooked with cinnamon and raisins.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 2 historical Polish kwarty of boiled water

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: for sprinkling the almonds and cooking the rice (replaced with water for a strictly vegan fast)

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 0.5–0.75 historical Polish funt (200–300 g) of fine sugar

steps: Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds in boiling water, remove their skins, and pound in a mortar or blend into a smooth paste, sprinkling with a little water or milk as you go to prevent the oil from separating.
Pour two kwarty (2 l) of boiled water over the almond paste, stir thoroughly, and wring out firmly through a fine sieve or clean cloth.
Pound the almond pressings a second time, moisten with part of the strained liquid or a little water, and wring out through the cloth again.
Stir the fine sugar into the resulting almond milk until completely dissolved.
Separately cook the rice until fluffy in milk (or water for a strictly meatless fast) with sugar, cinnamon, and raisins, spoon it into a tureen, pour the almond soup over it, and serve warm or cold.

name: Zupa poziomkowa (Wild strawberry soup)
summary: A summer fruit soup of fresh wild strawberries pressed through a sieve with water, sugar, sour cream, and light white wine, warmed without boiling and served with croutons.

ingredients.name: wild strawberries
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec of rinsed wild strawberries

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish funt of fine sugar

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta of thin sour cream

ingredients.name: white wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 glass of light white wine

ingredients.name: wheat roll croutons
ingredients.note: soaked in sweet cream and fried in butter (or scalded obwarzanki rings), for serving

steps: Press the rinsed wild strawberries through a fine sieve, moistening them as you go with half a kwarta (500 ml) of water.
Stir the fine sugar into the wild strawberry purée, pour in the sour cream and a glass of light white wine, and mix thoroughly.
Set the soup over the heat and warm thoroughly for about 5 minutes, taking care not to let it boil.
Serve with croutons soaked in sweet cream and fried in butter, or with scalded bread rings (obwarzanki).

name: Zupa z czarnych jagód (Polish bilberry soup)
summary: A summer fruit soup of sieved bilberries boiled with sugar, cinnamon, and a splash of red wine, finished with whole berries and served cold with croutons or small noodles.

ingredients.name: bilberries
ingredients.note: orig. 1 garniec (4 l) for cooking down plus 1 mug (250 ml) of the finest whole berries

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a glass for mixing with the flour (or use red wine), plus enough water to moisten the berries

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a historical Polish funt

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: orig. half a glass, used instead of water for mixing with the flour

ingredients.name: wheat roll croutons
ingredients.note: fried, or separately cooked hand-cut noodles, for serving

steps: Set aside one mug (250 ml) of the finest berries from the batch, tip the remaining garniec (4 l) into a pot, add just enough water to moisten them, and simmer for about 10 minutes until the berries burst.
Press the cooked berries through a sieve and let stand briefly for the sediment to settle, then carefully decant the clear juice into a clean pot.
Add the sugar and several pieces of cinnamon bark to the juice, and pour in half a glass of water or red wine mixed smoothly with half a tablespoon of wheat flour.
Set the soup over the heat, and once it comes to a boil, tip in the reserved mug of whole berries and bring briefly back to a boil.
Chill the soup thoroughly, add a piece of lemon peel for aroma before serving, and serve with fried croutons or separately boiled and cold-rinsed hand-cut noodles.

name: Zupa wiśniowa (Polish sour cherry soup)
summary: A chilled fruit soup made from ripe sour cherries pounded with their stones and macerated with cinnamon and cloves, pressed through a sieve, and boiled with sugar and red wine or sour cream.

ingredients.name: sour cherries
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec of ripe stemmed sour cherries

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish funt

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 glass (or alternatively half a historical Polish kwarta = 500 ml of thin sour cream)

steps: In a bowl or stoneware pot, pound the ripe, stemmed sour cherries together with their stones, add a little cinnamon and the cloves, and let stand for 2 hours to release their juice and aroma.
Press the cherry mixture thoroughly through a fine sieve.
Stir the sugar into the strained juice, and pour in a glass of red wine (or alternatively 500 ml of thin sour cream) and a kwarta (1 l) of water.
Bring the soup to a boil together, then chill thoroughly and serve cold with croutons.

name: Old Polish spiced beer and bread soup (Gramatka z piwa)
summary: A warming Old Polish beer soup thickened with grated stale bread and simmered with cinnamon, cloves, raisins, and fresh butter.
steps: Grate the stale bread on a fine grater.
Pour the beer into a pot, add the grated bread, raisins, cinnamon, cloves, and butter.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring for a few minutes until the bread softens and lightly thickens the soup, then pour into a tureen and serve hot.

name: Zacierki lub kluski gryczane na mleku (Buckwheat dumplings in milk)
summary: Spoon-dropped dumplings made from buckwheat flour scalded with boiling water and mixed with a touch of wheat flour, poached in boiling milk.

ingredients.name: buckwheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwarta

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: hot, several tablespoons for scalding the flour

steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with a tablespoon of wheat flour and salt in a bowl.
Gradually pour in several tablespoons of hot water at a time, stirring vigorously the whole time, until all the flour is evenly scalded and moistened.
Bring the milk to a boil in a wide saucepan or pot.
Using a metal spoon, quickly drop oblong dumplings of the scalded dough into the boiling milk.
Simmer for a few minutes until the dumplings float to the surface of the milk, then serve immediately.

name: Wine sago soup (zupa z sago na winie)
summary: An exquisite sweet dessert soup of translucent sago pearls simmered in white or red wine with sugar, cinnamon, cloves, and lemon.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 500 ml for wine + 500 ml to boil sago

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: zest for simmering and slices for tureen

steps: Scald the sago pearls with hot water, drain in a sieve, and rinse with cold water.
