Cover the sago with 500 ml of fresh water and cook over low heat for about 15–20 minutes, stirring constantly until the pearls turn translucent.
In a separate pot, bring the wine to a boil with the remaining 500 ml of water, sugar, lemon zest, cinnamon stick, and cloves.
Add the cooked sago pearls to the hot wine, heat gently together briefly, and ladle into a tureen lined with lemon slices.

name: Zupa nic na mleku (Floating island milk soup Zupa nic)
summary: Classic Polish sweet milk soup thickened with egg yolks beaten with sugar and scented with cinnamon or vanilla, served cold with baked meringue puffs and sweet spiced rice.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec of unskimmed milk

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 glass of sugar for the yolks plus a couple of tablespoons for the whites

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: beaten to stiff peaks for the meringues

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: cooked separately with sugar and cinnamon, for serving in the tureen

steps: Beat 6 egg yolks vigorously with a glass of sugar until pale and fluffy.
Set the milk over the heat and, stirring constantly, pour in the beaten yolks in a thin stream.
Heat over low heat for a few minutes until the soup thickens, taking care not to let it boil lest the yolks curdle.
Strain the hot soup into a tureen, dust with ground cinnamon or vanilla, and leave in a cool place until completely cold.

Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in two tablespoons of sugar and a touch of cinnamon, drop small spoonfuls onto a paper-lined baking sheet, and dry in an oven preheated to 120 °C for 10 minutes.
Place the separately cooked and cooled sweet rice in the tureen, pour the chilled soup over it, and float the baked meringue puffs on top.

name: White rice cooked for soups (ryż gotowany na biało do zup)
summary: Fluffy, snow-white rice scalded twice with hot water, soaked in cold water for an hour, and cooked with butter to serve with broth or tomato soup.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. a pot holding half a Polish kwarta (500 ml), plus water for scalding and soaking

steps: Place the rice in a bowl, pour over hot water, stir, and drain off the cloudy water; repeat the hot water scalding a second time.
Cover the scalded rice with cold water and leave for 60 minutes to make it snow-white, then drain.
Transfer the rice to a half-litre saucepan, cover with warm water, and simmer over low heat for about 15–20 minutes, stirring frequently so it does not scorch.
When the rice begins to soften, add the salt and butter, cook until fully tender, remove from the heat, and serve in the soup tureen or separately on a plate.

name: Makaron (Homemade egg noodles for broth)
summary: Classic homemade egg noodles for broth, made from a stiff dough of wheat flour and eggs alone, rolled very thin and cut into fine threads.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally half a Polish kwarta (500 ml) of finest wheat flour

ingredients.name: meat broth
ingredients.note: or salted water, for boiling and serving the noodles

steps: Knead a very stiff, smooth dough from the wheat flour and whole eggs alone.
Roll the dough out on a pastry board as thinly as possible, avoiding excess flour for dusting, and leave the sheets for about 30 minutes to dry slightly.
Cut the slightly dried dough into strips about 5–6 cm wide, stack the strips three high, roll them up together into a cylinder, and slice with a sharp knife into very fine threads.
Toss the cut noodles loosely with your fingers across the board to dry a little longer.

About 15 minutes before serving, ladle part of the broth into a smaller pot, bring to a boil, and drop in the noodles; as soon as they float to the surface, pour them along with their cooking broth into the tureen containing the rest of the hot broth.

name: French Soup Dumplings without Beaten Egg Whites (Kluski francuskie bez piany)
summary: Small, neatly shaped dumplings made by beating egg yolks, butter, and wheat flour for an extended time, cooked in boiling broth or served in chicken fricassee sauce.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: for the batter (plus a little for coating the balls)

steps: Cream the 4 egg yolks with 4 tablespoons of fresh butter until pale and whitish.
Gradually beat in the wheat flour 1 tablespoon at a time, add a pinch of salt, and beat continuously for 30 minutes until the mixture reaches the consistency of thick cream.
Shape the mixture on a pastry board into small round balls, roll them lightly in flour, and let rest briefly.
Drop the dumplings into boiling broth and cook until they float to the surface; serve in clear broth or in the sauce of a lemon-free chicken fricassee.

name: Choux Pastry Soup Dumplings (Kluski parzone)
summary: Delicate choux pastry dumplings made from butter, water, and wheat flour, beaten with eggs and dropped by the spoonful into boiling broth.
steps: Bring the water and butter to a boil in a small saucepan.
Dump all the wheat flour into the boiling liquid at once and stir vigorously over low heat until the dough forms a smooth ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing until completely smooth after each addition.
Drop small spoonfuls of the choux batter into boiling broth and cook over low heat until the dumplings float and puff up.

name: Homemade Cut Egg Noodles (Kluski krajane)
summary: Homemade egg noodles cut into strips or small squares from wheat flour, egg, and water, boiled in salted water for clear broth or cooked directly in mushroom or fish soup.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for kneading the dough and water for boiling and rinsing the noodles

steps: Knead a medium-firm dough from the wheat flour, egg, and a small amount of water, then roll it out thinly.

Cut the sheet of dough into strips about 2–3 cm (two fingers) wide, stack 3–4 strips on top of one another, and slice crosswise into finer or thicker noodles (or cut narrower strips into tiny squares).
Bring salted water to a boil in a pot, drop in the noodles, and cook until they float to the surface.

Drain the noodles in a colander, rinse with cold water to keep them from sticking together, and transfer to a tureen of clear broth (for mushroom or fish soup you may drop them directly into the simmering soup, but for clear broth always boil them separately so the broth does not turn cloudy).

name: Pulpety wołowe do barszczu (beef meatballs for borscht)
summary: Traditional small meatballs of minced beef and suet with roasted onion, cooked directly in borscht like uszka, small filled dumplings.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: tender beef, orig. half a historical Polish funt

ingredients.name: beef suet
ingredients.note: or beef marrow, orig. a quarter of a historical Polish funt

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: roasted in the oven and mashed to a paste

steps: Very finely mince the beef and suet (or marrow) with a knife or pass through a grinder twice.
Roast the whole onion in the oven and mash to a smooth puree.
In a bowl combine the minced meat, suet, mashed onion, egg, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper, kneading to a cohesive mixture.
Roll the mixture into tiny balls the size of a hazelnut.
Drop the meatballs directly into simmering borscht and cook gently for about 5–7 minutes until they float to the surface.
Serve the hot borscht with meatballs in a tureen or in individual soup plates.

name: Uszka do barszczu (small meat and mushroom dumplings for borscht)
summary: Classic ear-shaped borscht dumplings made from egg noodle dough and filled with finely minced boiled or roast beef, pork fatback, onion, and dried mushrooms.

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: finely minced together with the meat, for the filling

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: grated or baked, for the filling

ingredients.name: dried mushrooms
ingredients.note: orig. 1–2 cooked and chopped mushrooms along with a splash of their cooking stock

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of whole eggs, for the filling

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the filling and for the boiling water

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a Polish quart (approx. 325 g), for the dough

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for kneading the dough and sealing the edges (plus boiling water for cooking the dumplings)

steps: Chop the boiled or roast beef very finely together with the piece of pork fatback.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan, add the grated or baked onion, heat briefly without browning, and remove from the heat.
Add the minced beef and fatback, finely chopped cooked dried mushrooms, a splash of mushroom stock, breadcrumbs, 2 eggs, salt, and black pepper to the saucepan, and mix the filling thoroughly.
Knead a moderately soft dough from 500 ml of plain wheat flour, 1 egg, and water, roll it out thinly, and cut into small squares.

Place a portion of filling on each square, moisten the edges with water or egg white, fold in half diagonally into a triangle, and pinch the two opposite corners together to form an ear-shaped dumpling.

Drop the uszka into salted boiling water, cook until they float to the surface, drain, and transfer to a tureen of borscht (for a meatless version, make the filling with dried mushrooms alone and fry the boiled dumplings in clarified butter).

name: Pulpety ze szczupaka (pike quenelles)
summary: Delicate pike fish quenelles made with fresh pike fillet, bread soaked in milk, and grated onion, sliced into fish soups or served in cream sauce.

ingredients.name: pike
ingredients.note: pike fillet without skin or bones

ingredients.name: white roll
ingredients.note: soaked in milk and well squeezed

steps: Skin and debone the pike, then very finely mince with a knife or pass through a grinder.
Soak the roll in milk and squeeze out thoroughly.
Add softened butter, grated onion, squeezed roll, eggs, and salt to the fish, and knead into a uniform, fluffy paste.
Dust the work surface with flour and roll the paste into thick finger-length cylinders.
Drop the dumplings into a pot of salted boiling water (or fish stock) and cook gently for about 5 minutes until they float to the surface.
Lift onto a colander, cool slightly, and slice diagonally into a soup tureen (or serve whole in white cream sauce).

name: Grzanki do zup z parmezanem (Parmesan soup croutons)
summary: Classic croutons made from crustless white wheat roll slices dipped in melted unsalted butter, generously coated with grated Parmesan, and baked until golden before serving with soup.
steps: Trim the crust off the wheat roll on all sides and cut the crumb into even slices.
Melt the fresh unsalted butter or clarified butter in a small saucepan.
Dip each slice of roll into the melted butter so it soaks through, and immediately coat generously with grated Parmesan.
Arrange the croutons on a baking sheet and place in an oven preheated to 160 °C for 30 minutes before serving the soup.

name: Grzanki rozmaite do zup (Breaded soup croutons)
summary: Half-slices of wheat roll dipped in sweet cream, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs and fried until golden in clarified butter, served alongside fruit, tomato, or sorrel soups.

ingredients.name: sweet cream
ingredients.note: or milk, for soaking the roll

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: optional, when serving with fruit soup

steps: Cut the wheat roll into slices, then halve each slice.
Dip the half-slices in sweet cream or milk, then in beaten egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat clarified butter in a skillet and fry the croutons on both sides for about 5–8 minutes until golden brown.
Serve with tomato or sorrel soup, or dust with sugar before serving with fruit soups.

name: Pieczeń cielęca (roast veal)
summary: A quarter of a young calf, soaked in cold water, generously larded with fatback and roasted with butter and breadcrumbs, optionally basted towards the end with a velvety sauce of cream, butter, flour and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: roast veal
ingredients.note: veal roasting joint; a quarter of a young calf

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: fresh, cut into strips for larding

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for basting the roast while cooking

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for sprinkling towards the end of roasting

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of butter

steps: Wash the quarter of veal, rinse, and leave for 60 minutes in clean cold water.
Remove the meat from the water, pat dry, lard thickly with strips of fresh fatback, rub with salt, and let stand for at most 60 minutes.
Roast the veal on a spit or in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 2 hours, basting regularly with melted butter and collecting the drippings in the roasting pan.

Towards the end of roasting, sprinkle the top of the meat with breadcrumbs, drizzle with butter, and brown, then serve on a platter drizzled with its own pan juices (alternatively, bring 100 g of butter to a boil with 1 tbsp of flour and 250 ml of cream, cool, mix with 2 egg yolks and the pan juices, and baste the roast with this sauce while finishing).

name: Bone-in roast beef (rostbef z kością)
summary: A large fatty piece of bone-in beef rump or sirloin roasted in a very hot oven for two hours, served with potatoes roasted alongside and shaved horseradish.

ingredients.name: bone-in roast sirloin or rump of beef
ingredients.note: orig. 10–15 Polish funty (10 funty taken as 4 kg)

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled, to roast alongside the meat

steps: Rub a large cut of fatty bone-in sirloin or rump beef with salt and place it in a roasting pan.
Place the pan in a very hot oven (220 °C) and roast the beef for 120 minutes, turning frequently so it browns evenly without scorching.
During roasting, arrange peeled potatoes around the beef, and when the pan drippings reduce, prick the roast in several spots to release fresh juices.
Carve the roasted meat into thick slices, arrange on a platter surrounded by the roasted potatoes and shaved horseradish, and ladle over the pan juices.

name: Sztufada (larded braised beef)
summary: A large beef rump roast densely larded with pork fatback, sprinkled with vinegar, and slowly braised with root vegetables, beetroot, and allspice in its own sieved gravy.

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: cut into thick strips for larding the meat

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a piece of butter for the bottom of the pot

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of onions, chopped

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for dusting the meat before browning

steps: Pound a large piece of beef rump well, pierce it deeply with a knife, and lard it with thick strips of pork fatback dusted with black pepper, then rub the entire roast with salt and pepper.
Heat a deep casserole dish thoroughly, put the butter on the bottom, place the meat inside, sprinkle it with vinegar, and braise covered over low heat until it releases its juices.
Add the finely chopped onions, carrots, beetroot, celeriac, parsley root, and allspice berries, cover, and braise slowly until the meat is completely tender.
Remove the tender roast, dust it on all sides with plain wheat flour, press the braising juices through a sieve, and skim the rendered fat from the surface.
Pour the skimmed fat back into the pot, brown the flour-dusted roast in it, then pour in the sieved sauce and boil briefly together.
Transfer the braised beef to a platter, skim any excess fat from the surface of the sauce once more, and pour the sauce over the meat.

name: Legumina z kwaśnej śmietany (Sour cream soufflé pudding)
summary: A delicate, lightly tangy soufflé pudding made from sour cream, six eggs, a spoonful of wheat flour, and lemon zest, baked immediately before serving.

ingredients.name: sour cream 18%
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of good sour cream

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole eggs, yolks and whites separated

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: rubbed beforehand against a lemon peel

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: whole fruit (peel for rubbing the sugar plus 1 teaspoon of juice)

steps: Slowly beat the sour cream with a heaped tablespoon of wheat flour and the six egg yolks until smooth and lump-free.
Add two tablespoons of lemon-rubbed sugar, a teaspoon of lemon juice, and a pinch of salt, and mix thoroughly.
Just before placing in the oven, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gradually and gently into the sour cream mixture.
Pour the batter into a baking dish greased with clarified butter and place immediately in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 20 minutes.

name: Pieczeń huzarska (Hussar-style stuffed roast beef)
summary: Beef roast browned in butter, closely scored into diagonal slices without cutting through, stuffed between the slices with a paste of mashed baked onions, butter, breadcrumbs, and egg yolks, and braised for 30 minutes in its own juices.

ingredients.name: roasting beef
ingredients.note: orig. several funt of good meat (approx. 4 funt)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: approx. 3 tbsp for basting while roasting and 1 large tbsp for the stuffing

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of baked onions

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: or grated bread, enough to thicken the stuffing

ingredients.name: egg yolk
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of egg yolks

steps: Pound a cut of good beef well, salt it, and roast in an oven preheated to 190 °C (or on a spit) for about 90 minutes, basting frequently with melted butter, until the meat is browned and nearly tender.
Mash 2 baked onions into a smooth paste with 1 large tbsp of butter, pepper, breadcrumbs, and 2 egg yolks to form a thick stuffing (optionally adding finely chopped herring).
Remove the par-roasted beef, slice it diagonally at close intervals without cutting all the way through the bottom, and pack each cut with the onion stuffing.

Transfer the stuffed roast to a casserole, moisten with the pan juices collected during roasting, cover with a lid, and braise over low heat or in the oven for 30 minutes; serve with braised cabbage or potatoes.

name: Pierożki z gotowanym mięsem (boiled beef pierogi)
summary: Pierogi filled with cooked beef from broth, roasted onion, mushrooms, and breadcrumbs, served boiled or pan-fried until golden.
steps: Finely chop or grind the cooked beef from the stockpot along with the cooked mushrooms.
Melt butter in a saucepan, add the roasted grated onion, then stir in the minced meat and mushrooms, breadcrumbs, salt, pepper, and eggs to make a cohesive filling.
Knead plain flour, egg, warm water, and a pinch of salt into an elastic dumpling dough and roll out thinly.
Place small spoonfuls of filling on the dough, fold over, and cut out small dumplings with a cutter or small glass.
Drop into salted boiling water and cook for 3–4 minutes from the moment they float to the surface, then drain.
Transfer to a platter and pour hot butter browned with breadcrumbs over the top (or optionally pan-fry the dumplings until crisp and golden).

name: Nóżki cielęce osmażone w cieście (batter-fried calf's feet)
summary: Calf's feet boiled until tender, split lengthwise, dusted with flour, dipped in a fluffy batter of egg yolks, flour, and stiffly beaten egg whites, and fried in clarified butter.

ingredients.name: calf's feet
ingredients.note: cleaned and soaked, with the large bone removed

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for dusting the feet and 1 tbsp for the batter

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: 2 egg yolks beaten with flour and stiffly beaten whites from 2 eggs

steps: Clean and soak the calf's feet, remove the large bones, and boil in salted water until completely tender.
Remove the tender feet, let cool slightly, split each lengthwise in half between the hooves, and dust the pieces with wheat flour.
Beat 2 egg yolks with 1 tbsp of wheat flour, beat 2 egg whites into stiff peaks, and gently fold together into a fluffy batter.
Dip the halved feet into the batter and fry in hot clarified butter until golden; serve with lettuce salad or a fruit sauce.

name: Mostek cielęcy nadziewany (stuffed breast of veal)
summary: Thick breast of veal stuffed with a forcemeat of milk-soaked rolls, fatback sweated with scalded onion, chopped calf's liver, mushrooms, and eggs, roasted in a hot oven or braised on fatback.

ingredients.name: wheat roll
ingredients.note: orig. 2 white rolls, with the crust grated off

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter to half a funt (100–200 g) of fresh fatback

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: grated and scalded with hot water

ingredients.name: calf's liver
ingredients.note: orig. half a calf's liver, finely chopped

ingredients.name: button mushrooms
ingredients.note: fresh braised in butter or pickled

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the stuffing and approx. 2 tbsp for basting the roast

steps: Soak the breast of veal for 60 minutes in cold water, rinse, pat dry, cut a pocket in it for stuffing, and rub with salt.
Grate the crust off 2 rolls and soak them in warm milk.
Chop the fresh fatback very finely and sweat it covered together with the grated and boiling-water-scalded onion so that they soften without browning.
Mix the sweated fatback and onion with the finely chopped calf's liver, mushrooms, soaked rolls, 1 tbsp of butter, 3 whole eggs, salt, pepper, allspice, and mace.
Fill the veal breast with the prepared stuffing and sew the opening shut.

Place the breast immediately into a hot oven preheated to 200 °C and roast for about 75 minutes, basting regularly with melted butter without adding water (alternatively, braise the breast in a casserole lined with slices of fatback).

name: Pineapple jelly
summary: A crystal-clear dessert jelly made from pure pineapple syrup simmered with sliced fresh lemon and set with gelatine or isinglass.
steps: Dissolve or simmer the gelatine or finely chopped isinglass over low heat in 500 ml of water.
Add the sliced, carefully seeded lemon to the dissolved liquid and simmer over very low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat, lift out the lemon slices, and strain the liquid through a dense cloth or napkin, letting it drip through without squeezing.
Mix the strained liquid with the clear pineapple syrup, pour into a mould, and set in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until firm.

name: Krem pomarańczowy (Orange mousse)
summary: A fluffy citrus mousse of orange and lemon juice, egg yolks beaten with orange-rubbed sugar, gelatine, and stiff egg whites, served with fresh orange segments and candied peel.

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.note: whole fruit (juice and zest; plus extra quarters for garnish)

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole eggs, yolks and whites separated

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt, rubbed against the orange peel

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka, for dissolving the gelatine

steps: Rub the sugar against the scalded peel of the oranges, then squeeze the juice from all four oranges and the large lemon.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy, pour in the squeezed citrus juice, and warm over low heat, stirring constantly without letting it boil, then set aside to cool.
Dissolve the gelatine in the hot water, let it cool, pour it into the cooled egg and orange mixture, and whisk everything together until it begins to thicken.
Beat the remaining egg whites to stiff peaks, fold gently into the thickening cream, transfer to a mould greased with olive oil, and leave in a cool place until completely set (about 3 hours).
Unmould the cream onto a platter and surround with quarters of fresh orange and thin strips of candied orange peel.

name: Zrazy francuskie z polędwicy z pieczarkami (French-style beef tenderloin zrazy with mushrooms)
summary: Thin slices of beef tenderloin marinated in melted butter and slowly braised over low heat in a rich broth sauce with onions and mushrooms, served over parboiled potatoes.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for the roux plus extra melted butter for coating the meat

ingredients.name: bouillon cake
ingredients.note: orig. 2 łuts of bouillon (solid bouillon concentrate)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish kwaterka of water or meat broth

ingredients.name: button mushrooms
ingredients.note: fresh, peeled, scalded, and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: parboiled and sliced, for lining the bottom of the platter

steps: Trim the beef tenderloin of membranes, cut into thin cutlets, and pound lightly.
Arrange the cutlets on a platter, pour fresh melted butter over both sides, and let stand for 1 hour.
Dissolve the bouillon concentrate in 125 ml of water (half a historical Polish kwaterka), or use rich meat broth.
Heat a generous tablespoon of butter with a tablespoon of flour in a casserole, thin with the prepared broth, and add the sliced onions.
Lay the beef cutlets in the casserole, season lightly with salt and pepper, and scatter the thinly sliced, scalded button mushrooms on top.
Cover the casserole tightly with a lid and braise over very low heat for a full 2 hours.
Line the bottom of a serving platter with the sliced, parboiled potatoes, arrange the beef cutlets on top, and pour the braising sauce over the dish.

name: Omleciki czyli blinki bez drożdży (small omelette pancakes without yeast)
summary: Fluffy small egg pancakes made from egg yolks, wheat flour, sour cream and beaten egg whites, fried in lard or clarified butter and served with cinnamon sugar and sour cream or chaudeau sauce.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: 4 egg yolks and stiffly beaten whites from 4 eggs

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwaterka of fine wheat flour (approx. 160 g)

steps: Beat 4 egg yolks vigorously with a pinch of salt, add 250 ml of wheat flour, and stir in 1 tbsp of sour cream.
Beat 4 egg whites into stiff peaks and fold into the yolk mixture to form a fairly loose, fluffy batter.
Heat clarified butter or lard in a frying pan and drop the batter by the spoonful, 3–4 small pancakes at a time.
Fry the pancakes on both sides until golden brown, adding more fat to the pan as needed.
Arrange the hot pancakes on a platter, sprinkle with sugar mixed with cinnamon, and serve with fruit syrup, sour cream, or chaudeau sauce.

name: Pieczeń wołowa siekana (Polish minced beef roast)
summary: A succulent baked roast of finely minced beef seasoned with roasted onion, cubed fatback, and eggs, baked in butter and finished with sour cream.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: preferably beef round, orig. 5 historical Polish funty

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: roasted in the oven and rubbed through a sieve

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a tablespoon for the mixture and an extra portion for greasing the roasting tin

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for spooning over near the end of baking

steps: Finely mince the beef or pass it through a meat grinder.
Roast the whole onion in the oven until tender, then rub it through a fine-mesh sieve.
To the minced meat add the sieved onion, whole eggs, breadcrumbs, a tablespoon of softened butter, the diced fatback, and salt and pepper to taste.
Knead the mixture thoroughly by hand until cohesive and firm, then shape it into an oblong loaf.
Generously butter a roasting tin, place the loaf inside, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 45 minutes.
Towards the end of baking, spoon the sour cream over the top of the roast, bake until nicely browned, and serve hot or sliced cold.

name: Legumina z cytryny lub pomarańczy (Whole lemon or orange soufflé pudding)
summary: An airy citrus soufflé pudding made from a whole grated lemon or orange, plenty of eggs beaten with sugar, and a touch of flour, baked briefly in a serving dish.

ingredients.name: lemon or orange
ingredients.note: large fruit, scrubbed and grated whole without seeds

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: orig. 9–12 eggs, yolks and whites separated

ingredients.name: potato starch or plain wheat flour

steps: Wash and scald a large lemon or orange, then grate the whole fruit on a fine grater, carefully discarding all seeds.

Transfer the grated fruit to a bowl, add the sugar, and beat for about 30 minutes (or whisk with an electric mixer), adding the egg yolks one by one along with a level teaspoon of flour until the mixture is as thick as cream.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them carefully into the citrus mixture with a spoon.
Spoon the mixture into a buttered ovenproof serving dish and bake in an oven preheated to 170 °C for 15 minutes, taking care not to overbake the soufflé.

name: Mostek cielęcy z ryżem (breast of veal with rice)
summary: Breast of veal boiled until tender with soup vegetables, served with rice cooked gently in butter and veal broth, and topped with strong bouillon or butter with breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of rice (for 4 people)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for braising the rice and 1 tbsp for browning the breadcrumbs

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for browning in butter (or strong bouillon for pouring over)

steps: Wash the breast of veal, parboil briefly and skim off the scum, then boil until tender with the soup vegetables and salt.

Scald the rice twice with boiling water, rinse with cold water, transfer to a saucepan, cover with strained veal broth, add 1 tbsp of butter, and braise covered until the grains are completely tender.
Place the sliced cooked veal breast into the hot rice so that it heats through thoroughly.
Arrange the meat on a platter alternating with the rice and pour strong reduced bouillon or butter with browned breadcrumbs over the top.

name: Pieczeń wołowa z rożna (spit-roasted marinated beef)
summary: Traditional Polish beef roast marinated in vinegar, densely larded with fatback, and roasted at high heat with frequent butter basting.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: centre-cut beef round or rump, orig. 4–5 historical Polish funty

ingredients.name: wine vinegar
ingredients.note: mild, for marinating the meat overnight

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: fresh, cut into thin strips for larding

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: melted, for continuously basting the roast

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the roasting tin under the meat

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: optional, to arrange around the roast in the tin

steps: Trim the beef of any sinew and excess fat, pour mild vinegar over it, and set aside in a cool place overnight (or longer) to tenderise.
Remove the meat from the vinegar, pat dry with a cloth, and lard densely with strips of fatback.
About 15 minutes before roasting, salt the meat thoroughly on all sides (tying with kitchen twine if needed to hold its shape).
Place the meat on a rack over a roasting tin containing a few tablespoons of water (and optionally peeled potatoes) or thread onto a spit.
Transfer to an oven preheated to 220 °C and roast over high heat for 45–60 minutes, basting frequently with melted butter and turning once the first side has browned.
Remove the juicy roast, let it rest for 10 minutes before carving, and serve sliced with the buttery pan juices.

name: Legumina parzona (Steamed choux pastry pudding)
summary: A fluffy steamed pudding made from choux paste cooked with milk and clarified butter, enriched with eight eggs, steamed for an hour in a water bath, and served with raspberry syrup or wine sabayon.

ingredients.name: potato starch or plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally 1 Polish kwaterka (250 ml) of potato starch or wheat flour

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole eggs, yolks and whites separated

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for the water bath

steps: Bring the milk and clarified butter to a boil in a saucepan.
Gradually add the potato starch or wheat flour, stirring vigorously with a spoon over low heat until the paste thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan, then set aside to cool.
Beat the cooled paste, adding the egg yolks one at a time, along with a large tablespoon of sugar and a pinch of salt.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the egg batter.

Transfer the batter to a mould greased with butter and coated with breadcrumbs, set the mould in a wide pot of boiling water, and cook in the water bath over medium heat for 60 minutes, replenishing the boiling water as needed.

name: Legumina z jabłek w papilotach (Baked apples wrapped in crêpes)
summary: A baked dessert of whole parboiled apples stuffed with fruit preserves or raisins, individually wrapped in fluffy crêpes and baked with butter and cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole eggs, yolks and stiffly beaten whites separated, for the crêpe batter

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally 1 Polish kwaterka (250 ml), for the crêpe batter

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta, for the crêpe batter

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: 1 teaspoon for the batter, the rest for frying the crêpes and drizzling on top

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: small fruit, such as Papierówka or Reinette apples

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for scalding the apples

ingredients.name: fruit preserves or jam
ingredients.note: for stuffing the apples (or raisins with sugar and cinnamon)

steps: Whisk the egg yolks with the flour, milk, and a teaspoon of melted butter, gently fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites, then fry thin crêpes in clarified butter and let cool.
Peel and core the apples, plunge the whole fruit into boiling water for at most 5 minutes (without boiling them), and drain on a sieve.
Fill the hollowed apple centres with fruit preserves or jam and wrap each apple in a separate crêpe.
Grease an ovenproof casserole or baking dish with butter, coat with breadcrumbs, and line the bottom with crêpes.
Arrange the crêpe-wrapped apples in the dish, fill the gaps with the remaining crêpes, and drizzle the top with a full tablespoon of clarified butter.
Bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 60 minutes, then turn out onto a platter and sprinkle with sugar mixed with cinnamon.

name: Zrazy wołowe siekane w sosie śmietanowym (Minced beef zrazy in sour cream sauce)
summary: Oblong patties shaped from finely chopped beef enriched with beef suet, a soaked wheat roll, and grated onion, browned in butter and braised in broth with sour cream.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: orig. 3 historical Polish funts of good beef

ingredients.name: beef suet
ingredients.note: orig. half a historical Polish funt of fresh kidney suet

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: or stock from bones and soup vegetables, for braising

steps: Trim the beef of membranes and sinews, scrape with a knife or chop finely together with the fresh kidney suet into a smooth mass (nowadays you can pass it through a mincer).
Add the soaked and squeezed roll, grated onion, salt, and pepper, and knead the mixture very thoroughly.
Shape into large oval patties (zrazy) and brown them on all sides in browned butter for about 10 minutes.
Moisten the browned zrazy with broth or bone-and-vegetable stock, add a tablespoon of sour cream, cover, and braise over low heat for 15 minutes.

name: Ozór z chrzanem do sztuki mięsa (cured beef tongue with horseradish, served with boiled beef)
summary: Beef tongue dry-cured for 10 days with salt and saltpetre, then boiled until tender, peeled, and served in diagonal slices alongside boiled beef with grated horseradish and vinegar.

ingredients.name: potassium nitrate
ingredients.note: nowadays curing salt can be used

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for rinsing and boiling the tongue

steps: Clean the beef tongue thoroughly of slime and trim off excess gristle at the base without rinsing the meat in water.

Rub the tongue thoroughly with salt mixed with half a teaspoon of saltpetre, place in an earthenware or glass bowl, cover with a plate, and leave in a cool place for 10 days, turning the meat daily and rubbing it with the resulting brine.
After 10 days, rinse the tongue several times in cold water, place in a pot of water, and simmer for about 2.5 hours until completely tender.
Peel the skin off the hot tongue, cut the meat into diagonal slices, and serve alongside boiled beef with freshly grated horseradish seasoned with vinegar.

name: Orange jelly
summary: A fragrant citrus jelly made with sugar rubbed against the rind of six oranges and juice from the oranges and four lemons.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 500 ml for the syrup + 500 ml for dissolving the gelatine

steps: Rub the sugar cubes on all sides against the scrubbed rind of 6 fresh oranges so the sugar absorbs the aromatic orange oil.
Pour 500 ml of water over the zested sugar and simmer over low heat, skimming off the foam.
Squeeze the juice of 4 lemons and the oranges through a fine sieve and bring to a boil with the syrup; you may reserve some oranges and separate them into segments to arrange in the jelly.
Dissolve the gelatine or isinglass in the remaining 500 ml of warm water, combine with the hot citrus syrup, and strain through a tightly woven cloth.
Pour the jelly into a mould (optionally arranging orange segments inside) and leave in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until set.

name: Sztufada w galarecie (larded braised beef in aspic)
summary: A beef roast larded with pork fatback, browned in butter, braised for 3 hours with calf's feet, soup vegetables, and beetroot, and chilled in its sieved natural aspic.

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: cut into thick strips for larding the meat

ingredients.name: soup vegetables
ingredients.note: a large bunch (carrot, parsley root, celeriac), finely chopped

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: enough to cover the vegetables and calf's feet well

steps: Lard the beef roast with thick strips of pork fatback dusted with black pepper, rub the meat with salt, and set aside for just under 60 minutes.
Heat the butter in a large casserole pot, add the roast, and brown it well on all sides, turning frequently.
Add the cleaned and chopped calf's feet along with the finely chopped soup vegetables, beetroot, and onion, then pour in enough water to cover the vegetables.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and braise over very low heat for 3 hours.
Transfer the tender roast to a deep bowl, press all the braising liquid and vegetables through a fine sieve directly over the meat, and leave in a cool place for about 4 hours until completely set.
Unmould the chilled roast from the bowl, slice it together with the aspic, and serve cold.

name: Raspberry jelly
summary: A clear ruby-red dessert jelly made from sweet raspberry juice and fresh lemon juice set with gelatine or isinglass.
steps: Pour 250 ml of warm water over the gelatine and dissolve thoroughly without boiling (if using isinglass, simmer it over low heat down to 250 ml), then strain through a dense napkin.
Mix the dissolved gelatine with 750 ml of clear raspberry juice.
Squeeze the clear juice of 2 lemons through muslin into the mixture and stir.
Pour the jelly into a 1 l mould and leave in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until set; wrap the mould briefly in a cloth dipped in hot water before unmoulding onto a platter.

name: Szynka z cielęciny (cured and larded roast leg of veal)
summary: A large leg of veal dry-cured for 10–21 days with salt, saltpetre, and coriander seeds, marinated with juniper berries and hot vinegar, densely larded with pork fatback, and roasted with butter and sour cream.

ingredients.name: leg of veal
ingredients.note: orig. a hindquarter of veal weighing 12–15 funt (4.8–6 kg)

ingredients.name: potassium nitrate
ingredients.note: orig. 1/2 łut of crushed saltpetre (modern curing salt may be used instead)

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: fresh, cut into strips for larding

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for sprinkling towards the end of roasting

steps: Rub the leg of veal with the salt mixed with saltpetre, sprinkle with the coriander seeds, place under a weight in a stoneware crock, and cure in a cool place for 10 to 21 days, turning the meat daily and basting it with the juices released.
Remove the meat from the brine, rub it with the crushed juniper berries, pour the hot mild vinegar over it, and leave for about 12 hours.
Rinse the veal in the same vinegar, pat dry, and lard it densely with strips of fresh pork fatback.
Roast on a spit or in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 2.5 hours, basting regularly with melted butter and sour cream.
Towards the end of roasting, sprinkle the top of the meat with breadcrumbs so they brown; serve warm or cold, for example as part of the blessed Easter meal.

name: Pan-seared beefsteak in butter (Befsztyk wołowy)
summary: Thick slices of beef tenderloin or rump seared briefly over high heat in foaming browned butter and finished with fresh butter on a warmed plate.

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin, sirloin, or top rump
butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1/2 tbsp for frying plus 3 pieces of butter for the plate

steps: Trim the beef carefully of any silverskin and fat and cut into 3 thick slices about 2.5 cm thick; do not pound the meat or salt it before searing.
Heat about 10 g of butter in a flat skillet until foaming briskly and lightly browned.
Lay the beef slices in the skillet spaced apart and sear over very high heat for about 3–4 minutes without moving them until browned underneath.
Turn the steaks carefully with a fork, salt the browned top immediately, and sear for another 3–4 minutes over high heat.
Transfer the meat to a warm plate topped with 3 pieces of fresh butter (about 20 g), salt the second side, and press gently with the flat of a knife so a little meat juice mingles with the butter.

Return the steaks to the hot skillet for a dozen or so seconds, then place them back on the plate with the butter juices and spoon the pan drippings over them. Total cooking time should not exceed 10 minutes.

name: Ozór na szaro (beef tongue in Polish grey sauce)
summary: Beef tongue boiled until tender with soup vegetables and spices, sliced on the bias, and served in a sweet-and-sour Polish grey sauce made with caramel, vinegar, wine, raisins, and almonds.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the tongue (plus a drop to moisten the sugar)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of lumps of sugar, for caramel

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.note: orig. a handful of raisins and almonds

steps: Wash the tongue, parboil it in water until partially tender, remove it, and peel off the tough skin.
Return the peeled tongue to the pot, add the soup vegetables, spices, and salt, cover with fresh water, and boil until completely tender.
Moisten the sugar with a drop of water and caramelise it in a pan until dark, then add 1 tbsp of butter and 1 tbsp of wheat flour and fry briefly together.
Thin the roux with broth from the tongue, add 125 ml (half a szklanka) of vinegar, the wine, and lemon peel, bring to a boil, and strain the sauce through a sieve.
Add the thoroughly washed raisins and blanched, peeled almonds to the strained sauce.
Slice the tender tongue on the bias, place the slices in the sauce, and bring to a boil together before serving.

name: Steamed bread pudding with raisins and almonds
summary: A classic steamed pudding of fine white breadcrumbs soaked in milk, egg yolks creamed with butter and sugar, stiffly beaten egg whites, currants, sultanas, and almonds.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 3 tbsp + a little for greasing the mould

ingredients.name: white wheat breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta or 3 kubki, sifted

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a little, blanched and chopped

steps: Cream the egg yolks with the butter in a large bowl or mortar, gradually adding the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Stir in the sifted breadcrumbs and pour in the milk slowly, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Add the rinsed and dried currants and sultanas, chopped sweet almonds, pounded bitter almonds, and a pinch of salt; mix and let stand for about 20 minutes so the breadcrumbs swell.
Just before filling the mould, whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the batter.
Spoon the mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-dusted tube pudding mould, seal tightly, and set in a wide pot with boiling water reaching about 4 cm up the sides.
Boil briskly under a lid for at least 75 minutes, topping up with boiling water as needed. Remove the mould and turn the pudding out onto a platter.

name: Zrazy wołowe duszone w wywarze grzybowym (Braised beef zrazy in dried mushroom broth)
summary: Thin pounded beef cutlets dusted with flour, browned in butter, and braised with dried mushroom broth or meat stock.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of historical Polish funts of beef suitable for zrazy

ingredients.name: mushroom broth
ingredients.note: orig. several tablespoons of dried mushroom stock or meat broth

steps: Cut the beef into thin cutlets, season with salt and pepper, and dust each piece with wheat flour.
Heat and brown the butter in a casserole, put in the beef cutlets, and braise covered over low heat for 30 minutes.
Pour in several tablespoons of dried mushroom broth or meat stock and continue braising for about 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the liquid reduces away, leaving the fat, then serve.

name: Lemon Soufflé Omelette
summary: Feather-light soufflé omelette made from 4 egg yolks and 2 egg whites beaten with sugar and lemon zest, folded with stiffly beaten whites from 4 eggs, and baked for 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: separated into 4 yolks and 4 whites, with the whites to be beaten until stiff peaks form

ingredients.name: egg white
ingredients.note: extra, for beating with the egg yolks

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the platter very thinly

steps: Separate the yolks from the whites of 4 eggs; place the 4 egg yolks in a bowl, add 2 extra raw egg whites, 100 g of sugar, and the zest grated from half a large lemon, and beat with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes.
Beat the remaining 4 egg whites into very stiff peaks and carefully fold them into the beaten yolks with a spoon, making sure the mixture remains stiff.
Grease a metal or ovenproof platter very thinly with clarified butter, pile the entire mixture immediately into a high mound, and smooth the surface with a knife.
Place the platter for 15 minutes into a moderate oven (160 °C) with stronger bottom heat (if the top browns too quickly, cover it with a sheet of paper).
Serve the soufflé immediately upon removing it from the oven.

name: Potrawa z mostku cielęcego z warzywami i rakami (veal breast fricassee with vegetables and crayfish)
summary: Poached veal breast in a rich white butter sauce with cauliflower, asparagus, and crayfish tails, served with crisp breaded calf's brain cutlets.
steps: Cut veal breast into pieces, blanch briefly in boiling water, skim, and rinse under cold water.
Transfer the meat to a pot, cover with strained broth, add soup greens and salt, and simmer over low heat for 60–80 minutes until completely tender.
In a saucepan make a roux with a tablespoon of butter and a tablespoon of flour, whisk in veal broth, and simmer until thick.
Add cooked crayfish tails, cauliflower florets, asparagus, and chopped parsley to the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Parboil the calf's brain, slice, coat in beaten egg and breadcrumbs, and fry in butter until golden.
Arrange pieces of veal on a platter, pour hot vegetable and crayfish sauce over them, and garnish around the edge with crisp brain cutlets.

name: Legumina z poziomek (Wild strawberry soufflé pudding)
summary: A fluffy baked soufflé pudding made from ten eggs, sugar, and a purée of wild strawberries gently cooked in butter and dry white wine.

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: orig. half a glass of French wine

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon for cooking the wild strawberries and 1 tablespoon for greasing the mould

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole eggs, yolks and whites separated

steps: Cook the wild strawberries gently with half a glass of white wine and a tablespoon of butter for about 5 minutes, then press through a sieve and let cool.
Beat the ten egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and add them, together with a heaped tablespoon of potato starch and the cooled wild strawberry purée, to the beaten yolks.
Fold everything together gently, transfer to a buttered mould, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 20 minutes.

name: Omlet biszkoptowy z konfiturami (sponge omelette with fruit preserves)
summary: Fluffy oven-baked sponge omelette made from 6 eggs, sugar, and a little flour, folded in half over fruit preserves and dusted with sugar.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: 6 egg yolks and stiffly beaten whites from 6 eggs

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for the batter and 1 tbsp for sprinkling

ingredients.name: fruit preserves
ingredients.note: or thick fruit syrup, for filling

steps: Beat 6 egg yolks with 3 tbsp of sugar until pale and fluffy, then stir in 2 tbsp of wheat flour.
Beat 6 egg whites into stiff peaks and carefully fold into the yolk mixture.
Heat the butter in a shallow ovenproof pan or skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and place in a hot oven (200 °C) for at most 20 minutes.
Transfer the baked omelette to a serving platter, spoon the fruit preserves onto one half, fold the other half over, and sprinkle the top with sugar.

name: Zraziki na prędce w śmietance (Quick pounded beef in cream)
summary: A quick dish of finely pounded beef tossed with grated onion and flour, seared briefly in browned butter, and brought to a boil with sweet cream.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: orig. 1 historical Polish funt of rump or tender roasting beef

ingredients.name: sweet cream
ingredients.note: orig. a scant kwaterka of fresh cream

steps: Cut the beef into walnut-sized pieces, pound each piece very thoroughly with a mallet into fine shreds, and then pound the whole mass together once more.
Season the meat with salt and pepper, add the grated onion, dust with a tablespoon of flour, and mix thoroughly.
Heat the butter in a skillet or shallow pan until it begins to brown, then add the prepared meat.
Sear over high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring vigorously and breaking the meat apart with a spoon to prevent clumping, until it loses its raw colour.
Pour in a scant kwaterka of cream, stir, and bring briefly to a boil, taking care not to cook the meat too long. Serve immediately with separately pan-fried potatoes.

name: Lemon jelly
summary: A clear, sweet-tart jelly made from sugar syrup simmered with lemon juice and lemon slices, combined with dissolved gelatine or isinglass.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 500 ml for the syrup + 250 ml gelatine solution

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: 3 for juice and 1 small sliced and seeded

steps: Pour 500 ml of water over the sugar, bring to a simmer over low heat, and skim off the foam.
Squeeze the clear juice of 3 lemons into the syrup and add the fourth small lemon, sliced with the seeds removed; simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes until no more foam rises.
Dissolve the gelatine in the remaining 250 ml of warm water (or simmer the isinglass down to that volume) and combine with the hot lemon syrup.
Strain the mixture through a cloth or napkin, pour into a mould, and leave in a cool place for about 4 hours (240 minutes) until completely set.

name: Potrawa z główki cielęcej w sosie cytrynowo-winnym (calf's head with lemon-wine sauce)
summary: An elegant dish of boiled, breaded calf's head served with lemon-wine sauce and fried breaded calf's brains.
steps: Soak the calf's head in cold water for an hour, remove the brain, scald the meat with boiling water, and skim off any foam.
Simmer the head with soup greens and salt over low heat for about 2 hours until tender, then remove and cut into serving pieces.
Coat pieces of cooked calf's head in beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then brown in the oven with clarified butter.
Cut the parboiled brain into slices, dip in egg yolk and breadcrumbs, and fry in a pan until golden.
In a saucepan brown a tablespoon of butter with a tablespoon of flour, whisk in stock from the head, add white wine, lemon juice, grated lemon zest, and sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Arrange the browned calf's head on a platter, garnish with brain cutlets, and pour the hot lemon-wine sauce over the top.

name: Hamburg-style beefsteak with eggs and mushrooms
summary: A juicy round beef medallion seared in butter over sliced white onion in an individual pan alongside fried eggs, butter-braised mushrooms, and new potatoes.

ingredients.name: mushrooms or saffron milk caps braised in butter

steps: Shape the thick piece of beef with a knife or rolling pin into a round medallion (without pounding it flat), brush with olive oil, and salt lightly.
In a small round skillet (about 15 cm in diameter), heat half a teaspoon of butter over high heat until lightly browned.
Toss the sliced white onion into the butter and immediately lay the meat on top; sear briskly over high heat for about 3–4 minutes.
Once browned underneath, turn the meat carefully with a fork (without piercing it or pressing out the juices).

Arrange a spoonful of butter-braised mushrooms or saffron milk caps on one side of the meat, the small boiled potatoes on the other side, and carefully crack an egg into each of the two remaining sides.
Cook for another 2–3 minutes until the egg whites set while the beef stays pink and juicy inside, then spoon the hot strong bouillon over everything and serve right in the little skillet.

name: Breaded Calf's Brain Cutlets (Kotlety z mózgu cielęcego)
summary: Delicate cutlets of calf's or beef brain parboiled in water with vinegar, cleaned of membranes, coated in egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in clarified butter.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold for soaking and hot for parboiling

steps: Soak the calf's or beef brain in cold water for 60 minutes.
Cover the soaked brain with hot salted water and several tablespoons of vinegar, bring to a boil, parboil briefly, drain, and let cool.
Gently peel the outer membrane and veins from the cooled brain, then slice it into flat cutlets.
Dip the brain slices in beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs, and fry in hot clarified butter on both sides until golden brown; serve as a main dish or as an accompaniment to vegetables and fricassees.

name: Boiled calf's head à la vinaigrette
summary: A whole scalded calf's head simmered gently in a flour-and-vegetable blanc stock, sliced hot with its brains, and served with a cold vinegar, gherkin, and herb vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: for juice to rub the head

steps: Soak the scalded calf's head with its skin in cold water for 24 hours (1440 minutes), changing the water several times.
The next day, pat the head dry, rub it all over with lemon juice, and sew it tightly into a clean white linen cloth.

In a large pot, whisk the wheat flour with a little water, add the sliced soup vegetables, bay leaf, allspice, peppercorns, and salt, lay in the cloth-wrapped head, add enough water to cover completely, and simmer over low heat for 3.5 hours (210 minutes) until tender.
Meanwhile, prepare the cold vinaigrette: stir the finely chopped cornichons, dill (or chives), and parsley into the mild salted vinegar.
Lift the tender head from the stock, cut open the cloth, carefully remove the brains, slice the meat with the skin, garnish with the brains, and serve hot with the cold vinegar sauce.

name: Steamed yeast dumpling cake (pyza drożdżowa na parze)
summary: A fluffy sweet steamed yeast cake or pull-apart buns dipped in butter, gently cooked in a closed mould in a water bath and served with melted butter or fruit sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for dough + for mould and drizzling

steps: Combine part of the plain wheat flour with lukewarm milk mixed with yeast to make a starter and set aside in a warm place for about 30 minutes to rise.
Once the starter has risen, add the remaining plain wheat flour, eggs, 2 tbsp of butter, and sugar, kneading vigorously in a bowl until smooth and elastic.
Transfer the dough into a buttered mould (or shape into round buns, dip each in melted butter, and arrange closely together filling the pan halfway) and let rise for about 40 minutes.
Cover the mould tightly with a lid, place in a larger pot with boiling water reaching a depth of about 5 cm, and steam for 60 minutes, replenishing boiling water as needed.
Turn the steamed dumpling cake out onto a platter, drizzle with melted butter, and dust with sugar.

name: Legumina migdałowa z ryżu (Almond and rice blancmange)
summary: A chilled pudding of rice flour and finely ground sweet almonds cooked in whole milk with sugar, set in a mould and served with raspberry syrup or vanilla sauce.

ingredients.name: white rice or rice flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of rice pounded into flour and sifted

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of fine sugar

steps: Grind the rice into fine flour and sift through a fine mesh sieve (or use ready-made rice flour).
Blanch the almonds in boiling water, slip off their skins, and grind finely or pound in a mortar, then mix with the rice flour and fine sugar.
Bring the milk to a boil in a saucepan with a pinch of salt and add the rice-and-almond mixture spoonful by spoonful, whisking briskly the whole time.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture becomes very thick and glossy.
Spoon the hot pudding into a deep mould or bowl greased with olive oil and refrigerate for about 3 hours until set; before serving, unmould onto a platter and pour raspberry syrup over the top.

name: Pierożki kruche z konfiturami (fried shortcrust jam dumplings)
summary: Crisp shortcrust pastries enriched with egg yolks and butter, filled with thick fruit preserves, and deep-fried golden like doughnuts.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: 1 historical Polish kwarta, orig. a kwarta of flour

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: half a kwaterka, orig. half a kwaterka of milk

ingredients.name: fruit preserves
ingredients.note: thick cherry or rose petal preserve

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.note: or clarified butter for deep frying

steps: Sift the flour onto a pastry board, add softened butter, 7 egg yolks, and milk, then knead into a cohesive, smooth short pastry.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 3 mm.
Cut out rounds using a glass, spoon thick preserves into the centre, and crimp the edges tightly to form small turnovers.
In a deep saucepan heat lard or clarified butter to about 175 °C.
Fry the dumplings in batches of several at a time on both sides until golden brown, just like doughnuts.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on a sieve or paper towels, and dust with icing sugar before serving.

name: Pieczeń barania duszona ze śmietaną (mutton braised with sour cream)
summary: Leg or shoulder of mutton marinated for several days in spiced boiled vinegar, larded with fatback, and braised with root vegetables, juniper berries, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: roast mutton
ingredients.note: mutton roasting joint; leg or shoulder trimmed of membranes and excess fat

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: boiled with spices, for marinating the meat and basting while braising

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: for larding the meat or sliced on the bottom of the casserole

ingredients.name: sour cream 18%
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of sour cream

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or broth, for basting while braising

steps: Trim the mutton roast of membranes and excess fat and marinate for 2–3 days in a cool place in vinegar boiled with spices.
Remove the meat from the marinade, pat dry, lard with fatback, and rub with salt.

Melt the butter in a casserole, scatter the sliced celeriac, parsley root, onion, and juniper berries over the bottom, lay the roast on top, moisten with 1–2 tbsp of vinegar from the marinade, and braise over low heat, turning frequently and basting with a spoonful of water or broth at a time, until the meat browns.
Remove the browned roast, dust it on all sides with wheat flour, and rub the braising liquid and vegetables through a sieve.

Return the joint to the casserole, pour over the sieved sauce and 500 ml (half a kwarta) of sour cream, and braise covered until completely tender (before serving, you may add small shallots, capers or olives to the sauce).

name: Racuszki drożdżowe (small yeast pancakes)
summary: Fluffy small yeast pancakes made with milk, egg yolks, and butter, spooned into hot lard and dusted after frying with cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for dough and 1 tbsp for dusting

steps: Mix the plain wheat flour with the yeast dissolved in lukewarm milk and set in a warm place for about 30 minutes until bubbling.
Add the egg yolks, butter, 1 tbsp of sugar, and a pinch of salt, mix thoroughly to form a thick batter, and let rise for 60 minutes.
Heat the lard in a wide saucepan and drop round spoonfuls of the risen dough into the hot fat.
Fry the pancakes on both sides until golden brown, lift out with a slotted spoon to drain, and immediately sprinkle with the remaining sugar mixed with cinnamon.

name: French toast with mulled wine and raisin sauce (Grzanki z winem)
summary: Sweet wheat roll slices soaked in cream and egg, fried in clarified butter, dusted with cinnamon sugar, and served with a hot spiced wine and raisin sauce.

ingredients.name: wheat roll
ingredients.note: orig. 1 roll, outer crust grated off

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: or white wine, for the sauce

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the wine sauce and for dusting the croutons

ingredients.name: cinnamon stick
ingredients.note: orig. 1 piece of cinnamon stick, for the sauce

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: ground, for dusting the croutons with sugar

steps: Grate the outer crust off the wheat roll and slice the loaf lengthwise.
Dip the slices in sweet cream, then in beaten egg, and dust lightly with sifted breadcrumbs.
Fry the croutons in hot clarified butter for about 6–8 minutes, turning twice, until richly browned.
In a small saucepan, bring the red wine to a boil with sugar, a piece of cinnamon stick, and plenty of raisins, and cook for about 5 minutes.
Dust the fried croutons with cinnamon sugar and serve with the hot wine sauce in a sauceboat.

name: Ptysie parzone czyli pączki zaparzane (fried choux pastry doughnuts)
summary: Traditional choux pastry doughnuts deep-fried until crisp, sprinkled with sugar, and served with chaudeau sauce or fruit juice.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1 kwaterka, orig. a kwaterka of water

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: half a kwaterka, orig. half a kwaterka of clarified butter

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: 1 kwaterka, orig. a kwaterka of fine flour

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: beaten in one by one into slightly cooled dough

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.note: or lard with butter for deep frying

steps: In a saucepan bring a kwaterka (250 ml) of water to a boil with clarified butter (125 g).
When boiling, dump in sifted flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon over low heat until glossy and pulling cleanly away from the pan.
Remove the dough from the heat, cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one at a time, beating thoroughly after each until the mixture is light and uniform.
In a deep saucepan heat lard or clarified butter to about 175 °C.
Dip a spoon into melted butter, scoop walnut-sized portions of dough, and drop into the hot fat.
Fry until golden on both sides, remove with a slotted spoon to drain on a sieve, sprinkle with icing sugar, and serve with chaudeau sauce or fruit juice.

name: Mostek barani z ryżem (breast of mutton with rice)
summary: Breast of mutton parboiled with soup vegetables and onion, then cut into pieces and braised until tender with rice moistened with mutton broth, served with butter and browned whole shallots.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the breast and stock

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: part for braising the rice and part for browning the shallots

steps: Wash the breast of mutton, place it in a pot of water, bring to a boil and skim. Add the soup vegetables, whole onion and salt, then cook until the meat is partially tender.
Scald the rice with boiling water, rinse with cold water, and drain.
Melt a piece of butter in a saucepan, add the rice, moisten with strained mutton broth, and braise over low heat until the grains swell slightly.
Cut the half-cooked breast of mutton into pieces, add them to the rice, and continue braising together, gradually moistening with mutton broth (you may also add a few small onions).
Transfer the meat and rice to a serving platter and pour butter with whole, lightly browned shallots over the top.

name: Potrawka z pieczeni baraniej z agrestem (mutton fricassee with gooseberries)
summary: A traditional old Polish stew of roast mutton in a sweet-and-sour sauce with unripe gooseberries and broth.
steps: Carve leftover roast mutton into neat slices.
Brown a tablespoon of butter in a saucepan, add a tablespoon of flour, and fry the roux, stirring constantly.
Whisk the hot broth and defatted roast juices into the roux.
Add the stemmed unripe gooseberries and sugar, then cook gently for a few minutes until the gooseberries soften slightly.
Add the roast mutton slices to the sauce, warm thoroughly for 5 minutes, and transfer onto a serving platter.

name: Prosię w galarecie (suckling pig in clear savoury aspic)
summary: Pieces of young suckling pig simmered with soup vegetables, vinegar, and spices, then covered with clarified broth that sets into aspic.
steps: Cut cleaned suckling pig into neat serving portions, bring to a boil in water, and skim off foam.
Add soup greens, onion, dried mushroom, vinegar, allspice, bay leaves, and salt, and simmer over low heat until the meat is tender (about 60–75 minutes).
Lift out the cooked meat, rinse briefly in cold water, and arrange decoratively in a glass bowl or mould.
Boil down the broth, strain through a cloth, clarify with lightly beaten egg whites, and filter again.
Pour the cooled, clear broth over the meat in the dish and place in a cold spot until the aspic sets completely.
Serve with vinegar and olive oil or horseradish sauce.

name: Pork kidneys braised in Madeira sauce
summary: Thinly sliced pork kidneys, parboiled several times and then braised with puréed roasted onion in a sauce of roux, meat stock, and Madeira wine.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the roux and 1/2 tbsp for dusting

steps: Roast the onion in the oven until soft, peel, and mash or rub through a sieve to a smooth purée.
Trim the pork kidneys, parboil several times in boiling water while skimming carefully (about 15 minutes), then cool and cut into thin slices.
Brown the butter with 1 tablespoon of wheat flour in a skillet or saucepan, whisk in the bouillon and Madeira wine, stir in the sieved roasted onion, and bring the sauce to a boil.
Season the sliced kidneys with salt, dust with the remaining wheat flour and pepper, add to the sauce, and braise covered over low heat for about 60 minutes until tender.

name: Naleśniki z konfiturami, jabłkami lub serem (crêpes with preserves, apples or quark)
summary: Thin crêpes made with milk and clarified butter, lightened just before frying with beaten whites from 5 eggs, filled with fruit preserves, plum butter, apple marmalade, or sweet quark, and browned in butter.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: 5 egg yolks for the batter and 5 egg whites beaten into stiff peaks

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp of cold butter for the batter and approx. 2 tbsp for frying and pan-browning

ingredients.name: fruit preserves
ingredients.note: or plum butter, stewed apple marmalade with cinnamon, or fresh quark rubbed with butter, egg and raisins

steps: Beat 5 egg yolks with 1 tbsp of cold clarified butter, 250 ml of wheat flour, and a pinch of salt, then gradually pour in 500 ml of milk, beating into a thin, pourable batter.
Just before frying, beat 5 egg whites into stiff peaks and gently fold into the crêpe batter.

Heat a frying pan until very hot, brush thinly with clarified butter, pour in portions of batter, and swirl quickly to coat the entire surface; fry briefly and stack the cooked crêpes on an upturned soup plate.
Spread each crêpe with fruit preserves, plum butter, apple marmalade, or sweetened quark filling, and fold into triangles or roll into cylinders.
Brown the folded crêpes on both sides in clarified butter until golden and serve sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon.

name: Pasztet w pyzie (pull-apart meat-filled yeast buns)
summary: Casserole-baked pull-apart pie of yeast buns stuffed with finely minced beef or veal, sautéed onion, breadcrumbs, and eggs, generously dipped in melted clarified butter.

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: melted, for dipping the buns, pouring over in the casserole and greasing the pan

ingredients.name: boiled or roast beef
ingredients.note: or roast veal, chopped as finely as possible

steps: Make a sponge from 250 ml of warm milk, 25 g of fresh yeast and some of the wheat flour. Once it rises, pour in 4 beaten eggs and 2 tbsp of melted butter, add the remainder of the 1 litre of flour, knead thoroughly into a soft dough, and leave to rise.

Melt 2 heaped tbsp of butter in a frying pan, sauté a large grated onion in it, add the finely minced beef or veal, a handful of breadcrumbs, 2 eggs, salt, and pepper, and mix the stuffing thoroughly.
Pull off pieces of the risen dough, flatten them in your palm into rounds, place a portion of meat stuffing in the centre (you may fill some buns with plum butter), and seal into round buns.
Dip each bun in melted clarified butter and arrange them side by side in a casserole greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, filling the vessel halfway up.
Pour the remaining melted butter over the arranged buns, leave to rise a second time, and bake in a well-heated oven (190 °C) for 45 minutes; unmould onto a platter before serving.

name: Oszczędny i łatwy pasztet (economical and easy pâté)
summary: Festive layered pâté of roasted hare forequarters and small game birds alternating with a forcemeat of calf's and hare livers, fatback, butter, milk-soaked rolls, and egg yolks, baked under a puff-pastry lid and served with caper sauce.

ingredients.name: hare forequarter
ingredients.note: from 2 hares along with the heads

ingredients.name: quail
ingredients.note: orig. 6–8 pairs of waxwings (nowadays quails or squabs)

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt (400 g) of unsalted fatback for the forcemeat and approx. 100 g for larding the meat

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: 2 large onions half-baked in the oven for the forcemeat and 1 for the stock

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt (400 g) of fresh butter for the forcemeat, approx. 35 g for roasting the hares and 1 tbsp (15 g) for the sauce

ingredients.name: wheat roll
ingredients.note: round, with the crust grated off, soaked in milk and squeezed dry

ingredients.name: puff pastry
ingredients.note: for the rim and lid of the pâté

ingredients.name: bouillon tablet
ingredients.note: orig. 4 łuty of bouillon dissolved in 500 ml (half a kwarta) of hare stock

steps: Trim the sinews carefully from the hare forequarters, lard with fatback, salt, and roast in the oven while basting with butter, and fry the larded small birds over low heat in a skillet.

Simmer the bones, heads and trimmings from the hare forequarters with the soup vegetables, 1 onion, 2 dried mushrooms, bay leaf, allspice, mace and salt, reducing the stock to at most 500 ml (half a kwarta); remove the brains and pick the remaining meat from the bones, then pound them in a mortar.

Grate the calf's and hare livers, finely chop 400 g of unsalted fatback and 2 half-baked onions, place everything over 400 g of butter in a shallow pan, and bake uncovered in a moderate oven (160 °C) for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.

Combine the braised livers with the pounded hare meat, 4 milk-soaked, mashed, and squeezed rolls, salt, pepper, a pinch of mace, half a grated garlic clove, and 4 egg yolks, and knead the forcemeat thoroughly.
In a deep metal or ovenproof dish, alternate layers of forcemeat, pieces of roast hare with the larger bones removed, and roasted birds, finishing with a layer of forcemeat.
Place the pâté 60 minutes before serving into a moderate oven (170 °C); after 30 minutes cover the top with a puff-pastry lid and bake for another 15–30 minutes.

Dissolve 50 g of concentrated bouillon in the reduced hare stock, thicken with a roux of 1 tbsp of butter and 1 tbsp of flour, season with 1 tsp of lemon juice and 1 tsp of capers, and serve separately in a sauceboat.

name: Apple fritters in egg batter (Jabłka smażone w cieście)
summary: Slices or quarters of tart apples dipped in a light batter of egg yolks, flour, and stiffly beaten egg whites, fried golden in lard or butter and showered with cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for briefly dipping the peeled apple slices

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.note: or butter, generous amount for frying

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: ground, for dusting with the sugar

steps: Peel and core the apples, slice them into rounds, and dip briefly in water so the batter clings well.
Beat the egg yolks with a teaspoon of wheat flour, whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, and gently fold the two together.
Heat a generous amount of lard or butter in a skillet or wide saucepan.
Dip the drained apple slices into the egg batter, lay them in the hot fat, and fry carefully on both sides for about 4–5 minutes until golden-orange.
Immediately after frying, shower the apple fritters thickly with cinnamon sugar and serve hot.

name: Suflet z ryżu (baked rice soufflé)
summary: A fluffy soufflé of rice cooked in whole milk with butter and sugar, ground with bitter almonds and egg yolks, folded with stiffly beaten egg whites, and baked under a topping of sliced almonds.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of whole milk

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for cooking the rice, plus coarse sugar for sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: orig. 8 yolks and the stiffly beaten whites of 8 eggs

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: slivered or sliced, for sprinkling on top

steps: Cook the rice in 500 ml of whole milk with the tablespoon of butter and the sugar over low heat until completely soft, taking care that it does not catch on the bottom.
Let the cooked rice cool slightly, then mash it in a mortar-style mixing bowl with the 5 blanched, peeled, finely pounded bitter almonds.
Beat the 8 egg yolks into the rice mixture and mix thoroughly.
Beat the 8 egg whites to stiff peaks, gently fold them into the rice mixture with a spoon, and immediately transfer to an ovenproof serving platter.
Sprinkle the top with coarse sugar and sliced almonds, and place in an oven preheated to 170 °C.
Bake until the soufflé rises and turns golden brown, then garnish with whole-fruit preserves and serve immediately.

name: Calf's Brain Vol-au-Vents in Puff Pastry
summary: Puff-pastry vol-au-vent cases with lids, filled with a creamy ragout of parboiled calf's or beef brain, sautéed onion, broth, sour cream, egg yolks, and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: egg white for sealing the rounds and egg yolk for brushing the tops

ingredients.name: calf's brain
ingredients.note: or a small fresh beef brain (approx. 200 g)

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: for the water to parboil the brain

ingredients.name: meat broth
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of tablespoons of broth

steps: Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1 cm (half a finger) and cut out 40 rounds with a glass (for 20 vol-au-vents); cut a smaller circle about 2.5 cm in diameter out of the centre of half the rounds.

Brush the solid rounds with beaten egg white, top them with the cut-out rings, brush the tops of the rings and the small cut-out centres (lids) with egg yolk, and bake on a sheet in a hot oven (210 °C) for about 25–30 minutes.
Parboil the calf's or beef brain in water with salt and vinegar, remove the membranes, chop finely or mash with a spoon, and season with salt and pepper.
Sauté the grated onion in 1 tbsp of butter, stir in 1 tbsp of wheat flour, pour in 2 tbsp of broth, and bring to a boil.

Once the roux cools slightly, stir in 1 tbsp of sour cream, add the mashed brain, and bring briefly to a boil, then finally stir in 2 beaten egg yolks and the lemon juice and heat gently until thickened.
Fill the hollow centres of the baked puff-pastry cases with the hot ragout, top with the pastry lids, and return briefly to the oven to heat through.

name: Paszteciki w kruchym cieście (shortcrust pastry tartlets)
summary: Fluted shortcrust pastry tartlets filled with a ragout of parboiled calf's brains, veal spinal marrow, and mushrooms in a velvety lemon-butter sauce enriched with egg yolks, topped with fried parsley.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of fresh butter (plus extra for greasing the moulds)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the pastry (plus for salting the filling)

ingredients.name: veal spinal marrow
ingredients.note: orig. a bunch of veal spinal marrow (approx. 150 g)

ingredients.name: caster sugar
ingredients.note: on the tip of a knife

ingredients.name: button mushrooms
ingredients.note: fresh braised in butter or small pickled

ingredients.name: parsley leaves
ingredients.note: fried in clarified butter, for sprinkling

steps: Knead a shortcrust pastry in a cool place from 500 ml of wheat flour, 200 g of butter, 1 egg, and a pinch of salt.
Roll out the pastry, line buttered fluted metal tartlet tins with it, and bake in a moderately hot oven (180 °C) for 15 minutes until golden, then unmould the shells.
Parboil 2 calf's brains and the veal spinal marrow, peel off the membranes, cut into pieces, and salt lightly.

Mix 1 tbsp of fresh butter with half a tablespoon of wheat flour in an unheated small saucepan. Squeeze in the juice of a whole lemon, add 1 tbsp of broth and a pinch of sugar, and bring to a boil, then thicken the sauce with 2 egg yolks.
Add the cut brains, spinal marrow, and butter-braised (or pickled) mushrooms to the finished sauce and stir gently.
