Fill the baked shortcrust tartlet shells with the ragout, sprinkle the tops with parsley leaves fried in clarified butter, and place briefly in a warm oven to heat through.

name: Classic puff pastry for savoury pies, small filled pastries, or sweet pastries
summary: Traditional homemade puff pastry made from equal weights of wheat flour and chilled washed butter, given four three-fold turns in a cool room.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt + a little for dusting

steps: An hour (60 minutes) before making the pastry, work the butter in cold water to wash out excess salt, leave it in cold water to firm up, then pat thoroughly dry in a cloth and shape into a flat block about 2.5 cm thick.
Knead a smooth, supple dough from the wheat flour, egg, and cold water, work it on a pastry board, and let it rest for a dozen or so minutes.
In a cool room, flatten the dough, set the block of cold butter in the centre, and fold the edges of the dough over it like an envelope.
Roll the pastry out carefully in a single forward motion to a thickness of about 1.2 cm, fold in three, and chill in a cool place for 10 minutes.
Repeat the rolling, three-fold turn, and 10-minute chilling four times.
Always place savoury pies, small filled pastries, or sweet pastries made from this dough directly into a very hot oven (210–220 °C) and bake for about 20–25 minutes until flaky layers form.

name: Paszteciki z raków (crayfish-filled pastry cases)
summary: Puff-pastry or shortcrust bouchées filled with a thick ragout of chopped tails and claws from 20 crayfish sautéed in butter and flour and enriched with sour cream, dill, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: puff pastry
ingredients.note: or shortcrust butter pastry, for 20 bouchées

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for parboiling the crayfish and for the filling

steps: Parboil 20 medium crayfish in salted water, remove the meat from the tails and claws, and chop it finely.
Sauté the chopped crayfish meat in a small saucepan with 1 tbsp of butter and 1 tbsp of wheat flour.
Add 2 tbsp of sour cream, the chopped dill, salt, pepper, and 2 egg yolks, and heat over low heat, stirring, until the filling thickens.

Fill 20 baked puff-pastry shells with the filling and place briefly in the oven to heat through (or shape pastries from raw shortcrust butter pastry and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 15–20 minutes).

name: Orange Compote in Candied Peel Syrup (Kompot z pomarańczy)
summary: Fresh orange segments carefully stripped of their white membranes and covered with hot sugar syrup boiled with thin strips of orange zest.

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 oranges, including thinly pared zest from 1 orange

steps: Wash and scald one orange, thinly pare off only the orange zest (without the white pith), and cut it into very fine julienne strips.
Boil the water and sugar in a saucepan into a thick syrup, add the strips of orange zest, and bring to a boil several times.
Peel all the oranges, divide them into segments while carefully removing all white pith, and arrange in a serving bowl.
Pour the hot syrup along with the cooked zest over the orange segments.

name: Pasztet na zimno (cold meat terrine)
summary: A cold terrine that sets in a mould without further baking, made from three kinds of roasted meat (beef, pork, and veal) pounded in a mortar, calf's liver, dried mushrooms, and diced fatback, bound with stock from 4 calf's feet.

ingredients.name: roast beef
ingredients.note: beef roasting joint; orig. 2 funt of beef for roasting

ingredients.name: roast veal
ingredients.note: veal roasting joint; orig. 2 funt of veal for roasting

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for braising or roasting the meats

ingredients.name: dried mushrooms
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of boiled mushrooms along with their cooking liquid

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt of boiled fatback cut into small cubes

ingredients.name: calf's feet
ingredients.note: boiled down in water to 500 ml (half a kwarta) of strong calf's-foot jelly stock

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling down the calf's feet and cooking the mushrooms

steps: Braise the beef, pork tenderloin, veal, and calf's liver in a casserole, or roast them in a roasting pan, basting with butter. Then chop finely and pound in a mortar (or grind) into a smooth paste.
Boil 4 calf's feet in a separate pot, reducing the stock to about 500 ml (half a kwarta) of strong gelatinous stock. In another small pot, boil the mushrooms and chop them finely.
Boil the fatback until tender and cut it into small cubes.
Combine the pounded meats with the chopped mushrooms, diced fatback, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Pour in the calf's-foot jelly stock and the mushroom cooking liquid and mix very thoroughly (for a more festive version, you may add the meat from half a roasted hare or a few small game birds).
Pack the mixture into a mould or bowl, set in a cool place for several hours until completely firm, and before serving unmould onto a platter and cut into slices.

name: Legumina z jabłek, konfitur i marengów (Apple, preserve and meringue tart)
summary: An elegant baked dessert on a shortcrust base layered with apple marmalade, fruit preserves, and whole stuffed apples, crowned with meringue and chopped almonds.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: originally 1 full Polish kwaterka (250 ml), for the pastry

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt, for the pastry

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: 10 apples for the marmalade and about 6 apples poached whole

ingredients.name: fruit preserves
ingredients.note: generous amount, for the marmalade layer and for stuffing the whole apples

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: originally half a Polish funt (200 g) for the meringue, plus sugar for the apple marmalade and for sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: chopped, for sprinkling over the meringue

steps: Knead a shortcrust pastry from the wheat flour, butter, and two tablespoons of sugar, line an ovenproof platter or tart tin with it, and blind-bake until golden in an oven preheated to 190 °C (about 20 minutes).
Prepare a thick apple marmalade by stewing 10 peeled apples with a little sugar. Peel and core the remaining apples, parboil them whole, and stuff them with fruit preserves.
Spread the apple marmalade over the pre-baked crust, spoon a layer of fruit preserves on top, and arrange the whole stuffed apples over it.
Beat 5 egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in 200 g of fine sugar, and spread the meringue over the fruit.
Sprinkle the top with sugar and chopped almonds and bake in an oven preheated to 160 °C for 15 minutes, taking care not to let the meringue burn.

name: Cold Game Terrine (Pain de Gibier)
summary: Refined game terrine made from roast hare (or roe venison) and calf's liver rubbed through a sieve with strong bouillon and creamed in an earthenware bowl with 10 eggs, melted butter, and spices, baked in a pan lined decoratively with fatback.

ingredients.name: hare
ingredients.note: whole (or 3 hare forequarters or a roe-deer forequarter)

ingredients.name: calf's liver
ingredients.note: very large (or 2 smaller ones, approx. 500 g)

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: part for larding the meat and liver, and part boiled and sliced for lining the pan

ingredients.name: meat bouillon
ingredients.note: orig. half a Polish kwaterka of strong bouillon

ingredients.name: spices
ingredients.note: allspice, ginger and mace (a very small amount)

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: beaten in one at a time while creaming

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt of fresh butter, melted (plus a little for greasing the pan)

steps: Trim the sinews and lard the hare (or roe venison) and large calf's liver with fatback, roast until tender, and cool completely.

Remove the roasted meat from the bones, grate the meat and liver, pound the trimmings in a mortar, and rub everything through a wire sieve while moistening with 125 ml (half a Polish kwaterka) of strong bouillon.
Season the sieved paste with salt, pepper, the tiniest pinch of allspice, ginger, and mace, and 1 grated garlic clove.
Transfer the mixture to an earthenware mixing bowl and beat in one direction with a wooden pestle, cracking in 10 eggs one after another.
Pour 400 g of cool melted butter into the smoothly creamed mixture and blend thoroughly again.
Grease a saucepan or mould with butter, line the bottom and sides in a decorative pattern with slices of boiled fresh fatback, and fill with the prepared mixture.
Bake in a slow oven (150 °C) for about 45–60 minutes, then cool completely in the mould, turn out onto a platter like a cake, and serve sliced with olive oil and vinegar.

name: Paszteciki postne (Lenten eggs and fish served in shells)
summary: Quick meatless hors d'oeuvres served in buttered scallop shells, filled on one side with creamy scrambled eggs made from 6 eggs with butter and chives, and on the other side with strips of smoked salmon or smoked fish.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp of fresh butter for the scrambled eggs and half a tbsp for greasing the shells

ingredients.name: smoked salmon
ingredients.note: cut into thin strips (or anchovies, or smoked vendace or flounder)

steps: Lightly beat 6 eggs with a pinch of salt.

Melt 1 tbsp of fresh butter in a small saucepan, pour in the eggs, and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until a smooth, thick scramble forms; towards the end stir in a pinch of chopped chives.
Butter the baking shells and spoon a portion of scrambled eggs onto one side of each shell, arranging strips of smoked salmon or other smoked fish on the opposite side.

name: Paszteciki w kąchach z łososia, węgorza lub szczupaka (salmon, eel or pike baked in shells)
summary: Flaked cooked salmon, eel, or pike bound with a thick white fish-stock sauce seasoned with lemon juice and capers (or anchovies), baked for 15 minutes in scallop shells under buttered breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: salmon
ingredients.note: orig. 2 funt of raw fish (salmon, eel or pike), or 1 funt (400 g) of boned fish

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the fish and stock

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 large tbsp for the sauce and approx. 2 tbsp for greasing the shells and browning the breadcrumbs

ingredients.name: capers
ingredients.note: drained of vinegar (or 6 soaked and chopped anchovies)

steps: Boil the fish (salmon, eel, or pike) in water with the soup vegetables and salt, let cool, bone carefully, and flake into small pieces with a fork.
Make a blond roux in a small saucepan from 1 large tbsp of butter and 1 tbsp of wheat flour, stirring constantly, and thin with strained fish cooking liquid into a smooth sauce.
Squeeze the juice of half a lemon through a strainer into the sauce, add 1 tbsp of drained capers (or 6 soaked, chopped anchovies), fold in the flaked fish, and mix thoroughly.
Spoon the fish mixture into buttered baking shells, top generously with breadcrumbs browned in butter, and place for 15 minutes in a preheated oven (180 °C) until heated through.

name: Poached Sour Cherry Compote (Kompot z wiśni)
summary: Summer dessert of whole unpitted Morello sour cherries briefly simmered in a rich sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: sour cherries
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kopa (60 cherries, preferably Morello sour cherries, unpitted)

steps: Wash the sour cherries and remove the stems, leaving the stones inside the fruit.
Boil the water and sugar in a small saucepan into a thick syrup.
Drop the cherries into the boiling syrup, bring to a boil several times over low heat, and pour everything into a serving bowl.

name: Rough puff pastry for small savoury pies
summary: A flaky layered butter pastry made from flour, butter, eggs, and cream, folded in four several times and rolled out to make small round savoury pies.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 3 for the dough and 1 for sealing and brushing

steps: Knead a uniform dough from the wheat flour, chilled butter, 3 eggs, and the water or sweet cream.
Roll the dough out thinly, fold in four, and roll out again; repeat the folding and rolling 2–3 times, then let the folded dough rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the pastry out again into a thin sheet and cut out round discs with a glass or cutter.
Brush the edges of half the discs with egg white, place your chosen filling in the centre, cover with a second disc of pastry, seal the edges, and brush the tops with beaten egg.
Place in a well-heated oven (200 °C) and bake for 30 minutes until golden brown.

name: Stewed Prune Compote (Kompot z suszonych śliwek)
summary: Winter dessert compote of dried plums simmered until tender with sugar, cinnamon, and lemon peel, served in strained syrup.

ingredients.name: prunes
ingredients.note: orig. half a funt of French prunes or dried white Greek plums

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: enough to cover the prunes (plus lukewarm water for rinsing)

steps: Rinse the prunes in lukewarm water, transfer to a saucepan, and pour in enough fresh water to cover the fruit.
Add the sugar, a piece of cinnamon bark, and the lemon peel, and simmer over low heat until the prunes are completely tender.
Transfer the tender prunes to a serving bowl, strain the cooking syrup through a sieve, and pour it over the fruit.

name: Stewed Gooseberry Compote (Kompot z agrestu)
summary: Summer fruit dessert of half-ripe gooseberries scalded in boiling water and gently poached in a rich sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: gooseberries
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta of half-ripe gooseberries (approximately 600 g)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. more than half a funt

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka for the syrup, plus boiling water for scalding the gooseberries

steps: Top and tail the half-ripe gooseberries, place them in a sieve or colander, scald several times with boiling water, and drain thoroughly.
Boil 250 ml of water with the sugar in a small saucepan to make a clear syrup.
Drop the drained gooseberries into the boiling syrup, bring to a boil several times over low heat until the fruit softens without bursting, and transfer to a serving bowl.

name: Paszteciki do zupy (savoury pastries served with soup)
summary: Savoury pastries for clear broth or borscht, made from semi-shortcrust pastry kneaded from thick sour cream and flour, with a two-layer filling of chopped meat and parboiled calf's or beef brain.

ingredients.name: sour cream 18%
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwaterka of thick, not too sour cream

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of flour (approx. 325 g)

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: beaten with a little water, for brushing the pastries

ingredients.name: boiled or roast beef
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt of boiled or roast meat

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of fresh fatback or butter (plus butter for the baking sheet)

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: grated and scalded with boiling water

ingredients.name: calf's brain
ingredients.note: or beef brain, parboiled in salted water, deveined and cut into large cubes

steps: Mix 250 ml of thick sour cream with 500 ml of wheat flour in a bowl with a spoon, then knead the dough on a pastry board.
Finely chop the boiled or roast beef, mix with melted fatback or hot butter, the grated and scalded onion, salt, pepper, and 1 tbsp of broth, let cool, and beat in 2 raw eggs.
Parboil the calf's or beef brain in salted water, remove the membranes, and cut into large cubes.
Pinch off pieces of dough the size of a large walnut, roll them into balls, flatten with your fingers, and roll out lightly into round discs.
Place a portion of the dark meat stuffing on each disc, top with a layer of cubed white brain, and pinch the edges of the dough together over the filling into a lengthwise scalloped ridge.

Arrange the pastries on a buttered baking sheet, brush with egg beaten with water, and bake in a very hot oven (220 °C) for 15–20 minutes until golden; serve hot with clear broth, bouillon, or borscht.

name: Paszteciki z mózgu w naleśnikach (breaded crêpe rolls with calf's brain filling)
summary: Crêpes spread with a thick filling of parboiled and mashed calf's brain, butter-braised mushrooms, onion, lemon juice, and egg yolk, rolled into cylinders, breaded in egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in clarified butter.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwaterka of milk, for the crêpes

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the onion and braising the mushrooms

ingredients.name: meat broth
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of tablespoons of broth

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: for frying the crêpe rolls and parsley leaves

ingredients.name: parsley leaves
ingredients.note: in small sprigs, fried in butter with the crêpes

steps: Fry thin crêpes from a batter made with 3 eggs, 250 ml of milk, wheat flour, and a pinch of salt.

Mash the parboiled calf's brain with a spoon or pestle, transfer to a small saucepan with the butter and grated onion, add the chopped butter-braised mushrooms, 2 tbsp of broth, the juice of half a lemon, salt, and pepper, and cook together briefly until thickened.
Let the filling cool slightly, beat in 1 egg yolk, and mix thoroughly.

Spread the crêpes with the filling, roll into cylinders (or overlap the crêpes side by side, lay a cylinder of filling across, roll up together, and cut into oblong logs), dip in beaten egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry the crêpe rolls in hot clarified butter until golden brown, tossing small sprigs of parsley into the pan towards the end, and serve sprinkled with the crisp fried parsley.

name: Strasbourg-Style Liver Pâté
summary: Spreadable liver paste made from calf's liver thickly larded with fatback and braised in butter, grated, rubbed through a fine sieve, and blended with clarified butter.

ingredients.name: fatback
ingredients.note: cut into strips, for thickly larding the liver

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kubek of fresh clarified butter

steps: Lard the calf's liver generously with strips of fatback and braise it covered in butter until tender, then let cool.
Grate the braised liver on a grater, then rub it through a fine sieve.
Season the paste with salt and pepper, pour in 250 ml (1 kubek) of fresh clarified butter, and beat very thoroughly.
Pack the pâté into an earthenware crock or tin, chill, and serve for spreading on fresh rolls.

name: Poached Apple Compote (Kompot z jabłek)
summary: Halved tart apples poached in batches in a spiced white wine and cinnamon sugar syrup, arranged in a serving bowl and garnished with fruit preserves and jelly.

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: large, tart varieties (e.g. White Transparent or Reinette)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka for the syrup, plus cold water for soaking the apples

ingredients.name: white wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of French or Rhine wine

ingredients.name: whole-fruit preserves
ingredients.note: and apple or currant jelly, optionally for garnish

steps: Peel the apples, cut them in half, remove the cores, and drop the fruit immediately into cold water to prevent browning.
In a wide, shallow saucepan, bring 250 ml of water, the sugar, the piece of cinnamon stick, and the white wine to a boil to form a light syrup.
Place the first batch (10 halves) of apples into the boiling syrup, poach until tender while taking care they do not fall apart, and lift out with a slotted spoon into a serving bowl.
Poach the remaining 10 apple halves in the same manner and arrange them in the bowl.

Strain the remaining syrup, reduce over higher heat until slightly thickened, and pour over the arranged apples; before serving, you may garnish the dessert with whole-fruit preserves and fruit jelly.

name: Green lettuce salad with olive oil, tarragon vinegar, and eggs
summary: Crisp head lettuce coated first in olive oil, then sprinkled with tarragon vinegar and salt to prevent the leaves from wilting and releasing water.

ingredients.name: butterhead lettuce
ingredients.note: orig. ratio given per 1 head (assumed 2 heads for 4 servings)

steps: Hard-boil the eggs (about 10 minutes), cool, peel, and cut into quarters.
Trim the lettuce heads, rinse in cold water, and dry very thoroughly, gently squeezing out excess water.
Place the lettuce leaves in a salad bowl, drizzle first with the olive oil alone, and toss gently so the oil coats each leaf.
Next add the tarragon vinegar, then finally sprinkle with salt, pepper, and a little sugar. Toss carefully and thoroughly for a while.
Garnish the top with hard-boiled egg quarters and serve immediately.

name: Scalded red cabbage salad (sałatka z czerwonej kapusty)
summary: Finely shredded red cabbage scalded with boiling water until cooled, squeezed dry, and marinated for an hour with vinegar, oil, sugar, and salt.
steps: Shred the red cabbage very finely, place in a bowl, cover with boiling water, and let stand for about 30 minutes until the water cools.
Drain off the water, squeeze the cabbage very firmly to remove excess moisture, and transfer to a salad bowl.
Season the cabbage with salt, dress with vinegar and olive oil, add sugar, and mix thoroughly.
Set the salad aside for 60 minutes before serving to let the flavours meld.

name: Boiled carrot and onion salad (sałatka z marchwi)
summary: Thin slices of boiled carrot mixed while hot with raw onion, olive oil, vinegar, and pepper, then left to stand for an hour before serving.
steps: Boil the scraped carrots until completely tender in salted water for about 25 minutes and drain.
While still hot, slice the carrots as thinly as possible (halving thicker roots lengthwise first) directly into a salad bowl.
Finely chop raw onion directly over the steaming carrots so it softens in the residual heat.
Drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, season with pepper and a pinch of salt, toss, and let stand for 60 minutes before serving.

name: Apple salad with anchovies, capers, and olives (sałatka z jabłek z sardelami)
summary: A savoury side salad for meat dishes, made with grated tart apples sprinkled with vinegar and mixed with chopped anchovies, capers, olives, and olive oil.
steps: Peel the apples, coarsely grate (or dice very finely), and immediately splash with half the vinegar to prevent discolouring.
Rinse the anchovies to remove excess salt, bone, chop finely, and mix with the grated apples.
Add the capers, chopped olives, olive oil, and remaining vinegar to taste, season with pepper, toss thoroughly, and serve with boiled beef or roast meat.

name: Italian-style mixed vegetable salad with pickles and herring (sałatka włoska ze śledziem)
summary: A substantial salad of cooked root vegetables cut into thin strips, white beans, pickled mushrooms and saffron milk caps, gherkins, capers, and herring, dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: pickled saffron milk caps and mushrooms

steps: Boil the beetroot, potatoes, carrots, white beans, and celeriac separately in salted water until tender, then cool, peel the root vegetables, and cut into thin strips.
Cut the gherkins, pickled mushrooms, some of the saffron milk caps, and pickled shallots into strips. Combine with the vegetables, reserving the beetroot until the end, and add the capers.
Debone the herring, chop finely, and add to the salad mixture.
Pour in olive oil and vinegar, season with pepper, sugar, and salt if needed, fold in the beetroot strips at the very end to minimize discolouration, and toss gently.
Transfer the salad into a serving bowl and garnish with whole pickled saffron milk caps.

name: Potato salad with herring and gherkins (sałatka ziemniaczana ze śledziem)
summary: A classic salad of potatoes boiled in their skins, herring diced together with its milt, gherkins, and grated onion, dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec (2 Polish kwarty)

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender (for about 25 minutes), let cool, peel, and cut into strips, slices, or dice.
Clean the herring (without soaking) of skin and bones, and dice the meat together with the milt finely.
Slice the pickled gherkins thinly and grate the onion.
Combine the potatoes, herring with milt, gherkins, and onion in a salad bowl, add vinegar and olive oil, season with pepper and a pinch of sugar, and toss thoroughly.

name: Pasztet na zimno z gęsi (cold goose pâté)
summary: Cold pâté made from roast goose, two partridges, and butter-braised calf's and goose livers rubbed through a sieve with rich bouillon, mixed with diced boiled fatback and garlic, and chilled in a mould.

ingredients.name: goose
ingredients.note: fat, cleaned, along with the liver

ingredients.name: meat bouillon
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwarta of bouillon made by dissolving a quarter funt (100 g) of good bouillon tablet

steps: Roast the cleaned goose and 2 partridges unstuffed in the oven, let cool, remove the meat from the bones, skin, and sinews, chop finely, and pound in a mortar.
Braise the calf's liver and goose liver separately while basting with butter, then cool and grate.
Boil 400 g of fresh fatback, let cool, and cut into small cubes.
Rub the pounded poultry meat and grated livers through a coarse sieve, moistening with 500 ml of strong, jelly-like bouillon.
Season the sieved mixture with salt, pepper, a pinch of mace, and the grated garlic clove, fold in the diced fatback, and mix thoroughly.
Pack the mixture into a mould and leave in a cool place until completely set; serve the sliced pâté with olive oil and vinegar.

name: Baked pike-perch au gratin with mushrooms (sandacz au gratin)
summary: Pike-perch split into two halves and baked in white wine beneath a thick, crisp crust of button mushrooms cooked gently in butter, parsley, and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: pike-perch
ingredients.note: orig. 3–5 Polish funty (4 funty taken as 1.6 kg)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1/2 Polish funt (200 g) for topping + 50 g for the dish and mushrooms

steps: Fillet the cleaned pike-perch lengthwise into two halves, remove the backbone, salt, and let rest in a cool place for 3.5 hours (210 minutes).
Peel and finely chop the mushrooms, scald briefly with boiling water, drain, salt, and braise in 25 g of butter over low heat for 15 minutes.
Grease a metal platter or gratin dish heavily with 25 g of butter, dust with some breadcrumbs, sprinkle with half the parsley, and spread half the braised mushrooms.
Lay both fish halves flat side by side, pour over the white wine, and top with the remaining mushrooms, remaining parsley, pepper, and a thick layer of breadcrumbs.
Dot the surface evenly with pieces of the remaining 200 g of butter.
Bake in a hot oven at 210 °C for about 45 minutes without basting, turning the dish occasionally, until a thick, golden, crisp crust forms on top.

name: Baked soufflé sponge omelette (Grzybek)
summary: A fluffy baked sponge omelette made from egg yolks beaten at length with sugar and flour, with stiffly beaten egg whites gently folded in, served with sugar or fruit juice or as an accompaniment to spinach or sorrel.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the batter, plus extra for dusting

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: generous amount for the hot skillet

ingredients.name: fruit juice
ingredients.note: optional, for pouring over before serving

steps: Beat the egg yolks with the wheat flour and a tablespoon of sugar in a bowl for about 15 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them very gently into the beaten yolks at the last moment.
Heat a heavy ovenproof skillet until very hot, pour in a generous layer of clarified butter, and spread the egg foam in the pan.
Transfer the skillet to an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 10 minutes.
Serve the hot omelette dusted with sugar or drizzled with fruit juice, or cut into 8 pieces and arrange around braised spinach or sorrel.

name: Pierogi z grzybami (dried mushroom pierogi)
summary: Classic Lenten boiled pierogi filled with dried wild mushrooms and gently stewed onion, served with butter and browned onion.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a tablespoon for frying the onion

steps: Rinse the dried mushrooms, scald with boiling water, simmer in a small amount of water until tender, and chop finely.
Melt a tablespoon of butter in a frying pan and cook two chopped onions until translucent.
Remove the pan from the heat, combine the onions with the chopped mushrooms, crack in two eggs, and season with salt and pepper.
Knead plain flour, warm water, egg, and a pinch of salt into a springy dumpling dough and roll out thinly on a work surface.
Cut out rounds, place portions of mushroom filling in the centre, seal the edges securely, and drop into salted boiling water.
Boil the pierogi for 3–4 minutes from the moment they float to the surface.
Lift out with a slotted spoon onto a platter and drizzle with hot butter and browned onion.

name: Crayfish simmered in red wine (raki w czerwonym winie)
summary: Fresh crayfish cooked under a tight lid for ten minutes with red onion, parsley, dill, and a glass of red wine.

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.note: part for cooking and part for garnish

steps: Rinse the crayfish very thoroughly in plenty of cold water and drain.
Place the crayfish into a three-litre pot, add the sliced onion, sprigs of parsley and dill, salt, pepper, and red wine.
Cover the pot tightly and cook over high heat for 10 minutes, shaking the pot several times until the crayfish turn a vivid red.
Discard the cooked onion and herbs, pile the hot crayfish onto a napkin-lined platter, and garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Neapolitan-Style Italian Macaroni
summary: Thick Italian macaroni boiled in salted water or light broth, generously dressed with a thin sauce made from butter, flour, and rich bouillon, and served with grated Parmesan.

ingredients.name: Italian macaroni
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt of thick Italian macaroni

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwaterka of boiling water or broth for the sauce (plus water or light broth to boil the pasta)

ingredients.name: bouillon tablet
ingredients.note: orig. 4 Polish łuty of good French bouillon (nowadays thick bouillon concentrate)

steps: Break the long, thick Italian macaroni in half and boil it until tender in a wide pot of salted boiling water or light broth, then drain in a colander.
Dissolve 50 g of concentrated bouillon in 250 ml (1 Polish kwaterka) of boiling water or broth.
Bring 1 tbsp of fresh butter and 1 scant tbsp of wheat flour to a boil in a small saucepan, then gradually add the hot bouillon to make a fairly thin sauce.
Transfer the hot macaroni to a serving platter, pour the prepared sauce generously over the top, and serve with grated Parmesan.

name: Szczupak faszerowany po żydowsku (Jewish-style stuffed pike)
summary: Traditional whole pike stuffed (with head and tail intact) with a mixture of minced fish flesh, pike liver and milt, scalded onion, soaked wheat roll, butter, eggs, and mace, wrapped in a cloth and poached in vegetable broth.

ingredients.name: pike
ingredients.note: whole with head, liver, and milt (approx. 1.2 kg)

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: 1 scalded with boiling water and chopped for the stuffing, and 1 for the stock

ingredients.name: white wheat roll
ingredients.note: soaked in milk and squeezed dry

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of tablespoons of butter for the stuffing (plus optional extra for drizzling with breadcrumbs)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the soup-vegetable stock and scalding the onion

steps: Clean the pike, slit it lengthwise, and carefully remove all the flesh, leaving the skin intact along with the head and tail.
Carefully bone the fish flesh, salt it, and chop it very finely together with the boiling-water-scalded onion and the pike's liver and milt.
Add the milk-soaked and squeezed wheat roll, black pepper, a pinch of mace, 2 tablespoons of butter, and 2 eggs to the chopped fish, and knead the mixture thoroughly.
Fill the pike skin with the stuffing, sew it up tightly, wrap the fish firmly in a clean linen cloth, and tie with kitchen twine.
Lay the pike in an oblong fish kettle or pan, pour over the boiling stock made from the soup vegetables and onion, and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Lift out the fish, unwrap the cloth, and serve whole while hot (for example with melted butter and browned breadcrumbs or parsley sauce) or cooled and sliced with olive oil and vinegar.

name: Pierogi gotowane z kapustą (boiled sauerkraut and herring pierogi)
summary: Traditional Lenten pierogi filled with cooked sauerkraut, dried forest mushrooms, and chopped salted herring, topped with crisp fatback cracklings.

ingredients.name: salted herring
ingredients.note: lightly soaked, boned, and finely chopped

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the onion and filling

steps: Boil the sauerkraut in water without squeezing out its juice, drain in a colander, and chop finely.
Cook the dried mushrooms separately in a small amount of water until tender and chop finely.
Carefully debone the soaked herring and chop finely with a knife.
Melt butter in a frying pan, cook the chopped onion until translucent, add the sauerkraut, mushrooms, and herring, mix well, season with pepper, and fry briefly.
Knead plain flour, hot water, and salt into an elastic dough and roll it out thinly.
Cut out rounds, spoon portions of cooled filling into the centre, seal the edges securely, and drop in batches into salted boiling water.
Cook for about 3–4 minutes from the moment they float to the surface.
Transfer with a slotted spoon to a platter and top with melted fatback cracklings.

name: Marinated herrings in sweet cream and milt dressing (śledzie w śmietance)
summary: Soaked salted herrings layered with onion slices, peppercorns, and allspice, then covered with a dressing of sieved herring milt, cream, and vinegar.
steps: Soak the salted herrings in cold water for at least 36 hours (2160 minutes), then drain, pat dry with a cloth, and fillet, reserving the milt.
Layer the herrings in a glass jar alternating with onion slices, peppercorns, and allspice berries.
Chop the extracted herring milt, press through a fine sieve, blend with the sweet cream, and thin with boiled, cooled vinegar.
Pour the prepared sauce over the herrings and set in a cold place overnight (for about 8 hours). The next day they are ready to serve.

name: Wyborny szczupak z rożna (Roast pike in wine and sour cream sauce)
summary: Whole skinned pike roasted and basted generously throughout cooking with a hot sauce of dry white wine, sour cream, butter, and lemon.

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 glass of French white wine

steps: Skin the pike, clean the fish thoroughly inside, and season with salt.
Brace the fish from the inside with a wooden skewer and tie it in several places with kitchen twine (in the oven, set it on a rack over a roasting pan).
Combine the white wine, sour cream, lemon, and a heaped tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan and heat until very hot.

Roast the pike in an oven preheated to 190 °C (historically on a spit) for about 35–40 minutes, basting frequently with the hot wine-and-cream mixture until the surface cracks slightly and the flesh begins to flake.
Reduce the pan juices collected from roasting over high heat and pour the sauce over the pike arranged on a platter.

name: Buckwheat and wheat yeast blini
summary: Traditional airy yeast blini made with an overnight wheat-flour sponge and buckwheat flour, scalded with boiling water and baked in small pans brushed with clarified butter.

ingredients.name: lukewarm water
ingredients.note: orig. 250 ml overnight + approx. 750 ml in the morning

steps: In the evening (10–12 hours before baking), dissolve the yeast in 250 ml of lukewarm water and mix with the wheat flour to form a sponge; leave covered overnight to rise.
In the morning, add the buckwheat flour, salt, and about 750 ml of lukewarm water to the risen sponge, beating into a loose batter; set aside to rise again.
Once the batter has risen a second time, pour 125 ml of boiling water right into the centre, stir quickly (the batter should be slightly thicker than crêpe batter), and let rise a third time.
Heat small blini pans until very hot, brush with hot clarified butter, and ladle in a fairly thick layer of batter.
Bake the blini in a very hot oven (220 °C) or covered for about 4–5 minutes without flipping, until risen and browned on top. Transfer immediately to plates and serve hot.

name: Pierożki gryczane (buckwheat and curd cheese parcels in cabbage)
summary: Unusual old Polish dumplings made from buckwheat flour worked with sour cream, filled with cheese, and baked wrapped in cabbage leaves.

ingredients.name: buckwheat flour
ingredients.note: 1 historical Polish kwarta, orig. a kwarta of buckwheat flour

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: thick, fresh sour cream added gradually

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese
ingredients.note: curd cheese beaten with eggs and butter

ingredients.name: white cabbage
ingredients.note: large scalded leaves for wrapping the dumplings

steps: Work the buckwheat flour in a bowl with a rolling pin for about 30 minutes, gradually adding thick sour cream a tablespoon at a time and adding the salt, until smooth and pliable.
Beat the farmer's cheese with eggs and softened butter into a smooth filling.
Remove large leaves from the cabbage head and blanch them briefly in boiling water until softened.
Place a portion of buckwheat dough onto each cabbage leaf, spoon cheese filling into the centre, and fold the leaf in half, enclosing the dough and cheese completely.
Arrange the parcels on a baking sheet and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 30 minutes.
When the leaves soften and the dough inside turns yellowish, remove from the oven and serve with clarified butter or sour cream and sugar.

name: Saffron risotto Milanese-style (risotto alla milanese)
summary: Rice cooked gently in rich beef or veal broth with butter and soaked saffron, then generously sprinkled with grated Parmesan before serving.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kieliszek for soaking the saffron + boiling water for scalding the rice

ingredients.name: beef or veal broth
ingredients.note: orig. 500 ml at the start + approx. 250 ml during braising

steps: Steep the saffron in 30 ml of lukewarm water. Scald the rice with boiling water, drain, and rinse with cold water.
In a one-litre saucepan, bring 500 ml of beef or veal broth to a boil, add the rice, butter, and a pinch of salt, then braise covered over low heat for about 10 minutes.

When the rice is partly cooked, add the strained saffron infusion and the remaining 250 ml of hot broth. Cook for another 10–15 minutes until the rice is tender and golden and the mixture has thickened.
Spoon the thickened rice mixture onto a platter and sprinkle generously with grated Parmesan.

name: Dutch-style rice with fatback and tomato sauce (ryż po holendersku)
summary: Parboiled white rice simmered in broth with browned diced fatback and pepper, tossed with a rich buttery tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 Polish kwarta, for parboiling the rice and fatback

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: Name: fresh pork fatback; note: orig. 1/2 Polish funt

steps: Cover the rinsed rice with 1 l of cold water, boil for 5 minutes, then drain in a sieve and rinse with cold water.
Parboil the fatback diced into thick cubes for 5 minutes in boiling water, drain, dry the pan, return the fatback, and fry until nicely browned.

Pour 500 ml of broth or bouillon over the browned fatback, add a pinch of crushed black pepper, stir in the parboiled rice, season with salt, and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring frequently so the rice does not stick.
In a separate saucepan, cook the tomato purée with butter and plain wheat flour into a smooth sauce.
Remove the cooked rice from heat, fold in the tomato sauce, mix thoroughly, and mound onto a serving platter.

name: Zrazy rybne ze szczupaka (Stuffed pike rolls)
summary: Rolled fillets of pike stuffed with a filling of sautéed onion, breadcrumbs, and egg, breaded and pan-fried in clarified butter.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. several onions, for the stuffing

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for the stuffing plus extra for breading

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 whole for the stuffing and 1 beaten for breading

steps: Chop the onions for the stuffing, squeeze out their juice through a clean cloth, chop finely once more, and sauté in hot butter.
Mix the cooled onion with a tablespoon of breadcrumbs, a pinch of pepper, and one whole egg.
Split the pike lengthwise, bone it, cut into thin slices, and season lightly with salt.
Place a portion of the onion stuffing on each slice of fish and roll up tightly like beef rolls.
Dip the rolls in beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs, then fry in clarified butter for about 10–12 minutes until golden brown.

name: Stuffed fried herrings (śledzie smażone nadziewane)
summary: Desalted whole herrings stuffed with a seasoned filling of their own milt, onion, butter, breadcrumbs, and egg, breaded and pan-fried in clarified butter.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. 1 handful (40 g) for stuffing + 40 g for breading

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 whole for stuffing and 1 whole for breading

steps: Soak the herrings in cold water for at least 36 hours (2160 minutes), then drain and pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Without skinning, clean the herrings through the belly cavity, extract the milt, and mince it very finely together with the onion.
Combine the minced milt and onion with 1 tbsp of butter, half the breadcrumbs, 1 egg, and pepper into a uniform stuffing, and fill the herring bellies.
Dip the stuffed herrings in the second beaten egg, dredge in remaining breadcrumbs, and fry in hot clarified butter for about 5–6 minutes per side until golden brown.

name: Szczupak lub sandacz w majonezie w całości (whole poached pike or zander in aspic mayonnaise)
summary: A large whole pike or zander poached in vegetable court-bouillon, chilled, coated in a fluffy mayonnaise whipped from reduced fish aspic, olive oil, and vinegar, and richly garnished with vegetables, capers, olives, and hard-boiled eggs.

ingredients.name: pike
ingredients.note: orig. a pike or zander weighing 8–10 funt (3.2–4 kg)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for salting the fish and seasoning the mayonnaise

ingredients.name: gelatine
ingredients.note: orig. 2 łut of gelatine (or 3 łut = 37.5 g if making extra cubed aspic for garnish)

ingredients.name: fish cooking stock
ingredients.note: orig. 3 kwaterki of stock from cooking the fish

ingredients.name: assorted garnishes
ingredients.note: gherkins, cooked carrot and beetroot, green peas, capers, olives, pickled mushrooms, hard-boiled eggs, corn salad

steps: Clean the pike or zander whole, rub it inside and out with salt, and leave in a cool place for several hours.
In a large pot, boil a court-bouillon from the soup vegetables, onion, and spices.

Wrap the fish in a clean linen cloth (or bind just the head with cloth), place in a wide pan, cover with the warm vegetable court-bouillon, and poach covered over low heat until the flesh is tender without falling apart.
Carefully lift the hot fish from the pan, unwrap the cloth, and lay it whole on a long platter to cool completely.
Pour 750 ml (3 historical Polish kwaterki) of the fish cooking stock over 25 g of gelatine and boil until the liquid reduces by half, then strain the stock and let cool.

Add 250 ml of olive oil, 1 tablespoon of strong sweetened vinegar, and a pinch of salt to the cooled liquid jelly, and whisk until the mixture turns into a thick, white mayonnaise foam and begins to set.

Coat the cold fish completely with a thick layer of the whipped mayonnaise and garnish the top with decoratively cut gherkins, carrot, beetroot, green peas, capers, olives, pickled mushrooms, hard-boiled eggs, and corn salad leaves.

name: Kuropatwy duszone (Braised partridges in sour cream)
summary: Half-roasted larded partridges braised in butter with juniper berries, sour cream, and lemon juice, sprinkled with browned breadcrumbs before serving.

ingredients.name: partridges
ingredients.note: whole birds, cleaned and larded with pork fatback

steps: Roast the cleaned and larded partridges halfway on a spit or in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 15–20 minutes, then cut them in half.
Transfer the partridge halves to a casserole with the melted butter and a few juniper berries, and pour in the pan drippings from roasting.
Add two tablespoons of sour cream and the juice squeezed from the whole lemon, cover, and braise over low heat for about 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Remove the juniper berries, arrange the partridges on a platter, spoon the sauce over them, and sprinkle with browned breadcrumbs.

name: Pieczony zając z sosem z wątróbki i krwi (Roast hare with liver and blood sauce)
summary: Roast hare basted with butter and sour cream, served with a traditional hunter's sauce made from hare liver, dry white wine, broth, and hare blood.

ingredients.name: hare
ingredients.note: dressed, with the liver and blood reserved

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: for rubbing the meat before sprinkling with vinegar

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: for sprinkling the meat and preserving the blood

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the sauce, plus extra for basting the roast

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for basting the hare during roasting

ingredients.name: hare liver
ingredients.note: finely chopped or mashed for the sauce

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: a little, for thinning the sauce

steps: Trim the hare of membranes and sinews, rub with olive oil, sprinkle with vinegar, and prepare like venison (larded with pork fatback).

Place the hare in a roasting pan (optionally rubbing the top with a piece of hare liver for a glossy finish) and roast in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 60–75 minutes, basting frequently with butter and sour cream.
Finely chop or mash the hare liver and fry it in a tablespoon of butter together with the grated onion.
Stir in half a tablespoon of flour, pour in half a glass of white wine and a little broth, season with salt and pepper, bring to a boil together, and press through a sieve.
Enrich the strained sauce with the hare blood preserved in vinegar, bring briefly to a boil once more, and pour over the roasted hare.

name: Polish carp in grey sauce (Karp na szaro)
summary: Traditional Polish carp steaks cooked in a spiced beer and vegetable broth with rye bread crust, served in a thick grey sauce made with carp blood, caramel, red wine and raisins.

ingredients.name: carp
ingredients.note: orig. 1 carp with its blood and milt or roe

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: salted and boiled, for catching the carp blood

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: toasted salt, for salting the carp steaks and the vinegar

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of sugar lumps

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: orig. half a szklanka, or the juice of half a lemon

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: a little peel for the broth, plus slices for garnish

steps: While dressing the carp, catch its blood in boiled salted vinegar, then cut the cleaned fish into steaks (dzwonka) and salt them along with the milt or roe.
Simmer a court-bouillon in beer with the parsley root, celeriac, leek, carrot, dried mushroom, onions, peppercorns, allspice, bay leaf, and cloves for about 25 minutes.
Place the carp head on the bottom of a pot, lay the fish steaks on top, add the lemon peel and rye bread crust, pour in the hot beer broth, and boil briskly over high heat for about 20 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, brown a tablespoon of butter with a tablespoon of wheat flour and let cool slightly.
Whisk the carp blood in vinegar into the cooled roux, add the sugar and burnt caramel, and thin with the fish cooking liquor.
Pour the red wine into the sauce, add the scalded raisins, and simmer over low heat for about 10 minutes until thickened.
Arrange the cooked carp on a platter, garnish with lemon slices and raisins, and pour the hot grey sauce generously over the fish.

name: Buckwheat Groats in Mushroom Broth (Kasza na grzybowym smaku)
summary: Fine buckwheat groats slowly braised with a generous amount of hot melted butter in an aromatic dried mushroom broth.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. nearly 1 kwaterka, melted and hot

ingredients.name: dried mushroom broth
ingredients.note: orig. enough to reach 1 cal (2.5 cm) above the groats

steps: Pour the fine buckwheat groats into a saucepan and pour the hot melted butter over them.
Season the groats with salt and pour in the dried mushroom broth to a height of about 2.5 cm above the level of the groats.
Cover the pan with a tight-fitting lid and cook over very low heat for 60 minutes, shaking the pan frequently so the groats absorb the broth evenly without sticking.

name: Pierogi leniwe (lazy curd cheese dumplings)
summary: Tender dumplings made from sieved curd cheese, egg yolks, beaten egg whites, and raisins, sliced diagonally and served with clarified butter and sugar.

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese
ingredients.note: fresh, well drained of whey, orig. 1 historical Polish kwarta

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a tablespoon for the dough, orig. a spoon of butter

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: for the dough, plus extra for dusting the work surface

steps: Squeeze excess whey from the farmer's cheese through a cloth, then beat it in a bowl with a tablespoon of softened butter, the egg yolks, and a pinch of salt.
Add two tablespoons of plain flour and the rinsed raisins to the cheese mixture, beating until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the cheese mixture with a spoon.
Turn the mixture onto a generously floured board, shape into a long log, flatten slightly, score the top in a crosshatch pattern with a knife, and cut diagonally into dumplings.
Drop the dumplings into salted boiling water and cook gently for 2–3 minutes after they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon to a platter, drizzle with hot clarified butter, and sprinkle with sugar.

name: Potrawa z kaczki lub kury duszona z ryżem (braised duck or chicken with rice)
summary: Tender poultry braised gently under a lid with root vegetables in butter, served with fluffy braised rice and velvety pan sauce.

ingredients.name: duck
ingredients.note: or chicken, cut into serving portions

steps: Cut the prepared bird into serving pieces, place into a pot, add a knob of butter, peeled sliced root vegetables, and a splash of water and salt.
Braise covered over low heat for about 50 minutes, turning the meat pieces occasionally.
In a separate pot scald the rice with boiling water, drain, add a tablespoon of butter, and braise over low heat, gradually spooning in braising broth from the poultry until tender and fluffy.
Arrange the tender meat in the centre of a platter with breasts on top, and form a border of braised rice all around.
Strain the meat broth, thicken with a little flour whisked with a tablespoon of water, season with a pinch of nutmeg, bring to a brief boil, and pour over the meat and rice.

name: Fluffy boiled buckwheat groats (Kasza gryczana na sypko)
summary: Traditional Polish buckwheat groats simmered in a two-to-one ratio of salted boiling water with butter until fluffy and dry, served dressed with melted butter or rendered fatback.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for cooking, plus extra butter or fatback for serving

steps: Bring the water to a boil in a pot with a tablespoon of butter and salt.
Gradually pour the buckwheat groats into the boiling water, stirring constantly with a spoon.
Lower the heat to very low and cook covered for about 15–20 minutes until the groats absorb the water and become tender.
Turn the fluffy groats out onto a platter and drizzle with melted butter or rendered fatback.

name: Potrawa z kaczki z białą kapustą (braised duck with white cabbage)
summary: Duck pieces simmered with vegetables, served with quarters of white cabbage and baked under a dill and sour cream sauce topped with breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: white cabbage
ingredients.note: small heads of sweet white cabbage

steps: Cover jointed duck with a small amount of water, add soup greens, allspice, bay leaf, and salt, and simmer over low heat until tender (about 45 minutes).
Trim the cabbage heads, cook in salted water, drain, and cut into quarters.
In a saucepan make a roux with a tablespoon of butter and a tablespoon of flour, add chopped dill, whisk in duck broth, pour in sour cream, and cook until thick.
In a baking dish arrange duck pieces alternately with cabbage quarters, pour the prepared sauce over, and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 15 minutes until lightly browned and bubbling.

name: Roast stuffed turkey (Indyk pieczony nadziewany)
summary: A roast turkey generously larded across the breast and thighs with strips of fatback, with its neck cavity filled with turkey liver, breadcrumbs, roasted onion, eggs, and raisins.

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: fresh, cut into thin strips for larding and diced for the stuffing

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. 1 grated roll for the stuffing, plus extra for sprinkling toward the end of roasting

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the stuffing, plus extra melted butter for basting

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for rubbing the turkey and seasoning the stuffing

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.note: orig. 1 handful of sultanas or currants, rinsed

steps: Clean the turkey thoroughly, rinse, pat dry, insert thin strips of fatback at close intervals into the breast and thighs, and rub well inside and out with salt.
Finely chop the turkey liver and roasted onion and mix with the breadcrumbs, whole eggs, a tablespoon of butter, diced fresh fatback, salt, pepper, mace, sugar, and rinsed raisins.
Fill the neck cavity (crop) of the turkey with the stuffing and sew the opening shut with strong kitchen twine.
Place the turkey in an oven preheated to 220 °C for 30 minutes, then lower the heat to 180 °C and roast for about 90 minutes longer, basting frequently with melted butter.
Toward the end of roasting, sprinkle the turkey with breadcrumbs and finish roasting until the skin is evenly golden brown.

name: Prażucha (toasted flour porridge with fatback cracklings)
summary: A traditional old Polish peasant dish made from dry-toasted wheat or buckwheat flour cooked with boiling water and topped with fatback cracklings.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: or buckwheat flour, dry-toasted in a saucepan

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling, orig. a kwaterka of water for four people

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: fresh fatback rendered into crisp cracklings

steps: Place plain or buckwheat flour into a dry saucepan and toast over low heat, stirring constantly with a spoon until evenly browned and fragrant.
Sift the toasted flour through a fine sieve to remove any lumps.
In a separate saucepan bring a kwaterka (250 ml) of water to a boil with salt.
Gradually sprinkle the flour into the boiling water, stirring vigorously with a spoon over low heat until a thick, uniform dough forms that pulls away from the sides.
Dice the fatback and render in a frying pan until crisp and golden.
Spoon portions of prażucha onto a platter using a spoon dipped in fat, and pour generous amounts of hot cracklings over the top.

name: Potrawa z kurcząt z warzywami i rakami (chicken fricassee with crayfish and spring vegetables)
summary: A spring fricassee of young chicken with cauliflower, asparagus, carrots, and crayfish tails in a parsley butter sauce.
steps: Place chicken in a pot with water, soup greens, cauliflower florets, and salt; simmer over gentle heat until tender (about 25–30 minutes).
Remove the chicken and divide into quarters, transferring the cauliflower florets to a plate.
Cook the chopped asparagus and carrots separately.
In a saucepan melt a tablespoon of butter, blend in a tablespoon of flour, pour in reduced chicken broth, add chopped parsley, and stir constantly until the sauce thickens.
Add the chicken pieces, cooked cauliflower, asparagus, carrots, and crayfish tails to the sauce, and warm everything together gently.
Arrange the chicken on a serving platter, garnish with the vegetables and crayfish tails, and coat generously with the velvety sauce.

name: Pularda z serdelami (spit-roasted poulard with anchovy butter)
summary: A young fattened capon or poulard roasted on a spit, basted with butter, finished with crisp breadcrumbs, and filled with anchovy butter.

ingredients.name: poulard
ingredients.note: or capon, orig. capon or poulard

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for sprinkling near the end of roasting

steps: Thoroughly clean, rinse, and dry the poulard, rub with salt inside and out, and truss the legs with kitchen twine.
Secure the bird on a spit or place on a rack in an oven preheated to 190 °C.
Roast for about 70–80 minutes, basting frequently with melted butter.
Halfway through roasting dust the bird lightly with flour, and 10 minutes before the end sprinkle with breadcrumbs and pan drippings for a crisp skin.
Immediately upon removing from the oven, insert a tablespoon of anchovy butter (or butter creamed with freshly ground pepper) into the cavity.
Carve the poultry into portions and serve with the pan butter juices.

name: Potrawa z kur lub kapłonów po staropolsku (old Polish chicken or capon dish)
summary: An elegant dish of simmered chicken with dried mushrooms and button mushrooms in a velvety Rhenish wine and egg-yolk sauce, surrounded by puff pastry.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.note: two poulards or chickens, orig. two poulards or chickens

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter of a historical Polish funt of fresh butter

ingredients.name: puff pastry
ingredients.note: baked pastry rim around the platter

steps: Clean the chickens, cut into neat portions, rinse, place into a pot, and season with salt.
Add plenty of soup greens, dried porcini, and mace, then simmer gently covered for 2–2.5 hours in their own juices with minimal water so the broth is rich.
Cook fresh button mushrooms separately in a small amount of water with lemon juice.
In a saucepan rub butter with flour, blend with mushroom cooking liquid and strained chicken broth, and bring to a boil; add lemon juice and sugar.
Remove the sauce from the heat, temper with two egg yolks beaten with a little cooled broth, add a small glass of Rhenish wine, and warm gently without boiling.
Arrange chicken pieces in the centre of a platter with breasts on top, garnish with mushrooms and a hot baked puff pastry border, and coat with velvety sauce.

name: Braised rice with mushroom sauce and shallots (ryż duszony z pieczarkami)
summary: Fluffy rice cooked gently in butter with parsley sprigs, served with braised shallots and button mushrooms under a white lemon-and-egg-yolk sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: about 30 g for rice and 1 tbsp (15 g) for sauce

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: 1/2 tbsp for rice and 1 tbsp for sauce

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for braising rice and boiling mushrooms

steps: Scald the rice with boiling water, drain, steep in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain again.

Melt 30 g of butter in a saucepan, add the drained rice, dust with half a tablespoon of plain wheat flour, stir, splash with a few tablespoons of water, season with salt, pepper, and parsley sprigs, and braise covered over very low heat for about 25 minutes until tender.
In a separate saucepan, simmer the button mushrooms and whole peeled shallots in a little salted water for about 15 minutes, then drain, reserving the cooking liquid.

Make a pale roux with the remaining 15 g of butter and 1 tbsp of flour, whisk in the mushroom cooking liquid, add the juice of half a lemon, and bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the beaten egg yolks.
Discard the parsley sprigs, mound the tender rice onto a platter, arrange the cooked shallots and mushrooms on top, and pour over the hot sauce.

name: Omelettes
summary: Classic French omelette (aux fines herbes) made from 6 briefly beaten eggs with chives or parsley, cooked in piping-hot fresh butter and rolled into an oval cushion.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. slightly less than a quarter funt of fresh butter (with 8 eggs, a full quarter funt = 100 g)

steps: Crack 6 eggs into a bowl, add 3 pinches of salt, 3 pinches of pepper and half a teaspoon of chopped parsley or chives, and beat with a fork for exactly 1 minute (no longer, to prevent the eggs becoming watery).
Set a clean frying pan over high heat, add 80 g of fresh butter, and swirl the pan until the butter is thoroughly heated but not browned.
Pour the eggs into the pan and stir initially with a fork so that they set evenly across the entire surface.
Once the eggs begin to thicken, shake the pan and use a knife or spatula to fold both edges of the omelette toward the centre, giving it an oval shape.
Hold the omelette over the heat for a brief moment longer to lightly brown the underside, then turn out onto a platter.

name: Jajecznica (classic Polish scrambled eggs)
summary: Traditional Polish scrambled eggs made from six briefly beaten eggs cooked in hot fresh butter and seasoned with salt, pepper, and chives.
steps: Heat a tablespoon of fresh butter in a small saucepan or skillet until hot.
Beat the whole eggs in a bowl for exactly 1 minute, no longer.
Pour the beaten eggs into the hot butter and cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly with a spoon.
Season the finished scrambled eggs with salt and, if desired, black pepper and chopped chives.

name: Roast goose stuffed with apples (Gęś pieczona)
summary: A young goose rubbed with salt, stuffed with tart apples and marjoram, roasted over sliced onions until crisp, and served with the sweetened roasted apples and pan gravy.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: 1/2 tbsp for dusting the goose and 1/2 tbsp for the gravy

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for basting at the start of roasting

steps: Rub the thoroughly cleaned young goose inside and out with salt.
Fill the cavity of the goose with small whole or quartered tart apples tossed with marjoram, then sew up the opening with kitchen twine.

Spread the sliced onions in a roasting pan, set the goose on top, and roast in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 3 hours (180 minutes), basting at first with water and then with the rendered fat and pan juices.
Toward the end of roasting, dust the top of the goose with half of the wheat flour so the skin browns deeply.
Transfer the roast goose to a platter, scoop the roasted apples out of the cavity, arrange them around the bird, and sprinkle them with sugar.
Skim the excess clear goose fat from the roasting pan, dust the onion pan juices with the remaining half tablespoon of wheat flour, bring to a boil, and pour the gravy over the goose.

name: Baba łatwa a smaczna (easy yeast babka)
summary: A simple, reliable Easter yeast babka on milk or cream, with yolks, vanilla and clarified butter.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo for the starter, plus 250 g for the dough

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 10 deka do yolks i 2 łyżki for the vanilla

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: more if needed to knead the dough

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Stir the yeast into a glass of warm milk or cream, mix with 250 g of sifted warm flour, and leave the starter in a warm place to rise.
Beat 8 yolks with 100 g of sugar until pale, pound the vanilla with 2 spoonfuls of sugar, and clarify the butter and cool it slightly.
When the starter is moving, add the rest of the flour, the yolks, the vanilla, the salt and a little milk if needed. Knead until the dough comes cleanly away from your hands.
Pour in the melted butter (saving a little for the tin) and knead until the fat is fully absorbed.
Turn the dough into a buttered, crumbed tin, filling it to 1/3 of its height. Leave it covered in the warm until doubled, and bake in an oven heated to 180 °C for about 50 minutes.

name: Baba szafranowa (saffron yeast babka)
summary: A golden, traditional old Polish Easter yeast babka coloured with a saffron infusion, with raisins and candied orange peel.

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: orig. a pinch soaked in food-grade rectified spirit

ingredients.name: sultanas
ingredients.note: orig. a handful of light raisins

ingredients.name: candied orange peel
ingredients.note: orig. a handful of candied peel

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: The day before, pour a small glass of food-grade rectified spirit over a pinch of saffron and leave it to release its golden colour.
Make a starter from 125 g of flour, a glass of warm milk and the yeast, and leave it in a warm place to rise.
Beat the yolks with the sugar until pale. Once the starter begins to rise, add the remaining flour, beaten yolks, salt and saffron infusion.
Knead until the dough comes cleanly away from your hands, then pour in the melted warm butter, add the raisins and the candied orange peel, and knead smooth.
Turn it into a buttered, crumbed tin, leave it to rise to 2 fingers below the rim, and bake at 180 °C for about 50 minutes.

name: Baba parzona (scalded yeast babka)
summary: A traditional old Polish yeast babka scalded with boiling milk, rich in yolks, clarified butter, vanilla and grated lemon zest.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka for scalding, plus 3 szklanki for the dough (ok. 600 g)

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of boiling milk for scalding, plus about 50 ml of warm milk for the yeast

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 20 deka for the dough i 1 łyżka for the vanilla

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a few grated bitter almonds

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Scald a glass of sifted flour with a glass of boiling milk and beat hard so no lumps form, then cool it slightly.
When the dough has cooled, add the yeast dissolved in warm milk and the well-beaten yolks, mix, and leave the starter in a warm place to rise.
When the starter has cracked, add 3 glasses of flour and beat for 40 minutes, then add the sugar, salt, grated bitter almonds, vanilla, grated lemon zest and the clarified butter.
Knead until the dough comes cleanly away from your hands, then fill a buttered, crumbed tin to 1/3 of its height.
Leave it in the warm until it has risen almost to the rim, then bake at 180 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Baba rodzynkowa (raisin yeast babka)
summary: A rich Easter yeast babka with three kinds of raisin (large, sultanas and currants), ground almonds and yolks.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo for the starter, plus another a quarter kilo for the dough

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Make a starter from 250 g of flour, a glass of warm milk and the yeast, and leave it in the warm to rise.
Beat the yolks with the sugar until pale. Blanch the almonds, peel them and grind them. Rinse the raisins, dry them, and dust them with flour so they do not clump.
When the starter is moving, add the remaining 250 g of flour, the beaten yolks and the salt, and knead for about 30 minutes.
Pour in the melted warm butter, add the raisins and the ground almonds, mix well, and turn the dough into a buttered, crumbed tin, filling it to 1/3 of its height.
When the dough has risen almost to the top, bake in an oven heated to 180 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Baba tarta (large yeast babka)
summary: A large batch of the classic Easter yeast babka, with 15 yolks, clarified butter and whipped whites, baked until golden.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 80 deka for the starter, plus 80 deka for the dough

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of warm clarified butter

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tins

steps: Make a starter from 800 g of flour, a glass of warm milk and the yeast, and leave it in a warm place to rise.
Beat 15 yolks with 400 g of sugar until pale.
When the starter is moving, add the beaten yolks, the warm clarified butter, the salt and the remaining 800 g of flour, and knead the dough well.
At the end, fold in the stiff foam of 15 whites.
Divide the dough between two large buttered, crumbed tins and bake at 175 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Baba migdałowa drożdżowa (almond yeast babka)
summary: A delicate Easter yeast babka made from a loose batter with ground almonds, egg yolks, melted butter and whipped egg whites, beaten with a wooden spoon.

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Blanch the almonds, peel them, dry them, and grind them.
Make a starter from the flour, a glass of warm milk and the yeast, and leave it in a warm place to rise.
Add the yolks beaten with the sugar until fluffy, the melted butter and the salt, and beat the dough with a wooden spoon for 30 minutes. It is too soft to knead by hand.
Add the ground almonds and mix thoroughly, then gently fold in 3 egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Turn it at once into a buttered, crumbed tin, leave it covered in the warm to rise, and bake at 175 °C for about 45 minutes.

name: Baba petynetowa (light yeast babka beaten over hot water)
summary: An unusually fluffy, light yeast babka beaten over a water bath, with a great many yolks, cream, clarified butter and vanilla.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 20 deka for the yolks and 1 łyżka for the vanilla

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Place a bowl in a pan of hot water to form a water bath, then beat 20 yolks with the sugar in the bowl until very pale and thick.
Add the yeast dissolved in warm cream, the sifted flour, the salt and the pounded vanilla, and beat the dough steadily for 30 minutes.
Pour in the clarified butter and beat for another 30 minutes, then leave the bowl in a warm place to rise.
Turn the dough into a warmed, buttered, crumbed tin, filling it to 1/3 of its height, and leave it to rise almost to the rim.
Bake in an oven heated to 175 °C for about 45 minutes. Take it out very carefully, or this light babka will fall.

name: Baba czekoladowa z mąką chlebową (chocolate cake with finely ground breadcrumbs)
summary: A dark, moist Easter cake made with melted chocolate, grated wholemeal bread, potato starch and vanilla, lightened with whipped egg whites.

ingredients.name: finely ground wholemeal breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. half a szklanka of dried grated wholemeal bread

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. half a szklanka of potato starch

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 20 deka for the yolks and 5 deka for the vanilla

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Mix the sifted, finely ground dried wholemeal breadcrumbs with the potato starch.
Beat the yolks with 200 g of sugar until pale, add the chocolate melted over gentle heat and the vanilla pounded with the rest of the sugar, and beat to a smooth mass.
Whip the whites to a stiff foam.
Carefully fold the whipped egg whites into the chocolate mixture, gradually sprinkling in the mixture of finely ground breadcrumbs and potato starch a spoonful at a time.
Turn the batter into a buttered, crumbed tin and bake at 170 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Baba cytrynowa (lemon sponge cake)
summary: A light, refreshing Easter cake made with whole boiled lemons, beaten egg yolks, whipped egg whites, wheat flour and potato starch.

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Boil the whole lemons in water until soft, so a straw slips in easily. Halve them, discard the seeds, and grind the flesh and peel to an even mass.
Beat the lemon mass with the icing sugar in a bowl, and when it is smooth add 15 yolks one at a time, beating in one direction until pale and fluffy.
Whip the whites to a stiff foam.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the lemon-yolk mixture, alternating with the sifted wheat flour and potato starch and mixing lightly with a spoon.
Pour the batter into a buttered, crumbed baba tin and bake at 170 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Baba makowa (poppy-seed sponge cake)
summary: A fluffy Easter cake made with finely ground dry poppy seeds, egg yolks, almond flavouring, potato starch and whipped egg whites.

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a few bitter almonds, or a few drops of almond oil

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: orig. half a szklanka of potato starch (about 80 g)

ingredients.name: butter and breadcrumbs for the tin

steps: Grind the dry poppy seed twice in a mill to a very fine dust.
Beat 15 yolks with the sugar and the grated bitter almonds to a fluffy, pale mass.
Add the poppy seed to the beaten yolks and keep beating until the mass turns pale and clearly lightens.
Add the potato starch and stiffly beaten egg whites, folding gently with a spoon from the bottom upwards.
Turn it at once into a buttered, crumbed tin and bake at 175 °C for about 60 minutes.

name: Placek pomarańczowy (Layered candied-orange Easter yeast cake)
summary: Rich Easter yeast cake made with milk, eggs, and clarified butter, flavoured with lemon and orange zest, layered in baking tins with orange slices candied in syrup, and glazed with thick syrup.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 4 szklanki (640 g) for the sponge, plus about 360 g for kneading the dough

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.note: large thick-skinned: grated zest of 2 oranges for the dough, and all 3 sliced for the syrup

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag, for the orange syrup

steps: Bring 500 ml of milk to a boil, cool until lukewarm, mix with 640 g of plain wheat flour and the yeast dissolved in a little of the lukewarm milk, cover with a cloth, and set in a warm place to rise.

Once the sponge has risen, add a teaspoon of salt, four eggs beaten with 300 g of sugar, the melted clarified butter, and the remaining flour (about 360 g), kneading a soft dough until it pulls away from the hand; finally work in the grated zest of the lemon and two oranges and set aside for a second rise.

Cut the three thick-skinned oranges into thin slices with the peel on, remove the pips, and simmer in a syrup made from 400 g of sugar and 500 ml of water until translucent, then drain on a sieve (reserving the syrup).
Layer the risen dough into two tins greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, alternating layers of dough with slices of candied orange and finishing with a layer of dough on top.

Set the tins in a warm place for a third rise, then bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 35–40 minutes; meanwhile boil down the reserved orange syrup until thick and brush it over the hot cakes immediately upon removing them from the oven.

name: Placek kruchy z serem (Traditional Polish shortcrust Easter cheesecake)
summary: Classic Polish Easter sernik on a par-baked shortcrust pastry base topped with a kilogram of quark beaten with seven egg yolks, sugar, clarified butter, vanilla, currants, rum, and whipped egg whites.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo of rich butter

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo, for the pastry

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo, for the cheese filling

ingredients.name: Zante currants
ingredients.note: orig. 1 handful of small dark raisins

steps: Knead a shortcrust pastry from 500 g of plain wheat flour, 250 g of butter, and 250 g of sugar, roll out thinly, line a large shallow baking sheet, chill for 60 minutes, and par-bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 15 minutes until lightly golden.

Pass the well-pressed quark through a mincer, add 250 g of sugar, seven egg yolks, melted clarified butter, pounded vanilla, grated lemon zest, and a few drops of almond oil, and beat together until smooth and fluffy.
Fold a handful of currants, a kieliszek of rum or arrack, and the stiffly beaten whites of seven eggs into the cheese mixture.

Spread the cheese mixture in a thick layer over the par-baked shortcrust base and bake in an oven preheated to 175 °C for 60 minutes; after removing from the oven, you may glaze the top with thin punch icing.

name: Placek z marmoladą (Shortcrust fruit-jam and almond meringue sheet cake)
summary: Crumbly Easter shortcrust sheet cake spread after baking with a thick layer of fruit jam and topped with a meringue made from six egg whites and sprinkled with toasted almonds.

ingredients.name: fruit jam
ingredients.note: apple, plum, apricot, gooseberry, or raspberry

steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from the plain wheat flour, butter, and sugar, roll out thinly, fit into a shallow baking sheet, and chill in the refrigerator for 60 minutes.
Transfer the chilled pastry to an oven preheated to 180 °C, bake for about 20 minutes until lightly golden, and cool completely.
Spread the cooled shortcrust base with a thick layer of the chosen fruit jam.

Whip the six egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in the icing sugar, spread the meringue over the jam layer, scatter with chopped toasted almonds, and dry in a very low oven (about 120 °C) for about 60 minutes until crisp like meringue.

name: Klasyczny tort wiedeński z konfiturą malinową (Viennese four-layer butter torte with raspberry jam)
summary: A traditional four-layer torte of long-beaten butter-and-egg batter flavoured with bitter almonds, baked in four thin rounds, filled with raspberry preserves, and iced with lemon fondant.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag, plus a little for greasing the paper

ingredients.name: raspberry preserves or redcurrant jelly
ingredients.note: for filling the layers and garnishing

steps: Beat 400 g of butter until fluffy, add 400 g of icing sugar, and beat in 8 egg yolks one at a time, stirring in one direction until the mixture doubles in volume.

Add 20 scalded, peeled, and finely pounded bitter almonds, and gradually beat in 400 g of plain flour a few spoonfuls at a time, beating thoroughly (about 15–20 minutes with a mixer; historically an hour by hand).
Beat the 8 egg whites until stiff and fold gently into the batter.
Spread the batter over 4 buttered rounds of baking paper the size of a large plate and bake in a moderately warm oven (about 170 °C); peel off the paper immediately after removing from the oven.
