Sandwich the baked rounds with a thin layer of raspberry preserves or redcurrant jelly, ice the top with lemon fondant, dry for a few minutes in a warm oven, and garnish with preserves drained of syrup.

name: Tort piaskowy przekładany marmoladą (sand cake torte with plum or apricot jam)
summary: A beaten sand torte made from ten whole eggs and ten additional yolks with clarified butter, plain flour, and potato starch, filled with plum or apricot jam and iced with punch fondant.

ingredients.name: clarified butter
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag, plus a little butter for the tin

steps: Beat 400 g of sugar with 10 whole eggs until pale, then add 10 egg yolks one at a time along with 400 g of cooled clarified butter a spoonful at a time.
Once the mixture has risen and turned pale, stir in 200 g of plain flour and 200 g of potato starch and mix thoroughly.
Transfer the batter to a cake tin greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and bake in a moderately warm oven (about 165–170 °C) for about 50–60 minutes.
Once completely cooled, slice the torte horizontally in half and sandwich with plum or apricot jam.
Ice the top of the torte with punch fondant and dry for a few minutes in a warm oven.

name: Tort czekoladowy z masą migdałowo-likierową (chocolate almond torte with maraschino almond cream)
summary: A gluten-free chocolate-and-almond torte made with ten eggs, sliced into three layers and filled with a beaten mixture of blanched almonds, sugar syrup, lemon juice, and maraschino liqueur.

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.note: piece of pod pounded with sugar

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo, ground with their skins

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo, scalded, peeled, and ground

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo, for the syrup

ingredients.name: maraschino liqueur or crème de cacao

steps: Beat 10 egg yolks with 250 g of icing sugar, then add 250 g of grated chocolate, the vanilla pounded with sugar, and 250 g of almonds ground with their skins.
Beat the 10 egg whites until stiff, fold gently into the chocolate mixture, transfer to a cake tin greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and bake at 170 °C for about 45–50 minutes.
Leave the torte until the next day to cool completely, then slice it with a sharp knife into 3 equal layers.
Boil a light syrup from 250 g of sugar and 250 ml of water, pour it over 250 g of scalded, peeled, and ground almonds, and beat in a bowl until smooth.
Squeeze the juice of a whole lemon into the almond mixture and pour in 50 ml of maraschino or cocoa liqueur.
Sandwich the three layers of the torte with the prepared almond mixture, ice the top with chocolate fondant, and let stand for 6 hours before serving so the cake absorbs the aroma of the filling.

name: Podłużny tort czekoladowy łatwy do krojenia (oblong chocolate almond loaf torte)
summary: An oblong chocolate torte baked in a loaf tin from ten eggs and breadcrumbs, iced with chocolate fondant and studded thickly with slivers of sweet almonds.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka for the batter plus a little for dusting the tin

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: cut into thin slivers for studding the top

steps: Beat 10 egg yolks with 250 g of icing sugar until pale, add 250 g of melted chocolate, and continue beating until the mixture visibly increases in volume.
Stir in 250 ml (1 szklanka) of breadcrumbs and a few finely pounded bitter almonds, then gently fold in the stiffly beaten whites from the 10 eggs.
Transfer the batter to an oblong loaf tin greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and bake in a moderately warm oven (about 165–170 °C) for about 45–50 minutes.
Unmould the cake, let it cool completely, ice with chocolate fondant, and stud thickly with sweet almonds cut into thin slivers.

name: Tort aleksandryjski (Alexandrian shortcrust layer torte)
summary: A three-layer torte of deeply browned shortcrust rounds filled with cooked vanilla cream and butter, finished with punch fondant or apricot jam and toasted almonds.
steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from 500 g of plain flour, 400 g of butter, and 400 g of sugar, and chill it in a cool place for about 30–40 minutes.
Divide the dough into 3 equal parts, roll each out into a plate-sized round, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C until deeply golden brown.
In a saucepan, mix 375 ml of whipping cream or milk, 125 ml of sugar, the vanilla pounded with sugar, 100 g of sweet-cream butter, 2 eggs, and a tablespoon of plain flour.
Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened without letting it come to a boil, then remove from the heat and continue beating until it cools slightly.
Spread the cream over two of the baked rounds, stack them, and top with the third layer.
Coat the entire torte with punch fondant or apricot jam and sprinkle with coarsely chopped, lightly toasted almonds.

name: Tort z orzechów włoskich z pomadką kawową (walnut torte with almond-walnut cream and coffee fondant)
summary: A two-layer torte made from walnuts and sixteen eggs, filled with a rich cooked walnut-and-almond cream enriched with heavy cream and butter, and iced with coffee fondant.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for the batter plus extra for dusting the tins

ingredients.name: walnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 10 dag ground for the cream plus halves for garnishing

ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a filiżanka of thick sweet cream

steps: Grind 400 g of shelled walnuts in a nut mill.
Beat 16 egg yolks with 400 g of icing sugar, add the ground walnuts and 4 tablespoons of breadcrumbs, beat thoroughly, and gently fold in the stiffly beaten whites from the 16 eggs.
Divide the batter between two cake tins greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and bake at 170 °C for about 35–40 minutes.

Prepare the cream: mix 100 g of ground almonds, 100 g of ground walnuts, 200 g of icing sugar, 2 whole eggs, 100 g of butter, and 75 ml (half a filiżanka) of thick sweet cream, then heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened without letting it boil.
Sandwich the cooled cake layers with the prepared cream, ice the top with coffee fondant, and garnish with walnut halves.

name: Torcik z orzechów laskowych na opłatku (hazelnut wafer torte)
summary: An Easter torte of two wafer rounds spread with a hazelnut-meringue mixture and baked, sandwiched with hazelnut buttercream, and finished with clear fondant icing.

ingredients.name: wafer sheets
ingredients.note: rounds the size of a plate

ingredients.name: hazelnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 10 dag, ground for the cream

steps: Beat 4 eggs with 400 g of sugar until pale, then mix in 400 g of ground hazelnuts.
Spread the hazelnut mixture over 2 plate-sized wafer rounds and bake in a moderately warm oven (about 160–170 °C) for about 25–30 minutes.
Beat 100 g of sweet-cream butter until fluffy, add 100 g of icing sugar, 100 g of ground hazelnuts, and 2 eggs, and beat until smooth.
Sandwich the cooled wafer rounds with the prepared hazelnut cream.
Ice the top of the torte with clear fondant and garnish with toasted hazelnuts.

name: Tort hiszpański bezowy z bitą śmietaną (Spanish tiered meringue and whipped cream torte)
summary: A tiered torte of six progressively smaller meringue discs made from fifteen egg whites, layered an hour before serving with vanilla whipped cream and garnished with preserves, candied peel, and chocolates.
steps: Beat 15 egg whites until very stiff and fold in 400 g of icing sugar.
Cut 6 progressively smaller rounds from oiled baking paper, spread the meringue mixture over them, and smooth with a knife.
Dry the meringue rounds in a very low oven (about 100–110 °C) for about 2 hours until completely dry, then cool and carefully peel off the paper.
An hour before serving, whip 1 l of sweet heavy cream and fold in 250 g of icing sugar pounded with vanilla.
Place the largest meringue round on a platter, cover with whipped cream, and stack the remaining rounds in decreasing order with whipped cream between each layer, covering the top round as well.
Garnish the torte with preserves drained of syrup, candied citrus peel, and small chocolates, and serve shortly after assembly.

name: Tort kawowy „Mocca” (Mocha coffee buttercream sponge torte)
summary: A classic four-layer twelve-egg sponge torte made with wheat flour and potato starch, filled and decorated with a thick buttercream made from egg yolks whisked over steam with strong coffee and sweet-cream butter.

ingredients.name: egg yolks
ingredients.note: or 5 egg yolks and 2 tablespoons plain flour in the economical version

ingredients.name: strong black coffee
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of freshly brewed coffee without chicory

steps: Beat 12 egg yolks with 400 g of icing sugar until pale, then fold in a spoonful at a time a mixture of 100 g of potato starch and 150 g of plain flour, alternating with the stiffly beaten whites from the 12 eggs.
Transfer the batter to a cake tin greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, bake in a low oven (about 160–165 °C) for about 45–50 minutes, and leave until the next day.
The next day, slice the sponge horizontally with a very sharp knife into 4 equal layers.
Whisk 10 egg yolks with 200 g of sugar and 250 ml of very strong coffee over low heat until thickened (taking care that the yolks do not curdle), then let cool.
Beat 300 g of sweet-cream butter until fluffy and gradually beat in the cooled coffee custard.
Spread three sponge layers with the cream, cover with the fourth, coat the top and sides of the torte with the remaining cream, pipe decorative rosettes on top, and chill for 2 hours before serving.

name: Tort morelowy na biszkopcie (apricot jam and liqueur sponge torte)
summary: A three-layer torte on a twelve-egg sponge cake, soaked with abricotine apricot liqueur, filled and coated with apricot jam, and garnished with whole preserved apricots.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: per recipe no. 18 in the same book
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.note: per recipe no. 18 in the same book
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: per recipe no. 18 in the same book
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.group: Sponge cake per the Mocha torte recipe

ingredients.name: apricot jam
ingredients.note: for filling and coating the top and sides

steps: Bake a sponge cake as for the Mocha coffee torte: beat 12 egg yolks with 400 g of icing sugar, gently fold in 100 g of potato starch, 150 g of plain flour, and the stiffly beaten whites from the 12 eggs, transfer to a tin greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and bake at 160–165 °C for about 45–50 minutes.
Leave the baked sponge until the next day, then slice it horizontally into 3 equal layers.
Sprinkle each sponge layer with 30 ml of abricotine apricot liqueur, spread thinly with apricot jam, and stack together.
Coat the top and sides of the torte with the same apricot jam and garnish with whole apricots from preserves or compote.

name: Tort makaronikowy z kratką migdałową i konfiturami (almond macaroon lattice torte)
summary: An Easter almond-meringue macaroon torte baked on a wafer round with a piped macaroon rim and lattice, finished in the lattice squares with lemon fondant and drained fruit preserves.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag, scalded, peeled, dried, and ground

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: orig. a dozen or so, scalded, peeled, and ground

ingredients.name: lemon fondant
ingredients.note: for filling the spaces between the lattice

steps: Scald 400 g of sweet almonds and a dozen or so bitter almonds with boiling water, peel, dry thoroughly, and grind in a mill, then mix on a board with 300 g of icing sugar and divide into two equal parts.

Beat 15 egg whites until stiff. Combine half of the almonds with half of the beaten whites, spread in an even layer over a large wafer round placed on a flour-dusted baking sheet, and bake in a low oven (about 140 °C) until lightly golden.
Remove the parbaked base and let it cool slightly. Re-whip the remaining egg whites until stiff, mix with the remaining almonds, and fashion a decorative rim and lattice over the baked round.
Return the torte to a low oven (about 120–130 °C) so the lattice colours lightly and dries like a meringue, then remove and cool completely.
Fill the spaces between the lattice bars with lemon fondant and garnish with fruit preserves drained of syrup.

name: Torcik migdałowy na opłatkach (No-bake almond cream wafer torte)
summary: No-bake torte made from six round wafer sheets layered with a cream of butter, egg yolks, icing sugar, and ground almonds, weighted until firm and coated with cooked chocolate fondant.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched and finely ground, orig. 20 dag

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: blanched and finely ground, orig. several almonds

steps: Finely grind the blanched sweet and bitter almonds in a nut mill.
Beat the softened butter until creamy, and in a separate bowl beat the three egg yolks with the icing sugar until pale, then combine both mixtures with the ground almonds.

Spread five of the wafer sheets thinly with the almond cream, stack them one on top of another, cover with the sixth wafer sheet, weight down with a small board, and leave in a cool place for about 3 hours until firm.
Glaze the firm torte with boiled chocolate fondant.

name: Mazurek oszczędny (Economical egg-yolk and raisin Easter mazurek)
summary: Tender, crumbly Easter mazurek made from butter beaten with icing sugar and eight egg yolks, with bitter almonds, wheat flour, potato starch, and two handfuls of raisins.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 20 dag, or 300 g for a sweeter cake

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: orig. on the tip of a knife

ingredients.name: bicarbonate of soda
ingredients.note: orig. on the tip of a knife

steps: Beat the softened butter until creamy, add the icing sugar and eight egg yolks, and continue beating until light and fluffy.
Add the finely pounded bitter almonds, pinch of salt, pinch of bicarbonate of soda, plain wheat flour, potato starch, and both kinds of raisins.
Knead thoroughly into a smooth dough, roll out to a thickness of about 1 cm, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 20–25 minutes until golden brown.

name: Mazurek bakaliowy na białkach (Meringue dried-fruit Easter cake)
summary: Light meringue Easter mazurek baked on a wafer sheet with eight stiffly whipped egg whites, icing sugar, sliced dried figs, currants, and candied citrus peel, slowly dried in a cool oven.

ingredients.name: dried figs
ingredients.note: cut into strips, orig. a quarter kilo

ingredients.name: candied lemon or orange peel
ingredients.note: cut into fine strips, orig. a few pieces

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for dusting the baking sheet under the wafer

steps: Cut the dried figs and candied lemon or orange peel into thin strips and pick over the currants.
Whip the eight egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in the icing sugar, and gently mix in the prepared dried fruit.
Lay the wafer sheet on a flour-dusted baking sheet and spread the meringue-and-fruit mixture over it in an even layer.
Place the mazurek in a very low oven (about 120–130 °C) and dry for about 2 hours until lightly golden on top and thoroughly crisp.

name: Mazurek migdałowy na białkach (Almond meringue Easter mazurek on wafer)
summary: Macaroon-style Easter mazurek on a wafer sheet, made from eight stiffly beaten egg whites, icing sugar, and finely ground almonds, decorated with strips of candied orange peel and slowly dried in the oven.

ingredients.name: candied orange or lemon peel
ingredients.note: cut into strips for decorating the top

steps: Blanch the almonds in boiling water, peel, dry lightly without browning, and grind finely in a nut mill.
Whip the eight egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold in the icing sugar and ground almonds.
Spread the mixture in an even layer over the prepared wafer sheet and decorate the top with strips of candied orange or lemon peel.
Place in a low oven (about 130–140 °C) for about 60 minutes so the mazurek dries slowly and turns only faintly golden on top.

name: Mazurek cytrynowy (Whole-lemon Easter mazurek cake)
summary: Delicate Easter mazurek made without wheat flour from two whole boiled and puréed lemons, six eggs, icing sugar, and potato starch, finished with a thin coat of lemon fondant.

ingredients.name: sugar cubes
ingredients.note: several cubes for rubbing the zest from the lemons

steps: Rub the yellow zest off two washed lemons using sugar cubes and crush the cubes to a powder, then boil the lemons whole in water until completely soft (about 25 minutes).
Cut open the boiled lemons, discard the pips, and pass the pulp and peel through a mincer or sieve.
Combine the puréed lemons with the icing sugar and beat, adding the egg yolks one by one along with the potato starch and the crushed lemon-zest sugar.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, fold gently into the lemon mixture, and spread into a shallow tray (about 21 × 34 cm) lined with paper greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs.
Bake in a low oven (about 150–160 °C) for about 50 minutes until baked through and slightly dried out, then glaze thinly with lemon or punch fondant once cool.

name: Mazurek królewski (Royal almond butter Easter mazurek)
summary: Classic royal Easter mazurek with a crumbly, sandy texture, made from butter beaten with icing sugar, eight egg yolks, ground almonds, and wheat flour, and decorated with whole almonds.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag (400 g) for the batter plus about 1 tbsp for greasing the mould

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 15 dag (150 g) blanched and finely grated for the batter plus about 50 g whole for decorating the top

steps: Beat 400 g of softened butter with the icing sugar, adding the eight egg yolks one at a time, until the mixture turns pale and fluffy.
Stir in 150 g of blanched, finely ground sweet almonds and 10 ground bitter almonds, continuing to beat.
Fold in the sifted dry plain wheat flour, mix thoroughly, and spread the batter into a shallow tray lined with paper greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs.
Stud the top with whole sweet almonds and bake in a moderate oven (about 175 °C) for about 30–35 minutes; once cooled, you may glaze the mazurek with boiled chocolate icing or translucent fondant.

name: Mazurek czekoladowy pospolity (Everyday chocolate and breadcrumb Easter mazurek)
summary: Light, flourless chocolate Easter mazurek baked from eight eggs beaten with sugar, grated vanilla chocolate, and fine breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. 20 dag (200 g) for the batter plus about 1 tbsp for dusting the mould

steps: Beat the eight egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Stir in the grated chocolate and 200 g of breadcrumbs.
Whip the eight egg whites to stiff peaks and fold carefully into the chocolate mixture.
Transfer the batter to a paper-lined tray greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, bake in a moderate oven (about 165 °C) for about 35–40 minutes, and dry slightly at the end.

name: Mazurek w zimnej wodzie podchodzący (Water-risen yeast Easter mazurek)
summary: Traditional yeast mazurek whose dough is submerged overnight in cold water in a cloth, kneaded in the morning with sugar and cardamom or mace, and baked with almonds and raisins.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 15 dag, kneaded in after the dough rises in water

steps: In the evening, knead a smooth dough from the plain wheat flour, crumbled fresh yeast, butter, four egg yolks, and a szklanka of lukewarm milk, working it until it comes away cleanly from your hands.
Wrap the dough loosely in a clean, damp cloth, leaving enough extra space for it to double in volume, and submerge it overnight in a vessel of cold water.

In the morning, once the risen dough has floated to the surface, unwrap it from the cloth, add 150 g of sugar and a pinch of mace or cardamom, knead thoroughly again, and let rise a second time at room temperature (for about 60 minutes).

Roll the dough out thinly on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, scatter generously with slivered almonds, raisins, and coarse crystal sugar, and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 20–25 minutes.

name: Mazurek makowy (Poppy-seed shortcrust Easter mazurek)
summary: Crumbly shortcrust Easter mazurek made with plenty of dry poppy seeds, wheat flour, butter, eggs, and sour cream, scented with almond flavouring and sprinkled with coarse granulated sugar before baking.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 2 for the dough plus 1 for brushing the top

ingredients.name: sour cream 18%
ingredients.note: enough to bind the dough smoothly

steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from the poppy seeds, plain wheat flour, butter, two eggs, three drops of almond or lemon oil, and enough sour cream to make the dough smooth and workable.
Roll the dough out on a baking sheet to a thickness of about 1.5 cm (finger-thick).
Brush the top with beaten egg, sprinkle generously with coarse crystal sugar, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 25–30 minutes.

name: Mazurek cygański (Gypsy-style fruit and almond Easter cake)
summary: Simple, fruit-laden Easter mazurek beaten from whole eggs, sugar, and wheat flour with generous amounts of sultanas, currants, and unblanched slivered almonds.

ingredients.name: unblanched almonds
ingredients.note: cut into thin strips with skins on, orig. 2 filiżanki

steps: Beat the five whole eggs with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Fold in the dry plain wheat flour, sultanas, currants, thinly slivered unblanched almonds, and optional candied citrus peel, mixing thoroughly.
Spread the batter evenly into a paper-lined baking tray greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30–35 minutes; serve plain or glazed with translucent punch icing.

name: Mazurek różany (Rose-petal jam layered shortcrust Easter mazurek)
summary: Double-layered shortcrust Easter mazurek sandwiched with rose-petal preserves, glazed with pink lemon fondant made with rosewater, and scattered with chopped almonds or green pistachios.

ingredients.name: lemon fondant icing made with rosewater
ingredients.note: tinted with a few drops of pink food colouring

ingredients.name: almonds or pistachios
ingredients.note: coarsely chopped, for sprinkling the top

steps: Knead a shortcrust dough from the plain wheat flour, butter, sugar, and two tablespoons of thick sour cream, then chill in a cool place or refrigerator for about 2 hours.
Divide the chilled dough into two portions, roll out into two thin sheets, and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 20–25 minutes until deeply golden.
Sandwich the baked layers with the rose-petal preserves.
Spread the top with pink lemon fondant prepared with rosewater and scatter with coarsely chopped almonds or green pistachios.

name: Mazurek czekoladowy gotowany (Boiled chocolate and almond fudge mazurek)
summary: Rich, candy-like no-bake Easter mazurek boiled in sugar syrup from finely grated sweet almonds, vanilla chocolate, butter, and a spoonful of wild strawberry or strawberry preserves, poured onto a wafer sheet.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched and finely grated, orig. 40 dag

steps: Boil a thick syrup from the sugar and a szklanka of water in a saucepan, as for fruit preserves.
Stir in the finely grated sweet almonds and cook briefly over low heat, then add the broken chocolate, generous tablespoon of butter, and large tablespoon of wild strawberry or strawberry preserves.
Cook everything over low heat, stirring constantly from the bottom so the mixture does not scorch.

Once it begins to thicken, drop a few drops onto a cold saucer — when a drop holds its shape and does not stick to the fingers, pour the mixture into a wafer-lined tray and leave for about 2 hours to set.

name: Mazurek „Dzień i noc” (Day and Night marzipan and chocolate fudge Easter cake)
summary: Two-layer no-bake Easter mazurek with pale homemade rosewater marzipan on a wafer sheet and a thick layer of dark chocolate-and-cream fondant.

ingredients.name: rosewater
ingredients.note: added a little at a time to knead a smooth marzipan

ingredients.name: communion-style wafer sheet
ingredients.note: large sheet for lining the mould

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag (400 g) plus 1 tbsp (15 g) for pounding with the vanilla

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.note: piece of pod pounded with a tablespoon of sugar

steps: Blanch the almonds in boiling water, slip off the skins, dry thoroughly in a cloth, and grind finely in an almond mill or on a fine grater.
Mix the ground almonds thoroughly with the icing sugar and knead, adding rosewater a little at a time, until a smooth marzipan paste forms.
Press the marzipan in an even layer into a shallow tray formed from a wafer sheet.
Combine the grated chocolate, sugar, vanilla pounded with a tablespoon of sugar, and thick whipping cream in a saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring frequently to prevent scorching.

Once the fudge begins to thicken, test by dropping a little onto a cold saucer — if it holds its shape and does not stick to the fingers, pour it over the marzipan layer and leave until the next day to set completely before slicing.

name: Mazurek orzechowy na miodzie (Honey, walnut and almond nougat Easter mazurek)
summary: Nougat-style Easter mazurek on wafer sheets, made from slivered walnuts, hazelnuts, and almonds toasted in honey and sugar, then cooked with the stiffly beaten whites of twelve eggs.

ingredients.name: walnuts and hazelnuts
ingredients.note: shelled and cut into strips, orig. 80 dag

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for dusting the baking sheets under the wafers

steps: Cut the shelled walnuts, hazelnuts, and almonds into thin strips.

Heat the honey and sugar without water in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan; once lightly caramelized, tip in the walnuts, hazelnuts, and almonds and toast together over low heat, stirring so they do not burn.

Whip the 12 egg whites to stiff peaks, spoon them into the hot honey-nut mixture, and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the foam first puffs up high and then subsides slightly and thickens.
Spread the mixture in a layer about 2.5 cm thick over wafer sheets laid on flour-dusted baking sheets and set in a moderate oven (about 160 °C) for 15–20 minutes until lightly golden.

name: Mazurek prababek (Great-grandmothers' no-bake chocolate, almond and rye-crumb mazurek)
summary: Traditional Polish mazurek requiring no baking or cooking, made from sweet-cream butter, grated vanilla chocolate, icing sugar, roasted almonds, and sifted wholemeal rye breadcrumbs, sandwiched between wafer sheets.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: roasted until golden and finely ground, orig. 40 dag

ingredients.name: grated dark wholemeal rye bread
ingredients.note: dried, pounded, and sifted through the finest sieve

ingredients.name: whipping cream 30%
ingredients.note: optional, if the mixture is too dry

ingredients.name: communion-style wafer sheets
ingredients.note: for the bottom and top of two mazureks

steps: Beat the softened butter in a grinding bowl or mixing bowl with the grated chocolate, icing sugar, golden-roasted and finely ground almonds, and finely sifted rye breadcrumbs (if the mixture is too dry, add 2 tablespoons of thick whipping cream).
Spread the mixture in a layer about 1.5 cm thick (finger-thick) over two wafer sheets and cover the tops with two more wafer sheets.
Weight the mazureks down with a small board and weight, chill in a cool place or refrigerator for at least 4 hours, and bring to the table just before serving.

name: Mazurek z gotowanych żółtek (Hard-boiled egg yolk shortbread Easter mazurek)
summary: Exceptionally tender, crumbly Easter mazurek made from twelve hard-boiled egg yolks beaten at length in a grinding bowl with butter, icing sugar, four raw eggs, a small glass of rum, and wheat flour, then glazed the next day with punch fondant.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo (250 g) sweet-cream butter for the dough plus about 1 tbsp for greasing the mould

ingredients.name: punch or lemon fondant icing
ingredients.note: for glazing the top the day after baking

steps: Grind the 12 hard-boiled egg yolks to a smooth paste in a grinding bowl with a wooden pestle.
Add 250 g of softened butter, the icing sugar, finely grated lemon zest, and four whole raw eggs, beating until the mixture becomes fluffy and doubles in volume.
Pour in a kieliszek of rum or arrack, add the dry plain wheat flour, and beat for about another 30 minutes, or less time with a stand mixer.

Transfer the mixture to a tin lined with buttered paper dusted with breadcrumbs, smooth the top, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30–35 minutes. The next day, once completely cool, carefully remove the tin and coat the mazurek thickly with punch or lemon fondant.

name: Mazurek migdałowy kruchy (Tender almond and hard-boiled egg yolk Easter mazurek)
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth flourless almond mazurek made from twelve hard-boiled egg yolks ground with blanched almonds, icing sugar, and two raw eggs, glazed with lemon or chocolate fondant.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched, peeled, and ground, orig. 40 dag

ingredients.name: bitter almonds
ingredients.note: blanched, peeled, and ground, orig. a dozen or so

steps: Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds in boiling water, slip off the skins, dry thoroughly, and grind finely in a nut mill.
Mash and grind the hard-boiled egg yolks by themselves in a grinding bowl, then gradually work in the icing sugar, ground almonds, and finally the two whole raw eggs until smooth.
Spread the mixture in a thin layer over a sheet of baking paper greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs.
Bake in a moderate oven (about 165 °C) for about 30–35 minutes, and once cooled, glaze with lemon or chocolate fondant.

name: Mazurek rodzynkowy kruchy (Shortcrust currant and almond Easter mazurek)
summary: Rich shortcrust Easter mazurek made with ten egg yolks, butter, and sweet cream, generously studded with currants, chopped almonds, and candied citrus peel, topped with coarse crystal sugar and slivered almonds.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 20 dag (200 g) for the dough plus about 1 tbsp for greasing the baking sheet

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: orig. 10 dag (100 g) finely chopped for the dough plus about 50 g slivered for the top

steps: Knead a soft shortcrust dough from the plain wheat flour, icing sugar, ten egg yolks, 200 g of butter, and two tablespoons of thick sweet cream.
Work in the currants, 100 g of finely chopped sweet almonds, several chopped bitter almonds, and the candied orange and lemon peel until evenly distributed through the dough.
Press the dough out onto a buttered baking sheet to a thickness of about 1.5 cm (finger-thick), brush the top with beaten egg, and scatter with coarse crystal sugar and slivered almonds.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30–35 minutes until well browned.

name: Mazurek bakaliowy (Dried-fruit and nut Easter cake)
summary: Rich Easter mazurek baked on wafer sheets, packed with three kinds of raisins, figs, dates, almonds, and candied citrus peel suspended in a fluffy batter of twelve eggs and icing sugar.

ingredients.name: dried figs
ingredients.note: cut into thin strips, orig. 20 dag

ingredients.name: dried dates
ingredients.note: pitted and cut into thin strips, orig. 20 dag

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched and cut into thin slivers, orig. 20 dag

ingredients.name: communion-style wafer sheets
ingredients.note: for the bases of three mazureks

steps: Prepare the dried fruit and nuts: pick over the Malaga raisins, sultanas, and currants, cut the figs, dates, and blanched almonds into thin strips, and finely chop the candied citrus peel.
Beat the 12 egg yolks with the icing sugar until pale and fluffy, then stir in the prepared fruit and nuts.
Whip the 12 egg whites to stiff peaks and fold gently into the fruit mixture.

Spread in a thick layer over three wafer sheets (or par-baked shortcrust bases), bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes until golden, then crack the oven door slightly open and let the cakes dry for another 30 minutes.

name: Mazurek „Toinon” (Layered roasted-almond meringue Easter cake)
summary: Refined Easter mazurek made from two thin roasted-almond meringue layers baked on wafer sheets and sandwiched with a cream of sweet-cream butter, icing sugar, and ground almonds.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched, lightly roasted, and finely ground, orig. 60 dag

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched, roasted, and finely ground, orig. the remaining 20 dag

steps: Lightly roast all the blanched almonds (800 g in total) in a dry pan or oven until golden, grind finely in a nut mill, and divide into two unequal portions: 600 g and 200 g.

Fold 600 g of the ground almonds with 600 g of icing sugar and the stiffly whipped whites of 8 eggs, spread over two wafer sheets, and bake two thin layers in an oven preheated to 160 °C for about 25–30 minutes, then cool.
Beat the softened butter until fluffy and mix with 200 g of icing sugar and the remaining 200 g of ground almonds.
Sandwich the cooled almond layers with the almond buttercream, press under a board and weight, and leave in a cool place overnight so the layers bond firmly.

name: Mazurek „Duchesse” (No-bake chocolate and roasted almond Easter cake)
summary: Exquisite no-bake Easter mazurek of two wafer layers spread with a paste of hard-boiled egg yolks, chocolate, and roasted almonds, sandwiched with almond buttercream and topped with boiled chocolate glaze.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dag, for the chocolate paste

steps: Mash and grind the 12 hard-boiled egg yolks in a grinding bowl with 400 g of icing sugar, 400 g of grated chocolate, and 200 g of ground roasted almonds, working the mixture until it moistens and becomes completely smooth.
Spread the chocolate-almond paste evenly over two matching wafer sheets.
Cream the softened butter (200 g) until fluffy with 200 g of icing sugar and 200 g of ground roasted almonds.
Sandwich the two wafer-backed layers with the almond buttercream, weight down with a small board and weight, and leave in a cool place overnight (about 8 hours).
The next day, boil a glaze from 200 g of sugar, 200 g of chocolate, 125 ml of whipping cream, and a tablespoon of butter; as it begins to thicken, pour it over the mazurek and leave to set.

name: Lukier na białkach (Royal icing)
summary: Glossy white royal icing beaten in a grinding bowl from sifted icing sugar, four fresh egg whites, and strained lemon juice, used for glazing and decorating Easter babkas and sheet cakes.

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: sifted, orig. half a kilo of icing sugar or pounded loaf sugar

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: very fresh, 1–2 more if needed depending on egg size

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of a whole lemon squeezed through a strainer

steps: Tip the sifted icing sugar into a ceramic grinding bowl or mixing bowl, add the four fresh egg whites, and beat in one direction with a wooden pestle until smooth and fluffy (add one more egg white if needed).
Squeeze in the juice of a whole lemon through a fine strainer to make the icing whiter and firmer.
Beat the icing for a long time (about 15–20 minutes by hand or 8–10 minutes with a mixer) until it reaches a spreadable consistency that covers the cake smoothly and dries with a glossy sheen.
Spread the icing over baked babkas or sheet cakes, arrange dried fruit and nuts on the wet glaze, and place the cake in a barely warm oven (about 70–80 °C) for a few minutes to dry the icing.

name: Cooked chocolate icing
summary: A thick, shiny chocolate glaze cooked from grated chocolate, sugar, milk and a little butter, for pouring over babkas and tortes.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a small łyżka of sweet cream butter

steps: Combine the grated chocolate, the sugar, the milk and the butter in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring with a spoon the whole time, until the icing is clearly thicker and has a smooth shine.
While it is still warm and pourable, pour it at once over baked babkas, sheet cakes or tortes.

name: Masa kawowa „Mocca” (Mocha buttercream filling)
summary: Fluffy coffee buttercream beaten from sweet-cream butter, icing sugar, five egg yolks, and a concentrated brew of black coffee.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: softened, orig. a quarter kilo of sweet-cream butter

ingredients.name: strong black coffee
ingredients.note: very strong brew of real coffee without chicory

steps: Beat the softened butter until pale and fluffy.
Continuing to beat, gradually add the icing sugar a tablespoon at a time along with the five egg yolks one by one.
Slowly dribble in four tablespoons of very strong, cooled black coffee and beat until thoroughly combined.

If the mixture begins to curdle and resists absorbing the coffee, set the bowl briefly in a larger vessel of hot water until the emulsion comes together, then remove and continue beating in a cool place until completely cold.

name: Masa ponczowa (Lemon and rum punch cake filling)
summary: Aromatic lemon-and-rum custard filling made from whole eggs beaten with sugar, lemon zest and juice, thickened over heat with a little flour and finished with a small glass of rum or arrack.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: grated zest and squeezed juice of a whole lemon

steps: Beat the four whole eggs with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Add the grated zest and squeezed juice of the whole lemon, a tablespoon of plain wheat flour, and 300 ml of water, then mix thoroughly.
Warm the mixture over low heat, beating constantly, until it thickens noticeably.
Remove the pan from the heat, pour in a kieliszek of rum or arrack, and continue beating until completely cool; before filling the torte, sprinkle the cake layers with an appropriate spirit or syrup.

name: Walnut cream for tortes
summary: A quick filling for walnut and sponge tortes, of whipped thick cream, icing sugar and finely pounded walnuts.
steps: Pound the walnuts finely in a mortar, or grind them.
Whip the thick, chilled cream to a stiff foam.
Fold the icing sugar and the ground walnuts gently into the whipped cream, and use it at once to fill torte layers generously.

name: Butter-Glazed Chestnuts (Kasztany w maśle smażone)
summary: Sweet chestnuts boiled until tender, peeled, and glazed over low heat in unsalted butter and caster sugar, served as an accompaniment to roast poultry.

ingredients.name: fresh sweet chestnuts
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt (enough for a duck or capon; for a turkey, 2–3 funty, or 800–1200 g)

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: orig. a generous quarter funt per 1 funt of chestnuts

ingredients.name: caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter funt of caster sugar per 1 funt of chestnuts

steps: Place the whole, unscored chestnuts in a pot of cold water, salt lightly during cooking, and boil for about 25–30 minutes, as with potatoes, until tender and easy to peel.
Drain the water and carefully peel the warm chestnuts.
Melt the unsalted butter in a saucepan, add the peeled chestnuts, and sprinkle in the caster sugar.
Stir thoroughly and cook over low heat for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the chestnuts are coated in a buttery sugar glaze.
Arrange the hot chestnuts around a roast duck, turkey, or other roast poultry on a serving platter.

name: Pączki kartoflane (baked potato puffs)
summary: Oven-baked round mounds of grated boiled potatoes mixed with sour cream, butter, egg yolks, and onion, brushed with egg and sprinkled with breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. half a Polish garniec (2 l) of peeled potatoes

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for boiling the potatoes and for the mixture

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the mixture and 1 tbsp for greasing the baking sheet

steps: Peel the potatoes, boil in salted water until tender, drain, let steam dry, and grate or mash thoroughly so that no lumps remain.
Add 2 tbsp of sour cream, 1 tbsp of butter, 3 egg yolks, salt to taste, and optionally grated onion to the potato mixture, and beat thoroughly.
Spoon the mixture in round mounds onto a buttered baking sheet.
Brush the top of each puff with beaten egg and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Place the baking sheet in a well-heated oven (190 °C) and bake for about 15–20 minutes until golden; serve after soup instead of pastries or as a garnish around a roast.

name: Sliced potatoes braised with butter and herbs (Kartofle à la maître d'hôtel)
summary: Scalded potato slices braised gently under a lid with fresh butter and a splash of hot water or sweet cream, finished with chopped parsley or dill.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: hot water for braising (or 2 tbsp sweet cream), plus boiling water for scalding

steps: Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices, scald with boiling water, and drain.
Place a tablespoon of fresh butter in a saucepan, add the drained potato slices, salt lightly, and pour in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Cover the saucepan with a lid and braise the potatoes over low heat for 20 minutes, shaking the pan frequently without stirring with a spoon.
Sprinkle the hot potatoes with chopped parsley or dill before serving.

name: Young green peas gently cooked in butter
summary: Freshly shelled young green peas cooked gently, covered, in plenty of fresh butter with white onions and sugar, then thickened with butter blended with flour.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 2 × 1/4 funt (100 g for cooking the peas and 100 g for creaming with flour)

steps: Put the freshly shelled green peas into a two-litre saucepan with 100 g of butter, 125 ml of water, the sliced white onions, a pinch of salt, and the sugar.
Cover the saucepan and cook gently over low heat for 30 minutes.

Cream the remaining 100 g of butter with the wheat flour until smooth, add to the tender peas, and bring briefly to a boil, shaking the saucepan vigorously without stirring with a spoon, until the sauce comes together.
Remove immediately from the heat so the peas keep their bright green colour, and serve.

name: Braised savoy cabbage (Kapusta włoska duszona)
summary: Parboiled quarters of savoy cabbage braised gently in butter and beef or mutton broth, finished with a golden caramelized-sugar roux.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the roux, plus a piece for braising the cabbage

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: or mutton broth or bouillon, for braising

steps: Strip the tough outer leaves from the savoy cabbage, cut into quarters, and rinse.
Parboil the cabbage quarters for about 10 minutes in boiling salted water, then drain and squeeze firmly.
Place a piece of butter and the squeezed cabbage in a saucepan, pour in the broth, cover, and braise over low heat for about 30 minutes until the liquid evaporates and the cabbage is tender.
In a separate pan, cook a tablespoon of butter with a tablespoon of wheat flour and a little sugar until golden, taking care not to scorch the roux.
Stir the golden roux into the cabbage and braise together for another 5 minutes.

name: Gołąbki (stuffed cabbage rolls with pork and rice)
summary: Tender white cabbage leaves stuffed with minced pork braised with butter, grated onion, parsley, parboiled rice, and egg yolks, simmered in broth and finished with a browned flour and sour cream roux.

ingredients.name: white cabbage
ingredients.note: orig. a head of white cabbage, using the softest leaves

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: orig. 1 funt of raw pork, finely chopped

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp (or lard) for the filling and 1 tbsp for the roux

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the water and the meat

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: parboiled beforehand in broth or water

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: hot, for braising the cabbage rolls

steps: Separate the softest leaves from the head of white cabbage, parboil them for 3–5 minutes in boiling salted water, and lift them into a bowl.
Finely mince or grind the raw pork, place in a saucepan with 1 tablespoon of butter, the grated onion, chopped parsley, salt, pepper, and parboiled rice, and braise together for 15 minutes.
Cool the braised meat mixture, then beat in the egg yolks until well combined.
Place portions of filling on the parboiled cabbage leaves, roll up neatly into tight parcels, and pack them side by side in a wide saucepan.
Pour hot broth over the cabbage rolls and simmer uncovered over very low heat for about 45 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Brown a tablespoon of wheat flour in the remaining tablespoon of butter, whisk in the sour cream, and stir into the braising liquid around the cabbage rolls.

name: Italian Macaroni with Parmesan
summary: Boiled Italian macaroni generously sprinkled with coarsely grated Parmesan and drizzled with fresh butter and browned breadcrumbs (or baked with sour cream).

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: fresh, for browning the breadcrumbs and pouring over the pasta

steps: Drop the Italian macaroni into salted boiling water and cook until tender and floating to the surface.
Drain the macaroni and transfer it to a warmed serving platter.

Sprinkle the macaroni generously with coarsely grated Parmesan and pour fresh butter with browned breadcrumbs over the top (alternatively, toss the macaroni with several tablespoons of sour cream and cheese, transfer to a buttered baking platter, top with cheese and breadcrumbs, and bake for 15 minutes in the oven).

name: Szparagi (boiled white asparagus with buttered breadcrumbs)
summary: Fresh white asparagus boiled in tied bundles in salted water with a touch of sugar, served with golden buttered breadcrumbs and clarified butter or chaudeau sauce.

ingredients.name: white asparagus
ingredients.note: orig. tied in bundles of 10–12 spears (approx. 2 bundles)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling for cooking and cold for refreshing the asparagus

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for browning the breadcrumbs (plus clarified butter in a sauceboat)

steps: Select fresh white asparagus with purple-tinged tips, gently scrape off the thin outer skin holding the knife flat, and tie with kitchen string into bundles of 10–12 spears.
Place the asparagus bundles into a pot of generously salted boiling water with a lump of sugar and boil over high heat for about 20 minutes, taking care not to overcook them.
Lift out the cooked asparagus, dip them for a split second into cold water, remove the strings, and arrange on a platter with the tips pointing towards the centre.
Spoon the breadcrumbs browned in butter over the asparagus, and serve melted clarified butter or chaudeau sauce separately in a sauceboat.

name: Szparagi zielone, podane na sposób zielonego groszku (diced green asparagus in cream sauce)
summary: Young green asparagus cut into pea-sized dice and boiled until tender, served in a velvety sauce of butter, flour, whipping cream, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for boiling the asparagus and for the sauce

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon for the roux and 1 tablespoon of fresh butter for the sauce

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: orig. half a kwaterka of sweet cream

steps: Wash the green asparagus, cut off the tips, halve the thicker stalks lengthwise, and cut everything into fine pea-sized dice.
Boil the diced asparagus in salted water until completely tender, then drain.

In a small saucepan, cook 1 tablespoon of plain wheat flour with 1 tablespoon of butter into a roux, then add a pinch of salt, 1 teaspoon of caster sugar, the second tablespoon of fresh butter, 2 egg yolks, and 125 ml of whipping cream.
Heat the sauce over low heat, stirring constantly with a spoon, until the butter melts and the sauce is thoroughly heated and thickened.
Add the cooked asparagus to the hot sauce, stir over the heat for a moment, and serve immediately.

name: Saffron milk caps braised in butter (rydze duszone w maśle)
summary: Fresh saffron milk cap mushrooms cooked gently in plenty of butter with finely chopped onion, parsley root, and celeriac, then sprinkled with breadcrumbs before serving.

ingredients.name: fresh saffron milk cap mushrooms
ingredients.note: orig. half a garniec (2 Polish kwarty)

ingredients.name: finely chopped onion, parsley root, and celeriac

steps: Clean the fresh saffron milk caps, rinse several times in cold water, and drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the mushrooms, salt immediately, and place over low heat.

Once the mushrooms release their juices, add the finely chopped onion, parsley root, and celeriac, cover, and cook gently over low heat for about 30 minutes, shaking the pan often, until the liquid evaporates and only the mushrooms and clear butter remain.
Dust the mushrooms with pepper and breadcrumbs, toss, heat briefly, and serve hot.

name: Ripe Gooseberry Preserves
summary: Preserves made from ripe gooseberries and sugar, flavored with vanilla.

ingredients.name: ripe gooseberries
ingredients.note: Preferably uniform berries of a red variety; orig. a kilo.

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: Small piece of a pod; orig. a little bit.

steps: Cook the ripe gooseberries with the sugar into preserves.
Add the vanilla to the forming syrup while cooking.

name: Lingonberry Preserves with Apples and Pears
summary: Preserves made from lingonberries, sweet apples, and pears simmered together in syrup.

ingredients.name: lingonberries
ingredients.note: Weight after blanching; orig. a kilo.

ingredients.name: sweet apples
ingredients.note: Cut into balls or strips; orig. half a kilo.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: Peeled; orig. the same amount, i.e., half a kilo, as the apples.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: For blanching the lingonberries and preparing a light syrup; volume not specified.

steps: Sort the lingonberries.
Blanch the lingonberries in boiling water for 1 minute.
Drain the lingonberries on a sieve.
Cut the apples into strips or balls.
Peel the pears.
Boil a light syrup from the sugar and water.
Add the lingonberries, apples, and pears to the syrup.
Simmer the fruit over low heat until the apples and pears soften and turn red.
Transfer the hot preserves into jars.
Leave the preserves to cool completely.
Tie parchment paper over the cooled jars.

name: Chestnut Preserves
summary: Whole sweet chestnuts steeped repeatedly in a vanilla-scented sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 750 g for the first syrup, the rest for subsequent boilings; orig. one and a half kilos of sugar.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: For soaking, boiling, and the syrup; amount not specified.

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: orig. with a large piece of vanilla; piece size not specified.

ingredients.name: benzoin
ingredients.note: The source does not specify the dose; to_taste indicates an unspecified amount rather than seasoning to taste.

steps: Soak the raw chestnuts in water for several hours, i.e., several hundred minutes.
Peel off the outer shells of the chestnuts.
Boil the chestnuts in water.
Remove the thin inner skins, taking care not to break the chestnuts.
Arrange the chestnuts in a jar or pot.
Boil a thick syrup from 750 g of sugar, water, and vanilla.
Leave the syrup to cool.
Pour the cold syrup over the chestnuts and set aside for 2880 minutes.
Pour off the syrup and boil it with part of the remaining sugar.
Cool the syrup until lukewarm.
Pour it over the chestnuts again and set aside for another 2880 minutes.
Pour off the syrup and boil it with the rest of the sugar until very thick.
Add the benzoin.
Pour the hot syrup over the chestnuts.
Once completely cooled, cover and tie the jar.

name: Strawberry Jam
summary: Jam made from whole and crushed strawberries boiled with sugar.

ingredients.name: strawberries
ingredients.note: Leave half whole and crush the other half; orig. a kilo of the total prepared fruit.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: Minimal amount to dissolve the sugar; plus 15 ml for each benzoin tablet; orig. in a tablespoon of boiled water.

ingredients.name: benzoin tablets
ingredients.note: Ratio per kilogram of finished jam, not the number of tablets for the whole batch; orig. one benzoin tablet per kilo of jam.

steps: Leave half of the strawberries whole.
Crush the remaining strawberries with a wooden spoon.
Dissolve the sugar over heat in a minimal amount of water, taking care not to scorch it.
Add the whole and crushed fruit.
Boil over high heat, stirring frequently, until the mixture becomes translucent.
Dissolve a benzoin tablet for each kilogram of finished jam in 15 ml of boiled water per tablet.
Stir the dissolved benzoin into the jam.
Transfer the hot jam into thoroughly warmed jars.

name: Apple Marmalade with Orange Peel
summary: Marmalade made from tart apples cooked down with sugar and boiled orange peel.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: Weight after cooking down and sieving; use enough raw apples to yield 1 kg of puree; orig. a kilo of apple pulp.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilo of sugar

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: To cover the apples; volume not specified.

ingredients.name: boiled orange peel
ingredients.note: Here the pcs unit means two handfuls, not two peels; orig. a couple of handfuls of boiled and very finely chopped orange peel; not converted to grams.

steps: Cut the tart apples into quarters.
Place the apples in an ovenproof dish and add water to cover.
Cover the dish tightly with a lid.
Leave the apples in an oven at about 150°C overnight.
Pass the apples through a sieve, separating the peels and cores.
Weigh out 1 kg of apple puree.
Mix the puree with 500 g of sugar.
Cook in a pot, stirring from the bottom with a wooden spoon so the mixture does not scorch.
Finely chop the boiled orange peel.
Toward the end of cooking, add two handfuls of the chopped peel.
Check on a saucer whether a sample of the marmalade sets slightly and does not spread.
Transfer the hot marmalade into warmed, dry ovenproof dishes.
Place the dishes overnight in an oven at about 150°C so the surface of the marmalade dries.

name: Jajecznica na maśle (Polish scrambled eggs in butter)
summary: Classic Polish scrambled eggs cooked slowly in a generous amount of hot, unbrowned butter into large, tender curds.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, season lightly with salt, and beat thoroughly with a spoon or whisk.
Melt the butter in a skillet until hot and foaming, without letting it brown.
Pour the beaten eggs into the hot butter and cook over low heat for about 3–4 minutes.
As the eggs begin to set on the bottom, gently lift them with a spoon in large curds and serve hot as soon as they are set.

name: Scrambled eggs with smoked fatback cracklings
summary: Traditional Polish ten-egg scramble cooked in rendered smoked fatback drippings and folded at the end with tender cracklings.
steps: Trim the rind from the smoked fatback, cut it into thin slices, and render in a skillet for about 4 minutes without browning the cracklings or drying them out too much.
Lift the cracklings onto a plate with a slotted spoon and keep warm.
Beat the eggs with a minimal pinch of salt, pour into the hot rendered fat in the skillet, and cook slowly over low heat for about 3–4 minutes, lifting the set curds from the bottom.
Just before the eggs finish setting, fold the reserved cracklings back in and serve hot right from the skillet.

name: Soft scrambled eggs with milk
summary: Delicate, easily digestible scrambled eggs whisked with milk or sweet cream and gently set in melted butter.
steps: Crack the egg into a bowl, salt lightly, add the milk, and beat thoroughly with a spoon or whisk.
Melt the butter in a small skillet without letting it brown.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and cook over very low heat for about 3–4 minutes, gently pushing the setting curds with a spoon so they stay in larger pieces.
Serve immediately in the same pan as soon as the eggs are set, before they become watery.

name: German-style scrambled eggs
summary: Scrambled eggs stretched with milk and a spoonful of wheat flour, cooked in rendered smoked fatback or pork belly.

ingredients.name: smoked fatback
ingredients.note: generous amount for frying (or fatty pork belly)

steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the wheat flour and salt, and beat very thoroughly.
Pour in the milk and whisk until completely smooth and lump-free.
Render a generous portion of sliced smoked fatback in a skillet for about 4 minutes.
Pour the egg mixture into the hot fat and cook over low heat for about 4 minutes, lifting the set curds from the bottom with a spoon, then serve immediately.

name: Scrambled eggs with ham
summary: Classic Polish ten-egg scramble cooked in butter with thin strips of marbled ham.

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: marbled with fat, cooked or raw, cut into thin strips

steps: Cut the marbled ham into thin strips.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, season very lightly with salt, and beat (if using raw ham, stir it directly into the beaten eggs).
Melt butter in a skillet, pour in the eggs, and cook over low heat for about 4–5 minutes; if using cooked ham, fold it into the eggs as they begin to set.
Serve the hot scrambled eggs immediately once set.

name: Scrambled eggs with Parmesan and cream
summary: Creamy scrambled eggs made with six eggs and cream, cooked with grated Parmesan and served with crisp croutons.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: grated (half mixed in, half for sprinkling)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the croutons and scrambling the eggs

steps: Slice or cube the wheat roll and fry in butter for about 3 minutes until golden brown.
Beat the eggs with the sweet cream, stir in half of the grated Parmesan, and add only a tiny pinch of salt if needed.
Heat butter in a skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and cook over low heat for about 4–5 minutes, gently lifting the setting curds from the bottom with a spoon.
Sprinkle the finished scrambled eggs with the remaining Parmesan, arrange the warm croutons around them, and serve immediately.

name: Scrambled eggs with dried mushrooms
summary: Scrambled eggs cooked in butter, mixed with strips of cooked dried mushrooms and topped with a thick mushroom and sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for the sauce, plus extra for the onion and eggs

steps: Simmer the dried mushrooms in 250 ml of water for about 20 minutes until tender; drain, reserving the broth, and cut the mushrooms into thin strips.

Sauté the grated half onion in butter for 3 minutes, add a tablespoon of butter and the wheat flour, whisk in the reserved mushroom broth, season with salt, simmer for 3 minutes, and finish with the sour cream.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble in hot butter over low heat for about 5 minutes.
Gently fold the mushroom strips into the scrambled eggs, spoon the hot mushroom sauce over the top, and serve immediately.

name: Scrambled eggs with Polish sausage (Jajecznica z kiełbasą)
summary: Traditional Polish ten-egg scramble served with sliced kiełbasa browned in butter.

ingredients.name: Polish sausage (kiełbasa)
ingredients.note: regular, Kraków-style or serdelowa Polish sausage

steps: Cut thin sausage into rounds, or thicker sausage into large dice.
Brown the sausage pieces on both sides in hot butter for about 4 minutes, then lift them out of the pan and keep warm.
Beat the eggs with a tiny pinch of salt, pour into the drippings left in the skillet, and cook over low heat for about 4 minutes until set.
Fold the browned sausage into the finished scrambled eggs and serve immediately.

name: Baked scrambled eggs with herring and onion
summary: Oven-baked eggs and cream set over a savory layer of finely chopped soaked herring sautéed in butter with grated onion.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 generous tbsp for frying the herring and onion, plus extra before baking

steps: Skin and bone the well-soaked herrings and chop them finely; grate the onion.
Sauté the chopped herring and grated onion in a tablespoon of butter in a deep ovenproof skillet for about 5 minutes, then add the second tablespoon of butter.
Beat the eggs with the cream and a tiny pinch of salt, and pour over the hot herring layer without stirring.
Transfer the skillet to an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 10 minutes until the eggs set, and serve immediately, scooping all the way from the bottom.

name: Scrambled eggs à la Strasbourgeoise
summary: Rich scrambled eggs made with cream and butter, served with a ragout of goose liver, veal kidney, button mushrooms and ham, accompanied by croutons.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the eggs, plus extra for braising the offal and frying croutons

steps: Braise the goose liver and trimmed veal kidney (along with its surrounding fat) in butter for about 12 minutes until tender, then cut into thin slices.
Sauté the young mushrooms with the finely chopped onion in the same fat for 6 minutes, chop the mushrooms finely, toss with the sliced liver, kidney, and strips of cooked ham, and keep warm.
Brown the wheat roll croutons in butter for 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the thick sweet cream and a pinch of salt.
Melt 100 g of butter in a wide skillet or metal platter, pour in the egg mixture, and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes, gently lifting the set curds from the bottom with a spoon.
Push the scrambled eggs toward the edge of the dish, spoon the warm liver, kidney, mushroom and ham mixture into the centre, arrange the fried croutons around it, and serve immediately.

name: Scrambled eggs with young asparagus
summary: Ten-egg scramble folded just before finishing with tender simmered young asparagus tips and diced stalks.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for cooking the asparagus and seasoning the eggs

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: a small amount for cooking the asparagus

steps: Cut the tips off the trimmed asparagus and dice the tender stalks into small cubes.

Simmer the diced stalks in a small amount of salted water with a teaspoon of sugar for about 8 minutes; when nearly tender, add the tips and cook for another 3 minutes until only about two tablespoons of cooking liquid remain.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into a skillet with hot melted butter, and cook over low heat for about 4 minutes.
As the eggs begin to set, fold in the hot asparagus along with the spoonfuls of reduced cooking liquid, stir gently, and serve immediately.

name: Scrambled eggs with cheese croutons
summary: Butter-cooked scrambled eggs scattered right before serving with crisp diced bread croutons baked with melted butter and sharp cheese.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for drizzling the croutons and cooking the eggs

steps: Cut the wheat rolls with a sharp knife into small, even cubes, spread on a baking sheet, drizzle generously with melted butter, and sprinkle with grated sharp cheese.
Bake the croutons in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 10 minutes, tossing frequently, until golden and very crisp, then keep warm.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into a skillet with hot melted butter, and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes, lifting the set curds from the bottom.
Scatter the hot, crisp cheese croutons over the scrambled eggs and serve immediately in the same pan.

name: Jaja sadzone na maśle (sunny-side up eggs fried in butter)
summary: Classic fried eggs cooked slowly in a generous amount of clear melted butter, with runny yolks and set whites.
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet or metal platter and remove the pan from the heat.
Carefully crack the eggs in side by side so that the yolks remain whole.
Set the skillet over low heat and cook slowly for about 4–5 minutes, lightly scoring the whites with a spoon so the hot butter sets them evenly and basting the yolks with butter.
Sprinkle the setting eggs with fine salt and a pinch of white pepper, and serve immediately once the whites are set.

name: Jaja na śmietanie (eggs gently cooked in sour cream)
summary: Eggs cooked slowly in sour cream boiled with butter, basted on top with the hot sour cream sauce.
steps: Melt the butter in a metal platter or wide skillet, pour in the sour cream, boil briefly for 1 minute, season lightly with salt and pepper, and remove from the heat.
Carefully crack the ten eggs into the sour cream and return the pan to low heat.
Cook slowly for about 5 minutes until the whites are set, and sprinkle them with fine salt.
Tilt the pan slightly, scoop up the hot sour cream sauce with a spoon, and baste the tops of the eggs, especially the yolks, then serve immediately.

name: Jaja na occie (eggs poached in tarragon vinegar butter)
summary: Eggs gently cooked in a mixture of butter, tarragon vinegar, and water, served with white pepper.
steps: Melt the butter in a large metal platter or deep skillet, pour in the tarragon vinegar and water, bring to a boil together, and remove the pan from the heat.
Carefully crack the eggs into the hot liquid so that the yolks remain intact.
Return the pan to low heat and cook slowly for about 4–5 minutes, lightly scoring the whites with a spoon so they set evenly.
Sprinkle the set eggs with fine salt, place a tiny pinch of white pepper on each yolk, and serve immediately in the same dish.

name: Jaja w sosie pomidorowym (eggs poached in tomato sauce)
summary: Eggs gently cooked in warm, thin tomato sauce on a deep platter.
steps: Warm the tomato sauce, set aside a few spoonfuls in a warm place, and pour the rest into a deep metal platter or wide skillet.
Carefully crack the eggs into the warm sauce, taking care not to break the yolks.
Cook the eggs in the sauce over very low heat for about 5–6 minutes, gently scoring the whites with a knife so they set faster and more evenly.
Sprinkle the set eggs with fine salt, spoon a teaspoon of the reserved warm tomato sauce over each yolk, and serve immediately.

name: Jaja na szynce lub słoninie (eggs fried on ham or fatback)
summary: Classic sunny-side up eggs fried slowly atop thin slices of marbled ham, pork belly, or smoked fatback.

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: marbled with fat, cut into 6 equal slices (or pork belly or smoked fatback)

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: one per slice of cured meat

steps: Cut the marbled ham into six thin, large, even slices.
Arrange the ham slices evenly in a cold skillet, set over the heat, and fry for about 3 minutes until the fat turns translucent, then remove the skillet from the heat.
Crack one egg onto each slice of meat, return the skillet to very low heat, and cook slowly for about 4 minutes, gently parting the whites so they set evenly.
Sprinkle only the yolks with salt and pepper and serve immediately in the same skillet.

name: Jaja na pomidorach (eggs baked in tomato halves)
summary: Eggs cracked into hollowed, butter-seared halves of large tomatoes and baked in a hot oven.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for searing and baking the tomatoes

steps: Halve the large tomatoes horizontally and scoop out the seeds and juice with a teaspoon.
Heat an ovenproof skillet with a little butter and sear the tomato halves cut-side down for about 3 minutes.
Turn the tomatoes cut-side up, add a piece of butter to the skillet, crack one egg into each tomato half, and season with salt and pepper.
Place the skillet in an oven preheated to 200 °C and bake for 10 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve directly in the skillet, or transfer to a platter and spoon the butter and tomato pan juices over the top.

name: Sunny-side up eggs with porcini or button mushrooms
summary: Sunny-side-up eggs cooked in a butter-and-water emulsion in the pan used to fry porcini with onion, served topped with the hot mushrooms.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for frying the mushrooms and 1 tbsp for the eggs

steps: Clean the young porcini mushrooms, slice them into thin strips, and fry in a large skillet in a tablespoon of butter with the finely chopped onion for about 12 minutes, then season with salt to taste.
Transfer the fried mushrooms and onion to a small saucepan and keep warm.
Add the second tablespoon of butter and the water to the same skillet, bring to a boil, take briefly off the heat, and carefully crack the eggs in side by side.
Set the skillet over low heat and cook gently for about 5 minutes until the whites are set while the yolks remain runny.
Scatter the reserved warm mushrooms over the finished eggs and serve immediately right from the skillet.

name: Jaja w muszelkach (baked eggs in scallop shells)
summary: Individual eggs baked in buttered scallop shells or ramekins under a crisp topping of breadcrumbs, sharp cheese, and butter.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a hazelnut-sized piece for the top, plus extra for greasing the shell

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for dusting the shell and sprinkling over the egg

steps: Generously butter an ovenproof scallop shell or small ramekin and dust it with breadcrumbs.
Set the shell level on a baking sheet, crack one egg into the centre, and season lightly with salt.
Sprinkle the top of the egg with breadcrumbs and grated sharp cheese, and dot with about 10 g of butter.
Place in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 10–15 minutes until the breadcrumbs are golden brown, then serve immediately.

name: Jaja w muszelkach z wermiszelem (baked eggs in vermicelli nests)
summary: Eggs baked in ten buttered scallop shells or ramekins nestled in fine vermicelli pasta tossed with butter and sharp cheese.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the pasta, plus extra for greasing the shells

ingredients.name: hard cheese
ingredients.note: sharp, grated, for the pasta plus extra for sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: small, 1 for each of the 10 shells

steps: Boil the vermicelli pasta in boiling water for about 4 minutes, drain, rinse with cold water, and toss with a tablespoon of butter and 50 g of grated sharp cheese.
Generously butter ten scallop shells or ramekins and arrange the pasta inside them in the shape of nests with a hollow centre.
Set the shells level on a baking sheet, crack one egg into the centre of each nest, season lightly with salt, and sprinkle generously with grated cheese.
Place in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 15 minutes until the whites are set and the cheese is golden.

name: Jaja w muszelkach z szynką (baked eggs with ham in ramekins)
summary: Eggs baked in ten buttered scallop shells or ramekins on a bed of thinly sliced ham under breadcrumbs and sharp grated cheese.

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: raw or cooked, cut into thin strips

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the shells and drizzling on top

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for dusting the shells and sprinkling over the eggs

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: small, 1 for each of the 10 shells

steps: Cut the ham into very thin strips.
Generously butter ten scallop shells or ramekins, dust them with breadcrumbs, and line them with a layer of ham, making a slight hollow in the centre of each.
Set the shells level on a baking sheet, crack one egg into each, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and grated sharp cheese, and drizzle with melted butter.
Place in an oven preheated to 170 °C and bake for 15–20 minutes until the cheese melts and forms a thin crust.

name: Jaja z cebulą w muszelkach (baked eggs with onion and smoked fatback in ramekins)
summary: Eggs baked in ten scallop shells or ramekins on a savoury bed of butter-braised sweet onions and finely diced smoked fatback.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: small, 1 for each of the 10 shells

steps: Cut the smoked fatback into very fine dice, and finely chop the large onions.
Cook the chopped onions gently with a teaspoon of butter over low heat for about 10 minutes until soft, then mix with the diced fatback, season lightly with pepper, and let cool.
Divide the cooled onion and fatback mixture among ten scallop shells or ramekins, making a hollow in the centre of each.
Set the shells level on a baking sheet and crack one egg into the centre of each without salting them.
Place in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 15 minutes until the whites are set.

name: Jaja w muszelkach z serem (baked eggs in gougère rings)
summary: Eggs baked in buttered scallop shells inside a ring of Parmesan choux pastry under a glossy crust of grated Parmesan.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the choux pastry, plus extra for greasing the shells

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: one for the centre of each shell

steps: Bring the water and butter to a boil in a small saucepan, dump the wheat flour into the boiling liquid, and beat vigorously with a spoon for about 3 minutes until the dough pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Remove the pan from the heat, continue beating until slightly cooled, then beat in the two eggs and 30 g of grated Parmesan cheese and work into a smooth dough.
Generously butter ten scallop shells or ramekins and pipe or shape a thin ring of choux pastry around the rim of each like a bagel.
Set the shells on a baking sheet, crack one egg into the centre of each pastry ring, and sprinkle the tops with the remaining 30 g of grated Parmesan cheese.
Place in an oven preheated to 220 °C and bake for about 15 minutes until the pastry puffs high and browns lightly and the cheese forms a glossy glaze.

name: Jaja na grzankach z cynaderkami (poached eggs on toast with veal kidneys)
summary: Poached eggs served on buttered toast topped with thin slices of braised veal kidneys and grated Parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for braising the kidneys and browning the toast

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the kidneys and the poaching water

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the kidneys and poaching the eggs

steps: Soak the veal kidneys thoroughly in cold water for 20 minutes, pat dry, and braise whole in butter along with their surrounding fat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Salt the braised kidneys and cut each one into ten very thin slices.
Brown the oval slices of wheat roll on both sides in butter for about 3 minutes, taking care not to dry them out.
Bring salted water with vinegar to a boil in a wide saucepan, carefully crack in the eggs, and poach them for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny.

Place two slices of kidney on each warm slice of toast, top each with a poached egg, sprinkle generously with grated Parmesan, drizzle with the hot fat from cooking the kidneys, and serve immediately.

name: Egg croquettes
summary: Oval croquettes of chopped hard-boiled eggs bound with a thick white milk sauce, fresh dill, and breadcrumbs, breaded and deep-fried until golden.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 8 hard-boiled, 2 raw for binding, and 1 beaten for breading

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for the white sauce, plus extra for dredging

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for stiffening the mixture and for coating

steps: Hard-boil eight eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel, and chop finely.

Cook two tablespoons of wheat flour with a generous tablespoon of butter without browning, whisk in the milk, and simmer for about 4 minutes, stirring, until a very thick white sauce forms; let cool slightly.
Combine the thick sauce with the chopped hard-boiled eggs, chopped dill, salt, pepper, two raw eggs, and enough breadcrumbs for the mixture to hold its shape firmly.
Shape the mixture into egg-sized oval croquettes and coat each one just before frying in wheat flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry the croquettes in hot lard for about 3–4 minutes until golden brown and serve immediately.

name: Baked egg and ham timbales
summary: Delicate individual custards of eggs, sweet cream, and finely diced cooked ham, baked in a water bath and served unmolded with hot tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: tomato sauce
ingredients.note: pure, smooth, for pouring over before serving

steps: Generously butter six tall metal timbale molds or ramekins.
Beat the eggs thoroughly with the sweet cream and a pinch of salt, stir in the finely diced cooked ham, and divide the mixture among the molds.
Set the molds in a deep roasting pan filled with hot water reaching halfway up their sides.
Bake in the water bath in an oven preheated to 170 °C for about 25 minutes until the egg custard is completely set.
Carefully unmold the timbales onto a serving platter, pour hot pure tomato sauce over them, and serve immediately.

name: Jaja na twardo z sosem pomidorowym (hard-boiled eggs baked in tomato sauce)
summary: Halved hard-boiled eggs baked under a velvety tomato and sour cream sauce topped with sharp grated cheese.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the roux, plus extra for the tomatoes and greasing the platter

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: sweet cream butter, for finishing the sauce

steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, transfer to cold water, peel, and halve lengthwise.
Cook a tablespoon of butter with the wheat flour over low heat without browning, then whisk in the broth until a smooth sauce forms.

Sauté the sieved fresh tomatoes separately in butter for 5 minutes, combine with the sauce, season with salt and pepper, stir in the sour cream, bring once to a boil, and whisk in a teaspoon of fresh butter.
Arrange the egg halves on a buttered ovenproof platter, pour the tomato sauce over them, and sprinkle with grated sharp cheese.
Place the dish in an oven preheated to 190 °C for 5 minutes until the cheese melts, and serve hot.

name: Baked pasta and hard-boiled eggs in horseradish sauce
summary: A gratin of cooked pasta and hard-boiled eggs under a thick horseradish and sour cream sauce, topped with crisp breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 6 hard-boiled and 1 raw to enrich the sauce

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the pasta and 1 tbsp for the roux, plus extra for greasing the dish and drizzling on top

steps: Grate the horseradish root, salt it lightly, mix with a teaspoon of sugar, drizzle with vinegar, and let stand for 120 minutes to mellow its pungency.
Hard-boil six eggs for 10 minutes, peel, and slice into rounds or quarters.
