Cook the broken pasta in salted boiling water for about 8 minutes, drain, and toss with a tablespoon of butter.
Butter an ovenproof serving dish and arrange alternating rows of cooked pasta and hard-boiled eggs.

Cook a tablespoon of butter with the wheat flour, stir in the broth, add the sour cream and marinated horseradish, and simmer together for 3 minutes. Let cool slightly, then temper with the beaten raw egg.
Pour the horseradish sauce over the pasta and eggs, sprinkle with breadcrumbs, drizzle with melted butter, and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 15 minutes until golden brown.

name: Hard-boiled eggs in hot anchovy cream sauce
summary: Halved hard-boiled eggs cloaked in a hot, velvety sauce of grated onion, soaked anchovies, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: salted anchovies
ingredients.note: soaked and boned (or 1 ulik-style salted herring)

steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, peel, and halve them lengthwise.
Bone the soaked anchovies and chop them very finely.
Sauté the grated onion in a tablespoon of butter for 4 minutes, add the minced anchovies, and cook together for another 3 minutes until they form a smooth paste.
Dust the paste with wheat flour, stir in the water and sour cream, season with black pepper, and simmer over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Arrange the egg halves on a serving platter, pour the hot anchovy sauce over them, and serve immediately.

name: Jaja nadziewane (pan-fried stuffed eggs in shells)
summary: Hard-boiled eggs chopped with herbs, butter, and breadcrumbs, packed back into their half-shells and pan-fried in butter.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 6 hard-boiled and 2 raw to bind the filling

ingredients.name: parsley leaves
ingredients.note: chopped for the filling and sprigs for garnish

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: creamed or melted for the mixture, plus extra for frying

steps: Hard-boil six eggs for 10 minutes, let cool, and cut lengthwise in half through the shells with a very sharp knife.
Carefully scoop out the whites and yolks without damaging the shells, and chop them medium-fine.
Mix the chopped eggs with the dill, parsley leaves, chives, breadcrumbs, salt, pepper, a tablespoon of butter, and two raw eggs until uniform.
Pack the prepared filling into the half-shells.
Place the stuffed shells filling-side down in a skillet with browned butter, cover with a lid, and fry for about 4 minutes until the filling sets and browns, then garnish with parsley and serve.

name: Jaja nadziewane rakami i ryżem (eggs stuffed with crayfish and rice)
summary: Egg half-shells filled with a delicate mixture of crayfish tails, fluffy rice, chopped hard-boiled eggs, and fresh dill, pan-fried in butter.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 3 hard-boiled and 2 raw (plus reserved empty half-shells)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for cooking the rice, plus extra for frying the stuffed shells

steps: Hard-boil three eggs for 10 minutes, halve lengthwise through the shells with a sharp knife, scoop out the contents, and chop finely.
Cook the rice in salted water with a tablespoon of butter for about 18 minutes until fluffy, then let cool.
Cook the crayfish in boiling water for about 10 minutes, remove the meat from the shells, and chop it finely.
Mix the crayfish meat thoroughly with the cooked rice, chopped hard-boiled eggs, salt, chopped dill, and two raw eggs.
Pack the filling into the prepared egg half-shells and fry them filling-side down in hot butter for about 4 minutes until golden.

name: Jaja nadziewane mięsem (baked meat-stuffed eggs in shells)
summary: Egg half-shells mounded with a savory filling of chopped hard-boiled eggs, roast meat, and onion, baked under a crust of sharp cheese.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 6 large hard-boiled and 2 raw, halved lengthwise in their shells

ingredients.name: roast meat
ingredients.note: or boiled meat (beef, poultry, or game)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the meat and onion

steps: Boil six eggs hard for 10 minutes, cut them lengthwise in half right through the shells with a very sharp knife, scoop out the whites and yolks, and chop finely.
Pass the roast meat through a mincer or chop it finely, and fry in butter with the chopped onion for about 5 minutes.
Using a sharp knife, halve the two raw eggs lengthwise as well, reserving their half-shells, and mix their contents with the fried meat, chopped hard-boiled eggs, salt, and pepper.
Fill all sixteen half-shells with the prepared stuffing, shaping a dome on each, and sprinkle generously with grated sharp cheese.
Set the stuffed shells in a roasting pan and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 15 minutes until golden brown.

name: Jaja nadziewane grzybami (eggs stuffed with porcini mushrooms in shells)
summary: Egg half-shells filled with chopped hard-boiled eggs, porcini mushrooms, onion, and dill, fried golden in butter.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 5 large hard-boiled and 2 raw (plus 6 empty half-shells)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the onion, filling, and frying the shells

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for boiling the mushrooms and seasoning the filling

steps: Boil five eggs hard for 10 minutes, cut them lengthwise in half with their shells using a sharp knife, scoop out the insides, and chop finely, reserving the shells.
Boil the cleaned porcini mushrooms in salted water for about 15 minutes, drain, and chop finely.
Fry the finely chopped onion in butter for 5 minutes and mix it with the chopped mushrooms, hard-boiled eggs, chopped dill, a little melted butter, salt, pepper, and two raw eggs.
Fill sixteen egg half-shells with the prepared mixture.
Fry the stuffed shells filling-side down in hot butter for about 4 minutes until golden brown, and serve hot.

name: Jaja poszetowe w sosie szczawiowym (poached eggs in sorrel sauce)
summary: Poached eggs served warm with a thick sauce of young sorrel leaves gently cooked in butter with sour cream.
steps: Wash the young sorrel leaves, drain in a sieve, dry, pass through a mincer, and cook gently in butter for about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the cooked sorrel with the wheat flour, pour in the vegetable broth and sour cream, season with salt and sugar, and simmer together for 3 minutes.
Bring salted water with vinegar to a boil in a wide saucepan, carefully crack in the eggs, and poach for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny.
Arrange the poached eggs on an ovenproof platter, pour the hot sorrel sauce over them, heat briefly for 2 minutes, and serve.

name: Jaja poszetowe smażone (deep-fried breaded poached eggs)
summary: Cooled poached eggs coated in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs, then deep-fried until golden.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 10 for poaching and 1 beaten for breading

steps: Bring salted water with vinegar to a boil in a wide saucepan, carefully crack in ten eggs, and poach them for 2–3 minutes until the whites are firm and the yolks remain liquid, then remove, trim the edges neatly, and let cool.
Coat each cooled and dried poached egg thoroughly in wheat flour, then in beaten raw egg, and finally in breadcrumbs.
Lower the breaded eggs into a deep layer of very hot lard and fry for about 2 minutes until golden brown.
Drain the fried eggs on paper towels, arrange on a platter, garnish with parsley sprigs and lemon quarters, and serve with plain tomato sauce.

name: Jaja po rosyjsku — Draczena (Russian baked egg puff)
summary: A fluffy oven-baked puff omelette made from creamed butter, egg yolks, flour, milk, and stiffly beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for melting in the baking dish

steps: Cream 50 g of butter in a bowl until fluffy, add the egg yolks, salt, wheat flour, and milk, and beat everything together until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Melt a tablespoon of butter in an ovenproof skillet or deep baking dish and pour the egg batter into the hot fat.
Place the dish in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for 20 minutes until the drachena puffs high and turns golden brown, then cut into portions and serve immediately.

name: Plain omelette
summary: A classic omelette made from six whole eggs beaten with thick cream and cooked in browned butter.
steps: Beat the eggs vigorously in a bowl with four tablespoons of thick sweet cream and a pinch of salt.
Brown a generous tablespoon of butter in an ovenproof skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and cook over high heat for about 2 minutes until set underneath.
Transfer the skillet to an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 3–4 minutes (or cover over low heat) until the top sets evenly.
Fold the omelette in half with a wide spatula (or fold both edges toward the center), slide carefully onto a platter, and serve piping hot.

name: Soufflé omelette (Omelette soufflée)
summary: An airy French soufflé omelette made from egg yolks creamed with heavy cream and folded with stiffly beaten whites, browned in butter and puffed in the oven.
steps: Cream the egg yolks in a bowl with a pinch of salt and three tablespoons of heavy cream.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the yolk mixture.
Heat a generous amount of butter in an ovenproof skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and cook over high heat for about 2 minutes until browned underneath.
Transfer the skillet to an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 4–5 minutes (or finish over the lowest possible stovetop heat) until the top is set.
Gently fold the puffed omelette in half with a spatula and serve immediately on a warmed platter.

name: Lithuanian-style puffed omelette
summary: A fluffy, filling sponge-like omelette made from five eggs, milk and wheat flour, cooked in plenty of butter.
steps: Beat the egg yolks with the wheat flour, a pinch of salt, and the milk until smooth and lump-free.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them carefully into the yolk batter.
Heat a generous amount of butter in a skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and cook over medium heat for about 8–10 minutes, taking care not to burn the bottom, until the omelette rises and sets.
Fold the finished omelette in half, slide onto a platter, and serve immediately.

name: Ham omelette
summary: A classic six-egg omelette scattered with thin strips of marbled ham just before finishing and folded in half.

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: cooked or raw, marbled with fat

steps: Cut the marbled ham into very thin strips.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into a skillet with hot melted butter, and cook for about 3 minutes until set underneath while still slightly runny on top.
Scatter the ham strips evenly over the omelette and cook for another 2 minutes until the ham is heated through and its fat turns translucent.
Fold the omelette in half (or fold both edges toward the centre), transfer to a serving platter, and serve immediately while hot.

name: Omelette stuffed with creamed porcini mushrooms
summary: A six-egg omelette filled with fresh porcini mushrooms braised in butter with onion and bound in a thick sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for braising the mushrooms and frying the omelette

steps: Clean and slice the porcini mushrooms, then braise in butter with the finely chopped onion for about 12 minutes until tender.
Dust the mushrooms with a teaspoon of wheat flour, stir in the sour cream, season with salt, and simmer for 2 minutes until a very thick sauce forms.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into a skillet with hot butter, and cook the omelette for about 5 minutes.
Spoon the hot creamed mushrooms over one half of the omelette, fold the other half over, and serve immediately.

name: Asparagus omelette with cream
summary: A six-egg omelette filled with young asparagus in a thick cream-and-butter sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for cooking the asparagus and seasoning the omelette

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a dab for the asparagus, plus extra for frying the omelette

steps: Cut the tips off the young asparagus, dice the stalks, and simmer the stalks in salted water with a teaspoon of sugar for about 8 minutes.
Add the asparagus tips to the nearly tender stalks, cook for another 3 minutes, and drain off the water.
Dust the cooked asparagus with a teaspoon of wheat flour, pour in the cream, boil briefly for 1 minute to form a thick sauce, and stir in a little fresh butter.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, fry the omelette in butter for about 5 minutes, spoon the creamed asparagus into the center, fold in half, and serve immediately.

name: Jaja z beszamelem (soft-boiled eggs gratinated with béchamel)
summary: Peeled soft-boiled eggs baked under a fluffy dome of béchamel sauce enriched with raw eggs and grated Parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for the béchamel, plus extra for greasing the platter

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 2 raw for the béchamel and 10 soft-boiled peeled eggs

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: grated, sharp (a handful for the sauce and extra for sprinkling on top)

steps: Cook a tablespoon of butter with the wheat flour over low heat without browning, whisk in the milk, season lightly with salt, simmer for about 5 minutes, and set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, boil ten eggs in their shells in boiling water for 3 minutes, plunge into cold water, and peel carefully.
Beat two raw eggs into the cooled béchamel, add half of the grated Parmesan cheese, and mix thoroughly.
Butter an ovenproof platter, spread one-third of the béchamel on the bottom, arrange the peeled soft-boiled eggs on top, and cover with the remaining sauce in a dome.
Sprinkle the top generously with the remaining grated Parmesan cheese and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 15 minutes until golden brown, then serve immediately.

name: Jaja à la Tripe (eggs à la tripe)
summary: Hard-boiled eggs sliced into rounds and warmed in an aromatic spiced onion and sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 10 hard-boiled and 1 whole raw for the sauce

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling down the onions to 250 ml

steps: Hard-boil ten eggs for 10 minutes, let cool, peel, and slice into rounds.
Put the chopped onions into the water with the bay leaf, peppercorns, allspice, and a pinch of salt, then boil for about 15 minutes until 250 ml of liquid remains in the pot.
Add the butter mashed with the wheat flour to the onion broth and simmer, stirring, for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Transfer the sauce to a small saucepan, add the sliced hard-boiled eggs, and pour in the sour cream beaten with the raw egg.
Set the saucepan over the heat and boil gently for 1 minute, stirring carefully, then serve immediately.

name: Jaja po bretońsku (poached eggs Bretonne with mushroom sauce)
summary: Poached eggs served on buttered toast with a thick mushroom and onion sauce with lemon juice.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the sauce, plus extra for frying the toast

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: or water for thinning the sauce

steps: Clean the button mushrooms, cut them into strips, and fry with the finely chopped onion in butter for about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle the mushrooms with the wheat flour, stir in enough broth to make a thick sauce, season with salt, the juice of half a lemon, and a teaspoon of caramel colouring, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Fry the slices of wheat roll in butter on both sides for 3 minutes until golden.
Bring salted water with vinegar to a boil in a shallow saucepan, carefully crack in the eggs, and poach for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny.
Place the poached eggs on the hot toast, spoon the mushroom sauce over them, and serve immediately.

name: Eggs baked in tomatoes
summary: Large hollowed-out tomatoes stuffed with poached eggs, braised in butter and broth and topped with sharp cheese.

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: enough to come halfway up the tomatoes

steps: Poach the small eggs in boiling water for 3 minutes, transfer to cold water, and carefully remove the shells.
Slice the tops off the tomatoes, scoop out the seeds and juice with a spoon, and lightly salt the insides.
Place one peeled poached egg in each hollowed-out tomato and cover with the sliced-off tomato top.
Melt butter in a wide shallow pan, set the stuffed tomatoes side by side, salt lightly on top, and pour in enough broth to reach halfway up their sides.
Braise gently over low heat (or bake in the oven at 180 °C) for about 20 minutes until the broth reduces by half and the tomatoes are tender.
Scatter the hot tomatoes generously with grated sharp cheese and serve in the same dish.

name: Ham and egg tartlets
summary: Crisp shortcrust pastry tartlet shells filled with strips of marbled ham and whole eggs, baked under a blanket of grated cheese.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the pastry and the eggs

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: marbled, cut into strips (1 tbsp per tartlet across 10 tartlets)

steps: Knead a shortcrust pastry from the wheat flour, butter, sour cream, and a pinch of salt; cover with a bowl and let rest for 60 minutes.
Roll the dough out very thinly, line ten metal tartlet tins, weight with dried peas for blind baking, and bake in an oven preheated to 190 °C for about 18 minutes until golden.
Remove the dried baking peas from the pre-baked shells, set the tartlets on a baking sheet, and spoon a tablespoon of ham strips into each shell.
Crack one raw egg into each tartlet over the ham, season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Return to the oven at 180 °C for about 7 minutes until the whites are nicely set, and serve warm.

name: Jaja w sosie majonezowym (eggs mayonnaise)
summary: Hard-boiled egg halves served cold in a homemade mayonnaise sauce based on a light roux, egg yolks, olive oil, and lemon.

ingredients.name: broth
ingredients.note: or boiled water (plus a splash of cold liquid to thin the sauce)

steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel, and halve lengthwise.
Simmer a teaspoon of wheat flour with a teaspoon of butter and two tablespoons of broth in a small saucepan for 2 minutes, then cool completely.

Add the raw egg yolks, salt, sugar, a dab of mustard, and vinegar to the cooled base, and whisk vigorously while trickling in the olive oil a few drops at a time until a thick, smooth mayonnaise forms.
Squeeze the lemon juice into the mayonnaise and thin it with a splash of cold broth to the consistency of a coating sauce.
Arrange the egg halves on a platter, pour the mayonnaise sauce over them, and chill for about 120 minutes before serving.

name: Jaja w sosie chrzanowym (hard-boiled eggs in horseradish sauce)
summary: Hard-boiled egg halves in a thick, cold sauce made with grated horseradish, sour cream, and a pale roux.
steps: Grate the horseradish root on a fine grater, season with salt and sugar, sprinkle with vinegar, and let stand for about 120 minutes to lose its harsh pungency.
Cook the butter and wheat flour over low heat without browning, whisk in the broth, simmer for 3 minutes until thickened, and let cool.
Mix the cooled white sauce with the marinated horseradish and sour cream.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, let cool, peel, halve, and arrange on a platter.
Spoon the thick horseradish sauce over the egg halves and chill for about 20 minutes before serving so the flavours meld.

name: Potato and hard-boiled egg salad with olive oil and herbs
summary: A chilled salad of alternating rows of sliced boiled potatoes and hard-boiled eggs dressed with olive oil, fresh lemon juice, chives, and dill.
steps: Boil the unpeeled potatoes for about 25 minutes until tender, and hard-boil the eggs in a separate pot for 10 minutes.
Cool and peel both the potatoes and the eggs, then slice them into even rounds.
Arrange alternating rows of potato slices and egg slices in a salad bowl, scatter generously with finely chopped chives and dill, and season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and freshly squeezed lemon juice, then chill in a cool place for about 120 minutes before serving so the flavors meld.

name: Kapuśniak (Polish sauerkraut soup)
summary: Sauerkraut soup made with beef, pork, and dried mushrooms, clarified with egg whites.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: orig. 3 funty; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: orig. 1½ funty; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: sauerkraut juice
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta; historical measure, converted approximately; amount from the ingredient list

ingredients.name: sauerkraut
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta; volume of sauerkraut; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: at least 4 l; orig. a garniec or more; historical measure, converted approximately

steps: Place the beef and pork in a pot.
Add the mushrooms, whole peeled onions, sauerkraut, salt, allspice, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Cover with the water.
Cook until the meat is tender.
Strain the broth, reserving the pork for serving.
Skim the fat from the surface of the broth.
Add the sauerkraut juice to the broth.
Clarify the hot broth with the egg whites, heating until they set.
Strain the broth again.
Cut the pork into pieces.
Add the pork to the soup before serving.

name: Raw Fish Cutlets
summary: Cutlets made from ground fish, soaked bread roll, and onion, breaded in breadcrumbs and fried.

ingredients.name: fish flesh
ingredients.note: skinless and boneless; orig. sixty dag

ingredients.name: bread roll
ingredients.note: soaked in water and squeezed well; orig. fifteen dag

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: large; two small ones can be used

steps: Separate the flesh of the cleaned fish from the bones and carefully remove any remaining bones.
Soak the bread roll in water and squeeze it out well.
Grate the onion.
Grind the fish, bread roll, and onion together.
Knead the mixture with the egg, salt, and a small amount of pepper until uniform.
Shape into fairly thin cutlets.
Coat the cutlets in breadcrumbs.
Fry the cutlets in lard.

name: Fish Soufflé
summary: Baked soufflé made from ground fish and potatoes, lightened with beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: fish flesh
ingredients.note: raw or cooked, boneless; orig. sixty dag

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the mixture; orig. ten dag

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: separate the yolks from the whites; use both parts

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the dish; amount not specified

steps: Remove the bones from the fish.
Grind the fish together with the boiled potatoes.
Cream 100 g of butter until fluffy.
Add the ground fish and potatoes and beat thoroughly.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites.
Add the yolks, salt, and pepper to the mixture, then beat thoroughly.
Beat the egg whites until stiff.
Grease a baking dish with additional butter.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Just before baking, gently fold the beaten egg whites into the mixture.
Mound the mixture into a dome in the dish and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serve the soufflé immediately after removing from the oven, before it falls.

name: Cauliflower with butter and rusks
summary: Boiled cauliflower topped with browned butter and crushed rusks.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for rinsing and boiling; volume not specified

steps: Remove the cauliflower leaves.
Divide the cauliflowers, checking inside the florets.
Rinse the cauliflowers in water with vinegar.
Boil the cauliflowers in boiling salted water.
Drain the cauliflowers in a sieve.
Brown the butter with the crushed rusks.
Arrange the cauliflowers on a platter with the florets facing up.
Pour the butter and rusks over the cauliflowers.

name: Savoy cabbage cooked gently with roux
summary: Quarters of savoy cabbage cooked gently, covered, in bouillon and thickened with a butter roux.

ingredients.name: savoy cabbage
ingredients.note: heads; orig. 3–4 heads; lower bound used

ingredients.name: bouillon
ingredients.note: orig. ½ szklanka; composition of the bouillon is not specified

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1–2 tbsp; upper bound used, for cooking the cabbage and for the roux

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for parboiling and rinsing the cabbage

steps: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage.
Cut the heads into quarters.
Rinse the cabbage.
Parboil the cabbage in boiling salted water.
Drain the cabbage.
Rinse it with cold water and squeeze it out.
Pack the cabbage tightly in a saucepan.
Add the bouillon and half of the butter.
Cook until tender and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Fry the flour in the remaining butter until pale golden.
Add the roux to the cabbage.
Cook gently, covered, a little longer until the sauce thickens.

name: Cabbage stuffed with mushroom filling
summary: Cabbage quarters layered with a filling of dried porcini mushrooms, rice, and eggs, cooked gently, covered, in sauce.

ingredients.name: white or savoy cabbage
ingredients.note: heads; orig. 2–3 heads; lower bound used

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1–2 tbsp; upper bound used, for the filling and sauce

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling and for the sauce; mushroom cooking broth may be used for the sauce

steps: Clean the cabbage and cut each head into four quarters.
Parboil the cabbage in salted water, leaving it half-firm.
Drain and squeeze out the cabbage.
Boil the porcini mushrooms in water.
Chop the cooked mushrooms and the onions.
Sauté the mushrooms and onions in part of the butter.
Boil the rice in water.
Mix the mushrooms with the rice, salt, pepper, and eggs.
Place the filling between the leaves of the cabbage quarters.
Tie the quarters with kitchen twine.
Pack the cabbage tightly in a saucepan.
Prepare a sauce from the flour, remaining butter, and boiling water or mushroom cooking broth.
Pour the sauce over the cabbage.
Cook gently, covered, until tender.
Sprinkle with the crushed rusks before serving.

name: Brussels sprouts with butter and rusks
summary: Boiled Brussels sprouts topped with butter browned with crushed rusks.

ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts
ingredients.note: small heads only; orig. 1 funt; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the water; the tablespoon in the ingredient list refers to the butter

steps: Detach the small Brussels sprout heads from the stalk, discarding the large leaves and stalk.
Boil the Brussels sprouts in boiling salted water.
Drain the Brussels sprouts.
Transfer the Brussels sprouts to a platter.
Crush the rusks.
Brown the butter with the crushed rusks.
Pour the butter and rusks over the Brussels sprouts.

name: Baked cabbage with béchamel and mutton breast
summary: Cabbage baked with a milk sauce thickened with egg yolks, served with a prepared mutton breast.

ingredients.name: white cabbage
ingredients.note: heads; orig. 2–3 heads; lower bound used

ingredients.name: mutton breast, boiled and fried in butter and rusks

steps: Cut the cabbage into pieces the size of łazanki pasta squares.
Boil the cabbage in salted water until tender.
Drain the cabbage.
Melt the butter.
Fry the flour in the butter.
Thin the roux with the milk.
Stir in the egg yolks.
Heat the sauce, stirring.
Transfer the cabbage to an ovenproof dish.
Pour the sauce over the cabbage.
Bake the cabbage in the oven until the top is browned.
Serve with the mutton breast boiled and fried in butter and rusks.

name: White cabbage with mutton
summary: Quarters of white cabbage braised in layers with mutton breasts and a roux.

ingredients.name: mutton cooking broth
ingredients.note: for pouring over the cabbage; reserve the broth obtained from parboiling the mutton breasts

steps: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage.
Cut the cabbage heads into quarters.
Boil the cabbage in salted water for 15 minutes.
Drain the cabbage.
Parboil the mutton breasts in water until half tender, reserving the broth.
Rinse the meat with cold water.
Skim the fat from the broth.
Cut the mutton into pieces.
Arrange alternating layers of cabbage and mutton in a casserole, finishing with cabbage.
Season the top with salt and pepper.
Pour the mutton broth over the layers.
Braise, covered.
At 60 minutes before serving, brown the flour in the butter.
Add the roux to the cabbage.
Braise until tender, cooking off the excess liquid.

name: Sour white cabbage with apples
summary: White cabbage cooked gently, covered, with sour apples and pork fat, thickened with a roux.

ingredients.name: bouillon
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of szklanki; taken as 2 szklanki; historical measure, converted approximately

steps: Shred the cabbage.
Scald the cabbage with boiling water.
Squeeze out the cabbage.
Transfer the cabbage to a saucepan.
Pour the hot bouillon over the cabbage.
Add the salt, pepper, and part of the fat.
Peel the apples.
Cut up the apples.
Add the apples to the cabbage.
Cook the cabbage and apples gently, covered, until tender.
Brown the flour in the remaining fat.
Stir the roux into the cabbage.
Cook off the excess liquid.

name: Sauerkraut with mushrooms and sour cream
summary: Sauerkraut cooked gently, covered, in dried porcini broth with sour cream and a butter roux.

ingredients.name: sauerkraut
ingredients.note: orig. 1½ kwarty; volume of sauerkraut; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka; amount from the ingredient list; historical measure, converted approximately

steps: Boil the porcini mushrooms in water until tender, reserving the broth.
Shred the cooked mushrooms.
Scald the sauerkraut with boiling water.
Drain the sauerkraut.
Pour the mushroom broth over the sauerkraut.
Add the shredded porcini.
Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauerkraut with the mushrooms.
Add the sour cream.
Brown the flour in the butter.
Stir the roux into the sauerkraut.
Cook gently, covered, until tender.

name: Artichokes with butter and rusks
summary: Boiled artichokes topped with butter browned with a crushed rusk.
steps: Trim the sharp tips from the artichoke leaves.
Remove the inedible fibrous chokes.
Rinse the artichokes in water with lemon.
Place the artichokes in a pot.
Cover them with boiling water seasoned with salt and sugar.
Boil for 30–40 minutes, until tender.
Drain the artichokes and arrange on a platter.
Brown the butter with the crushed rusk.
Pour the butter and rusk over the artichokes.

name: Potatoes fried with onion
summary: Sliced potatoes cooked gently, covered, in butter with onion until tender and browned.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. ½–three quarters of a garniec; 2–3 l, volume measure of potatoes (historical measure, converted approximately)

steps: Peel and rinse the potatoes.
Cut the potatoes into slices and season with salt.
Chop the onion, if using.
Melt the butter in a saucepan.
Sauté the onion in the butter.
Add the potatoes.
Cook gently, covered, over low heat until the potatoes are tender and browned.

name: Potato balls fried in butter
summary: Balls scooped from raw potatoes, scalded and fried in butter.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. 1–1½ kwarty; 1–1.5 l, volume measure of potatoes (historical measure, converted approximately)

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of tbsp; 30 ml, described in the method as a generous amount

steps: Peel the raw potatoes.
Using a melon baller, scoop small balls from the potatoes.
Scald the balls with boiling water.
Season the balls with fine salt.
Melt the butter in a frying pan or saucepan.
Fry the potato balls in the butter until tender.

name: Gooseberry Preserves
summary: Preserves made from unripe gooseberries, prepared over several days in a vanilla-scented sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: unripe gooseberries
ingredients.note: large, fleshy; orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: divide into two equal parts; orig. one kilogram

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: piece of a pod tied in thin muslin

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, blanching, chilling, and preparing a light syrup; amount not specified

steps: Clean the gooseberries and remove the seeds with a thin tool.
Place the cleaned fruit into cold water.
Transfer the drained gooseberries into boiling water and remove the pot from the heat until the fruit turns slightly pale and softens.
Transfer the fruit with a slotted spoon into ice-cold water.
Leave the gooseberries in the ice water in a cool place for about 120 minutes.
Drain the fruit thoroughly on a sieve.
Prepare a light syrup from water and 500 g of sugar, adding the vanilla tied in thin muslin.
Pour the completely cooled syrup over the gooseberries in a jar.
Set the fruit in the syrup aside for about 1440 minutes.
Pour off the syrup and boil it with the remaining 500 g of sugar.
Pour the completely cooled syrup over the gooseberries again.
Repeat pouring off, boiling, cooling the syrup, and pouring it over the fruit twice more, waiting about 1440 minutes each time.
Bring the gooseberries to a boil in the thickened syrup, heating them only briefly.
Transfer the preserves to a bowl to cool.
Pack the cooled preserves into very clean, thoroughly dried jars.

name: Pineapple in Syrup
summary: Thin pineapple slices macerated in sugar and then cooked in a thick syrup.

ingredients.name: caster sugar
ingredients.note: for layering over the pineapple; orig. one kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the separate syrup; orig. one kilogram

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for moistening the sugar for the syrup, only as much as the sugar absorbs; amount not specified

steps: Peel the pineapple and cut it into thin slices.
Layer 500 g of pineapple in a glass jar, sprinkling generously with 1000 g of caster sugar.
Leave the jar in a warm place for 1440 minutes so the sugar dissolves.
Moisten the remaining 1000 g of sugar with as much water as the sugar absorbs.
Boil into a fairly thick syrup.
Add the pineapple along with its released juice to the boiling syrup.
Bring the mixture to a boil several times over low heat.
Pour into a bowl and leave until the next day.
The next day, boil again until the syrup thickens.
Test a drop of syrup on a cold knife: stop cooking when the drop thickens and does not spread.
Leave the pineapple to cool.
Pour the excess syrup into bottles.

name: Pineapple Preserves
summary: Pineapple slices steeped over successive days in progressively warmer syrup and briefly boiled at the end.

ingredients.name: pineapple
ingredients.note: peeled and trimmed; orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: divide into two equal parts; orig. one and a quarter kilograms

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: only as much as the sugar absorbs when moistened; amount not specified

steps: Peel and trim the pineapple.
Cut it into slices and weigh out 500 g.
Moisten 625 g of sugar with only as much water as the sugar absorbs.
Boil it into a thick syrup, skimming the foam carefully.
Pour the slightly cooled syrup over the pineapple and leave in a cool place until the next day.
On the second day, pour the syrup off into a pot.
Add the remaining 625 g of sugar and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Pour the syrup, slightly warmer than before, over the pineapple and leave until the third day.
On the third day, pour off and boil the syrup again without adding sugar.
Pour the even warmer, thick syrup over the fruit and leave until the fourth day.
On the fourth day, place the pineapple into the rapidly boiling syrup.
Simmer over very low heat for a few minutes.

name: Watermelon Rind Preserves with Ginger
summary: Pieces of white watermelon rind seasoned with ginger and white pepper, prepared in syrup over several days.

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: for generous sprinkling; amount not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for parboiling and preparing the syrup; amount not specified

steps: Trim the white part of the watermelon rind and cut it into oblong pieces.
Drop the pieces into boiling water and parboil, leaving them still slightly firm.
Drain them on a sieve.
Trim the pieces to an even shape and arrange them on a platter.
Sprinkle generously with ginger and white pepper.
Leave for 1440 minutes.
Prepare a clear syrup from 1000 g of sugar and water.
Pour the cooled syrup over the watermelon rind.
For the next three days, repeat pouring off, straining through muslin, boiling, and cooling the syrup before pouring it over the fruit again.
When the syrup is sufficiently thick, place the watermelon rind into the boiling syrup and bring to a boil once.
Remove the watermelon rind pieces and leave them to cool.
Arrange the watermelon rind in jars.
Pour the cooled, clarified syrup over it.

name: Lemon Preserves
summary: Lemons soaked and boiled at length, then gradually steeped in progressively thicker syrup.

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: the source specifies 5–6 pieces; 5 was used

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: divide into three 500 g portions; orig. one and a half kilograms

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, boiling, and the syrup; amounts not specified

steps: Soak the lemons in boiled, cold water for 14400 minutes, changing the water every 1440 minutes.
Prick the fruit densely with a wooden skewer.
Arrange the lemons side by side in a pot and cover with fresh, boiled, cooled water.
Simmer over low heat for about 300 minutes, until the fruit is completely tender.
Transfer the tender lemons to a platter lined with a cloth.
Leave to cool completely, if necessary until the next day, about 1440 minutes.
Cut the fruit into slices or quarters and remove the seeds.
Boil a light syrup from the first 500 g of sugar and water.
Cool the syrup before pouring it over the lemons.
Leave the lemons in the syrup until the next day, about 1440 minutes.
Pour off the syrup, add the second 500 g of sugar, and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Pour the lukewarm syrup over the lemons and leave until the third day, about 1440 minutes.
Pour off the syrup, add the final 500 g of sugar, and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Pour the slightly warmer, but not hot, syrup over the lemons and leave for 7200 minutes.
If the syrup becomes watery, boil it again until thickened, cool it, and pour it back over the fruit; after a few hours, transfer into jars, seal, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Lemon Preserves Steeped in Cold Syrup
summary: Lemon slices soaked at length, then steeped over four days in a gradually thickened, cooled syrup.

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: weight after boiling, slicing, and removing seeds; orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: added gradually over four days; orig. one kilogram

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, boiling, rinsing, and the syrup; amounts not specified

steps: Soak the lemons in water for 7200 minutes, changing the water every 1440 minutes.
Cover the fruit with cold, boiled water in a pot.
Boil until tender enough to be easily pierced.
Leave the lemons in the water to cool slowly.
Cut the fruit into slices.
Remove the seeds.
Weigh out 500 g of the prepared lemons.
Rinse the slices with water.
Drain the lemons and place them in a jar.
Boil a light syrup from part of the sugar and water, reserving the rest of the sugar for the following days.
Cool the syrup completely and pour it over the lemons.
Leave until the next day, about 1440 minutes.
On the second day, pour off the syrup, add part of the remaining sugar, and bring to a boil again.
Cool the syrup before pouring it over the lemons again.
Repeat pouring off, adding sugar, boiling, and cooling the syrup on the third and fourth days, waiting about 1440 minutes between steepings and using 1000 g of sugar in total.

name: White Sweet Cherry Preserves
summary: White sweet cherries briefly cooked in a very thick syrup with vanilla.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for a very thick syrup; amount not specified, inferred from the source's instruction to prepare the syrup without rose water

ingredients.name: vanilla
ingredients.note: piece of a pod wrapped in muslin; the source does not specify the size

steps: Pit the sweet cherries.
Boil a very thick syrup from the sugar and water.
Wrap a piece of vanilla in white muslin.
Place the wrapped vanilla into the syrup.
Add the sweet cherries to the syrup.
Cook briefly so the fruit does not lose its color.
Set the preserves aside to cool.
Transfer into jars.
Seal the jars tightly.

name: Cornelian Cherry Preserves in Wine
summary: Ripe Cornelian cherries slowly cooked in a sugar and wine syrup.
steps: Pit the Cornelian cherries.
Bring a syrup of the sugar and wine to a boil.
Skim the foam carefully from the syrup.
Add the prepared Cornelian cherries.
Simmer over very low heat for 60 minutes, skimming the foam carefully and removing the pot from the heat while skimming.
Check the thickness of the syrup by placing a drop on a knife.
Set the preserves aside to cool completely once the syrup has thickened.
Transfer into jars.
Store in a cool, dry place.

name: Hawthorn or Rosehip Preserve
summary: Preserve made from large garden hawthorn berries or rosehips, pitted and simmered until translucent in a thick lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2 glasses for the syrup, plus cold and boiling water for soaking and blanching the fruit

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of the whole lemon and a few small pieces of peel

steps: Remove the stems from large garden hawthorn berries picked before the frosts, pit the seeds, and drop the berries immediately into cold water.
Transfer the rinsed berries to boiling water and blanch covered until tender, taking care that they do not burst.
Transfer the parboiled hawthorn berries twice into progressively colder water, then spread on a sieve to drain thoroughly.

For every 500 g of pitted hawthorn berries, boil a syrup from 1.5 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water, adding the juice of 1 lemon, a few pieces of lemon peel, and optionally a few tablespoons of gooseberry juice.
When the syrup becomes clear and begins to pearl, add the drained hawthorn berries and simmer slowly until the fruit becomes translucent and sinks to the bottom; once cooled, transfer to jars.

name: Hawthorn Preserve Another Way
summary: Three-day preserve of pitted hawthorn berries steeped in progressively thickened sugar syrup with lemon juice.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: divided into portions: 500 g on the first day and 250 g each on the second and third days

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice squeezed in toward the end of cooking

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the syrup and cold water for soaking and blanching the hawthorn berries

steps: Pit the hawthorn berries, dropping them into cold water, then rinse and simmer in fresh water over very low heat until soft without bursting.
Drain the hawthorn berries in a colander, rinse with cold water, and leave on a sieve to drain.
Boil a light syrup from 500 g of sugar and water, skim, strain through muslin, and pour lukewarm over the fruit in a bowl for a day.
On the second day, drain the syrup, add 250 g of sugar, bring to a boil, skim, strain, and pour the lukewarm syrup back over the hawthorn berries.

On the third day, drain the syrup, add the remaining 250 g of sugar, bring to a boil, strain, add the hawthorn berries and the juice of half a lemon, and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes; once cooled, transfer to jars.

name: Hawthorn Preserve Yet Another Way
summary: Preserve of pitted hawthorn berries simmered in a syrup of sugar, water, and white wine.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1 glass for the syrup, plus boiling water for blanching the fruit

steps: Remove the stems from ripe hawthorn berries, pit the seeds, weigh out 500 g of fruit, blanch in boiling water until tender (taking care that they do not burst), and drain on a sieve.
Boil a thick syrup from 1 kg of sugar, 250 ml of water, and 250 ml of white wine, skimming off the foam carefully.
Add the drained hawthorn berries to the boiling syrup and cook for 30 minutes — first over higher and then over lower heat.
Transfer the cooled preserve into jars, tie tightly, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Pears in Syrup
summary: Preserve of whole peeled and cored white pears cooked over two days in a lemon and vanilla syrup.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: unripe white varieties such as Williams bon chrétien, peeled and cored from the bottom

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: chopped into small pieces, divided into two equal parts

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 1 lemon for the water and juice of 1 lemon for the syrup

ingredients.name: vanilla bean
ingredients.note: piece of pod tied in muslin, optional for aroma

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup and cold water for soaking the peeled pears

steps: Peel the pears, trim the stems in half, core the seeds from the bottom, and place the fruit immediately into cold water acidulated with the juice of 1 lemon.
Boil a light syrup from half of the sugar (375 g) and the water, squeeze in the juice of the second lemon, add the drained pears, and cook until tender, then leave in the syrup until the next day.
On the second day, drain the syrup, add the remaining 375 g of sugar and the piece of vanilla bean tied in muslin, and bring to a boil.
Add the pears to the boiling syrup and simmer over low heat until translucent.
Once cooled, arrange the pears with the syrup in jars, tie tightly, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Pears (Alternative Method)
summary: Four-day preserve of whole peeled pears parboiled until tender and steeped daily in progressively thicker and warmer lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: medium-sized, half-ripe pears (bon chrétien, cukrówki, bergamoty, or panny varieties)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 750 g for the first syrup and 250 g added on each of the 3 following days

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2.5 glassfuls for the syrup, plus cold and hot water for soaking and parboiling the pears

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 1 lemon for the cold water and juice of 1 lemon for the syrup

steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stems intact, remove the cores from the bottom, and immediately place the fruit in cold water acidulated with the juice of 1 lemon.
Transfer the pears to a pan of hot water, cook until tender (until a straw passes easily through the fruit), and spread on a sieve to drain completely.
Make a syrup from 750 g of sugar and 625 ml (2.5 glassfuls) of water, skim, add the juice of the second lemon, let cool, and pour over the pears in a dish.
For the next three days, drain the syrup daily, strain through a fine sieve or muslin, add 250 g of sugar each day, boil and skim, and pour the progressively warmer syrup back over the pears.
On the fourth day, place the pears into the cooled syrup, bring to a single boil, skim, and once completely cooled, pack into dry jars.

name: Unpeeled Pears
summary: Preserve of half-ripe bergamot pears cooked whole in their skins over two days.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 500 g on the first day and 500 g on the second day

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1.5 glasses for the first syrup, plus cold water for soaking

steps: Select fine, half-ripe bergamot pears, prick them densely with a pin, trim the stems slightly, core the seeds from the bottom, and drop into cold water.
Boil a thin syrup from 500 g of sugar and 375 ml (1.5 glasses) of water, add the drained pears, and cook until tender, then set aside until the next day.
On the second day, drain the syrup, strain through a fine sieve or muslin, add the remaining 500 g of sugar, and simmer with the pears until the syrup thickens properly.
Transfer the cooled pears together with the syrup into jars and seal tightly.

name: French-Style Pears
summary: Pear quarters macerated overnight in sugar with lemon juice and a splash of rum, then simmered in a thick syrup with lemon peel.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: panny or bon chrétien varieties, peeled and quartered

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 1 lemon for the water and the juice and thinly sliced peel of a second lemon for the preserve

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: good quality, for sprinkling the layers

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for soaking the pears after peeling

steps: Peel the pears, halve them, remove the cores, cut into quarters, and drop into cold water acidulated with the juice of 1 lemon.
In a bowl, arrange alternating layers of fine sugar and drained pear quarters, sprinkling each layer with the juice of the second lemon and a little rum; let stand until the next day.
On the second day, remove the pears from the bowl, pour the resulting syrup into a pan, bring to a boil, and skim thoroughly.
Add the pears to the boiling syrup and simmer until the syrup thickens and the fruit becomes translucent.
Once completely cooled, transfer the preserve into jars, adding thinly sliced lemon peel, and seal tightly.

name: Apples in Syrup
summary: Preserve of unpeeled White Transparent apple slices rubbed with lemon and cooked in batches in a clear sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: White Transparent apples
ingredients.note: half-ripe, unpeeled, sliced into rounds with the cores removed

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice for the water, halved lemon for rubbing the slices, and thinly sliced peel for the jars

ingredients.name: vanilla bean
ingredients.note: several small pieces for layering in the jars, optional

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the syrup, adding 2 tablespoons at a time during cooking, and cold water for soaking

steps: Slice the unpeeled White Transparent apples into rounds, remove the cores, and drop into cold water with lemon juice, then rub each slice on both sides with a lemon half after removing from the water.
Boil a moderately thin syrup from 1 kg of sugar and water, leave 1/3 of the syrup in the pan, and pour the rest into a separate vessel.
Arrange a single layer of apple slices on the boiling syrup and simmer over very low heat, skimming, until translucent.

Remove the cooked slices with a slotted spoon onto a platter, and before adding the next batch of apples, pour a little of the reserved cold syrup and 2 tablespoons of water into the pan so that the syrup stays pale.
Arrange the cooked apples in jars, layering with thinly sliced lemon peel or small pieces of vanilla bean, and pour the cooled pale syrup over them until the fruit is completely covered.

name: Apples Another Way
summary: Preserve of thin julienne strips of White Transparent apples generously tossed with lemon juice and simmered in a thick sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: White Transparent apples
ingredients.note: half-unripe, peeled and cut into thin oblong strips

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juicy, squeezed juice with seeds removed

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: for moistening the tissue paper rounds when sealing the jars

steps: Quickly peel the half-unripe White Transparent apples, cut into thin oblong strips, and immediately toss with the juice squeezed from 2 lemons.
Boil a thick, pearling syrup in a stoneware pan from 750 g of sugar and 375 ml (1.5 glasses) of water.
Add the prepared apples with the lemon juice to the boiling syrup and simmer for 15–20 minutes — first over higher and then over lower heat — until the preserve thickens.
Transfer the cooled preserve into jars, cover with a parchment round dipped in rum, tie tightly, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Crabapples
summary: Three-day preserve of whole pricked crabapples parboiled until tender and steeped in progressively sweetened syrup.

ingredients.name: crabapples
ingredients.note: freshly picked, not overly ripe, blemish-free

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 500 g on the first day, 750 g on the second day, and 125 g on the third day

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1 glass for the syrup, plus cold water for parboiling and chilling the fruit

steps: Clean the crabapples, prick with a wooden pin, place in a pan of cold water, and heat very carefully over low heat until slightly softened without bursting.
Drain the parboiled crabapples, cover briefly with cold water, then drain thoroughly on a sieve.
Briefly boil a light syrup from 500 g of sugar and 250 ml (1 glass) of water, cool it, and pour over the crabapples for a day.
On the second day, drain the syrup, add 750 g of sugar, bring to a boil, and pour the warm syrup back over the fruit.
On the third day, drain the syrup, add the remaining 125 g of sugar, bring to a boil, drop in the crabapples for a brief single boil, and transfer to jars once cooled.

name: Crabapples Another Way
summary: Crabapples blanched in boiling water and shocked in ice water, then simmered in a thick syrup scented with rose or vanilla.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: or up to 1 kg if more syrup is desired

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus cold, boiling, and ice-cold water with ice for blanching the fruit

steps: Trim the crabapple stems in half, prick the fruit deeply with a wooden pin, and submerge in cold water for 15 minutes.
Transfer the crabapples to boiling water for 10 minutes, then remove and submerge in cold water with ice for 30 minutes, and dry thoroughly.
Boil a fairly thick syrup from 750 g of sugar and water (optionally with rose syrup or vanilla), add the dried crabapples, and simmer slowly, skimming carefully.
Remove the fruit onto a platter as each piece softens, and once completely cooled, pack into jars, cover with the syrup, and tie tightly.

name: Rowanberries in Syrup
summary: Preserve of frost-sweetened rowanberries scalded in boiling water, steeped overnight in rose-scented syrup, and simmered until translucent.

ingredients.name: rowanberries
ingredients.note: very ripe, picked after the first frosts

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: chopped into small pieces, or 750 g for a tarter flavor

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1.5 glasses for the syrup, plus boiling and cold water for scalding the berries

steps: Prick each frost-sweetened rowanberry with a wooden pin, scald with boiling water, immediately rinse with cold water on a sieve, and leave to drain thoroughly (omit the scalding for a sharper flavor).
Boil a syrup from 1 kg of sugar, 375 ml (1.5 glasses) of water, and optionally 2 tablespoons of rose water, and let cool.
Add the drained rowanberries to the cooled syrup and leave overnight.
On the second day, simmer the preserve — first over higher and then over lower heat — skimming carefully and taking care that the syrup does not thicken excessively; once cooled, transfer to jars.

name: Raspberry jam
summary: A classic nineteenth-century jam of whole, carefully picked raspberries chilled overnight and cooked in a thick sugar syrup without stirring with a spoon.

ingredients.name: fresh raspberries
ingredients.note: large, picked on a dry day, orig. half a kilogram

steps: Pick over large firm raspberries very carefully, lay them in a single layer on platters or plates, and put them overnight (about 8 hours) in a cool cellar or the refrigerator.
The next day, cook a syrup from 1 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water, skimming carefully, until it is clear and begins to bead.
Tip the raspberries into the boiling syrup without taking the pan off the heat, and cook first over a higher heat and then over a lower one, shaking the pan often so the fruit cooks evenly.
Skim the foam that rises with a spoon, gently, without touching the raspberries themselves, until a drop of syrup taken on a knife begins to thicken and falls slowly.
Leave the jam to cool completely, then spoon the fruit into scalded jars, cover them with the syrup strained through a small sieve, and seal them.

name: Raspberry jam, Bukovina way
summary: Jam of large raspberries sprinkled with rum and chilled on ice, cooked in a very thick syrup by four quick boils over high heat, with the pan cooled on ice between them.

ingredients.name: fresh raspberries
ingredients.note: large, not overripe, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: for sprinkling the raspberries before chilling

steps: Pick over large firm raspberries carefully, lay them on a platter, sprinkle them with good rum, and put them on ice or in a very cold refrigerator for about 3 hours.
Cook a very thick syrup from 1 kg of sugar and 375 ml of water.
Tip the chilled raspberries straight into the boiling syrup over a very high heat so they come quickly to the boil and rise to the top. Then move the pan at once onto a bowl of ice to cool fast.
Repeat the quick boil over very high heat and the cooling on ice four times (five times if needed), skimming carefully each time and lifting out the seeds that float up.
Pack the cooled raspberries into jars and cover them with the clear syrup strained through a fine sieve.

name: Raspberry jam, the plain way
summary: A simple one-day jam of half a kilogram of fresh raspberries dropped straight into a beading syrup of a kilogram of sugar and cooked slowly until thick.

ingredients.name: fresh raspberries
ingredients.note: dry, not overripe, orig. half a kilogram

steps: Pick over dry firm raspberries carefully, removing the stems.
Put the sugar into a wide pan, pour in 400 ml of water, bring it to the boil and skim it, cooking the syrup until it is clear, thick and beginning to bead.
Drop the raspberries into the boiling syrup and cook slowly, first over a higher heat and then over low heat, skimming carefully with a spoon so the fruit is not crushed.

When a drop of syrup taken on a knife thickens and falls slowly, take the pan off the heat, cool the jam, lift the loose seeds out of the syrup on a sieve, and pack the raspberries with the clear syrup into jars.

name: Raspberry jam covered with hot syrup
summary: Jam of large raspberries covered with hot thick sugar syrup in a pan stood in cold water, chilled overnight and finished the next day.

ingredients.name: fresh raspberries
ingredients.note: large and dry, orig. half a kilogram

steps: Bring a thick syrup to the boil from 1 kg of sugar and 375 ml of water.

Put the picked-over raspberries into a stoneware or enamel pan stood in a bowl of cold water, cover the fruit with the hot syrup, and leave it overnight (about 8 hours) in a cool place or the refrigerator.
The next day, bring the raspberries to the boil in the syrup, skim carefully, and cook first over a higher heat and then over a lower and lower heat until the right thickness.
Lift out the floating seeds with a teaspoon, cool the jam, and pack it into scalded jars.

name: Melon jam with rum
summary: Jam of half-ripe melon cut into square pieces, cooked briefly, shocked in iced water, macerated for three hours in rum and cooked in a thick syrup.

ingredients.name: half-ripe melon
ingredients.note: peeled and seeded, orig. half a kilogram of raw melon

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1.5 small glasses for the syrup, plus water for the brief cooking and iced water for shocking

steps: Peel a half-ripe melon, cut out the seed cavity, and cut the flesh into neat long square pieces about the size of small apple quarters.

Put the melon into a pot, cover it with cold water, and cook for about 10 minutes until just soft (do not let it fall apart). Then drain it in a colander, rinse it several times with iced water, and leave it for 60 minutes to drain.
Pack the drained melon tightly on a platter, sprinkle it generously with good rum, and leave it for 3 hours.

Bring a thick syrup to the boil from 1 kg of sugar and 375 ml of water, add the melon and the rum, and cook first over a higher heat and then over a lower and lower heat, skimming, until the syrup thickens. Once cool, pack it into jars.

name: Melon jam, another way
summary: A three-day jam of pieces of half-ripe melon cooked briefly in boiling water and covered on three successive days with an ever thicker sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: half-ripe melon
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into square pieces, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 kg in all: 500 g on the first day, 250 g on the second and 250 g on the third

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus boiling water for the brief cooking

steps: Peel a half-ripe melon, remove the seed cavity, cut the flesh into square pieces, drop them into boiling water, and bring it once to a hard boil (do not let them fall apart). Then drain them and put them in a bowl.
Cook a fairly thick syrup from 500 g of sugar and 350 ml of water, cover the melon with the warm syrup, and leave it for 24 hours.
On the second day, pour the syrup off through muslin, add 250 g of sugar, bring it to the boil, and cover the melon with the hot syrup for another day.

On the third day, pour off the syrup again, add the remaining 250 g of sugar, boil it until thick, drop the melon into the boiling syrup, bring them to the boil once together, and once cool pack them into jars.

name: Melon jam, Bukovina way
summary: A jam of several days: pieces of half-ripe melon firmed in limewater, rinsed for two days, and covered again and again with hot sugar syrup, lemon juice and rum.

ingredients.name: half-ripe melon
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into pieces, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: slaked food-grade lime
ingredients.note: calcium hydroxide for the bath that firms the fruit, orig. half a handful per 1 melon

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, rinsing, the brief boil, and the syrup

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram (750 g for the first syrup and 250 g on the third day)

steps: Peel a fleshy half-ripe melon, remove the seed cavity, cut the flesh into neat pieces, and soak them for 12 hours in water with 15 g of slaked food-grade lime.

Take out the pieces, rinse them very thoroughly in several waters, then soak them in clean cold water for 2 days, changing the water several times. After that, cover them with fresh cold water, bring it to the boil once, drain them on a sieve, and cool them.
Cook a syrup from 750 g of sugar and 350 ml of water, add the cooled melon, bring it to the boil once, and leave it in the syrup for 24 hours.
For the next 2 days, take the pieces out each day, prick them densely with a wooden toothpick, and put them back into the strained, reboiled syrup.

On the third day, take out the melon, add the remaining 250 g of sugar, the lemon juice and a small glass (30 ml) of rum to the syrup, boil it until thick, put the melon back in, bring it once to a good boil, and once cool pack it into jars.

name: Watermelon Rind in Syrup
summary: Preserve of firm white watermelon rind cut into squares or strips and simmered over low heat in a thick lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: watermelon rind
ingredients.note: white layer of watermelon trimmed of the green skin and pink flesh

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: in lumps for the syrup plus a little fine sugar for dusting

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 0.5 lemon for the cold water and grated zest and juice of 2 lemons for the syrup

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1.5 glasses for the syrup, plus cold and boiling water for parboiling the rind

steps: Trim the white layer of watermelon rind of its green outer skin and pink flesh, submerge in cold water with the juice of half a lemon, then cut into even squares or strips and parboil in boiling water until it begins to soften.
Rub the zest of 2 lemons onto the sugar lumps (1 kg), chop the sugar, place in a stoneware pan, pour in 375 ml (1.5 glasses) of water, and boil a thick syrup with the juice of the 2 lemons.
Add the parboiled watermelon rind to the boiling syrup and simmer very slowly over low heat, skimming thoroughly.
During cooking, remove the pan from the heat several times and lightly dust the fruit on top with fine sugar; cool the finished preserve and transfer to jars.

name: Jam of whole apricots
summary: A four-day jam of whole apricots pricked to the stone, blanched in hot water and cooked again and again in an ever thicker sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: apricots
ingredients.note: almost ripe, firm, whole with the stone, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram (500 g on the first day, plus 500 g added gradually over the next 3 days)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: hot, for blanching the apricots and for the syrup

steps: Prick almost-ripe firm apricots densely with a wooden toothpick right to the stone, cover them with hot (not boiling) water so it covers them, and leave them for 60 minutes.

Lift out the apricots. Cook a syrup from the blanching water and 500 g of sugar, put the slightly cooled apricots into it, bring it to the boil a few times over low heat, and leave it until the next day.

For the next 3 days, take the apricots out each day, strain the syrup, add a portion of the remaining sugar (500 g in all), bring the syrup to the boil, skim it, and put the apricots back so they boil once in the syrup, shaking the pan often.
Once fully cooked and cool, pack the apricots and syrup into scalded jars and seal them.

name: Konfitura z zielonych orzechów włoskich (green walnut preserve)
summary: Young green walnuts simmered in thick sugar syrup, studded with cloves and cinnamon.

ingredients.name: green walnuts
ingredients.note: young, soft; orig. half a kilogr.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a kilogr.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.note: for studding the walnuts; orig. a few

ingredients.name: cinnamon bark pieces
ingredients.note: for studding the walnuts; amount not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the walnuts and cloves, boiling, and syrup; amount not specified

steps: Prick the walnuts thoroughly all over with a wooden skewer.
Soak them in cold water for 12960 minutes, changing the water morning and evening.
Drain the walnuts in a sieve.
Boil them in fresh water until a thick skewer pierces them easily.
Drain the boiled walnuts in a sieve.
Soak the cloves in water.
Stud the walnuts with the soaked cloves and small pieces of cinnamon.
Cook a syrup from 750 g sugar and water.
Simmer the walnuts in the boiling syrup until soft.
Set everything aside to cool.
Transfer the walnuts into jars.
Boil the remaining syrup until thickened.
Pour the completely cooled syrup over the walnuts.
If the syrup becomes watery after some time, boil it again and pour it over the walnuts once cooled.

name: Konfitura z białych porzeczek z pestkami (White currant preserve with seeds)
summary: White currants briefly simmered in thick sugar syrup with seeds left intact.

ingredients.name: white currants
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogr.; leave the seeds in

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a kilogr.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for rinsing and preparing very thick syrup; amount not specified

steps: Rinse the white currants in cold water.
Leave on a sieve until very well drained.
Prepare a very thick syrup from sugar and water; the source does not specify the water amount.
Add the currants to the vigorously boiling syrup.
Simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes, skimming off the foam very carefully.

name: Konfitura z poziomek (Wild strawberry preserve)
summary: Whole wild strawberries gently simmered in thick sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: wild strawberries
ingredients.note: large, dry, and not overripe; orig. half a kilogr.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: upper value of the 375–500 ml range; orig. one and a half or two small szklanki

steps: Select large, dry, and not overripe wild strawberries.
Crush the sugar.
Place the sugar and water in a pot.
Cook a thick syrup, carefully skimming the foam, until it begins to pearl.
Add the wild strawberries to the syrup.
Bring the preserve to a boil three times over moderate heat, moving the pot off the heat each time to skim the foam.
Continue cooking over low heat for about 15 minutes, shaking the pot frequently.
Test a drop of syrup on a cold knife: it should run off slowly and thicken as it flows.
Cool the preserve.
Transfer the preserve into jars.
Seal the jars with lids.

name: Konfitura z białych poziomek ananasowych (White pineberry preserve)
summary: Delicate white pineberries chilled with rum and simmered in sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: white pineberries
ingredients.note: large, ripe, and dry; orig. half a kilogr.

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: for generous sprinkling over the fruit; amount not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki

steps: Select large, ripe, and dry white pineberries.
Arrange the berries on plates in a single layer.
Sprinkle the berries generously with rum.
Chill the berries in the refrigerator for 240–300 minutes.
Crush the sugar.
Place the sugar and water in a pot.
Bring the syrup to a boil, carefully skimming the foam.
Cook the syrup until it thickens and begins to pearl.
Add the chilled berries to the syrup.
Cook over moderate heat, frequently and gently shaking the pot and skimming the foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the syrup with fruit thickens.
Cool the preserve.
Transfer the preserve into jars.
Seal the jars with lids.

name: Konfitura z zielonych pomidorów (Green tomato preserve)
summary: Green tomatoes parboiled and simmered in sugar syrup with lemon juice.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters or one kilogr.; source allows 750–1000 g

steps: Cut the tomatoes in half and remove the seeds.
Cover with cold water and bring slowly to a boil.
Remove the tomatoes and drain in a sieve lined with a clean cloth.
Boil half of the sugar with 250 ml water and skim off the foam.
Add the lemon juice and bring the syrup to a boil again.
Pour the hot syrup over the tomatoes and set aside overnight, approximately 720 minutes.
The next day, remove the tomatoes and add the remaining sugar to the syrup.
Boil the syrup, skim off the foam, and add the tomatoes.
Simmer until the syrup thickens.
Cool the preserve, transfer into jars, and seal.

name: Konfitura z czerwonych pomidorów (Red tomato preserve)
summary: Halved ripe tomatoes macerated with rum and simmered in sugar syrup with lemon juice.

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: for sprinkling over the tomatoes; amount not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki

steps: Cut the tomatoes in half and scoop out the seeds.
Arrange the halves on a platter and sprinkle with rum.
Set aside in a cool place for 1440 minutes.
Boil the sugar with water into a thick syrup and skim off the foam carefully.
Add the tomatoes to the syrup and cook first over higher, then lower heat until the syrup thickens.
Towards the end, stir in the lemon juice and bring to a boil again.
Cool the preserve, transfer into jars, and seal.

name: Gorzkie pomarańczki w syropie (Bitter oranges in syrup)
summary: Whole bitter oranges soaked, simmered, and gradually steeped in sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one kilogr.; divide into 500 g, 250 g, and 250 g

ingredients.name: light sugar syrup
ingredients.note: for the first pouring; amount and proportions not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, boiling, and preparing the main syrup; amount not specified

steps: Soak the bitter oranges in cold water for 14 400 minutes, changing the water daily.
Prick each bitter orange thoroughly with a wooden toothpick.
Cover with fresh water and boil for 210 minutes.
Drain the oranges and wrap them gently in a clean cloth so they cool slowly without losing their shape.
Cover the cold bitter oranges with light sugar syrup and set aside for 1440 minutes.
Pour off all the light syrup.
Prepare a fresh syrup from 500 g sugar and water, the quantity of which is unspecified by the source.
Pour the lukewarm syrup over the oranges and set aside for 1440 minutes.
Remove the oranges, dissolve another 250 g sugar in the syrup, and pour the warmer syrup over the fruit for the next 1440 minutes.
Pour off the syrup, add the remaining 250 g sugar, and pour even hotter syrup over the fruit for 1440 minutes.
On the fourth day, heat the drained syrup to a boil and pour it over the fruit for another 1440 minutes.
On the fifth day, place the oranges into the boiling syrup and bring to a boil several times.
Once completely cooled, transfer into jars, seal, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Mirabelle Plum Preserve
summary: Ripe mirabelle plums prepared over four days in a gradually thickened sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: half for the first syrup, the remainder for subsequent thickenings; orig. one kilogram

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, blanching, cooling, and the syrup; amount not specified

steps: Prick each mirabelle plum with a wooden skewer and immediately place into cold water.
Drain the fruit.
Scald them with boiling water in a pot until softened.
Transfer the mirabelle plums to very cold water.
Cook a light syrup from 500 g of sugar and water.
Cool the syrup completely.
Drain the mirabelle plums and cover with the cold syrup, pressing the fruit down lightly so they are completely submerged.
Leave until the next day, for about 1440 minutes.
Remove the fruit, add part of the remaining sugar to the syrup, and bring it to a boil.
Cool the syrup until lukewarm, pour it over the fruit, and leave for another 1440 minutes or so.
Remove the fruit, boil the syrup with the rest of the sugar, and pour the hot syrup over the mirabelle plums.
Leave until the fourth day, for another 1440 minutes or so.
Simmer the mirabelle plums in the boiling syrup, taking care not to overcook them.
Pack the fruit tightly into jars, pour the syrup over them, and press down lightly so they remain submerged.

name: Large Yellow Plum Preserve
summary: Large yellow plums steeped in increasingly hotter syrup for four days and simmered on the fifth day.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for scalding, cooling, and the syrup; amount not specified

ingredients.name: ice
ingredients.note: for the cooling bath; amount not specified

steps: Prick each plum with a wooden skewer and place into cold water.
Scald the plums with boiling water until tender.
Transfer the plums to cold water with ice.
Prepare a syrup from the sugar and water.
Pour the syrup over the plums for four days, using an increasingly hotter syrup each time.
Leave the fruit in the syrup between pourings until the next day, about 1440 minutes.
On the fifth day, simmer the plums in the syrup slowly, with pauses, until the syrup thickens, taking care that the fruit do not fall apart.

name: Sour cherries preserved in spirit
summary: Fresh Łutówka sour cherries scalded with boiling water, pricked and covered in a jar with hot thick sugar syrup, cinnamon and coriander, then combined the next day with diluted spirit and macerated for four weeks in the sun.

ingredients.name: sour cherries (łutówki)
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of ripe, freshly picked sour cherries, stems trimmed to half their length

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: orig. about 2 small pieces of cinnamon bark

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilogram of sugar per 1 kilogram of cherries

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1/3 part of the best spirit to 2/3 parts of boiled water

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml of boiled water to dilute the spirit (2/3 of the volume) and about 250 ml for the thick syrup (plus boiling water for blanching the cherries)

steps: Trim the stems of 1 kg of freshly picked, ripe Łutówka sour cherries to half their length, scald the fruit with boiling water, and leave it for 5 minutes on a warm metal tray to dry.
Prick each cherry with a wooden pin and pack them in a jar with 2 small pieces of cinnamon and a little coriander.
Cook a thick syrup from 250 g of sugar and 250 ml of water and pour it hot over the cherries in the jar until the next day.

The next day, add diluted spirit made from 250 ml of the best spirit (1/3 part) and 500 ml of boiled water (2/3 parts). Tie a cover securely over the jar and leave it in the sun for 4 weeks. Discard the spices before serving.

name: Apricots or peaches preserved in spirit
summary: Ripe apricots or peaches left whole with their stones, blanched, peeled and briefly cooked in a thick sugar syrup, then covered in the jar with the syrup mixed with diluted spirit.

ingredients.name: apricots or peaches
ingredients.note: orig. 3 kilograms of ripe but not overripe apricots or peaches

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilogram (250 g) of sugar for every half kilogram (500 g) of fruit

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of good spirit per 3 kg of fruit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml (half a litre) of boiled water to dilute the spirit, and about 1 l of water for the thick syrup (plus boiling water for blanching the fruit)

steps: Drop ripe but firm apricots or peaches into boiling water. When they float, lift them out and peel them, leaving the fruit whole with the stones (if the fruit is very ripe, do not blanch or peel it: wipe off the fuzz with a cloth and prick it with a wooden pin).

Cook a thick syrup from 1.5 kg of sugar and about 1 l of water (using 250 g of sugar for every 500 g of fruit). Put the fruit into the boiling syrup and bring it to the boil several times over low heat, taking care it does not burst.
Take the pan off the heat, lift the fruit out carefully, and pack it into a large jar.
Mix the still-hot syrup with 500 ml of good spirit diluted beforehand with 500 ml of boiled water, pour it over the fruit in the jar, and seal it.

name: Greengages preserved in spirit
summary: Ripe greengages blanched in water with lemon juice and fresh spinach to keep them green, covered twice with boiling sugar syrup, and preserved in the syrup mixed with spirit.

ingredients.name: greengages
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half kilograms of ripe but not overripe greengages (or mirabelles or pale plums)

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: the squeezed juice goes into the boiling water to keep the greengages green

ingredients.name: spinach
ingredients.note: orig. 1 handful of green spinach in the boiling water to keep the colour

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilogram (250 g) of sugar for every half kilogram (500 g) of fruit

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of good spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml (half a litre) of boiled water to dilute the spirit, and 500 ml of water for the thick syrup (plus boiling and cold water for blanching)

steps: Wipe ripe greengages with a cloth, prick them densely with a wooden pin, and drop them into boiling water with the juice of 2 lemons and a handful of green spinach.
Move the pan at once onto a lower heat. When the plums float, lift them out into cold water, and once completely cool drain them on a sieve.
