Cook a thick syrup from 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, add the drained greengages, bring it to the boil a couple of times, and leave them in the syrup until the next day.
On the second day, pour off the syrup, boil it, and pour it back over the plums.

On the third day, pour off the syrup, bring it to the boil, skim it carefully, mix it with 500 ml of spirit diluted with 500 ml of boiled water, and pour the cooled spirit syrup over the greengages packed in a jar. Seal it.

name: Pears preserved in spirit
summary: Smaller, firm pears cooked in sugar syrup on three successive days, then packed under the reduced syrup mixed with diluted spirit.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: smaller, not too ripe, of a fine variety

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: a juicy one; the squeezed juice goes into the cold water while peeling

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar per 1.5 kg of pears

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2 szklanki (500 ml) for the syrup, plus about 250 ml of boiled water to dilute the spirit (and water for softening and soaking the pears)

steps: Put the pears into hot water and keep them over low heat until they soften slightly and peel easily. Peel them and drop them at once into cold water with the juice of 1 juicy lemon.
Cook a syrup from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, put the pears into the boiling syrup, bring it to the boil once, and leave it until the next day.
On the second and the third day, pour off the syrup, bring it to the boil, put the pears back in, and bring it to the boil once more, taking care the fruit does not become too soft.
Pack the cooled pears into a jar. Mix the boiled-down syrup with 500 ml of spirit diluted with 250 ml of boiled water, pour it over the fruit, and seal the jar.

name: Green walnuts preserved in spirit
summary: Young green walnuts, completely soft, peeled, cooked in water with lemon juice, covered with boiling syrup for three days, and on the fourth day covered with the syrup mixed with spirit.

ingredients.name: young green walnuts
ingredients.note: completely soft, the skin peeled carefully

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: the squeezed juice goes into the boiling water while the walnuts cook

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for the syrup and 250 ml of boiled water to dilute the spirit (plus boiling water for cooking the walnuts)

steps: Peel young green, completely soft walnuts carefully with a penknife and drop them into boiling water acidulated with the juice of 1 lemon.
When the walnuts are soft, drain them and cover them with a thick syrup cooked from 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water.
For 3 days in a row, pour off the syrup each day, bring it to the boil, and pour it back over the walnuts.

On the fourth day, pack the walnuts into a jar, reduce the syrup until thick, mix it with 500 ml of spirit diluted with 250 ml of boiled water, strain it through fine-weave muslin over the walnuts, and seal the jar.

name: Russian ruffe fish soup (ucha z jazgarzy)
summary: A clear, spicy ruffe soup cooked with potatoes, parsley root, and onions retaining their thin yellow skin to give the broth a golden colour.

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.note: with only the innermost thin yellow skin left on

steps: Carefully scale the ruffe, snip off gills and tails with scissors, gut, salt, and set aside for 60 minutes before rinsing.
In a pot, bring 2 l of water to a boil with the parsley root quartered into 4 pieces, bay leaf, coarsely crushed peppercorns, and halved onions left in their thin yellow skins.
Peel the potatoes, cut into walnut-sized pieces (about 25 g), and drop into the simmering broth.
After cooking the potatoes for 5 minutes, add the rinsed ruffe and simmer for about 15–20 minutes until the fish flesh begins separating from the bones.
Remove the ruffe, flake the meat from the bones (discarding the heads), place the picked meat into a soup tureen, and ladle over the hot soup with potatoes.

name: Barszcz czysty z ziemniakami (clear beetroot soup with potatoes)
summary: Meatless clear beetroot soup made with root vegetable stock and boiled or baked beetroot, soured with vinegar or citric acid and served with potatoes.

ingredients.name: vinegar or citric acid
ingredients.note: 1 tablespoon of vinegar or 1 teaspoon of citric acid

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. 50 dkg, boiled or baked in their skins

steps: Wash the beetroots thoroughly and boil or bake them whole in their skins until tender.
Simmer the parsley root, carrot, and onion in 2 liters of water with the bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt to taste to make a vegetable stock.

Peel the cooked beetroots, cut them into thin julienne strips, add to the hot stock, and bring briefly to a single boil (if serving the borscht in cups, cut the beetroots into 4–6 pieces, simmer in the stock for 10 minutes, and strain).
Season the borscht with vinegar or citric acid so that it regains its deep ruby color.
Separately boil the potatoes in their skins and peel them just before serving (or bake them in the oven and serve in their skins) alongside the hot borscht.

name: Zupa ze stynki z ziemniakami (European smelt and potato soup)
summary: A delicate freshwater fish soup of fresh European smelt simmered with potatoes in a seasoned onion broth.
steps: Wipe the smelt thoroughly with a coarse cloth, salt, and let stand for 60 minutes before cooking.
Boil about 1.5 l of seasoned broth from the onions, peppercorns, bay leaf, and water for 15 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, cut into large dice or rounds, add to the boiling broth, and cook for about 10 minutes until parboiled.
Add the smelt to the partially cooked potatoes and simmer for another 10 minutes until the fish turns opaque and flakes from the bone. Serve immediately.

name: Ruffe fish soup with quenelles (zupa rybna z jazgarzy z pulpetami)
summary: An aromatic ruffe fish broth served with tender poached and sliced fish quenelle rolls made of minced ruffe, bread roll, and onion.

ingredients.name: large onions
ingredients.note: 1 whole for broth and 1 whole for fish mixture

steps: Carefully fillet the meat from the raw ruffe, and using the heads, bones, one onion, bay leaf, and pepper, simmer a fish broth in 1.5 l of salted water for about 30 minutes, then strain.
Mince the fish fillets in a meat grinder, add the second onion (finely grated) and the soaked and well-squeezed bread roll, then chop with a cleaver on a pastry board until a smooth paste forms.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper, beat in the egg, and knead thoroughly once more.
Shape the mixture into rolls the thickness of a slender candle, dredge in plain wheat flour, and simmer in the boiling fish broth for about 10 minutes.
Slice the cooked rolls into thin rounds and serve in the hot broth.

name: Thrifty Sauerkraut Soup (Kapusniak Oszczedny)
summary: Homestyle Polish sauerkraut soup slowly simmered with pork fatback rinds and root vegetables, thickened with a wheat flour slurry.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the soup and blending the flour

steps: Place the sauerkraut and pork fatback rinds in a pot, pour in the water, add the peppercorns and bay leaf, and simmer slowly until the sauerkraut and rinds begin to soften.
Add the peeled and halved carrot, parsley root, and onion, and continue simmering covered over low heat until all the vegetables are completely tender.
Just before serving, remove the pork rinds, dice them finely, and return them to the soup.
Thicken the soup with the wheat flour blended in cold water, season with salt if needed, bring to a boil together, and serve.

name: Kapuśniak leniwy (lazy fresh cabbage soup)
summary: Mild Polish cabbage soup made with fresh white cabbage and potatoes in a pork bone and vegetable broth, enriched with sour cream and served with dill.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half liters for the broth

ingredients.name: sour cream or milk
ingredients.note: orig. 10 dkg sour cream or 1 szklanka (250 ml) milk

steps: Boil 1.5 liters of broth from the pork bones, carrot, parsley root, onion, peppercorns, bay leaf, and salt.
Cut the white cabbage into wedges, scald with boiling water, add to the strained broth, and simmer.
About 20 minutes before serving, add the peeled and diced potatoes.
When the potatoes are tender, thicken the soup with the wheat flour blended in a little cold water and bring to a boil.
Pour the hot cabbage soup into a tureen over the sour cream tempered with a few tablespoons of hot soup, and sprinkle with dill.

name: Zupa szczawiowa z omletem bez jaj (sorrel soup with eggless pancake strips)
summary: A tangy soup of stewed sorrel in vegetable and mushroom broth, finished with sour cream and served with strips of a fluffy pancake made with flour, milk, and baking powder.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the broth and mixing the flour

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 tbsp (15 g) for soup and 5 dkg (50 g) for pancake

ingredients.name: butter, lard, or margarine
ingredients.note: orig. 2 dkg, for stewing sorrel and frying pancake

steps: Cook a vegetable broth from the carrot, parsley root, onion, dried mushroom, bay leaf, and peppercorns in about 1.5 l of water for 30 minutes, then strain.
Sort and wash the sorrel, pass through a meat grinder, and braise gently in half of the fat (10 g) until completely softened.

Mix 15 g of plain wheat flour with a splash of cold water, stir into the braised sorrel, whisk in the hot vegetable broth, bring to a boil, take off the heat, stir in the sour cream, and season with salt.

Whisk the remaining 50 g of plain wheat flour with the milk, a pinch of salt, and baking powder into a thick batter. Pour into a skillet containing the remaining heated fat (10 g), forming a layer about half a finger thick, and fry over low heat on both sides.
Roll the fried pancake into a log, slice diagonally into strips, and arrange in soup plates before ladling in the piping hot sorrel soup.

name: Barley Krupnik Soup with Root Vegetables
summary: Thick homemade barley krupnik with finely chopped root vegetables, finished with pork fatback cracklings and fresh dill.
steps: Peel and finely dice the carrot, parsley root, and onion.
Put the barley groats and diced vegetables into a pot, pour in 2.25 liters of water, add the peppercorns, bay leaf, and salt, and simmer slowly until the broth reduces to about 1.5 liters.
Finely dice the pork fatback, render in a skillet until golden cracklings form, pour into the soup, and simmer together for another 15 minutes.
Ladle the piping hot barley soup into a tureen and sprinkle with chopped dill or parsley.

name: Polish Vegetable and Cabbage Milk Soup (Miszkulancja)
summary: Mild Polish vegetable soup of julienned carrots, parsley root, and leek simmered with shredded cabbage and diced potatoes, finished with milk and butter or rendered pork fatback.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half liters

steps: Peel the carrots, parsley root, and leek, cut into thin strips, and bring to a boil in 1.5 liters of salted water.
Add the coarsely chopped cabbage, peppercorns, and bay leaf, and simmer over low heat.
About 20 minutes before serving, add the peeled and diced potatoes.

After the potatoes have cooked for 10 minutes, pour in the milk and simmer for another 10 minutes until all the vegetables are tender, then pour the soup into a tureen with the butter or rendered pork fatback.

name: Żur z mąki owsianej z ziemniakami (sour oat soup with potatoes)
summary: A homemade sour oat soup fermented with a wholemeal bread crust, diluted with vegetable stock, topped with fatback cracklings, and served with potatoes.
steps: Pour the lukewarm water over the sifted oat flour, add the wholemeal bread crust, and leave in a warm place for 2 days (2880 minutes) to ferment.
Peel the potatoes, boil separately in salted water until tender, and cut into quarters or rounds.
Discard the bread crust from the fermented oat sour, dilute with the vegetable stock, season with salt, and bring to a boil.
Dice the fatback, render into crisp cracklings, and pour with the hot fat directly into the soup.
Add the cooked potatoes, return briefly to a boil, and serve piping hot.

name: Zupa chlebowa na wywarze jarzynowym (bread soup with vegetable broth)
summary: A quick, hearty soup made by pouring boiling vegetable broth over thoroughly dried, finely ground wholemeal bread.

ingredients.name: dry wholemeal bread
ingredients.note: orig. 1 full szklanka, measured after grinding

steps: Finely grind the thoroughly dried wholemeal bread in a meat grinder.
Bring the vegetable broth to a boil, dissolve the bouillon cubes, and season with salt if needed.
Pour the boiling broth over the ground wholemeal bread, stir, and serve immediately.

name: Zupa jarzynowa z kluskami kładzionymi bez jaj (vegetable soup with eggless drop dumplings)
summary: A clear vegetable soup with fluffy drop dumplings made from creamed butter or lard, wheat flour, and baking powder, served with dill.

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.note: to reach drop dumpling batter consistency

steps: Beat the butter or lard until fluffy, stir in the plain wheat flour, and continue beating while adding cold water teaspoon by teaspoon until a soft drop-dumpling dough forms.
Stir in the baking powder and a pinch of salt, and mix thoroughly.
Bring the vegetable stock to a boil and drop small portions of the dough into the simmering soup using a teaspoon.
Simmer the dumplings gently for about 8–10 minutes until they all float to the surface and are tender, then ladle the soup into a tureen over the chopped dill.

name: Dried fruit compote (suszenina wigilijna)
summary: A traditional Christmas Eve dried fruit soup made from dried apples, pears, and prunes simmered with cloves and cinnamon, lightly thickened with potato starch.

ingredients.name: mixed dried fruit: apples, pears, and prunes

steps: Rinse the dried fruit thoroughly and soak overnight (for about 8 hours) in 3 l of cold water sweetened with sugar.
The next day, chop the plumped fruit into smaller pieces and simmer in the same water together with the cloves and cinnamon stick for about 35 minutes until completely tender.
Mix the potato starch with a little cold water, stir it into the simmering fruit, and bring briefly to a boil while stirring.
Allow the dish to cool completely before serving.

name: Braised Stuffed Whole Chicken Galantine
summary: Whole boned chicken skin filled with a smooth forcemeat of twice-ground chicken meat, soaked bread roll, boiled potatoes, egg, and fresh herbs, browned in fat and braised until tender.

ingredients.name: lard or margarine
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg: 20 g for the stuffing and 40 g for browning

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the roll, mixing the stuffing, and basting during braising

steps: Slit the skin down the back of the hen with a sharp knife and carefully peel it off in one piece without tearing, then sew up the wing and leg openings with kitchen twine.
Strip all the meat cleanly from the bones and pass it twice through a meat grinder (the second time using a fine pate plate together with the soaked and squeezed bread roll and the boiled potatoes).
Add 20 g of fat, the egg, chopped dill and parsley, salt, and a few tablespoons of water to the ground mixture, and knead thoroughly until completely smooth and uniform.
Stuff the chicken skin loosely with the forcemeat, sew up the slit along the back with strong twine, and reshape into a whole bird.

Brown the stuffed hen in a Dutch oven in the remaining 40 g of hot fat, then add a splash of water and braise covered for at least 60 minutes, basting frequently; slice thinly with a sharp knife and serve hot or cold.

name: Russian Kurnik (Chicken and Buckwheat Crepe Pie)
summary: Festive savory pie baked in a springform pan lined with thin crepes and filled with cooked chicken meat, white buckwheat groats, dried forest mushrooms, and hard-boiled egg.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 raw egg for the crepe batter and 1 hard-boiled egg for the filling

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the crepe batter and for cooking the groats with the mushrooms

ingredients.name: cooked chicken meat
ingredients.note: orig. meat picked from half a hen cooked for broth

ingredients.name: unroasted buckwheat groats
ingredients.note: orig. 1 cup of white cracked buckwheat groats

ingredients.name: margarine or lard
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg, for the pan and the filling

ingredients.name: chicken broth
ingredients.note: a few tablespoons for moistening the filling

steps: Whisk the raw egg with the wheat flour, a pinch of salt, and water, and fry 12–15 thin crepes in a skillet greased with the pork fatback rind.
Cook the white buckwheat groats until fluffy together with the dried mushrooms, then remove the mushrooms and chop them finely.
Pull the meat from the half cooked hen into bite-sized pieces, and coarsely chop the hard-boiled egg.
Gently toss together the chicken meat, buckwheat groats, chopped mushrooms, and hard-boiled egg, adding a few tablespoons of broth and most of the melted fat.

Grease a springform pan or shallow baking dish with the remaining fat, line the bottom and sides with the crepes, pack in the filling, cover the top with a crepe, and bake in a hot oven (190 °C) for about 25–30 minutes until golden.

name: Pasztet z gołębi w naleśnikach (pigeon pie in crêpes)
summary: A festive baked pie of tender pigeon meat layered with pearl barley, green peas, and fatback inside thin crêpes, served with white sauce.

ingredients.name: Polish soup vegetables (włoszczyzna)
ingredients.note: orig. soup vegetables as for broth

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the broth and crêpes

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 1 cup (150 g) for crêpes and 2 tbsp (30 g) for the sauce

ingredients.name: pork rind (fatback rind)
ingredients.note: for greasing the skillet and baking dish

steps: Cook a rich broth from the pigeons and soup vegetables in about 2 l of salted water for about 60 minutes. Set aside 500 ml of clear broth for preparing the sauce.
Remove the cooked pigeons, separate the meat from the larger bones, and chop it along with the giblets into medium pieces.
Cook the pearl barley and green peas separately in salted water until tender, and slice the fatback into thin flakes.
Whisk a batter from 150 g of plain wheat flour, the egg, water, and a pinch of salt, and fry 12 very thin crêpes in a skillet rubbed with fatback rind.

Grease a shallow saucepan or springform tin with fatback rind and line the bottom and sides with crêpes. Arrange alternating layers of barley, pigeon meat and giblets, cooked vegetables, green peas, and fatback flakes, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Once filled, cover the top with the remaining crêpes and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 40 minutes until well browned.

Heat 20 g of fat, cook a roux with the remaining 30 g of plain wheat flour, whisk in 500 ml of the reserved broth, bring to a boil, and finish with the sour cream, salt, and pepper. Turn the baked pie onto a platter and serve with the white sauce.

name: Oszczędne sznycle cielęce (thrifty veal schnitzels)
summary: Thinly pounded veal schnitzels spread with a thick, cooled roux instead of egg, coated in breadcrumbs, and fried until golden.

ingredients.name: lard or refined vegetable oil
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg (10 g for roux and 50 g for frying)

steps: Cook a thick roux from the plain wheat flour, 10 g of lard or oil, and a splash of water as for a rich sauce, then let it cool.
Slice the veal into 4 equal cutlets, pound thoroughly with a meat mallet, and leave on a board for about 2 hours (120 minutes).
Just before frying, spread the cutlets thickly with the cooled roux and coat thoroughly in finely crushed breadcrumbs.
Fry in the remaining 50 g of moderately heated lard or oil for about 4–5 minutes on each side until golden. Season with fine salt immediately after frying.

name: Oszczędne kotlety schabowe (thrifty breaded pork cutlets)
summary: Pounded pork loin or pork leg cutlets coated without egg using a thick roux and breadcrumbs, then fried in lard or oil.

ingredients.name: lard or vegetable oil
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg (10 g for roux and 50 g for frying)

steps: Slice the pork into 4 equal cutlets and pound vigorously with a mallet to prevent shrinking during frying.
Prepare a thick roux from the plain wheat flour, 10 g of lard or oil, and a splash of water as for a dense sauce, and let cool.
Coat the pounded cutlets with the roux paste and dredge in finely crushed breadcrumbs or oat flour.
Fry the cutlets in the remaining 50 g of hot lard or oil for about 4–5 minutes on each side until golden, salt after frying, and serve piping hot.

name: Pounded beef steaks (bitki wołowe)
summary: Classic pounded beef steaks browned in fat and braised until tender with onions and dried mushrooms in their own rich gravy.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 cup (250 ml) for braising + 50 ml for flour

steps: Soak the dried mushrooms overnight (for about 8 hours) in cold water, then slice into thin strips, reserving the soaking water.
Cut the beef across the grain into 4 large or 8 smaller steaks, pound thoroughly with a meat mallet, salt, and dust lightly with pepper.
Sear the steaks on well-heated lard or margarine and transfer to a saucepan.
Add the finely chopped onion and mushroom strips, pour in 250 ml of water along with the mushroom soaking liquid, and braise gently covered for about 60–70 minutes until tender.
Before serving, whisk the plain wheat flour in 50 ml of cold water, stir into the sauce, and bring briefly to a boil.

name: Homestyle Meat Goulash
summary: Classic homestyle goulash of browned beef, veal, or pork slowly braised with onions and paprika in a generous, rich gravy.

ingredients.name: beef, veal, or pork
ingredients.note: orig. 40 dkg of tender meat free of sinew

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for braising the meat and thinning the flour

steps: Cut the meat into walnut-sized pieces, pound lightly, season with salt, and brown well on all sides in hot fat.
Transfer the browned meat to a saucepan along with the sliced onions, pour in water, and braise slowly under a lid until completely tender.
Blend a tablespoon of wheat flour with a little cold water, stir into the tender meat, add the ground paprika, and simmer for a few minutes longer until a generous, thick gravy forms.

name: Goulash and Poached Eggs on Toasted Rolls
summary: Hollowed-out crusty roll halves layered with a thick paprika goulash of finely minced meat and onions, topped with poached or soft-boiled eggs, and heated through in the oven.

ingredients.name: oblong crusty rolls
ingredients.note: larger oblong rolls known as parki

steps: Slice the rolls in half lengthwise and scoop out their soft centers (which can be dried for breadcrumbs).

Mince the meat and onions as finely as possible, brown them together in hot fat, sprinkle with flour, pour in water, season with salt, and simmer over low heat until tender, stirring in the paprika toward the end to form a thick, rich red sauce.
Poach the eggs or soft-boil them (for 3 minutes) and peel.
Spoon a tablespoon of the hot goulash sauce into each hollowed roll half, place the halved large eggs (or whole small eggs) on top, and cover with the remaining sauce.
Place the filled rolls into a hot oven (200 °C) for a few minutes until piping hot and serve immediately.

name: Horsemeat pâté (pasztet z koniny)
summary: A festive baked pâté of vinegar-marinated and braised horsemeat, fatty pork belly, onions, and potatoes, reminiscent of game pâté.
steps: Marinate the horsemeat in vinegar with allspice berries, then braise covered until tender for about 90 minutes.
Braise the pork belly separately with whole peeled onions, and boil the potatoes in their skins, peel, and add to the tender pork belly.
Pass the braised horsemeat, pork belly, onions, and potatoes twice through the fine plate of a meat grinder.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, season with salt, pepper, grated nutmeg, and marjoram, beat in the whole eggs, and beat thoroughly for about 30 minutes.
Transfer the mixture into a springform pan greased with braising fat and dusted with breadcrumbs, then bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 60 minutes.
Once the pâté cools slightly, turn it out onto a board and set in a cold place overnight (for about 8 hours). The next day, slice thinly.

name: Minced Ruffe Fish Cutlets
summary: Golden pan-fried fish cakes made from twice-ground ruffe or other small freshwater fish blended with boiled potatoes, soaked bread roll, and grated onion.

ingredients.name: ruffe or other small freshwater fish
wheat or oat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg, for dredging the cutlets

steps: Clean the ruffe thoroughly, cut off the heads and gills, and soak the bread roll in water and squeeze dry.
Pass the fish twice through a meat grinder, grinding it the second time together with the squeezed roll, boiled potatoes, and grated onion.
Beat in the egg, season the mixture with salt and pepper, and knead at length by hand until completely smooth and uniform.
Shape eight cutlets, dredge them in flour, and fry on both sides in hot oil until golden brown.

name: Ryba faszerowana po żydowsku z drobnych rybek (Jewish-style minced small-fish roll)
summary: A Christmas Eve roll of minced small freshwater fish, onion, bread roll, and potatoes poached in a cloth napkin in an aromatic vegetable broth.

ingredients.name: small freshwater fish
ingredients.note: cleaned; if using ruffe, remove heads and gills

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.note: 4 whole for fish mixture and 1 whole for broth

ingredients.name: ice-cold water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka, for mixing the fish mixture + water for the broth

steps: Pass the cleaned small fish through a meat grinder together with 4 onions, the soaked and squeezed wheat roll, and the boiled, peeled potatoes.
Turn the mixture onto a pastry board and chop with a cleaver or knead, gradually adding 250 ml of ice-cold water until smooth and sticky.
Beat in the eggs, season with salt and plenty of pepper, and mix thoroughly once more.

Scald a clean linen napkin with boiling water, wring out thoroughly, and grease the center with oil or lard. Shape the fish mixture into an oblong roll, wrap in the napkin, and tie with kitchen twine.
Boil a court bouillon from the remaining onion, bay leaf, allspice berries, pepper, and salt, cool slightly, lower in the fish roll, bring to a boil, and simmer gently for 60 minutes.
Once cooked, remove the fish roll, immediately unwrap from the napkin so it does not stick, wrap loosely again, and keep warm in the broth until serving, then slice finger-thick.

name: Small fish fried in batter (rybki w klarze)
summary: Small fish threaded onto skewers, dipped in a fluffy batter of flour, egg yolk, and beaten egg white, and fried until golden.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: small, separated into yolk and white

steps: Clean the fish (for ruffe, cut off heads and gills; leave smelts whole), salt, and set aside for 60 minutes.
Thread the fish in bunches of 6–8 onto thin skewers.
Whisk the plain wheat flour with the egg yolk, water, and a pinch of salt to make a batter the consistency of sour cream, then gently fold in the egg white beaten to stiff peaks.
Dip the skewered fish into the batter and fry in well-heated vegetable oil for about 4–5 minutes per side until golden.

name: Pan-fried skewered small fish (rybki smażone na oleju)
summary: Small freshwater fish threaded onto skewers, coated in flour, and pan-fried crisp in hot vegetable oil.
steps: Thoroughly clean the small fish (for ruffe, cut off heads and gills), rinse, pat dry, and salt.
Thread the fish in groups of 6–8 onto thin wooden skewers and dredge in plain wheat flour.
Fry in well-heated vegetable oil for about 4–5 minutes per side until golden brown.

name: Grzybek z rybkami (soufflé pancake with small fish)
summary: Fluffy skillet pancake made from wheat flour, egg yolks, and stiffly whipped egg whites, scattered with fried small fish before flipping and finishing in hot fat.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: enough to make a batter slightly thicker than crepe batter

ingredients.name: fried small fish
ingredients.note: orig. 20 dkg of fried and cooled small fish

ingredients.name: vegetable oil or lard
ingredients.note: orig. 4 dkg, divided into two equal portions

steps: Beat the egg yolks with the wheat flour, salt, and enough water to form a batter slightly thicker than crepe batter.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Heat half of the fat in a skillet, pour in the batter, and cook slowly until browned underneath and beginning to set on top.
Scatter the fried small fish over the top of the pancake, flip it over onto the freshly heated second half of the fat, finish frying briefly, and serve hot straight from the skillet.

name: Steamed Minced Fish Pudding
summary: Christmas Eve savory fish pudding steamed in a water bath from minced small freshwater fish, boiled potatoes, braised onions, a thick oil roux, and eggs lightened with stiffly whipped whites.

ingredients.name: small freshwater fish
ingredients.note: orig. 80 dkg, raw or cooked from broth

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: orig. 6 dkg: for the onion, roux, and greasing the mold

steps: Braise the chopped onions in a teaspoon of oil, then pass the cleaned small fish (raw or cooked) through a meat grinder together with the onions and boiled potatoes.
Make a roux from the flour and the remaining oil, thin it with water or stock to the consistency of a thick sauce, and combine with the minced fish mixture.
Beat two egg yolks into the mixture, work thoroughly, season with salt, pepper, grated nutmeg, and chopped dill, and finally fold in the stiffly whipped egg whites.
Transfer the mixture into a pudding mold greased with oil and coated with breadcrumbs, then cover tightly with a lid.
Place the mold into a pot of boiling water and steam in the water bath for 75 minutes from the moment the water returns to a boil, then unmold onto a platter.

name: Świeże śledzie smażone z musztardą (fried fresh herrings with mustard)
summary: Fresh herring coated in flour and fried until golden in oil, slit along the back, spread with mustard, and briefly braised.

ingredients.name: fresh herrings
ingredients.note: orig. 2 fish weighing 50–60 dkg in total

steps: Clean and scale the fresh herrings, salt, and let rest for 2 hours (120 minutes).
Dredge the fish in plain wheat or oat flour and fry in hot vegetable oil for about 5 minutes on each side until well browned.
Score the fried herrings along the backbone, spread the cuts with mustard, pour 2 tbsp of water into the skillet, and braise for another 2–3 minutes.

name: Fresh herring baked with potatoes (śledzie zapiekane z kartoflami)
summary: A casserole of cooked fresh herring and potatoes layered with thin raw onion rings and covered with a sauce of fish broth and sour cream.
steps: Clean the fresh herrings, salt, and let stand for 60 minutes, then simmer in a small amount of water with a piece of onion, peppercorns, and bay leaf for about 10 minutes.
Remove the cooked herrings, debone, and break into generous chunks, reserving the poaching liquid.
Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel, and slice into rounds, and slice the remaining raw onion into very thin rings.
Prepare a pale roux from the plain wheat flour and part of the vegetable oil, whisk in the herring broth, bring to a boil, and stir in the sour cream.
Grease a baking dish with the remaining oil, layer the potatoes and herring pieces interspersed with raw onion slices, pour over the sauce, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 40 minutes.

name: Fresh herring Greek-style (śledzie po grecku)
summary: A Christmas Eve dish of poached fresh herring fillets topped with a thick layer of braised root vegetables, cabbage, and onion in a tomato-vinegar sauce.

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables: carrots, parsley root, onion, and savoy or white cabbage

steps: Clean the fresh herrings, salt, halve lengthwise, and cut each half crosswise into 3 equal portions.
Poach the herring pieces in very little water with pepper and bay leaf for about 10 minutes, then cool and transfer to a serving platter, reserving the poaching liquid.
Cut the carrots, parsley root, onion, cabbage, leek, and celeriac into julienne strips and braise gently in the herring broth with vegetable oil for about 25 minutes until tender.
Add the tomato paste and vinegar to the tender vegetables and bring briefly to a boil.
Cover the arranged herrings on the platter with a generous layer of braised vegetables and refrigerate for 24 hours (1440 minutes) before serving.

name: Sos chrzanowy do ryb (horseradish sauce for fish)
summary: A classic Polish white fish sauce made from fish or vegetable stock thickened with roux, flavoured with freshly grated horseradish, vinegar, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: orig. 50 dkg — corrected typographical error to 5 dkg as in other variants

steps: Cook the plain wheat flour in vegetable oil into a pale roux, whisk in 500 ml of fish or vegetable stock, and bring to a simmer to form a smooth white sauce.
Finely grate the horseradish root, sprinkle with salt, and drizzle with vinegar.
Add the grated horseradish to the simmering sauce, bring to a boil, stir in the sour cream, and season to taste with a pinch of sugar.

name: Placki ziemniaczane (crispy potato pancakes)
summary: Thin, crisp potato pancakes made from freshly grated raw potatoes, fried until golden brown in hot oil.
steps: Peel, rinse, and grate the potatoes on a fine grater.
If the grated potato mass releases excess liquid, pour off 1 tbsp of liquid from the surface, then season with salt to taste and stir.
Heat the vegetable oil well in a skillet, spoon out portions of the mixture (about 16 small pancakes in total), and fry thin pancakes for about 3–4 minutes on each side until deeply browned.

name: Racuchy ziemniaczane z mąką owsianą (potato and oat flour pancakes)
summary: Thin savoury pancakes of finely grated raw potatoes thickened with sifted oat flour, pan-fried in hot oil.
steps: Peel the raw potatoes and grate them on a fine grater.
Add the sifted oat flour, season with salt, and mix thoroughly into a uniform mixture.
Heat the vegetable oil well in a skillet and fry fairly large, thin pancakes on both sides for about 3–4 minutes until golden.

name: Peeled Oat-Dusted Roasted Potatoes
summary: Peeled medium potatoes salted generously an hour before baking, dredged in oat flour, and roasted until golden crisp in the oven.
steps: Peel the medium-sized potatoes, salt them generously on all sides, and let stand for at least 60 minutes.
Dredge the salted potatoes evenly in the oat flour.
Arrange the potatoes on a baking tray and roast in a hot oven (200 °C) for about 40–45 minutes until tender and golden brown.

name: Kartofle — bomby (whole golden roasted potatoes)
summary: Evenly sized whole potatoes parboiled in their skins, peeled, and roasted in hot oil until golden brown all over.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for parboiling and shocking the potatoes

steps: Parboil the evenly sized potatoes in their skins until half tender, then plunge them briefly into cold water and slip off their thin skins.
Heat two tablespoons of oil in a roasting pan or deep skillet, arrange the peeled potatoes inside, and sprinkle with salt.
Roast in a hot oven (200 °C) or covered on the stovetop, turning several times, until evenly browned on all sides.

name: Old Potatoes Cooked Like New Potatoes
summary: Old potatoes soaked overnight in cold water, diced, and boiled with lard or oil, fresh dill, and parsley.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. 80 dkg of large old potatoes

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold water for soaking overnight and water for boiling

steps: Peel the large old potatoes and soak them overnight in cold water.
The next day, cut the potatoes into walnut-sized cubes and boil in plenty of salted water, taking care not to overcook them.
Drain the potatoes thoroughly, toss quickly with the hot lard or oil and chopped dill and parsley, and serve immediately.

name: Molded Potato and Sheep Cheese Bake
summary: Savory potato cake made from julienned raw potatoes tossed with chopped onions, fat, and bryndza sheep cheese, packed tightly into a breadcrumb-lined mold and baked for an hour.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil or lard
ingredients.note: for the mixture plus a little for greasing the mold

ingredients.name: bryndza sheep cheese or green herb cheese

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into very thin julienne strips.
Season the potatoes with salt and mix thoroughly with the finely chopped onion, oil or melted lard, and crumbled bryndza (or grated cheese).
Grease a baking mold with fat, coat with grated bread or breadcrumbs, and pack the potato mixture into the mold, pressing it down as firmly as possible.
Bake in a hot oven (200 °C) for 60 minutes, then unmold onto a platter and serve hot.

name: Boiled Broad Beans with Pork Cracklings
summary: Dried broad beans soaked overnight and boiled until their skins burst, served hot topped with crisp pork fatback cracklings.

ingredients.name: dried broad beans
ingredients.note: orig. 1 cup of large or small broad beans

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for soaking and boiling the broad beans

steps: Cover the dried broad beans with cold water and leave to soak overnight.
The next day, cook the broad beans in the same water with salt over low heat until the beans are very soft and begin to split open, then drain.
Fry the finely diced pork fatback in a skillet until golden cracklings form, pour over the hot broad beans, and serve immediately.

name: Braised Potato-Stuffed Onions
summary: Large hollowed-out onions mounded with a savory filling of chopped onion centers, grated boiled potatoes, and pork fatback cracklings, slowly braised until tender.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. 4 large onions (or 8 medium) weighing 40–50 dkg in total

steps: Peel the large onions and hollow out their centers, leaving walls about 1 cm thick.
Finely dice the pork fatback and render it in a skillet until crisp cracklings form, reserving the rendered fat.
Finely chop the hollowed-out onion centers, mix them with the boiled and grated potatoes and the pork cracklings, and heap the filling into the onion shells.
Heat the rendered pork fat in a shallow saucepan, arrange the stuffed onions inside, season with salt, and pour in water to reach halfway up their sides.
Braise covered over low heat until the liquid has almost completely evaporated and the onions are tender, and serve in the same dish.

name: Stuffed Baked Rutabaga
summary: Halved boiled rutabagas hollowed out and mounded with a savory filling of mashed rutabaga pulp, grated boiled potatoes, and onions braised in pork fatback, browned in the oven.

ingredients.name: rutabaga
ingredients.note: orig. 2 medium rutabagas weighing approx. 80 dkg

steps: Wash the unpeeled rutabagas thoroughly and boil them whole until tender in water or vegetable stock, and boil the potatoes separately.
Cut the cooked rutabagas in half and scoop out the flesh, leaving walls about 1 cm thick.
Finely chop the onion and braise it in a skillet with the diced pork fatback.
Chop or mash the scooped-out rutabaga flesh, combine it with the braised onion and pork fatback as well as the grated boiled potatoes, and season with salt and pepper.
Heap the filling into the hollowed rutabaga halves and bake in a hot oven (190 °C) for about 15–20 minutes until browned on top.

name: Pan-Fried Braised Pumpkin Slices
summary: Slices of ripe pumpkin dredged in wheat flour, slowly browned in oil or lard, and braised covered with a splash of bouillon until tender.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil or lard
ingredients.note: 2 tablespoons of oil or 40 g (4 dkg) of lard

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for dissolving the bouillon cube and adding liquid during braising

steps: Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds and stringy pulp, and cut into even pieces about 1.5 cm thick.
Season the pumpkin pieces with salt and dredge them in wheat flour.
Slowly brown the pumpkin in hot oil or lard, then cover and braise until tender, adding hot water with the dissolved bouillon cube as needed.

name: Boiled White Beans with Rendered Pork Fat
summary: Dried white beans soaked overnight and boiled until very tender, served hot tossed with rendered pork fatback.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for soaking and boiling the beans

steps: Cover the beans with cold water and leave to soak overnight.
The next day, boil the beans until completely tender, seasoning with salt toward the end of cooking, and drain.
Toss the hot beans with the rendered pork fatback and serve immediately.

name: Kapusta z grzybami (sauerkraut with mushrooms)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve dish of sauerkraut braised with onions, vegetable oil, and whole dried forest mushrooms, lightly sweetened with sugar and thickened with flour.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the mushrooms and blending the flour

steps: Soak the dried mushrooms overnight in a small amount of water.
Put the sauerkraut into a pot, add the oil and chopped onions, and braise under a lid.
When the sauerkraut is half tender, add the soaked mushrooms along with their soaking liquid and continue braising until completely tender.
Stir in a tablespoon of sugar, thicken the sauerkraut with the wheat flour blended in a little water, and bring to a boil once more.
Mound the sauerkraut on a platter and arrange the whole mushrooms around it.

name: Steamed White Cabbage Pudding
summary: Savory cabbage pudding steamed in a water bath from finely shredded boiled white cabbage, a lard roux, and eggs folded with stiffly beaten whites.

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.note: orig. 4 dkg, plus a little for greasing the mold

ingredients.name: cabbage cooking liquid
ingredients.note: orig. 2 cups of the water in which the cabbage was boiled

steps: Boil the whole head of white cabbage in salted water or vegetable stock, reserving 500 ml of the cooking liquid, then cut out the core and finely shred the cabbage.
Make a roux from the lard and wheat flour, thin it with 500 ml of the cabbage cooking liquid, and mix with the shredded cabbage.
Beat the mixture with two egg yolks, season with salt and pepper, and finally fold in the stiffly whipped egg whites.
Transfer the mixture to a pudding mold greased with fat and generously coated with breadcrumbs, cover tightly with a lid, and steam in a pot of boiling water for 75 minutes.

name: Fried salsify (salsefia smażona)
summary: Scraped salsify roots boiled tender, dredged in flour, and pan-fried golden in vegetable oil.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour or oat flour

steps: Thoroughly scrape the salsify roots, rinse, and boil until tender in salted water for about 20–25 minutes.
Drain the cooked salsify, pat dry on paper towels, and dredge in plain wheat or oat flour.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and fry the salsify for about 5–8 minutes on all sides until golden brown.

name: Pan-Fried Jerusalem Artichokes
summary: Partially cooked Jerusalem artichoke tubers cut into thick slices, coated in wheat flour, and fried in oil until golden.

ingredients.name: Jerusalem artichokes
ingredients.note: orig. half a kg of tubers

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a small amount of saccharin for the cooking water

steps: Scrape the Jerusalem artichoke tubers clean and boil them until tender in salted water with a touch of sugar.
Remove the cooked tubers from the water, pat dry, and cut larger ones into thick slices.
Dredge the slices in wheat flour and fry in hot oil on both sides until golden brown.

name: Vegetable pâté baked in crêpes (pasztet z jarzyn w naleśnikach)
summary: A hot baked pâté of chopped cooked vegetables, potatoes, and dried mushrooms with fatback cracklings, enveloped and baked in thin crêpes.

ingredients.name: mixed soup vegetables: carrots, parsley root, onion, and cabbage
fatback rind (pork rind)
ingredients.note: for frying crêpes and greasing baking pan

steps: Boil the mixed vegetables, potatoes, and dried mushrooms until tender (for about 30 minutes, e.g. as a soup broth), then drain and chop finely.
Dice the fatback, render into cracklings, and mix with the chopped vegetables, mushrooms, and potatoes; season with salt and pepper or paprika.
Prepare a batter from the plain wheat flour, egg, water, and a pinch of salt, and fry 10–12 thin crêpes in a pan rubbed with fatback rind.
Grease a shallow saucepan or baking dish with the fatback rind and line it with crêpes so that they hang over the edges.
Fill with the vegetable filling, fold the crêpes over tightly to cover, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 30 minutes.
Turn the finished pâté out of the mould onto a platter and serve hot.

name: Cold vegetable pâté (pasztet jarzynowy na zimno)
summary: A cold pâté of white beans and potatoes with lard or fatback, mustard, and marjoram, cooked in a mould.
steps: Soak the white beans overnight (for about 8 hours) in cold water, then boil until tender for about 40 minutes and drain.
Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel, and thoroughly mash or pass through a ricer.
Mince the cooked beans in a meat grinder and combine with the mashed potatoes, egg, lard or finely chopped fatback, and mustard.
Season the mixture to taste with salt and marjoram, and knead thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture to a greased pâté mould and cook in a water bath for 90 minutes after the water returns to a boil.
Cool the pâté completely and serve cold with bread.

name: Thick gooseberry jam
summary: A tart, thick gooseberry jam made by cooking finely chopped unripe gooseberries in thick sugar syrup, for filling cakes and soufflés.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half kilograms

steps: Remove the stems from unripe gooseberries and chop them very finely.

Bring a syrup made with 1.5 kg of sugar and 750 ml of water to the boil. Add the chopped gooseberries and cook over low heat, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until the jam is very thick and pulls away from the bottom of the pan.
Pack the hot jam into an earthenware pot or scalded jars. If too thin, dry it in a gently heated oven first. Let cool, then seal tightly.

name: Orange marmalade
summary: A traditional marmalade of whole thinly sliced oranges soaked for a day in water, simmered for three hours until soft, mashed and cooked with an equal weight of sugar and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the day-long soak, and fresh water for the three-hour cooking

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: a juicy one, the juice squeezed through a sieve

steps: Wash and dry 3 kg of ripe oranges, slice them thinly, peel and all, discarding the seeds. Put them in an earthenware or enamel pot, cover them with water, and leave them covered for a full day (24 hours).
The next day, pour off the soaking water, transfer the orange slices to a wide pan, cover them with fresh water, and cook over low heat for 3 hours, carefully lifting out any seeds that float up.
Pour the liquor into a separate bowl, and mash the soft oranges in a bowl or blend them to a smooth mass.
Put the mashed oranges back in the pan, pour in the liquor you set aside, add 3 kg of fine sugar, and cook over low heat for about 1.5 hours, until the syrup is clear and thick.
Near the end, squeeze the juice of one juicy lemon through a sieve, mix, and pack the warm marmalade into scalded jars.

name: Thick plum jam
summary: A thick, fragrant plum jam made with peeled ripe węgierka plums layered with sugar and cooked without added water, with a few cloves wrapped in muslin.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for blanching the plums, and cold water for shocking them

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.note: wrapped in muslin, orig. a few

steps: Blanch ripe węgierka plums in boiling water, slip off the skins, and drop them at once into cold water so they do not darken.
Drain the peeled plums, cut them in half, remove the stones, and pack them in a wide pot in layers with 1 kg of fine sugar, adding not a drop of water.
Put a few cloves wrapped in muslin into the pot and cook the plums over moderate heat, stirring often with a wooden spatula.
When the jam is very thick and no longer sticks to a cold saucer, remove the cloves and pack the hot jam into scalded jars.

name: Thick bilberry jam with pears
summary: A thick bilberry jam made with blanched bilberries cooked in sugar syrup with finely chopped pears and candied orange peel, served with roast meat.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus boiling water for blanching the berries

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped very finely, orig. a few

steps: Blanch ripe bilberries in boiling water and turn them onto a sieve to drain well.
Cook a syrup in a wide pan from 1 kg of sugar and 250 ml of water, add the drained berries, and bring it to the boil.
When the berries begin to boil, add peeled, very finely chopped pears and finely chopped candied orange peel.
Cook everything over low heat, stirring often, until the jam reaches the desired consistency, then pack into jars.

name: Plums pickled in spiced vinegar
summary: Classic węgierka plums studded with cloves and pickled for four days in a liquor of vinegar, sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel, or in a milder version with red wine.

ingredients.name: węgierka plums
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of fine ripe węgierka plums, the bloom wiped off

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar chopped into small pieces

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki of the best, not too strong vinegar

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.note: for studding the plums in several places

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: a piece of bark, added on the third day

ingredients.name: lemon peel
ingredients.note: thinly sliced, added on the third day

ingredients.name: dry red wine
ingredients.note: optional in the wine variant (orig. 1 bottle = 750 ml of red wine and 500 ml of vinegar per 2 kg of plums)

steps: Wipe the bloom off 1 kg of ripe węgierka plums, stud each one in several places with cloves, and pack them in an earthenware jar.

Bring 500 g of finely crushed sugar to the boil with 375 ml of good vinegar (for a milder version use 250 ml of strong vinegar and 375 ml of dry red wine per 1 kg of plums), skim carefully, and pour the lukewarm liquor over the plums.
On the second day, pour off the vinegar liquor, bring it to the boil, and pour it a little warmer over the plums.
On the third day, pour off the liquor again, add cinnamon and thinly sliced lemon peel, bring it to the boil, and pour it boiling over the plums.

On the fourth day, pour off the liquor, bring it to the boil, add the plums, and bring it once gently to the boil so the skins do not burst. Cool completely, pack into a jar, seal, and store in a dry, cool pantry.

name: Peeled plums pickled in vinegar
summary: Ripe węgierka plums, peeled, cooked briefly in a spiced liquor of vinegar, sugar, cinnamon and cloves, then pasteurized in jars for half an hour.

ingredients.name: węgierka plums
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of ripe węgierka plums, peeled

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar per 1 kg of plums

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of very good vinegar per 1 kg of plums

steps: Peel 1 kg of ripe węgierka plums.
Bring 500 ml of very good vinegar to the boil in a pan with 500 g of sugar, cinnamon and cloves.
Drop the peeled plums briefly into the boiling vinegar liquor and bring it to the boil once. Then lift out the fruit, pack it into jars, and cover it with the well-cooled liquor.

Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle of cold water, and pasteurize for 30 minutes from the moment the water boils. Leave the jars in the water until completely cool, wipe them dry, and store them in a dry, cool place.

name: Sour cherries pickled in vinegar
summary: Dark sour cherries or red Łutówka sour cherries covered on three successive days with an increasingly warm vinegar-and-sugar syrup containing cloves and cinnamon, then briefly brought to the boil in the syrup on the fourth day.

ingredients.name: sour cherries
ingredients.note: orig. 2 litres of dark sour cherries or red Łutówka sour cherries (about 1.4 kg), stemmed

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar per 2 litres of cherries

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter litre of good vinegar per 2 litres of cherries

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.note: orig. a dozen or so cloves, added on the third day

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: a piece of bark, added on the third day

steps: Stem 2 l of dark sour cherries or red Łutówka sour cherries and put them in an earthenware jar or a porcelain bowl.
Bring 250 ml of good vinegar to the boil with 500 g of sugar, cool it, and pour it over the cherries until the next day.
On the second day, pour off the vinegar liquor, boil it, and pour the warm syrup over the cherries.
On the third day, pour off the syrup again, add a dozen or so cloves and a little cinnamon, bring it to the boil, and pour it boiling over the fruit.

On the fourth day, pour off the syrup, bring it to the boil, add the cherries, and bring it to the boil once. Once cool, pack the fruit into jars so it is completely covered by the syrup, seal, and store in a dry, cool place.

name: Spiced pickled pears in vinegar syrup
summary: Sweet-sour bergamot, bonkreta or muscatel pears cooked soft in a syrup of vinegar, sugar, cloves and cinnamon, then covered twice more with the boiled syrup at intervals of several days.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: bergamot, bonkreta or muscatel pears, peeled and cored

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of good vinegar per 1 kg of pears

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half kilograms of sugar per 1 kg of pears

steps: Peel the pears, remove the cores, halve the larger fruit and leave the smaller ones whole.
Bring 500 ml of good vinegar to the boil with 1.5 kg of sugar, 6 cloves and a piece of cinnamon. Add the pears and cook over low heat for about 60 minutes, until soft.
Lift the soft pears with a slotted spoon onto a sieve to drain well, and once cool pack them into jars.
Boil the remaining syrup a few more times so it thickens, skim it carefully, cool it, and pour it over the pears in the jars.

After a few days, pour the syrup off the pears, boil it a couple of times, and pour it back over the fruit once cool. After another 2 days, do this one last time. Once cool, seal the jars and store them in a dry, cool place.

name: Spiced pickled melon in vinegar syrup
summary: Pieces of ripe melon cooked soft in vinegar, then covered for three days with an ever thicker sugar syrup of cloves and cinnamon, to serve with roast meat.

ingredients.name: melon
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of ripe but firm melon, peeled and cut into pieces

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: cold, good vinegar for cooking the melon

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 500 g on the first day, 125 g (half a quarter kilogram) on the second day, and about 125 g on the third

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of water for the syrup

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: a piece of bark, added on the third day

steps: Peel a ripe but not overripe melon, cut it into neat pieces, put them in a wide pan, cover with cold good vinegar, and cook covered until soft. Then pour off the vinegar.
For every 500 g of melon, cook a syrup from 500 g of sugar and 250 ml of water, and cover the pieces with the lukewarm syrup until the next day.
On the second day, pour off the syrup, add 125 g of finely crushed sugar, bring it to the boil, and pour it hot over the melon.
On the third day, pour off the syrup again, add the remaining 125 g of sugar, the cloves and the cinnamon, bring it to the boil, pour the hot syrup over the melon, and leave it to cool.
On the fourth day, pack the melon and syrup into jars (if after a few days the syrup is too thin, pour it off once more, boil it, and pour it back once cool) and store them in a dry, cool place.

name: Pickled melon in spiced vinegar
summary: Pieces of half-ripe melon blanched in water that is never allowed to boil, then covered on four successive days with an ever thicker syrup of vinegar and sugar, with cloves and cinnamon.

ingredients.name: melon
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a kilogram of half-ripe melon, cut into pieces

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of good vinegar

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.note: a piece of bark, added on the fourth day

steps: Cut a half-ripe melon into neat pieces, put them in an earthenware or enamel pan, cover with cold water, and heat over low heat until the fruit softens, without letting the water boil. Then drain.
For 750 g of melon, bring 500 ml of good vinegar and 500 g of sugar to the boil together, cool the syrup, and pour it lukewarm over the pieces of fruit.
Every day for 4 days, pour off the syrup, reduce it, and pour it back over the melon, each time a little thicker. On the fourth day, add cloves and cinnamon while the syrup boils.
Once completely cool, pack the preserve into jars, seal them, and store them in a dry, cool pantry.

name: Crabapples pickled in vinegar
summary: Whole crabapples blanched in boiling water and cooked soft in a syrup of vinegar, sugar, cinnamon, cloves and vanilla.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a kilogram of sugar

steps: Prick the crabapples with a thin wooden pin and blanch them in boiling water.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 1 l of good vinegar, 750 g of sugar, cinnamon, cloves and, if you like, a small piece of vanilla.
Drop the drained crabapples into the boiling vinegar syrup and cook over a moderate heat until soft.

Lift out the soft crabapples and pack them into jars. Reduce the syrup until thick, skimming all the time, cool it, and pour it over the fruit (if after a few days the syrup thins, pour it off, boil it again, and pour it back once cool). Seal the jars and store them in a dry, cool place.

name: Mixed fruit pickled in wine vinegar
summary: A layered preserve of seasonal fruit—Łutówka sour cherries, halved apricots, melon and greengages—added in turn and cooked in a spiced syrup of wine vinegar, sugar, cloves, cinnamon and white wine.

ingredients.name: wine vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a quarter litres of the best wine vinegar

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 2 kilograms of sugar chopped into small pieces

ingredients.name: sour cherries (łutówki)
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of red sour cherries

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.note: orig. half a deka of cloves

ingredients.name: apricots
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram, halved and stoned

ingredients.name: greengages
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of ripe greengages (optionally also bergamot or bonkreta pears, early transparent apples, and węgierka plums)

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of white French wine, to top up the syrup if needed

steps: Bring 1.25 l of the best wine vinegar to the boil with 2 kg of finely crushed sugar, pour it into an earthenware jar, and once completely cool add 500 g of red Łutówka sour cherries.
After 2 days, pour the syrup into a pan, add 5 g of cloves and 10 g of cinnamon, bring it to the boil, and pour it boiling over the cherries.
When apricots come into season, pour off the syrup from the cherries and cool it. Put 500 g of halved, stoned apricots into the cold syrup, bring it to the boil, and pour it hot over the cherries.

In the same way, as each fruit ripens, pour off and cool the syrup, add 500 g of cut melon and 500 g of ripe greengages (and, if you like, bergamot pears, summer early transparents and węgierka plums), bring it to the boil, and pour it over the fruit already in the jar. If there is not enough syrup, add 500 ml of dry white wine and boil them together.

name: Dried Peeled Pears
summary: Choice dried pears of noble varieties, partially dried in a lukewarm oven, pressed under a weight with a dusting of sugar, and dried again.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: large, ripe, not overly juicy, of a choice variety

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for lightly sprinkling the layers under the press

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for submerging the peeled pears

steps: Peel the ripe pears, cut them in half, remove the cores, and drop the fruit immediately into cold water.
Remove the pears from the water, drain, arrange on baking sheets, and place into a lukewarm oven until slightly wilted.
Take out the fruit, smooth each piece by hand, and return to the lukewarm oven.
Pack the still-undried pears tightly in layers in a vessel, sprinkling lightly with sugar, cover with a wooden board, weight down with a stone, and leave under the press for several days.
Remove the pressed pears, finish drying in a lukewarm oven, and pack into dry jars.

name: Dried Peeled Pears (Alternative Method)
summary: Pears poached in lightly sweetened water, optionally stuffed with thick apple preserve, sprinkled with citrus sugar, and dried in a low oven.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for soaking and cooking the pears

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: part for cooking in the water, the rest crushed for dusting on top

ingredients.name: lemon or orange zest
ingredients.note: grated, for mixing with the sugar for dusting

steps: Peel the ripe pears, remove the cores, and submerge the fruit in cold water.
Cover the drained pears in a pot with fresh cold water and a little sugar, and cook until completely tender (subsequent batches of fruit can be cooked in the same liquid by adding a little water).
Remove the cooked pears, optionally fill the cavities with thick apple preserve, and dry slowly in a very low oven.
Sprinkle the fruit with crushed sugar mixed with grated lemon or orange zest, then finish drying until the candied pears are dry, soft, and translucent.

name: Steamed Millet Pudding
summary: Savory-sweet millet pudding steamed in a water bath from millet groats cooked in milk, enriched with rendered pork fatback, egg yolks, dill, and whipped egg whites.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling water for scalding the groats twice

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. 1/2 liter for cooking the groats (plus an optional 500 ml for serving)

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: orig. 4 dkg, plus a little fat for the mold

steps: Rinse the millet groats thoroughly and scald them twice with boiling water to remove any bitterness.
Pour the groats into the boiling milk, cook over low heat until they begin to thicken, then place the covered pot into a preheated oven (160 °C) for 30 minutes and let cool.
Pour the rendered pork fatback into the cooled millet, beat in two egg yolks one at a time, and season with a teaspoon of sugar, salt to taste, and chopped dill.
Gently fold in the stiffly whipped egg whites, transfer the mixture to a greased and tightly sealed pudding mold, and steam in a water bath for 90 minutes from the moment the water returns to a boil.

name: Pan-Fried Barley Groat Cakes
summary: Thickly cooked barley groats chilled in a flat layer until firm, cut into squares, dredged in wheat flour, and pan-fried until golden on both sides.
steps: Cook the barley groats in salted water until thick.
Spread the hot groats on a platter in an even layer about 1 cm thick and leave to cool completely until firm.
Cut the chilled barley into even squares, dredge each piece in wheat flour, and fry on both sides in hot oil or lard until lightly browned.

name: Placki owsiane z ziemniakami (oat and potato yeast pancakes)
summary: Hearty yeast pancakes made from oat flour blended with cooked and raw grated potatoes, pan-fried skillet-wide until golden.

ingredients.name: cooked potatoes
ingredients.note: orig. 25 dkg, boiled in their jackets

steps: Dissolve the fresh yeast in 250 ml of lukewarm water, mix with the oat flour, and set in a warm place for about 30 minutes to rise.
Peel the jacket-boiled potatoes and press them through a ricer, and peel and grate the raw potato on a fine grater.
Add the mashed cooked potatoes and grated raw potato to the risen yeast mixture, salt to taste, and thoroughly work the batter.
Heat the vegetable oil well in a skillet and fry large pancakes the full width of the pan for about 4–5 minutes on each side until golden. Serve piping hot.

name: Śledź wędzony faszerowany (stuffed smoked herring)
summary: A cold appetiser of soaked smoked herring mashed with boiled potatoes and sautéed onion, shaped into a whole fish on a platter.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the onion and 1 tbsp for drizzling

steps: Soak the dry smoked herring in cold water for 24 hours (1440 minutes), then reserve the head and tail, carefully bone the flesh, and grind or mash into a smooth paste.
Boil the potatoes until tender for about 20 minutes, drain, and pass through a ricer.
Finely chop the onions and sauté in 1 tbsp of vegetable oil for about 5 minutes.
Combine the herring paste with the mashed potatoes and sautéed onion, season with liquid seasoning, pepper, and salt if needed, and work into a uniform paste.

Shape the mixture into the form of a fish on a serving platter, attach the reserved head and tail, drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp of vegetable oil, and chill for 3 hours (180 minutes) before serving.

name: Smoked Cod in Olive Oil
summary: Boneless, skinless pieces of smoked cod lightly seasoned with black pepper and marinated in refined vegetable oil for twenty-four hours before serving.
steps: Carefully remove the skin and bones from the smoked cod and break the flesh into neat, even lengthwise pieces.
Arrange the pieces of fish in a serving dish, season with a pinch of freshly ground black pepper, and pour the oil over them.
Set aside in a cool place for 24 hours before serving so the fish absorbs the oil.

name: White cabbage and apple slaw (surówka z kapusty i jabłka)
summary: A crisp raw slaw of finely shredded white cabbage and tart Antonówka apple dressed with citric acid, sugar, and vegetable oil.
steps: Shred the white cabbage very finely, and peel and grate or equally finely shred the Antonówka apple.
Combine the cabbage with the apple, season with salt, and sprinkle with sugar.
Dissolve the citric acid in 1 tbsp of water, pour over the salad together with the vegetable oil, and toss thoroughly.
Cover the dish and set aside for 6 hours (360 minutes) to let the cabbage soften and absorb the seasonings before serving.

name: Stynki marynowane w occie (pickled fried smelt)
summary: Smelt fried in oil and covered with a lukewarm vinegar marinade flavoured with peppercorns and bay leaf.
steps: Clean, gut, rinse, dry, salt, and dredge the larger smelt in plain wheat flour.
Fry the fish in hot vegetable oil for about 8–10 minutes, cool completely, and arrange in a bowl or jar.
Bring the vinegar to a boil with the peppercorns and bay leaf, then let cool until lukewarm.
Pour the lukewarm vinegar marinade over the smelt and leave in a cool place overnight (about 8 hours). Serve the next day.

name: Strucle postne drożdżowe (Lenten yeast loaves)
summary: Economical Lenten yeast loaves prepared with water, vegetable oil, honey, and almond flavouring, topped with poppy seeds or nigella.

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.note: orig. 2 tbsp honey and 25 saccharin tablets

steps: Mix about 450 g of plain wheat flour with 750 ml of lukewarm water, the dissolved fresh yeast, and salt, beat vigorously, and leave in a warm place for about 45 minutes until the sponge rises and cracks on the surface.
Pour the vegetable oil, honey, and almond flavouring into the risen sponge, add the remaining plain wheat flour, and knead well until the dense dough no longer sticks to your hands.
Set the dough aside to rise again, then divide into 6 portions, shape into oblong loaves, and place on flour-dusted baking sheets.
Let the loaves rise a third time, brush the tops with water mixed with a little honey, and sprinkle with poppy seeds or nigella seeds.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 40 minutes until the loaves feel light and release easily from the sheet.

name: Hard Candies
summary: Homemade brittle sugar candies cooked with strong vinegar and flavored with a chosen flavoring oil, raspberry juice, or chocolate.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: as much as the sugar absorbs when dipped

ingredients.name: flavoring oil
ingredients.note: a few drops of rose, vanilla, lemon, or peppermint oil

steps: Dip 500 g of sugar briefly in water until it stops hissing, then transfer to a saucepan and set over high heat.
Once the sugar comes to a boil, pour in 2 tablespoons of strong vinegar and boil until the caramel thickens and a drop plunged into cold water becomes brittle and snaps when bitten.
Add a few drops of the chosen flavoring oil (rose, vanilla, lemon, or peppermint), stir quickly, and pour the mixture onto a marble slab greased with olive oil.
When the candy cools slightly while still pliable, score it into strips, and once completely cooled, break into pieces and wrap in colored papers.

name: Iced Coffee
summary: Strong black coffee chilled on ice and served in cups with lightly sweetened, whipped, and ice-chilled heavy cream.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: fine, for lightly sweetening the cream

steps: Brew strong black coffee, pour into bottles, cork tightly, and pack in ice until thoroughly chilled.
Whip the fresh heavy cream to stiff peaks, sweeten lightly with sugar, mix gently, and set the bowl in ice as well.
To serve, pour the cold coffee into cups, add a portion of ice-chilled whipped cream, stir very gently, and top with another portion of whipped cream.

name: Piernik owsiany z marchwią (oat and carrot gingerbread)
summary: A gingerbread cake that keeps well, made with oat and wheat flours, plenty of finely grated carrots, and aromatic spices.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing the tin

ingredients.name: crushed mixed spices: black pepper, allspice, cloves, cinnamon, ginger, and mace

steps: Peel the carrots and grate them on the finest grater.
Thoroughly knead the grated carrots with the oat flour and plain wheat flour.
Add the sugar, egg, vegetable oil, baking soda, and crushed spices, then knead the dough for about 30 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a baking tin greased with oil and dusted with breadcrumbs.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.

name: Honeyless spiced gingerbread (piernik bez miodu)
summary: A fluffy spiced gingerbread cake made with dark caramelised sugar and beaten eggs, baked without added honey.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 25 dkg (200 g for egg yolks and 50 g for caramel)

ingredients.name: ground mixed spice: cloves, allspice, and cinnamon
lard or vegetable oil
ingredients.note: plus extra for greasing cake pan

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 1 cup (250 ml) + a few tbsp (30 ml) for caramel

steps: Beat the egg yolks with 200 g of sugar and 1 tbsp of lard or oil until pale and fluffy.
Caramelise the remaining 50 g of sugar in a skillet to a dark caramel, dissolve in 30 ml of water, then bring to a boil with the mixed spice and the remaining 250 ml of water.
Mix the plain wheat flour with baking powder, gradually pour in the hot caramel mixture while stirring continuously, then combine thoroughly with the beaten egg yolks.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold gently into the batter.
Transfer the batter into a springform pan greased with fat and dusted with breadcrumbs. Bake in an oven preheated to 160–170 °C for 45–60 minutes.

name: Mint gingerbread cookies (pierniczki miętowe)
summary: Simple Lenten mint gingerbread cookies leavened with baker's ammonia, shaped into small balls and baked until pale golden.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 3 cups + extra for dusting baking sheet

steps: Knead the plain wheat flour, water, sugar, baker's ammonia, and peppermint oil into a uniform, smooth dough.
Shape the dough into balls the size of a small walnut (about 20–25 g), remembering that they expand significantly during baking.
Arrange the balls spaced apart on a baking sheet dusted with plain wheat flour and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 15 minutes until very lightly golden.

name: Paluszki na soku owocowym (fruit syrup cookie sticks)
summary: Crisp baked cookie sticks kneaded with thick raspberry, currant, or strawberry fruit syrup.

ingredients.name: raspberry, currant, or strawberry fruit syrup
ingredients.note: to achieve the right dough consistency

steps: Beat the eggs with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Add the plain wheat flour mixed with the baking powder.
Gradually pour in enough raspberry, currant, or strawberry fruit syrup to knead a moderately soft, elastic dough, then knead it well.
Roll the dough into thin ropes and cut into pieces about 12 cm long.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 20 minutes until golden.

name: Thin Potato and Poppy Seed Cookies
summary: Thinly rolled, crumbly potato-and-yeast cookies with plenty of poppy seeds, cut out with a glass.
steps: Combine the wheat flour with the boiled and riced potatoes, sugar, crumbled fresh yeast, oil or lard, and dry poppy seeds, and knead into a fairly firm dough.
Roll out the dough on a board as thinly as possible and cut out round cookies with a glass.
Arrange the cookies on a baking sheet and bake in a preheated oven (180–190 °C) for about 15–20 minutes until lightly golden.

name: Solanki owsiane z kminkiem (savoury oat and potato caraway crackers)
summary: Crisp, savoury crackers made with oat flour, boiled potatoes, and caraway seeds, cut into rounds with a drinking glass and baked until golden.
steps: Sift the oat flour into a bowl and mix with the baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds.
Add the riced cooked potatoes, vegetable oil, and egg, and knead everything into a firm, cohesive dough.
Roll out the dough very thinly and stamp out rounds using a drinking glass.
Arrange the rounds on a baking sheet and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 15 minutes until lightly browned.

name: Christmas Eve Kutia (Wheat Berry and Poppy Seed Pudding)
summary: Traditional Polish Christmas Eve dish of soaked and boiled whole wheat berries tossed with scalded, finely ground poppy seeds and sweetened with sugar or honey.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold water for soaking and boiling the wheat plus boiling water for scalding the poppy seeds

steps: Soak the whole wheat berries in cold water overnight, and scald the poppy seeds with boiling water in a separate bowl and leave overnight as well.
The next day, boil the soaked wheat berries in fresh water until completely tender, then drain.
Drain the poppy seeds, pat them dry, and pass twice through a meat grinder fitted with a fine plate.
Mix the ground poppy seeds with the cooked wheat berries and sweeten to taste with sugar or honey.

name: Raspberry Jelly
summary: Classic nineteenth-century jelly made from raspberries and red currants boiled with fine sugar over high heat and strained through a fine sieve.

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: approx. 1.5 l; in a ratio of 0.5 l sugar per 0.5 l fruit

steps: Pick over the raspberries and red currants, place them in a wide stoneware or copper pan, and cover with the fine sugar.
Place the pan over very high heat and bring the fruit to a boil without stirring with a spoon.
Bring the mixture to a boil three times, removing the pan from the heat and carefully skimming off the foam each time.
Pour the hot mixture onto a very fine sieve set over a bowl, and pour the clear strained juice immediately into jars.
Leave the jelly in the jars until completely cooled and set, then tie with parchment paper and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Raspberry Jelly Another Way
summary: Clear jelly made from raspberry juice extracted in a water bath and combined with gooseberry or currant juice.

ingredients.name: raspberries
ingredients.note: ripe, for 2 glasses (500 ml) of strained juice

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: 6 glasses (2 glasses of sugar per 1 glass of mixed juice)

steps: Place the picked-over raspberries into a stoneware pot, set it inside a larger pot of hot water, and heat on the stove (or in a warm oven) until the fruit releases its juice.
Pour the heated raspberries onto a sieve and drain the clear juice without pressing.
Measure 500 ml of the strained raspberry juice, combine with 250 ml of gooseberry or currant juice, and add 1.2 kg of fine sugar.
Cook the mixture first over higher and then over lower heat, removing the pan from the burner several times and carefully skimming off the foam.
Test with a drop on a cold saucer to see if the jelly sets; pour hot into warmed jars and seal tightly once cooled.

name: Red Currant Jelly
summary: Traditional jelly made from red currants layered with fine sugar, optionally flavored with ripe raspberries.
steps: Stem the currants, rinse in cold water, and drain (optionally adding the ripe raspberries).
In a stoneware pan, arrange alternating layers of fine sugar and fruit until all ingredients are used.
Place the pan over the heat, bring to a boil, and skim off the foam three times, removing the pan from the burner each time.
Strain the hot mixture through a fine sieve into a bowl, then pour the clear juice back into the washed pan.
Bring the juice to a boil once more, skim off the foam, pour into warmed jars while hot, and cover and secure the jars once cooled.

name: Currant Jelly Another Way
summary: Jelly made from ripe currants cooked with a splash of water until burst, then boiled five times with sugar over high heat.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: chopped into pieces, in a ratio of 1 kg per 1 l of strained juice

steps: Transfer the stemmed and rinsed currants to a stoneware pan, add 250 ml of water, and heat on a hot stove, stirring, until the berries burst and soften.
Transfer the hot fruit onto a fine sieve and leave until the juice has drained completely.
Measure the volume of the collected juice and weigh out 1 kg of finely chopped sugar for each 1 l of juice.
Place the sugar into a clean pan, pour the strained currant juice over it, and set over very high heat.
Bring the syrup to a boil five times, removing the pan from the heat and thoroughly skimming off the foam each time.
Test a drop on a cold plate to see if the jelly sets, then pour it hot (without straining again) into warmed jars and seal once cooled.

name: Armenian-Style Currant Jelly
