summary: Jelly made from a blend of red and white currants whose juice is extracted in a water bath without pressing and boiled for fifteen minutes with dissolved sugar.

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: in a ratio of 1 kg per 1 l of strained juice

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for sprinkling the sugar, plus water for the water bath

steps: Place the cleaned and rinsed red and white currants into a covered stoneware vessel, set it in a pot of water, and heat over high heat without letting the berries themselves come to a boil.
As the currants release their juice, carefully ladle it off into a bowl, and transfer the remaining fruit into a linen bag hung to drain freely without squeezing.
Measure the collected juice and weigh out 1 kg of fine sugar for each 1 l of juice.
Place the sugar in a pan, sprinkle it with the water, and heat while stirring constantly with a spoon until half-dissolved and beginning to boil.
Pour the hot currant juice into the sugar, mix thoroughly, and boil together for 15 minutes, skimming off the foam carefully.
When a drop of jelly sets on a cold plate, pour it warm into well-heated jars and tie tightly once cooled.

name: Wild Strawberry Jelly
summary: Fragrant jelly made from fresh wild strawberry juice combined with gooseberry juice for a firm set.

ingredients.name: wild strawberries
ingredients.note: ripe, for 2 glasses (500 ml) of pressed juice

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: 3 glasses (1 glass of sugar per 1 glass of mixed juice)

steps: Crush the ripe wild strawberries and press the juice through a fine sieve or muslin.
Bring the wild strawberry juice alone to a boil, skim it thoroughly, and strain again through a fine sieve.
Measure 500 ml of the clarified wild strawberry juice, mix with 250 ml of gooseberry juice, and add 600 g of fine sugar.
Place the pan over high heat and bring to a boil three times, removing from the burner and skimming off the foam each time.
Lower the heat and finish cooking the jelly while stirring constantly until it begins to set, then pour hot into warmed jars.

name: Rose Petal Jelly
summary: An elegant jelly made from an infusion of fresh rose petals used for preserves and juice from half-ripe gooseberries, boiled with sugar until clear.

ingredients.name: rose petals suitable for preserves
ingredients.note: fresh, trimmed of their white bases

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: boiling: 1 l for cooking the gooseberries and approx. 0.5 l for scalding the rose petals

steps: Pick over the rose petals, trim off the white bases, place in a stoneware pot, and add just enough boiling water to cover; cover and leave until completely cool.
Bring 1 l of water to a boil, add 4 l of half-ripe gooseberries, cook until the juice is released, and strain through a sieve.
Place 1.5 kg of sugar in a stoneware pan and add 750 ml (3 glassfuls) of strained gooseberry juice and 250 ml (1 glassful) of rose infusion.
Bring the mixture to a boil three times over high heat, removing from the burner and skimming the foam each time, then simmer over low heat until thickened.
Strain the hot jelly through a fine sieve and pour immediately into warmed jars.

name: Strawberry Jelly
summary: Fragrant jelly made from ripe pineapple strawberries and white currants, boiled with sugar without stirring.
steps: Hull the strawberries and stem the white currants, place them in a stoneware pan, and cover with the fine sugar on top.
Set the pan over high heat and bring to a boil without stirring with a spoon.
Bring the mixture to a boil three times, removing the pan from the heat and thoroughly skimming off the foam each time.
On the fourth boil, pour the contents of the pan onto a fine sieve set over a bowl.
Pour the strained hot juice immediately into jars, leave to set, and tie tightly.

name: Cranberry Jelly
summary: Ruby-red jelly made from fresh cranberries and sugar, briefly boiled and strained through a fine sieve or muslin.
steps: Pick over the cranberries to remove leaves and stems, rinse thoroughly, and drain.
Place the fine sugar in a stoneware pan, sprinkle it with the water, and spread the cleaned cranberries on top.
Set the pan over high heat and heat without stirring with a spoon until the berries begin to burst and the syrup bubbles.
Bring the mixture to a boil three times, removing from the heat and skimming off the foam each time, then simmer over low heat for just under 15 minutes.
Strain the hot mixture through a fine sieve or muslin and pour the clear juice into warmed jars.

name: Rosół z kurczęcia (Delicate young-chicken broth)
summary: Clear, delicate Polish broth simmered from a small whole chicken with parsley root, carrot, and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.note: small, whole, thoroughly cleaned; orig. half-kilo

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for a 500 g chicken; orig. a litre and a quarter

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the chicken and the broth

steps: Rub the cleaned chicken with salt.
Truss the chicken so it does not fall apart during cooking.
Bring the water to a boil with the parsley root, carrot, and dill.
Lower the chicken into the boiling stock.
Bring the broth back to a boil over high heat.
Skim the foam from the surface of the broth.
Lower the heat so that the broth barely trembles.
Season the broth with salt.
Simmer a small chicken for about 25 minutes until cooked through; an older chicken may require up to 45 minutes.
Cut the cooked chicken into quarters.
Serve the chicken in the broth.

name: Pineapple liqueur
summary: A fragrant liqueur of thin slices of very ripe pineapple and a vanilla pod, macerated for 10 days in spirit and then for a week in a cold sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: pineapple
ingredients.note: a fine, very ripe one, sliced thinly

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 2 litres of the best spirit

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.note: orig. 1 dekagram of vanilla, left whole

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1.25 kilograms of sugar per litre of spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of water per litre of spirit

steps: Slice a very ripe pineapple thinly, put it in a demijohn, add 10 g of whole vanilla, and cover it with 2 l of the best spirit.
Tie the vessel tightly and leave it in the shade for 10 days.

After 10 days, pour off the spirit and strain it through muslin. Cover the pineapple slices left in the bottle with a cold, carefully skimmed syrup cooked from 2.5 kg of sugar and 1 l of water (1.25 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water per litre of spirit) and leave it for 7 days, so the syrup draws out the rest of the aroma and the alcohol.

After a week, pour the syrup off the pineapple and combine it with the spirit set aside earlier, pouring the spirit slowly into the syrup. Filter it through paper, bottle it, cork it firmly, and leave it for 2 months before serving.

name: Lemon liqueur
summary: A clear lemon liqueur made by macerating the peel of two fresh lemons, lightly dried at room temperature, and half a vanilla pod in spirit for four days.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: fresh; the yellow peel pared thinly and lightly dried at room temperature

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre for macerating the peel, plus 0.5 litre of plain spirit added at the end

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of cold boiled water

steps: Pare the yellow peel thinly from 2 fresh lemons and immediately leave it to dry slightly at room temperature to remove the sharp bitterness.
Put the lightly dried lemon peel and half a vanilla pod into a demijohn with 1 l of the best spirit, cover the opening with a clean cloth tied securely in place, and leave in the shade for 4 days.
After 4 days, cook a syrup from 1 kg of crushed sugar and 500 ml of cold boiled water. Skim it carefully after a single boil, and cool it completely.
Slowly pour the lemon spirit strained through muslin and an extra 500 ml of plain spirit into the cold syrup, stirring constantly and keeping the vessel partly covered. Then bottle the clear liqueur.

name: Hawthorn liqueur
summary: A simple liqueur of frost-nipped hawthorn fruit, crushed with a rolling pin and macerated for 10 days in a warm place in a mixture of spirit, rye vodka and crushed sugar candy.

ingredients.name: ripe hawthorn
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre of ripe, frost-nipped hawthorn (about 600 g)

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre of the best spirit (1.5 l in the less sweet version)

ingredients.name: rye vodka
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre of clean, strong rye vodka (1.5 l in the less sweet version)

ingredients.name: sugar candy
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of finely crushed sugar candy

steps: Put 1 l of ripe, frost-nipped hawthorn into a bowl and crush the fruit thoroughly with a rolling pin.

Transfer the crushed hawthorn to a demijohn, pour in 1 l of the best spirit mixed beforehand with 1 l of strong rye vodka (or 1.5 l of each spirit in the less sweet version), and add 1 kg of finely crushed sugar candy.
Leave the demijohn in a warm place for 10 days, shaking it every day.
After 10 days, filter the liqueur, bottle it, cork it, and store it in a cool place.

name: Rowanberry liqueur
summary: A traditional liqueur of frost-nipped rowanberries, blanched several times in boiling water, macerated for a month in spirit, then combined with a sugar syrup and cleared for another month.

ingredients.name: rowanberries
ingredients.note: orig. several litres of fine, ripe, lightly frost-nipped rowanberries

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: the best, enough to cover the rowanberries completely

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of crushed sugar per 1 litre of spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki of cold water for the syrup, per 1 l of spirit (plus boiling water for blanching the rowanberries several times)

steps: Pour boiling water several times over 2 l of ripe, lightly frost-nipped rowanberries in a colander, and leave them to drain well.
Put the blanched rowanberries into a large demijohn, cover them with 1 l of the best spirit so the fruit is completely covered, seal it, and leave it in a warm room for 1 month.
After a month, pour off and strain the rowan spirit. Cook a syrup from 1 kg of crushed sugar and 375 ml of cold water, skim it carefully, and cool it.

Mix the clarified, cooled syrup with the strained rowanberry spirit, pour into a clean demijohn, cork, and leave in a cool place for another month. Then filter through paper, bottle, cork, seal with wax, and leave for 6 months before serving.

name: Coffee liqueur
summary: A fragrant coffee and vanilla liqueur on spirit macerated first for 4 days with a vanilla pod, then for a week with 35 lightly roasted mocha beans.

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre of the best spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter litre (250 ml) of boiling water for the spirit, and two and a half szklanki (2.5 szklanki = 625 ml) of cold water for the syrup

ingredients.name: mocha coffee beans
ingredients.note: orig. 35 mocha beans roasted light brown

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a quarter kilograms of crushed sugar

steps: Mix 1 l of the best spirit with 250 ml of boiling water, pour it into a demijohn, add 1 large vanilla pod, and leave it in the shade in a warm room for 4 days.
After 4 days, take out the vanilla pod, add 35 mocha beans roasted light brown to the spirit, and leave it for 7 days.
After a week, strain the spirit through white flannel. Cook a syrup from 1.25 kg of crushed sugar and 625 ml of cold water, skim it carefully after a single boil, and cool it completely.
Pour the strained coffee spirit into the cold syrup, mix well, filter it, bottle it, cork it, and keep it in a cool place for 6 months before serving.

name: Benedictine-style herbal liqueur
summary: A homemade Benedictine-style herbal and spice liqueur made with spirit and rum, saffron, angelica root, juniper berries, a small piece of yellow gentian root and a vanilla pod, sweetened with thick sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter litre of very good rum

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre (500 ml) for soaking the roots, plus one and a half litres (1.5 l) poured through paper

ingredients.name: angelica root
ingredients.note: orig. 1 dekagram of fresh angelica, or dried angelica crushed in a mortar

ingredients.name: juniper berries
ingredients.note: orig. 1.5 dekagrams of lightly crushed juniper

ingredients.name: yellow gentian root
ingredients.note: orig. a scrap of Gentiana lutea root the size of half a pea

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a quarter litres of cold water

steps: Soak 2.5 g of saffron in 250 ml of very good rum for 24 hours.

In a separate vessel, combine 500 ml of the best spirit with 10 g of fresh angelica or crushed dried angelica, 15 g of lightly crushed juniper berries, a piece of yellow gentian root (Gentiana lutea) the size of half a pea, and 1 vanilla pod. Leave to soak in the shade for 3 days.
After 3 days, pour 1.5 l of plain spirit through filter paper into a three-litre demijohn, add the filtered spirit from the herbs and the rum with the saffron, and mix well.
Cook a syrup from 2 kg of crushed sugar and 1.25 l of cold water, skim it carefully, pour the boiling syrup into a bowl, and cool it completely.
Pour the aromatic spirit gradually into the cooled syrup, stirring constantly. Cover for a few hours, then bottle, cork, seal with wax, and keep in a cool place for 6 months before serving.

name: Capuchin-style spice liqueur
summary: A rich monastic-style spice and herb liqueur of sweet flag, myrrh, cinnamon, angelica, dried orange peel, green oranges, saffron, nutmeg, cloves, ginger and vanilla.

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre for soaking the roots, plus one and a half litres (1.5 l) of plain spirit added to the syrup

ingredients.name: dried orange peel
ingredients.note: orig. 30 dekagrams of dried orange peel

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: orig. named twice in the printing: 8 dekagrams (80 g) and 2 dekagrams (20 g)

steps: Combine 1 l of the best spirit with 140 g of sweet-flag rhizome, 140 g of myrrh, 140 g of cinnamon, 80 g of angelica root, 300 g of dried orange peel, 100 g of saffron, 10 g of nutmeg, 40 g of cloves, 40 g of ginger, 1 large vanilla pod and 4 small green oranges. Leave to soak for exactly 3 days.
After 3 days, strain the infusion off the roots through soft white flannel.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 2.5 kg of crushed sugar and 1.25 l of cold water, then leave it to cool completely.

Slowly pour 1.5 l of plain spirit and the strained spice infusion into the completely cold syrup, stirring constantly. Leave for 60 minutes, then filter through paper, bottle, cork, seal with wax, and leave for a year before serving.

name: Raspberry liqueur
summary: A fragrant raspberry liqueur made by steeping two successive batches of fresh, ripe raspberries in the same spirit for 24 hours each, preserving the full aroma without excessive acidity.

ingredients.name: raspberries
ingredients.note: orig. about 3 litres of fresh ripe raspberries for the first pour, and about 2 litres (half a 4-litre demijohn) for the second

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: the best, enough to cover the raspberries completely (yielding about 1 l of filtered infusion)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half kilograms of crushed sugar per 1 litre of filtered spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 3 szklanki of cold water per 1.5 kg of sugar

steps: Put 3 l of freshly picked ripe raspberries into a four-litre demijohn, cover them with the best spirit so it covers the fruit with a little to spare, and leave it in the shade for 24 hours.

After a day, pour off the spirit, discard the spent fruit, fill the demijohn halfway (about 2 l) with fresh raspberries, cover them with the spirit you poured off, and leave it in the shade again for exactly 24 hours.
Pour off the raspberry spirit a second time and filter it at once through paper.

For every 1 l of filtered spirit, dissolve 1.5 kg of crushed sugar in 750 ml of cold water, bring to the boil, skim carefully, cool completely, and combine with the raspberry spirit, stirring constantly. Bottle, cork, seal with wax, and keep in a cool cellar for 8 months.

name: Wild-strawberry liqueur
summary: A fragrant liqueur of fresh ripe wild strawberries macerated for 24 hours in spirit, then combined, after filtering, with a cold sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: wild strawberries
ingredients.note: ripe and fresh, filling the demijohn to 3/4 of its volume

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: the best, enough to cover the wild strawberries with some to spare

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of crushed sugar per litre of spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of cold water per litre of spirit

steps: Fill a good-sized demijohn to 3/4 of its height with fresh ripe wild strawberries, cover them with 1 l of the best spirit so it covers the fruit with some to spare, and leave it for 24 hours.

The next day, pour the spirit off the wild strawberries and filter it through paper (the fruit left behind can be covered with sugar for 8 days, strained without pressing, and combined with plain spirit at 500 ml of spirit per 1 l of juice as a second, lighter liqueur).
Bring a syrup to the boil from 1 kg of crushed sugar and 500 ml of cold water for every litre of filtered spirit, then take it off the heat and cool it completely.
Pour the filtered wild-strawberry spirit into the cold syrup, stirring constantly, leave it for 2 hours, then bottle it, cork it, and keep it in a cool cellar for 6 months before serving.

name: Vanilla liqueur
summary: A classic vanilla liqueur of 80 g of vanilla pods macerated for two weeks in 2.5 litres of spirit, then filtered and combined with a cold syrup of 3 kg of sugar.

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 2.5 litres of the best spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half litres of cold water

steps: Pour 2.5 l of the best spirit into a demijohn, add 80 g of vanilla pods, cork it tightly, and leave it in a room, in the shade, for 2 weeks.
After 2 weeks, pour the spirit through soft white flannel and filter it through paper.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 3 kg of crushed sugar and 1.5 l of cold water, skim it carefully, and once it is boiling well take it off the heat and cool it completely.
Pour the filtered vanilla spirit into the completely cold syrup, stirring constantly, and leave for 2 hours. Then bottle, cork, seal with wax, and keep in a cool place for 3 months before serving.

name: Rose liqueur
summary: A pink liqueur scented with rose oil dissolved for a day in spirit, combined with a cold sugar syrup and coloured with alkermes.

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 2 litres of the best spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half litres of cold water

ingredients.name: alkermes
ingredients.note: orig. 2 teaspoons of alkermes for colour

steps: Pour 2 l of the best spirit into a demijohn, add 8 drops (about 0.4 ml) of rose oil, cork it tightly, and leave it in the shade for 24 hours.
The next day, cook a syrup from 3 kg of crushed sugar and 1.5 l of cold water, skim it carefully, and once it boils take it off the heat and cool it completely.
Pour the aromatic spirit a little at a time into the completely cold syrup, stirring constantly, then pour it back into the demijohn and leave it in the shade until the next day.
The following day, add 2 teaspoons of alkermes to give it a pink colour, leave it in the demijohn for another 4 days, then bottle it, cork it, and keep it in a cool place for 4 months before serving.

name: Rose liqueur, another way
summary: A fragrant homemade rose liqueur of sugar-rose petals macerated for four days in spirit and combined with a sugar syrup cooked with a further portion of rose petals and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: sugar-rose petals
ingredients.note: the white tips removed: 500 g for the maceration in spirit and 250 g for the syrup

ingredients.name: 95% rectified spirit
ingredients.note: enough to cover the rose petals in the demijohn

ingredients.name: currant juice
ingredients.note: optional, a few teaspoons of clear juice for colour

steps: Cut the pale tips off sugar-rose petals, put 500 g of petals into a glass demijohn or a large jar, cover them with spirit so it covers them completely, and leave it in a shaded place for 4 days.

Cook a syrup from 1 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water (or rose water), add the remaining 250 g of trimmed rose petals, squeeze in the lemon juice (and, if you like, a few teaspoons of currant juice for colour), and cook briefly over low heat.
Combine the cooled rose syrup with the spirit infusion, petals and all, and leave it in the closed demijohn for a few more days.
Strain the finished liqueur through thick muslin or gauze and bottle it.

name: Orange liqueur
summary: A fragrant liqueur of the segments of 12 peeled malinówka oranges, macerated for 3 weeks in spirit and 4 days in syrup, scented for 3 days with fresh orange peel, and finished with pineapple syrup and rum.

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.note: orig. 12 ripe malinówka oranges, peeled and divided into segments with the white pith and the seeds removed, plus the thick peel of 1 fresh orange

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1 litre of the best spirit

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of sugar for the syrup

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of water for the syrup

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka of the best rum

steps: Peel 12 ripe malinówka oranges carefully, remove the white bitter layer and the seeds, divide the flesh into segments in their thin membranes, put them in a demijohn, cover them with 1 l of the best spirit, and leave it in the shade for 3 weeks.
After 3 weeks, pour off the spirit, cover the orange segments with a cold syrup made from 1 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave it for 4 days.
After 4 days, pour off the syrup, mix it with the spirit set aside earlier, pour it back into the demijohn, add the thick peel of 1 fresh orange, and leave it for exactly 3 days.

Pour the liquid off the orange peel, add 250 ml of pineapple syrup and 250 ml of the best rum, mix well, filter it through paper, bottle it, cork it, and keep it in a cool place for 3 months before serving.

name: Orange and lemon liqueur “Luizan”
summary: A fine citrus and spice liqueur of 8 whole malinówka oranges and 6 lemons studded with cloves and macerated for two weeks in 4 litres of spirit with vanilla and cinnamon.

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: fine, whole, each studded with 2 cloves

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.note: 2 cloves stuck into each of 8 oranges and 6 lemons

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 4 litres of the best spirit

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kilogram of finely crushed sugar for each of the 4 litres of spirit (4 kg), plus about 200 g for a light syrup for the 2-day rinse of the fruit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre of cold water for each of the 4 litres of spirit (2 l), plus about 500 ml for the light syrup

steps: Stud 8 malinówka oranges and 6 lemons with 2 cloves each (28 cloves in all). Pack them in an eight-litre demijohn with a wide neck, add 1 large vanilla pod and 1 cinnamon stick, cover them with 4 l of the best spirit, seal it, and leave it in the shade at room temperature for 2 weeks.

After 2 weeks, pour off the spirit and cover the fruit with a very light cold syrup of 200 g of sugar and 500 ml of water for 2 days, to draw out the rest of the alcohol (then pour this first light syrup off into lesser vodkas).

Cook the proper syrup from 4 kg of finely crushed sugar and 2 l of cold water (1 kg of sugar and 500 ml of water per litre of spirit), skim it carefully, take it off the heat after a single boil, and cool it completely.
Pour the strained citrus spirit a little at a time into the cold syrup, stirring constantly. Then filter it, bottle it, cork it, and leave it in a cool place for 8 months before serving.

name: Mint liqueur
summary: A homemade green mint liqueur made from fresh peppermint macerated in spirit for a day, with pharmacy-supplied mint essence and sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: fresh peppermint
ingredients.note: orig. 35 dekagrams of fresh peppermint (or 25 dekagrams = 250 g of dried mint)

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter litre (250 ml) for soaking the mint, plus 1 litre poured into the cooled syrup

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a quarter kilograms of crushed sugar

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a litre of cold water

ingredients.name: mint essence
ingredients.note: orig. 30 drops of pharmacy-supplied mint essence (oil)

ingredients.name: food-grade chlorophyll
ingredients.note: a few drops of spirit-soluble chlorophyll for colour (optional)

steps: Soak 350 g of fresh peppermint (or 250 g of dried mint) in 250 ml of the best spirit for 24 hours.

The next day, bring a syrup of 1.25 kg of crushed sugar and 750 ml of cold water to the boil once, take it off the heat, and once it has cooled a little pour in 1 l of plain spirit, stirring all the time.

When the syrup and spirit are completely cold, add 250 ml of the spirit strained off the mint and 30 drops (about 1.5 ml) of mint essence (and, if you like, a few drops of spirit-soluble chlorophyll for a bright green colour).
Mix the liqueur thoroughly, immediately filter through paper, bottle, cork, seal with wax, and keep in a cool place for 6 months before serving.

name: French herbal liqueur
summary: A golden herbal and spice liqueur of anise, angelica root, sage and separately macerated saffron, combined hot with a sugar syrup acidulated with tartaric acid.

ingredients.name: spirit
ingredients.note: orig. half a litre (500 ml) for the herbs, half a szklanka (125 ml) for the saffron, and 3.5 litres poured into the hot syrup

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: orig. 1 dekagram of saffron, soaked separately

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. 4 kilograms of finely grated or crushed sugar

ingredients.name: tartaric acid
ingredients.note: orig. half a teaspoon of tartaric acid

steps: Soak 250 g of anise, 30 g of angelica root and 10 g of sage in 500 ml of the best spirit.
In a separate vessel, soak 10 g of saffron in 125 ml of spirit, and leave both infusions for 4 days.
After 4 days, bring a syrup to the boil from 4 kg of finely crushed sugar and 2 l of water, skim it carefully, add half a teaspoon of tartaric acid, and take the pan off the heat.

Pour 3.5 l of plain spirit into the still-hot syrup a little at a time, stirring constantly, then add the herb and saffron infusions strained through flannel. Once completely cool, bottle the crystal-clear liqueur, cork, seal with wax, and leave in a cool place for 6 months.

name: Kurczaki pieczone z beszamelem (Roast chickens glazed with béchamel)
summary: Roast chickens coated in a thin, browned crust of sweet-cream béchamel enriched with egg.
steps: Roast the chickens in the oven until golden brown and tender.
Cook the flour in the butter without letting it brown.
Whisk the sweet cream into the roux.
Bring the sauce to a boil.
Set the sauce aside to cool slightly.
Whisk the cooled sauce with the egg and salt.
Coat the chickens with a very thin layer of the sauce, repeating the basting two or three times.
Bake the chickens in the oven until the sauce forms a golden crust.
Carve the chickens carefully into pieces, keeping the sauce crust intact.
Serve immediately while hot.

name: Raspberry cordial on raspberry juice
summary: A classic cordial of fresh raspberries macerated for ten days in the sun in plain spirit, then combined 3 to 2 with a not-too-thick cooked raspberry juice.

ingredients.name: 95% rectified spirit
ingredients.note: orig. 1.5 bottles of drawn-off spirit infusion, plus a few teaspoons at the end

ingredients.name: raspberry juice cooked with sugar
ingredients.note: not too thick, orig. 1 bottle of juice per 1.5 bottles of spirit

steps: Put fresh ripe raspberries into a glass demijohn, cover them with plain spirit, and stand it in a sunny window for 10 days, until the fruit has turned completely pale.
Pour the spirit infusion off the fruit and combine it with cooked raspberry juice at 750 ml of juice per 1125 ml of drawn-off spirit.
Leave the demijohn for a few days in a window that gets the morning sun, shaking it now and then so the liquids combine well.
Strain the cordial (adding, if you like, two teaspoons of plain spirit), bottle it in clear bottles, cork it, and store it in the cellar.

name: Raspberry cordial, another way
summary: A mild cordial of fresh ripe raspberries covered with a cooled sugar syrup and spirit, macerated for twelve days in a warm place.
steps: Bring a light syrup to the boil from 3 kg of sugar and 8 litres of water, then cool it completely.
Put 2400 g (4 litres) of ripe fresh raspberries into a very large demijohn, cover them with the cold syrup and 2 litres of spirit, and seal it.
Leave the demijohn in a warm place out of the sun for 12 days, shaking it twice a day.
After 12 days, when the sediment has settled and the cordial is clear, pour it carefully into dry bottles, cork them, and store them in a cool, dry place.

name: Podolian cordial of sweet and sour cherries
summary: A traditional Podolian cordial of two parts black sweet cherries and one part ripe sour cherries, macerated for three months in spirit and sweetened with a hot sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: ripe sour cherries
ingredients.note: orig. 1 part (a third of all the fruit)

ingredients.name: 95% rectified spirit
ingredients.note: to cover the fruit; orig. the syrup proportion is given per 1 litre of drawn-off spirit

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. from a quarter kilogram (250 g) to one and a half quarters of a kilogram (375 g) per 1 l of spirit

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter litre for the syrup

steps: Put two parts of black sweet cherries (1000 g) and one part of ripe sour cherries (500 g) into a demijohn, cover them with spirit, and leave it in a shaded place for 3 months.
After 3 months, pour the spirit off the fruit and strain it through white flannel or thick muslin.
For every 1 litre of drawn-off spirit, cook a syrup from 300 g of sugar and 250 ml of water, then pour the still-hot syrup into the cold fruit spirit and mix well.
Bottle the cordial, cork it, and leave it in a cool place for another 6 months to mature fully.

name: Homemade maraschino made with raspberry and sour-cherry juice
summary: A homemade non-alcoholic maraschino-style syrup made with raspberry juice, sour-cherry juice, orange-flower water and sugar, left to clarify in a demijohn for six months.

ingredients.name: cooked raspberry juice
ingredients.note: orig. two and a half litres

ingredients.name: orange-flower water
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a litre

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three and a quarter kilograms of fine sugar

steps: Pour 2.5 litres of raspberry juice, 1 litre of sour-cherry juice and 750 ml of orange-flower water into a large glass demijohn.
Mix the juices and dissolve 3250 g of fine sugar in them cold.
Stopper the demijohn tightly and leave it undisturbed for 6 months, until the liquid is completely clear.
Draw off the clear liquid into bottles, filtering the sediment from the bottom through filter paper. Cork the bottles, seal with sealing wax, and store in a cool, dry place.

name: Cream ice
summary: Classic vanilla cream ice of one and a half litres of thick cream infused with a vanilla pod and thickened on the heat with twelve yolks beaten with half a kilogram of fine sugar.

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: fresh and thick, orig. one and a half litres

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of very fine sugar

steps: Bring 1.5 litres of fresh thick cream to the boil with a split vanilla pod.
Beat 12 yolks with 500 g of very fine sugar in a pan with a whisk until the mass thickens noticeably and turns pale.

Set the pan of yolks over very low heat and pour in the boiling cream gradually, beating with a whisk all the time, until the cream thickens and rises a little. Do not let it boil or the yolks curdle.
Move the pan to a cool place and stir the cream until completely cold. Then pour it into an ice-cream maker and freeze it, stirring every 15 minutes until fully set (about 2–3 hours).

name: Wild-strawberry or raspberry ice
summary: A classic sorbet of a kilogram of fresh ripe wild strawberries or raspberries rubbed through a sieve and combined with a cooled lemon sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: alkermes or pomegranate juice
ingredients.note: optional, to deepen the colour and the aroma

steps: Rub fresh ripe wild strawberries or raspberries through a fine sieve.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 500 g of sugar and 1 litre of water, skimming carefully. Squeeze in the juice of two lemons while it cooks, and leave it to cool completely.
Pour the sieved fruit pulp into the cold syrup (and, if you like, a teaspoon of alkermes), mix well, and freeze it in an ice-cream maker (about 2–3 hours).

name: Lemon or orange ice
summary: A classic citrus sorbet on a thick syrup of sugar rubbed on the peel of six lemons, water, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: in pieces, rubbed on the lemon peel, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: peel for rubbing the sugar, and the squeezed juice

steps: Rub pieces of sugar on the yellow peel of six washed lemons, cover them with 1 litre of water, bring a thick syrup to the boil, and leave it to cool completely.
Squeeze the juice of all six lemons into the cold syrup (and, if you like, a teaspoon of rum), mix well, and strain through a fine sieve.
Pour the mixture into an ice-cream maker and freeze it until smooth (about 2–3 hours).

name: Rose ice
summary: A delicate rose-scented sorbet of a thick sugar syrup, half a litre of rose syrup, and the freshly squeezed juice of two lemons.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half quarters of a kilogram

steps: Bring a thick syrup to the boil from 1 litre of water and 375 g of sugar, then cool it completely.
Squeeze the juice of two lemons into the cooled syrup, pour in 500 ml of rose syrup, and mix well.
Pour the mixture into an ice-cream maker and freeze it to a smooth sorbet (about 2–3 hours).

name: Pineapple ice
summary: A refreshing sorbet of fresh pineapple, half grated and half cut into very thin slices softened in a hot syrup, with the juice of three lemons.

ingredients.name: fresh pineapple
ingredients.note: peeled: half grated, half cut into very thin slices

steps: Peel a fresh pineapple, grate half of it, and cut the other half into very thin small slices.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 500 g of sugar and 1 litre of water, skim it carefully, pour part of the hot syrup over the pineapple slices, bring it briefly to the boil, and leave them to soften.
Squeeze the juice of three lemons into the remaining syrup, add the grated pineapple together with the syrup from the slices, mix, and strain through a sieve.
Add the drained pineapple slices to the strained liquid, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it to a smooth sorbet (about 2–3 hours).

name: Punch ice
summary: A fine punch sorbet on a syrup of sugar rubbed on oranges, an infusion of black tea, the juice of four oranges and three lemons, finished while freezing with a small glass of maraschino.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: in pieces, rubbed on the orange peel, orig. a quarter kilogram

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.note: juicy ones: peel for rubbing the sugar, and the squeezed juice

steps: Rub the sugar on the peel of four oranges, cover it with 500 ml of water, bring the syrup to the boil, and leave it to cool.
Pour 185 ml of strong black-tea infusion into the cooled syrup, together with the juice of four oranges and three lemons strained through a sieve, and mix well.
Pour the mixture into an ice-cream maker and start freezing. When the mass is half set, pour in a small glass (30 ml) of maraschino and finish freezing (about 2–3 hours in all).

name: Melon ice
summary: A fragrant sorbet of sieved ripe pineapple-melon flesh combined with a sugar syrup and the juice of two lemons.

ingredients.name: ripe melon flesh
ingredients.note: scooped out and rubbed through a sieve, orig. half a kilogram

steps: Cut a ripe, fragrant melon in half, remove the seeds, and rub the flesh through a sieve, measuring out 500 g of purée.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 500 g of sugar, 1 litre of water and the juice of two lemons, then cool it completely.
Combine the cold syrup with the melon purée, rub the whole thing through a sieve once more, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Apricot or peach ice
summary: A fruit sorbet of sieved flesh of very ripe fresh apricots or peaches, combined with a sugar syrup and the juice of two lemons.

ingredients.name: ripe apricot or peach flesh
ingredients.note: peeled and rubbed through a sieve, orig. half a kilogram

steps: Peel very ripe fresh apricots or peaches, remove the stones, and rub the flesh through a sieve, measuring out 500 g of purée.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 500 g of sugar, 1 litre of water and the juice of two lemons, and leave it to cool.
Mix the cooled syrup with the fruit purée, rub it through a sieve once more, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Chocolate ice cream
summary: Creamy chocolate ice cream on hot whipping cream with melted vanilla chocolate, thickened on the heat with ten yolks beaten with sugar.

ingredients.name: dessert or dark chocolate
ingredients.note: grated, orig. one and a half quarters of a kilogram of vanilla chocolate

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of fine sugar

steps: Grate the chocolate and pour 2 litres of hot whipping cream over it, stirring constantly until the chocolate has dissolved completely.
Beat ten yolks with fine sugar in a pan to a pale, fluffy mass.
Set the pan of yolks over very low heat and pour in the hot chocolate cream gradually, beating with a whisk all the time, until the mixture thickens. Do not let it boil.
Strain the cream through a sieve, cool it thoroughly, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Grape ice
summary: A fruit sorbet of freshly pressed and sieved juice from two kilograms of ripe sweet grapes, combined with a sugar syrup and the juice of half a lemon.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: the juice of half a lemon

steps: Pull the grapes off the stems, crush them, press the juice, and rub it through a fine sieve.
Bring a syrup to the boil from 500 g of fine sugar, 1 litre of water and the juice of half a lemon, then leave it to cool.
Mix the cooled syrup with the fresh grape juice, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Cranberry ice
summary: A sharp sorbet of freshly pressed cranberry juice combined with a sugar syrup cooked with blanched, crushed sweet almonds.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. three quarters of a kilogram

ingredients.name: sweet almonds
ingredients.note: blanched, peeled and crushed, orig. a dozen or so

steps: Bring a syrup to the boil from 750 g of sugar and 1 litre of water, adding a dozen or so blanched and crushed sweet almonds to the boiling syrup.
Take the boiled syrup off the heat to cool, then pour in 500 ml of pressed cranberry juice.
Strain the whole thing through thick cloth or a sieve, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Coffee ice cream
summary: A fine ice cream of fresh thick cream infused hot with whole beans of freshly roasted mocha, thickened on the heat with ten yolks and sugar.

ingredients.name: roasted coffee beans
ingredients.note: freshly roasted whole mocha beans, orig. half a quarter kilogram

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of fine sugar

steps: Bring 2 litres of thick cream to the boil, add the whole beans of freshly roasted coffee, cover, and leave it to cool completely so the cream takes on the coffee aroma. Then strain it through a sieve.
Beat ten yolks with fine sugar in a pan, set it over very low heat, and pour in the strained coffee cream gradually.
Beat constantly with a whisk over low heat until the cream has thickened well. Do not let it boil.
Strain the thickened cream through a sieve, cool it, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Caramel ice cream
summary: Smooth caramel ice cream made with caramelized sugar dissolved in boiling thick cream, thickened with four egg yolks and frozen in an ice-cream maker.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilogram (250 g) for caramelizing, plus 2 tablespoons (30 g) for beating with the yolks

ingredients.name: whipping cream
ingredients.note: thick: 1 l of boiling cream for the caramel, plus 250 ml (a quarter litre) of cold cream for the yolks

steps: Put 250 g of sugar into a heavy pan and heat it until it caramelizes to a light brown. Then pour in 1 litre of boiling thick cream gradually, stirring constantly until the caramel has dissolved, and cool it.
Beat four egg yolks with two tablespoons (30 g) of sugar and 250 ml of cold cream until thick, then combine with the cooled caramel cream.
Heat the mixture over very low heat, stirring all the time, until it thickens. Do not let it boil.
Cool the caramel cream completely, pour it into an ice-cream maker, and freeze it (about 2–3 hours).

name: Frozen cream parfait
summary: A rich parfait, not churned, of ten yolks scalded with a glass of milk and sugar, folded with whipped thick cream, vanilla and finely chopped candied fruit.

ingredients.name: icing sugar or caster sugar
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilogram twice (250 g for the yolks and 250 g for the whipped cream)

ingredients.name: whipping cream or double cream
ingredients.note: thick, orig. three quarters of a litre

ingredients.name: candied fruit
ingredients.note: finely chopped dry preserves for the mixture and for lining the mould, orig. a quarter kilogram

steps: Beat ten yolks until white with 250 g of fine sugar and 250 ml of milk. Warm them over very low heat, stirring constantly and not letting them boil, then cool them thoroughly in a cold bath.
Whip 750 ml of thick cream until stiff. Fold in the remaining 250 g of fine sugar, the crushed vanilla pod, and most of the finely chopped candied fruit.
Fold the whipped cream gently into the cooled yolk mixture.

Line a metal mould with paper, sprinkle the remaining candied fruit over the bottom, pour in the cream, cover it tightly, and put it in the freezer (or pack it in ice and salt) for about 3–4 hours, until frozen through.

name: Allasch Caraway Liqueur
summary: Sweet caraway liqueur made with rectified spirit and aged for three months.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. one and a quarter kilograms

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold; orig. one and a half liters

ingredients.name: rectified spirit
ingredients.note: for dissolving the essential oil; orig. a quarter of a liter

ingredients.name: caraway essential oil, drops
ingredients.note: 40 individual drops; orig. forty drops; the glossary does not specify drop volume, so the count was kept

ingredients.name: rectified spirit
ingredients.note: added after dissolving the essential oil; orig. two liters

steps: Dissolve 1250 g of sugar in 1500 ml of cold water.
Bring the solution to a boil and skim off the foam.
Mix 40 drops of caraway essential oil with 250 ml of rectified spirit.
Add the remaining 2000 ml of rectified spirit to the mixture.
Remove the syrup from the heat.
Pour the spirit mixture into the hot syrup, stirring constantly.
Transfer the liqueur to another vessel and leave to cool.
Pour it into bottles.
Seal the bottles tightly.
Leave the liqueur in a dry, cool place for three months.

name: Wódka „Orange” (Orange and French prune vodka)
summary: A delicate fruit vodka macerating green oranges and French dried prunes in separate demijohns before combining.

ingredients.name: dried French prunes
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilo; cut into small pieces or halves

steps: Mix the rectified spirit with the boiled water.
Divide the mixture between two 2 l demijohns.
Place the green oranges into one demijohn.
Cut the dried prunes into small pieces or halves.
Place the prunes into the second demijohn.
Set both demijohns aside in the shade for 4320 minutes.
Filter the contents of both demijohns through filter paper.
Combine both filtered liquids.
Cork the container tightly and set aside in a cool cellar for three months.

name: Wódka orzechowa (Green walnut liqueur)
summary: A sweet liqueur made from green walnuts, cloves, and cinnamon.
steps: Cut the green walnuts into quarters.
Place the walnuts into a glass container with the rectified spirit.
Add the cloves and the cinnamon stick.
Set aside in the shade for 4320 minutes, which is 3 days.
Strain the macerate through a fine cloth.
Bring the sugar and cold water to a boil to make a syrup.
Remove the syrup from the heat after the first boil.
Pour the strained macerate into the hot syrup.
Mix the liquids.
Filter the liqueur through filter paper.
Bottle and seal tightly with corks.
Set aside in a dry and cool place for about 129600 minutes, which is 3 months.

name: Sour Cherry Syrup
summary: Sweet syrup from sour cherries boiled in water, strained, and boiled again with sugar.

ingredients.name: sour cherries
ingredients.note: Ripe, rinsed, and pitted; orig. four liters.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: Amount per 1 l of obtained juice, not for the whole batch; orig. one kilogram.

steps: Drop the sour cherries into 1 l of boiling water.
Bring the sour cherries to a strong boil several times.
Pour the contents of the pot into a loosely woven linen bag.
Tie the bag tightly and, as the juice drains, retie it progressively lower.
Strain the juice through muslin or a fine strainer.
Set the juice aside for about 120 minutes for the sediment to settle.
Measure the clear juice.
Pour the juice over crushed sugar, keeping a ratio of 1 kg of sugar per 1 l of juice.
Leave the mixture until the sugar dissolves.
Bring the syrup to a boil, skimming the foam carefully and simmering over low heat toward the end.
Leave the syrup to cool.
Pour the syrup into bottles.
Seal the bottles and store in a dry, cool place.

name: Gooseberry Compote Preserve
summary: Compote preserve of ripe gooseberries briefly steeped in hot sugar syrup, cooled, and pasteurized in jars for fifteen minutes.

ingredients.name: gooseberries
ingredients.note: ripe but not overripe: green, yellow, or red

steps: Clean the ripe gooseberries, carefully trimming off the stems and blossom ends with a small knife without piercing the skin of the fruit.
Boil a medium-thick syrup from 500 g of sugar and 250 ml of water, and skim it thoroughly.
Drop the gooseberries into the hot syrup and the moment the syrup begins to boil again, remove the pan immediately from the heat and leave to cool completely.

Transfer the cold gooseberries with the syrup into jars, leaving approx. 5 cm of headspace at the top, seal tightly, and pasteurize in a pot of water lined with hay or a cloth for 15 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Gooseberry Compote Preserve Another Way
summary: Raw gooseberries packed into jars, covered with completely cooled sugar syrup, and pasteurized in a water bath.

ingredients.name: gooseberries
ingredients.note: large, ripe: red, yellow, or green

steps: Carefully trim the stems from the ripe gooseberries with a small knife, wipe the berries with a clean cloth, and pack directly into jars.
Boil a medium-thick syrup from 500 g of sugar and 250 ml (1 glass) of water, skim thoroughly, and let cool completely.
Pour the cold syrup over the gooseberries in the jars to 3/4 of the height of the vessel.
Seal the jars tightly, place in a kettle or pot of cold water, and pasteurize for approx. 25–30 minutes after the water comes to a boil, then leave in the water until cooled.

name: Peaches in syrup
summary: A nineteenth-century bottled compote of whole or halved ripe peaches, blanched in hot water, covered with a very thick sugar syrup and pasteurized for half an hour in a water bath.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the thick syrup (plus warm water for blanching the peaches)

steps: Choose ripe, sound peaches with no spots, prick each one with a wooden pin or a toothpick, and put them in a pan of warm water.
Heat the fruit over low heat until the water is steaming hard (do not let it boil) and the skin of a peach lifted out to test slips off easily.

Pour off the water, dry the peaches briefly on a sieve, and peel them at once before they firm up again (you may also leave the skins on). Leave the fruit whole or cut it in half and remove the stones.
Pack the peaches into jars and cover them with a very thick syrup made ahead from 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water. Seal the jars tightly (originally they were tied with a bladder).
Stand the jars in a kettle or a tall pot of water and pasteurize for a good 30 minutes from the moment the water boils (or bake them in the oven). Once cool, store them in a cool place.

name: Double-steeped canned peeled peaches
summary: Peeled peaches softened in hot water, soaked for a day in cold water and another day in a light syrup, then covered with a fresh thick syrup and pasteurized for 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 450 g for the first light syrup and 750 g for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for each of the two syrups (plus cold water for heating and for the 24-hour soak)

steps: Peel ripe peaches carefully with a small knife, put them in an earthenware or enamel pan of cold water, and heat over low heat until the water steams (do not let it boil) and the fruit softens.
Transfer the hot peaches to a pan of fresh cold water and leave them there for 24 hours.
The next day, pour off the water, cover the fruit with a light syrup cooked from 450 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave it for another 24 hours.

After a full day, pour off the first syrup (it can be used for compotes or cordials). Pack the peaches whole or halved into jars and cover them with a fresh thick syrup of 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water.
Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle lined with hay or a cloth, and pasteurize for 25 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Bilberry Compote Preserve Another Way
summary: Bilberries scalded with boiling water, simmered for fifteen minutes in a thick sugar syrup, and pasteurized in jars.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 3 glasses of hot water for the syrup, plus boiling water for scalding the berries

steps: Carefully pick over 2 l of bilberries, cover with boiling water in a bowl, and drain immediately on a sieve.
Boil a syrup from 1.5 kg of sugar and 750 ml (3 glasses) of hot water, and skim it thoroughly.
Add the scalded bilberries to the boiling syrup, cook for a few minutes over high heat, and then simmer for 15 minutes over low heat.
Transfer the cooled preserve into jars, seal tightly, and pasteurize in a pot of water lined with hay or in the oven.

name: Czerechy (sour–sweet cherry hybrids) preserved in syrup
summary: Jarred compote of large ripe Kleparów czerechy (a cross of sour and sweet cherries), covered with sugar syrup and pasteurized in a water bath.

ingredients.name: czerechy (sour–sweet cherry hybrids)
ingredients.note: large ripe Kleparów czerechy (or ordinary sweet cherries)

steps: Remove the stems from large ripe czerechy, wipe each fruit with a clean cloth, and fill the jars to the top.
Make a standard sugar syrup with 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and pour it over the fruit in the jars.
Seal the jars tightly (originally with a clean cloth and a bladder, or with albumin paper tied with string), stand them in a kettle or a pot of water, and pasteurize for about 20–25 minutes.
Leave the jars in the kettle until the water has cooled completely, and store them in a cool place.

name: Canned bergamot pears
summary: A pale preserve of bergamot pears peeled whole, briefly cooked in a light syrup with lemon juice, packed in jars under the thickened syrup and pasteurized for half an hour.

ingredients.name: bergamot pears
ingredients.note: or sugar pears or panny, peeled whole with the stems left on, or halved with the cores removed

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 1 lemon in the cold water while peeling, and juice of 1 lemon in the syrup

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 500 g for the first light syrup, plus 250 g added when the syrup is boiled again

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup (plus cold water to hold the peeled pears)

steps: Peel the bergamot pears, leaving the trimmed stems (or halve the fruit and remove the cores), and drop each one at once into cold water with the juice of 1 lemon.
Cook a light syrup from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, skim it, squeeze in the juice of the second lemon, and put the pears into the boiling syrup.
Cook the pears briefly, then lift them with a slotted spoon onto a sieve to drain and pack them into jars.
Add the remaining 250 g of sugar to the syrup, bring it to the boil, skim it carefully, cool it, and pour it over the pears in the jars.
Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle of water, and pasteurize for 30 minutes from the moment the water boils. Take them out only after the water bath has cooled completely.

name: Canned apples
summary: Jarred compote of halved peeled early transparent, Stettin or reinette apples, briefly cooked in a light syrup with lemon juice, covered with the thickened syrup and pasteurized for 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: early transparent apples that are not overripe, or ripe Stettin apples or reinettes, peeled, cored and halved

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice for the cold water while peeling, and for the syrup at the end of the brief cooking

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 500 g for the light syrup, plus 250 g added before the jars are filled

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrup (plus cold well water to hold the peeled apples)

steps: Peel the apples, remove the cores, cut the fruit in half, and drop the halves at once into cold water acidulated with the juice of half a lemon.

Cook a light syrup from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, skim it, add the drained apple halves, and cook carefully for a few minutes until just soft, squeezing in the rest of the lemon juice at the end.
Lift the apples gently with a slotted spoon onto a sieve to drain, and once they have cooled a little pack them into jars.
Add 250 g of sugar to the remaining syrup, bring it to the boil several times, skim it, and once cool pour it over the apples in the jars.
Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle lined with hay or a cloth, and pasteurize for 25 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned whole crabapples in heavy syrup
summary: Whole crabapples with the stems trimmed, softened in hot water without boiling, soaked for a day in a light syrup, then covered with a fresh thick syrup and pasteurized for 20–25 minutes.

ingredients.name: crabapples
ingredients.note: sound, with the stems trimmed to 1/4 of their length

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 450 g for the first light syrup and 750 g for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for each of the two syrups (plus hot water for softening the crabapples)

steps: Trim the crabapples, cut the stems so that 1/4 of their length remains, remove the flower ends, and prick the fruit densely with a wooden pin.
Put the crabapples into a pan of hot water and heat over low heat until they soften, without letting the water boil, so the fruit does not burst.
Pour off the water, cover the soft crabapples with a light syrup made ahead from 450 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave them for 24 hours.
After a full day, pour off the first syrup, pack the crabapples into jars, shaking so they settle evenly, and cover them with a fresh thick syrup of 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water.
Seal the jars and pasteurize them in a kettle of water for 20–25 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned blackberries
summary: A simple preserve of fresh ripe blackberries covered in the jars with sugar syrup and pasteurized in a water bath for at most 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for a syrup of ordinary thickness

steps: Pick over the ripe blackberries carefully, removing leaves and bits of debris, and fill the jars to the top without shaking them, so the fruit is not crushed.
Cook and cool a syrup from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, then pour it over the blackberries in the jars.
Seal the jars and pasteurize them in a kettle lined with hay (or in the oven) for at most 15 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned raspberries
summary: A fragrant preserve of raspberries picked on a fine day, covered with a thick cooled sugar syrup and pasteurized for a quarter of an hour in a water bath.

ingredients.name: raspberries
ingredients.note: freshly picked on a dry, fine day, large and picked over

steps: Pick over large raspberries gathered on a dry day and fill the jars without shaking them, so the fruit is not crushed.
Cook a thick syrup from 600 g of sugar and 400 ml of water, cool it, and pour it over the raspberries in the jars.
Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle of water lined with hay or a cloth, and cook over low heat for exactly 15 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: French-style canned raspberries
summary: Raspberries cooked for exactly 1 minute in boiling thick sugar syrup, cooled in the syrup, packed into jars and pasteurized for 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: raspberries
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of fine, not overripe red raspberries

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar chopped into small pieces

steps: Bring 500 g of finely crushed sugar to the boil with 500 ml (2 szklanki) of water and skim it thoroughly, until you have a thick syrup almost as for a jam.
Drop 500 g of picked-over raspberries into the boiling syrup and keep them on the heat for exactly 1 minute, watch in hand.
Take the pan off the heat and leave the raspberries in the syrup until completely cool.

Transfer the cooled raspberries and syrup carefully with a silver spoon into jars, leaving 5 cm of headspace. Seal them and pasteurize in a kettle of water for at most 15 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned melon in rum syrup
summary: Pieces of ripe pineapple melon softened in hot water, soaked for a day in a light syrup, then packed under a fresh thick syrup with rum and pasteurized for 20 minutes.

ingredients.name: melon
ingredients.note: ripe pineapple melon, peeled, seeded and cut into cubes or sticks

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 450 g for the first light syrup and 750 g for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for each of the two syrups (plus cold water for heating and rinsing the melon)

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. 2 tablespoons of very good rum in each jar

steps: Peel a ripe pineapple melon, remove the seeds, and cut the flesh into moderately sized oblong or square pieces.
Put the melon in a pan, cover it with cold water, and heat it until the pieces soften, without letting the water boil.
Pour off the hot water, rinse the melon several times with cold water in a colander so it cools quickly, and drain it well.
Cover the cooled melon with a light syrup cooked from 450 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave it for 24 hours.

The next day, pour off the first syrup, pack the melon into jars, cover it with a fresh thick syrup of 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, add 2 tablespoons of good rum to each jar, seal, and pasteurize in a kettle of water for 20 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned apricots in heavy syrup
summary: Whole ripe apricots softened in water over low heat, soaked for 10 hours in cold water and for 24 hours in a light syrup, then covered with a fresh thick syrup and pasteurized for 20–25 minutes.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 450 g for the first light syrup and 750 g for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for each of the two syrups (plus cold water for heating and for the 10-hour soak)

steps: Lay ripe, firm apricots in an earthenware or enamel pan, cover them with cold water, and heat over low heat until the fruit is soft enough.
Lift the apricots out with a slotted spoon into a porcelain bowl of fresh cold water and leave them for 10 hours.
Drain the fruit, cover it with a light cooled syrup of 450 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave it for 24 hours.
The next day, pour off the first syrup, pack the apricots into jars, and cover them with a fresh thick syrup cooked from 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water.
Seal the jars and pasteurize them in a kettle of water for 20–25 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned young walnuts
summary: Young fresh walnut kernels peeled carefully of their thin skin, covered in the jars with a cooled sugar syrup and pasteurized in a water bath.

ingredients.name: young walnuts
ingredients.note: fresh, the thin skin peeled carefully with a penknife

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for a syrup of ordinary thickness

steps: Peel young fresh walnuts carefully with a penknife so they are completely white, and pack them into jars.
Cook a syrup of ordinary thickness from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, skim it carefully, cool it, and pour it over the walnuts.
Seal the jars and pasteurize them in a kettle of water lined with hay (or in the oven) for about 25–30 minutes. Take the jars out of the kettle only after the water has cooled completely.

name: Canned currants
summary: Red or white currants (optionally mixed with raspberries), covered in the jars with a very thick sugar syrup and pasteurized for at most 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: currants
ingredients.note: large ripe red or white currants, the stalks removed carefully (optionally mixed with raspberries)

steps: Strip large ripe currants gently from the stalks, taking care the fruit stays whole and does not release its juice.
Fill the jars with the currants without shaking them (optionally layered with raspberries), leaving about 7.5 cm (3 cal) of headspace.

Cover the fruit with a very thick syrup cooked from 750 g of sugar and 400 ml of water, seal the jars, and pasteurize them in a kettle of water (or in the oven) for at most 15 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned węgierka plums
summary: A compote of firm węgierka plums in two versions: skins left on, covered overnight with syrup and pasteurized for an hour, or peeled after blanching, steeped for a quarter of an hour in the syrup and pasteurized for 45 minutes.

ingredients.name: węgierka plums
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of ripe but firm węgierka plums

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram (500 g) of sugar for the first syrup, plus about 150 g of sugar to reboil the syrup before the jars are filled

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. 2 szklanki of water for the syrup (plus hot water for blanching in the peeled version)

steps: For the version with the skins on, wipe 500 g of firm węgierka plums with a cloth, put them in an earthenware pan, cover them with a boiling thick syrup cooked from 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave them until the next day.

On the second day, pack the plums tightly into jars. Boil the poured-off syrup with an extra 150 g of sugar to the right thickness, cool it completely, pour it over the fruit, seal the jars, and pasteurize over low heat for 60 minutes from the moment the water in the kettle boils (or in the oven).

For the peeled version, blanch the plums a few at a time in hot water and peel them carefully with a small knife. Drop them into a boiling, skimmed syrup of 500 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, move the pan to the side of the stove for 15 minutes, and then cool completely.

Pack the peeled plums tightly into jars, reboil the syrup with an extra 150 g of sugar, cool it, pour it over the fruit, seal, and pasteurize in a kettle of water (or in the oven) for 45 minutes (three quarters of an hour) from the moment the water boils.

name: Plums preserved in syrup
summary: A preserve of ripe white, yellow, red or green plums, heated in water until the first bubbles appear, firmed for 3 hours in cold water, soaked for a day in light syrup, and pasteurized in fresh thick syrup.

ingredients.name: plums
ingredients.note: white, yellow, red or green, ripe, large and unblemished

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 450 g for the first light syrup and 750 g for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 500 ml for each of the two syrups (plus cold water for heating and for the 3-hour soak)

steps: Prick ripe, sound plums with a wooden pin, put them in a pan of cold water, and heat them until the first bubbles show on the surface, without letting the water boil hard.
Pour off the hot water and put the plums into cold water for 3 hours, so they firm up well.
After 3 hours, drain the plums, cover them with a light lukewarm syrup of 450 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, and leave them in it for 24 hours.

The next day, pour off the first syrup (it can be used for fruit soups or cordials), pack the plums into jars, cover them with a fresh thick syrup of 750 g of sugar and 500 ml of water, seal, and pasteurize in a kettle of water (or in the oven) for about 25–30 minutes. Take the jars out only after the water has cooled.

name: Canned greengages
summary: Firm, slightly underripe greengages blanched and soaked in water with alum, then soaked for a day in a light syrup, packed into jars with a fresh thick syrup and a teaspoon of rum, and pasteurized.

ingredients.name: greengages
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kopa (60 pieces, about 2 kg) of firm, underripe, unblemished greengages

ingredients.name: alum
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter deka (2.5 g) for the brief cooking, and half a teaspoon (about 2.5 g) for the soak, per 1 kopa of greengages

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: about 500 g for the first light syrup and 1 kg for the fresh thick syrup in the jars

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for both syrups (plus boiled water for heating, and cold soft water for soaking and rinsing the plums)

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. 1 teaspoon of good rum on top of each jar (optional)

steps: Choose sound, slightly underripe greengages, prick them densely with a wooden pin, pack them tightly in a pan, cover them with boiled water with 2.5 g of alum per 60 fruit, and heat until air bubbles appear and the plums soften, without letting the water boil.

Transfer the greengages to a porcelain bowl of cold soft water mixed with half a teaspoon of alum and soak them for 3 hours. Then pour off the water and rinse the fruit very thoroughly in several changes of cold water.
Cover the rinsed greengages with a light syrup of 500 g of sugar and 750 ml of water and leave them for 24 hours.

The next day, pour off the first syrup, pack the greengages into jars, cover them with a fresh, thick, cold syrup of 1 kg of sugar and 750 ml of water, pour 1 teaspoon of good rum on top of each jar, seal, and pasteurize in a kettle of water for 20–30 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned strawberries
summary: A preserve of freshly picked strawberries steeped for a quarter of an hour in a thick sugar syrup, packed into jars with a teaspoon of rum and pasteurized for 10–12 minutes.

ingredients.name: strawberries
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of ripe but not overripe strawberries picked on a dry, sunny day

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar chopped into small pieces

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki of water

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. 1 teaspoon of very good rum in each jar

steps: Hull 500 g of freshly picked ripe strawberries.
Cook a syrup from 500 g of finely crushed sugar and 375 ml of water, and skim it carefully.
Drop the strawberries into the boiling syrup, take the pan off the heat at once, and leave the fruit in the syrup at the side of the stove for 15 minutes. Then cool it.
Pack the cooled strawberries and syrup into jars, pour 1 teaspoon of very good rum into each, seal, and pasteurize in a kettle of water for 10–12 minutes from the moment the water boils.

name: Canned sour cherries
summary: Łutówka or Hiszpanka sour cherries, with the stones left in or removed, cooked for 5 minutes in thick sugar syrup, packed into jars once cooled, and pasteurized for 20 minutes in a water bath.

ingredients.name: sour cherries
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of Łutówka or Hiszpanka sour cherries, with the stones left in or removed

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogram of sugar chopped into small pieces

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki of water for the syrup

steps: Cook a thick syrup from 500 g of finely crushed sugar and 375 ml of water, and skim it carefully.
Drop 500 g of prepared cherries (with the stones or stoned) into the boiling syrup and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat. Once the cherries have cooled a little, pack them with the syrup into jars (you can also cover raw cherries in the jars with the thick syrup).
Seal the jars, stand them in a kettle lined with hay and filled with cold water, and pasteurize for 20 minutes from the moment the water boils (or bake them in the oven).

name: Canned grapes
summary: Jarred compote of large, fine bunches of half-ripe grapes, covered with a thick sugar syrup and pasteurized for 10–20 minutes in a water bath.
steps: Pack large, fine, half-ripe bunches of grapes into jars.
Cook a thick syrup from 600 g of sugar and 400 ml of water, cool it, and pour it over the grapes in the jars.
Seal the jars and pasteurize them in a kettle of water for about 20 minutes from the moment the water boils (or for 10 minutes if the grapes are riper). Once cool, store them in a dry, cool place.

name: Candied Dried Lemons
summary: Lemon strips gradually candied in syrup and air-dried.

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: ripe, unblemished; orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the initial syrup; orig. three-quarters of a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: additional for subsequent boilings of the syrup; amount not specified

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, boiling, rinsing, and the syrup; amounts not specified

steps: Soak the lemons in water for 7200 minutes, changing the water every 1440 minutes.
Cover the fruit with fresh water in a pot.
Boil until tender enough to be easily pierced.
Leave the lemons in the water to cool.
Cut the fruit into lengthwise strips.
Rinse the strips thoroughly in clean water.
Boil a light syrup from 750 g of sugar and water.
Leave the syrup to cool completely.
Arrange the lemons in a jar and cover with the cooled syrup.
Over several days, repeat boiling the drained syrup, adding a little extra sugar each time.
After each boiling, cool the syrup before pouring it over the lemons again.
Repeat the steeping until the lemons lose their rawness.
After the final boiling, leave the lemons in the syrup for a longer period.
Remove the strips from the syrup and spread them out on platters.
Leave to air-dry at room temperature.

name: Pears Dried in Sugar Another Way
summary: Pears candied over four days in progressively thickened syrup, then glazed in thread-stage sugar syrup or dried in fine sugar.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: half-ripe, of a choice variety, peeled with stems left on

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 kg on the first day, 250 g 3 times over the following days, and approx. 500 g of fresh sugar for drying

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 3 glasses for the syrup, plus cold water for soaking and parboiling the pears

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice for the cold water when peeling and parboiling

steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stems intact (halve large ones), remove the cores, and submerge in cold water with lemon juice.
Transfer the pears to a stoneware pan with fresh cold water and a little lemon juice, cook covered until tender (without overcooking), and drain on a sieve.
Boil a light syrup from 1 kg of sugar and 750 ml (3 glasses) of water, skim, cool, and pour over the pears.
For the next three days, drain the syrup daily, add 250 g of sugar each day, bring to a boil, and pour the progressively warmer syrup over the pears.
On the fourth day, place the pears into the thick syrup, bring to a single boil, skim, cool, and store in jars covered with the syrup.

As needed, remove a portion of pears onto a sieve to drain, then dip them in freshly boiled, very thick sugar syrup (cooked to the thread stage) and dry on a wire sieve, or coat in fine sugar and dry in a lukewarm oven.

name: Pears Dried in Rock Sugar
summary: Whole flattened pears cooked until tender and repeatedly dried in a low oven with crushed rock sugar until a crystalline coating forms.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: large, ripe, of a choice variety, peeled whole with stems intact

ingredients.name: rock sugar
ingredients.note: finely crushed rock sugar, for repeated coating

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, soft water for soaking and cooking the pears

steps: Peel the pears whole without trimming the stems, and place immediately into cold water acidulated with lemon juice.
Arrange the peeled pears in a large stoneware pan, cover with cold soft water, and cook until a straw passes easily through them.
Remove the fruit with a slotted spoon onto a sieve, and when slightly cooled, gently flatten each pear on its side with a silver spoon.
Arrange the flattened pears on sieves, coat each with finely crushed rock sugar, and place in a very low oven overnight.
Turn the fruit daily, add a fresh coating of crushed rock sugar, and dry again in a low oven until a crystalline coating forms; pack in boxes with paper between the layers.

name: Pears Dried in Honey, Stuffed
summary: Large pears poached in a honey syrup made from a decoction of the peels, stuffed with an almond-citrus mixture, and repeatedly dried with honey and sugar.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: large, of a choice variety, peeled and cored, with the peels reserved for the decoction

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the peels into 2 glasses (500 ml) of strained decoction

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.note: 1 glass per 2 glasses of strained decoction

ingredients.name: candied citron or orange peel
ingredients.note: finely crushed candied lemon peel or orange peel

steps: Peel the large pears and neatly hollow out the cores, then cover the peels and cores with water in a pot and boil into a concentrated decoction.
Strain 500 ml (2 glasses) of the peel decoction, combine with 250 ml (1 glass) of honey, bring to a boil, and cook the pears in this syrup until tender, taking care that they do not fall apart.
Remove the pears onto a sieve to drain and cool, then stuff them with a mixture of crushed almonds, finely chopped candied citron or orange peel, and cinnamon or vanilla.
Boil down the remaining honey syrup until thick.
Dip the stuffed pears in the thick honey syrup, dust with fine sugar, and dry repeatedly in a lukewarm oven or in the sun; once completely cooled, pack into jars.

name: Pears Dried in Honey, Stuffed Another Way
summary: Pears cooked until translucent in a peel decoction with honey and beer, stuffed with a spiced apple-and-pear puree, and glazed in syrup.

ingredients.name: pears
ingredients.note: approx. 1 kg of large pears for stuffing plus 500 g of peeled pears for the filling and the peels for the decoction

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.note: cooled for the beer decoction plus a little for sweetening the filling

ingredients.name: beer
ingredients.note: mixed half-and-half with the honey and peel decoction

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the peels into a decoction

steps: Cook the large pears in the peel decoction combined with the cooled honey and beer until they turn yellow and translucent, taking care that they do not overcook.
Remove the pears onto a sieve and flatten each one slightly.
Prepare the filling: cook the peeled apples and smaller pears, press through a sieve, add the boiled and chopped orange peel, cinnamon, cloves, and a little honey, cook down until thick, and cool.
Stuff the pears generously with the spiced fruit mixture.

Boil down the cooking liquid from the pears into a thick syrup, dip the stuffed fruit in it, and dry in a slow oven over several days, repeating the dipping in syrup daily to give them a glossy finish.

name: Apples Dried in Sugar
summary: Whole peeled and cored apples cooked until translucent in a thin syrup, stuffed with thick apple preserve, and dried with crushed sugar.

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: large, of a choice variety, ripe, peeled whole and cored

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 500 g for the syrup and approx. 150 g of coarsely crushed and sifted sugar for dusting

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: at least 3 glassfuls for the syrup, plus cold water for soaking

ingredients.name: thick apple preserve
ingredients.note: for generously filling the cored apples

steps: Carefully peel the large apples, hollow out the cores without damaging the fruit, and submerge immediately in cold water acidulated with lemon juice.
Make a thin syrup from 500 g of sugar and 750 ml (3 glassfuls) of water, arrange the drained apples in a single layer, and cook gently until completely translucent without letting them fall apart.
Transfer the cooked apples to platters or a sieve and let cool completely, then fill each cavity generously with a heaped mound of thick apple preserve.
Coat each stuffed apple with sifted, coarsely crushed sugar and finish drying on sieves in a very low oven, taking care not to overdry the fruit.

name: Crabapples Dried in Sugar
summary: Dry confit of ripe crabapples scalded in boiling water, poached in syrup, and dried with sugar in a lukewarm oven.

ingredients.name: crabapples
ingredients.note: fully ripe, hand-picked from the tree

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 500 g for the syrup and approx. 100 g for the final dusting
