ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1.5 glasses for the syrup, plus cold and boiling water for scalding the fruit

steps: Prick the ripe crabapples with a wooden pin, trim the stems in half, and drop into cold water.
Cover the drained fruit with boiling water, let stand for 15 minutes, then rinse again in cold water and drain.
Boil a moderately thin syrup from 500 g of sugar and 375 ml (1.5 glasses) of water, and cook the crabapples in batches, removing the fruit as it softens so that it does not overcook.
Arrange the cooled crabapples on sieves and dry in a very lukewarm oven or in the sun, brushing with a feather dipped in clear syrup and dusting with sugar before the final drying.

name: Two-Tone Apple Pastila
summary: Pink-and-white apple pastila made from thickly reduced tart apple puree and fine sugar, half tinted pink with alkermes and scented with rose oil.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: small, summer or autumn apples of a choice variety

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: 500 g of sugar per 500 g of strained apple puree

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: a splash for moistening the apples while cooking down

ingredients.name: alkermes
ingredients.note: juice or liqueur made from szkarłatnica (pokeweed), for tinting half the mixture pink

ingredients.name: rose oil
ingredients.note: a few drops for the pink half of the mixture, optional

steps: Peel 4 kg of tart apples, cut into pieces, add a splash of water, and cook until soft.
Press the hot apples through a colander, weigh the resulting puree, and add 500 g of fine sugar for every 500 g of puree.
Stir thoroughly in a pan and reduce over high heat, stirring constantly, until the paste pulls away from the sides; remove immediately to avoid overcooking.
Divide the hot mixture into two equal parts: leave one half white, and tint the other half pink with 2 teaspoons of alkermes and optionally a few drops of rose oil.
Transfer both portions to platters, bringing the two colors together; once cooled, cut into pieces of any desired shape and dry in a very low oven or a warm room.

name: Jabłeczne serki (Apple Cheese, Alternative Method)
summary: Spiced apple cheese made from cooked tart apples and candied orange peel, pressed under a weight for two to three days and dried in a low oven.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: of a choice variety, peeled and cut up

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: a splash for moistening the apples during cooking

steps: Peel the tart apples, remove the cores, cut into pieces, and cook covered in a stoneware pot with a splash of water until soft.
Press the cooked apples through a colander or fine sieve and return the puree to the pan.
Add sugar to taste, the sifted cloves, cinnamon, and mace, and the finely chopped candied orange peel.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until the thick paste pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Pack the mixture into a dampened, thoroughly wrung-out linen bag, shape, and leave under a press or heavy stone for 2–3 days; remove and finish drying in a low oven or a sunny, well-ventilated place.

name: Jabłeczne serki suszone z miodem (Apple Cheese Dried with Honey)
summary: Traditional apple cheese made from slow-baked tart apples, honey, citrus peel, and spices, pressed in linen bags and dried.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: peeled and cut up, for 4 kg of baked and sieved puree

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.note: good quality, per 4 kg of apple puree

ingredients.name: almond oil
ingredients.note: optional for greasing the linen bags instead of wetting them in cold water

steps: Peel the tart apples, remove the cores, cut into pieces, place in earthenware pots, and bake in a warm oven for approx. 8 hours until completely soft, then press through a colander.

Weigh out 1 kg of honey per 4 kg of sieved apple puree, bring the honey to a boil in a saucepan, and mix with the sifted spices (cinnamon, cloves, a pinch of black pepper), grated lemon zest, and chopped candied orange peel.
Combine the spiced honey with the apple puree and cook together for 10–15 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pack the hot mixture into linen bags (dipped in cold water and wrung out, or greased with almond oil), shape into round loaves, and place under a press for 6–7 days.
Remove the shaped apple cheeses from the bags and dry on wooden boards in a very low oven or a sunny, well-ventilated place.

name: Jabłeczne serki krystalizowane (Crystallized Apple Cheese)
summary: Small crystallized pastilles and balls made from grated raw apples cooked down with an equal volume of fine sugar and dried in coarse crystal sugar.

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: summer or autumn apples of a choice variety, peeled and grated

ingredients.name: fine sugar
ingredients.note: approximately 3 glassfuls; 1 glassful of sugar per 1 glassful of drained apple pulp

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.note: coarsely crushed, for coating the cut-out rounds

steps: Peel the tart apples, grate them on a grater, and drain off the excess juice (which can be used for jelly).
Measure the drained apple pulp and add a glassful (approximately 200 g) of fine sugar for each glassful (250 ml) of pulp.
Transfer the combined mixture to a wide pan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it becomes uniform and translucent.
Pour onto a platter lightly greased with fresh olive oil and place in a low oven for several hours to dry slightly.
Cut out small rounds with a small cutter or liqueur glass, coat with coarsely crushed granulated sugar, and finish drying on boards or sieves in a very low oven.

name: Apple Balls Dried in Sugar
summary: Balls scooped from White Transparent apples, simmered until translucent in lemon syrup and dried in fine sugar, accompanied by a jelly made from the peels and trimmings.

ingredients.name: White Transparent apples
ingredients.note: not overly ripe, for 500 g of scooped balls, with the peels and trimmings reserved for jelly

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 1 kg for the syrup per 500 g of balls and approx. 200 g of finely crushed sugar for dusting

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2 glasses for the syrup, plus cold water for soaking and a small amount of water for boiling the peels

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: juice of 1 lemon for the water and juice of a whole second lemon for the syrup

steps: Peel the slightly underripe White Transparent apples, scoop round balls from the flesh with a melon baller, and drop them immediately into cold water with the juice of 1 lemon.
Boil a syrup from 1 kg of sugar and 500 ml (2 glasses) of water until it begins to pearl, squeeze in the juice of the second lemon, and add the drained apple balls.
Simmer over low heat, removing with a slotted spoon onto platters those balls that have already become translucent, and adding the remaining raw ones.
Dust the cooled balls with finely crushed sugar, dry on sieves in a very lukewarm oven, and pack into jars or paper-lined boxes.

Boil the remaining apple peels and trimmings in a small amount of water, strain through linen cloth, combine with the syrup left over from cooking the balls, boil several times over low heat while skimming, and pour as a pale-yellow jelly into small jars.

name: Chestnuts Candied in Sugar
summary: Boiled chestnuts peeled hot, glazed in a thick, lightly caramelized sugar syrup, and shocked in ice water.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 0.5 glass for the syrup, plus water for boiling the chestnuts and cold water with ice

steps: Place 500 g of chestnuts into a pot of cold water, boil until tender, and then remove one at a time from under the lid to peel them while still hot.
Boil a thick, nearly browned caramel syrup from 375 g of sugar and 125 ml (0.5 glass) of water.
Drop the hot peeled chestnuts into the boiling syrup and toss thoroughly to coat them in the glaze.
Remove the chestnuts one by one with a wooden skewer, dip for a split second in cold water with ice, and arrange side by side on a porcelain platter for immediate serving.

name: Melon dried in sugar
summary: A dry preserve (candied melon) of square pieces of green melon soaked for four days in an ever thicker sugar syrup, then rolled in a syrup cooked to the thread stage.

ingredients.name: green half-ripe melon
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into square pieces, orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: 750 g for the syrups over several days (500 g + 250 g), plus 250 g for the thick glaze for drying

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the syrups, plus water for softening and shocking the melon

steps: Peel a green half-ripe melon, cut out the centre, and cut the flesh into neat square pieces. Cover them with cold water and heat slowly until just soft, then drain them on a sieve, rinse them with cold water, and drain them (you may cover them the first night with a light syrup, which you pour off in the morning).
On the second day, cook a fresh syrup from 500 g of sugar and 300 ml of water, cover the melon with the hot syrup, and leave it for a day.

On the third day, pour off the syrup, add 250 g of sugar, bring it to the boil, and cover the melon with the boiling syrup. On the fourth day, boil the syrup together with the melon a few times and cool it.

To dry the fruit, lift the pieces onto a sieve to drain. Cook a very thick syrup from the remaining 250 g of sugar to the thread stage, add the melon, bring it to the boil once, cool it while stirring with a spoon, and lift the pieces onto a platter to dry.

name: Almonds dried in sugar
summary: Crisp pralines of whole unpeeled almonds toasted in a pan with an equal weight of sugar and a little water until caramelized and brown.
steps: Put the unpeeled almonds and the fine sugar into a wide heavy pan and pour in just enough water (about 150 ml) to cover the sugar.
Cook them together over moderate heat, stirring often, until the water has evaporated and the sugar begins to dry on the almonds.

Move the pan for a moment onto a lower heat and stir constantly with a wooden spoon until the sugar is completely dry. Then set it back on a higher heat and stir until the sugar coating browns lightly.
Tip the hot almonds onto a platter, separate them one by one with a fork so they do not stick, and put them for a few minutes into a gently heated oven (about 100 °C) to dry.

name: Skórki pomarańczowe suszone w cukrze (Candied dried orange peels)
summary: Thick orange peels gradually infused with syrup, then coated in crystallising sugar.

ingredients.name: thick orange peels
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilogr.; from large oranges, weighed before boiling

ingredients.name: light sugar syrup
ingredients.note: enough to cover the peels; proportions not specified

ingredients.name: water for second syrup
ingredients.note: orig. one and a half szklanki

ingredients.name: water for soaking and boiling
ingredients.note: for soaking and boiling; enough to cover the peels

steps: Score the peels of large oranges into six sections, remove them gently, and weigh 500 g before boiling.
Soak the peels in cold water for 7200 minutes, changing the water daily.
Cover with fresh water and boil for about 120 minutes until the peels are completely tender.
Drain the water and cover the peels with cold water for 1440 minutes.
Drain the peels in a sieve.
Cover them with lukewarm, light syrup so they are submerged, and leave until the next day.
Pour off the first syrup and drain the peels thoroughly again.
Boil 500 g sugar with 375 ml water and pour the hot syrup over the peels.
Set aside for 1440 minutes.
Drain the peels, add the remaining 500 g sugar to the syrup, and boil without adding water until thickened.
Pour the hot syrup over the peels and leave until the fourth day.
On the fourth day, pour off and boil the syrup, add the peels, bring to a boil again, and leave to cool.
Remove the peels onto a sieve for several hours, saving the syrup.
Boil half of the reserved syrup until dipping a fork and blowing on it releases sugar threads instead of drops.
Place the peels into the syrup and stir for a few minutes; when the sugar begins to cool, remove from heat, keep stirring, then lift the peels with a fork onto a sieve or platter to dry naturally.

name: Candied Dried Greengage Plums
summary: Half-ripe greengage plums repeatedly steeped in syrup, simmered, and dried with sugar.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, warming, cooling, and the syrup; amount not specified

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: additionally for subsequent thickenings of the syrup and for generously sprinkling the fruit; amount not specified

steps: Prick the half-ripe greengage plums deeply with a wooden skewer and place into cold water.
Transfer them to hot, non-boiling water and warm until softened.
Cool them briefly in cold water.
Drain the fruit and place into a jar.
Cook a thin syrup from 500 g of sugar and water.
Cool the syrup.
Pour the cooled syrup over the greengage plums and press down lightly so they are completely submerged without being crushed.
Repeat the pouring about five times, each time draining off the syrup, adding a little sugar, boiling it, and cooling before pouring over the fruit again.
On the final boiling, simmer the greengage plums in the syrup.
Sprinkle the fruit generously with fine sugar.
Dry the greengage plums to obtain a dry preserve.

name: Candied Dried Mirabelle Plums
summary: Mirabelle plums infused in sugar syrup for four days and then dried.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the syrup; orig. half a kilogram

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking, blanching, cooling, and the syrup; amount not specified

steps: Prick the ripe mirabelle plums with a needle or wooden skewer and immediately place into cold water.
Scald the fruit with hot water until softened.
Transfer them back to cold water to cool.
Drain the mirabelle plums thoroughly on a sieve.
Cook a thick syrup from the sugar and water.
Cool the syrup.
Arrange the mirabelle plums in a jar and pour the cooled syrup over them.
Press the fruit down lightly with a glass tumbler so they remain submerged.
Repeat the pouring over 5760 minutes, or four days, using a warmer syrup each time.
Dry the syrup-infused fruit to obtain a dry preserve.

name: Baranina wędzona w żołądku baranim (cold-smoked mutton in sheep stomach, kindziuk barani)
summary: A traditional Eastern Borderlands cured meat made from pieces of mutton rubbed with spiced salt, packed tightly into a cleaned sheep stomach and sewn shut, then cold-smoked for ten days.

ingredients.name: mutton
ingredients.note: rack, breast, neck, shoulder, or leg cuts trimmed of excess fat

ingredients.name: potassium nitrate
ingredients.note: optional, to preserve the pink colour of the meat

ingredients.name: sheep stomach
ingredients.note: thoroughly cleaned and salted, for stuffing the meat

steps: Trim the mutton of excess suet and rub thoroughly with the salt mixed with black pepper, crumbled bay leaf, coriander, marjoram, and optionally a teaspoon of potassium nitrate.
Pack the seasoned meat as tightly as possible into a thoroughly cleaned and salted sheep stomach, then sew the opening shut with strong thread.
Hang the stuffed stomach for a few days in a breezy place to dry well in the wind.

Cold-smoke in dense, cold smoke for about 10 days, then air out and store in a cool, dark larder; serve boiled and hot with horseradish, cold as a cured meat, or as a meat addition to borscht and potato soup.

name: Tradycyjna kiełbasa wiejska wędzona (cold-smoked Polish country pork and beef kiełbasa)
summary: A long-keeping smoked kiełbasa (Polish sausage) made from finely knife-chopped marbled pork and lean beef in a 3:1 ratio, seasoned with salt, black pepper, allspice, and garlic, dried for a week and cold-smoked.

ingredients.name: marbled pork
ingredients.note: in a ratio of 3 parts pork to 1 part beef (per 9 kg meat)

ingredients.name: lean beef
ingredients.note: in a ratio of 1 part beef to 3 parts pork (per 9 kg meat)

steps: Finely chop marbled pork and lean, tender beef with a sharp knife in a 3:1 ratio (e.g. 6.75 kg of pork and 2.25 kg of beef for a 9 kg batch).
For 9 kg of meat, add 400 g of salt, 15 g of potassium nitrate, 20 g of crushed black pepper, 10 g of crushed allspice, and mashed garlic, and knead the mixture very thoroughly.
Stuff the mixture into medium-thin pork casings and hang the kiełbasa (Polish sausages) on rods in a cool, frost-free larder for 7 days.
Before smoking, air-dry the kiełbasa (Polish sausages) for a few hours in the wind, then smoke for about a week in cool smoke.

name: Głowizna wielkanocna nadziewana (stuffed pig's head galantine)
summary: A boned pig's head stuffed in layers with seasoned forcemeat, slices of smoked bacon, ham, calf's liver, hard-boiled eggs, and gherkins, simmered in a vinegared vegetable stock and served in aspic.

ingredients.name: pig's head
ingredients.note: salted, with brain and tongue removed

ingredients.name: minced pork, beef, or veal
ingredients.note: orig. 1 to 1.5 kg, for the forcemeat

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. several tablespoons of strong vinegar

steps: Remove all bones from the salted pig's head without damaging the skin, then sew the snout and eye openings shut with strong thread.
Prepare a seasoned forcemeat from 1.5 kg of minced pork, beef, or veal mixed with soaked bread roll, 2 eggs, and seasonings, as for minced-meat patties.
Pack the head in layers with the meat forcemeat, slices of smoked bacon and ham (400 g), soaked calf's liver (400 g), quarters from 6 hard-boiled eggs, and gherkins.
Sew the neck opening closed with clean linen, splint the ears with wooden sticks tied with string to preserve their shape (and optionally sew the entire head into a cloth).

Place the stuffed head in a large pot along with the removed bones, soup vegetables, onion, bay leaf, black pepper, and salt, cover with hot water and several tablespoons of vinegar, and simmer gently for 3 hours from the moment it boils.
Remove the head, let it cool, and remove the threads; reduce the cooking stock to a clear jelly, let it set, and use it to garnish the sliced galantine.

name: Rolada wieprzowa gotowana w żołądku (pressed pork, ham, and fatback roll boiled in stomach)
summary: A homemade charcuterie roll of strips of fresh pork, smoked ham, fresh fatback, and pig's ears seasoned with onion, garlic, and marjoram, sewn into a pork stomach, simmered in vinegared water, and pressed under a weight.

ingredients.name: pig's ears
ingredients.note: finely chopped after discarding the thick cartilage

ingredients.name: bay leaf
ingredients.note: for the filling and cooking liquid

ingredients.name: allspice
ingredients.note: for the filling and cooking liquid

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: for the filling and cooking liquid

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: for acidulating the cooking water and moistening the wrapping cloth

ingredients.name: pork stomach
ingredients.note: from a small pig, thoroughly cleaned

steps: Cut 500 g of fresh fatback, 500 g of smoked ham, and 2 kg of moderately lean fresh pork into strips, and finely chop 2 pig's ears (after removing the thick cartilage).
Add 2 finely chopped Spanish onions, 2 mashed cloves of garlic, and salt, black pepper, allspice, crumbled bay leaf, and marjoram to taste, then mix everything thoroughly.
Pack the meat mixture into a thoroughly cleaned pork stomach and sew the opening shut with strong thread.
Place the roll in a pot of water acidulated with vinegar along with bay leaf, black pepper, and allspice, and simmer gently for 2 hours from the moment it boils.
Remove the cooked roll, press firmly under a weighted board, and keep in a cool place for 24 hours before serving; store wrapped in a cloth moistened with vinegar.

name: Domowa biała kiełbasa wieprzowa do smażenia (homemade fresh pork kiełbasa for frying)
summary: Traditional fresh kiełbasa (Polish sausage) made from finely knife-chopped lean and fatty pork with grated onion, marjoram, black pepper, and garlic, kneaded with cold water or stock and stuffed into pork casings.

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.note: half lean pork and half fatty, well-marbled pork

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: orig. half a kilo, grated or ground

ingredients.name: cold water or pork bone stock
garlic
ingredients.note: orig. a couple of cloves mashed with salt, optional

steps: Chop 4 kg of pork (2 kg lean and 2 kg fatty, well-marbled) very finely with a sharp knife.
Add 100 g of salt, a tablespoon of rubbed marjoram, 10 g of black pepper, 500 g of grated onion, and optionally garlic mashed with salt.
Knead the meat for a long time, gradually adding 500 to 750 ml (2–3 szklanki) of cold water or bone stock until the meat absorbs all the liquid.
Stuff the meat mixture into pork casings (not too tightly, so they do not burst during cooking) and prick any air pockets with a fine needle.
Simmer and fry the kiełbasa (Polish sausages) just before serving, or store hanging from a rod in a dry, cool larder.

name: Półgęski litewskie wędzone na kości (Lithuanian cold-smoked bone-in goose breasts)
summary: Authentic Lithuanian smoked goose breasts on the bone from fattened geese, dry-cured with toasted salt, coriander, black pepper, allspice, bay leaf, and cloves, then cold-smoked for a week.

ingredients.name: bone-in goose breasts
ingredients.note: from large fattened geese (about 16 kg in total)

steps: Cut the whole breasts on the bone from large, fattened geese (10 breasts weighing about 16 kg in total).
Mix 500 g of toasted salt with 20 g of potassium nitrate and the coarsely crushed spices: 40 g of coriander, 10 g of black pepper, 5 g of allspice, 10 g of bay leaf, and a few cloves.
Pack the goose breasts in a deep vessel, sprinkling each layer with the spiced salt, press down with a weighted board, and leave for 2 days in a moderately warm room.
Move the vessel to a cool larder and cure for up to 3 weeks, turning the breasts from top to bottom every day.
Before smoking, wipe the goose breasts dry, wrap in paper, tie with string, hang for a day in a breezy place to dry completely, and cold-smoke for a week.

name: Półgęski zwijane bez kości wędzone (rolled boneless cold-smoked goose breasts)
summary: Boned fattened geese cured for eight days in spiced salt with lemon zest and coriander, rolled tightly into cylinders, dried in paper, and cold-smoked for a week.
steps: Clean and singe large fattened geese carefully, slit them down the back, and bone them completely without damaging the skin or meat.
Rub the boned birds with salt and potassium nitrate, and sprinkle with coarsely crushed black pepper, allspice, cloves, coriander, and finely chopped lemon zest.
Pack the geese in pairs, skin-side out, in a deep vessel, press down with a weighted board, and cure for 8 days, turning them from top to bottom daily and basting with the brine they release.

Remove the geese from the brine, wipe thoroughly dry, roll up lengthwise into a tight cylinder (splitting very large birds lengthwise down the breastbone first) so the meatier breast sections remain in the centre, and sew shut with thick thread.
Wrap the rolls in paper, tie with twine, hang for several hours in a breezy place to dry well, and cold-smoke for a week in completely cool smoke.

name: Kiełbasa gęsia wędzona (cold-smoked goose, beef, and pork sausage)
summary: An Eastern Borderlands smoked kiełbasa (Polish sausage) made from finely diced goose meat, tender beef, pork neck, and raw goose fat, cured for three days and cold-smoked.

ingredients.name: goose meat from legs and carcasses
tender beef
ingredients.note: orig. the same amount as the goose meat

ingredients.name: pork neck
ingredients.note: orig. twice as much marbled pork neck

ingredients.name: raw goose fat
ingredients.note: orig. a quarter kilo per 3 kg meat, ground

steps: Cut the goose meat from legs and carcasses (750 g), an equal amount of tender beef (750 g), and twice the amount of marbled pork neck (1.5 kg) with a sharp knife into tiny dice.
For 3 kg of meat, add 250 g of ground raw goose fat along with salt, potassium nitrate, and finely powdered black pepper, allspice, marjoram, and coriander, then mix thoroughly.
Pack the seasoned meat into a bowl, press down with a weighted board, and keep for 3 days in a cool storeroom.
Stuff the mixture as tightly as possible into medium-wide casings and air-dry for 2–3 days in the wind.
Cold-smoke the kiełbasa (Polish sausages) for about a week.

name: Kiszki kaszane (buckwheat blood sausage, kaszanka)
summary: Traditional homemade kaszanka made from buckwheat groats, fresh pork blood, and rendered pork intestinal fat with marjoram, allspice, and black pepper, poached in pork casings.

ingredients.name: buckwheat groats
ingredients.note: orig. 2 kwarty of buckwheat groats (or 1 l of barley groats scalded with hot milk)

ingredients.name: pork blood
ingredients.note: orig. 2 kwarty, strained to remove clots

ingredients.name: rendered pork intestinal fat
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwarta of rendered intestinal fat

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the mixture and the poaching water

steps: Mix 2 l of buckwheat groats with 2 l of strained pork blood and 1 l of rendered pork fat.
Season the mixture with salt, black pepper, a handful of rubbed marjoram, and ground allspice, and mix thoroughly.
Fill strong pork casings halfway with the mixture (so the groats have room to swell) and tie or pin the ends securely.

Place the sausages in a large pot of well-salted boiling water, bring back to a boil, and cook over very low heat for about 45–60 minutes until the groats are tender, taking care that the casings do not burst.
Remove the cooked blood sausages, cool, and store in a cool, dry place; to serve, cut into thick slices and fry in melted fresh fatback.

name: Roast turkey with liver stuffing
summary: Roast turkey stuffed with calf's liver, bread roll, and raisins.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. ¼ funt; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: orig. a szklanka or 1½; source allows 250–375 ml, lower bound used.

ingredients.name: sugar lumps
ingredients.note: orig. 2 lumps; weight of lumps not specified.

steps: Clean the turkey.
Leave the turkey in the refrigerator to tenderize for several days, that is, for more than 2880 minutes.
Season the turkey with salt.
Cook the liver until tender.
Finely chop the liver.
Soak the bread roll in the milk and squeeze it out.
Mix the liver with the bread roll, egg yolks, eggs, the butter for the stuffing, raisins, sugar, allspice, and salt.
Stuff the skin at the neck of the turkey with the filling, and if needed also its cavity.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Roast the turkey in a roasting pan until cooked through, basting with the butter reserved for roasting.

name: Roast capon
summary: Capon roasted with butter, served with a crushed rusk and pan juices.

ingredients.name: rusk
ingredients.note: source states 1–2 pieces; lower bound used; crushed

steps: Clean and dress the capon.
Salt the capon.
Wrap the capon in baking paper.
Roast the capon in a roasting pan in an oven at 180 °C, basting with butter, until cooked through.
Sprinkle the roasted capon with the crushed rusk.
Spoon the butter collected in the roasting pan over the capon.

name: Capon with juniper
summary: Capon stuffed with breadcrumbs, eggs, and juniper berries, roasted with butter.

ingredients.name: juniper berries
ingredients.note: orig. ½ tbsp; the source mentions juniper in the stuffing and on the surface of the capon without specifying how the amount is divided

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 2 tbsp; half for the stuffing, half for rubbing

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kwaterka; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: rusk
ingredients.note: source states 1–2 pieces; lower bound used; crushed

steps: Salt the capon.
Crush the juniper berries.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the eggs, half of the butter, and part of the juniper.
Fill the capon with the stuffing.
Rub the capon with the remaining butter mixed with the rest of the juniper.
Wrap the capon in baking paper.
Roast the capon in a roasting pan in an oven at 180 °C.
Remove the paper.
Sprinkle the capon with the crushed rusk.
Finish roasting the capon until browned.
Spoon the roasting juices over the capon.

name: Capons with truffle sauce
summary: Capons braised with vegetables and fatback, served with truffles in a sauce of red wine, rum, and olive oil.

ingredients.name: pork fatback
ingredients.note: orig. ¼ funt; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: bouillon
ingredients.note: 500–625 ml; orig. 2–2½ szklanki; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: rum
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kieliszek; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kieliszek; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: orig. 1 kieliszek; the method confirms equal volumes of olive oil, wine, and rum; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: portable soup cake
ingredients.note: a piece; the source does not specify the weight

steps: Cut the carrot, parsley root, leek, and onion.
Cut the fatback into slices.
Line the bottom of a casserole with the vegetables and part of the fatback.
Place the capons on the vegetables.
Cover the capons with the remaining fatback.
Add the salt, allspice, bay leaves, and cloves.
Pour in the bouillon.
Braise, covered, until the meat is tender.
Cut the capons into portions.
Cut the truffles into slices.
Pour the wine, rum, and olive oil over the truffles.
Add the portable soup cake and the braising juices from the capons.
Bring the sauce to a boil.
Pour the truffle sauce over the capons.

name: Ducks with brown sauce
summary: Roast ducks with a brown bouillon sauce flavoured with capers and sugar.

ingredients.name: duck
ingredients.note: source states 2–3 birds; lower bound used

ingredients.name: sugar lumps
ingredients.note: orig. 2–3 lumps; lower bound used; weight of lumps not specified

steps: Salt the ducks.
Roast the ducks in a roasting pan in an oven at 180 °C, using the butter reserved for roasting.
Brown the butter reserved for the sauce.
Fry the flour in it, stirring so that no lumps form.
Pour in the bouillon.
Bring the sauce to a boil.
Strain the sauce.
Add the capers and sugar.
Simmer the sauce briefly.
Pour the sauce over the ducks cut into portions.

name: Ducks with homemade noodles and mushrooms
summary: Ducks stuffed with homemade noodles and dried porcini mushrooms, braised in mushroom broth with sour cream.

ingredients.name: duck
ingredients.note: source states 2–3 birds; lower bound used

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.note: source states 3–4 pieces; lower bound used; crushed

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.note: orig. 3 szklanki; amount from the ingredient list, differing from the amount in the method

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: two for the noodles, one for the stuffing

ingredients.name: dried porcini mushrooms
ingredients.note: source states 8–10 pieces; lower bound used; reserve the cooking broth

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for cooking the mushrooms and noodles; the source does not specify the volume

steps: Slit the ducks along the back and remove the bones, leaving the leg and wing bones in place.
Season the ducks with salt, pepper, and crushed cloves.
Boil the porcini mushrooms in water, reserving the cooking broth.
Chop part of the cooked porcini for the stuffing, reserving the rest for braising and the sauce.
Knead a noodle dough from 750 ml of flour and two eggs.
Roll out the dough and cut it into noodles.
Boil the noodles in water and drain.
Mix the noodles with the remaining egg, egg yolks, chopped porcini, butter, and salt.
Fill the ducks with the stuffing and sew the openings shut.
Pour the mushroom broth with part of the reserved mushrooms over the ducks in a casserole.
Braise, covered, until tender.
Cut the ducks into portions.
Mix the sour cream with 7.5 ml of flour.
Combine the braising liquid with the sour cream and the remaining sliced mushrooms.
Pour the sauce over the duck portions.

name: French-style carp
summary: Carp poached in a vinegared stock with lemon, onion, and warm spices.

ingredients.name: carp
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 funty; 1600–2000 g (historical measure, converted approximately)

ingredients.name: wine vinegar
ingredients.note: orig. 1 szklanka; for scalding the fish and for the stock

ingredients.name: allspice and black peppercorns
ingredients.note: A total of 8–10 berries/corns; the source does not specify the ratio of the two spices.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: For the stock: two parts water to one part vinegar, just enough to cover the fish.

steps: Clean the carp, keep the head, and cut the fish into crosswise steaks.
Arrange the pieces side by side, pour part of the boiled wine vinegar over them, and cover while preparing the stock.
Pour the remaining wine vinegar into a pot and add twice as much water, just enough to cover the fish.
Cut the lemon into slices and chop the onion finely.
Bring the stock to a boil with the lemon, onion, bay leaves, cloves, allspice, black pepper, and salt.
Place first the head and then the carp steaks into the stock and cook over high heat until the fish is done.
Cover the cooked fish with baking paper.
Transfer the carp to a platter with the cooked onion and lemon.
Sprinkle with parsley leaves and serve with olive oil and vinegar.

name: Carp in red wine, with scales
summary: Carp cooked, covered, in red wine with lemon, cinnamon, and cloves.

ingredients.name: carp with scales and reserved blood
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 funty; 1600–2000 g (historical measure, converted approximately)

ingredients.name: strong bouillon with soup vegetables
ingredients.note: orig. ½ kwarta (historical measure, converted approximately)

steps: Split the gutted carp with its scales left on and cut it into pieces, reserving the blood.
Arrange the fish together with the blood in a pot.
Sprinkle with salt, cinnamon, and pounded cloves.
Cut the lemon into slices.
Add the wine, vinegar, bouillon with soup vegetables, olive oil, lemon, and sugar.
Cook, covered, over high heat until the fish is cooked and the sauce has reduced.

name: Carp fried in a rusk coating
summary: Carp pieces coated in egg and crushed rusks, fried in butter and served with parsley.

ingredients.name: carp
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 funty; 1600–2000 g, lower bound used

ingredients.name: rusks
ingredients.note: crushed; orig. 6–7 rusks; lower bound used

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 2 tbsp; for frying the fish and parsley

steps: Scale and gut the carp.
Split the carp and rinse it.
Cut the fish into portions.
Score the skin along the back.
Sprinkle the fish with salt.
Set aside to absorb the salt.
Pat the fish dry.
Beat the eggs.
Crush the rusks.
Dip the carp pieces in the eggs.
Coat the fish in the crushed rusks.
Heat most of the butter.
Fry the carp until golden brown.
Fry the parsley in the remaining butter.
Serve the carp sprinkled with the parsley.

name: Baked sturgeon with mustard sauce
summary: Sturgeon baked on vegetables under a layer of onion, eggs, and grated bread, served with a wine and mustard sauce.

ingredients.name: sturgeon
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 funty; range 1600–2000 g, lower bound used; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: Divide between the vegetable bed and the egg mixture.

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.note: For grating and sprinkling over the fish; the source does not specify the portion size.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: orig. 1½ tbsp; for the baking sheet and for frying the onion.

steps: Cut the carrot, parsley root, and part of the onion into slices.
Grease a baking sheet with part of the butter.
Line the baking sheet with the sliced vegetables.
Clean the sturgeon.
Salt the fish and lay it on the vegetables.
Chop the remaining onion.
Sauté the chopped onion in the remaining butter.
Leave the sautéed onion to cool.
Mix the cooled onion with the beaten eggs.
Coat the fish with the onion and egg mixture.
Grate the bread and sprinkle it over the fish.
Bake the fish in an oven preheated to 220 °C until cooked through.
Remove the fish from the baking sheet.
Boil the baked vegetables with the wine, bouillon, vinegar, and mustard.
Pour the sauce over the fish.

name: Grilled sturgeon
summary: Sturgeon marinated with onion and olive oil, grilled and served with mustard sauce.

ingredients.name: sturgeon
ingredients.note: orig. 4–5 funty; range 1600–2000 g, lower bound used; historical measure, converted approximately

ingredients.name: mustard sauce
ingredients.note: Prepared sauce for serving; the source does not give its ingredients.

steps: Scald and clean the sturgeon.
Cut the fish into thin slices.
Finely chop the onion and press out its juice.
Sprinkle the fish with salt, pepper, and the onion.
Drizzle the fish with olive oil.
Leave the fish in the marinade for 120 minutes.
Brush the fish with butter.
Grill the fish over glowing coals on both sides until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the mustard sauce.

name: Crucian carp baked in sour cream
summary: Crucian carp fried in butter, then baked with sour cream and crushed rusks.

ingredients.name: rusks
ingredients.note: crushed; orig. 1–2 rusks; lower bound used

steps: Clean and salt the crucian carp.
Fry the fish in the butter until golden brown.
Arrange the fish in an ovenproof dish.
Pour the sour cream over them.
Sprinkle with the crushed rusk.
Bake in the oven until the top is browned.
Serve in the dish in which the fish was baked.

name: Zupa ze świeżych ogórków (fresh cucumber soup)
summary: A delicate vegetable soup with gently cooked fresh cucumbers, enriched with cream, egg yolks, butter, and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: sweet cream butter for creaming with the egg yolks, plus a piece for cooking the cucumbers

ingredients.name: porcini mushroom
ingredients.note: small, fresh mushroom for the broth

steps: Peel the fresh cucumbers, cut them into thin slices, and cook gently in a small saucepan with a piece of butter over low heat for about 15 minutes until completely soft.
In a separate pot, simmer one and a half litres of broth from the soup vegetables and the small fresh porcini mushroom with salt for about 30 minutes, then strain the broth.
Mash the cooked cucumbers with the wheat flour, stir in the cream, pour into the strained vegetable broth, and briefly bring to a boil.
Beat the egg yolks in a soup tureen with a teaspoon of butter and the chopped dill.
Temper the egg yolks with one ladleful of hot soup, mix thoroughly, pour in the rest of the soup, and serve immediately.

name: Zupa z białej fasoli przecierana (puréed white bean soup)
summary: A creamy soup of puréed white cukrowa beans in a vegetable and mushroom broth, enriched with butter, cream, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the broth, plus extra cold water for soaking and boiling the beans

ingredients.name: white beans
ingredients.note: large white beans of the cukrowa variety, soaked the day before

ingredients.name: sweet cream
ingredients.note: sweet cream, or milk (half a szklanka)

steps: Cover the white beans with cold water in a bowl in the evening and soak for about 480 minutes.
Put the carrot, parsley root, leek, onion, and dried mushroom in a pot, pour in 2 l of water, add salt, and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until the broth reduces to 1.5 l, then strain.
Boil the soaked white beans separately until tender for about 70 minutes, drain the water, dry the beans over the heat for 2 minutes, and press through a sieve into a smooth purée.
Combine the bean purée with the strained vegetable broth, add the butter and the wheat flour mixed with the sweet cream, and boil everything together for 3 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks in a soup tureen, temper them with a spoonful of hot soup, pour in the rest of the soup, stir briskly, and serve.

name: Farsz ryżowo-cebulowy do postnych pasztecików (rice and onion filling for Lenten soup pastries)
summary: A classic vegetarian filling for soup pastries made from firm-cooked rice and sweet onion fried golden in butter, seasoned with white pepper.
steps: Boil the rice in water in a pot for about 12 minutes so that it remains slightly firm, then drain thoroughly.
Peel and finely dice the onion, then fry it in a skillet in hot butter for about 8 minutes until pale golden.
Mix the drained rice with the fried onion and its butter, season with salt and white pepper, and use for filling soup pastries.

name: Pasztet jarski w kruczym cieście (layered vegetarian pie in shortcrust pastry)
summary: A rich layered vegetarian pie baked in shortcrust pastry, filled with tomato rice, porcini mushrooms braised in sour cream, butter-tender pumpkin, and hard-boiled eggs.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for the shortcrust pastry, plus a little extra for dusting the mushrooms

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the shortcrust pastry, plus extra for the rice, mushrooms, and pumpkin

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold for the pastry and for boiling the rice

steps: Quickly knead a shortcrust pastry from the wheat flour, butter, salt, and cold water; reserve one-quarter of the pastry for the top, and line the bottom and sides of a springform pan with the rest.
Boil the rice in water for 15 minutes until fluffy, drain, and mix with 1 tablespoon of melted butter, the tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Slice the porcini mushrooms and chop the onion, cook them gently in butter for 15 minutes, then dust with a little wheat flour, stir in the sour cream, and bring to a boil until thick.
Boil the eggs hard for 10 minutes, cool, peel, and slice them, and cook the pumpkin slices gently in butter for 10 minutes until tender; let all the filling layers cool.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C and arrange alternating layers of rice, porcini mushrooms, pumpkin, and eggs in the pastry-lined pan until all the ingredients are used.
Cover the pie with the rolled-out reserved pastry, crimp the edges tightly, prick the top with a fork, and brush with the egg yolk.
Place the pie in the oven preheated to 220 °C and bake for 40 minutes until golden brown.

name: Timbale z makaronu (pasta timbale)
summary: A baked timbale of long Italian pasta coiled inside a mould and filled with finely broken pasta in a thick mushroom sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for boiling the pasta and seasoning the mixture

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the mould and dotting the top

ingredients.name: mushroom sauce
ingredients.note: thick, made from fresh or dried mushrooms (plus extra for serving)

steps: Cook the long Italian pasta whole in well-salted water for about 10 minutes, and in a separate pot cook the finely broken pasta for 8 minutes, then drain both.
Generously butter a smooth metal mould and dust it with breadcrumbs.
Line the bottom and sides of the mould with the long pasta coiled in a spiral so that no gaps remain, reserving some of the long strands for the top.
Mix the thick mushroom sauce with the whole eggs and the cooked broken pasta, then season the mixture with salt, nutmeg, white pepper, and marjoram.
Fill the centre of the mould with the pasta mixture, cover with the reserved long pasta, and dot the top with pieces of butter.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and bake uncovered for about 35 minutes (or cover the mould tightly with a lid and steam for 45 minutes).
Unmould the finished timbale onto a platter and serve hot with additional mushroom sauce.

name: Timbale z ryżu (rice timbale)
summary: A baked rice timbale lined with mashed rice and eggs, filled with fluffy braised rice layered with button mushrooms and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for mashing into the rice mixture

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the onion, plus extra for the mushrooms, mould, and top

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: or salted water for moistening the rice

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: large, ripe, cut into coarse dice

steps: Boil the first portion of rice in water until very soft, about 25 minutes, then drain, salt, and mash thoroughly with a spoon along with the teaspoon of butter and the eggs until completely smooth.

Cook the finely chopped onion in a tablespoon of butter until translucent, add the second portion of rice, and fry over low heat, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes until the rice turns slightly yellow.
Gradually add the vegetable broth a few spoonfuls at a time and cook the rice gently, covered, over low heat for about 20 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Cook the cut button mushrooms gently in butter, covered, for 10 minutes, and cut the tomatoes into coarse dice.
Generously butter a smooth mould, dust it with breadcrumbs, and line the bottom and sides with part of the mashed rice mixture.
Fill the centre of the mould with the fluffy rice layered with the cooked mushrooms and tomatoes, cover with the remaining mashed rice mixture, and dot the top with pieces of butter.
Place the mould in an oven preheated to 180 °C and bake for about 60 minutes until golden brown (or cover with a lid and steam for 60 minutes).
Unmould the timbale onto a platter and serve with plain tomato sauce.

name: Domowy makaron zapiekany (baked homemade egg noodles with mushrooms)
summary: A baked casserole of thinly cut homemade egg noodles layered with a thick dried mushroom and onion ragout under a crisp cheese crust.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the dough, plus extra for the boiling water and mushroom filling

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: enough to knead a firm dough, plus water for boiling

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for thickening the mushrooms

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: melted for the noodles, plus extra for the filling, baking dish, and top

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: whole, for mixing with the noodles

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for dusting the baking dish and sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: hard cheese
ingredients.note: grated, sharp, for sprinkling on top

steps: Knead a very firm dough from the wheat flour, egg, salt, and a small amount of water, roll it out as thinly as possible, let it dry slightly, cut into strips, and shred finely into thin noodles.
Boil the slightly dried noodles in plenty of salted boiling water for about 5 minutes, drain in a colander, and rinse with cold water.
Boil the dried mushrooms in water until tender, about 30 minutes, reserve the broth, slice the mushrooms into strips, and fry them in butter with the chopped onions for 8 minutes.
Sprinkle the mushrooms with the wheat flour, stir in the reserved mushroom broth to make a thick sauce, bring to a boil, and season with salt and pepper.
Toss the cooked noodles with the melted butter and whole eggs.
Butter a shallow baking dish and dust it with breadcrumbs, spread half of the noodles on the bottom, cover with the mushroom filling, and top with the remaining noodles.
Sprinkle the top generously with grated cheese mixed in equal parts with breadcrumbs, dot with pieces of butter, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 30 minutes until golden brown.

name: Budyń z kapusty słodkiej (savory cabbage pudding)
summary: A steamed savory pudding of white or savoy cabbage bound with a thick white sauce and beaten eggs.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for the roux, plus extra for the mould and serving

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for blanching the cabbage and seasoning the mixture

steps: Finely shred the cabbage, blanch it in boiling salted water for about 5 minutes, drain thoroughly, and squeeze out the excess water.
Cook the wheat flour with the butter over low heat without browning, whisk in the milk, and cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes until thick.
Mix the squeezed cabbage with the thick milk sauce, season with salt and white pepper, stir in the egg yolks, and finally fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Butter a pudding mould, dust it with breadcrumbs, pack in the cabbage mixture, and fasten the lid tightly.
Steam the pudding for 60 minutes, then unmould onto a platter and serve with melted butter.

name: Budyń ze szpinaku (savory spinach pudding)
summary: A delicate steamed pudding of fresh spinach, milk-soaked bread rolls, and beaten eggs.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for blanching the spinach and seasoning the mixture

ingredients.name: wheat roll
ingredients.note: two small rolls for the mixture, plus extra for croutons to serve

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the mould, browning the croutons, and pouring over the pudding

steps: Pick over and wash the spinach, blanch it in boiling salted water for about 3 minutes, drain thoroughly, and pass it through a mincer.
Soak the two rolls in milk, squeeze them out, and mash until smooth, then mix with the spinach, salt, nutmeg, and egg yolks.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the spinach mixture.
Butter a pudding mould, dust it with breadcrumbs, fill with the mixture, close tightly with a lid, and steam for 60 minutes.
Turn the pudding out onto a platter immediately after steaming, pour browned butter over it, and surround with butter-fried bread croutons.

name: Budyń grzybowy (savory mushroom pudding)
summary: A steamed savory pudding made from dried mushrooms, onion, milk-soaked wheat rolls, and beaten eggs.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the onion and mushrooms and greasing the mould

steps: Boil the dried mushrooms in water until tender, about 30 minutes, drain (reserving the broth for a sauce), and chop them very finely.
Fry the chopped mushrooms in butter together with the finely chopped onions for about 8 minutes.
Soak the wheat rolls in milk, squeeze them out, and mash until smooth, then mix with the mushrooms, egg yolks, salt, and pepper.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the mushroom mixture.
Butter a pudding mould, dust it with breadcrumbs, transfer the mixture into the mould, cover tightly with a lid, and steam for 60 minutes.

name: Budyń z kartofli (savory potato pudding)
summary: A fluffy steamed potato pudding enriched with butter-braised onions, fresh dill, sour cream, and eggs.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for cooking the onions, greasing the mould, and pouring over

steps: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water until tender, about 25 minutes, drain the water, and let them steam dry covered.
Cook the chopped onions gently in butter for about 8 minutes without browning them, then pass them through a mincer together with the potatoes.
Add the chopped dill, salt, white pepper, sour cream, and egg yolks to the potato mixture and mix thoroughly.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the potato mixture.
Transfer the mixture to a buttered and breadcrumb-dusted pudding mould, cover tightly with a lid, and steam for 60 minutes.
Unmould the finished pudding onto a platter and serve hot drizzled with browned butter.

name: Budyń z jaglanej kaszy (savory millet pudding)
summary: A steamed savory pudding of millet groats cooked in milk, enriched with butter, fresh dill, and eggs.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a generous tablespoon for the mixture, plus extra for greasing the mould

steps: Scald the millet groats three times with boiling water, draining the water each time to remove any bitterness.
Cook the millet groats in milk until tender, about 20 minutes, and set aside to cool.
Add the butter, chopped dill, salt, and egg yolks to the cooled millet and beat thoroughly until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them carefully into the millet mixture.
Butter a pudding mould, dust it with breadcrumbs, fill with the mixture, close tightly with a lid, and steam for 60 minutes.

name: Pyzy drożdżowe z cebulą gotowane na parze (steamed yeast dumplings stuffed with onion)
summary: Fluffy yeast dumplings stuffed with butter-braised onions, layered in a buttered pudding mould and steamed.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: 200 g for the sponge and 400 g for kneading the dough

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the dough, plus extra for the onions, mould, and pouring over

steps: Mix 200 g of the wheat flour with the crumbled fresh yeast and lukewarm milk, then leave the sponge in a warm place for 20 minutes to rise.

Add the remaining 400 g of wheat flour, 1 tablespoon of butter, the eggs, salt, and sugar to the risen sponge, knead for 10 minutes until the dough pulls away from your hands, and leave to rise for 30 minutes.
Peel and finely chop the onions, then cook them gently in butter for 15 minutes until soft.
Butter a pudding mould and dust it with breadcrumbs.
With hands dipped in melted butter, pinch off small pieces of the risen dough, flatten them, stuff each with a teaspoon of braised onion, and layer the balls halfway up the mould.
Cover the mould tightly with its lid, steam for 90 minutes, then turn the dumplings out onto a platter and pour melted butter over them.

name: Hreczuchy ze śmietaną (buckwheat patties with sour cream)
summary: Patties made from scalded buckwheat dough, stuffed with a farmer's cheese and egg filling, fried until golden brown and served with sour cream.

ingredients.name: buckwheat flour
ingredients.note: plus a little extra for dusting

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the dough, plus extra for frying

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the dough and cheese filling

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: for the cheese filling (plus optional extra for serving)

ingredients.name: coconut oil
ingredients.note: added to the butter for frying

steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with boiling salted water and a tablespoon of butter to form a thick paste, then set aside until completely cool.
Press the farmer's cheese dry and mash it thoroughly with the eggs, salt, and a teaspoon of sugar until smooth.
Shape the cooled buckwheat dough into thin rounds, dusting them with buckwheat flour, place a portion of the cheese filling on each, and pinch the edges tightly so the cheese does not leak out.
Fry the hreczuchy in hot butter mixed with coconut oil for about 4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown.
Serve the hot hreczuchy with sour cream.

name: Mędrzyki (Polish quark patties)
summary: Traditional patties of minced fresh farmer's cheese, eggs, and flour with a dimple in the centre, pan-fried until golden and served with thick sour cream.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: enough to work into a smooth dough

ingredients.name: coconut oil
ingredients.note: added to the butter for frying to prevent burning

steps: Pass the farmer's cheese through a mincer into a bowl.
Add the whole eggs, salt, sugar, and enough wheat flour to knead a smooth, pliable dough.
Shape the dough into round balls, flatten them with your palm, and press a dimple in the centre of each patty with your finger.
Heat the butter with a little coconut oil in a skillet and fry the mędrzyki for about 15 minutes on both sides until golden brown.
Serve hot with fresh, thick sour cream in a sauceboat.

name: Risotto jarskie zapiekane z grzybami i pomidorami (baked vegetarian mushroom and tomato risotto)
summary: Vegetarian risotto cooked in a mushroom and root-vegetable broth, layered with butter-sautéed mushrooms and tomatoes, and baked under grated Parmesan.

ingredients.name: dried mushrooms
ingredients.note: young, or 200 g fresh button mushrooms

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the mushroom and vegetable broth

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: 1 for the broth and 2 finely chopped for the rice

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the mushrooms and tomatoes

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: sharp grated cheese for sprinkling on top

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for making a sauce with the remaining mushroom broth

steps: Put the dried mushrooms, carrot, parsley root, celeriac, leek, and 1 onion into a pot, cover with water, and simmer the broth for 30 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, add the remaining 2 finely chopped onions, and cook until translucent for 5 minutes, then add the rice and fry, stirring, until lightly yellowed.
Add the hot mushroom broth a few spoonfuls at a time and cook gently, stirring, for about 15 minutes until the rice is completely tender.
Slice the cooked dried mushrooms and the tomatoes and sauté them separately in a skillet in butter.

Preheat the oven to 200 °C, layer the rice, mushrooms, and tomatoes in a deep ovenproof dish, finish with a layer of rice, sprinkle generously with grated Parmesan cheese, and bake for 5 minutes until the cheese melts.
Mix the remaining mushroom broth with the sour cream, bring briefly to a boil, and serve the sauce in a sauceboat alongside the risotto.

name: Kartofle z sosem chrzanowym (baked potatoes with horseradish sauce)
summary: A baked gratin of sliced boiled potatoes, hard-boiled eggs, and fresh tomatoes under a thick horseradish and sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for greasing the dish and dotting the vegetables

steps: Boil the unpeeled potatoes until tender, about 25 minutes, peel while still hot, and cut into slices.
Boil the eggs hard for 10 minutes, peel, and slice them, then slice the washed tomatoes as well.
Butter a baking dish, arrange the slices of potato, egg, and tomato in rows, and dot with pieces of butter.
Pour the thick horseradish and sour cream sauce evenly over the dish and sprinkle the top with breadcrumbs.
Place the dish in an oven preheated to 200 °C and bake for 10 minutes until the top is lightly browned.

name: Kotlety z fasoli (white bean and walnut cutlets)
summary: Tender vegetarian cutlets made from boiled white beans and finely crushed walnuts, breaded in egg and breadcrumbs and pan-fried in butter.

ingredients.name: white beans
ingredients.note: preferably large runner beans, soaked overnight

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold, for soaking and boiling the beans

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the bean mixture, plus plenty of extra butter for frying

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 2 whole for the mixture and 1 beaten for breading

steps: Cover the white beans with cold water in a bowl and leave to soak overnight for about 480 minutes.
Boil the beans in the same water until tender for about 75 minutes, drain off the liquid, and leave the pot covered for 5 minutes so the white beans dry thoroughly.
Pass the still-hot beans through a mincer until smooth.
Cream 1 tablespoon of butter in a small bowl until fluffy, add the finely crushed walnuts, 2 whole eggs, and the minced beans, and beat for 5 minutes until uniform.
Turn the mixture out onto a board dusted with wheat flour, shape into 10 neat cutlets, brush them with the remaining beaten egg, and coat thickly in breadcrumbs.
Heat a generous amount of butter in a skillet, fry the cutlets on both sides until golden for about 10 minutes, and remove them carefully from the skillet, as they are very delicate.

name: Kotlety z włoszczyzny (root vegetable cutlets)
summary: Delicate vegetable cutlets made from boiled carrots, parsley root, celeriac, leeks, and onions, coated in breadcrumbs and pan-fried in butter.

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for binding the mixture and coating the cutlets

steps: Peel and boil the carrots, parsley root, onions, celeriac, and leeks until tender for about 35 minutes, then drain thoroughly and cool.
Pass the cooled vegetables through a mincer.
Season the minced vegetables with salt, beat in the eggs, and add enough breadcrumbs that the mixture can be easily shaped into cutlets.
Shape into cutlets and coat them on all sides in breadcrumbs.
Heat a generous amount of butter in a skillet and fry the cutlets for about 10 minutes on both sides until golden brown.

name: Kotlety ze szpinaku (spinach and potato cutlets)
summary: Cutlets of fresh spinach and boiled potatoes, coated in egg and breadcrumbs and served with sour cream heated with butter.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the boiling water and the mixture

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 large for the mixture and 1 beaten for brushing the cutlets

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 0.5 tbsp for the mixture, 1 tbsp for the sauce, and extra for frying

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for binding the mixture and breading

steps: Peel the potatoes, boil them until tender for 20 minutes, cool, and pass through a mincer.
Plunge the spinach into boiling salted water, boil for 3 minutes, drain in a sieve, squeeze dry, and chop finely or pass through a mincer.
Mix the spinach with the minced potatoes, add 1 large egg, 0.5 tablespoon of butter, and enough breadcrumbs to form a firm mixture, and knead well.
Shape into neat small cutlets, brush with the second beaten egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry the cutlets in hot butter for about 10 minutes on both sides until golden brown.
Bring the sour cream and 1 tablespoon of butter to a boil in a small saucepan for 2 minutes and serve in a sauceboat alongside the fried cutlets.

name: Kotlety z jaj (hard-boiled egg cutlets)
summary: Vegetarian cutlets of chopped hard-boiled eggs bound with a thick white sauce, fresh herbs, raw eggs, and breadcrumbs, fried until golden brown in butter.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 8 hard-boiled, 2 raw for the mixture, and 1 beaten for breading

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the roux, plus extra for frying

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for thickening the mixture and breading

steps: Boil 8 eggs hard for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel, and chop finely.
Cook 1 tablespoon of wheat flour with 1 tablespoon of butter over low heat for 2 minutes without browning, then pour in the milk and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until a thick sauce forms.
Mix the chopped eggs with the thick sauce, add the chopped dill, 2 raw eggs, salt, pepper, and enough breadcrumbs for the mixture to hold together well.
Shape the mixture into cutlets, dip each one in the remaining beaten egg, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat the butter in a skillet and fry the cutlets for about 10 minutes on both sides until golden brown.

name: Zrazy z kaszy gryczanej nadziewane grzybami (buckwheat zrazy rolls stuffed with mushrooms)
summary: Rolled cutlets of buckwheat groats cooked soft in mushroom broth, stuffed with a mushroom and onion filling and baked in an onion and sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling the mushrooms to make broth

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 1 for the buckwheat mixture and 1 for breading

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for binding the buckwheat mixture and thickening the onion sauce

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the filling, browning the rolls, and the sauce

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: 1 for the mushroom filling and 1 for the onion sauce

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for the filling and the sauce

steps: Boil the dried mushrooms in water in a pot for 30 minutes, drain them, and divide the mushroom broth into two equal parts.
Add the buckwheat groats to half of the mushroom broth, season with salt, cook for 20 minutes until very soft, and let cool, then beat in 1 egg and add enough wheat flour to shape into flat patties.
Finely chop the cooked dried mushrooms and 1 onion, fry them in a skillet with butter for 5 minutes, and mix with a little of the sour cream.
Shape the buckwheat mixture into oblong patties, place a portion of the mushroom filling on each, and roll up into zrazy cylinders.
Brush the rolls with the second beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs, brown on all sides in butter for 5 minutes, and arrange in a deep ovenproof dish.

Fry the second chopped onion in butter with a little wheat flour, stir in the remaining mushroom broth and the rest of the sour cream, pour the sauce over the rolls, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for 5 minutes.

name: Klops z soczewicy (lentil loaf with soubise sauce)
summary: A baked roulade made from ground lentils, stuffed with young carrots, onion, and dill, served with a velvety soubise onion sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the lentil mixture, plus extra for baking the loaf and cooking the vegetables

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: enough to form a firm, flat layer

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: for sprinkling over the loaf near the end of baking

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for cooking the onions for the sauce

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: sweet cream butter, for finishing the sauce

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the lentil mixture and sauce

ingredients.name: white pepper
ingredients.note: for the lentil mixture and sauce

steps: Soak the lentils in water overnight, then boil them in the same water until tender, about 35 minutes, drain, and dry briefly over the heat.

Pass the hot lentils through a mincer, season with salt and white pepper, and add a tablespoon of butter, the eggs, and enough wheat flour to knead into a mixture that can be shaped into a flat layer about 2 cm thick.
Cook the young carrots gently in butter, covered, for 15 minutes until tender, chop them finely, and mix with the onion fried in butter and the chopped dill.
Spread the carrot filling over the lentil layer, roll it up tightly like a roulade, and transfer carefully to a roasting pan with browned butter.
Bake the loaf in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 35 minutes, basting frequently with butter, then sprinkle with breadcrumbs near the end of baking and brown.

Make the soubise sauce: cook the five cut onions gently in a tablespoon of butter, covered, for 15 minutes without browning. Pass them through a mincer, season with salt, sprinkle with a tablespoon of wheat flour, pour in the milk, and bring briefly to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir in a teaspoon of fresh butter and a pinch of white pepper.
Slice the baked lentil loaf and serve hot with the onion sauce in a sauceboat.

name: Kapusta faszerowana (stuffed whole savoy cabbage)
summary: A whole head of savoy cabbage stuffed between its leaves with a braised cabbage and tomato filling, then braised in sour cream.

ingredients.name: savoy cabbage
ingredients.note: heads: one whole for stuffing, the other for the filling

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the onions and browning the cabbage

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for blanching the cabbage and seasoning the filling

ingredients.name: tomato paste
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for the filling and 1 tbsp for the sauce

steps: Blanch one head of savoy cabbage in boiling salted water for about 8 minutes, drain on a cloth, and carefully fold back the leaves without detaching them from the core.
Boil the second head of cabbage until tender, about 20 minutes, drain, and chop finely.
Fry the chopped onions in butter for 5 minutes, mix with the chopped cabbage and two tablespoons of tomato paste, and season with salt and pepper.
Pack the filling between the folded-back leaves of the first cabbage head, reshape it into a whole head, and tie with cotton twine so it holds its shape.
Brown the stuffed cabbage head in butter in a casserole on all sides for about 10 minutes until golden.
Baste the cabbage with sour cream mixed with the remaining tomato paste and braise covered over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.
Transfer the cabbage to a platter, remove the twine, cut into wedges, and serve with the strained braising sauce.

name: Brukiew lub kalarepa faszerowana (stuffed rutabaga or kohlrabi)
summary: Young rutabaga hollowed out and stuffed with its own mashed flesh, butter, onion, mushrooms, and egg, braised in a sour cream sauce.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for gently cooking the flesh and baking in the saucepan

steps: Peel the young rutabaga, parboil it in boiling water for about 15 minutes until half-tender, then hollow out the centre with a metal teaspoon.
Cook the scooped-out rutabaga flesh gently with butter, covered, for 10 minutes and mash thoroughly, then fry the onion and chopped mushrooms separately in butter.
Mix the mashed pulp with the fried onion, mushrooms, a little butter, and the egg, then pack the filling back into the hollowed rutabaga, shaping a dome on top.
Place the stuffed rutabaga in a small saucepan with melted butter, pour in the vegetable broth, add the sour cream, and season with salt.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then braise gently over low heat for about 20 minutes until the rutabaga is tender and the sauce reduces to one-third of its volume.
Serve the rutabaga hot with the reduced braising sauce spooned over it.

name: Grzyby suszone faszerowane (stuffed dried mushrooms)
summary: Large dried mushroom caps stuffed with a savory mushroom and onion filling, baked with sour cream and served with mashed potatoes.

ingredients.name: dried mushrooms
ingredients.note: 10 large caps for stuffing and 5 smaller mushrooms for chopping into the filling

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the onion and baking the mushrooms

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for the pan sauce, plus extra for spooning over the mushrooms before baking

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for deglazing the pan, plus water for boiling the mushrooms

steps: Boil all the dried mushrooms in water until tender, about 30 minutes, and drain.
Press the ten large mushroom caps between two small boards to squeeze out excess water, and finely chop their stems along with the smaller mushrooms.
Fry the chopped onion in butter for 5 minutes, mix with the chopped mushrooms, egg, and enough breadcrumbs to hold the mixture together, then mound the filling onto the large mushroom caps.
Arrange the stuffed mushrooms in an ovenproof skillet with melted butter, drizzle with butter, spoon sour cream over them, and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 15 minutes.
Mound the mashed potatoes in the centre of a serving platter and arrange the baked mushrooms around them.
Pour two tablespoons of water and a tablespoon of sour cream into the baking skillet, boil for 1 minute, and pour the resulting pan sauce over the mashed potatoes.

name: Jaja faszerowane (stuffed eggs in shells)
summary: Eggs stuffed in their shells with chopped egg, chives cooked in butter until translucent, dill, and parsley leaves, then pan-fried in butter.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 4 large hard-boiled and 2 raw to bind the mixture

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the chives and pan-frying the stuffed eggs

ingredients.name: breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: a handful, for thickening and sprinkling

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: just enough to keep the mixture moist

steps: Hard-boil four eggs for 10 minutes, cool them, and cut them lengthwise in half right through the shells using a very sharp knife.
Carefully scoop out the whites and yolks, keeping the half-shells intact, and finely chop the cooked eggs.
Sauté the chopped chives in butter for 2 minutes and mix them with the chopped eggs, two raw eggs, dill, parsley leaves, breadcrumbs, and a little sour cream.
Fill the reserved half-shells with the prepared stuffing.
Place the stuffed eggs cut-side down in a skillet with hot butter and fry for about 3–4 minutes until golden.

name: Omlet biszkoptowy do nadziewania (puffy soufflé omelette)
summary: A fluffy soufflé omelette made from egg yolks beaten with milk and flour and folded with stiff egg whites, browned in butter on the stove and finished in the oven.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and separate the yolks from the whites of the 5 eggs.
Beat the egg yolks with the wheat flour, milk, and salt until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the beaten yolks.
Melt a generous amount of butter in a large ovenproof skillet, pour in the egg mixture, smooth the top with a knife, and cook on the stove for 4 minutes until the underside is golden brown.
Transfer the skillet to the oven preheated to 180 °C for about 6 minutes until the omelette is set on top, then fold in half and serve immediately.

name: Nadzienie włoskie do omletu (Italian pasta, tomato, and Parmesan omelette filling)
summary: An Italian omelette filling of finely broken pasta tossed hot with butter, tomato paste, and grated Parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: tomato paste
ingredients.note: or 2 fresh tomatoes sliced into rounds

steps: Break the pasta into small pieces, drop into boiling salted water, and cook for about 8 minutes until al dente, taking care not to overcook it.
Drain the cooked pasta, return it to the pot, and toss while hot with the butter, tomato paste, and grated Parmesan cheese for 2 minutes.
Spoon the hot filling directly onto a cooked omelette.

name: Nadzienie „aux fines herbes” do omletu (fines herbes mushroom and onion omelette filling)
summary: An aromatic omelette filling of butter-braised onions, button mushrooms, fresh dill, and parsley leaves.

ingredients.name: button mushrooms
ingredients.note: or 2 cooked dried mushrooms, finely chopped

steps: Peel and thinly slice the onions, and finely chop the button mushrooms, dill, and parsley leaves.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the onions, and cook gently over low heat for about 10 minutes until soft.
Add the chopped button mushrooms, dill, and parsley leaves to the onions, sauté everything together briefly for 2 minutes, and use the hot filling for an omelette.

name: Nadzienie z fasolki szparagowej do omletu (green bean and buttered breadcrumb omelette filling)
summary: A vegetarian omelette filling of boiled green beans tossed with breadcrumbs generously browned in butter.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: generous amount, for browning the breadcrumbs

steps: String the green beans, drop them whole into boiling salted water, and boil for about 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Melt a generous amount of butter in a skillet, add the breadcrumbs, and fry for 3 minutes until golden brown.
Toss the hot green beans with the butter-browned breadcrumbs and spoon the filling into an omelette.

name: Bliny gryczane zaparzane (scalded buckwheat blini)
summary: Traditional yeast blini made with wheat and buckwheat flour scalded with boiling milk, enriched with melted butter and egg yolks.
steps: Dissolve the fresh yeast in the lukewarm water, mix with the wheat flour, cover, and leave in a warm place for about 45 minutes to rise.
Salt the risen sponge, add the buckwheat flour, and mix thoroughly.
Bring the milk to a boil, pour it boiling hot into the batter, and beat with a wooden spoon until completely smooth.
Once the batter has cooled slightly, add the melted butter and egg yolks and beat well again.
Leave the batter to rise a second time for about 30 minutes, then fry the blini in a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side.

name: Bliny pszenne (wheat blini)
summary: Light wheat yeast blini made with water and milk, enriched with melted butter and folded with stiffly beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: divided into two equal parts of 300 g each

steps: Dissolve the fresh yeast in the lukewarm water, mix with half of the wheat flour, season with salt, beat well, and leave in a warm place for about 40 minutes to rise.
Add the egg yolks, melted butter, remaining wheat flour, and lukewarm milk to the risen sponge, then beat thoroughly with a wooden spoon.
Leave the batter in a warm place for another 30 minutes to rise a second time.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them carefully into the risen batter.
Immediately fry the blini in a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown.

name: Bliny bardzo smaczne (yeast blini)
summary: Fluffy yeast blini made from wheat flour scalded with boiling milk, enriched with egg yolks and folded with stiffly beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: part for scalding, the rest for thickening the batter

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: part boiling for scalding the flour, part lukewarm for mixing the batter to sour-cream consistency

steps: Bring part of the milk to a boil, pour the boiling milk over half of the wheat flour, and beat thoroughly until the mixture cools.
Add the crumbled fresh yeast, the remaining dry wheat flour, and enough lukewarm milk to make a batter the consistency of sour cream.
Add the egg yolks beaten with a pinch of salt, mix well, and leave the batter in a warm place for about 45 minutes to rise.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the risen batter.
Fry the blini in a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown.

name: Bliny kartoflane (potato blini)
summary: Yeast blini made from grated raw potatoes and milk-soaked wheat roll, lightened with beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: for dissolving the yeast and soaking the roll

steps: Soak the wheat roll in a little milk, squeeze it out, and pass it through a mincer, then dissolve the fresh yeast in the remaining lukewarm milk.
Grate the raw potatoes on a fine grater and mix them with the minced roll, egg yolks, thick sour cream, salt, and dissolved yeast.
Leave the batter in a warm place for about 40 minutes to rise.
Just before frying, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the batter so that it does not deflate.
Fry the blini in a hot pan for about 3 minutes per side until golden.

name: Hreczuchy (buckwheat fritters)
summary: Simple fritters made from buckwheat flour and sour cream, deep-fried until golden brown.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: for mixing the batter and for serving

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for deep-frying (mixed in equal parts with coconut oil)

steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with enough sour cream to form a thick batter that drops easily from a spoon, and season with salt.
Heat equal parts of butter and coconut oil in a deep skillet.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot fat and fry the fritters for about 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain the fried hreczuchy on paper towels to remove excess fat and serve hot with sour cream.

name: Knedle (savory bread dumplings)
summary: Savory bread dumplings made from breadcrumbs scalded with hot milk, bound with egg yolks, browned onions, and beaten egg whites.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for creaming with the yolks, plus extra for browning the onions and pouring over the dumplings

ingredients.name: plain wheat flour
ingredients.note: for the mixture, plus extra for coating the dumplings

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: 2 finely chopped for the mixture and 1 for the browned butter topping

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the mixture and boiling water

steps: Pour the hot milk over the breadcrumbs and let stand for 10 minutes to swell.
